messages.mission.briefing.text:
I'm finally starting to see some progress around here. No thanks to the Republic though. It's mainly down to independent pilots such as yourself that the system isn't being totally overrun by pirates. And to the rebels. Yeah, I know they're whacky and delusional, but at least they're actively fighting all those opposing the Republic here in Ani. I can't count the number of times they've saved my ass in the last few weeks.

Though I can't agree with their agenda, I can approve of their methods. But let me get to the point. In the chaos we have here whole shiploads of army goods are being misplaced, mishandled or simply stolen every day. I got my hands on some pretty neat GI Paradise Cruise Missiles the other day, don't ask how. These GI versions are the blast.

I've befriended some of the more sane rebels and I want to pay them back for all the help they've given me. I have a crate of the missiles sitting in a hangar on a station in Hek. I'm not stupid enough to have them in my own cargo hold in case old Merchor over there gets nosy all of a sudden. There's a rebel guy waiting on the Sister of EVE station here in Traun waiting for the delivery. All I need is someone capable to get the missiles to him. Interested? I can offer you some pretty rare Republic ammo as a reward.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I'm finally starting to see some progress around here. No thanks to the Republic though. It's mainly down to independent pilots such as yourself that the system isn't being totally overrun by pirates. And to the rebels. Yeah, I know they're whacky and delusional, but at least they're actively fighting all those opposing the Republic here in Ani. I can't count the number of times they've saved my ass in the last few weeks.

Though I can't agree with their agenda, I can approve of their methods. But let me get to the point. In the chaos we have here whole shiploads of army goods are being misplaced, mishandled or simply stolen every day. I got my hands on some pretty neat GI Paradise Cruise Missiles the other day, don't ask how. These GI versions are the blast.

I've befriended some of the more sane rebels and I want to pay them back for all the help they've given me. I have a crate of the missiles sitting in a hangar on a station in Hek. I'm not stupid enough to have them in my own cargo hold in case old Merchor over there gets nosy all of a sudden. There's a rebel guy waiting on the Sister of EVE station here in Traun waiting for the delivery. All I need is someone capable to get the missiles to him. Interested? I can offer you some pretty rare Republic ammo as a reward.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I've been ordered to support our troops in the contested complex here in Traun. We're trying to wrench control for it from the Angel cartel. It's not going all that well, so I've been expecting this for some time. I don't like jumping into a situation totally unprepared, so I've been gathering what information about what is really going on there. The general Republic communication lines don't yield all that much useful information, but through the contacts I'm building with the rebels I actually found out some pretty important thing.

It seems the Angels in the complex, or one of the groups associated with them, have managed to tap into the Republic communication links. No wonder nothing has been going for our troops, all they're movements are known beforehand. Beats me how they did it, but it needs to be dealt with. I'm trying to get the brass to act upon this, but they just point at each other. I know it's hopeless for me to talk directly to our guys in the complex, it will only be intercepted.

But you're not part of the Republic's line of communications so you can act freely. I know the Angels are using a scanner housed in an old Nefantar tactical depot in the complex. I don't know if it's the only one they're operating, but let's start by hitting that one and see what happens. At least it will make me feel a little bit better when I move in there myself sometimes in the near future. Get me a piece of the scanner array. You may have to hit several of the scanners before a useful specimen comes up. Do this for me and I got this rare BPC to give you.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The job's done.  Here's the data chip you requested.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
So you're looking for a job eh? I might have something that's suited for your needs, as long as you're a competent combat-pilot.

If you look over near the ruins of the old Pleasure Gardens, you'll see that no-good thief Rozor Mothrus. He appeared here at the Carnival a few months ago, claiming to be 'just another passerby'. What a rotten lie that was. From the moment I saw him I knew there was something out of place ...

Anyway, we spent some time in the Carnival pub, and I happened to get caught up in a conversation with him about this and that. I was fairly intoxicated at the time, so I can't remember much of it, but somehow he managed to drag out of me the location of my hideout in Barkrik. It's a nice little spot inside an area of space which we call 'deadspace', near an asteroid belt filled with low-life miners and rogue mechanical drones, not exactly a family resort if you know what I mean. But for someone like me avoiding those pests is not much of a problem, and it's the perfect hiding place when you have a run in with the law.

Now if allowing him to discover my favorite hiding place isn't enough, it so happens that I stashed my latest invention, a very valuable hacker-program, in a storage container right there! It's my only copy, and very very illegal here in Minmatar space. If Rozor gets his grubby hands on it, I'm ruined!

Now you might be thinking, why don't I just run over there and pick up the data chip? Well, the problem is Rozor has apparently hired some Maru mercs to do the dirty work for him. The last time I tried to enter the asteroid belt leading to the storage bin, I noticed some of them hiding by the miner's quarters. I escaped without them noticing me, and after some info-digging I found out they had been hired by Rozor.

I want you to fly out there and see if the Maru have miraculously not found the data chip I had hidden in the storage bin. If you find it, bring it to me for a sizable reward.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: You ... you're back {[character]player.name}.  I didn't expect you to make it.  Well, let's get on to your next assignment, shall we?

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I won't take any part in your criminal activities, {[character]agentID.name}.  Go find someone else to do your dirty work.

localizedName.text: Kutill's Warez - Hack The Station Mainframe! (2 of 3)

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The data chip has been delivered to your accomplice, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Since you passed the test with flying colors, it's time for you to complete the assignment. Deliver this data chip to the Brutor station in Lustrevik. My contact there will use it to upload my program into it's computer mainframe. That's all you need to know. Do this fast and I'll throw you a bone.

Just whatever you do don't get caught. Remember, this program is very illegal. If the customs officials find it in your cargo hold, there'll be hell to pay, and it may compromise this operation. But since their scanners haven't been able to detect it yet, you don't have to worry too much.

You've saved me a heap load of trouble, {[character]player.name}.  And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here is Machul's decapitated head, as you requested, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's just one last thing I need done before we're through, {[character]player.name}. Ever since you retrieved that data chip for me, Rozor Mothrus has been extremely 'excited'. I'm afraid he might strike at any moment, if he learns what I'm up to. But I can't take him and his buddies by myself.

You'll probably find Machul and 3 Brutor mercenaries orbiting Rozor's ship. When you do, take them out, and bring me Machul's head from the wreckage if you can. I'll use it to tease Rozor ... right before I put an end to his miserable existence.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: You're asking me to commit murder?  This is outrageous, I refuse!

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You've rid me of my biggest hindrance, {[character]player.name}.  The next time I bump into Rozor in the Carnival, he's toast!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Someone once told me that the road to eternal damnation is paved with good intentions. Welcome to that road, friend. I know people are already mocking the Republic Fleet for its lack of progress here in Ani, but those people don't have a clue about what's really going on here. The Parliament obviously thought it would be enough for us to show up here like we were on some damn military parade and the pirates would fall all over themselves trying to get out of the way. This political blunder has already cost many a good soldier his life. We're not getting any support from back home and morale is at an all time low after we lost our headquarters. You can see what's left of them over there.

Command decided to launch a retaliation attack against the pirates and most of our forces are currently embroiled in the local complex trying to wrench control of it from the Angel Cartel. But the Cartel and us are not the only players out here and I'm not even sure the Cartel was behind the attack on our headquarters. All the same, most of my time is spent on rebuilding our outpost here and give logistic support to our troops in the contested complex. I'm woefully short of staff, meaning many important tasks are not being done. Such as going through the ruins of our former headquarters and retrieve the bodies of our fallen comrades. But such a trivial job is beneath someone of your caliber. I have something more important to ask of you.

One of our squadrons in the contested complex was ambushed recently by particularly mean Angels. The pirates are still hovering around the squadron's remains, gloating over their victory. I need someone well acquainted in the arts of war to teach them a lesson, and most importantly, to retrieve the bodies of the Republic pilots so they can be properly treated. I think you're ideally suited for a task such as this, my best men are already engaging the pirates around the system and the soldiers I have here are too green to be of any use. Interested?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Thanks to the efforts of you and other good pilots, a lot of families are getting the bodies of their loved ones back. You can well imagine how important that is, not having to sit in anguish over the fate of those you love. But having those bodies sitting in the Redoubt's freezer isn't accomplishing this, I need to get these bodies to a Fleet station where they can be properly taken care of. I know it sounds as a menial task, and in many ways it is, but getting the bodies of these soldiers quickly and safely back to their loved ones is critical if we're to have any public support back home.

Take care of this for me and I'm bound to have something more suitable to your talents next time around. Just to make it a little more interesting I'll throw in a good amount of bonus reward if you can finish this quickly.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The loss of our headquarters was a tremendous shock to us. Not only did many good man and women lose their lives there, but it also gave the rest of us a serious fright. The combat efficiency of our troops is abysmal and the worst part of it all is that the desertion rate has climbed dramatically. Only in the last month almost hundred pilots deserted. Most have fled home and they're are out of our reach and not our concern. But some are still around, having joined the rebels, or worse, become brigands themselves. It is the latter I'm especially keen on tracking down.

I need to get out a strong sign that deserters will not be treated kindly. Deserting from the Republic Fleet is treason and is punishable by death. Morale is bad enough as it is and if people start thinking that desertion is the easy way out, our cause is lost. Unfortunately, those that desert, particularly those that go and join the pirates, know this. So they have dug themselves in, waiting for the inevitable repercussion to arrive. That means that those that go after these brigands must have exceptional battle prowess. They will be going up against trained soldiers caught in a corner with nowhere to run. That makes them desperate, and desperate people are always more dangerous. I have marked you as someone capable to handling such a difficult assignment. You will be well rewarded if you choose to hunt these deserters down and bring them back to me. Dead or alive.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Thanks again for a job well done with those deserters. One of the pilots I've hired to hunt them down managed to catch one alive. He's been in interrogation for awhile now. He was stubborn at first, but we've been persistent and now he's squealing like a pig. Most of it is just gibberish, but some of it's been sensible. And if what he's telling is true, we've got a serious situation on our hands.

It seems that many of these desertions are not just some random panic attacks. There's a Thukker tribe leader, going by the name Norak Pakkul, hiding out in the contested complex here in Traun that actually has the nerve to recruit Republic pilots for his band of gangsters. And with the jittery nerves of our pilots, he's actually been quite successful. Needless to say, this guy has to be brought down before he damages our cause further.

The only problem is that you cannot access the room he's in without the proper authorization. The Angels keep a tight control on their access cards, so I've been at a loss on how to get to this guy. But I've been digging around and found out that there is another way. It seems the old Nefantar access cards are still useable. I heard about a guy out by the Sister Camp that had repaired some damaged cards he received and made them operational again. My pilots have brought back all kinds of stuff they've picked up in the contested complex and I actually have a good number of these old Nefantar keycards.

All I need are the tools to fix one of these keycards. I want to do this quickly before this Pakkul guy discovers we're on to him and makes himself scarce. So I'm asking you to whisk over into Minmatar space and bring me one of those Fleet repair kits that makes this kind of a job a breeze. Again, I'll make this interesting for you by giving you a good bonus reward if you hurry. Once this is done, we're all set to take this Norak Pakkul out of the picture for good.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Ok, we're all set to take this Norak Pakkal out of business. The card I gave you gives you and your friends entrance to the inner most room of the contested complex. And you're going to need your friends for this one. You can only enter the room in cruisers, but you should expect some very heavy resistance in there, from what I've heard. Nothing that a pilot of your caliber can't handle, but if my army life has taught me anything it is that the careful survive.

Bring me Pakkul's DNA and I'm authorized to give you a very rare BPC as a reward.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The Republic's invasion into the sacred home of our Ammatar allies is an abomination that cannot go unpunished. I know the Republic calls it a resettlement of a territory that is theirs. But the Republic is nothing but a bunch of ignorant thieves and scoundrels. How can they argue that the Ani constellation is theirs? It just goes to show that history is written by the victors. Sure, the constellation is marked on all the right maps as belonging to the Republic, but it's the ancestral home of the Nefantar and by right it should be their scions, the Ammatar, who inherit this place.

It's a disgrace that our beloved late Holy Emperor did not take action regarding this most unholy act. Many Amarr Holders are of the opinion that we Amarrians cannot sit idly by and let this travesty go on unabated. This time, we will be the victors and write our own glorious history about how the Republic was humiliated here in Ani.

I was sent here for a very special mission by my master. I'm looking for people to assist me in my task, and if you prove yourself, I will give you more lucrative missions down the line. But first you have to show that you're a true friend of the Amarrians and an enemy of the Minmatar slave-dogs.

The Republic is trying to overrun the military complex here in Traun held by the Angel Cartel. I've been sending pilots on secret missions to hamper Republic efforts there, and I want you to do the same. Bring me eight REF Insignias looted from the dead corpses of Republic pilots and I will grant you further opportunities to make history, a correct history. Search for REF pilots in the contested complex ― they bear the insignia I'm asking for.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I congratulate you again on a job well done with those Republic pilots. Their forces are in a disarray in the system, and I feel we won't have long to wait for a final victory over those pathetic Minmatar rats. You have proven yourself just as ruthless and capable as I like my employees to be, so it's time to let you in on my true mission here.

My Amarr lord, who shall remain nameless, is adamant that the Republic not succeed in gaining total control over Ani. But because we lack the official support of the Empire, we need to be discreet and open-minded in our dealings out here. The Angel Cartel is the strongest pirate force in the constellation. If we're to have any chance of success here, we must strike a deal with the Angels for assistance. I know it is loathsome to be forced to deal with pirate scum, but the importance of our mission here must override any such qualms. The failure of the Republic is what matters most here.

I've been locked in negotiations over the past few weeks with leaders from the Cartel. I feel we've made good progress, but the Cartel requires a token of good faith before they'll continue the discussions. I have graciously offered them large quantities of the highly corrosive Aqua Regia acid as a gift, and they have accepted. Now, all I need is someone who can quickly ferry the acid to me so I can continue the negotiations. Do this for me and we're one step closer to bringing the Republic to its knees here.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Ah, {[character]player.name}! Thanks to your timely assistance, my negotiations with the Angels are going well. But there's a Thukker leader who's constantly sabotaging the discussions. The Angels and the Thukker are allies, unfortunately, so they listen to this guy; all I can do is sit by and seethe when he starts undermining my efforts. I've had quite enough of this Thukker chieftain, but I can't do anything directly to him myself for fear of damaging my fragile relations with the Angels.

You, on the other hand, are an unknown entity in the eyes of the Angels, so if you were to take him out, there's little risk of the Angels ever being able to trace his killing back to me. I don't even know the name of this bigshot Thukker. All I know is that he's some sort of a chief. He likes to hang out in the contested complex here in Traun: You should be able to track him down there.

By the way, I'm still sending people to hunt REF pilots, and they often return with various interesting items they've looted. Amongst the stuff I've received is some rare ammo that I'll give you when you return with the remains of this annoying Thukker chieftain.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ah, {[character]player.name}! Thanks to your timely assistance, my negotiations with the Angels are going well. But there's a Thukker leader who's constantly sabotaging the discussions. The Angels and the Thukker are allies, unfortunately, so they listen to this guy; all I can do is sit by and seethe when he starts undermining my efforts. I've had quite enough of this Thukker chieftain, but I can't do anything directly to him myself for fear of damaging my fragile relations with the Angels.

You, on the other hand, are an unknown entity in the eyes of the Angels, so if you were to take him out, there's little risk of the Angels ever being able to trace his killing back to me. I don't even know the name of this bigshot Thukker. All I know is that he's some sort of a chief. He likes to hang out in the contested complex here in Traun: You should be able to track him down there.

By the way, I'm still sending people to hunt REF pilots, and they often return with various interesting items they've looted. Amongst the stuff I've received is some rare ammo that I'll give you when you return with the remains of this annoying Thukker chieftain.

messages.mission.briefing.text: I just received some disturbing news. It seems the Minmatar are becoming suspicious and have sent out some of their top troopers to investigate. I don't know if these guys are hunting for me in particular, or just anyone plotting against the Republic. Nevertheless, I can't have some snooping commandos messing up my negotiations with the Angels. I want those so-called special forces to receive a very special welcome here in Traun. I feel you're naturally suited to head the welcoming committee. Do you take my meaning? I want those fools dead, so I'm offering you a rare BPC as a reward if you do this for me. Kill all the hunters you find in the area and blow up their command post as well. Bring back a sample of their inferior DNA to get your reward.

localizedName.text: Reign of Chaos - Pidgeon Shooting (1 of 3)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The infidel slave-dogs in their so called Republic have gone too far this time. If they think they can spread their barbaric ways over the ancestral home of our friends and allies the Ammatars, it just confirms they're as stupid as I always thought. The emperor may be fooled by the soothing lies of the Republic, but the Sarum family is not. We know that behind this false facade the Minmatars are constantly scheming to undermine our glorious Empire and we will not tolerate it.

It is here in Traun were we intend to stop this folly and drive the Republic back to where it belongs. I was sent here by a leading member of the Sarum family to organize the resistance to the Republic's drive into Traun. I'm recruiting pilots for various tasks and I'd like to add you to my roster.

I already have plenty of people engaging Republic forces. But there are other groups that are a thorn in our side and need to be dealt with. The constellation is awash with Thukker nomad scum. Even if they are also a nuisance for the Republic, many of them are actively working against us. We cannot allow that. The Thukkers like nothing better than to steal and plunder. You are certain to find a number of them scavenging in the contested complex, stealing items that our Ammatar allies left behind. Kill a few of these scavengers and bring me what they've looted.

localizedName.text: Reign of Chaos - Take Two (2 of 3)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Your Thukker assignment was a total success, so I'm sending you on another mission to slaughter Minmatar infidels. This time around it's a small rebel base that I want you to target. The rebels, or freedom fighters as they idiotically call themselves, have set up a small base within the contested complex and are using it to aid the Republic's efforts in there. It needs to be dealt with.

I want you to find this rebel base and annihilate it. Then pick whatever rebel remains you can find and bring them to me. I have a lot of uses for grade-A biomass. Thought I personally wouldn't grade any Minmatar bodily remains as being A. If you take care of this quickly and efficiently I'll even throw in a decent BPC as a bonus reward.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Our plan to bring total anarchy to Traun is on a good course. But the cursed Sisters of EVE witches are bothersome. If it wasn't for them I'm sure the Republic would have fled a long time ago. And I also have reliable sources telling me that the rebels are operating in the Sister's shadows.

These witches have to be taught a lesson to leave things alone that do not concern them. An agent of mine has infiltrated the local Sister station, all set to reap havoc. All I need is to provide him with those means and that's where you come in, {[character]player.name}. Sneak into the station with this bomb here and our man will take care of the rest. I hope. If we manage to pull this off it could bring the Republic forces here to its knees on one fell swoop and bring us the constellation on a silver platter. With so much at stake, I'm offering you a very good BPC as a reward.

localizedName.text: Corpse Dealer - The Bodypart Trade (1 of 3)

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm here to find work, actually. You know of any interesting job opportunities in these parts?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
To get straight to business, I deal in body parts. Now don't get all pale and shocked on me, eh? I'm not one of those crazy Blood Raider flesh-eaters, ya know. All I do is acquire body parts of the deceased and sell them to the highest bidder, usually to the medical divisions within some of the major corporations of the Republic. You know, for research or cheap transplants to needy patients.

Anyway, I need some frozen livers I recently purchased to be transferred to the Eifyr and Co. research center in Eram. I'll provide you with a bookmark and everything; all you need to do is drop off the goods at your hangar there and my associates will pick it up.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
If that's the case, I got something I think you're suited for. People here avoid me like the plague, and I can't fathom why. I just make my living like the next guy ... I got a family to feed, ya know.

Anyway, to get straight to business, I deal in body parts. Now don't get all pale and shocked on me, eh? I'm not one of those crazy Blood Raider flesh-eaters, ya know. messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Good job, now if you're up for some risky business then let me know.

localizedName.text: Corpse Dealer - Bring Back the Goods (2 of 3)

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: So, what's the job?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I don't know if you're up for risking that ship of yours, but if you are then I got just the job for ya. This morning I was contacted by a distraught Gallente traveler. Apparently he came here with a group of colleagues from Quafe Company while on vacation. They decided to pay Barkrik a visit along their route. Yesterday they had planned to visit some ancient ruins near one of the outlying settlements within this system ... bad idea. Fortunately for my Gallente friend, he was sick that day, and so he decided to stay behind on the station while his companions went on their "sightseeing" trip.

Well, it didn't end too good for them. The ancient ruins are located inside a deadspace pocket frequented by the Gist. Of course, the local who suggested they visit the ruins didn't tell them that, and I'd hazard a guess he was in league with those scoundrels as well. Anyway, to cut the story short, these tourists were massacred by sentry guns as soon as they appeared near the ruins.

Now here's where you come in. The Gallente who contacted me wants his colleagues' remains to take back with him to their families when he returns home. He was asking some mercenaries to brave the ruins and retrieve the bodies, and I overheard their conversation. I offered to get the job done for a very low price. Of course, any organs left intact after their deaths will mysteriously disappear before I let the Gallente have them, but that's a detail I left out of our conversation. Ha ha.

You'll find the wreckage of the craft carrying the Gallente tourists near the ancient ruins. There are a couple Angel sentry guns that will attack you on sight. I suggest ignoring them; if you retaliate it will only cause more Gist to arrive at the scene. The ships guarding the wreckage will have to be taken care of, though. But like most Gist, they will probably be too arrogant to call for backup, at least until it's too late.

If you feel you're up for this task, then let me know. I'll pay well for those corpses.

localizedName.text: Corpse Dealer - Kutill's Hacker Program (3 of 3)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's just one last thing that I need. I was contacted a few months ago by one of the elders within the Brutor Tribe about a rogue Sebiestor agent operating from the Carnival in Barkrik. Although I may be Sebiestor myself, I bear no love for those I used to call family. The suspected rogue agent is none other than Dagras Kutill, a filthy wench who deals in drugs and other illegal wares.

I've spoken to her on numerous occasions, and in one of our conversations I stumbled upon some pretty interesting info. She claims to have discovered a way to hack into the Brutor Tribe's station database, giving her enormous power over any Brutor station. Apparently she uses some kind of program that is stored on database chips she keeps hidden in one of her compounds.

When I tried to ask her more questions about this program, she became extremely agitated and started accusing me of being a traitor to the Sebiestors. A few weeks later, I was almost killed by a gang of Maru thugs, and I'm sure she was behind it. She's been after my neck ever since, so I've had to call in a group of Brutor mercenaries to keep me safe. Without them, I'd probably be dead by now.

Since she doesn't know you yet, {[character]player.name}, I'm sure you will have an easier time acquiring this data chip than me. If you do, I'll pay a hefty price for it.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: If all else fails, you could just take the data chip from her by force, pulling it from the wreckage after you've blown her to bits. But don't mention to anyone what I just told you!

localizedName.text: Scandal In Barkrik - Deliver The Ambassador (1 of 4)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I am an agent working for the Republic Parliament, and I was sent to Barkrik to investigate rumors of an incredible breach of Minmatar law by the Amarrian corporation Joint Harvesting. This corporation was given rights to this patch of space a few years ago, after some of their key members were the first major Amarrian figures to officially expressed 'regret' for the crimes committed by the Empire, and so far we have had little trouble with them, other than the strong opposition from hard-liners within the government.

But certain rumors are afloat within the inner circles of the Republic, and beyond, that Joint Harvesting actually employs slaves on at least one of their plantations within Barkrik. This rumor has never been proven, and therefore we have not yet taken action. Powerful 'elements' within the Minmatar government have been pressing for the military to directly intervene and make a political scene out of this mess.
This is exactly what the Republic does not need. If this rumor turns out to be true, the late Karin Midular's agenda of peace between the Republic and the Empire will go up in smoke, and all our hard work for the past years will be for nothing. The skirmishes you see today between our forces will be nothing compared to what follows if war is officially declared, and I'm sure the hard liners within the Republic will be pressing hard for that to happen as soon as this gets out.

Now you're probably asking yourself, where do you come into all of this? Well, I was sent to Barkrik on a mission, which unfortunately I can't complete due to a breakdown in my ship's engine. I'd like you to complete my objectives for me, as I don't have much time. I'll pay you for it, of course.

Your first job is to escort the Republic ambassador, Hugo Farin, from {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} to his office in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. He was visiting the Joint Harvesting chief of staff in Barkrik, as well as taking a good look at their plantations here. I was assigned to transport him back home, but obviously I can't complete my assignment on time.

localizedName.text: Scandal In Barkrik - Retrieve The Inspector (2 of 4)

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've brought back the inspector as you wished.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Your second job is to bring one of our inspectors, Layna Whizon, to me.  She is one of two plantation inspectors that we haven't retrieved yet after our ambassador's visit to Barkrik.  I warn you, the trip will be a long one, the Amarrians there had the crazy idea of placing the beacon leading into the deadspace pockets very far away from the acceleration gates linking the rooms.  I suggest you take a fast ship on this trip, and I'm also afraid your micro-Warpdrive will be inoperable due to the effects of deadspace.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
You were attacked by mercenaries while inside the premises of the Joint Harvesting plantation? Interesting. I truly hope they did not cause too much damage to your ship, I certainly did not expect this to happen.

I'll have a word with the Joint Harvesting Chief of Operations in Barkrik, but I'm quite sure he will deny everything and blame it on pirates. I'm also starting to wonder if they were actually behind the Cartel attack on our convoy into Barkrik to begin with ... And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!

localizedName.text: Scandal In Barkrik - Deliver The Inspector (3 of 4)

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: So, what's the next assignment?

messages.mission.briefing.text: Now that I've gotten Layna's report, it's time for her to return back to our bureau in Orduin.  Please take her there, {[character]player.name}.  After this has been done, prepare yourself well for the final assignment.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Now that I've gotten Layna's report, it's time for her to return back to our bureau in Orduin.  Please take her there, {[character]player.name}.  After this has been done, prepare yourself well for the final assignment.

localizedName.text: Scandal In Barkrik - The Final Inspection (4 of 4)

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Amazing stuff. You succeeded where we failed, {[character]player.name}. I was about to give up on the search for our agent, and the plantation. I will report these findings straight away to Maleatu Shakor, and I'm sure the senate will hear of it soon.

I must ask you though to please keep this matter quiet for the time being. This is a huge political issue which must be treated with utmost care, or we'll cause a riot. The political scene in the Republic is very brittle at the moment, and this information has the potential to destroy the current government if it leaks out.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
After we came to Barkrik on our mission for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}, we stumbled upon some local rumors of a hidden Amarr slave plantation within the system. We tried investigating it for some time, but to no avail. However, one of our top secret agents, Bono Zakan, went missing during the investigation. The last we heard from him was a transmission from a remote area of Barkrik where he called for help. We couldn't trace it unfortunately, but I firmly believe he found something he wasn't supposed to.

I don't know if Bono's alive or dead, but I want him or his body returned to me for proper burial. I also want you to investigate the claims of this hidden plantation while you're at it, perhaps the two are linked. To search for the plantation, I suggest you use scan probes within Barkrik. With luck the Amarrians will have placed some sort of cosmic signature near the entrance to lead their own convoys to the area. You could also fly to every moon within the system and hope to stumble upon it's entrance, if you have no way of acquiring a scan probes. Good luck.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Hey, no need to be rude. I just came here looking for some work.

messages.mission.briefing.text: I've been trying to hack into the Gist database in their stronghold within Hjoramold for some time now, but I can't get by their security codes. Get me those codes, and I'll make you rich. You might find them off the Gist overseer Arrak Nutan. He usually roams around Hraldar's ruins, within the old Legendary Stronghold. <font color = #EE3B3B>The acceleration gate leading into the complex is inaccessible for anything bigger than a battlecruiser, but the Gist have manufactured a few battleships inside the deadspace pockets.</font> Needless to say, this Overseer Nutan flies one of them.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ah, a capsuleer, I see. In that case, you might be of some use after all. Fair enough.

I've been trying to hack into the Gist database in their stronghold within Hjoramold for some time now, but I can't get by their security codes. Get me those codes, and I'll make you rich. Deal?

Oh, yeah, you might find them off the Gist overseer Arrak Nutan. He usually roams around Hraldar's ruins, within the old Legendary Stronghold. The acceleration gate leading into the complex is inaccessible for anything bigger than a battlecruiser, but the Gist have manufactured a few battleships inside the deadspace pockets. Needless to say, this Overseer Nutan flies one of them.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
Amazing, you actually managed to infiltrate the Gist stronghold and retrieve the codes from the overseer? Wow, and here I thought I had sent you into a certain death-trap. With these codes I will be able to hack into the Gist database within their stronghold and do all sorts of mischief.

After I transfer a sizable sum of ISK into my personal bank account, what should I do next? Hmmm... Yeah, maybe I'll upload a virus, destroying all their database files ... or maybe I'll disable all their sentry guns ... ooh, but what about sending all their plans, trade routes, and such straight to the Republic security forces? Oh, heck, so much to do, so little time.

And don't you leave just yet. You're obviously very capable, so I have another assignment for you!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Get these reports to the Republic Security Forces base in Uisper. My cousin works as an officer there. The reports contain information on Angel Cartel plans and smuggling routes, which I extracted from the Gist database within Hjoramold. This information is way too important to just send through conventional means; I can't risk the transmission being hacked.

Once my cousin gets a hold of these reports and presents them directly to Bjongausen Agnake, I'm sure he'll get a promotion.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Get these reports to the Republic Security Forces base in Uisper. My cousin works as an officer there. messages.mission.briefing.text:
Our intelligence operatives have compiled the information you brought, along with information provided by others, in a dossier which should give our strike force all it needs to intercept that convoy and grab whatever goodies they're carrying. They'll never know what hit them.

I need you to take the dossier to a station in Otitoh and leave it in your hangar there. One of our agents from the outpost in Otitoh will get to it, hopefully in time for us to make the strike as quickly and efficiently as possible. If you can do this quickly, I'll throw in an extra reward for you. Good luck.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
I don't know how I can ever repay you for saving my ass, {[character]player.name}, but I hope you like these laser rifles. One of my hobbies is modifying weapons such as these to increase their effectiveness. They will probably fetch a decent price, 'cause I'm well known in these parts as a weapons dealer.

Safe travels.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Something's come up that's perfectly suited to your ... er, talents. The Gist somehow managed to track down the signal from my computer while I was busy hacking their database. They shut me out and changed their codes. Fortunately, the interference from the Hyperbole Nexus prevented them from finding my exact location, but they at least know who I am.

Apparently, the assassin they sent to deal with me is none other than Kael Nutan, the son of the Gist overseer you killed earlier. Kael is a much better combat pilot than his dad ever was, certainly a force to be reckoned with. He completely obliterated my residence here in Barkrik, despite all the booby-traps I had laid for his men.

If you could fly to the coordinates of my residence and take care of Kael and his henchmen, I would be eternally grateful. Just don't expect it to be easy: You'll have to face a large squadron of Gist ships, including Kael's battleship, which is one of the best in their entire armada. I wish you luck, {[character]player.name} ― you're gonna need it.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Something's come up that's perfectly suited to your ... er, talents. The Gist somehow managed to track down the signal from my computer while I was busy hacking their database. They shut me out and changed their codes. Fortunately, the interference from the Hyperbole Nexus prevented them from finding my exact location, but they at least know who I am.

Apparently, the assassin they sent to deal with me is none other than Kael Nutan, the son of the Gist overseer you killed earlier. I wish you luck, {[character]player.name} ― you're gonna need it.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Since you're a trusted operative of the State, I'm going to let you in on my current operation in the hope you can render me some assistance. I am, along with a few other agents, on an undercover mission to infiltrate some of the bandit gangs in this area, in an effort to get the Navy a better foothold in these blasted badlands.

We need some supplies from the outlying areas, but we need to maintain complete secrecy. In fact, it's best if we don't show our faces anywhere, and thus we need inauspicious people such as yourself to gather some materials for us. First off, we're creating a disguise to try and infiltrate the Roving Dodgers, a gang that's been terrorizing some of the outposts in this constellation. We're going to need some specialized polymer fabrics in order to create disguises that pass inspection, yet provide protection in the event that we're discovered.

I need you to head out to the Nugoeihuvi Development Studio in Sakkikainen and pick me up some TX-890 polymers. Nugoeihuvi manufactures them specially for that idiotic extreme reality show, and our insider has allowed us access to some of it. Head over there and bring me back some of it, and I'll probably have another job for you.

First off - thanks again for the polymers. They will come in very handy. Our technicians have most things they need to complete the disguise now, but one crucial thing is still missing. In order to create certain facial characteristics required for the impersonation of one of the people we'll be, ahem, "replacing," we're going to need some silicon from one of the Lai Dai factories in the constellation.

Head out to Sakkikainen, get us that silicon, and we'll be one step closer to our goal.

We've just discovered that one of the operatives on our team was a double agent from the very gang we're trying to infiltrate! Just before he decamped, we managed to plant a homing beacon on his ship. We can give you a bookmark to the location of the beacon. When you activate the bookmark, the beacon shoots out from his ship to prevent you colliding with him straight out of warp.

He's probably at a rendezvous point right now, waiting for someone to give the information to. Move quickly, or all our work here will be for nothing! I want his head. I will reward you handsomely if you complete this job in time for our mission to be salvaged.

localizedName.text: The Plantation Workers - Caught In A Storm (1 of 4)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Ah so it's you, {[character]player.name}. You've made quite a name for yourself within the inner circles of the Empire, I'm sure you will come in handy. I have a few tasks that need to be carried out a.s.a.p., in the name of Joint Harvesting. Acquiring mercenaries in these parts has been quite difficult to say the least, considering the locals absolutely despise us. Their ungratefulness is astounding, considering how well we treated them during our reign over the Minmatar territories.

Well enough of that, I'll get to the point. We had a convoy incoming from the Amarrian territories to one of our plantations in Barkrik when disaster struck. A group of vile 'freedom fighter' terrorists ambushed them as soon as they appeared out of hyper-jump within Barkrik. The escort ships managed to fend off the attackers, allowing the freighter to escape relatively unharmed. But due to the interference, it went a little off course and ended up crashing into an area of deadspace we call 'The Dustbowl'. It's not far from here, and all travelers are advised to avoid it at all costs. What a stroke of bad luck for our convoy to end up in there!

Needless to say, we haven't heard from it since. The Dustbowl is infested with rogue drones and criminals hiding from the law. No sane person without a bounty on his head ventures in there, it's a virtual death trap. I'm certain our freighter has either been destroyed or so badly damaged that it can't escape. I want you to fly in there and investigate, if you find the freighter bring back anything you can salvage from it to me. And don't speak a word of your findings to anyone! This is top secret business.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: So some of the slaves actually survived the ordeal, very nice. You've earned your reward, slaves are an incredibly valuable asset so deep in Minmatar space. And do not forget, don't speak of this to ANYONE, not even your closest ally! There are already rumors afloat that our plantations in Barkrik have slaves on board, but if the rumors are substantiated then our entire operation within Minmatar space will be compromised. And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!

localizedName.text: The Plantation Workers - Treat The Injured (2 of 4)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The slaves you brought back in your last mission are almost all injured, some critically. We need medical supplies here ASAP, I don't even dare move them to the plantation in this state. I don't know how long some of them will last, so time is of the essence here. If you're fast, I'll give you a hefty bonus.

I couldn't come up with the required medical supplies fast enough, so you'll have to find them on your own. I suggest looking at the market in this or neighboring regions.

localizedName.text: The Plantation Workers - Save The Plantation (4 of 4)

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm ready for your assignment, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You've done Joint Harvesting and the Empire a great service again, {[character]player.name}.  We won't forget this.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Ok the assignment is simple, but easier said than done. One of our hidden plantations within Barkrik has been infiltrated by the Freedom Fighter terrorist organization! They somehow managed to follow me there undetected while I transported the slaves you ferried here in your last mission to the plantation premises. A very devious plan of theirs ...

The last I heard the security defenses around the plantation had been overwhelmed. The plantation itself is hidden deep within an asteroid belt within deadspace, it will take them a while to reach it. Hopefully this will give you enough time to intercept their forces before they destroy all of our structures there! Defend our control tower at all costs! Succeed in this task and you will be well rewarded.

localizedName.text: The Plantation Workers - Extra Hands (3 of 4)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Although it looks like we will save most of the injured slaves you brought back in a previous mission, the current number of them is insufficient to satisfy the plantation overseer. Plus many of the ones that are getting better won't be ready for work for some time.

Now I know we have an oversupply of slaves in Hjoramold currently, the Joint Harvesting plantations there don't really need so many workers. They've agreed to supply us with an extra 50 slaves from their own stock. If you could just bring them here, past the Minmatar customs officials undetected, I'll reward you well.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I don't know if you've heard of me yet, but if you spend more time in this constellation you're sure to. Anyway, the name's Rie Nissiken. I'm owner and proprietor of the House of Flowers, finest little ladies' house in this here corner of the universe. Now, most days everything's just hunky-dory, but today I seem to have a problem.

See, there's this little sweetheart called Lucia whom I've been grooming to be one of my girls. She's a natural at it, and happy with the job and the money it pays, but there's a problem: her overbearing, abusive ex-fiancee, Roark. Just yesterday he grabbed her and whisked her off in his ship, screaming and cursing that this lifestyle wasn't for her.

Now, call me libertarian, but I do believe people should be allowed to choose what they do for a living. I think Roark needs to learn that the hard way. If you agree, then how about this: there's a little watering hole built in an old astrofarm in system, where he and scum like him hang out. Head on over there, show him the light, and bring darling Lucia back to me. Sound good?

localizedName.text: House of Flowers - Escort Service (2 of 3)

messages.mission.briefing.text: There is a high-level executive party tonight at the Nugoeihuvi Corporation Publisher station in Friggi, and they've asked us to provide some discreet female companionship for some of these discerning gentlemen.  If you can bring a few of my ladies safely down to the station, I will see to it that you're rewarded for your efforts.

localizedName.text: House of Flowers - Hell Hath No Fury (3 of 3)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Today is a dark day for the House of Flowers, {[character]player.name}. A group of ruthless cads came barging into my beautiful establishment just yesterday, drunken and loutish, and manhandled some of my girls rather badly. Now, there's nothing which makes me quite as mad as just that - pathetic cowards rough-housing my ladies just for kicks.

These bastards like to hang out at the Red Roid, a sleazy, run-down miner's dive in this system. One of them is the proprietor, and the others are his two sons. They cater to the slimiest of clientele; half-hearted miners from the contested facilities in Friggi, good for nothing but downing firewater shots and killing plants with their breath. I want you to go in there, kill these worthless scum and destroy their disgusting little honky-tonk. For that, you will have my gratitude and a shedload of cash to boot.

localizedName.text: Treasure Hunter - The Vherokior Medallion (1 of 4)

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm interested.  Got any clues as to where I can find these artifacts?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The first artifact I'm looking for is the famous Vherokior Medallion. Since ancient times, the Vherokior tribe has awarded it's greatest achievers and leaders with medallions, signifying their status within the community. These medallions are rare, and usually they are buried along with the wearer after his death. The medallion worn by the leader of the Vherokior is an exception, as it is given to whoever takes control of the tribe to signify a change of leadership.

A long time ago, before the Great Rebellion, the Nefantar claimed the Vherokior Medallion as tribute when they took control of most Minmatar worlds. It was never returned to the Vherokior, and although it was eventually remade after the Minmatar rebellion, the original is worth more than you can imagine.

After tracking down this artifact for many years, I finally found out where it is being kept. To my utter dismay I was told it had fallen into the hands of the Cartel, sold to one of their leaders for an obscene amount of ISK from a private dealer. This Gist overlord's name is Arrak Nutan, and he currently resides in the Legendary Minmatar Stronghold within Hjoramold. Getting to him will be difficult, as the place is a virtual deathtrap.

I'll pay a very handsome amount for this medallion, as long as it's still fully intact. Not that I expect you to get past the Gist fleet inside ...

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: I can't believe it!  You managed to get past the entire Gist armada defending their stronghold, take out Arak, and return unharmed?  You're amazing {[character]player.name}, and you definately earned your reward.  And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!

localizedName.text: High Noon - A Few Cards Short (1 of 2)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Have you ever had a nemesis, {[character]player.name}? If you have, you know how it feels. That everpresent lingering burn in the pit of your stomach, sweat and chills when you see his name written, the obsession, the overpowering strength of emotion. In fact, it's not unlike... ahem. Yes, well.

So! I have a nemesis. And hoo boy, what a nemesis. He's the most down-and-dirty rat bastard you'll ever meet, the meanest of the mean, vilest of the vile. Heck, he even has the Zs and Xs in his name to prove it. And tomorrow at noon, we've decided to settle our differences once and for all. A straight-up duel, the way men used to do it when men were men, women were women, violets were blue and that one other thing.

But, you see, I think my nefarious tub of nemesishood isn't playing with a full deck. A bit loopy in the head, you know? He's gotten it into his head that he can bring an additional friend to a two-man duel, that low-down fink, and furthermore, he thought he could do it without my finding out! So what I need you to do is head on down to the contested mining facilities over in Friggi and dispatch the friend he thought he'd be clever enough to bring, then grab his ID tags from the wreckage and show them to me as proof he's dead. We're gonna have a fair duel if it kills me.

The guy's name is Garp Soolim. Take him out for me, would ya?

localizedName.text: High Noon - Tipping the Scales (2 of 2)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Now that Xyxzorn's putrescent minions have been eliminated, it's time to see if we can't hedge our own bets a bit. What, did you think I was going to sit by and let that cheating bastard get a fair fight? Not a chance.

I have a few friends down at the station where we're going to have our duel. We're going to set up a little surprise for the old fella, but for them to work their magic they're going to need a spot of rocket fuel.

What, why are you looking at me that way? Trust me, there are perfectly good and honorable uses for rocket fuel within the context of a man-to-man duel. You think it's a coincidence that "fuel" and "duel" rhyme? Don't be naive, my friend.

Get the fuel to the Propel Dynamics factory at Ishisomo VII, and you'll have my eternal gratitude.

The next artifact on the list is Hraldar's sculpture. Hraldar was a Nefantar general which defected to the Minmatar cause during the rebellion. After his death a sculpure was made of him to honor his name. Originally it was placed within the Legendary Minmatar Stronghold, but after it was abandoned the sculpture was moved to the historical museum in Barkrik. A few years ago however, it was stolen by Maru raiders.

I have reliable information that the current owner of the sculpture is Bazeri Palen, one of the leaders of the Maru Rebels. He's an old-time criminal who pretends to be a 'freedom fighter', like most of those Maru scum. He flies a formidable battleship, and usually has a few of his goons around for protection. Taking him out will be hard, but I'm confident in you, {[character]player.name}.

I don't know where you will find him, but the last I heard he was orbiting one of the moons of Hjoramold. The Maru are extremely protective of their territory, so he might attack you when you find him. But don't worry about the legal implications of killing him, he's a wanted man within the Republic and therefore I doubt they will look harshly upon his murder.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Telligman's stone is an old symbol of Minmatar independence. Crad was the famous Amarrian architect who designed the Nefantar palace in Hjoramold, shortly before the Rebellion took place. When the Minmatar forces tore down the palace during the rebellion, they left a single stone intact which they called 'Telligman's stone'. It was later moved to the Bastion museum to be shown as one of the symbols of Minmatar victory in Ani over the occupation.

Find the Bastion museum and steal the stone. I don't care how you do it, just bring it to me intact and I will reward you well.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Great!  Now that I have what I came for, it's time to head back to the Empire.  But there's one final assignment I have in store for you, so don't go anywhere yet.

messages.mission.briefing.text: The last task I have for you, {[character]player.name}, is to transfer my artifacts to Sasta, which is located within Ammatar space.  The system is en route to my home world within the Empire, so I'll pick up the goods there.  I'm much more confident in your abilities to smuggle these items out of Minmatar space undetected than my own, and I certainly wouldn't want to be caught by the Republic authorities with these items in my cargo hold.  No telling what they'd do to me, especially considering I'm a citizen of the Amarr Empire.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: The last task I have for you, {[character]player.name}, is to transfer my artifacts to Sasta, which is located within Ammatar space. No telling what they'd do to me, especially considering I'm a citizen of the Amarr Empire.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I'll wait for you here in Hjoramold, you know where to find me.  I have some unfinished business here which I have to take care of.  My associate in Sasta will take care of the artifacts until I'm ready to make my own journey there.

localizedName.text: Attack of the Killer Drones - ST 58 (1 of 3)

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Combat missions are my bread and butter. What's the problem?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Well, it's rather complicated. But to keep it simple, I'll give you the short version. A few days ago, I completed my latest project, the ST 50 series. They were supposed to be ultra-intelligent fighter drones, specifically ordered by the Minmatar Fleet to serve in our armed forces. In all of the tests I performed on them, they seemed to be in fine condition, easily dispatching all the previous models in our combat simulation tests. However, shortly after they were released from our lab and sent into action, they went missing. The loss was an enormous blow to Boundless Creation, especially considering all the time, effort, and money we spent creating those things.

The sortie that they were on when they went missing was to attack a massive rogue drone hive within Barkrik. They were accompanied by over a dozen human pilots, who also haven't been seen since. I'm not sure exactly what happened there, but a rumor is spreading that they were overwhelmed and captured by the rogue drone mothership. I can't imagine such a thing happening, but...

Anyway, a few days later we heard of a terrible tragedy in Hjoramold. An entire settlement was destroyed by rampaging rogue drones. I didn't think much of it at the time, considering rogue drone attacks are pretty frequent in these parts, but later that day I turned on the evening news I heard something that chilled me to the bone. The recent rogue drone attacks were led by none other than one of my own ST drones! I couldn't believe my ears at first, but it was true. I don't know how, but the rogue drones have somehow managed to reconfigure the ST's AI chip and turn it into a rampaging monster! It must be stopped at all costs; its existence is a terrible blow to my career, and the more damage it causes, the more likely I am to lose my job. You must help me!

Unfortunately, the rogues seem to have deactivated the tracking devices I had installed into the STs. However, I have managed to triangulate the location of two of them, and the third has already been destroyed by local independent capsuleers. You'll find ST 58 at the bookmarked location that I'm about to upload into your NeoCom, floating around a deadspace pocket filled with asteroids. Destroy all drones you find at that location and bring back ST 58's memory chip so that I can study it and find out what went wrong.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: You call that a short version?! You almost put me to sleep with your rambling! I refuse!

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: You've done me and Boundless Creation a great service, {[character]player.name}, but I have one other drone to recover, so please stick around.

localizedName.text: Attack of the Killer Drones - ST 59 (2 of 3)

messages.mission.briefing.text: Model ST 59 has somehow ended up in Evati, many jumps from here. It was destroyed by militia forces in the system, and its remains transferred to the Republic Justice Department station there. I made a deal with them to allow me to access the memory chip to investigate the cause of the malfunction, but I couldn't find a convoy heading to Hjoramold in time. Could you fetch it for me ASAP? I have to return it in a couple of weeks, so the faster you get it here, the better.

I have to return it in a couple of weeks, so the faster you get it here, the better.

localizedName.text: Attack of the Killer Drones - ST 60 (3 of 3)

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You've been an enormous help, {[character]player.name}, and I can't thank you enough. Hopefully by disabling those drones, you will have saved me my job at Boundless Creation. Good luck in your future endeavors.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The last drone memory chip I need you to fetch is ST 60's. The '60 is my finest drone of the ST series, a prototype, and certainly a force to be reckoned with. I think you might have to find some friends to help you take it on ― yes, it's really that tough, if I do say so myself.

It's currently orbiting a rogue drone installation near Hjoramold XII Moon I, located deep within what we call "Glittermore," the xenon gas cloud of Hjoramold XII. It's a very hostile part of space, but a magnificent sight nonetheless and one frequented by tourists. Good luck finding those drones, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text: The asteroid belts here, as everywhere, are infested with pirates and murderers. I need you to bring me a few finger bones collected from pirates around the constellation. Yes, finger bones: I need nine for my divination to hold true.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Come close, child. I am blind and my cerebro-audial sensors are weak. Still, even so I can sense your inner strength and passion. They match my own. That is good. Very good.

The Ani constellation is a place in turmoil. I can see it as frantic swirl in my mind's eye. This place has become the playground of many great powers, some visible to the eye and some not. Lives are being taken and lives are being thrown away. Right and wrong hold little sway here; anger and hate are the driving forces. This flood of emotions pouring into this melting pot makes it hard for me to perceive the currents of the future. I need to undertake my most potent divinations to pierce this veil of uncertainty and proclaim the great prophecy I feel building within me.

I need your help, {[character]player.name}. That is your name, correct? {[character]player.name}, the asteroid belts here, as everywhere, are infested with pirates and murderers, curs all, worthless dogs who prey on fear and passivity. I need you to bring me a few finger bones collected from pirates around the constellation. Yes, finger bones: I need nine for my divination to hold true.

messages.mission.briefing.text: My incantation is complete and my prophecy freed. I have another favor to ask of you, {[character]player.name}. I have a friend not far from here who has access to a public network. If I can get the prophecy to him, he can spread it throughout the Republic as a virus. What I need you to do is smuggle the prophecy virus to my friend. I'm much too well-known a figure to Republic authorities to have a chance of doing this myself.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
My incantation is complete and my prophecy freed. Now I need to get it out to the people. But I'm not a popular man in the Republic. The tribal elders see me as a threat to their precious stability. Yet all I do is tell the truth as I see it. As I see it.

Lethargy has settled upon our government and the Amarrians are exploiting it to their own advantage. I have seen a dusty road filled with blood-covered slaves. Minmatar slaves. Yes, the Empire dreams of conquering us once again; already they have woven a web of deceit and treachery around our mighty Republic. The elders are being deceived and the public lulled. Only my prophecies can make them realize the peril we all are in. A peril that is all too real and all too close. The Empire is building its strength and its hunger is rising.

My words and my works have been banned from Republic space. But my message must be heard or all is lost. So I have another favor to ask of you, {[character]player.name}. I have a friend not far from here who has access to a public network. If I can get the prophecy to him, he can spread it throughout the Republic. Masking my prophecy as a virus is not something I relish, but it must be done. What I need you to do is smuggle the prophecy virus to my friend. I'm much too well-known a figure to Republic authorities to have a chance of doing this myself.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Please help these unfortunate souls by transporting them over to the Servant Sisters of EVE station in Lanngisi, where they can be properly cared for. Meanwhile, I will have my disciples locate this crazed Holder so he can be dealt with before he hurts anyone else.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
My head is still aching from my last divination. I don't think I will be ready for another one for some time now. These old bones of mine are getting tired; I must rest soon. But before I do, you must swear to me you'll take care of an ugly business that came to my attention just now.

It seems an Amarr Holder exiled from the Empire has taken up a residence here in Ani. This particular Holder is notorious for his disgusting depravities. He holds slaves like they were his pets, forcing them to participate in his cruel games. Fortunately, several of these poor slaves managed to escape the evil clutches of their master. They are now in my care, but are in need of more aid than I am capable of giving them.

Please help these unfortunate souls by transporting them over to the Servant Sisters of EVE station in Lanngisi, where they can be properly cared for. Meanwhile, I will have my disciples locate this crazed Holder so he can be dealt with before he hurts anyone else.

localizedName.text: Blind Seer - Tit for Tat (4 of 4)

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I thank you once again, {[character]player.name}. May Lady Fortünna shine upon you.

messages.mission.briefing.text: I managed to track down the depraved Amarr Holder of whom I spoke at our last meeting. He's in the Traun system, visiting a station controlled by some lackeys of the Angel Cartel. He has fitted out an old Bestower as a pleasure ship, so look for a Bestower docked at an Angel station. You should find it in the contested complex in the Traun system. I'm offering you a rare blueprint copy, to be given to you once you take care of this Amarrian.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
How good of you to visit me again, {[character]player.name}. I've been awaiting your return for some time now. I managed to track down the depraved Amarr Holder of whom I spoke at our last meeting. He's in the Traun system, visiting a station controlled by some lackeys of the Angel Cartel. I do not know what his business is there, and really I don't care. Whatever it is it will die with him. He has fitted out an old Bestower as a pleasure ship, so look for a Bestower docked at an Angel station. You should find it in the contested complex in the Traun system.

By the way, I was contacted by the Sisters in Lanngisi just before you arrived and they informed me that one of the slaves you brought them is a distant relative of mine. Even though my concern extends to all Minmatars, this makes the matter personal. As such, I'm offering you a rare blueprint copy, to be given to you once you take care of this Amarrian quickly and efficiently. Bring me his head when you're done. Then I can go and rest with my mind at peace.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Did you bring me that Tri-Vitoc I need? No? You're not the guy Tarkur sent out to me? Damn! Where is that guy? I'm starting to think he was waylaid by CONCORD on the way. Friggin' cops! I need that Tri-Vitoc!

Man, what am I gonna do now? Hey! Maybe you're willing to help. Could you scoot over to Eystur for me? My pal Tarkur works in the cargo hangar on a Security Service station there. Lousy job, excellent location. Gets him close to all kinds of good stuff. Got me hooked on that Tri-Vitoc awhile ago, brilliant stuff, highly recommend it... Oh yeah. Now, where was I?

Oh, yes, you. Go to Eystur, bring Tri-Vitoc from Turkur. Bring it to me. It sounds so simple a monkey could do it. So, stop this monkey business and get going! Har, har! Sometimes I kill myself... Mm, Vitoc. Yeah.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Good job on the Tri-Vitoc delivery. Ooh, yeah, I feel like a new man. Heck, with the potency of this stuff, I probably am! My DNA's probably all screwed up.

You're a pilot after my own heart, direct and brutal. So perhaps we can work together, what do you say? If you're interested in bringing a bit of mayhem to this uptight world, then follow my lead. I've been out hunting pirates in this constellation; there sure are a lot of them around here these days. Why do I hunt pirates, an inquiring pilot such as yourself might ask? Because they don't belong here, that's why. This is my home sweet home, and those pirates can go play their little bandit games somewhere else. This is my territory. Are you with me? I know you're with me ― if you weren't, you'd be dead.

No, that's just a little joke I make. Don't be alarmed. Heh. Man, this is some good Vitoc.

Uhm... oh, yeah, so some of the pirates around here, particularly those in the contested complexes, are sporting these new ID slices. I've become quite the avid collector of them, and I'm willing to reward you well if you bring me a few. The tags I'm looking for are dropped by tough cruiser pirates, so take care. Ah, what am I saying, it's those pirates that should take care. You're {[character]player.name} the menace! Har, har. I'm joking again, of course. You know I am.

Ah, what am I saying, it's those pirates that should take care. You're {[character]player.name} the menace! Har, har. I'm joking again, of course. You know I am.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Well done on that tag-collecting business. These Sniper ID slices now hold a place of honor in my collection. That blood splatter on one of them, man, that was pure genius! Makes it so deliciously eerie! I feel like we're really bonding here, uh... what´s your... oh, yeah, {[character]agentID.name}. No, wait, that´s me. Ehh, {[character]player.name}, right? This might be the beginning of something beautiful, I tell you.

I have such a good feeling about you I'm even willing to let you in on one of my many schemes: A while ago, I came into the possession of some forged transit documents from the Amarr Empire. I have a bit of skill in forgery myself, so I altered them a bit to make them look like imperial orders instructing the bearer to head to a certain location here in Ani for colonization purposes. These Amarrians are always looking to expand, so it's easy to bait a group of wannabee colonists into thinking they have in their hands official permission to settle here. As if the Empire had any say in who settles here and who not? Bah, the fools!

Needless to say, the location here in Ani is in the middle of nowhere; just some old rogue drone hive long since cleaned out. I've already taken out several settlers in the past myself, but with you and me getting on so well, I thought I'd give you a shot at it.

It's nasty business, I can tell you, killing innocent Amarr civilians in cold blood when they're only looking for a place to call home. But I know you have the stomach for it. After all, how innocent can they be, with the blood of my ancestors on their hands? Kill them all, and good riddance to them is what I say. Spit in their eye as they die, mother, father, child and all. Show me you got the guts and I'll reward you with a rare BPC.

Oh, one more thing. Bring the forged documents back to me. This little trap is too sweet not to spring a few more times before they get suspicious.

localizedName.text: Urban Management's Census - Civilian In Custody (1 of 3)

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I am in charge of Urban Management's annual census gathering operation here in Hjoramold. My team flies between settlements in every corner of the system and gathers information on the population count. Then we process this information and finally send it to our headquarters in Abudban along with our report.

Sounds like a pretty simple and straight forward job, eh? And in the more civilized areas of Republic space, it is. But out here you never know what can happen. Every year some disaster strikes, and this year is no exception.

Two of my team have gone missing in addition to one getting stranded in an asteroid belt on her way back, due to her ship breaking down. Needless to say, I need some help getting them back.

First I'd like you to go looking for Kardimo Palettan, one of the workers who went missing. He's my cousin twice removed, and we've known each other since we were kids. I would be terribly unhappy if something has happened to him.

He was on duty near Hjoramold X, collecting census data from some of the bio-dome settlements on the moons there, when he was beset by local thugs. We have a very strict policy here in Urban Management to stay well clear of all pirate infested areas, so we weren't expecting this. Seems one of the local gangs, calling themselves the 'Maru Rebels', thought Kardimo was trespassing on their territory and decided to punish him. I just hope he's still alive. I suggest you scour the area around Hjoramold X's moons, hopefully the Maru will have a base there somewhere. If you find him or any clues leading to him, then return to me for your reward.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Look for a 'Maru Prison Facility' near Hjoramold X's moons, and rescue Kardimo Palettan.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Seeing Kardimo alive again brings tears to my eyes.  You've done me a great service, {[character]player.name}, but there's still more to be done.  Two other members of my crew still need to be rescued before I can complete my report.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Yea, I'm lookin' for work.  What you got?

The other census worker who's having problems is currently stranded on Hjoramold XIII due to an unexpected rogue drone attack. Those drones seem to be randomly attacking all travelers going to and from the planet. The pilots are so scared Kyra, the census taker, can't even find a single one to transport her off XIII. I'd like you to eliminate this threat ASAP so that Kyra can finally get her ass back to base. Republic security forces are taking too damn long to get the job done.

The only thing I need you to do is destroy the Searcher Drone. That will render the drone squad unable to scan all areas around the planet and should allow travelers safe passage as long as they avoid the dust cloud the buggers have been hiding in.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Another job well done, {[character]player.name}.  You've certainly earned your keep.  And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I'm sorry to see that Yttora didn't make it out alive.  She was one of my favorite subordinates, always joyful and energetic.  She was also always available for the risky missions, and I guess her luck finally ran out.  A sad day indeed, {[character]player.name}, but at least now we know what happened to her.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The last issue I need you to deal with is our stranded census worker, Yttora Lyn. She was sent into the infamous 'Gas Storm' of Hjoramold, which is really a massive gas cloud that orbits Hjoramold's star. Her objective was to take census of the populace in an asteroid colony located deep inside that hostile territory, a pretty dangerous task considering various pirate groups tend to use the area as a hideout. Not to mention it's been infested with rogue drones for years.

The last transmission I received from her was a call for help. Her ship apparently broke down not far from the colony, and as a result she's stranded there for at least a week, when the next convoy arrives. I'd like you to get her out of there ASAP, {[character]player.name}, we can't just leave her there with the psychopaths inhabiting that colony for a week!

If you're careful, you will be able to avoid contact with the pirates. But I warn you, the acceleration gates in the Gas Storm are old and crude and have drifted quite far from the beacons originally placed next to them. Due to the lack of interest in the area, nothing has been done to rectify the situation. So I suggest you head out there on a pretty fast ship, if you want to stay sane that is heh heh.
