Good luck out there, soldier.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Awesome job, {[character]player.name}. I'm puzzled why there were no live guards at their headquarters, just drones and sentry guns, but at least their structures were destroyed. Now I just hope most of their personnel were located inside. Either way, you did what I asked you to and for that you deserve your reward.

Dismissed.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Welcome to the Nickel & Dime Store, {[character]player.name}. It is a humble little shop owned and operated by the Thukker tribe, catering to the needy souls in this beautiful constellation. Hm, something tells me you can be of some assistance to us ― perhaps you've worked for the Thukkers in the past?

Let's see if you've got what it takes to help our fledgling business grow. I have a small task for you: nothing complicated or risky, but it should let me gauge your talents. Deliver a few crates of goods to a nearby station for me. The rewards are modest, since this is such an easy task, but it's only the start.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Good work on your previous assignment. Despite it being a tedious one, you pulled it off without any qualms. Now for something a little more interesting.

You see, things have not been easy around here lately. The Caldari mega-corp Wiyrkomi is intent on tapping into the vast natural resources found in the constellation, much to the dismay of the many environmentalists here in the Federation. The struggle between the two sides draws unwanted attention to our little enterprise here and is making our operation difficult. Down the road, I might be tempted to have you help us with this unpleasant situation. But not just yet. First, we have to take care of another small problem that just came up.

The Serpentis drug lords are out in force here in Algintal, overseeing traffic between Federation and Republic space. We Thukkers are not into the drug scene, so we generally leave them alone. The same applies for them, for the most part. Live and let live, huh? Thing is, many of the Serpentis have grown too fond of their own goods and can get a little wild at times. One such incident occurred the other night when a gang of renegade Serpentis junkies stole some goods we were receiving from our associates in the Republic. The goods aren't all that valuable, but we must send a clear sign to the Serpentis that our goods are to be left alone.

I know that the fools who stole our goods are relaxing at the Skeleton Comet complex over in Deltole. If you're willing to go over there and teach them a lesson, a hard lesson ― a permanent lesson, get me? ― then I would be much obliged. And if you could return with some of the goods they stole, I'd be even happier.

localizedName.text: Concerned Citizens - Run, Boy, Run! (3 of 3)

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good job, {[character]player.name}. Now, take the business card I just gave you and go talk to Iliere Angetyn.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Oh, {[character]player.name}, you've come at an opportune moment. Things are progressing as I feared they would. The continuous struggle between Wiyrkomi and the activists have cast a spotlight on the constellation. While we here are the Nickel & Dime Store are running a perfectly legal business, our associates and clients like to operate in the dark. Already, I've lost several important clients, and some employees are getting restless. So much so that I'm having difficulties making my more demanding deliveries.

Unfortunately, I do not have the means or the knowledge to do much about the situation, but my business associate Iliere Angetyn is a most resourceful Gallentean, and I'm sure he's already contemplating how to put things right. But Angetyn doesn't deal with just anyone. Only those clearly in favor with the Trust Partners company get his attention. So I have a proposal for you. Run an errand for me that one of my just-departed couriers was supposed to, and I'll give you a Trust Partners Business Card. Show this to Angetyn and he's certain to offer you something lucrative.

The errand in question is a simple delivery over the border into the Republic. It has a very small chance of getting you in trouble with the customs, but I'm sure a resourceful pilot such as yourself can pick the right route to avoid any unwanted attention.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent! I'm already feeling more confident about this whole thing. I think I can count on you and Angetyn together to sort this mess out.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I know how to keep my mouth shut. What kind of work do you have?

messages.mission.briefing.text: I want you to head over to the Wiyrkomi surveillance outpost here in Augnais and take out their shuttle. Make sure you locate the surveillance recordings; confiscate them and bring them back to me.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Hm. Alright. You see, Algintal was such a nice place a few years back. The traffic through its systems and the many tourists meant we could operate with minimal risk. But now that has all changed with the arrival of the Wiyrkomi corporation and their lackeys, Roden Shipyards. What were once standard border-running operations now require much more time and effort to pull off.

What is worse, the Caldari think they own the place just because they exploited a loophole in the trade agreement between the State and the Federation. They're trying to muscle us out. I want to nip that bullshit in the bud and strike back at the Wiyrkomi. That's where you come in, {[character]player.name}.

The Wiyrkomi have installed a surveillance outpost here in Augnais. The problem is, I only found out about it a few days ago, after I'd just completed an important deal with a Republic contact of mine. If the Wiyrkomi listened in on the deal, they could compromise the Thukkers' position here in Algintal. I thought it was too late to do anything about it, but the security measures of the Wiyrkomi are working against them here. The surveillance outpost operates in total radio silence and only sends out its recordings in a shuttle once a week to the Wiyrkomi headquarters over in Fluekele. The shuttle will depart tomorrow, so there is still time to take care of this ... problem. I want you to head over to the surveillance outpost and take out that shuttle. Make sure you locate the surveillance recordings and confiscate them. Bring them back to me, and we're back on track.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Nice. Good work. But now something else has come up...

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: You got it, boss. On my way.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Absolutely. What do I need to know?

messages.mission.briefing.text: Head over to the Skeletal Comet in Deltole, locate the wrecked ship, and get the drugs out.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
It seems every time the Thukkers get themselves in trouble they come running to me to clean things up. I mean, I can't complain ― the Thukkers don't admit many foreigners into their ranks, so I'm in a privileged position, but still...

Anyway, as you might know, this constellation is full of activists fighting the Wiyrkomi and their plans to "spoil the natural beauty" to harvest resources. We've gotten into contact with some of the more belligerent activists, making them think we're here to support them, but of course we're just using them for our own benefit. We've provided them with some old ships and have even been providing full maintenance service for them. What they don't know is that we've used the opportunity when we service the ships to stuff their hidden cargo hatches full of contraband for them to ferry around for us. Heh. Pretty neat, eh? Yeah, well, it would be if these idiot FON guys would just shuttle peacefully around.

Thing is, one of them had to get into a fight with some Serpentis pirate over in Deltole and get blown to pieces. Of course the ship was full of drugs, and we need to clear that stuff up before anyone notices. Can you head over to the Skeletal Comet over in Deltole, locate the wrecked ship, and get the drugs out? I suspect they must be spoiled by now, what with the explosion and all, but we need to get them out anyway before the activists ― or worse, the authorities ― find them.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: That's what I like to hear. Git 'er done.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes, in fact. I'm feeling very confident in your abilities, so I'm setting up a big job for you. But before that, I need you to take care of a smaller matter for me. I have acquired certain items that cast Veko Tallaja, the operation supervisor for Wiyrkomi here in Algintal, in a rather negative light. I'm not going to use this stuff just now, but I need to store it somewhere safe.

I want you to head over to Fluekele and drop it off at the Pend Insurance station there. A friend of mine will then place it in a safe-deposit box there. I know it's a trivial thing I'm asking, but this is very sensitive material that absolutely can't get into the wrong hands ... and, besides, I need more time to prepare for your big mission.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Done, {[character]agentID.name}. Now what's this big job you mentioned?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Hey, as long as there's a decent, big job coming next, I'm willing.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Patience, my friend. I just need to arrange one more thing. Talk to me again in a minute.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Anything else come up for me?

messages.mission.briefing.text: I want you to head over to Fluekele and drop this container off at the Pend Insurance station, where a friend of mine will place it in a safe-deposit box there. I know it's a trivial thing I'm asking, but this is very sensitive material that absolutely can't get into the wrong hands ... and, besides, I need more time to prepare for your big mission.

localizedName.text: Business Associates - Kill the Competition (4 of 4)

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You kidding? I was born ready. Watchya got?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Mission accomplished. Those smugglers won't be bothering you again.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Some smugglers have built themselves a nice little hideout near here. We're not playing any games here, so killing them is the only item on the agenda. It was hell to track them down, so make sure you take them all out in one go so I don't have to repeat the process later.

If you pull this off with style, I'm sure some associates of mine would love for you to work a bit for them. When you bring me those dead smugglers' DNA, I'll give you some ship logs that my associates need to tamper with a bit to make them seem as innocent as a virgin's butt. Those logs should be ample proof to them that you're a trusted friend.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Algintal has always been a favored spot for smugglers. It's far enough out of the way so as not to attract too much attention from the authorities. Besides us at Trust Partners, the Serpentis are out here in force, as well as several independents. Usually we try to stay well clear of each other, but sometimes a group arrives that thinks it can muscle everyone else out. One such group has been making a nuisance of itself recently, and it's time to take them out. We've played Mr. Nice Guy until now, but no longer.

The smugglers in question have built themselves a nice little hideout near here. We're not playing any games here, so killing them is the only item on the agenda. It was hell to track them down, so make sure you take them all out in one go so I don't have to repeat the process later.

If you pull this off with style, I'm sure some associates of mine would love for you to work a bit for them. When you bring me those dead smugglers' DNA, I'll give you some ship logs that my associates need to tamper with a bit to make them seem as innocent as a virgin's butt. Those logs should be ample proof to them that you're a trusted friend.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: That's what I like to hear, {[character]player.name}. You've proven yourself to me, at least. Glad to have you onboard.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We try to keep our operation here at the Forgery under the radar, with a little bribery on the side to take care of over-zealous bureaucrats. Still, even if we're not exactly advertising our services we've established a rather formidable reputation in the underworld. We like to keep things as they are and sometimes we have to engage in some aggressive weed-killing to rid ourselves of unwanted baggage that can come back and haunt us later.

Which brings me to the job I want to offer you. A few months ago we entered an agreement with some local thugs here in Deltole. At the time we were anxious as to what the Serpentis druglords at the Skeleton Comet were up to, so we hired these guys to snoop around for us. Things went well for awhile, but now we have reason to believe the thugs have been playing both sides, offering their service to the Serpentis as well. That won't do, of course. We gave the thugs a ComLink encoder/decoder for secure communications. But what we didn't tell them was that the encoder also acts as a bug device. We only put it in their as a precaution, never intending to use it, but now we need to retrieve the encoder to confirm our believe that the thugs are two-faced bastards.

Get me that encoder so I can exact my punishment on them. I've already hatched a devious plan, if I say so myself, for framing those thugs and setting them up for the Serpentis to chew on. But first I need that encoder. The thugs have entrenched themselves deep inside the Skeleton Comet complex, acting as any other small time smuggling cartel. The encoder should be located in their Relay Station, so target that.

localizedName.text: The Forgery - Mark it for Market (2 of 5)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I'm glad you came along, {[character]player.name}. As you probably already know the arrival of the Wiyrkomi corporation in the constellation has stirred things up a bit. Tourism is way down and the authorities are unfairly blaming us smugglers. It's getting harder and harder to conduct any decent smuggle run and we have to be twice as careful. Not that it harms us here at the Forgery much, if anything it only makes our services even more sought after.

A Minmatar associate of mine needs to get a large quantity of high quality X-Instinct into Gallente space, but he's not willing to risk the Federation customs at times like these. That's were we come into the picture. I need a small favor from you. I ordered a large quantity of dolls, but they're sitting in a TranStellar Shipping warehouse over in Adiere. Are you willing to fetch them for me? It's a trivial assignment, I know, but I'm positively swamped at the moment, as you can well understand.

messages.mission.briefing.text: I'm having the dolls 'enhanced' as we speak. Your next assignment is much more tricky. Are you willing to take the drug-filled dolls deep into Gallente space? The risk is less than it sounds, as only very thorough scan of your vessel will reveal what hides inside the innocent looking dolls. But occasionally it does happen and then you'd be in deep trouble. I'd understand if you back down now, but it would be a real shame after having accomplished so much for us. But as it's your ass on the line, I won't pressure you any further. The choice is yours.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You've come through for me big time in the past, {[character]player.name}. So I have an important task for you now. First, I'll let you in on a little secret. You've probably already encountered some of the activists here in Algintal, fighting to get Wiyrkomi out. Well, we Thukkers are in the same boat. We also want Wiyrkomi out. Not because we care for the environment, but because Wiyrkomi's presence here is hitting our business hard. But the problem is we can't draw attention to ourselves. If Wiyrkomi or the Federation start perceiving the Thukker tribe as a real threat in the constellation they will come down on our heads real hard. And we don't want that to happen, now do we?

So we've been trying to manipulate things as much as we can behind the scenes. By discreetly supporting the more militant elements of FON we hope the activists can be of enough nuisance to the Wiyrkomi that the Caldari will flee with their tail between their legs. We've used every method we can come up with for this, including stirring some of the Serpentis druglords into action.

A few weeks ago a powerful druglord associated with the Angel Cartel, known as Don Rico, agreed to help out. At the time we didn't think that FON would amount to much, so we invested pretty heavily in getting Don Rico involved. The results were immediate and at first his diligence thrilled us. But recently it has started to get out of hand, with Don Rico getting ever more outrageous fighting Wiyrkomi and their cronies. Our sources close to the druglord tell us that Don Rico has grown much too fond of his own product and is completely out of control.

We need to restrain Don Rico before his actions jeopardize the whole operation. I know that the Federation Navy and CONCORD are starting to take notice and the last thing we need is for him to fall into their hands. He knows too much. So we need to take him out quickly. And you're just the pilot for the job. Unfortunately, I don't know the exact whereabouts of Don Rico. He likes to cruise around in his pleasure yacht and he could be lurking anywhere in the constellation. We need to flush him out and I know just the thing to stir him into showing his face. He owns a drug factory not far from here and I want you to raid it. Kill a few of his henchmen. Don Rico's greatest weakness is his vanity and vengefulness. A direct attack on his possessions will certainly make him come screaming in revenge. And that's our chance to take him out. But first, the raid. All Don Rico's henchmen have a smuggler signet. Collect a few of these signets and bring them to me. Let's see what happens then.

localizedName.text: The Forgery - Tie the Knot (5 of 5)

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Very well done, {[character]player.name}! I have an urgent message for you to deliver to Drusk Amakkit over in Parchanier. He will explain matters to you. Please hurry!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Just as I predicted the raid on the drug factory got just the results we wanted. Don Rico is screaming fury on all the underworld channels trying to find the culprit. Don't worry, we'll keep you identity hidden long enough for you take him out for good. It's a dangerous assignment, but if you don't do it you'll have Don Rico's revenge hanging over your head for the rest of your life. Sorry to put you in this position, but look at it from my point of view, it was a win-win situation. Anyway, you're getting handsomely rewarded for all of this, so don't sulk too much.

When you accept this mission I'll give you the coordinates to the place where Don Rico is hiding out at the moment. Like all druglords he's even more paranoid than I am, so rest assured he's got artillery and plenty of it. Perhaps bringing a few friends along would be a good idea.

Just as I predicted the raid on the drug factory got just the results we wanted. Don Rico is screaming fury on all the underworld channels trying to find the culprit. Don't worry, we'll keep you identity hidden long enough for you take him out for good. localizedName.text: Power to the People - Seed (1 of 3)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You probably know already that we've been subtly manipulating FON and Serpentis into working together against Wiyrkomi. While this is not without risk we feel it's the best chance of driving the Caldari megalomaniacs out of Algintal so we can get back to some serious smuggling.

But things are now rapidly progressing out of control and we have to get more directly involved to get things under control again. There's this Serpentis agent by the name of Elere Febre that we linked up with a FON contact. Febre is the main liaison between the two sides and has worked wonders in the short time she's been involved. But according to this message you brought me her cover is blown. Wiyrkomi is on to her and is probably planning to take her out as we speak. Or worse, take her into custody and interrogate her. We cannot let that happen as she could then reveal the Thukkers involvement.

Time is of the essence here, so the first thing we need to do is distract the Wiyrkomi until we come up with a real plan. I don't have time to assemble squad of my own so some improvisation is the order of the day. You're the only one here, so I guess I must rely on you. We must instigate a fake attack on the Wiyrkomi by FON. To do that we need an authentic FON banner. I know that FON has an operation station inside the Skeletal Comet complex over in Deltole. It's overlooking the huge rogue drone hive in there. What do you say about raiding the place and steal me a FON banner? Return with it here and we're half way home in throwing Wiyrkomi off the scent.

localizedName.text: Power to the People - Toil (2 of 3)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I must congratulate you on being so quick in bringing me the banner. I wasn't feeling all that optimistic about our chances in thwarting Wiyrkomi as they were already on the move, but now things look different. I've already put in motion a fake sabotage attack on one of the Wiyrkomi stations in the system. All my agents there need is the banner to leave behind after the raid.

The Caldari are a suspicious lot, so any member of the Thukkers entering one of their stations is bound to attract attention. But you're presence there will not. To complete your recent success in getting the banner all you need to do now is getting the banner into the Wiyrkomi station and we'll take care of the rest.

localizedName.text: Power to the People - Reap (3 of 3)

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent job, {[character]player.name}. You did well, especially as it seems like the guy tried to ambush you. Considering the fact I sent you there to kill him, who can blame him? But good job, nevertheless. We can now breath easier knowing that all loose ends have been tied up. Wiyrkomi will get nowhere with their enquiry.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The sabotage attack on the Wiyrkomi station in Jolia was only a limited success, but it was enough to divert their attention long enough for Elere Febre to cover her tracks. She's abandoned her habitation module and gone into hiding for the time being. Wiyrkomi is bound to raid her place soon, but she was careful in leaving no traces of her own DNA there, though she left a fake one that hopefully will have them running in circles.

But there is still one loose end we need to tie up. Febre's contact within the FON is making a nuisance of himself and before he does something rash we must take him out. Before Febre went into hiding she set up a meeting with the guy to discuss the future. She gave me the coordinates for that meeting and I want you to go over there and kill the guy. Just remember, even if he's a pansy activists doesn't mean he's a walkover and he may very well have some backup with him. So take care. And perhaps take some backup with you. The situation is intense and you never know what might be lying ahead.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm up for it.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Great to hear that. Now the first task I have for you is pretty dangerous. We were expecting a large group of tourists here from Du Annes today but unfortunately their cruiser's warp-drive broke down in Deltole. On top of that they stumbled into a deadspace pocket filled with rogue drones. The last we heard of them was their distress signal indicating they were under attack. I can only hope that they managed to escape, but at this time it's impossible to tell.

I would like you to fly into the deadspace pocket where they were last seen and search for them. Destroy every rogue drone ship that you find. If they are still alive they might need some help repairing their warp-drive, if not then they at least would need help fighting off the drones.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: You've done us a great favor, {[character]player.name}.  The captain of the pleasure cruiser managed to contact us shortly after you finished your objective, and informed us that they were safe and on their way here.  Their deaths would have been terrible publicity for the Information Center ...

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Before I even contemplate working with you, I must be certain you are a true friend of the Trust Partners. For me to be sure, you need to give me a Trust Partners Business Card. You can get one by doing well for other agents of our firm. Try talking to some in the vicinity and get back to me once you have an appropriate business card.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: The door's over there.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I will return with a Trust Partners Business Card.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Yeah, I'll get right on it, loser.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Until then. So, bye.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm not sure what you mean. How can I prove that?

messages.mission.briefing.text: Try talking to some in the vicinity and get back to me once you have a Trust Partners Business Card.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Very good, I can see you are to be trusted with sensitive Thukker matters. I think we can begin to do business.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The next mission in line is rather simple. A Federal Intelligence officer is scheduled to inspect our outpost this week. He was supposed to arrive later today but his ship was delayed. The Federal Intelligence Office demanded that we provide him with a quick transport so that he is able to complete his assignment on time. My take on this entire situation is that they did this on purpose just to see how far we're willing to go to please Federation authorities.

Now, considering that you completed your last assignment with flying colors I assume this will be a piece of cake for someone of your caliber. Just pick up the FIO officer at {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} and get him back here as quickly as possible.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Nicely done.  But don't leave yet, there's one more task I have in store for you.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: You have some ship logs, eh? Could you hand them over, please?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: No sweat, just come and talk to me when you have the right documents for me.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Don't worry, you can trust me. I have with me ship logs from another agent of the Trust Partners.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sorry, I don't have any documents for you.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Ok, let's see those documents you have, then.

messages.mission.briefing.text: You have some ship logs, eh? Could you hand them over, please?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Ah, they're from Angetyn. Excellent! Yes, I can doctor them for him. Not that I haven't done so many times in the past, mind you. But what to do with you? Angetyn only sends me pilots he thinks highly of, so let's see if you're as talented as he thinks.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: I have no time to deal with just anyone. Do you have some business with me? I'm waiting for an urgent message from an agent friend of mine. If you don't have the message then you can be of no help to me. So don't bother trying to talk to me any further unless you have that message with you.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I hope to see you later when you have something of interest for me.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I have an urgent message from Krester Rupptofs to you. He told me you would tell me what the big hurry is.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I do not have any message for you, sorry. I will come back later when I have one.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: A message from Krester? I was expecting as much. Here, let's see what it says.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Give Drusk the message from Krester Rupptofs.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Ah! This is urgent indeed! It seems the Wiyrkomi bastards are more clever than I gave them credit for.
You've done all I've asked you to, with style.  I suggest you take a look at the Wiyrkomi Survey Station in Colelie or the Command Center in Fluekele if you're in need of some more work.  Good luck!

messages.mission.briefing.text: Now that you've finished the most pressing tasks I have, it's time to send my report to Miloise Roden in the Roden Shipyard headquarters.  It contains some pretty sensitive information, so I want it kept safe and secure until it's in the hangar of {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  Don't mess this up!

Dismissed.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Tell me what kind of business we're talking about and I'll think about it.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Ok, I'm here on official business from {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}. I was sent here to inspect the Central Command station of Wiyrkomi in Algintal, and as a side project keep an eye out on Roden Shipyards, who've been Wiyrkomi's primary allies in Federation space.

Now my first objective is to make sure there isn't any illegal trade going on here. I haven't been able to discover any contraband during my stay here, but I'd like to test something before I fill my first report. I'd like to see how well prepared the Temko mercenaries guarding this installation are concerning illegal goods. So I want somebody inconspicuous to try to infiltrate the compound with drugs inside of his cargo hold. You look like just the person for that assignment.

You'll find the drugs on {[location]objectiveLocationID.name}, simply grab them and bring them to me. Federation customs officials won't touch you, they know it's my crash. Temko don't however, hence the test. If you get attacked by Temko, then flee and come back later, I'll explain everything to them once the test is complete.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: So the guards didn't lift a finger to stop you?  Intriguing.  I'll have to mention this in my report!  But don't go far, I have some more work for you.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
For your second assignment I'd like you to investigate a Wiyrkomi storage facility in Jolia. I stumbled upon some documents revealing it's location while inside the Central Command control tower. They were a bit startled when I informed them of what I had discovered, so I'm thinking something fishy might be afloat there.

I will add a bookmark to the mission details in your Opportunities interface which sends you to a deadspace pocket. Inside you'll find this storage facility. Take a look inside, and tell me what you find.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: So they replaced the sign on the acceleration gate leading to the storage facility with one leading to a drone hive?  This will go straight into my report.  I'll also take a look at this data chip you found in the storage facility itself, but I'm sure there's nothing of interest inside it.  If they knew you were coming and managed to replace the sign on the acceleration gates, they probably had enough time to empty the storage containers as well.  But good work anyway.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: First of all, do you have something for me...? If you know what I'm talking about, then hand it over, please. If you don't, then I'm sorry, but I don't have anything for you.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: There you go.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Yeah, I have it here.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Bring the top-secret information into Preaux Gallot's possession.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm sorry, I have no idea what you're talking about.  Ta.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm sorry, I must have misunderstood.  I don't have what you're looking for.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Very well, then, let's see it.

messages.mission.briefing.text: First of all, do you have something for me...? If you know what I'm talking about, then hand it over, please. If you don't, then I'm sorry, but I don't have anything for you.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Excellent, thank you. I'm going to take a look at this; get back to me in a minute or two.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
First, a proper introduction. I'm Preaux Gallot, one of FON's chief coordinators in this area. As you may know, the Wiyrkomi corporation is trying to move into this area, corrupting the vast tracts of natural beauty found here with their horrible industry. Moreover, the piece of evidence you just brought me seems to indicate there are things at play here far worse than we originally suspected.

It appears the Wiyrkomi corporation has been hiring mercenaries to stage attacks on their own outposts in the area, attacks which they then frame us for in order to lessen our stature in the public eye. We need to put a stop to this as soon as possible. If we lose our lobbyist support, the Federation is likely to succumb to the deals being proffered by the corrupt Caldari business machine, and this entire area will be turned into just another locale for these corporate bigwigs to ravage.

An operative of ours, Suho Tatanal, has just returned from a protest on Parchanier II. He's a canny investigator with an eye for details; I want you to bring him the aggregated evidence we've gathered on the case so far, then report back to me. I'll have another assignment for you very soon.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I have the decoder.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
It's now time to turn our eyes towards Roden Shipyards. They have always been a shady corporation, and their alliance with Wiyrkomi certainly raised a few eyebrows. I was specifically told to find out exactly what part they play in all of this.

Yesterday I stumbled upon something that may be of vital importance to my investigation. My ship's sensors picked up an encoded transmission from a Roden Shipyards outpost located in Fluekele. I haven't been able to make much of it yet, but with the proper data decoder I will be able to tell what the contents of this transmission are. So my assignment to you is to find such a decoder and bring it to me. My suggestion is to scour the asteroid belts of Jolia, there is a Serpentis agent there called Pourpas Aunten who is renowned for decoding CONCORD and Federation Navy signals. If there's anyone in the galaxy which has the decoder I need, it's him.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Nice job.  I hope you gave Pourpas Aunten my regards, heh heh.  Now just give me a moment to analyze the transmission ...

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I've managed to decode the transmission but I can't make much of it. The interesting part though is that it originates from Maqeri Camcen's ship within the Contested Gallente Roden Shipyard Outpost. I checked my database and Maqeri is in fact rumored to be part of the Angel Cartel. What the Cartel would be doing in a Roden Shipyard Outpost in Fluekele is beyond me, unless there are Serpentis there. My best guess is that there are Serpentis operating inside the same deadspace are as Roden Shipyard, and this Maqeri is some sort of envoy from the Cartel.

Anyway I must get to the bottom of this. Meet with this Maqeri fellow and see if you can convince him to have a chat with me in person. If he's hostile and refuses to speak with you then you have my full authority to eliminate him. If you choose the gun rather than your wit, then at least bring evidence of his demise to me.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Well, it's unfortunate that he had to be killed.  But these things happen ...

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Congratulations on a job well done.  I have no more tasks for you, so I suggest talking to someone else if you're still in need of work.  Just stay away from those Wiyrkomi agents, I think they're up to no good ...

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Now that I've finished my report, I'd like you to transport it to my boss on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. The information inside is confidential, so please do not even think about reading the document.

Once the report is safely in the hands of my superiors, then you will have your reward. Good luck.

{[character]player.name}!  Please help me.  My friend, Isone Flosin, has gone missing.  We were just cruising around on our shuttles within the inner areas of this complex when we were attacked by rogue drones!  I managed to escape, but in my haste I didn't notice that Isone had stopped following me.  I need to know what happened to her, and my ship is in no shape to venture back in there.  Please, you have to help me.  Find Isone and bring her back!

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Find Isone Flosin inside the Contested Gallente Roden Shipyard Outpost, dead or alive, and bring her back to Nilla Elermare.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Please hurry, I'm certain she's in grave danger!

messages.mission.briefing.text: {[character]player.name}!  Please help me.  My friend, Isone Flosin, has gone missing. I managed to escape, but in my haste I didn't notice that Isone had stopped following me.  I need to know what happened to her, and my ship is in no shape to venture back in there.  Please, you have to help me.  Find Isone and bring her back!

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
How horrible! I never thought something like this could happen here. I don't know how I will be able to face her parents, they told us never to venture any further into the complex than the first area but we just couldn't resist. I'm so ashamed ...

Could you at least talk to Isone's father, in the Central Administration complex in Fluekele. Tell him I sent you, Isone's DNA will prove that. Please tell him the whole story, I'm just too traumatized at the moment to meet him myself. Thank you.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll look for her.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: As a matter of fact, I found her.  I am sorry to give you these sad tidings but ...

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Have you seen my daughter, Isone Flosin, by any chance? She went missing some time ago while inside the Roden Shipyard Outpost in Fluekele. If you find her, tell her I'm very displeased and she should come see me immediately.

I heard Nilla Elermare was asking about Isone, too. You may want to start by talking to her.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Arg! I can't believe those two! I told them never to venture deep into the Roden Shipyard outpost. How could they betray me like this! Please, wait a moment for me to gather my senses ...

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll find the person who killed your daughter, you can count on me.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: So, would you like to talk or do you need more time alone?

messages.mission.briefing.text: Isone must be avenged.  The Serpentis must be responsible for her death.  We've catered to their needs for far too long.  I couldn't believe my ears when they told me we were supposed to treat the Serpentis living in the outpost as comrades!  But enough of this rambling, back to the mission at hand.  I want you to infiltrate the Corelum Drughouse again and look for clues which might lead to whoever is behind her death.  I know of one person who might know, he serves as a guard at the Serpentis storage facility inside that deadspace area.  His name is Jark something.  Good luck.

I want you to infiltrate the Corelum Drughouse again and look for clues which might lead to whoever is behind her death.  I know of one person who might know, he serves as a guard at the Serpentis storage facility inside that deadspace area.  His name is Jark something.  Good luck.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: You brought back Jark himself?  Well, hopefully he will be able to reveal who's behind the tragedy when I interrogate him.  Stay tuned, as soon as he talks I might have another job for you.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
While I interrogate the prisoner, I would like you to bring Isone's things to her mother on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} as well as a note from me describing the situation. I am simply too busy to make the trip myself anytime soon, and I know she will manage to find some comfort in receiving Isone's things as a memento of her short life.

Everything you need to transport is in these sealed containers. Take care not to lose any, they might not be very valuable on the market but to me and my wife they are priceless.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Thank you, {[character]player.name}.  But there is just one more thing I need you to do before I let you go ...

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Serpentis science lab has been destroyed.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I've managed to extract the information I needed out of poor Jark. It seems that my Isone was accidentally killed by 'rogue' drone ships guarding the Serpentis drug storage area. Now I cannot really blame a computer for her death, but I can blame it's creators. In fact these drones are not 'rogue' at all, they are just programmed to act like them. An ingenious gallente scientist working for the Serpentis actually managed to reprogram these rogue drones to serve Salvador Sarpati and his wild schemes. The Federation Navy also tends to ignore areas infested with rogue drones, which is beneficial to the Serpentis.

Fortunately Jark knew of a Serpentis science lab in Colelie which is behind all of the drones in the Roden Shipyard complex. I want this science lab destroyed. Whoever resides in there is undoubtedly responsible for Isone's death, and must pay the ultimate price.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent news.  Although I do not feel better.  Killing those Serpentis will not bring my Isone back, nothing will.  Even if I have her cloned it will not be the same ...  Now leave me, I would like to be alone for a while.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Ok first of all I'll need a large batch of dense veldspar, around 14 portions should do, with each portion size being 333 units. You will probably find veldspar in one of the asteroid fields in Colelie, if not then try a neighboring system. If you're fast, I'll even get a bonus and of course I'll split it with you.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: I was sent here by {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} to help gather ore for Wiyrkomi's construction workers in the Survey Station. They're hoarding up minerals and ore for the eventual construction of the power plant in Azure Canyon. The only problem is I'm not much of a combat pilot and I didn't expect there to be such an abundance of pirates festering the asteroid belts in Colelie. So I was thinking, maybe you could help me out a little? I'll split the earnings I would have received for doing the same job with you. What do you say, {[character]player.name}?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Your second job is to get me 4 portions of Omber, or 2000 units to be exact. You might find it a bit difficult to find that type or ore around these parts, but you're in luck. I know of a great spot to mine some. You see I was in Fluekele a few days ago scouting for some ore, this is before I decided the job was too dangerous for me, and I managed to stumble upon a small cluttering of asteroids in the middle of nowhere. And lo and behold, there was an asteroid brimming with minerals, which on closer inspection was Omber! Unfortunately as soon as I had discovered this magnificent find, a group of Serpentis who had been following me attacked. I believe they were being led by that scoundrel Ansedon Blat, I could be wrong though. I met him while I was at the Roden Shipyards Outpost in Fluekele, and he must have decided to follow me when I left on my expedition. That backstabber and his goons must pay.

On second thought, I'm not satisfied with just getting the omber. You'll have to kill those Serpentis bastards too, if you find them. Return to me with the omber when you're done.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Well that's about it, I believe I've fulfilled my contract by turning in this last batch of ore.  There's just the trip back to my boss left.  I'd rather not make that run myself, just in case the Serpentis think I was responsible for killing their guys and decide to get some revenge.  I'm perfectly safe in the Survey Station ... so if you wouldn't mind I'd like you to make the run for me.  If you do, just wait a sec and let me grab my report.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Ok, my boss is located in our warehouse in Ane.  Just drop this report at his desk and he'll wire the payment to my account.  I'll give you something in return for your efforts as well.  Just some items that I think you might find useful, and frankly I have no need of.  Take it or leave it.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Ok, my boss is located in our warehouse in Ane.  Just drop this report at his desk and he'll wire the payment to my account.  I'll give you something in return for your efforts as well.  Just some items that I think you might find useful, and frankly I have no need of.  Take it or leave it.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: FON?  That some kind of fertilizer company?  Seriously, I'm just here for some work ...

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I didn't tell you to kill him!  I'm ready to die for my beliefs, but I won't take part in cold blooded murder!  I guess I owe you your reward, but this is the last time I'll ever do business with you, {[character]player.name}.  You're a bad, bad man.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You don't know what FON stands for?! Friends of Nature of course! We ... errr they stand for everything that's good about the Federation. Originating from a group battling to save rare animal species from extinction, it has grown somewhat after space travel became more common. Now it fights for the preservation of the natural phenomena which decorate our night sky.

Now you said you were looking for some work. As a matter of fact there is something that you could do for me which would really make my day. Temko are evil corporate peons who care nothing for our heritage, the Azure Canyon. They work for a no-good money-grubbing Caldari corporation which intends to destroy our natural reserves for its own gain. It so happens that one of Temko's commanders, Maschteri Markan, had the audacity to try and blackmail us when we sabotaged one of Wiyrkomi's construction sites, where they were building a survey station. He recorded the event and threatened to release it to The Scope and the Federation authorities if we wouldn't give in to his demands.

Find these records and bring them to me, or somehow convince him to hand them over himself, and I will reward you generously.

I suggest you refrain from accepting this mission if you have no idea how hard finding Maschteri is. Otherwise you might be in for a rude awakening

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Okay, Suho's gears have started turning. The evidence you brought him helped greatly. His investigation will be a tremendous boon in our struggle against the corporate monster. We'll have to wait a while to see what he comes up with. I'm not worried about him, though; he works magic when he gets going.

While we wait, {[character]player.name}, I have another job for you. Our organization is staging a massive protest tomorrow in the Wiyrkomi Corporation Factory in Jolia, but there seems to have been a slight miscommunication between some of our activists. If you could hop over to the Pend Insurance Investment Bank in Augnais and bring a few bags of fedo blood over to the Wiyrkomi station in Jolia, the Friends of Nature would be much obliged.

You've proven yourself a trustworthy operative, {[character]player.name}, so I'm going to give you an assignment slightly more clandestine than the ones you've gotten from me so far. Technically speaking, we're going to be breaking the law here, but I trust you realize we're doing what we're doing for a higher cause. Okay, that said, here goes.

We just received word from our man on the inside that Wiyrkomi have just ordered 15 high-powered drills for their prospecting operations on Fluekele V, a planet home to many unique, highly endangered varieties of flora and fauna. The drills are currently sitting at the Wiyrkomi factory in Fluekele, awaiting transport to the site where they're intended to be used.

Our operatives at Fluekele have managed, through their connections with sympathetic station personnel, to pilfer these tools, but we can't keep them hidden for long. We need someone to get the drills safely out to our people in the Poteque station in Augnais. Head out there and show me how devoted to our cause you truly are.

Something urgent just landed on my desk. One of our industrial ships, carrying a load of soil intended for our reservations on Deltole, was shot down yesterday with no survivors. We need to get some soil over there soon, or a large part of our efforts in the area will be wasted.

Looks like Wiyrkomi are using our alleged aggression against them as an excuse to gun down innocent people whose aims they don't agree with. Can't say I'm surprised, frankly, although I wouldn't have thought they'd go this far.

Bring 200 units of soil to me, and you will have done us a great service.

Suho has made a lot of headway in his investigation, and the results are disturbing as all hell. What I'm about to tell you is for your ears only. I want to make that absolutely clear.

It appears the attacks we've been hearing about against Wiyrkomi assets are not being staged by Wiyrkomi themselves, as we originally suspected. The most recent threads of Suho's investigation are, in fact, pointing squarely toward members of our own organization. I regret to say this, but it appears we have a vigilante rogue in our midst, someone who obviously has no conception of the harm he could be doing to our cause.

Furthermore, there's compelling evidence to the effect that this party, whoever he or she is, have been in contact with the Serpentis smugglers operating in this area, conspiring to strike against Wiyrkomi assets, murdering people in order to further our cause. Makes me feel dirty just thinking about it.

This weed in our garden needs to be rooted out, but first we need to learn its identity. The information is being held by Suho at his office in Parchanier. Needless to say, it's far too sensitive to be sent over normal channels, so I need someone I can trust to head out there and bring it back to me. That means you. We need to straighten this situation out, post-haste.

And remember, not a peep about this to anyone.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Hmm. Pretty much who I suspected. Damn it.

Okay, here's what I need you to do. Take this letter and give it to Ystvia Lamuette over at the Ebony Tower in Barmalie. She's one of our most respected operatives, and a great servant of the cause. When she gets the information, she'll set the right wheels in motion. And I'm sure she'll have plenty of use for a skilled pilot such as yourself.

Thank you again for what you've done for us. Good luck, and fly safe.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Do you have something for me? A letter, perhaps?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Yep. Right here.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Give Preaux Gallot's letter to Ystvia Lamuette.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Huh? Letter? Sorry lady, no idea.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm sorry, I must have misunderstood.  I don't have this letter you speak of.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Do you have something for me?  A letter, perhaps?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thank you very much.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Nice to meet you. My name is Ystvia Lamuette, and I'm one of the chief coordinators of FON's activities in this constellation. Preaux tells me great things about you; apparently you can be of great help in our struggle.

I'd like to get a feel for you myself, nonetheless. Show me how fast you can be. There's a rare specimen of plant, a Colelian spider spruce, sitting in the Core Complexion Warehouse at Deltole. Bring it back to me within 15 minutes and I'll reward you handsomely. Then we can talk about what needs to be done for our organization.

We need to move fast. The situation is evolving in unexpected ways. No no, don't sit down. I'll explain this as fast as I can.

While you were out on your last assignment, Ekire himself was mortally wounded in an assassination attempt by unknown assailants. We suspect Wiyrkomi, of course - they have the most to gain from his death, both politically and pragmatically speaking. Likewise, if he dies we stand to take a massive political blow.

Ekire is currently at the Egonics Inc. Development Studio at Parchanier V, bleeding severely and fading fast. Due to a rare blood condition he contracted in an Umokkan jungle while serving as a Legion marine a decade back, transfusion via normal means would kill him. For the procedure to be at all possible he needs an aortal purifier, a seldom-used piece of medical equipment which they don't have at that particular station's med bay.

I need you to head out to Auderne immediately, to the Poteque Pharmaceuticals Biotech Production plant there, and pick up what may be the only aortal purifier available in this whole damn constellation, then bring it out to the doctors in Parchanier. His life - and our success in our campaign here - may very well depend on your speed in this matter.

Go! Fly swiftly.

Alarus Ekire is safe and sound, thanks to you. We've uncovered solid evidence of what he's been up to in the sector, and we're making arrangements to have him delivered to the proper authorities safe and sound.

There's only one loose end that needs tying up, after which we can go back to business as usual, sticking it to the man. You see, I have this large shipment of wheat here that desperately needs to get dumped in the cogs of the Wiyrkomi station in Fluekele… *grins wickedly*

How about it, friend?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: The Friends of Nature extend their thanks to you for your help in this whole situation.  You've been a tremendous asset to our organization.  Thanks to you, we'll be able to continue our struggle to help the natural wonders of Algintal remain just that.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Nice work on the spider spruce.

So here's the situation, then. There's a guy named Alarus Ekire. He's the most militant person within our ranks - a real piece of work. Most of us have disagreed with his methods in the past, but he has an authoritative air about him which rouses admiration in the weak. For this reason he's never short of followers, and has managed to maintain his position within FON.

It has now been brought to our attention, due in no small part to your diligent work, that Ekire is the weed in our garden, the one that's been causing all this trouble in the past few weeks. We have to get rid of him, but we can't kill him. If the Wiyrkomi spin doctors have the opportunity to make him into a figurehead, we're finished. So we need to try and smoke him out, lure him into revealing himself.

We need to lay the groundwork first, though, and try to undo some of the damage he's caused. First off, we need to send the clear-cut message that FON do not wish to cast their lot with known cutthroats and murderers. To this end, we need to put our own propaganda machine to work.

There is a Serpentis outpost in one of the outlying systems. According to our intel, no detachments are stationed there at present. I want you to head out there, destroy the outpost, neutralize any opposition you may find, and report back to me. One of our other operatives will shadow you to the area and record the attack, so we can spin this to our advantage and hopefully countermand any bad publicity.

Go to it. Good luck.

The photographer who recorded your strike has given his footage to the post-production people. We should see something from them soon.

We've decided there's no choice but to take the Ekire matter into our own hands. According to our intelligence, he has something like four hundred men under his command, conducting his terrorist operations. Some of them are our own FON activists, others are mercenaries - Navy rejects, working for the highest bidder.

The Deltole system is a key tactical location; many of Ekire's mercs are stationed at an outpost there, and we have solid reports that they're preparing to stage some sort of attack on the Wiyrkomi factory there. This must not be allowed to happen.

We need you to conduct a pre-emptive strike on the outpost, eliminating any personnel you find in the vicinity. As you're not flying under our flag, there should be nothing linking you to the FON, and indeed there can't be - we would never survive the political backlash. Please know that we don't undertake the killing of people lightly. It's our hope that this is the greatly lesser of two evils.

Report back to me when the deed is done. I'll be here.

Well, well, what have we here? An eager puppy pilot all raring to go? Asking every stranger to be his friend. Tut, tut, did your mother never tell you not to talk to strangers, {[character]player.name}? But now that you're here, what to do with you? Ah, well, maybe you're not as green behind the ears as you seem. Might be I have something for you after all. You might not like it, but it's all I have at the moment.

What I'm talking about is a simple errand, so it shouldn't tax your skills too much. My friends at Egonics Inc. have come up with new tapes for the Latent Transmitter that I need to collect from them.

I can see you're curious about the transmitter, but what you don't know can't hurt you. Hm, I guess that's not exactly true, is it? Well, anyway, don't worry: I'll keep you all safe and tucked in. Run this errand for me and perhaps my opinion of you will rise above the level of "haughty indifference." Then I might allow you to sink your teeth into a juicier bone next time around.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: I see you have mastered the art of fetching, little pup. Might come in handy later on, but let's do something more fun now, eh?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Run along, now, there's a good puppy.

localizedName.text: Rogue Crop - Root of the Problem (3 of 4)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The techies have taken a quick look at the links you brought me and they're telling me it's something they've never seen before and are totally baffled by. I'm not sure what to make of their comments, is this radical new design a threat or not? I must get a definite answer before deciding how to proceed.

My observations and the data that you and others have collected for me, as well as information on these links, needs to be looked at by more talented techies. Take this data over to the Illinfrik system, to the Trust Partners station there. They will analyze this data and give me feedback I can work from.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Perhaps on your long journey to Auberulle and back you spent the idle minutes wondering what a member of the Angel Cartel was doing here in Algintal? I asked that exact same question when our chief told me he was sending me here. What is there here in Algintal for the Cartel? We have no presence to speak of here and even less authority. The few Angels who frequent the area are loners and nuts, acting pretty much of their own accord.

Well, to put things bluntly, we want to usurp the stranglehold the Serpentis and Thukkers have on smuggling and other lucrative activities here on the Gallente side of the Federation/Republic borders. The Thukkers, those devious buggers, are putting the latent transmission technology of Egonics Inc. to good use, but I've managed to worm my way into the deal.

But while I'm engaged in political machinations with the Thukkers and Egonics, the Serpentis are running rampant. I need you to take them down a peck or two. One of their main areas of operation is over in the Skeleton Comet complex in Deltole. They wrenched the place from Federation hands some years ago and now consider it their own little haven. Hitting them there would send a clear message that there's a new player in the sandbox and that they'd better watch out.

To put it simply: Go over there, locate some Serpentis smugglers, and pop them. Return with the smuggler tags they drop to claim your reward ... and of course glowing praises from me.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Fine work, {[character]player.name}. We'll soon have the Serpentis on the run. Talk to me again for further missions against them.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Oh, we got their attention now, {[character]player.name}! The Serpentis are seething, and it's all thanks to you. There's only problem: Now that the Serpentis know that we Angels are barging in, they're planning to retaliate. How very idiotic of them! Heh. Well, of course we must counter their counter-threats.

My most loyal and reliable source within the Serpentis tells me that an elite strike force is arriving from Fountain. I'm already quivering in my boots, as you can see. No, seriously, the fools have made one grave error. The strike force's gear arrived ahead of the team itself. It is now sitting deep inside the Skeleton Comet complex over in Deltole. "Only by exploiting the errors of others can we enlighten the world," my mother always told me, and who am I to defy my mother, eh? We must act quickly.

Go to the Skeleton Comet complex, locate the Serpentis Command Outpost, and destroy it. Then return with the strike force's gear to me. That should paralyze their whole operation.

localizedName.text: Rogue Crop - Trimming the Edges (1 of 4)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Algintal is one of the primary smuggling routes between the Federation and Republic space and Deltole is the main hub for smugglers in the constellation. The Serpentis have taken over a local complex, a natural beauty spot called the Skeleton Comet, and made it their own. Us Thukkers do our best to keep up and fortunately we're in good enough standing with most of the Serpentis to be allowed in their haven for some R&R.

But a week or two ago the Serpentis asked us to pay them back some of their hospitality. It seems parts of the complex are crawling with rogue drones. And not just any rogue drones, but pretty lethal ones. I understand their presence there contributed greatly to the Gallenteans evacuating the Skeleton Comet in the first place. And now it seems the rogue drones are stirring once more and the Serpentis are edgy what they might do. My superiors asked me to look into the matter and I'm interested in hiring you to do some reconnaissance for me in the complex.

What I want you to do is enter the complex and locate the rogue drone hive. Kill a few of their perimeter guards and return to me with whatever they drop. Until we know more about what makes these drones such a threat we should tread carefully, so don't try to act the hero and take on the whole hive in one go. Just pick out a few outer guards and we'll take it one step at a time from there.

And now it seems the rogue drones are stirring once more and the Serpentis are edgy what they might do. My superiors asked me to look into the matter and I'm interested in hiring you to do some reconnaissance for me in the complex.

What I want you to do is enter the complex and locate the rogue drone hive. Kill a few of their perimeter guards and return to me with whatever they drop. Until we know more about what makes these drones such a threat we should tread carefully, so don't try to act the hero and take on the whole hive in one go. Just pick out a few outer guards and we'll take it one step at a time from there.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Good work, {[character]player.name}. I'll get our techies to take a look at those links you collected and we'll see what they come up with.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Happy to have you aboard. Don't let a drone bug bite you.

localizedName.text: Rogue Crop - Neither Safe nor Sorry (2 of 4)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
This Aether Hive Link you returned with is a puzzle. It looks as if these drones are capable of more intimate communications than otherwise believed, but there are also hints that even more advanced hive mind links exist. I'm not a technician, so I can't go into all that much details, this information is just something relayed to me from our techies at the Thukker Mix. They say that they suspect that a truly symbiotic drone hive might be evolving. They sound exited about it, but they are safe in their labs, so what do they know? It's us that have to deal with these drones face to face that have to worry.

In any case, we must verify whether this is true or not. I need you to go back into the complex and now I need stuff from drones closer to the hive. There are some drone workers orbiting close to the hive that seem like ideal targets. Take a few of them out and, again, return with whatever they drop. I will then forward it to our techies and see what the situation is. Just be extra careful when you take the workers out, you never know what might be protecting them. Maybe nothing, maybe something heavy.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Ok, I have your code.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: You want me to find some sort of a binary code in the asteroid belts? Ok, I'll have a look.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I have no idea what you're saying and I'm not interested.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I have no patience in finding your stupid code.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The Serpentis are not taking us seriously enough, it seems. My spies tell me their leadership thinks your strike was a one-time occurance that they need not concern themselves with. And more importantly, it did little to weaken their grip on the smuggling in the constellation. So we need to take more drastic steps to show them that we mean business.

With all the hype surrounding the Wiyrkomi's presence here in Algintal, smugglers have to be extra careful. The Serpentis are no idiots, and they've reacted fast. They built a huge repackaging factory in the middle of nowhere, where they ship all their illegal goods to be repacked into something looking a bit less suspicious. I understand they learnt the technique from the Thukkers, who've done the same for years. Be that as it may.

What I'm asking of you is no small feat. Take out the repackaging factory, and the Serpentis will not only become very aware of our presence here, but their operation will take a severe hit. My informant has given me the coordinates of the repackaging factory, but I have only very limited information about the defenses around the installation. No doubt they're formidable, so taking a few friends along is a good idea. But I'm pretty sure the defense systems are not yet fully operational since the factory only recently opened.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Amazing! Looks like the drones in the Skeleton Comet beat you to it. Thankfully they left enough of the new breed drones intact for you to complete your assignment and me to have something to send to my superiors. But now we can rest assured that these evolutionary drones won't pose a threat to us in the future. And we have you to thank for that, {[character]player.name}!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I've received a preliminary report from Illifik. It seems a new strand of rogue drones evolved in that hive over in the Skeleton Comet complex. At first, this new strand was incorporated into the existing hive and used to augment it. These strange links you got me are a case in point. But here's the interesting thing. It seems the queen in the drone hive in the Skeleton Comet eventually turned against these new rogue drones and chased them away.

The techies in Illifik managed to extract imbedded commands in the hive links you brought them that showed that the queen has ordered her drone army to destroy all these evolved rogue drones. Obviously she fears they might pose a threat to her authority. I don't know if her drone army is already on the prowl, but I do know where one group of these evolved rogue drones is located at. I've been ordered to retrieve a functional hive mind from these new drones for further analyzes of their capabilities. Getting in a cross-fire between two opposing rogue drone factions seems kinda dangerous to me, thus I'm asking you if you're up to the job. I have no idea what you should expect in this drone hive location, be on the lookout for the drone army sent by the queen in the Skeleton Comet.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: As a matter of fact there is.  I'm looking for some work.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The drones have been taken care of, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text: One of our supply depots in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} was recently attacked by rogue drones.  Fortunately no-one was killed, but they refuse to leave the area.  I want them destroyed, every last one.  Return to me when you've accomplished your task.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: In that case I have something that's right up your alley.  Well, as long as you can handle yourself in combat, anyway.  One of our supply depots in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} was recently attacked by rogue drones.  Fortunately no-one was killed, but they refuse to leave the area.  I want them destroyed, every last one.  Return to me when you've accomplished your task.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Excellent.  But unfortunately I've received reports of more attacks, my office has been virtually swamped with complaints from inhabitants of outlying settlements.  So if you're up for it, I've got another mission waiting for you.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
As I told you after your last mission, the rogue drone problem just keeps growing. Don't get me wrong, it's no threat to our major outposts here, but we just don't have the manpower to constantly patrol every corner of the Araz constellation. So we need people like you to clean up the mess sometimes.

Your last mission put to an end a small force of rogue drones which had roamed too close to one of our supply depots. This time I want you to take care of the root of the problem, a Strain Drone Matriarch which reportedly carries the mother-brain of the hive. Destroy it and the hive collapses.

The problem is finding the Matriarch. Our surveillance forces have been working 24/7 to locate some of these 'mother-drones', and there is one in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that I want you to take care of. And for that we have a plan. You must lure the Matriarch drone out of her 'nest', as attacking it head-on is risky and unnecessary. All you have to do is assault a small base near the nest which is infested with the drones, and the Matriarch will come. We have plenty of experience with situations like this and our estimates suggest that she will arrive in around 20 minutes.

So to cut the story short, warp to the bookmarked location in the mission details and make your presence known. Wait until the Matriarch shows up and destroy her. I suggest clearing the area of rogue drones before she arrives, as that would save you the hassle of having to deal with them all at the same time.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Excellent work.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You have any more work for me?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You're still here? Well then, yes I have some more work. A large group of Serpentis were seen enter {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, with two industrials in tow. We are pretty sure this is a group of smugglers on their way through Araz, to where we don't know. They somehow got past our customs officials but we know their approximate coordinates now and therefore we can set up an ambush. I'll give you the coordinates of a small asteroid belt where we have set up a warp disruptor. That will force their ships to materialize from warp, and gives you the perfect chance to launch your ambush.

From what we've seen, they aren't traveling in a single group, so don't expect them all to arrive at once. Change your tactics accordingly.
