messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great!  Your achievements for us have not gone unnoticed.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Quite right, {[character]player.name}. I think it's time for you to know the objective of my mission here in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. We were to infiltrate Kois City, the central administrative complex in G5ED-Y, from where the Caldari send all of their expeditions, and answer the question that has been nagging my superiors back home, "Why are they here?".

Now getting into Kois City will be no easy task. It's heavily fortified. But on the bright side I think I know exactly what we're looking for. My sources tell me that the expeditionary forces store most of the data they have collected in a computer within the city's science labs. Backup data is also stored in data chips within their storage facility in the civilian sector of the city. Therefore your task is to somehow get into the civilian quarter and acquire at least one of those data chips. From this data we will hopefully be able to piece together their objective, and find out if it's worth our time to get involved.

This used to be Black Jack's task, but I assume he discovered something that convinced him to cut ties with us and go solo. But I will tell you this, it is in your best interest to complete this task at any cost. Should you fail, or decide to 'keep' the data for yourself, the Syndicate will hunt you down like a dog and force you to watch your own family executed in the cruelest of ways. Is that clear?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Yes ma'am.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Infiltrate Kois City, find the storage facility in the Civilian Quarter and destroy it.  Loot the Expeditionary Data from the wreckage and return to your agent.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good.  Now you'll find the storage facility I referred to in the civilian sector of the city.  You will probably have to destroy it to access the data chips due to the heavy security of the structure.  So just keep your fingers crossed that the data isn't destroyed with the building!

You have the data! Incredible, I truly thought the mission I gave you was close to impossible. Yet here you are.

Enjoy your reward, {[character]player.name}, you've certainly earned it. As for myself, I'll be heading back to Syndicate space soon enough with my findings, have a nice day.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ah, it's nice to see a friendly face around here for a change, {[character]player.name}. But to answer your question, I came here to investigate Constellation E-8CSQ, which has been reported to contain massive gas clouds full of material used in booster manufacturing. There have been a lot of rumors about it within {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}, and I thought I'd take a look for myself. Unfortunately, the number of rogue drones and outlaws here has me quite worried, so I dare not go looking for the clouds myself. Hence, I might have a job for you...

However, I suggest you refrain from accepting my task unless you have access to a gas cloud harvester module. Without that, you will just be wasting my time.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I found one of the gas clouds you've been looking for, {[character]agentID.name}, and it's at these coordinates ...

messages.mission.extrainfo.header.text: A Brief Guide to Booster Manufacturing

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll take anything you got as long as it's worth my time.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Boosters are made by processing chemicals extracted from special gas clouds that can be found in certain deadspace areas in many regions. Some constellations, such as E-8CSQ, 09-4XW, 9HXQ-G, OK-FEM, Pegasus, Assilot, I-3ODK, and 760-9C, however, are rumored to have massive clouds of a scale not seen anywhere else. Finding these clouds requires the ability to conduct long-range scanning, for example via scan probes. Finding them is not always an easy task, though; it sometimes requires quite a bit of exploration.

The downside of searching for these clouds is the fact that they are generally located in dangerous pirate-infested space. Few if any of these clouds exist in civilized space, having been depleted long ago by the mega-corporations. Hence, searching for them can be quite risky and is not recommended for any but the most experienced combat pilots.

To extract the chemicals from the gas clouds, you need a gas cloud harvester module. You also need to find the correct type of gas cloud. Not all clouds have chemicals that the gas cloud harvester can extract, and therefore you might have to go through some trial and error at first before you get the hang of gas cloud harvesting.

Today, most boosters are very much illegal in civilized space, due to the horrible side-effects experienced by users during the Great Booster Craze many decades ago. Manufacturing them must therefore be done in lawless space, outside the spheres of power of the major civilized factions. Similarly, anyone caught smuggling illegal boosters into civilized space can face very steep penalties.

Manufacturing boosters can broken into a few phases. Phase 1 involves extracting the material from the gas cloud. Phase 2 requires a refinery structure with the appropriate service module to process the chemicals and create reactions. Phase 3 also requires a structure or station with the equipment for booster manufacturing to process the reaction and create the booster. This simple 3-step process will result in the creation of a fairly common booster. With additional work, the right blueprint, and a combination of several low-quality boosters, one can create higher-quality versions.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Okay, what I need you to do for me is find one of the famed E-8CSQ gas clouds. Now of course I'm referring specifically to those gas clouds containing the materials I need for booster manufacturing. You must tell me where the cloud is and get me a sample from it. If you do this for me, I'll give you a booster blueprint copy, plus a little extra cash if you're fast. And you'll learn something in the process. Sounds useful, huh?

You will find information on how to find and access the clouds in the message I uploaded to the mission details in your Opportunities interface.

localizedName.text: All Things Come to an End (1 of 2)

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: I am the mayor, yes. But you might find the inhabitants to be a bit ... independent. Anyway, I assume, from looking at the database information on you, that you're a freelancer. Looking for a job, perhaps?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I have completed the task, Rakka.  Now for my reward ...

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: As a matter of fact, I am. Anything I can do for you or this fine station?

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Excellent. Yes, you will receive your reward, don't worry. But before you leave, I have one more task for you. The competence you showed in your last assignment has given me an idea ...

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Makeinu has a thorn in its side that I want drawn out, the sooner the better. As you might know, some of our residents have had a fairly violent history. And it so happens that DED felt the urge to send assassins all the way out here to settle the score with a couple of my people who had some run-ins with the law some time ago. Or this could be a private vendetta by an angry DED commander. Who knows? But either way, they need to be dealt with before they find us. We're ill equipped to deal with an encounter like that, and quite frankly most of us are too old and worn out to fight.

I've had the DED squadron tracked for some time now. I'll upload a bookmark for their current location to the mission details in your Opportunities interface. Find them and take out their leader ― that should be enough to send them crawling back to their homeland with their tails between their collective legs.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Greetings, Rakka.  I hear you call the shots here in Makeinu?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes, your next assignment is a little more personal in nature. You see, I was born and raised in the Venal system, and during my teens I joined the Guristas militia. I never knew my parents, but I assume they were loyal to the Guristas. I did have a few comrades that I could call friends, and my life was relatively stable. But then came the assignment that would change everything.

I was sent to E-8CSQ to find and apprehend a traitor, Akkeshu Karuan. My orders were specific, to bring him back dead or alive to Jirai Laitanen at the Guristas headquarters. I was not to return, not ever, until and unless this task was accomplished. I never questioned my orders, and frankly I don't give a damn what Akkeshu was accused of. For my entire life, I have known nothing other than the Guristas, the organization that fed and clothed me during my darkest of times, and I owe them my life.

But unfortunately the mission did not go as planned. I fought Akkeshu and his men inside what is now known as "Cadaver Reef." I was victorious in that battle, but Akkeshu still slipped through my grasp. He and what remained of his gang fled deeper into the deadspace pocket, and of course I followed with the fleet under my command. That action turned out to be a terrible mistake. Akkeshu knew the area like the back of his hand, and he managed to use that knowledge to his advantage. Once he warped away from our targeting systems, all we could find was an acceleration gate. When we activated it, it propelled us deeper into the rock-filled deadspace complex. But somehow Akkeshu had managed to reconfigure the gate, and instead of finding him on the other side, we were sent straight into a massive drone hive. messages.mission.extrainfo.header.text: A Brief Guide to Booster Manufacturing

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll take anything you got as long as it's worth my time.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Boosters are made by processing chemicals extracted from special gas clouds that can be found in certain deadspace areas in many regions. Some constellations, such as E-8CSQ, 09-4XW, 9HXQ-G, OK-FEM, Pegasus, Assilot, I-3ODK, and 760-9C, however, are rumored to have massive clouds of a scale not seen anywhere else. Finding these clouds requires the ability to conduct long-range scanning, for example via scan probes. Finding them is not always an easy task, though; it sometimes requires quite a bit of exploration.

The downside of searching for these clouds is the fact that they are generally located in dangerous pirate-infested space. Few if any of these clouds exist in civilized space, having been depleted long ago by the mega-corporations. Hence, searching for them can be quite risky and is not recommended for any but the most experienced combat pilots.

To extract the chemicals from the gas clouds, you need a gas cloud harvester module. You also need to find the correct type of gas cloud. Not all clouds have chemicals that the gas cloud harvester can extract, and therefore you might have to go through some trial and error at first before you get the hang of gas cloud harvesting.

Today, most boosters are very much illegal in civilized space, due to the horrible side-effects experienced by users during the Great Booster Craze many decades ago. Manufacturing them must therefore be done in lawless space, outside the spheres of power of the major civilized factions. Similarly, anyone caught smuggling illegal boosters into civilized space can face very steep penalties.

Manufacturing boosters can broken into a few phases. Phase 1 involves extracting the material from the gas cloud. Phase 2 requires a refinery structure with the appropriate service module to process the chemicals and create reactions. Phase 3 also requires a structure or station with the equipment for booster manufacturing to process the reaction and create the booster. This simple 3-step process will result in the creation of a fairly common booster. With additional work, the right blueprint, and a combination of several low-quality boosters, one can create higher-quality versions.

You must tell me where the cloud is and get me a sample from it. If you do this for me, I'll give you a booster blueprint copy, plus a little extra cash if you're fast. And you'll learn something in the process. Sounds useful, huh?

You will find information on how to find and access the clouds in the mission details in your Opportunities interface.

Few if any of these clouds exist in civilized space, having been depleted long ago by the mega-corporations. Hence, searching for them can be quite risky and is not recommended for any but the most experienced combat pilots.

To extract the chemicals from the gas clouds, you need a gas cloud harvester module. You also need to find the correct type of gas cloud. Not all clouds have chemicals that the gas cloud harvester can extract, and therefore you might have to go through some trial and error at first before you get the hang of gas cloud harvesting.

Today, most boosters are very much illegal in civilized space, due to the horrible side-effects experienced by users during the Great Booster Craze many decades ago. Manufacturing them must therefore be done in lawless space, outside the spheres of power of the major civilized factions. Similarly, anyone caught smuggling illegal boosters into civilized space can face very steep penalties.

Manufacturing boosters can broken into a few phases. Phase 1 involves extracting the material from the gas cloud. Phase 2 requires a refinery structure with the appropriate service module to process the chemicals and create reactions. Phase 3 also requires a structure or station with the equipment for booster manufacturing to process the reaction and create the booster. This simple 3-step process will result in the creation of a fairly common booster. With additional work, the right blueprint, and a combination of several low-quality boosters, one can create higher-quality versions.

And you'll learn something in the process. Sounds useful, huh?

You will find information on how to find and access the clouds in the mission details in your Opportunities interface.

messages.mission.briefing.text: We've been encountering a tremendous amount of pirate activity in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name} lately.  Our convoys are constantly under threat, and our CEO demanded that we do something about the situation.  We are to hire trustworthy and competent mercenaries to help us out, as the security forces in this constellation are swamped with work.  So I ask you, {[character]player.name}, will you help us out this time?  If your answer is yes, then I have a difficult assignment for you.  I need you to eliminate a heap load of pirates at a few coordinates.  You will receive bookmarks to these locations, all of them within the system {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}.  Hopefully this will put a dent into their plans, and relieve our security forces a bit of their workload.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Alright, I'll tell you a little story. My expedition had discovered an area filled with gas clouds thicker than I had ever witnessed in my life, and we were ecstatic. For days we harvested the gas fields, with no end in sight. At that time I was already starting to daydream about where I would retire when I finished this job. It was probably the greatest moment of my life. Unfortunately, followed by the worst.

Once we had filled our cargo holds, we started to align our ships for warp. It was then that they hit us. They came from nowhere and warp scrambled our industrials and jammed the two merc ships escorting us. They demanded over half of our cargo. We debated. But before we could give an answer, they attacked. Half the expedition was wiped out, including some of my closest friends. The ones who survived were told to go back to camp and relay our story to the rest of the miners and harvesters, so that the next time one of our expeditions runs into the Guristas we follow their orders immediately.

Now I just want to leave this dreadful place, I knew I took a huge risk by coming here but now that I've seen the face of death ... I just don't think I have it in me anymore.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm sorry for your loss.  Perhaps I can help.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: You're some fighter, I didn't expect you to come back alive.  But I'm happy you did, here's your reward.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
I know some of the families of my colleagues who perished on that fateful day, and I would like their bodies returned to me so that I can bring them back to Caldari space for proper burial. If you're up for the job, I'll give you a bookmark to the deadspace area where they lost their lives. You should be able to find the wreckage of their ships there.

You'll probably have to navigate through at least two pockets though to find all of them, once the Guristas attacked we tried to flee via the acceleration gates there, some of us only made it past one gate before being mowed down.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Although the loss of my friends can never be replaced, you have certainly gone far to ease the burden of their deaths.  For that I will be forever thankful.  Take your reward, and be safe.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Your success in the last mission has given me some hope.  Perhaps my comrades can be avenged.  The captain of the Guristas gang which attacked us is still at large.  But some of my people have tracked him down, and I have the coordinates to his hideout.  I will give you these coordinates, if you promise to destroy him and anyone under his command.  You will receive a reward, of course.

You're observation is correct, I AM frustrated!  And it's rather embarrassing to tell you the truth ... but if you're a merc for hire then I'll spill the beans, as long as you promise to help me.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I brought back the stash.  Some advice though, carry a backup of that damn password!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I promise.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
Hey! Don't tell me what to do! If I didn't have another job for you, I'd keep the reward for myself. Learn some manners!

Besides, you have no idea how much CPU a complex password like that takes. Hacker-proof passwords are no laughing matter these days.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Ok, just promise you won't laugh. You see, before I came here I was a computer programmer. I specialized in creating and maintaining artificial intelligence for Kaalakiota, probes and drones and that sort of stuff. Well after I got here, I realized I needed some heavy duty protection considering the relative lawlessness of this place, and the mercs here were just way too expensive.

So I used my expertise to set up a self-maintaining drone facility, which provided me with enough backup to safely harvest the gas fields around here. It worked like a charm to begin with ... until hardware failure wiped out the secret password I've been using to access the mother-drone computer's mainframe.

Now I can't even get into my own home! I've been sitting around here for days but none of these good-for-nothing mercs have the guts to face my drones. Maybe you've got it in you?

Anyway first I want my stash of extracted gas chemicals. You'll find a few containers full of it in my storage facility. I'll give you the coordinates, all you have to do is warp there, take out the drones guarding the stash, loot it, and bring it back here.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You look frustrated.  What's up?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll do it.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Don't come back until the Drone Creation Compound has been destroyed, that's where the drone mother-computer is stored.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Not bad, not bad.  You'll do quite nicely here, {[character]player.name}, I know there's a bunch of people looking for someone of your caliber.  Take care.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Have I got any? Are you mad? I've been sitting here all day looking for contractors with some combat experience. Now I need someone I can rely on for this job, and I have to say I'm impressed with the way you've dealt with some of your previous assignments for Caldari agents. So maybe you're cut out for this ...

Anyway, I've been informed that a few gangs of Guristas scoundrels have decided to attempt a full scale assault on our little town here. Inside sources tell me that they are not working for the core Guristas leadership in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, so they won't be as deadly and organized as I first feared. But they're still a major threat, and as such I need someone to take care of 'em. If you can do the job, in other words take 'em out before they reach Pioneer's Sanctuary, then I'll reward you generously.

It so happens that I know where one of their stopping points will be, I will give you the coordinates of course.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll take the job.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Excellent work!  You saved us from a nasty encounter, and for that I thank you.  But there's more, so stick around.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Just a word of advice before you leave, they will arrive at the rendezvous point in waves, so I suggest shooting them with all you got to prevent them from overwhelming you.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: No problem.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Make them suffer.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You mentioned you had some more work for me.

messages.mission.briefing.text: I'm in a bit of a dilemma at the moment.  I managed to find an area of deadspace filled with lucrative gas clouds, but as always there was a catch.  The Guristas had apparently erected an outpost next to an acceleration gate leading directly into the deadspace pocket containing the clouds.  I haven't detected any signs of them actually harvesting the gas, but I dare not try to enter the area with them nearby.  Could you please remove their presence for me?

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: The pirates are gone?  I'll have to take a look myself.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Anything else I can do for you?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thanks for retrieving the data, {[character]player.name}.  Hopefully this data will lead me to gas clouds far away from those pesky pirates.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Hmmm, yes there is one more thing.  I have a long range scanner in I1-BE8 which I use to look for promising sites which may harbor harvestable gas clouds.  The problem is I'm afraid of going back there and retrieving the data, the last time I tried I noticed a couple pirates nearby who I thought might be waiting in ambush.  Anyway I don't want to take any chances, but if you're willing then I'll pay you for getting me the data.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You're the mayor of Pioneer's Sanctuary, aren't you {[character]agentID.name}?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Your observation is correct. And I've been watching you, {[character]player.name}, for a while now, and you seem to fit the criteria I've been looking for.

Now I have a task for you that may prove to be extremely dangerous. As you probably know already we've had a long standing quarrel with the Guristas forces in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. And it's really showing a toll on the settlers here. But I want to propose a truce, and I want you to be the one that brings them the offer. I will supply you a bookmark to the Guristas Headquarters in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, all you have to do is warp in there and bring it to their leaders.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: It's as I expected, they won't listen to reason.  Then I guess it's time for us to face the cold hard facts, the town must be abandoned.  Unless someone is brave enough to stand up to those scoundrels and teach them a lesson ...

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You are, huh. Unfortunately there is only one way to truly stop the Guristas from enslaving us, at least temporarily. And that is to annihilate their high command in 1QH-0K. I know it sounds foolhardy and it probably is, but it's the only way ... if we don't strike them down at the root they will just keep on coming.

I'm probably getting way ahead of myself here, I really can't ask you to try something insane like assault their most powerful stronghold in the entire constellation. But if you do, I will give you a very nice reward for the insignia from their leader.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Guristas high command in {[location]agentConstellationID.name} is no more.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I will do it.  The Guristas will fall before me.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I fear for your life, but on the other hand you are our only hope.  So I wish you good luck.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm willing to help you fight the Guristas

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You have managed the impossible once again, {[character]player.name}.  But this time you surprised even myself.  Pioneer's Sanctuary owes you a great debt which can never be repaid in full.  But hopefully your reward will at least repay your expenses.  Good luck in whatever the future holds for you.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm lookin' for some work. You got any?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The job is done, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text: I need someone to investigate a distress signal from an industrial registered to a group of harvesters in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I'd like you to fly them back here to safety, and we'll fetch the industrial later.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Sure, {[character]player.name}. Something up your alley just hit my desk this morning, in fact. I need someone to investigate a distress signal in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It was sent from an industrial registered to a group of harvesters that recently came to Fatimar Outpost from Amarr space. It's probably just an engine failure or something, but I don't have spare mechanics to deal with that problem just now. So I'd like you to fly them back here to safety, and we'll fetch the industrial later.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: From your report, I can only assume that the hapless harvester expedition was beset by Sansha pirates and murdered; the distress signal must have been sent by the enemy to lure us in. Clever, I suppose, but I feel bad for the harvesters' families. They were simple, hard-working men and women, and they'll be missed here in Fatimar.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: So what's next? You seem like you have something on your mind.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I guess my work here is done.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Deliver the bad news to the slain workers' colleagues. They reside in a small outpost in a nearby system; I'll upload the coordinates directly into your NeoCom. As usual, all you have to do is fly close to the outpost structure and the message should automatically be uploaded into their communications database.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Your an observant one, {[character]player.name}. You'll go far, I imagine. Now that we know of the harvester's fate, it's time to deliver the bad news to their colleagues. They reside in a small outpost in a nearby system; I'll upload the coordinates directly into your NeoCom. As usual, all you have to do is fly close to the outpost structure and the message should automatically be uploaded into their communications database.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Yes, thanks for the help, {[character]player.name}. Wish I could find more for you to do right now, but most of the jobs around here are beneath a capsuleer like you.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You need any help?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Yes I do. I'm the leader of a small gang of harvesters, and I'd like to hire you to clear a rogue drone infestation near a gas field we've been working on. They have been continually harassing us, and it's come to a point where my gangmates have refused to venture back there. Armed escort would cost a fortune over a long period, so we believe the most cost effective approach is simply eradicating the threat all-together.

Your first mission is to clear the area of rogue drones. Once that is done then report back to me immediately.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Excellent.  But there's one more thing to be done to completely end our drone problem.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: What's next?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You've done us a great service, {[character]player.name}.  I'll notify my crew immediately, they'll be ecstatic.  Take care.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Now it's time to strike at the root of the problem, the Drone Hive.  The drones are manufactured there, so as along as it's around they will just keep coming.  Destroy it and report to me for your reward.

Who am I? WHO AM I? I am Kushan Horeat, Baron of Dagamar. I came here with my forces when Nimpor requested my assistance. And perhaps you are curious as to why a prestigious Imperial lord would waste his time answering a peon like yourself...?

The answer is that I need a little help. I have a dangerous mission that needs doing, and I would rather not risk my own men if possible. So, on behalf of the Amarr Empire, I desire you to help me.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You... you, you worthless, impudent fool! If I wasn't so busy looking for servants to do my bidding, I'd strike you down right now! Get out of my sight, worm!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Yes, sir! Whatever you command!

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: How dare you speak to me like that, you whey-faced monkey! Out here, you're a nobody, just like me, so sit down and mind your manners ― before I give you something to curse about... Stupid windbag.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: I see you've done my bidding in a timely manner.  Maybe after all this is over I'll hire you as my wine steward.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
That's more like it.

Your task is simple. There is a stargate in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} that I had built recently, to transport my troops secretly past the Sansha louts. Somehow, though, one of my incompetent commanders managed to reveal himself ... and the stargate ... to a Sansha patrol. Now they're all over it, probably scavenging the place for spare parts.

I want you to destroy it. Completely. Don't even leave the debris behind. There is data in the computer systems inside the stargate that might reveal the location of all our positions to the Sansha, including Fatimar Outpost. This data must not fall into the hands of the enemy.

Dismissed.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Yes, there's one more thing I want done. Immediately, you understand? If you stumble upon a complex of theirs, then return to me immediately and give me the exact coordinates.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: How DARE you speak to me like that! I'll have your head on a platter! I'll, I'll ... why, I'll have your whole family thrown into slavery! I'll tear down your ship and build my vacation resort out of it! Just you wait and see!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll do it.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sorry, but I don't have time for arrogant louts like yourself. Later, mouthpiece.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent, servant. Get to work, then, and be quick about it or I'll lower your reward.

The expedition you faced in your last mission hails from a colony in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and they'll probably not be happy when they find out what happened to their colleagues. I want you to completely obliterate their outpost and any ships nearby, that way I can safely venture back to the asteroid field without worrying about reprisal attacks. You know who you're speaking to, right? I'll educate you regardless. I am {[character]agentID.name}, protector of Fatimar Outpost. Basically I run this place, and have ever since Frolo died.

Now I have a mission that would require you to be extremely meticulous and discreet. From looking at your accomplishments here in Fatimar Outpost you probably have what it takes to get it done. And oddly enough I trust you to keep a lid on this more than Kushan Horeat and his men.

If you're still interested, let me know.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm interested.  Keep going.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sounds too risky for me.  I'd rather do garbage hauling missions.  Wait ... what on earth am I doing in 0.0 space?!!

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Jamur escaped?  Too bad, but at least you got someone.  I'll have them interrogated immediately.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
I'll start from the beginning. I joined Frolo's crew many years ago, when I was a young lad, and served under him right up to his death. Those were some good times, and we made a fortune from harvesting gas clouds in this area and neighboring constellations. Dorim, Frolo's second son, also served under his father and we became the best of friends.

Now life here was simple, until Frolo died. He was a great man, a remarkable leader. The pioneers out here all looked up to him and followed the rules while he was around. But soon after his death that was about to change.

A few months after Frolo passed away, his firstborn, Jamur Fatimar, arrived in Fatimar Outpost. He had lived all his life with his mother in Amarr space, far away from the grueling life we have here in no-man's-land. Basically he was fed with a silver spoon his entire life, and that rubbed off on him.

As soon as he arrived he claimed ownership of the Outpost. We decided to play along with his little game, as neither I nor Dorim had any real ambition to take on the leadership role. But people quickly started to despise him. He was much harsher than Frolo ever was, and was very detached from the local miners and harvesters here who Frolo used to work along-side. He was a strict, traditional Amarrian ruler who had zero tolerance for any difference of opinion from his own. He implemented a hefty tax which was largely used to pay for his extravagant lifestyle. Needless to say, things got hairy around here. Some of pioneers split away from Fatimar Outpost and founded their own colonies elsewhere, and there were rumors of a rebellion.

When I saw everything that we had built virtually crumbling beneath us, I was forced to intervene. I claimed leadership over Fatimar Outpost. A power struggle ensued, which I eventually won. As you might expect, Jamur was not very fond of losing his title and decided to split away from us, forming his own colony elsewhere in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. But I've always had the impression that he was out for revenge, and therefore I've had his little colony under surveillance for quite some time. And that's what alerted me to an extremely worrying turn of events. Jamur had been in contact with someone from outside {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}, who my sources tell me has promised to help him in 'his war with Fatimar Outpost'. I can't imagine what a bitter, power hungry man like Jamur would do to reclaim his title. I want you to find out for me. I will upload the coordinates of the meeting point into your NeoCom, all you have to do is warp there and disrupt the meeting. Bring this 'agent' to me for questioning.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes, they coughed it up immediately. Apparently they aren't very loyal to their former master. The leader of the group has been in close contact with Jamur and claims he's gone mad. His hatred of me has clouded his judgment, and he's done the unthinkable. The secret agent in your previous mission was in fact an agent of the Sansha's Nation! Talk about striking a deal with the devil ... he's gone way too far this time.

The good news is that we can trace Jamur's exact whereabouts. The bug I had implanted into his ship is still functional, and I can see his location on our scanner. I want you to find him immediately and take him out. Every minute that passes is crucial, he must not be allowed to reveal our location to the Sansha's Nation. If that happens then all may be lost.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Jamur is no more.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: He's as good as dead.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: You better be right.  We can't let him escape.

Standard procedure requires that they be inspected for any possible diseases or mental disorders before they're allowed on board.

We need to help them out, and I'd like you to deliver the necessary goods to them.

Simple enough, eh? Well, are you interested or not? I know of several others who would happily take this offer in your stead.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Done. Batteries delivered, crisis averted. So, about my pay...?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm interested, I'm interested. No need to be hasty. Just give me the coordinates and the batteries, and I'm off.

It's an easy job, and pays well. Just be sure you have enough space in your cargohold: This is a pretty big shipment.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Batteries delivered, crisis averted. Thanks for the job. Easy money.

Take these planetary vehicles and bring them out there, so the lazy gits can get back to work.

Don't worry about getting busted by customs for transporting the viral agents: We've cleared the matter with them and they'll be expecting you.

I have put in a formal request for their termination, but the powers above don't seem to be in agreement.  Which, of course, only reinforces my opinion that they are all corrupt.  Seeing as we can't throw them out of the nearest airlock, I'm going to do the next best thing

I'm sending you out there with a new security officer and some guards to back him up.  It's your responsibility to make sure they make it to the station safe.

These people simply refuse to leave, some are laid off workers of ours while others are simply outsiders who think they can come and live off our hospitality indefinitely.  Since there are strict regulations against sending them out the airlock for no reason, and since we can't simply frame every single one of them for a crime worthy of such a fate, we've no choice but to forcibly move them somewhere else.  Another station will do.  In fact I'd like you to move a heap-load of them to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  I never liked those bastards over there anyway, let them deal with this 'human problem'.

So, to keep the buyer happy, I'm gonna send you over his way with a sample of our high-quality slug throwers.  Hopefully this will buy me an extra day to get it sorted.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I've been looking for someone of your talents. It has come to our attention that an armada of Amarr crusaders has arrived in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. According to our sources, their primary objective is to destroy the Pagera Manton, which they view as being a sacrilegious icon of the Blood Raider faith. They believe the Blood Raider organization is defiling the graveyard of their ancestors, and their aim is to 'give them rest'.

These sorts of incursions are nothing new, but this time they mean business. I've never seen such a huge armada threaten our beloved holy site, and to top it off it's being led by one of the Amarrian High Priests, Heftah Nekmar, which is of some concern to us. He has recently led a campaign of propaganda against the Blood Raider religion from inside the Amarrian territories, and the destruction of the Pagera Manton would certainly be viewed as a mighty victory by his people.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Their scouts have been taken care of, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Ok, what do you want me to do?

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
One of the most revered holy sites of the Blood Raiders is located in the constellation OK-FEM, called the Pagera Manton. The Pagera Manton was a giant space-ship that was at the head of a massive Amarrian exploration team that had ventured into unknown lands hundreds of years ago. A malfunction in its warp-drive stranded the ship, far away from the rest of the fleet. During that time space-communication was not as sophisticated as today, and it had no way of contacting other vessels of the expedition. Years passed and the crew had finally lost all hope of survival. Food supply was running dangerously low, and it seemed that starvation was inevitable. It was then that one of the officers, an Ammatar by the name of Kalorr Makur, took matters into his own hands. He staged a successful coup against the commanding officer of the ship and had his most loyal followers bind and gag the dissidents inside a secure chamber under his control. These unfortunate souls became the crews new food supply, unbeknownst to most of the crewmembers. For over a year this plan worked, although Kalorr did have to turn to his own followers eventually to replenish his stock of human meat.

Over a century later the ship was discovered by Blood Raider pioneers scouring the distant solar-systems of OK-FEM. They found the remains of the crew, and more importantly a few dozen gigantic tanks encasing millions of liters of blood. Unbeknownst to them the blood had been collected by Kalorr who dried the human meat before consumption. The blood had been meant as a final foodsource after the meat supply had run out, but was never actually consumed as the machine responsible for recycling the air supply malfunctioned which caused the remaining crew to slowly suffocate. Fortunately the blood containers were kept in sub-freezing temperature, which despite over a centry of decay were still up and working when the Pagera was found. And not only that, Kalorr Makur's body was discovered in its very own container, along with his closest allies.

News of the find quickly spread through the Blood Raider territories, and their revered High Priest at the time declared it a 'gift from God'. The blood was stripped from the tanks and brought back to the Blood Raider headquarters for examination and ritualistic purposes. Kalorr was cloned, using genetic material retrieved from his body taken from the Pagera, and he was immediately instated as an officer of the Blood Raiders. Years later he was even made into a saint.

And to this day the Pagera is closely guarded by Kalorr and his small army of clones, extremely loyal to the Blood Raiders. Drugs, many generations of cloning and a terrible history has rendered the former Amarrian expeditioner completely insane. And despite the Pagera being a popular point of pilgrimage for the members of the Blood Raider organization, few venture there outside of large, heavily armed groups. Kalorr is known to pick off stragglers for his sinister rituals, no matter to which religion or organization they belong to.

Those blasted migrants are causing trouble again. Because of the abundance of gas clouds in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, our space is just crawling with them. As a matter of fact, a large group of Khanid harvesters built an outpost right next to my hideout in M0O-JG! I spent years building that place, and now they want to keep me out of my own home. I can't even go back without being shot at. It's just not right I tell you.

What I need you to do is find their outpost and blow it to bits. That should nudge them away, but it's not going to be easy. They locked and booby-trapped the acceleration gate leading into the deadspace pocket containing their base, so we have to find the key somehow. I know where they normally work, which is near a collection of massive gas clouds which they tend to harvest. I want you to ambush them there, and bring back captives for interrogation.

They managed to convert a few of our pod clones to their side, and together they have made an audacious get-away from the slave pens. Fortunately, we still have them on our radar, but we fear they might try to use one of the smuggler gates in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} to escape.

Obviously, it will set a very bad precedent should they manage to successfully get away. We can't have that. There's enough rebelliousness and infighting as it is within our ranks.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
One of the most revered holy sites of the Blood Raiders is located in the constellation OK-FEM. The original Pagera Manton was a gigantic battleship, flagship of a massive Amarrian exploration team seeking unknown systems roughly 200 years ago. However, a malfunction of the then newly built jumpgate into OK-FEM caused an explosion in the Pagera Manton's tachyonometry, resulting in the destruction of its subwarp drives. The ship was stranded in a distant and uninhabited system, and space communication not being as sophisticated as it is today, the Manton had no way of contacting other vessels of the expedition.

Years passed and the crew eventually lost all hope of survival. The food supply running dangerously low, starvation was imminent. Then, one of the senior officers, an Amarr Holder (and secretly a Sani Sabik adherent) by the name of Lieutenant-Commander Kalorr Makur, took matters into his own hands: He staged a successful coup against the ship's commanding officer and had his most loyal followers bind and gag the dissidents within a secure chamber. These unfortunate souls became the new leadership's food supply, although Makur apparently managed to keep this fact secret from most of his followers. According to the ship's logs, maintained by Makur, this plan worked for several years... although there is evidence that Makur did occasionally turn to his own followers to replenish his "stock," hiding his motives behind the guise of executions for crimes supposedly committed against the commander. Eventually, the ship's air supply malfunctioned, and the sixty or so remaining crewmembers slowly suffocated.

Over a century later, some time before the Amarr invasion of the Minmatar homeworlds, the ship was discovered by Amarr outlaws. They found the remains of the crew, and more importantly a few enormous tanks holding thousands of liters of human blood; it seems Makur had dried his human meat before consumption. The blood had been intended as a final food source after the meat supply had run out, but was never actually consumed before Makur and his crew died. Fortunately the containers were kept in cryo-vaults, which despite over a century of decay were still up and working when the Manton was found. And Kalorr Makur's body was discovered in its very own cryo-tank, along with those of his closest allies.

News of the find quickly spread throughout the pirates in the region and thence into the territories of the nascent Blood Raiders, whose revered High Priest declared the Manton a "gift from God." The blood was brought back to the Raider headquarters. Kalorr Makur was cloned using genetic material retrieved from his body, and immediately instated as an officer of the Blood Raiders. Several years later, he was beatified and sainted.

To this day, the floating wreck of the Pagera Manton is closely guarded by Makur and his small army of clones, all extremely loyal to the Blood Raiders. Drugs, many generations of cloning, and a terrible personal history have rendered the former Amarrian capsuleer completely insane. And despite the Pagera being a popular point of pilgrimage for the members of the Blood Raider organization, few even of that cult venture there outside of large, heavily armed groups, for Makur is known to pick off stragglers for his sinister rituals no matter to what religion or organization they belong.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Excellent.  But don't run off just yet, as I have one more task in store for you.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Get going then.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I heard you had some work.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I need someone to help me retrieve one of my clones. He's stuck near the Pagera Manton, his ship pretty much destroyed by Kalorr's gang when it accidentally ventured too close to the Pagera. We must act quickly, before Kalorr decides to make a meal out of the guy.

I will give you a bookmark to the Pagera. But whatever you do, don't venture too close to the holy site. Kalorr will not look too kindly upon that, and I have a feeling he's not in the best of moods ... not ever.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: I believe it's time to turn our eyes towards the defilers, led by the vile High Priest Heftah Nekmar. He's been a problem for years, and now he has the audacity to venture into our territory to attack our beliefs! He must be punished! An example must be set! And you shall be the deliverer of our wrath.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll do it.  But how do I find Nekmar?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: You won't have to look hard for Nekmar.  We know of his base of operations; I'll supply you with a bookmark to it.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Do you have any more tasks for me?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Your destiny obviously lies with the Blood Raider Covenant. And this day is a further testament of that fact. May your reward serve you well.

localizedName.text: Kaymotin's Scout - Gas Cloud Survey (1 of 2)

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll get that sample for you in no time.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Welcome to Yakura Harvesting Depot, {[character]player.name}. I have use for someone like you. You see, I'm not the typical Serpentis member, in fact I never took up the stereotypical practice of piracy. Instead I've devoted my life to creating a business which specializes in harvesting gas and rock from the Pegasus constellation. I still work for the Serpentis of course, but I've more interest in finding lucrative roid and gas fields than bullying the passersby.

Anyway, I have a small job for you. Our scanners have indicated that there is a large quantity of gas clouds in a certain area in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We think the source is pretty close to a certain asteroid belt, which has been claimed by an Astral Mining Inc. expedition. I want you to warp over to this asteroid belt and take a sample from one of the asteroids there, bring it back to me for inspection. We're hoping to find gas residue on the rock which would indicate the presence of gas clouds nearby.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent.

localizedName.text: Kaymotin's Scout - Remove The Miners (2 of 2)

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Anything else?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've completed the assignment, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The results of our tests indicate that vast swaths of gas clouds should be located not far from where you retrieved the sample. Since we expect the profits of harvesting these clouds to be extremely profitable, we're willing to risk a possible confrontation with Astral Mining Inc.

But first I want you to take care of their current expedition in the area. I want you to go back to where you found the sample and wait for the expedition to arrive. Destroy as many of their ships as you can, but it's imperative that you at least take out their commanding officers. That should cripple them long enough for us to move in and set up our defense perimeter before any reinforcements arrive.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent work, {[character]player.name}!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Hey there, {[character]player.name}. I have a task I want you to complete. If you do it right, I might have a small reward for you.

The next Legends Trial battle starts at midnight tonight, and as head of security around here, my job is to make sure it goes as smoothly as possible. However, there is a small problem. The documents detailing the fighters and their ships were scheduled to be delivered to me from {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} this morning. However, the courier assigned to the task has obviously failed us, and as such I need you to step up and fill his place. Go get the documents and bring them to me. Do it quickly and I will have a little something extra waiting for you.

Fly safe.

localizedName.text: Wessette Gauze - Making It So (1 of 2)

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Done deal, i forsee no problems in dealing with this.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Precisely one week from today, the Gallente Gaming Commission will have another Legends Trial tournament. The famed contestant, Kuroki Tselmi, will be going up against his long-time rival, Hadni Riiuto. Now, everybody loves to see two fighters face each other when they also have a personal dislike for each other. It makes the entire fight that much more intense. Of course, given the nature of mankind, everybody and their pet has placed some money on the outcome of this fight. 
Acquaintances of mine also placed money on this fight and we are all hoping that Kuroki Tselmi will win. He usually does, but it probably won't hurt if we try to give fate a little nudge, here. This is where you come in. 

I need you to go to Riiuto's agent. When you meet him, have a word with him about this whole business. He'll know what to do next, and we'll all be able to sleep a little easier at night knowing important people won't lose a lot of money on the match. 

Now, I have spoken to Riiuto's agent and he sounds fine with it, but keep your wits about you; don't go thinking this is going to be a walk in the bio-dome. This needs to go precisely as planned with no screw-ups, otherwise the Betting Commission will be on top of this like a Gallente escort, and they'll ride this thing for all it's worth if they find out.. I suggest you bring some friends to make sure the agent doesn't feel like telling anyone about this. What do you say, do we have a deal?

localizedName.text: Wessette Gauze - Making It So (2 of 2)

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Of course, a genuine fan, and I'd hate to see our favourite          lose. You can count on me to make sure Riiuto chances upon “unforeseen circumstances.”

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: ISK in the bank. Excellent job, my dear lad. I foresee a great future for you with us.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
As it turns out, you did your job a little too well. We seem to have scared Riiuto into seeking protection from the Gaming Commission. Perhaps we should have stuck to bribery. Oh well, we'll remember that for next time. We still need Tselmi to win this match against Riiuto and one way of accomplishing that is having Riiuto pull out of the match prematurely due to “unforeseen circumstances,” or whatever the Commission will choose to call it when you blow him out of the sky.

Because of our previous attempt of nudging fate into the right and profitable direction for my friends, our boy Riiuto is a little more concerned about his safety. He is flying with a heavy escort, but luckily for you I have a plan that cannot fail if you follow the instructions to the letter. It's not that complicated; just go to the location and hide behind an asteroid. After some time you'll see Riiuto and his escort meet up with a fuel tanker to refuel their ships. This will be the time to come out of hiding and attack them. If you attack before this moment, Riiuto and his escort will know something is up.

I trust you will perform as well as you did before. Don't let me down now, because I took the liberty of placing a little more money on this, using another friend of mine. If you're good to me, I might add you to the payroll during the next Legends Trial, or get you better seats if you want to play it safe. You do want to Tselmi to win, right? I mean, you're a sports fan, right?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We had a team of people doing mining work for us in one of our harvester outposts. It's a thankless and hazardous job, eons away from the safe mining you ship pilots get to engage in. The harvesting equipment they have to use is incredibly dangerous in untrained hands and requires both physical strength and endurance, particularly for the length of time these people have to work. I daren't even think of the accidents that might have occurred had the Minecore harvesters not taken it on themselves to ease their working days a bit with some innocent entertainment. It breaks up the monotony somewhat, so that one's focus on the mining laser won't accidentally slip, leaving some poor soul plastered all over the nearby asteroids.

The Minecore harvesters aren't allowed to have any signals in their suits apart from the ones required to run their equipment. All they have is closed communication channels. So a few began telling jokes, and some of them shared stories from past work, and eventually it turned out that one or two of them, embarrassed though they were at first, could even carry a tune. There is now a core troupe of harvesters who have dedicated themselves to keeping up their coworkers' spirits, maintaining a steady stream of radio talk all through the day. These are men whose only thoughts were how long it was until the end of their shift and how much they were going to drink when they got back to their quarters, and now for the first time they all have something to look forward to.

Except that their workplace is now under siege by rogue drones, and the company apparently refuses to waste manpower rescuing 'expendable resources'. If these people die, the tradition dies with them, and the entire workforce slides back into old, ugly habits. I cannot let that happen, no matter what the company thinks. I want you to go in there and get them.

Thank you for your task. I know not everyone cares about company morale, but with these poor people, distraction and boredom can kill. I'm sure the whole mess will give them plenty to talk about when they feel up to returning to work.

Unfortunately, we have a new problem. Not everyone feels so philanthropical toward their fellow man, even under circumstances where you'd think that people would stick together and help one another out. Now that you've cleared the last of the Minecore harvesters out of the area, the scavengers arrive. I have reason to believe that these rogue harvesters, unaffiliated with Minecore, have moved in and are proceeding to rob us of our equipment. These people undoubtedly intend to set up a business of their own, and plan to use our property as a starting point. The next step will certainly be attempts to headhunt our own employees, with extravagant offers of better working conditions, higher pay, more benefits and time off. Total and utter lies, all of it. Rogue operators pay even less, and if you desert the company to go work for them, you might as well have placed yourself in indentured servitude. I am not letting that happen to my people, especially now that they've built so much camaraderie and trust. I want you to return to the outpost, find these cowardly harvesters and destroy them, and retrieve our mining equipment.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: No worries. I´ll be back with him as soon as possible. And no boy bands. Got it.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent. Now we just have to hope our dear friend recovers from his trauma and can get back to work A.S.A.P. But we still have to deal with thouse CTF Forces before the inflict more damage to our operation, so talk to me again in a minute, after I take this Com-call.

messages.mission.briefing.text: One of our labs a few systems out is under a DED blockade, and all our "material" there is being confiscated. Our guards are being hit with serious firepower even as we speak. Now, most of our mobile research facilities are expendable, but this one is a bit special. Get in there and retrieve the imprisoned chemist, Achove Oullen.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
One of our labs a few systems out is under a DED blockade, and all our "material" there is being confiscated. Our guards are being hit with serious firepower even as we speak. Now, most of our mobile research facilities are expendable, but this one is a bit special. Our lead chemist there, Achove Oullen, was recruited after his rather embarrassing fall from grace at Poteque Pharmaceuticals. The man was an incredibly hard worker, often spending entire nights in his laboratory, and had been doing sterling work for the company.

Unbeknownst to his superiors, though, he had a tendency to use the lab for certain pet projects outside office hours. Most of these were completely illegal, of course, and poor Achove was found out when he attempted to synthesize a new drug that would allow the user to experience synesthetic highs, in which you see smells, taste sounds, and so on. His first test of the drug held him in rapt fascination all night.

All seemed to be going well until his radio alarm rang. Bit of a funny story, actually. Due to his frequent overnight stays at the lab, he had set the alarm to wake him at a preset hour in the morning so that he could take a quick shower and shave before his associates poured in, and had unwisely tuned it to a station that played almost nothing except the top 20 hits in the region. The songs apparently smelled and tasted so vile that he vomited, splattering equipment and furniture with chunky bile. He was still retching when his coworkers arrived on the scene, and to this day he still screams at the very mention of pop music.

All that aside, we felt he showed promise, so after he had been dismissed from Poteque, we snapped him up and set him back to work in earnest on his synesthetic drug, a booster called Sikes-8. The drug will be a key factor in our operation for the next year, but all this work will be for naught if poor Achove is taken into custody. Heh. No doubt they'll play an endless sequence of boy bands until he just cracks and tells them everything! Ha! But seriously, it would only be a matter of time before the Cartel got their hands on the information and used it to strengthen their hold on the drug market.

You have to intervene; retrieve the imprisoned Achove for us. Just be careful what you play on your ship's loudspeakers when you're on your way back....

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent work! Hopefully CTF will finally give up their efforts in our region ― or at least they won't be able to re-supply their ships in our space anymore ― and we can finally start mass-production of our new drugs. Oh, and by the way, Achove Oullen is doing well and extends his thanks. For what it's worth, he's taken up listening to Amarrian choral chanting, of all things...

messages.mission.briefing.text:
While on a routine courier job, one of my pilots recently ran into CTF forces that nearly destroyed his ship. Fortunately, his systems were intact enough that he could track their heading. Our covert ops ships later scanned the area and eventually discovered what is likely a DED communications and supply station.

I want you to scope out the location, and if you find any hint of a CTF depot there, I want you to conduct a surgical strike on them before they know what's happening. If you come across any shipyards or supply facilities, I want them blown to pieces so they can't fuel and repair their ships, and if anyone stands in your way, hull their ships. Show no mercy.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ah, {[character]player.name}! Thanks again for saving Achove. I hope you remembered to place him a sound-proofed cabin on your way here.

The DED activities have begun to trouble us. There have been far too many sightings of their ships, including ones that would not be here unless they had a safe-house of some kind nearby. While on a routine courier job, one of my pilots recently ran into CTF forces that seemed entirely blasé about their ammo supplies ... at least judging by the prodigious amount they fired into his shield, armor, and structure. He barely escaped the onslaught; his ship was taking direct hits to its hull, and the barrage of munitions was such that it nearly roasted him in his pod. Despite being wounded and needing medical attention, he reported to me directly after he'd docked. Stout fellow.

He told me that after the CTF forces had fragged his ship for a while, they'd casually and inexplicably taken off, and fortunately his systems were intact enough that he could track their heading. He gave me as much information as he could, then headed off to the med labs to have new eyebrows tattooed on.

The information he gave me wasn't much to go on, but it was enough. Our covert ops ships scanned the area and eventually discovered a location that is extremely likely to hold a DED communications and supply station. As much as I'd like to avenge my brave pilot and his scorched eyebrows, we don't dare risk a full-scale attack on the depot for fear that they will pick up the fleet's signal on their scanner post. Instead, we need to send in a single ship, or maybe a small squad of pilots if you have some willing allies, hoping that they can sneak in without triggering a full-scale reaction.

I'm putting you in command of this operation. I want you to scope out the location, and if you find any hint of a CTF depot there, I want you to conduct a surgical strike on them before they know what's happening. If you come across any shipyards or supply facilities, I want them blown to pieces so they can't fuel and repair their ships, and if anyone stands in your way, hull their ships. Show no mercy.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good on you, {[character]player.name}! Destroy every one of those shipyards and make sure all the defending forces are destroyed. No prisoners, and no survivors.

localizedName.text: Cliene Veine - Fixing the Problem (1 of 2)

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: No worries, I'll do this for you.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
For quite some time now, we have been aware of a security leak within our organization. Federal operatives have always been willing to pay a lot of money for inside information, and it has become abundantly clear to us in recent days that one of our commanders has fallen prey to the temptation of working for both sides.

We have no proof as to who the leak might be, but recently some of our people retrieved an encoded computer chip from the wreckage of a scout outpost. The chip contained documents which we think provide clues to the mole's identity. The chip is slightly damaged, so some parts are unencrypted and other parts missing entirely.

I want you to take the chip and bring it to our best code decryptor. He currently resides deep within the A8-XBW system, and you might have to go through some rogue drones to reach him there. Don't annoy him too much: He values his privacy and doesn't like being disturbed. There is a data terminal at his docking bay, so dock there and then bring me back the news.

localizedName.text: Cliene Veine - Fixing the Problem (2 of 2)

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: No worries. This informant and his contact will be dead before the day has passed.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Lets hope our dealings with the Gallente Fleet is over and we can get back to making ISK.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Our decryption expert just got back to us with the results. Fortunately, the chip was not too damaged. We have some very trustworthy indications that the snitch is a well known commander within the organization. It came as quite a surprise to me personally that he would start playing for the other team, though in retrospect it does make sense that only someone in his position would have been able to feed the enemy the information they've apparently been receiving.

The commander is on vacation right now at his residence and doesn't go on active duty for three days, so now is the time to strike. His residence is in the A8-XBW system. Gear up and fly there as fast as you can. Make the bastard suffer for betraying us ― let's hope it will be sufficient warning for others not to do the same.

Return to me when you have completed your task.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Consider them in yulai.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We have a big problem, and very little time to deal with it, {[character]player.name}. Four days ago, two of our squadrons conducted a strike on a small outpost not far from here, not realizing the place was a key tactical and scientific asset belonging to the Federation. In retaliation, Fed Navy HICOM has issued three platoons of combat ships to attack the Fountain region. According to our intel, they will be striking several vital targets of ours in the next twenty-four-hour period. Rumor has it the order came from President Roden himself, so we can expect them to bring big guns and larger numbers.

Losing these outposts is something we cannot afford, so we have to move swiftly and meet them head-on before they do their damage. Two teams have already been sent to intercept the first two squads. I want you to handle the third. We believe that they are currently residing at 4-EP12. Get over there and send them back to Yulai.

Great work. 
But somthing tells me they aren't done yet. So be ready if i need you in short notice.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Im on the case.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: The Serpentis family thanks you for your contribution. Here is your reward. Enjoy

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Something even bigger has come up, and I'm putting my best pilot, you, on the job. We've just learned that the group of Fed ships you took out wasn't just there for retaliation. It appears that through an informant within our ranks, the Federation have caught wind of our next-gen booster project. The platoons in question were reportedly dispatched for one purpose: to locate and terminate our star scientist, the one who masterminded the project and who currently holds the prototype formulas. The Federate officers you took care of were getting awfully close to him and managed to relay their information back to Fed Central before you took them out, so now we have an even larger Fed group attacking our primary research facilities in 4-EP12. 

The facility itself is not as important as the scientist himself, and the plans he holds. Should these designs fall into the wrong hands, years of research will be lost and those responsible, myself included, would probably find ourselves swiftly exiled from existence. Load up your guns and put an end to this siege. Save our scientist, and return to me when your task is complete.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You seem eager and willing to work for me. I have this little problem you could help me out with. Yesterday I was tricked into telling my supervisors I would take care of a situation in the area, not fully knowing all the details. Next time I´ll be more careful and not be baited. Anyway, I looked into it and scout reports indicated a large Serpentis operation in the ppg-xc system. It appears they're setting up their own tournament to compete with the Legends Trial. Some of our advertisers have a real problem with this, so they need the operation brought to a halt.

Naturally, I'd do it myself, but I figure since you are such an eager puppy you would just love to do it for me, wouldn't you?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Those blasted Serps just keep bouncing back. They seem determined to profit from the proceedings in some way. After we took out their tournament site, they appear to have immediately put their backup plan into action, namely to put up a brothel for tournament visitors in need of some after-hours entertainment. 

Their hiring practices leave a lot to be desired. They've abducted some of the finest exotic dancers this system has to offer. My immediate superior, bless his heart, has a particular affinity for one of these dancers, a girl who goes by the name of Layla. I need you to head out to the brothel, blow the living you-know-what out of it and bring the girl back. The Scope will be in your debt, friend.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Ah, {[character]player.name}! It is good to see there are freelancers who still maintain some loyalty to the Federation. It pleases me greatly that capsuleers like yourself still prove willing to help us out at need. Anyway, if you are looking for something to do, I know a little job that might just mix profit with pleasure.

The Serpentis are setting up a little shop in this area where they are training their fighters, intending to bring them into the tournament. Now, we aren't afraid of a little competition, but these fighters aren't all-natural, if you know what I mean. We're going to need them kidnapped and brought back here. Chances are you're going to find the substance the Serps have been feeding their fighters as well, and I know some people who are very interested to see it recovered. Purely for research, of course. I wouldn't dream of touching the stuff myself....

OK, OK, so maybe years ago when I was younger I might have tried some, but everyone experiments a little. No harm in that. Right? Just don't let me find out that you've kept a little for yourself. I need ... I mean, I want it all. To give to our researchers, of course. Ahem. Yes.

So, well, before you go ... listen, I would appreciate it if you could keep this matter to yourself. I'm sure you'll agree that not everybody needs to know about this, hm?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Thanks for meeting me in person, {[character]player.name}. We have a problem: My superiors have transcripts of our earlier communication and know about the drugs you brought back. It's okay, though, they've given me a chance to get rid of the stuff.

I need you to head out to Q-UA3C. The Serps have had a small shipping checkpoint there for a while, one which our investigative reporters have been monitoring for a big exposé on the way Serpentis supply chains work. Since my bosses want this little "mistake" of mine rectified quietly in order to prevent a scandal, they want the drugs taken there and the outpost destroyed. And that's what will happen.

Between you and me, though, I can't stand the idea of letting such a valuable commodity go to waste. So what I want you to do is head out there and kill everything you see, but leave the drug disposal to me. I'll convince my superiors and anyone else who asks that the drugs were destroyed at the outpost, and everyone will be happy ? at least, assuming that you can keep this a secret. And that is what you will do, I trust.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Good day. Looking for a job, are you? I have just the thing for a strapping capsuleer such as yourself. 

We're helping with putting on the Legends Trial, that great and massive confrontation. We've hit a snag, though; we had a shipment of supplies that were supposed to get here this morning, but the convoy ran into some technical difficulties and it appears they won't get here in time.

We've had wind of a Serpentis outpost in the vicinity, though, so we're thinking we might just outsource and play them at their own game. How about it? You up for a little hit-snatch-and-run?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Great job on the supplies. We seem to be good to go, now that most of the logistical details are taken care of. This will be greatest tournament ever. And I'm sure the Serpentis don't mind us borrowing some of their things.

I have another mission for you. Just another small supply run, one for which I'll reward you handsomely, to show our appreciation for... hold on.  Give me a second, here. I have something coming in over the wire.

...

Oh, lord. Oh, sweet sister of mercy. Looks like we made the Serpentis mighty mad. In retaliation for our little loan of goods, they've gone all-out and attacked a Gallente station in XG-D1L

Navy squadrons are already on the way, but it's going to take them some time to get there. What we need now is someone to repel the first wave of attack, buy some time for the reinforcements to get there. What do you say, pilot? In the mood to be a hero today?
