messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: One can never have too much loot- ... glory, I mean.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Welcome back, and congratulations on your task. Not that I had anything to do with it in any way whatsoever, but I'm very happy with your efforts. Which I know nothing about. But good job nonetheless. Whatever you did.

While you were away, we received orders that I've been praying for. We've located the booster manufacturing facility itself, and it's time to strike at the source. There are some that claim this recent attack by an unnamed pilot on a smuggling convoy was badly timed, and that we now have only a few days before the Cartel decides to move its operation to a new secret location. But then, I don't recall those same people giving any good reason why we should allow even one parcel of drugs to pass into the hands of our citizens.

Nevertheless, fingers have been pointed, and people are quite annoyed at having to rush in. While I don't have the slightest doubts that I made the right decision in sending you to destroy that convoy - NOT sending you to destroy that convoy, I should say, because of course I had nothing to do with it - it may nonetheless be a wise decision on our part to get there first and destroy that manufacturing facility all by ourselves. It will give us a little added glory, just in case someone decides to get clever about that convoy business.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I've had my fill of glory for the time being. Thanks, but no thanks.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The thing you asked me not to do has been ... not done.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm sorry to hear that. I had hoped you would see things my way.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: We certainly do. I'll be back after I've not destroyed the convoy that's not flying through space nearby.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm not doing this. And when I say "not", I mean "not". At all. You understand that, I trust.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Splendid! You've saved lives, you know.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent! I'll see you back here after you've done whatever it is you were going to do that I had nothing to do with in any way whatsoever.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You've heard, I hope, of the Angel Cartel drug smuggling into Minmatar space. No one will ever know how many lives have been destroyed by this ugly scourge, but while we cannot help those poor souls who have already fallen prey to booster abuse, I'm not going to sit by and let the drugs continue spreading to new victims. 

I am aware that not everyone around here shares my sentiments. My superiors feel that it's useless to strike at the dealers and the couriers, that the only way to uproot this problem is to stop it at its source. They say that to do otherwise is a waste of time and money.

And they're right, I'm sure. Of course they're right. So what I am absolutely not going to do is send out a single rogue pilot and tell him to cut off a supply convoy carrying drugs to Minmatar children. Let's be crystal clear on that. I am certainly not asking you to help me out on a secret task to rid us of one clandestine shipment, just one, even if nobody would notice its disappearance anyway. We understand one another, I trust.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Rubin is dead.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: That's a shame. Her uncle will have to make an extra effort to teach her the error of her ways, then.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll help out. It's for the girl's own good.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I can't take part in this. Something stinks.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you. I'm sure the young woman will learn her lesson from this.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent. The girl's uncle assures me that he will take good care of her from now on. Very good care indeed.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I've been contacted by one of the mining harvesters working in the vicinity. It's a private matter, and the poor man is desperate for assistance. His niece, a good-looking but rather quiet woman, lives with him and takes care of their living quarters, but when he got home a few days back, she was gone. After much searching, he discovered that she had been kidnapped by the Angel Cartel, in an operation led by the pirate captain Rubin Sozar.

We need you to go find the girl. Her uncle is beside himself with worry and is willing to give up all his savings for her safe retrieval, along with the destruction of the man who put him through all this grief. It is imperative that you get his niece back to us before going after Rubin Sozar, because if anything goes wrong with the rescue we will need him alive to barter for her return. Needless to say, her uncle's savings will not go to you unless the young woman is back where she belongs, safe and sound.

Okelle Alash has not yet broken under questioning. However, now that his fleet failed to save him, we have reason to believe that his brother Martokar is going to try it. This is the big break we were hoping for. Martokar is the very man we've been after, a brutal criminal who arrived here on the run, having been implicated in kidnappings, slave trade and the murder of CONCORD officers. He hasn't been here long and has already established himself a big player in the booster smuggling business. We need this man taken down.

Martokar is amassing an attack fleet at the moment, and one of the people he tried to recruit has been spotted by our agents in a nearby establishment, ranting about the lousy offer he got. This man is the only chance we'll get at discovering Martokar's precise location, so we need you to retrieve him right away. If we screw this up, Martokar may strike at any time while we're completely unprepared, and good people will die. Obviously, Martokar is going to want to silence this poor fellow before he can reveal anything, so we need to get there first.

However, we mustn't let Martokar think that we've got sensitive information on him, since that'll only make him change his plans and will ruin any advantage we had. We therefore need you to lay waste to the entire location, making it look like our informant perished in the process. Once you've destroyed the place and anyone snooping around, bring the guy back to us.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Martokar is dead, dead, dead.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: ... did you fall into the cloning vat or something?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Once I'm done, there will be nothing left but dust.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm scared! I don't wanna do it!

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. I'll let Duliner Nerhoger know we've got our best pilot on the case.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
It's time to end the reign of Martokar Alash. The informant you brought in gave us all the information we needed, and we now know where the warlord is.

I cannot emphasize enough how important it is that you wipe out not only this man but the entire force you see there and anything else in the vicinity. Before Martokar came here, he was on the verge of being a target for a Republic invasion fleet. Duliner Nerhoger, the chief of intelligence in the Republic Justice Department, has personally contacted my superiors to notify them that if we fail, we can expect repercussions.

That's not to mention the scourge of organized crime, which we know is always trying to get a toehold. Unless we show Martokar and everyone else that we mean business, someone else will simply move in to fill the gap he left. We have to ensure that the only thing remaining in that place are the burnt and wrecked remains of the last criminal who dared oppose us. But at the same time we don't dare bring in a massive fleet, for fear that Martokar get wind of it and take off. We've trusted you this far, and I have complete faith in your abilities to take care of the matter.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great, great, great. Thank you for your services.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
As you may know, Minecore has been launching expeditions into BLC-X0 in order to find more gas cloud sites. We've been pretty successful so far, if I do say so myself. But success breeds the need for more success, and also breeds a certain type of man who expects that success. My superior, Akrada Ubje, is that type of man.

Akrada is one of the few people in Minecore who can deal with the pirates on their own terms. The Angel Cartel have us in a stranglehold, but Akrada is so defiant of everything and everyone that the Angels respect him, and even if it's the grudging respect a predator may show its prey, it's one of the things that has kept them from completely devouring our operations here. Problem is, Akrada expects everyone else to be defiant, showing constant bravery and strength so that the pirates won't think us weak. This means he occasionally demands too much, and the rest of us have to ensure he doesn't push us into something dangerous.

We've recently received word of quite a promising gas cloud. However, we have also heard that Sansha's Nation plans to establish a base there, intending to beat us to the punch. They have put up a scanning sentry there which will call for backup the instant an enemy force approaches. I want you to destroy this sentry, and do it quickly. No matter what Akrada says, we cannot deal with this on our own.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The sentry is dust.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm saddened to hear how unconcerned you are about our safety.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm saddened to hear how unconcerned you are about our safety.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sure, I'll give it a look.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I've got better things to do than shoot out a sentry.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Uh, there's no one there. Probably. I couldn't be bothered to check.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks very much. Don't mention this to Akrada, though.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Splendid. Hopefully the area will now be safe for us to enter.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Unfortunately, the Sansha's Nation isn't so easily deterred. They received backup right after you left, and have now set up a full base in the area. The place is crawling with Sansha's pirates and we desperately need your services again. I can't let this get to Akrada, since he'll go berserk and demand we all fly in there, guns blazing. Anyone who refuses will find themselves out of a job at the very least, which in this part of space is tantamount to death by starvation.

So we need this done on the quiet, like. No major forces, no big deal made, and no bragging afterwards. You simply head back out there, kill everything you see, then silently head back to me for debriefing. I should warn you that if you find yourself in trouble, no one will be able to help you, and I will not admit to knowing anything about your mishaps.

All I wanted was to do my nice desk job in this company, pay my dues to Minecore and the Angel Cartel, and head back home at the end of the harvesting season. Flying out on suicide missions wasn't part of the job description, and neither was having to hire freelance pilots to sneak around behind my boss's back.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The area is clear.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm very disappointed. This means Akrada will want me to go there instead

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm very disappointed. This means Akrada will want me to go there instead.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Don't worry, I'll take care of it.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Find someone else to do your grunt work.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I don't like the look of those Sansha's. I'm leaving.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks very much. I'll go back to ordering my pens according to color, then.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Wonderful! And you'll be happy to hear that I've finished ordering my pens. Would you care for a red one?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
The concept of 'miner's justice' is new to some freelancers here. Have you heard of it? No? It's rather simple, really. Space can be dangerous, and we at the Angel Cartel are charged with keeping the peace, ensuring that people don't step out of line. We don't have the luxury of courts and lawyers, nor the option to hold long and protracted trials, so justice tends to be meted out in swift, decisive doses. It's quite a convenient arrangement for the most part, and the mining harvesters only need to defray the slight cost involved.

Sadly, though, not everyone sees it this way. There are some who feel themselves to be beyond the reach of justice, and who apparently believe they won't have to face the consequences of their rebellious actions. I've received word of a group of harvesters who have been misreporting their earnings and paying only a fraction of what they should, thus swindling the Cartel out of our rightly-earned tribute. Needless to say, this kind of behavior is absolutely unacceptable.

You are to head out, destroy their equipment and ships along with anything else you find, but return the harvesting personnel to us intact. While normally I wouldn't hesitate in demanding their bodies be splattered all over deep space, we need them alive to extract information about any other rogue operations.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: So you've joined the ranks of the insurrection. I hope you've prepared your last will and testament.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Your funeral.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: My justice will be swift and merciless.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't deal with corporate henchmen, sorry.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Well done. For their sake, I hope they were acting alone.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks for your services. Our specialists will now interrogate them.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Here are the harvesters.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm not going after the miners. Do your own dirty work.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We've finished with the harvesters you brought in, and it turns out they weren't just skimming the profits. There is a gas cloud there, a very valuable gas cloud, which they had discovered and were hoping to keep all for themselves.

This isn't some minor act of subterfuge, it's outright betrayal! I cannot express how angry I am at this. Here we are, working day and night to ensure the safety of these people, and for very little pay, I might add, and this is how they treat us. Rest assured, we will make a memorable example of these traitors. Their bodies will be flayed open and their skin will flap in the wind like the bloodied flags of a failed uprising.

As for the gas cloud, since you were the one who brought these miscreants to justice, you're the only one I trust to inspect the cloud and verify whether it's as valuable as they claimed. Head out there, give it a look, and tell me what you saw. I suppose it's possible that the Minmatars will get a little cranky at the fact that you were responsible for the mutilation and death of their kind, but I'm sure they won't do anything drastic about it. Still, I'd appreciate if you also made sure that the area was clear of enemies.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The cloud looks fine. So did the Minmatar forces that ambushed me.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm disappointed. Let's hope you won't end up like those traitors you brought in earlier.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm disappointed. Let's hope you won't end up like those traitors you brought in earlier.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: It'll be a walk in the park, I'm sure.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I can't be a part of this any longer. You need serious therapy.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've got better things to do than look at clouds and wait to be attacked.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Off you go, then.

Still, I'd appreciate if you also made sure that the area was clear of enemies.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I'm sure you had no problems handling them.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You are talking to the last survivor of a vicious, dishonorable assault. I used to soar through this area with the rest of my gang, taking care of business, talking to people who needed a good talking to, maybe knocking them around a bit, keeping things tight and running. I loved my job, and I was good at it.

But then we ran into a bunch of Sansha's, and things went very wrong. They snuck up on us while we were minding our own business, and they murdered every single one of my gangmates. I still have nightmares about those last few seconds, when each one of my communication channels to them was filled with screams, then static. Then nothing at all. The Sansha's left me alive only so that I could crawl back to home and tell the tale, a message that they were coming to push us out of the territory.

We're going to send them a message in return. We don't dare risk total war, though, so we need a freelancer. You are going to head out, find a bunch of Sansha's puppets, and kill them. Bring me back their tags so that I can hang them over my bed like a set of wind chimes; that ought to stop then nightmares for good.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Your gang has been avenged. Here are the tags of the dead.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: They don't belong among the innocent, you fool, and not among the living, either.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You have no understanding of honor.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I will carve out a fitting memorial to your gangmates, written in Sansha's blood.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: You want me to retaliate with a vicious, dishonorable assault of your own. Sorry, but no.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm not going to help you kill innocent victims. I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I'm glad you feel the same about it as I do.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You are talking to the last survivor of a vicious, dishonorable assault. I used to soar through this area with the rest of my gang, taking care of business, talking to people who needed a good talking to, maybe knocking them around a bit, keeping things tight and running. I loved my job, and I was good at it.

But then we ran into a bunch of Sansha's, and things went very wrong. They snuck up on us while we were minding our own business, and they murdered every single one of my gangmates. I still have nightmares about those last few seconds, when each one of my communication channels to them was filled with screams, then static. Then nothing at all. The Sansha's left me alive only so that I could crawl back to home and tell the tale, a message that they were coming to push us out of the territory.

We're going to send them a message in return. We don't dare risk total war, though, so we need a freelancer. You are going to head out, find a bunch of Sansha's puppets, and kill them. Bring me back their tags so that I can hang them over my bed like a set of wind chimes; that ought to stop then nightmares for good.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Thank you. I look forward to the night now.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Abufyr and all his cohorts are dead. Here's what's left of him.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Suit yourself. Abufyr's head won't be the only one on my desk, then.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You have no understanding of honor.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Abufyr's as good as dead.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Clearly, no number of deaths will be enough for you. Get someone else to be your butcher.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've had enough. Go behead Abufyr yourself.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
After you left, I got to thinking. Killing some random gang of Sansha's is good, but it's not enough. All we did was send the message that someone had wanted to kill their grunts. We need more.

As luck would have it, the person reputed to be Sansha's provincial leader in this area, a man named Abufyr Joek, is situated not far from us. If we take him out, along with all his staff and guards, we will be sending a clear message to those brainless drones. They won't dare declare war on us, since they'll have nothing to officially tie the attack to our forces, but they'll know exactly who was responsible. Abufyr probably gave permission for his troops to roam around and viciously murder anyone they met, and even if he didn't he's still the nominal figurehead for them, so his death will be a statement. 

Kill everyone you see at that place, then bring me back Abufyr's head, and we'll show Sansha's Nation what happens when you get the stupid, stupid idea to attack the Angel Cartel. Don't worry about special storage, either, just put it in your cargo hold like everything else. We want it to be good and ripe before we vacuum-seal it to send off to the Sansha.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Marvelous. And he looks so surprised, too.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
This one is personal. I haven't usually bothered too much about Sansha's Nation; they're here, and we're going to kick them out eventually, but until now they haven't been worth the effort. That's all changed. They have taken my sister.

Understand, this is one of very few people in the world who means anything to me. We grew up together, and since I was older by a few years, I was the protector. She isn't too clever, dear Nokana, but she always meant well, and all the times I had to pull her out of trouble were paid for a thousand times over by the times she stood by me when no one else would. When I got this job as an Angel Cartel agent, she demanded that she be employed here as well so that she could keep an eye on me. It's risky business sometimes, being an agent for the pirates, and Nokana wouldn't let me do it alone.

But now it's all gone wrong. Nokana apparently heard of a group of Sansha's who had it in for me, and went to try and negotiate with them. She's wonderful, my sister, but she's no diplomat, and they ended up kidnapping her. If my bosses find out about her meddling they'll fire both of us, so I need you to go in, get her, and return her to me before anyone else finds out. I hear they're keeping her in a slave pen, the barbarians!

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Nokana's back, unharmed.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I hope you don't have brothers or sisters of your own.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I hope you don't have brothers or sisters of your own.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll save her from the clutches of evil, no problem.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I've got better things to do than hunt down wayward siblings.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I really can't be bothered to find her.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I have full confidence in you. Remember, this is family.

I hear they're keeping her in a slave pen, the barbarians!

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Thank you so much.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Now that Nokana is safe, I've decided it's too much of a risk to let her stay here. Wanting to protect me is good and fine, and exactly what I'd expect from her, but she's going to end up getting both of us into serious trouble, and if anything happened to her I would never forgive myself. Not to mention that I'd have to tell our parents, and they'd have my hide.

I would like you to take her back to my parents' place in Cartel space. I know this is a little outside the realm of your usual work, to be escorting someone home like a chaperon, but I'd really appreciate it. You did a good job in bringing Nokana back, and I'm sure you're as eager as I am to ensure that she doesn't cost us any more time and effort.

I'll arrange matters here, talk to her superiors and give them some reasonable explanation. A friend of mine will meet Nokana at the landing point, so once you've docked safe and sound, let me know and we'll take care of the rest.

Just don't let her convince you to turn around or do anything silly. Head straight home with her. And for heaven's sake, don't tell her anything about this conversation. I'll take care of that as well.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Nokana is back where she belongs.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: That is my little sister you're talking about, you ogre!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm disappointed. I had hoped you would put this sensitive matter above your usual routine of murder and carnage.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Don't worry. I'll take good care of her.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm not a babysitter. Find someone else.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Nokana and I are eloping. We're in love, and wanted you to be the first to know. I'm taking her to my quarters instead.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. I trust you completely.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I'm very glad to hear that. Now I can get back to business with a clear conscience.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've run into a little trouble. Word has spread that Okelle Alash is being held captive, and his legion is going absolutely insane. Apparently it's all right for them to terrorize innocent citizens, but not for us to start hitting back. They're tearing through the constellation, firing at everything in sight and demanding that Okelle be returned to them in one piece.

This, unfortunately, is no longer an option, not unless they have a surgeon on their team who specializes in reattaching fingers. We will have to fight them. Their fleet is disorganized as you'd expect pirates to be, but nonetheless they have a small scouting party that flies ahead and coordinates the primary fleet. You have to take out the scouting party first, so that the primary fleet will be left blinded and confused. Once you're done with that, report to me and we'll see if we can use you in taking care of the remnants of Okelle's fleet.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm interested.  Give me more details.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Congratulations, you've just proven yourself as a competent mercenary fighter pilot.  Now that you've completed this task, I suggest you look for more {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} agents in {[location]agentRegionID.name} and surrounding regions.  I have no more work for you, but I'm sure you'll find some others from my corporation who do.  If all else fails, you could always work for the other {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} corporations, they have their own agents which hand out jobs as well.  Good luck in your travels, friend.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Right now I'm looking for {[item]objectiveTypeID.quantityName, quantity=objectiveQuantity}. These tags have been implanted into certain pirates which infest {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} space, which they use to identify each other with. To acquire them you will most likely have to kill them, or buy them off someone who did exactly that. I don't really care either way, as long as they have been taken care of I'm satisfied.

This might not be the very best way to confirm deaths, but we've been quite successful in the past using this method. Forgeries are almost non-existent, as each tag costs more to manufacture than it's worth on the bounty market. Not only that but we can usually tell a fake apart from a genuine pirate tag. And they have remarkable survivability, usually found in the charred wreckage of the pirate ships despite everything else, including the pirate's corpse, having been completely vaporized.

You can find the pirates carrying the {[item]objectiveTypeID.name} in many places, but I'd first check the asteroid belts in the surrounding systems as attacking defenseless miners is their favorite past-time. Good luck, and have fun.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We ran Okelle's hard drive through disinfection and decryption, and we got lucky! Sometimes these things are set to self-destruct after unauthorized access, or they've been planted and are full of things that attempt to infect our reader programs the instant we start picking them apart. I'd have thought that our data extraction people would be professional enough not to hook the darn things right up to our systems, but sometimes they get a little overzealous. It took us a month to clear out the last infection we got.

At any rate, we now know Okelle's whereabouts. Remember that he's undoubtedly aware that we're after him, and that we intend to use him as a bartering chip to lure his brother out of hiding, so he's not going to come quietly. Try not to hang around, either, or he'll just escape. Go in there, kill any backup forces you see, and bring Okelle back to us alive.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I have a problem. It's about my son, Torin. He recently graduated from the academy, and I was giving him a tour of {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} in his brand-new Kestrel. We were going to have such a wonderful time celebrating his achievement when we were set upon by rogue drones. A battle ensued, which eventually I won, but when I looked for Torin his ship was a smoking hulk. He has very little practical experience with combat, despite graduating in the top 5 percentile of his class. However, his capsule was nowhere to be found: I think some of the drones must have captured his pod and fled before I noticed them. If he had died, my sensors would have registered the destruction of his pod, but they found nothing.

I want my son back, or at least vengeance on whoever is responsible for his death. I'll be out searching myself, but for each moment that passes...

I just want to find him and destroy those drones before they attack anyone else.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I am...truly grateful for your assistance. I've detected a number of anomalies in this system that may indicate the presence of rogue drones. I've passed by a number of them and destroyed numerous drones, but have found no hive yet; perhaps you will have better luck. I will upload the coordinates of one of the reconnaissance points to the mission details in your Opportunity interface. Please take a look and see if you can find a drone hive. If you do, destroy it; we must ensure the safety of the people in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} above all else.

But I am certain you have other obligations at the moment, so I will leave you now to your own business. Enjoy your reward ― you have definitely earned it!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I was assigned the task of finding a missing scientist. His name is Lazron Kamon. I think the crazy old coot got bored with life and took a trip out the airlock, but who knows. I'm getting fed up with these find-a-needle-in-a-haystack jobs to be honest.

Anyway, if you ever stumble across this guy, let me know, k?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Actually, you were wrong.  I DID find him.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll find him. Read mission details in Opportunities first.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Look buddy, I have no idea where he is.  I've looked everywhere ... so just give it up ok?  You won't find him.

messages.mission.briefing.text: If you have managed to find Lazron Kamon, then return him to {[character]agentID.name}.  Do not bother looking unless you have some idea of his whereabouts, he could be anywhere.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Well I'll be ... you found the SOB!  My boss will be pleased, maybe I'll even get a promotion ... Anyway, here's your dough as I promised.  Take care.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I will do as you ask, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent work, {[character]player.name}!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I have a very special mission for you today, {[character]player.name}. A high-ranked Overseer of a secret {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} compound in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} has requested items of ours that must be delivered to him A.S.A.P. This job must be done in complete secrecy; we do not want the contents of this delivery to fall into the wrong hands. As a precautionary measure, we have set up an explosive mechanism inside the cargo containers that will trigger should anyone attempt to tamper with them.

I trust you on this, {[character]player.name}. Be very discreet and, at any cost, avoid confrontation with hostiles en route to your destination. Make haste!

As a precautionary measure, we have set up an explosive mechanism inside the cargo containers that will trigger should anyone attempt to tamper with them.

I trust you on this, {[character]player.name}. Be very discreet and, at any cost, avoid confrontation with hostiles en route to your destination. Make haste!

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Please make this delivery your first priority, {[character]player.name}. It must go smoothly and quickly.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Pirates have set up a blockade near a hidden stargate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and are swarming over any passersby, which are mostly merchants and civilians.  Pirates tend to create these temporary blockades at ill-defended stargates, usually ones which have been set up by civilians and are not guarded by our forces.  But we still have an obligation to protect the citizens of {[location]agentConstellationID.name}.  Therefore I want you, {[character]player.name}, to fly to the stargate and eliminate the illegal blockade.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I have cleared the blockade as you requested, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Oh comon now, it isn't that hard.  Ah well, I'll find someone else to finish the job then.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
A DED strike-force has set up a blockade near a hidden stargate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and are swarming over any passersby, which are mostly smugglers loyal to {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name}. DED tend to create these temporary blockades at ill-defended stargates, to catch some of our employees which have broken the law within 'Empire' space. And we tend to send in hired guns to disperse the pigs.

Yes you guessed it, I want you, {[character]player.name}, to take care of this business.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's the data you need.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I do wish you people wouldn't put your own needs first all the time.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: So long as it doesn't have to be organic, I'm your man.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'd much rather pay the place an unofficial visit. Thanks, but no thanks.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Very good. Don't dally there, mind.

messages.mission.briefing.text: I'm glad to see you. Things are heating up. You may be aware that we've been hunting the infamous Thukker warlord named Martokar Alash. He's proved quite difficult to provoke out of hiding, but we've finally been given a good lead. Unfortunately it's not to him, but to his brother, Okelle Alash. I don't know if our capturing Okelle will drive Martokar out of hiding, but at the very least it will give him one more thing to worry about. Okelle is a bit of a wild one. He's reportedly done just about every drug in existence, goes through a girlfriend a month and ends up leaving them at that harem of his, has built up a reputation for being near-suicidal in battle, and all in all lives the definite pirate lifestyle. You should be aware that once you start hunting him, though, he may be a little more cautious. He's only foolhardy when he's the one who chooses the battlefield, and this time we're aiming to catch him with his pants down. He'll probably manage to escape before you reach his harem, so if you don't find him there, I want you to bring back something he left that'll allow us to determine his whereabouts. It's a fairly well hidden place, so you'll have to search hard.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thanks. I hope you didn't pick up anything else at that place.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The container you delivered to me was completely empty! Those damned Serpentis must have snatched the documents as you were loading the container aboard your ship.

I'm putting the blame for this mess squarely on your back. You need to solve this, {[character]player.name}! If my superiors find out the documents have been lost, we can expect some heads to roll ... your head, to be precise. Find the documents and bring them to me straight away. They cannot have gotten very far; I'm actually pretty sure they're in this very system.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
While the royal family does not officially condone the fighting between Methros and Arachnan, they do not see it as any major threat to their claim to power in this region. To that end they are willing to let it continue as the infighting is bringing a much needed economic boost to the region.

With this in mind, it is our duty to monitor the conflict and inform the Emperor and his council should either of the parties engage in business detrimental to the empire.

We have a mission suited to your talents my friend. Lord Methros and Arachnan have secret outposts inside their sphere of influence in Araz, from where they conduct various operations. We are of course aware of these outposts, as the Emperor Family has ears and eyes in all corners of the Empire, figuratively speaking of course. I want you to make an unannounced visit to these outposts and retrieve an encrypted data burst located inside them.

I want you to start with Lord Methros' outpost. I'll give you a bookmark to it's exact location, of course. I will inform his guards of your visit as soon as you arrive, since doing it any earlier would compromise your mission.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I have the Encrypted Data Burst, but I have some disturbing news as well ...

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll get that data chip back here in no time.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: The presence of the Blood Raiders is disturbing news, I have another assignment for you already if you feel up to the job?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Do this for me and you will go far within the Amarr Empire.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Do you have any work for a servant of the Empire?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You would leave the poor damsel to her fate?  How cruel.  You've failed me today, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'll just have to find someone else then.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll get her back, I promise.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I give up.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good to hear.  Just keep a lookout for this Kruul character, he's known for being quite the scoundrel.

messages.mission.briefing.text: It has come to my attention that one of our employee's daughters has gone missing.  She was last spotted in a disreputable nightclub in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and we're afraid she's been forced into slave labor, or even prostitution.  We request that you find her immediately and bring her safe and sound back to her family.  I will give you the coordinates of this nightclub, I believe it is called 'Kruul's Pleasure Hub', and I expect you to take care of the rest.  Good luck.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I need a shipment of Synthetic Oil delivered to this station as soon as possible. It's currently stored in one of our warehouses in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}; I'll give you the coordinates, of course. Just warp to our outpost, navigate to the warehouse, and pick up the shipment, and then return it to {[location]agentStationID.name}. Simple, ain't it?

Just make sure you keep a lookout for any suspicious activity. You can't be too careful these days.

These tags can be acquired only by removing them from their dead body. I'm an expert on appraising tags, so don't even try to trick me with forgeries. If you have the genuine stuff, then I'll pay for it. And you'll earn some good will with {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} at the same time. A win-win situation if you ask me.

I'm currently on the lookout for {[item]objectiveTypeID.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I'd like you to do some reconnaissance for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}, my friend. Our operatives in an outpost within {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} have requested a convoy of goods, through some pretty hostile territory. There are a few routes we could take to reach the destination, and you're going to help us find the safest route.

All I need you to do is scout ahead and see if there are any pirates, rogue drones or dangerous terrain. Report your findings to me. I'll upload a bookmark to the first area into your NeoCom.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: So where's my next assignment?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I have the second location for you to scout for us, I will upload it into your NeoCom shortly. We've had reports that the area has been claimed by some obscure mining corporation, who've hired mercenaries to defend their assets. It's in a pretty remote area in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, so don't expect the local security forces to back you up if you get confronted by the mercs.

Your job is to go in there, fly to the rendezvous point and report what you find back to us. If the mercs leave you alone, and you don't find any pirates roaming around there, then we've found our safe route.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Hmm.  So the acceleration gate is in working order, but there's nasty radiation covering the entire area. messages.mission.briefing.text:
The next area you'll be scouting is known to be filled with hazardous, radioactive materials. It used to be a waste dump for {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle}, but it also contains no mineral wealth at all so it's not a popular attraction for gold diggers fortunately.

I know there is still an acceleration gate inside the area and I want you to make sure it's still functioning and doesn't send you straight into something deadly. It's a dangerous job, but I'm not paying you for garbage hauling now am I. Get to it and report back to me with your findings!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I have the second location for you to scout for us, I will upload it into your NeoCom shortly. We've had reports that the area has been claimed by some obscure mining corporation, who've hired mercenaries to defend their assets. It's in a pretty remote area in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, so don't expect the local security forces to back you up if you get confronted by the mercs.

Your job is to go in there, fly to the rendezvous point and report what you find back to us. If the mercs leave you alone, and you don't find any pirates roaming around there, then we've found our safe route.

messages.mission.briefing.text: I want you to escort a convoy of trade goods heading out to our headquarters. It's just a formality, but a necessary one nonetheless. You'll find a bookmark to their current location in your NeoCom.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Rogue drones looting trade convoys? Might be that there's a new hive nearby, I suppose, or maybe it's someone sinister pulling their strings. Who knows? Regardless, you did good ― can't blame you for the convoy's destruction. It was probably destroyed before you set out from the station. Take your reward, you've earned it.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Hm. Guess I was wrong about you.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: In this mission you must find and destroy a structure in space, the repair station.  It will not appear in your overview unless you have 'Large Collidable Structure' selected in your overview settings.  Make sure that your settings are correctly configured, finding structures without using the overview is not always easy.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Oh, and also be on the lookout for the mercenary gang that owns the repair station. I doubt they'll look too kindly upon your attacking their precious structure.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've discovered a small repair station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. By itself, this station is no issue, but when our patrols scanned the site they detected pirates in the area. This particular repair station is owned by a local mercenary gang that allows felonious individuals to dock there, and they are therefore aiding and abetting known criminals.

I would like you to do us all a favor and remove this repair station from existence. It's not registered in the government's official database and it's being used to break the law ― that is all the information I need to authorize decisive action against it. It may be guarded, so be careful.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent! That repair station will aid pirates and outlaws no more.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Hm. Guess I was wrong about you.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've discovered a small repair station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} which by itself is no issue, but when our patrols scanned the site they detected a gang of our rivals in the area. This particular repair station is owned by a local mercenary corporation, which obviously allows our enemies to operate it and are therefore just asking for retribution.

I would like you to do us all a favor and remove this repair station from existence. It's not registered in our database and this mercenary corporation is late on their tribute, which gives us a perfectly valid reason to obliterate them.

Be on your way now.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent, that repair station should no longer be of any use to our enemies.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Oh and be on the lookout for the mercenary gang that owns the repair outpost, I doubt they will look kindly upon you attacking their precious structure.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've discovered a small repair station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. By itself, this station is no issue, but when our patrols scanned the site they detected pirates in the area. This particular repair station is owned by a local mercenary gang that allows felonious individuals to dock there, and they are therefore aiding and abetting known criminals.

I would like you to do us all a favor and remove this repair station from existence. It's not registered in the government's official database and it's being used to break the law ― that is all the information I need to authorize decisive action against it. It may be guarded, so be careful.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent! That repair station will aid pirates and outlaws no more.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Hmph. I'd heard you were a force to be reckoned with. Just goes to show you can't believe everything you hear.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Oh, and also be on the lookout for the mercenary gang that owns the repair station. I doubt they'll look too kindly upon your attacking their precious structure.

messages.mission.briefing.text: We have reports of terrorists wreaking havoc in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Our convoys have been attacked, as well as some outlying outposts; they seem to be intent on causing as much damage as possible. I'd like you to take care of them as quickly as possible. And be aware that they may not all be gathered together when you arrive... if so, you will be able to pick them off as they warp in to the rendezvous point.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I knew I could count on you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I see.  Well, perhaps you will be of some use next time.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
One of our patrol teams noticed a suspicious looking craft on its system scanner. I'd like you to investigate the matter. If the craft is hostile, destroy it. Report back to me with your findings.

I'll supply you with a bookmark to its approximate location, just be wary of any other hostile activity in the area. I expect a swift return {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I'm truly sorry, {[character]player.name}.  We'll launch an inquiry into why the surveillance team failed to notice any sign of a set up.  The responsible parties will be punished.  I just hope the mission reward soothes your anger.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Our surveillance teams have discovered a disturbance near some old ruins in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.  I'd like you to take a look, it's awfully close to one of our outposts.  Report your findings to me.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I'm sorry that you got ambushed, {[character]player.name}.  You have my regrets.  I'll have someone take care of any ships or sentries that you left behind.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I need someone to safely transport these Data Sheets. They contain various files that relate to matters of national security — not something we can entrust to anyone less than a capsuleer.

Once you have delivered them, contact me and let me know you've completed the mission. I'll have something else ready for you by the time you get back.

Don't forget to put the Data Sheets in your cargohold before you set off!

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Well done, {[character]player.name}. Let me know when you're ready to begin your next assignment. I've found a job you could profit and learn from at the same time.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: You've done well, {[character]player.name}. You should enroll in other training courses and learn as much as you can before making any long-term plans.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Since you seem to have forgotten, I asked you to bring me a frigate, {[character]player.name}. I've given you a whole week and there is still no word of your progress. I'm afraid I'm going to have to give the job to someone else. A word of advice for the future; take your obligations seriously, people don't like to be let down.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Congratulations, {[character]player.name}! With the successful production of that Burst you've proven that you have what it takes. I hate to see you go, but you have mastered all the challenges I have for you.

There are plenty of mining agents out there who would be happy to employ someone like you who can get the job done. You can find them in the Agency Mining Agents. Or, if you are interested in broadening your skills into other areas you can start a conversation with any of the other career agents here in station.

Best of luck in the future, my friend. Stick with the Republic and you'll do well.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You've done a great job so far, mastering the intricacies of industry - mining, reprocessing, manufacturing, and hauling. All while murdering everyone who stands in your way. You're now ready for your final assignment.

You're going to bring me a full-fledged frigate. I'll give you a blueprint copy with more than enough runs for this task. If you choose to use it, finding the resources is up to you. But time is money, and however you choose to acquire the ship is fine by me.

Good luck!

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I've given you a whole week to think about my job offer, {[character]player.name}. I can only assume your lack of commitment means you aren't interested. I'm going to have to give the job to someone else I'm afraid.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Turns out one of my production assistants was a spy for the enemy. He's gone into hiding, so I need you to draw him out.

You'll act as a decoy, mining until enemy forces turn up. Destroy them and bring the spy back to me. You may keep whatever ore you find out there.

Make sure you use a mining laser, so they'll notice you out there.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Praise the Republic! Well done! And now, I'm sad to say, I have just one more task for you.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The Black Box you retrieved indicates that the Angel Cartel has built a surveillance facility nearby, using it to launch attacks on convoys from the {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}.

You need to take out the outpost and any vessels defending it. Once the area is clear, use the Civilian Data Analyzer I'm giving you to hack the data storage device in the area. Bring back whatever it contains.

I've given you a whole week and there is still no word of your progress. I'm afraid I'm going to have to give the job to someone else. A word of advice for the future; take your obligations seriously, people don't like to be let down.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Amazing work, {[character]player.name}. With the destruction of that outpost we now have time to go over the evidence and prepare for any upcoming attacks.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I'll get right down to it then. I am {[character]agentID.name}, an operative of C.E.R.N., a corporation with strong ties with CONCORD. We oversee a part of their technological research and development, that's all I can tell you. My role within the corporation is confidential, but I am here on official business.

The problem we currently face is in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We set up a number of particle accelerators there, for various testing and research purposes, which we abandoned a few years ago. We stripped them of everything we needed, but apparently one of them was still in a condition to continue functioning.

A few weeks ago we were informed that someone, or rather something, had managed to override the system lock we placed on one of the particle accelerators and turn it back on. The problem is whoever did this doesn't seem to have a clue of the dangers involved in running these things, the type of particle accelerator involved has instruments inside which can in theory create energy in enormous quantities. The catch is that once the energy level reaches a certain point, the operation becomes extremely unstable and liable to cause a chain reaction resulting in an explosion of catastrophic proportion, and cause conditions to arise which may result in the formation of a miniature black hole. The latest reports indicate that the particle accelerator has become so unstable it could blow at any minute.

The last transmissions we heard from their leader indicated that they had found a strange object which was draining energy from the accelerator. It appears that this object is causing the dangerous energy bursts which we are afraid may cause the conditions necessary for the formation of the black hole. If you were to remove this object, then we expect the particle accelerator to quickly defuse as its capacitor has already drained and relies on external energy output managed by this object.

I would however advise you to bring along some friends, the gate leading to the site in question is only configured to work with small frigates which may be poorly equipped to deal with the situation by themselves. A squadron of them however ...

We set up a number of particle accelerators there, for various testing and research purposes, which we abandoned a few years ago. We stripped them of everything we needed, but apparently one of them was still in a condition to continue functioning.

A few weeks ago we were informed that someone, or rather something, had managed to override the system lock we placed on one of the particle accelerators and turn it back on. The problem is whoever did this doesn't seem to have a clue of the dangers involved in running these things, the type of particle accelerator involved has instruments inside which can in theory create energy in enormous quantities. If your shields and armor are depleted and you're close to taking hull damage, warp out immediately. You can either dock at a nearby station and pay its repair shop to fix your ship, or you can use an armor repairer module while in space.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
The State is grateful for your service, {[character]player.name}. Thanks to your combat expertise we've got one less scumbag pirate boss to worry about.

If you would like to further your career in enforcement, there are Agents hiring across the cluster. I've heard the Sister's of EVE are looking for capable pilots, check out The Blood-Stained Stars for more information. If you'd rather broaden your skill set instead, you could start a conversation with any of the other Career Agents in this station.

Thanks again for everything, and good luck out there!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
{[character]player.name}, war never stops, and we need to stoke it with raw materials. I want you to go mine some Veldspar ore for me.

Remember to fit a mining module to your ship before you go, and keep in mind that you might have to make more than one trip before you report back to me.

To make it clear, I want you to mine at least some ore from the location I've uploaded for you.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Well done, my friend. I may have another task for you.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There is one other thing our security forces need before they are fully prepared for the coming battle with these insufferable pirates.

Our forces are suffering a shortage of afterburners for their frigate contingents, and the resulting lack of speed is costing them dearly. I need two 1MN Afterburner I modules from you - buy them, build them, or loot them from the cooling wreckage of other ships. I won't ask questions.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: I needed you to acquire those afterburners quickly, {[character]player.name}. I've given you a whole week and there is still no word of your progress. I'm afraid I'm going to have to give the job to someone else. A word of advice for the future; take your obligations seriously, people don't like to be let down.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Thank you, {[character]player.name}! There was already mounting pressure on our financiers to delegate us more resources, but this will surely guarantee that we get what we need.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I've given you a whole week to think about my job offer, {[character]player.name}. I can only assume your lack of commitment means you aren't interested. I'm going to have to give the job to someone else I'm afraid. The window of opportunity to fix our funding problems is passing us by.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Any industrial mogul worth their salt knows how to fight for their bounty.

I'm sending you to mine in an area infested with Rogue Drones. Let's see if you can survive the trip and bring me the processed goods.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: You've done well, {[character]player.name}. You should enroll in other training courses and learn as much as you can before making any long-term plans.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Well done, {[character]player.name}. Here is your Wreathe, as promised; use it well. You've completed all my tasks and shown yourself to be a savvy entrepreneur. There is an entire cluster filled with opportunities for someone like you.

To find other agents you can just check the Agency, Distribution Agents might be of interest to you. Or if you want to broaden your skill set you can reach out to the other Career Agents here in this station.

Whichever future business endeavors you decide to pursue, good luck!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
A transport ship carrying sensitive cargo has been destroyed by pirates in the area. I'm giving you a Civilian Salvager module so you can go in, use it on the ship's wreckage, and extract anything of use from their databanks. Once you have that Black Box, return it to me.

Also, there may be some hostiles still lingering around too, so be ready for combat, {[character]player.name}. If you're successful, I may reward you with a brand new mining frigate.

I need someone to safely transport these Data Sheets. They contain various files that relate to matters of national security — not something we can entrust to anyone less than a capsuleer.

Once you have delivered them, contact me and let me know you've completed the mission. I'll have something else ready for you by the time you get back.

Don't forget to put the Data Sheets in your cargohold before you set off!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Well, lemme tell you: A warlord who's been visiting my people in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} station for a while now has a thing for long-limb roes, and I need to get some over there for him. This man is very important and very dangerous, {[character]player.name}, and I want him on my good side, so let's make every effort to get his needs fulfilled.

Can you help me out?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Alright, delivery completed. You mentioned payment?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I can help you out, sure. I can't do it for free, though.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Do I look like a putz? Of course I'll pay you. Just get the stuff over there as fast as you can.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I do, yeah, and I am… depending on what you need.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Deliver 5 cases of long-limb roes to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}  station.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Fantastic. Your ISK has been deposited to your account. And don't worry, my friend, I won't forget you when I rise to higher places.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
To complete this mission, you will require a ship with a hacking module online, as well as an available cargo capacity of at least 2,000 m3 volume (and preferably 6,000 m3).

I recently learned that a manufacturer for the Imperial Navy has taken over a complex in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, where they build components for their slave transports. I want you to defeat whatever guards or defenses they've put in place and bring back the freight containers they've got stored there. This isn't as simple as it sounds, of course.

I understand that the Amarr, fearing an action just such as the one I'm proposing, have booby-trapping these cargo containers: You'll need to hack the floating containers to get the secure containers inside, and the outer containers will no doubt detonate if you fail to hack them properly. There may be other decoy containers in the compound, too ― you'll need to find the ones with the secure containers inside.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes, my friend, you have. I have a proposal that could make us both a great deal of ISK, as well as inconvenience the Imperial Navy. How does that sound?

I recently learned that a manufacturer for the Imperial Navy has taken over a complex in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} ― yes, the sheer audacity, I know! ― where they build components for Bestowers, which as you know are their favored slave transports. By going in there and destroying the outpost, we can set their production well back and reduce the efficacy of their entire imperial slave transport apparatus; further, by taking their finished ship's components and modifying them for our own use, we can gain valuable help in advancing our own interests.

I want you to go into that complex, defeat whatever guards or defenses they've put in place, and bring back the freight containers they've got stored there. This isn't as simple as it sounds, of course, and that's why I need someone with your skills and resources: The whole deadspace complex will be heavily guarded, without a doubt … and it gets more complicated than that.

I understand that the Amarr, fearing an action just such as the one I'm proposing, have booby-trapping these cargo containers: You'll need to hack the floating containers to get the secure containers inside, and the outer containers will no doubt detonate if you fail to hack them properly. There may be other decoy containers in the compound, too ― you'll need to find the ones with the secure containers inside.

To complete this mission, you will require a ship with a hacking module online, as well as a cargo capacity of at least 2,000 m3 volume (and preferably one with a capacity of 6,000 m3).

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Amarr manufacturer's complex is destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}. Victory is ours.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Good thinking. I mean, the whole Amarr slavery problem will surely take care of itself, right!?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Do you think I'd have asked you if I had the whole navy fleet at my beck and call...!!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I will see every one of those slaver swine die a fiery death.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sounds awfully dangerous. Hm. No, this sounds like a job for the navy, backed by their demolitions experts.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Sorry, I can't finish this job for you.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I see we're of the same mind. Excellent. Be careful out there.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Well, well ... seems like I've arrived right on time.

Whatever your reasons, you did not clear out the Bestower manufacturing outpost in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The Amarrians have moved elsewhere now, it seems, and taken our resources with them.

Well done, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent news, {[character]player.name}. Thank goodness you arrived when you did.

From there, they've been supplying certain radical Caldari military pseudo-corporations, and maybe even the Guristas themselves.

I want you to go defeat whatever guards or defenses they've put in place and bring back the freight containers they've got stored there. This isn't as simple as it sounds, of course, and that's why I need someone with your skills and resources: For sure the whole deadspace complex will be heavily guarded, but it's more complicated than that.

These Caldari are known for booby-trapping their cargo containers: You'll need to hack the floating containers to get the secure containers inside, and the outer containers will no doubt detonate if you fail to hack them properly. There may be other decoy containers in the compound, too ― you'll need to find the ones with the secure containers inside.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I have a proposal that could make us both a great deal of ISK, as well as throw a wrench into the gears of the Caldari military-economic infrastructure. How does that sound? Very good, I'd say.

I recently learned that Caldari Steel, one of the biggest producers of munitions and hybrid weaponry out there, has taken over a complex in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Like most Caldari corporations, they mistreat their workers and destroy moons and planets at an astonishing rate in order to maximize their profit ― and, in this case, contribute directly to the steady increase of Caldari military power. Obviously, it is the duty of people like us to stop them however we can, as I'm sure you'll agree. But in this case we have even more impetus to act: I have it on good authority that this outpost of theirs has been supplying certain radical Caldari military pseudo-corporations, and maybe even the Guristas themselves.

{[character]player.name}, I want you to go into that complex, defeat whatever guards or defenses they've put in place, and bring back the freight containers they've got stored there. This isn't as simple as it sounds, of course, and that's why I need someone with your skills and resources: For sure the whole deadspace complex will be heavily guarded, but it's more complicated than that.

I guess the guards these Caldari Steel people have hired are known for booby-trapping their cargo containers: You'll need to hack the floating containers to get the secure containers inside, and the outer containers will no doubt detonate if you fail to hack them properly. There may be other decoy containers in the compound, too ― you'll need to find the ones with the secure containers inside.

To complete this mission, you will require a ship with a hacking module online, as well as a cargo capacity of at least 2,000 m3 volume (and preferably one with a capacity of 6,000 m3).

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Caldari Steel storage complex is destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}. And not a moment too soon.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I see. Take the job, then quit. You don't feel the same way about these blackhearted fiends as I do, I guess.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Where there's a will, there's a way. Surely someone who shares my views will come along. Good day.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Those capitalist pigs! Selling weapons illegally to the Guristas? They must be stopped!

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sounds pretty damned risky. No, I don't think you can pay me enough for this one.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've changed my mind. Sorry, I can't do this job.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I see we're of the same mind. I'm glad of that. Hey, be careful out there.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Fortunate...? What do you mean, exactly?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
{[character]player.name},

I guess you couldn‘t be bothered to clean out those cultists in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} after all. They‘ve disappeared, and all that beautiful loot with them.

Nice work.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent news, my friend. One more blow struck for democracy!

These “cultists” are really just a bunch of freebooters who've been storing all of their loot in this outpost, presumably until they can haul the stuff away to sell.

Head on out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and recover the freight containers, and I'll give you a hefty reward. This isn't as simple as it sounds, of course: You'll need to hack the floating containers to get the secure containers inside, and the outer containers will no doubt detonate if you fail to hack them properly. There may be other decoy containers in the compound, too ― you'll need to find the ones with the secure containers inside.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I have a proposal that could make us both a great deal of ISK. How does that sound? Now, what I am about to say should remain between you and me, {[character]player.name}. I trust you can agree to that? Good.

According to some intelligence I've just received, one of these bizarre Intaki cults that have been cropping up so much among the Gallente lately has just inhabited a complex in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. These cultists are more than they appear, though: They're really just a bunch of freebooters, apparently, who've been using their cult as a cover while raiding and looting all sorts of low-sec settlements. They're storing all of this loot in their outpost, presumably until they can fill a freighter and haul the stuff away to sell.

Well, I think you must know where I'm headed with this… I want you to head on out to that system and recover the freight containers for me; do that and I'll give you a hefty reward. This isn't as simple as it sounds, of course, and that's why I need someone with your skills and resources: For sure the whole deadspace complex will be heavily guarded, but it's more complicated than that.

I guess these “cultists” are known for booby-trapping things like asteroids and cargo containers, then picking up the scraps after some unsuspecting sap blows one up: You'll need to hack the floating containers to get the secure containers inside, and the outer containers will no doubt detonate if you fail to hack them properly. There may be other decoy containers in the compound, too ― you'll need to find the ones with the secure containers inside.

To complete this mission, you will require a ship with a hacking module online, as well as a cargo capacity of at least 2,000 m3 volume (and preferably one with a capacity of 6,000 m3).

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Intaki “cult” is no more, and I have what you asked for.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I see. Take a job, then quit. Your work ethic needs some polishing, I fear.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Hey, suit yourself. I'm sure I can find someone else with a little more enterprise ― and maybe a little more courage.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Hey, ISK equals double un-bad. Count me in.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Like the Caldari, the Intaki were once subjugated by the Gallenteans; some remain part of the Federation, but others long ago departed en masse to form the Intaki Syndicate, an independent state on the borders of the Gallente Federation. This “Syndicate” is not overtly political in any real sense ― each member station enjoys complete autonomy ― but the Intaki share economic information and generally help each other, for instance banding together when necessary in their common defense.

In reality, the Syndicate is a haven for various undesirable elements of society, yet without being too rough and tough. It has long fostered the role of mediator between merchants from the empires and the outer regions, which makes trading with Syndicate space quite brisk, and the Intaki are generally known as a highly individualistic, spiritual people.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sounds pretty risky. Nah, I don't think you can pay me enough from the looks of you.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've changed my mind ― sorry, but I'm not much interested in finishing this job.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: That's what I like to hear, {[character]player.name}. That's what I like to hear.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Fortunate...? What do you mean, exactly?

I'm told these raiders have a supply outpost in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}; I want you to head out there and recover the freight containers. This isn't a simple job, though, and that's why I need someone with your skills and resources to do it.

First off, I'm sure the compound, built in a deadspace complex, will be heavily guarded. Also, the Minmatar are known for booby-trapping their structures and containers; you'll need to hack the floating containers to get the secure containers inside, and the outer containers will no doubt detonate if you fail to hack them properly. There may be other decoy containers in the compound, too ― you'll need to find the ones with the secure containers inside.

(Of course, the Kameiras who failed to guard these assets have been properly dealt with.) Now, I don't like the implications of this activity any more than you do, so I want it dealt with, and dealt with yesterday. You get me?

Alright, I'm told these Minmatar raiders have a supply outpost in and around the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system; I want you to head out there and recover the freight containers ― we can use that stuff just as well as they can. This isn't a simple job, though, and that's why I need someone with your skills and resources to do it.
