messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The complex is cleared of resistance, and I have your cargo here.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I see. Take a job, then quit. Your work ethic needs some polishing, I fear.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Not all of a capsuleer's work need involve violence, {[character]player.name}. You ought to broaden your horizons, perhaps.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I've about had enough of these bloody-minded Minmatar. Forget enslaving them ― I say we just eradicate the whole lot. I'm in.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Kameiras are elite foot soldiers originally drawn from among the Minmatar slaves by the Amarr Empire. Raised from birth to become hardened, highly disciplined and emotionless soldiers, they are savage and ruthless in personal combat. They serve the Empire, the Khanid Kingdom, and the Ammatar lordlings well, although always on a tight leash, often used as personal bodyguards for Holders and other people in positions of power.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sounds a little too much like common labor for my liking. Freight hauling? Nope, not my thing.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've changed my mind ― sorry, but I'm not much interested in finishing this job.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Well, I think these raiders certainly deserve your wrath, at least. Be careful out there, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: A fine greeting! How can I be of service, {[character]agentID.name}?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Fantastic! And here is your reward for a difficult job well done.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Recently, an Ammatar captain was given command of an Amarr station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} not too long ago, and he‘s been sending ships out into nearby low-security systems to harass our supply ships ever since. My scouts reported just a few hours ago that a large force of Amarr ships has left the base, so I´ve sent every ship I can spare to intercept them. I want you to head out there and destroy the station along with every damned Amarr or Ammatar you find.

Still, you're going to need a few tough allied ships; I'm sure they'll have reasonably strong stationary defenses.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
The Amarr, as you must know, have been raiding our outlying planets, enslaving our people with the help of their Ammatar slaves. Recently, a Fawning lapdog captain took command of a station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} not too long ago, and he‘s been sending ships out into nearby low-security systems to harass our supply ships ever since. CONCORD does nothing, of course, and I don't have the resources to guard every transport flying near the border systems.

These raids must stop, {[character]player.name}. We know where the enemy base is, but my calls for reinforcement have fallen on deaf ears ― those squabbling slaves in the Republic Parliament can't walk five meters without tripping in their own shit. Now matters have gotten worse, and that's why I need you: My scouts reported just a few hours ago that a large force of Amarr ships, by all accounts their entire fleet, has left the base, so I´ve sent every ship I can spare to intercept them. That's why you're here: With all of their ships away from the station, we can make a sudden strike at them while their defenses are down.

{[character]player.name}, I want you to head out there and destroy that station along with every cursed Amarr or Ammatar in it.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The station is so much scrap, Commander. Might wanna send some salvagers in there ― I left a few scraps behind.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Damn you! This was our first real opportunity to strike back at those slave-takers. You're no better than those fools in parliament.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: And here I thought we were all fighting on the same side. Whose side you on, {[character]player.name}?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm on it. Those slavers won't know what hit them.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The Nefantar go by many names, but Ammatar is the most common ― though their former Minmatar brethren sometimes refer to them as “the Lost Tribe” in pity, but more often “the Fawning” or “the Yoked” in scorn. The Nefantar have left behind their tribal heritage and taken up many (but not all) aspects of the Amarrian religion, a movement that has resulted in a unique blend of cultures.

The Ammatar Mandate and the Minmatar Republic have been locked in a state of cold war for a few years now; since the Vindication Wars, there hasn't been a large-scale battle between them, mainly due to former Prime Minister Karin Midular's diplomatic efforts. However, after Midular's passing, the animosity between the two peoples cannot be denied. The Ammatar aristocracy see themselves as the rightful rulers of all the Matar tribes; for their part, most Minmatar hold little more than bitter animosity toward the tribe that long ago betrayed its cousins, and a widespread hatred of the Ammatar is still common among them.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Commander, I‘ve got places to be, people to see. Why not roll your fat ass out from behind that desk and fire up your own engines for a change?

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: You nuts?! That was a fully armed battlestation! Gimme a couple dozen heavy assault cruisers and maybe I‘d stand a chance.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. If you're quick, you can crush them before they know what's happening. Still, you're going to need a few tough allied ships; I'm sure they'll have reasonably strong stationary defenses.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Thanks, Commander. I heard you could use me. Whaddya need?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
Because of your failure to deal with the station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, many Minmatar lost their lives fighting an overwhelming number of Amarr and Ammatar ships. You are not the only capsuleer working in the Republic, {[character]player.name}, and I‘d remind you to remember whose side you‘re on ― there may well come a day when you'll rue this occasion.

Captain {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Hooo, yes!! Haha! I knew you were the right pilot for the job, {[character]player.name}. Take this ― you've earned it, my friend.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
{[character]player.name},

Due to your lack of response, I was forced to find another pilot to deal with the Amarr station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Fortunately, you are not the only capable capsuleer working in the Republic.

Commander {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Recently, the Caldari seized a shipment of extremely valuable blueprints from us and rerouted them to a station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Intelligence assures me that they haven't moved the blueprints yet; our spies have determined that the Caldari are holding the materials for inspection before they move them elsewhere. Those blueprints must be destroyed before that happens. I want you to head out there and destroy that storage outpost.

This won't be an easy task. You're going to need a few good ships along with you; the owners of the station have paid a great deal for strong stationary defenses.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Of course. I‘ll have it brought in at once...

Now, in the meantime, {[character]player.name}, can we talk business? As you know, the Caldari megacorps have imposed a unilateral, if entirely “unofficial” trade embargo on all Gallentean transports. Recently, they seized a shipment of extremely valuable blueprints, which they rerouted to a station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I don't see that there's any way we can recover the shipment, so I want to do the next best thing.

Intelligence assures me that they haven't moved the blueprints yet; our spies have determined that the Caldari are holding the materials for inspection before they move them elsewhere. Those blueprints must be destroyed before that happens. You see where I'm headed with this?

{[character]player.name}, I want you to head out there and destroy that storage outpost. Right down to the foundations, non!? As a private holding subcontractor, the corporation that owns the station doesn't have any combat-worthy starships, but the structure is well protected nonetheless. What do you say?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The station and its contents are no more. Those Caldari pigs will not benefit from our Gallente ingenuity.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Sacre…!! Well, what am I supposed to do now, hmm? Leave those blueprints to the capitalist pigs?!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Merde alors!! What about the sanctity of the Federation, huhn!? F'agh! You, you, you capsuliers … you're all the same ― some day you'll need to choose a side.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text:
I'm happy to help, {[character]agentID.name}. Anything to show those Caldari automatons that the Federation is not to be trifled with. Just give me the coordinates and I'll be on my way.

…Once I finish my drink, of course.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The oligarchic Caldari State stands for corporate capitalism in its purest form. There are eight great "mega-corporations" that together own more than 90 percentage of all property within the State. Each corporation is made up of thousands of companies of various sizes, each with any number of specific market interests, ranging from simple mining companies to powerful security companies. There is no single, unified government as such; each megacorp rules its territories like a kingdom with little or no interference from the others.

In State matters such as foreign policy, the all-powerful Board of Directors, which consists of the CEOs of the eight megacorps, determines the behavior of the State (the tiebreaker vote in deadlock situations belongs to the CEO of Modern Finances). The Board also makes sure that the social infrastructure of the State remains intact and settles all major quarrels between the corporations.

The eight major corporations are Kaalakiota, Sukuuvestaa, Nugoeihuvi, Ishukone, Wiyrkomi, Hyasyoda, CBD, and Lai Dai.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: {[character]agentID.name}, I'm afraid I can't do this for you right now: I have an appointment at my favorite spa, and … oh, look at the time ― better be going!

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Are you completely, incurably mad?! What were you thinking!?? You‘d need a squadron of dreadnoughts to take down a fully armed outpost!

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Haha. Naturellement. Enjoy.

Now, I hope I have not misrepresented this matter: This won't be an easy task. You're going to need a few good ships along with you, for, as I mentioned, the owners of the station have paid a great deal for ... how do you say? "state-of-the-arts"? ― c'est ca? ― for strong stationary defenses.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You are too kind. The journey was nothing I couldn't handle. And make it Lusean rum, white, and Quafe Ultra, if you please. A double.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
Because of your failure to deal with the station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, the capitalist regime of the Caldari State has won another small victory over the democratic union of our noble Federation.

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: C'excellent!! I knew you wouldn't let me down, {[character]player.name}. Here, now, take this reward ― you have earned it, my friend.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
{[character]player.name},

Due to your lack of response, I was forced to find another pilot to deal with the Caldari station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Fortunately, you are not the only capable capsulier working in the Empire.

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Some Gallente warehousing firm has a station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} where they‘ve been stockpiling all sorts of old, unused armaments and ammunition. Thing is, some pirates have heard about the stockpile, and they keep trying to get their hands on it. Of course, we can't let that happen. The Gallente, being as soft as they are stupid, don't post guard ships around the place at all, so the longer it sits there, the more likely it is that some criminals will figure out a way past the stationary defenses.

Head out there and just destroy the whole bloody station. We'll call it a terrorist attack or something, don't worry. Your back is covered. Still, you're going to need a few tough ships along with you; the Gallente navy may be laughable, but I'm told the company that owns the station has paid top kredits for some pretty sturdy stationary defenses out there.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Heh. Humble and selfless, just like they said you‘d be. Listen, {[character]player.name}: Some Gallente warehousing firm has a station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and they‘ve been stockpiling all sorts of old, unused armaments and ammunition there for months now. Thing is, some pirates have heard about the stockpile, and they keep trying to get their hands on it. We can't let that happen; the Guristas and other pirate scum keep us busy enough as it is, and we don't need them causing any more trouble than they already do.

Of course, the Gallente, being as soft as they are stupid, don't post guard ships around the station at all, so the longer it sits there, the more likely it is that some jackass will figure out a way past the stationary defenses and hit the jackpot. We've got little use for the stuff ourselves, considering how outdated it is, so here's what I need you to do: Head out there and just destroy the whole bloody station, stockpile and all. I'm serious ― just take it down, no questions asked. We'll call it a terrorist attack or something, don't worry. Your back is covered.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Gallente warehouse station is no more, Commander. Those weapons will never see pirate hands, or any others for that matter.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Damn! Who knows when someone will retrieve that evi― ehh, those weapons. This was a matter of national security, {[character]player.name}!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Well. I see. I had heard you were Caldari through and through ― but I see now that the State holds little place in your mercenary heart.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sounds good, Commander. You've called on the right capsuleer for this job.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Gallentean society is currently enjoying the fruits of unprecedented economic prosperity and growth, undergoing a cultural and spiritual revitalization. President Foiritan, still popular despite being ousted by President Roden, takes credit for ushering in this age, expanding trade with other nations and pouring money into massive projects. In all of New Eden, no other nation has as many concurrent terraforming initiatives underway as the Federation; the demand for labor has grown so great that it now draws immigrants from many other nations, especially from the Minmatar Republic.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Commander {[character]agentID.name}, I think you ought to find someone else to do your dirty work. Let me ask you: Somebody giving you a kickback to take care of this “stockpile“?

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm afraid you're going to need to call in the Navy capital fleet on this one, Commander. That station is remarkably well protected for a simple arms storage facility…

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. I should warn you, however, that you're going to need a few tough ships along with you; the Gallente navy may be laughable, but I'm told the company that owns the station has paid top kredits for some pretty sturdy stationary defenses out there.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Thank you, Commander, I am flattered. But let us not waste any time discussing my small successes: I understand you would have me perform some task for the benefit of the State?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
Pirates in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} have just seized the contents of that warehouse, {[character]player.name}. There is more at stake in this matter than you know ― this is now a matter of national security.

Good day,
Commander {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
That is good news, my friend. Though I could not speak of it (and it remains a matter of highest security), there was more at stake here than a simple pirate threat. Yes, good news indeed.

Take this reward ― you've certainly earned it.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
{[character]player.name},

Due to your lack of a suitably timely response, I was forced to find another capsuleer to deal with the Gallente situation in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Fortunately, you are not the only capable capsuleer working in the Empire.

Commander {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Recently, a Sebiestor chieftain took command of a Minmatar station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and he‘s been sending raiding parties out into nearby systems to harass our transport caravans. I want you to head out there and destroy the raiders' base along with every damned Minmatar you find. If you're quick and decisive, you can take these worthless dogs down.

Still, you're going to need a few tough allied ships along with you; I'm sure the Minmatar will have reasonably strong stationary defenses.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
{[character]player.name}, these Minmatar rebels, as you know, have been getting more and more daring in their raids on outlying planets. Recently, one of their chieftains ― a Sebiestor, I think, for all it matters ― took command of a station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and he‘s been sending out raiding parties into nearby low-security systems to keep our transport caravans from getting to their destination. CONCORD intervention is minimal, of course, in low-sec, and I simply don't have the ships or the men to spare to guard every convoy within five jumps.

These raids must be stopped. We've known for some time where the enemy base is located, but my requests for reinforcements haven't been answered. Now matters have escalated, and that's why I need you: My scouts reported just a few hours ago that a large force of Minmatar ships, virtually their entire fleet, has left the base, so I´ve sent every ship I can spare to intercept them. The good thing is that, with all of their ships away from the station, we can make a sudden strike at them while their defenses are down.

{[character]player.name}, I want you to head out there and destroy the raiders' base along with every damned Minmatar you find.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The station is no more, Commander. Those Minmatar scum all died fiery deaths, every last one of them. And I laughed the whole time.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Bloody hell! This was our first real opportunity to strike back at those Minmatar pirates. I guess I'd better call for more reinforcements ... won't hold my breath, though.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Dammit, {[character]player.name}, I thought you were on our side! You capsuleers are all the same ― some day, pilot, you'll need to choose a side.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll ready my ship and summon my allies to strike at once, while the iron is still hot. Those pathetic barbarian fools won't know what hit them.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The Sebiestor tribe hails from the inhospitable steppes of the Mikramurka continent in the northern arctic region on the Minmatar homeworld of Matar. The Sebiestors are the most technically inclined of the Minmatar tribes; they were at the forefront in the tentative space exploration program the Minmatars were undertaking just before the Amarrians arrived to subjugate them. Today, most Minmatar ships, and especially stations, tend to be engineered by Sebiestors.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Commander {[character]agentID.name}, {[character]player.name} isn‘t a pawn in anyone‘s little war. Find someone else to do your dirty work.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Are you insane?! You‘d need a squadron of dreadnoughts to take down a fully armed battlestation! I‘m getting the hell away from here before those Minmatar come looking for me.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I knew I could count on you, {[character]player.name}. If you're quick and decisive, you can take these worthless dogs down. Still, you're going to need a few tough allied ships along with you; I'm sure the Minmatar will have reasonably strong stationary defenses.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: The pleasure is mine, Commander. I came as soon as I heard you had need. What seems to be the problem?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
Because of your failure to deal with the station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, many good Amarrians lost their lives fighting an overwhelming number of Minmatar cruisers. You are not the only capsuleer working in the Empire, {[character]player.name}, and I‘d remind you to remember whose side you‘re on ― there may well come a day when you'll rue this occasion.

Commander {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Ha! Victory!! I knew you wouldn't let me down, {[character]player.name}. Take this reward ― you've more than earned it, my friend.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
{[character]player.name},

Due to your lack of response, I was forced to find another pilot to deal with the Minmatar menace in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Fortunately, you are not the only capable capsuleer working in the Empire.

Commander {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Nine days ago, my spies found out about a capital ship repair facility, owned secretly by the Amarr, residing in our sovereign space. I must warn you that what I propose is not authorized by Command, and if you get caught I will be forced to deny all knowledge of you and your actions.

An Amarr carrier was heavily damaged yesterday by a few Blood Raider battleships, badly enough that it was apparently forced to head to the repair facility of which I've spoken. Whether its repairs are complete by now or not I don't know, but regardless, I want you to head out to that facility and destroy the carrier. That should make them think twice about using our space for troop movements.

But I imagine it will be a tough fight. You ought to call on some of your friends before you tackle this one.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I was hoping you'd ask, of course ― that's why you're here. I won't lie to you: We need someone with your talents, {[character]player.name}.

Amarrian ships have been passing through our space. Low-sec space, mind you, so not heavily patrolled, but our space nonetheless. And large numbers of them are capital ships, carriers that we're pretty certain are ferrying drop ships for their damnable slave-hunting surface raids in outlying constellations. I've sent several requests to every admiral in High Command, but the replies are always the same: Our ships are needed elsewhere, and there are no ships to spare unless these Amarr actually open hostilities.

Nine days ago, my spies found out about a capital ship repair facility, owned secretly by the Amarr, residing in our sovereign space. Of course, the very existence of this station is a breach of multiple treaties and is actually reason enough to declare open war. I get the sense, though, that that isn't something we're ready to do ― not just yet, at least. But that doesn't mean my hands are tied completely. I must warn you that what I propose is not authorized by Command, and if you get caught I will be forced to deny all knowledge of you and your actions.

Understood? Very well.

My spies inform me that an Amarr carrier was heavily damaged yesterday in a firefight with a few Blood Raider battleships; it was hurt badly enough that it was apparently forced to head to the repair facility of which I've spoken. Whether its repairs are complete by now or not I don't know, but regardless, I want you to head out to that facility and destroy that carrier; if the attack isn't undertaken by ships bearing our signatures, we can simply declare it an act of piracy and be done with it. Heh. That should make those bastards think twice about using our space for troop movements.

But just to be safe, let's keep this conversation between the two of us.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Ah, that was a good fight. The mothership is no more, {[character]agentID.name}. Next time you have trouble with those stinking fedo-lovers ... well, you know who to call, right?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Well, {[character]player.name}, I understand that this was not an easy task, but, given your reputation, I really didn‘t expect you to give up so easily. Just goes to show, you can‘t trust everything you hear...

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I see how it is, {[character]player.name}. We are men of action: Lies do not become us. You needn‘t hide your cowardice behind your politics.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sounds like a tough fight. That settles it: I'm in.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Religion is of great importance to every Amarrian ― at least in public, if not in private. This fervor has at various times been the cause of both great good and great evil, as has religion in every age of humankind.

Shortly after recovering from the closure of EVE, millennia ago, the Amarrians began to expand their realm and colonize other planets and, eventually, constellations. The worlds they conquered were enslaved, a practice justified by the Amarr Scriptures. Ever since, the Amarrians have attempted to enslave every nation and race they have encountered, and slavery remains an essential part of Amarr society. This practice has, of course, tainted their relations with other races.

And the Lord spake, and said, Lo, my people,
Witness, for I have made the worlds of Heaven;
And these worlds I give to you, My Chosen,
So Amarr shall rule the worlds of the Heavens.

None shall stand higher than you save the Sefrim,
Who serve Me as others shall serve you,
For all things under Me serve one higher;
So Amarr shall rule the worlds of the Heavens.

As Garrulor rules the skies; as Frisceas rules the sea;
As Emperor rules Holder; as Holder rules Serf;
Yet all under Heaven serve Me;
So shall Amarr rule the worlds of the Heavens.

―Book of Reclaiming 3.19–21

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: {[character]agentID.name}, I appreciate your confidence in me, but I‘m afraid I can‘t afford to entangle myself in your political maneuverings. Hope you understand.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I just got my ass handed to me out there. How in all the hells did you expect me to do this!? Give me a fleet of battleships, and then maybe....

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Ha! That's the spirit! But I imagine it will be a tough fight, yes. You ought to call on some of your old friends to tackle this one.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text:
Don't mind if I do ... Ah, the good stuff. Thanks.

So, {[character]agentID.name}, I hear there's been some Imperial Navy activity around here lately. Anything I can help with?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
{[character]player.name},

Unfortunately, given the amount of time that has passed since we last met, the Amarr carrier we discussed has now left {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and rejoined its fleet. At this time, I must ask you to stand down.

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Indeed I do. I expected no less, {[character]player.name}. Put the right person on the job, and it always gets done well.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
{[character]player.name},

Due to your lack of response, I was forced to find another capsuleer to deal with the Amarr menace we discussed. Sadly, having little time to prepare for the task I required, the pilot of that expedition lost his ship and barely escaped in his pod. The Amarr ship remains at large.

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Caldari ships, some of them capital, have been traveling through nearby low-security systems in our sovereign space. Now, a few days ago, my scout discovered a capital ship repair facility, secretly controlled by the Caldari State, in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}! One of their carriers was heavily damaged yesterday by some Guristas battleships and forced to head to this secret base; I want you to destroy that carrier before it has a chance to rejoin its fleet.

I imagine this will be a tough fight. You ought to gather some allies before you head out.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Well, I've been hearing reports of Caldari ships ― many, and some of them capital ships ― traveling in nearby low-security systems, {[character]player.name}. Apparently they think they can reduce the amount of jump fuel they use by taking short cuts through our sovereign space. Of course, this is a clear breach of our treaties; the very appearance of capital ships in such numbers is cause to declare open war! I have issued formal complaints to Fleet Command, but it's always the same: “You need to bring in ‘concrete evidence' of these ships' movements.” And implicit in that is the fact that I'm not supposed to ruffle any political feathers... Well, frankly, I've had it. These ships undermine my authority and make me look bad.

Now, a few days ago, my scout discovered a capital ship repair facility, secretly controlled by the bloody Caldari State, located in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}! Yes, within our jurisdiction! There's good news, too, though: One of their carriers was heavily damaged yesterday by some Guristas battleships, and it was apparently forced to head to this secret base. I want you to destroy that carrier before it has a chance to rejoin its fleet. As long as it's a mercenary like yourself who does the deed, we can just call the whole thing an unfortunate random act of piracy and leave it at that. Heh.

I should warn you that this mission is not authorized by the Federation or the Fleet, and if you get caught I'll be forced to deny all knowledge of you and your actions. Fair enough?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Caldari mothership is destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}. My pleasure.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text:
You're giving up?! Zut alors!

Alright, fine. Fine. Good effort, and all that. I guess this was a pretty tough job.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Your mother, eh? Good one. Never heard that before, not in all my years.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Very well. You find a tough problem, you've got to send out a tougher solution.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The Caldari Navy is smaller in terms of personnel and total ships than both the Federation Navy and the Imperial Navy, yet it has more battleships than any other fleet, and the average age of the Caldari ships is considerably less. (The Caldari regularly replace their oldest ships with newer ones and constantly add better hi-tech equipment.) The strategic doctrine of the Caldari Navy, as reported by Kutatala Ikao, Chief Coordinator of Navy Public Relations, is simple: to be able to defeat any other navy in the world.

Most experts believe it is.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Oh, I just realized that I had forgotten I´m supposed to go visit my mom today. Boy, what a memory I have! Haha. Ha. Ha. (Ha.) Well, see you later…

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I might as well have attacked a Fleet armada in a Velator. Are you mad?! I'm done with this “mission” of yours.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: That's what I hoped you would say. What a relief! Take care out there.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: That´s precisely why I'm here, {[character]agentID.name}. How can I help?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Wonderful news, {[character]player.name}. Please accept this reward as a small token of my gratitude.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Lately, we've been getting reports of large numbers of Gallente ships in nearby low-sec border systems. Not just any ships, either, but capital ships. These ships in my jurisdiction undermine my authority and make me look bad. However, a Gallente carrier was heavily damaged yesterday by some Serpentis battleships, enough that it was apparently forced to head to a capital ship repair facility, secretly run by the Federation, in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I want you to go out there and destroy that carrier before it has a chance to rejoin with its fleet.

I imagine this will be a tough fight. You ought to gather a squad of allies before you head out there.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
No, no, honest. We're just huge fans of yours here at {[location]agentStationID.name}. Especially after seeing that Impetus docureel of you destroying those pirates not far from here a couple of months back? Remember that, just a few constellations over? Man, that was a good one.

Anyway, we really do need your help. Lately, we've been getting reports of large numbers of Gallente ships in nearby low-sec border systems, apparently cutting jumps out of their travels by using our sovereign space as a “shortcut.” Not just any ships, either, but capital ships. I'm talking dreadnoughts, motherships.

Of course, they're breaching multiple treaties in this; their appearance in our space is enough reason to declare open war. I have sent several reports about it, but the replies are always the same: that I need to bring in “concrete evidence” of these ships' movements. And I have also been given tacit instructions about not “rocking the boat.” Yeah. Well, I've had enough. These ships in my jurisdiction undermine my authority and make me ― and our government ― look bad.

And it gets worse. A few days ago, my spies found out about a capital ship repair facility, secretly run by the Federation, again in our territory! But apparently a Gallente carrier was heavily damaged yesterday by some Serpentis battleships, enough that it was forced to head to this secret facility. I want you to head out there and destroy that carrier before it has a chance to rejoin with its fleet. As long as it's a privateer like yourself who does the deed, we can just claim the whole thing is a “random act of piracy” and leave it at that. Right?

Alright, then ― now, to be fair, I should warn you that what we're doing here is not authorized by the Board or the Navy, and if you get caught I'll be forced to deny all knowledge of you and your actions.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Damn, that was a good fight. The carrier is dispatched, {[character]agentID.name}. Happy to be of help. And my reward?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You're giving up?! But, but … you're {[character]player.name}!!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: But you're this great thing! This famous capsuleer! I … I don't know what to say…

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Well, now, this sounds like it might be a challenge worthy of … me. I accept.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Impetus is the biggest and most widely known producer of holoreels in the entire known EVE universe, making everything from epic feature films and indie art films to cheap porn flicks. Production Manager Baemedier Andenget, herself once the most trusted newscaster in the Federation, has in recent years led the development of much-anticipated instant news arrays, a technology that, once complete, will no doubt revolutionize the news industry.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: {[character]agentID.name}, a carrier. A carrier. CAR-ri-er. You realize what that means? I'm out of here.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Well, I'm done. A carrier?! I might as well attack the nearest moon.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Oh, well, that's what I'd hoped you'd say. With you on our side, we can't fail. Good luck out there. Even though you don't need it.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Are you mocking me, {[character]agentID.name}? I came to see if you needed my help, but I can leave…

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Yes, yes, of course. Thank you. I'm only sorry I can't give you more...

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Recently, Minmatar ships have been spotted in unprecedented numbers in various low-sec border systems. My spies recently found out about a secret Matar capital ship repair facility in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and yesterday a Minmatar carrier was heavily enough damaged in a firefight with a some Ammatar ships that it was forced to head to this facility. I want you to destroy that carrier.

I imagine it will be a tough fight. You ought to call on some of your friends before you tackle this one.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Heh. Don't waste any time, eh? I like that. And I won't lie to you: We do need your help.

Recently, Minmatar ships have appeared in unprecedented numbers in various low-sec border systems. And that's not all: Many of them are capital ships, carriers that we're pretty certain are ferrying swarms of assault frigates. Now, I've sent several requests to every admiral I know, but the replies are always the same: Our forces are needed elsewhere, and there are no ships to spare unless the heathens actually initiate open hostilities.

But it gets worse. A few days ago, my spies found out about a capital ship repair facility, owned secretly by the Republic, residing in our sovereign space. Of course, the very existence of this station is reason enough to declare open war. I get the sense, though, that that isn't something we're ready to do ― not just yet, at least. But that doesn't mean I have to sit here fingering my nasal implants. I must warn you that what I propose is not authorized by Command, and if you get caught I will be forced to deny all knowledge of you and your actions. Got that?

Alright, well then: My spies inform me that a Minmatar carrier was heavily damaged yesterday in a firefight with some Ammatar outriggers; it was hurt badly enough that it was apparently forced to head to this illegal repair facility of theirs. I have no idea if they've had the time or resources to repair it yet, and I don't care. I want you to head out to that facility and destroy that carrier, I don´t care how, before it has a chance to rejoin with its fleet.

Now, as long as the attack isn't undertaken by our ships, we can declare the whole thing a “random act of piracy” or something and leave it at that. Right? That'll teach these upstart dogs to use our space for troop movements. But just to avoid any political repercussions, let's keep this all between the two of us.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Now that was a good fight. The mothership is no more, {[character]agentID.name}. Next time you have trouble with a capital ship infestation ... well, you know who to call, right?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text:
You're giving up...? I mean, you‘re just giving up!?

Inconceivable.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: {[character]player.name}. {[character]player.name}. {[character]player.name}. You truly, deeply, profoundly disappoint me.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I've been looking to test my latest ship fittings against a worthy opponent. Now's as good a time as any.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Religion defines the Amarr Empire, where slavery and colonization are defended with direct reference to the Holy Scriptures. Philosophers of other races have tried, with little effect, to argue these matters with theologians of Amarr, but the practice of slavery is so deeply ingrained in the Amarrian mindset that the Empire would no doubt collapse under its own ponderous weight if slavery were ever abolished ― which is not something any Amarrian, Holder or otherwise, could ever imagine happening.

And the Lord spake, and said, Lo, my people,
Witness, for I have made the worlds of Heaven;
And these worlds I give to you, My Chosen,
So Amarr shall rule the worlds of the Heavens.

None shall stand higher than you save the Sefrim,
Who serve Me as others shall serve you,
For all things under Me serve one higher;
So Amarr shall rule the worlds of the Heavens.

As Garrulor rules the skies; as Frisceas rules the sea;
As Emperor rules Holder; as Holder rules Serf;
Yet all under Heaven serve Me;
So shall Amarr rule the worlds of the Heavens.

―Book of Reclaiming 3.19–21

I give to you the destiny of Faith,
And you will bring its message to every planet and every star in the heavens:
Go forth, conquer in My Name, and reclaim that which I have given.

―Book of Reclaiming 22.13

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: {[character]agentID.name}, I hope you‘ll understand when I say I‘d rather lick fedo slime out of my grandmother‘s ear than do this mission for you.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Are you crazy?! All the holy relics of Amash-Akura couldn't take out that mothership!

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Wonderful. I knew I could count on you. Your reputation is not unwarranted.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: No, {[character]agentID.name}, nothing I couldn't deal with. I understand you need some help?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Damned straight I do! But to be honest, I expected no less, {[character]player.name}. Fine work. Fine work indeed.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Intelligence has discovered a number of unsolicited broadcasts washing over this constellation recently. We believe the Gallente to be the source of the signals; they've been overriding our local broadcasts and filling the airwaves with their crazy libertine, anti-establishment dogma. It may sound trivial to you, but if we don't stop these broadcasts, they're going to cause serious problems for us. Workers have started believing the trash they're hearing, and if this doesn't stop soon, we may face full-scale revolt.

I need you to go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and take these Gallente-controlled towers offline by destroying the broadcast station that controls them. Rest assured, the State will be most grateful.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Don´t worry, my friend, you'll be suitably compensated. Here's the deal: The {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system has been somewhat unstable lately ― workers in the colonies here have been acting up and black market trading has been steadily on the rise, and as a result several lucrative contracts have been lost to the Gallente. We recently moved to quell the situation, but now we've hit upon another problem.

Intelligence has discovered a number of unsolicited broadcasts washing over this constellation recently. We believe the Gallente to be the source of the signals, trying to turn the situation to their advantage. They've been overriding our local broadcasts and filling the airwaves with their crazy libertine, anti-establishment dogma.

It may sound trivial to you, but believe me ― if we don't stop these broadcasts, they're going to cause serious problems for us. Workers have started believing the trash they're hearing, and they now believe our efforts to stabilize the region is an attempt to “keep them down,” whatever that means. We're already hearing stories of people who've been kidnapped, tortured, spied on. All totally unfounded, of course. And to add to the problems, local companies have begun grumbling about moving out of the system, and we have even had reports of small corporations accepting Gallente contracts in favor of the State's! All in all, if this doesn't stop soon, we may face full-scale revolt.

Luckily, our latest recon patrols encountered what seemed a lost convoy, which we of course intercepted; after holding the pilots for questioning, we found that they were Gallente agents involved in this whole conspiracy, and a little … gentle persuasion soon convinced them to reveal the location of the tower. However, the ships I sent to the location soon broke contact and have not yet returned. That, coupled with the fact that the broadcast array must be quite extensive given the strength of the signal, convinces me that the array must be heavily guarded.

{[character]player.name}, I need you to go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and take these towers offline by destroying the broadcast station that controls them. Rest assured, the State will be most grateful.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Well, they meant business ― had some pretty serious defense towers in place. Nothing I couldn't handle, though.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Hm. Yes, pathetic. But hey, I hear they're looking for a new line cook down at J.C.'s Grill House...

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Yes, well, I suppose the security of this great State doesn't mean anything to you...? Hmm? Bloody mercenaries.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Not my usual style, {[character]agentID.name}, but the money sounds good. Count me in.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Despite the use of jump gates for travel purposes, communication across the vast distances of space must be transmitted at the speed of light. The Amarrians were the first to master jump gate technology and thus the first to face the problem. In the end, they suspended all research, accepting the fact that FTL communications were unattainable.

Hundreds of years later, a young Gallentean woman, Li Azbel, came up with a solution that was so simple yet deeply rooted in arcane physics that it was at first rejected as a hoax. The root of the solution lay in the “EPR paradox,” a name shrouded in mystery. The EPR paradox is famous for contradicting quantum physics in some very important ways; specifically, it shows another old theory, the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle, to be untrue.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Hm. Not really my style, {[character]agentID.name}, blowing up com-stations. I think I'll go see if someone else has some capital ships they need owned.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Wow, I must be in the wrong line of work. I just got my ass handed to me by a broadcast station!! Pathetic! I need to go have a shower...

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Glad to hear it. Glad to hear it. Go, silence them … with prejudice.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Oh? What is it? And what's it gonna be worth?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Excellent news, {[character]player.name}. Excellent news indeed.

Here. Don't spend it all in one place, eh?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I've had a lot of reports come across my desk the past few weeks about unrest in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. It turns out that there have been unsolicited broadcasts washing over this region recently, very cleverly insinuating themselves into the local media. They're having a noticeable effect in the region already, and it's only a matter of time before we get something more serious than a few weird cults popping up.

Luckily, our latest recon patrols intercepted an apparently lost convoy, and after holding the pilots for questioning, we have discovered the location of the tower. Patrols I have sent to the location have not returned, and coupled with the fact that the broadcast array must be quite extensive given the strength and reach of the signal, we can only assume that it's heavily guarded.

I need you to go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and take these towers offline by destroying the broadcast station that controls them. Rest assured, the Republic will be grateful.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
{[character]player.name}! Right. I thought you looked familiar. And yes, you‘ve come to the right place.

I've had a lot of reports come across my desk the past few weeks about unrest in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. It wasn't anything too much to worry about at first, it seemed, but then several cults sprouted up, virtually overnight, that bear a discomforting similarity to the revolting religion of the Amarr. Naturally, Republic Security Services sent some people out to investigate.

It turns out that there have been unsolicited broadcasts washing over this region recently, very cleverly insinuating themselves into the local media. The subversiveness of the broadcasts is astounding: an advert changed slightly here, there a holoreel modified with very subtle textual changes.

It may sound trivial, but believe me, if we don't stop these broadcasts, they are going to cause serious problems. They're having a noticeable effect in the region already, and it's only a matter of time before we get something more serious than a few cults popping up. At the moment, it's just a few hundred susceptible minds, but the broadcast techniques are improving and we can't seem to override the signal ― they must have a relay or broadcast tower in the system that's jamming our efforts at the same time it's spamming its own signals.

Luckily, our latest recon patrols intercepted an apparently lost convoy, and after holding the pilots for questioning, we have discovered the location of the tower. Patrols I have sent to the location have not returned, and coupled with the fact that the broadcast array must be quite extensive given the strength and reach of the signal, we can only assume that it's heavily guarded.

I need you to go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and take these towers offline by destroying the broadcast station that controls them. Rest assured, the Republic will be grateful.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: It's done, {[character]agentID.name}. But somebody had set up some pretty serious hardware to protect that station. This whole thing stinks. Stinks like an Amarr privy.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: What!? You're quitting? Alright, fine, fine. I'll notify Fleet Command.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Hmph! You mercs are all the same. Ever consider that the integrity of our Republic might be at stake?! Ah, why bother...

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Not my usual fare, but the money's good. Count me in.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Despite the use of jump gates for travel purposes, communication across the vast distances of space must be transmitted at the speed of light. The Amarrians were the first to master jump gate technology and thus the first to face the problem. In the end, they suspended all research, accepting the fact that FTL communications were unattainable.

Hundreds of years later, a young Gallentean woman, Li Azbel, came up with a solution that was so simple yet deeply rooted in arcane physics that it was at first rejected as a hoax. The root of the solution lay in the “EPR paradox,” a name shrouded in mystery. The EPR paradox is famous for contradicting quantum physics in some very important ways; specifically, it shows another old theory, the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle, to be untrue.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm in the business of crushing battleships, and you send me to deal with some measly broadcast station? No thanks, my friend.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: There's some heavy damned hardware out there around that station! Call in the Republic Fleet on this one; no way am I going back there.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Very well, then. Silence them with prejudice. Glad to have you on board, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm {[character]player.name}. I see you've heard of me. I understand I might be of some service?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Hm. Yes, very alarming. I'll notify Fleet Command and the Justice Department at once.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
A former slave, a member of my tribe, recently managed to escape from Amarr and make her way here to {[location]agentStationID.name}. That in itself is good news, of course, but there's bad as well. She told me she recently overheard some Amarrian officials talking about a military project at a hidden station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} ― yes, in our dominion! She doesn't know what goes on there, but its top secret.

The thing is, our scans can't find anything out of the ordinary except a couple of unlicensed jumpgates that appear to lead nowhere. Because of the lack of evidence, Republic Security won't authorize an official investigation beyond what we've already found, but I think there's more going on here than meets the eye. I need you to head out there and see what's going on. It could be that the Amarr are hiding behind some kind of cloaking array or something.

If you do happen to discover any cloaking arrays, destroy them. It may be that they're concealing the actual gate to this Amarr base we heard about, as well as the base itself. Regardless, destroy every enemy ship you see, if there's anything at all, and blow up the station if you can find it.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes, fine, thanks. But I'm glad you're here: I need your help.

A former slave, a member of my tribe, recently managed to escape from Amarr and make her way here to {[location]agentStationID.name}. That in itself is good news, of course, but there's bad as well. She told me she recently overheard some Amarrian officials talking about a military project at a hidden station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} ― yes, in our dominion! She doesn't know what goes on there, but its top secret.

The thing is, our scans can't find anything out of the ordinary except a couple of unlicensed jumpgates that appear to lead nowhere. Because of the lack of evidence, Republic Security won't authorize an official investigation beyond what we've already found, but I think there's more going on here than meets the eye. I need you to head out there and see what's going on. It could be that the Amarr are hiding behind some kind of cloaking array or something.

If you do happen to discover any cloaking arrays, destroy them. It may be that they're concealing the actual gate to this Amarr base we heard about, as well as the base itself. Regardless, destroy every enemy ship you see, if there's anything at all, and blow up the station if you can find it.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Your hunch was right, {[character]agentID.name}. They'd hidden themselves with cloaking arrays ― but I found them anyway.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: That's ... unfortunate.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Yes, and vitally important. But apparently our national security doesn't mean much to you.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll signal my first officer to fire up my ship right now. On my way.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Uh, sounds pretty complicated, {[character]agentID.name}. I'll pass.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've had enough of this, {[character]agentID.name}. You're going to have to find someone else.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Be careful out there, {[character]player.name}. Who knows what you're going to find.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Good day, {[character]agentID.name}. I trust you've been well?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work! Here, take this. I only wish it was more.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You've heard of NMA, right? The Nefantar Mining Association? Well, an associate of mine who has some sizeable contracts with them has run into some problems. He has a small but lucrative mining concern in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that was recently taken over by some claimjumpers.

Turns out the guys who moved in are actually working for Core Complexion Inc. ― some Minmatar mining conglomerate that's in bed with the Sebiestor tribe ― and that they apparently got access to mining rights there through some loophole in some treaty. I don't know the details, and it's obviously not legit, but you've got to be careful when lawyers get involved, eh? Anyway, one of these ruffians got drunk one night and let it slip that they were sent in to get their hands on whatever valuable ore they could … I guess for building new ships. I don't know what that means, but it can't be good.

Anyway, here's the thing: Until the legal crap gets dealt with, these guys are untouchable by the authorities. Not to mention the fact that they've been working away to put up some pretty hefty defense towers around the place. But you ... you could roll on in there and just waste them, and we could pretend some pirates or freebooters had taken it on themselves to deal with the Minmatar scum.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ah, {[character]player.name}, right. Yes, I do have a matter here that requires someone of your caliber. You've heard of NMA, right? The Nefantar Mining Association? Well, an associate of mine who has some sizeable contracts with them has run into some problems.

My friend, whose name I'm afraid I'm not at liberty to reveal, has a small but lucrative mining concern in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Until now, he‘s been subcontracting NMA to do the work there for him, but recently some claimjumpers came in and started throwing their weight around, waving datacards around saying they had just bought the rights to mine there. They came in a couple of transports, sporting some pretty advanced small arms and carrying themselves like they knew how to use them, so the NMA guys played it safe and pulled out; they weren‘t armed to resist a hostile takeover of that magnitude.

Since then, a few well-spent kredits from a couple of his agents uncovered the fact that the guys who moved in are actually working for Core Complexion Inc. ― some Minmatar mining conglomerate that's in bed with the Sebiestor tribe ― and that they apparently got access to mining rights there through some loophole in some treaty. I don't know the details, and it's obviously not legit, but you've got to be careful when lawyers get involved, eh? Anyway, one of these ruffians got drunk one night and let it slip that they were sent in to get their hands on whatever valuable ore they could … I guess for building new ships. I don't know what that means, but it can't be good.

Anyway, here's the thing: Until the legal crap gets dealt with, these guys are untouchable by the authorities. Not to mention the fact that they've been working away to put up some pretty hefty defense towers around the place. But you ... you could roll on in there and just waste them, and we could pretend some pirates or freebooters had taken it on themselves to deal with the Minmatar scum. Nobody'd be the wiser. Whaddya think? The ISK is good.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Well, they put up a tough fight ... but not tough enough. Now, you'd mentioned a substantial reward?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Oh, I see: When the going gets tough, the tough ... run away like a ... a ... person who's running away!? Really ... fast?? <ahem> Ooh, and screaming? Yeah, and waving your hands in the air? Like this…?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: We live in dangerous times, {[character]player.name}, when we must take calculated risks from time to time. But suit yourself. Now if you'll excuse me...

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Hm. Hardly seems like the Minmatar to behave this way ― they're usually a lot more straightforward ― and I don't like it. Count me in.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The Nefantar Miner Association is primarily a mining company, but one with a strong militaristic overtone. This is because it operates mostly in the areas between Ammatar and Minmatar space. The area has deeds and mining rights for many well-hidden, rich mineral zones, making it coveted by more or less everyone.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Hm. Too many political complications here for my liking. Don't you have something where I just go nuke some dumb pirates or outlaws or something??

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Uh, you said “some defense towers.” Now, I may be wrong, but that in no way suggests a fully armed battle array, including warships!! I'm outta here.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Perfect. Reduce those defenses to scrap, along with every Minmatar scum in them. You'll be rewarded handsomely.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm {[character]player.name}. I  was told I should speak with you about some work? Something discreet?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
Because of your failure to deal with the Minmatar claimjumpers in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, as you had agreed to do, the asteroid field there has been depleted entirely. Who knows what the thieves stole from NMA, and to what end?

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Ah, excellent. My friend will be most pleased to hear he can move his men back into the site. And here's the reward I promised. Nice working with you.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You've heard of Minedrill, right? Big mining corporation, tied to the Caldari Navy? Well, an associate of mine has a lucrative mining concern subcontracted out to Minedrill in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. But recently some claimjumpers came in, waving datacards around saying they had the real rights to mine there. They came in a couple of transports, guarded by a bunch of assault frigates, so the Minedrill guys played it safe and pulled out; they weren‘t armed to resist a hostile takeover like that.

We managed to question one of the claimjumpers, and we found out that they are actually working for Astral Mining Inc. ― you know, that Gallente mining conglomerate that's in bed with CreoDron? They apparently got access to mining rights there through some legal sleight of hand. I don't know the details, and I don't care. It's not legit, far as I'm concerned, and the megacorps won't care one way or another as long as this problem just goes away.

Anyway, here's the thing: These Gallente crooks have been working away putting up some pretty hefty defense towers around the place, and since the Navy can't really get involved, we need a privateer like yourself who really knows starship combat. You can just warp on in there and waste them, and all we say is that some pirates took it on themselves to destroy the operation out there. Whaddya think?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ah, {[character]player.name}, right. Yes, I do have a matter here that requires someone of your caliber. You've heard of Minedrill, right? Big mining corporation, tied to the Caldari Navy? Well, an associate of mine who has some sizeable contracts with them has run into some problems.

Since then, we managed to, er, question one of the claimjumpers, and we found out that they are actually working for Astral Mining Inc. ― you know, that Gallente mining conglomerate that's in bed with CreoDron? They apparently got access to mining rights there through some legal sleight of hand. I don't know the details, and I don't care. It's not legit, far as I'm concerned, and the megacorps won't care one way or another as long as this problem just goes away.

Anyway, here's the thing: These Gallente crooks have been working away putting up some pretty hefty defense towers around the place, and since the Navy can't really get involved, we need a privateer like yourself who really knows starship combat. You can just warp on in there and waste them, and all we say is that some pirates took it on themselves to destroy the operation out there. Whaddya think?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: All in an hour's work. Heh. Now, you'd mentioned a reward?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Ah. And you're quitting doesn't have anything to do with the fact that you're a coward, I suppose?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You're snuffling up the wrong vlutar, {[character]player.name}. I have more important things to do, if you don't mind.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Hm. Hardly seems like those Gallente pansies to push like this ― and I don't like it. Somebody needs to put them back in their place. Somebody like me.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Minedrill traces its history back to the Great Caldari-Gallente War. Founded as a special forces unit within the Caldari Navy that rigged asteroids with explosives and used them as booby traps, it became a civilian corporation several years after the war ended ― though it maintains to this day a close affiliation with the Navy. The company's personnel, even today remaining largely ex-military, have used their special knowledge to gain prominence within the mining industry.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Hm. Sounds risky. Don't you have something where I just shuttle some freight around for a huge profit or something??

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: There's no way the reward you offered will cover my expenses for a single week! This mission stinks.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Perfect. Take those Gallente defenses apart and you'll be rewarded handsomely.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm {[character]player.name}. I  heard I should talk to you about some ... er, work?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
Because of your failure to deal with the Gallente claimjumpers in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, as you had agreed to do, the asteroid field there has been depleted entirely. Who knows what technology the thieves stole from Minedrill, and to what end?

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Wonderful! My friend will be most pleased to hear he can move his men back into the site. Here's the reward I promised.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You've heard of Kaalakiota, right? Well, an associate of mine who has some rather sizeable mining contracts around here has run into some problems with them. Kaalakiota owns a mining concern in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} ― a relic of some conciliatory treaty made following the Great War ― and my friend‘s company was contracted by KK to do the work there for them.

Well, now things there have gotten entirely out of hand. A number of workers went missing in the past few weeks, supposedly sent off to “work elsewhere,” and the Caldari have set up a bunch of powerful sentry towers. We've lost contact with the operation altogether now, and industrial ships have been seen flying in and out of the compound constantly. Rumors have even indicated that those convoys have been heading into Amarr space, making the fate of those missing workers a matter of profound concern.

Anyway, Kaalakiota refuses to comment, and since the Federation Navy can't really get involved because of the treaty, we need a free agent like yourself, someone who really knows starship combat. We need you to go in there and destroy the Caldari defenses so we can send in some personnel transports to get those workers out!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Well, I suspect we do, yes. But you're {[character]player.name}, aren't you? How fortuitous. Actually, at the moment, I have a private matter here that requires someone of your caliber.

You've heard of Kaalakiota, right? Of course you have. Who hasn't? Well, an associate of mine who has some rather sizeable mining contracts around here has run into some problems with them. Kaalakiota owns a mining concern in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} ― a relic of some conciliatory treaty made following the Great War ― and my friend‘s company was contracted by KK to do the work there for them. However, the workers there, mostly locals and all good people, started issuing formal complaints almost at once about their treatment at the hands of the KK foremen.

Well, now things there have gotten entirely out of hand. A number of workers went missing entirely in the past few weeks, supposedly sent off to “work elsewhere,” and the Caldari have set up a bunch of powerful sentry towers, turning the place into something more like a military base than a mining operation. We've lost contact with the operation altogether now, and industrial ships have been seen flying in and out of the compound at a much higher rate than the amount of mining there would suggest being necessary. Rumors have even indicated that those convoys have been heading into Amarr space, making the fate of those missing workers a matter of profound concern.

Anyway, Kaalakiota refuses to comment, and since the Federation Navy can't really get involved because of the treaty, we need a free agent like yourself, someone who really knows starship combat. We need you to go in there and destroy the Caldari defenses so we can send in some personnel transports to get those workers out! You'll be rewarded generously, of course.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: All taken care of, {[character]agentID.name}. And while I'd like to say “keep the reward,” it does take a lot of ISK to keep a ship spaceworthy…

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Dammit! And what happens to those poor workers now!?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm sorry to hear that, {[character]player.name}.  And here I thought the plight of those poor workers would be incentive enough in itself...

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Those damned capitalist Caldari pigs! I'm in. And while I appreciate the reward, this one's personal.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Kaalakiota is the largest of the Caldari mega-corporations, most often referred to as the KK, with its fingers in most everything ― manufacturing, distribution, retail, and research, as well as politics. Its greatest rival within the Caldari State, in both business and politics, is the Sukuuvestaa Corporation (which in turn is closely allied with the Nugoeihuvi Corporation). Like all of the Caldari megacorps, save perhaps Ishukone, Kaalakiota is infamous for treating its working-class employees as little better than slaves.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Are you sure this is a good idea? No, sorry, I can't afford the headaches this kind of political action would cause. Sorry.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm afraid you're going to have to come up with another plan. Those defenses are too tough.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: That's the spirit. I'm glad you came by ― I don't know what we'd have done.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm told {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} might have some work for me?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
Because of your failure to deal with the Caldari slavemasters in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, as you had agreed to do, the asteroid field there has been depleted entirely and the entire complement of workers has vanished. Who knows what has really happened there, and to what end?

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Understood, {[character]player.name}. Of course you do. You've done democracy a great service this day.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
An associate of mine owns a mining concern in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and a few months ago he contracted a small, private mining sompany to do the work there. However, we have just discovered that the company he hired is secretly run by the Amarrians. Unbelievable, I know, but those Scripture-spouting lunatics are cunning.

Well, things there in the past 24 hours have very quickly gone downhill. Knowing the jig is up, the Amarrians behind the whole thing sent in a task force of ships and supplies, and they've set up a bunch of powerful sentry towers, turning the place into a labor camp so they can strip the place and flee before the military can be called in to deal with them. No doubt taking all the laborers with them at gunpoint to be made into slaves when they return. Cunning bastards.

Since the navy likely won't be able to rally a response soon enough, we desperately need someone like you, who knows starship combat. We need you to go in there and destroy the Amarrian forces so we can send in some personnel transports to get those workers out!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ah, straight to the point. Good. Wait ... you're {[character]player.name}, aren't you? Perfect. At the moment, I have a matter here that requires someone of your ability.

No doubt taking all the laborers with them, at z-stick-point, to be made into slaves when they return. Cunning bastards.

Since the navy likely won't be able to rally a response soon enough, we desperately need someone like you, who knows starship combat. We need you to go in there and destroy the Amarrian forces so we can send in some personnel transports to get those workers out!

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Those Amarr swine are dead, every last one. Gods, I love the smell of thermoplasm in the morning!

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Dammit, {[character]player.name}! What happens to those poor workers now!? Argh!!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Black-hearted coward!!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll be there before you can pour yourself a cup of Quafe, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Religion is of great importance to every Amarrian ― at least in public, if not in private. This fervor has at various times been the cause of both great good and great evil, as has religion in every age of humankind.

Shortly after recovering from the closure of EVE, millennia ago, the Amarrians began to expand their realm and colonize other planets and, eventually, constellations. The worlds they conquered were enslaved, a practice justified by the Amarr Scriptures. Ever since, the Amarrians have attempted to enslave every nation and race they have encountered, and slavery remains an essential part of Amarr society. This practice has, of course, tainted their relations with other races.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: This force of theirs is intended to withstand a Fleet counterattack for long enough that they can escape? And you want me to go in there? Uh ... no.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm afraid you're going to have to hope a Fleet response can be mounted in time. I couldn't stand against them.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. I'm glad you came in just now ― I don't know what we'd have done otherwise.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm told you might have some work for me?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I knew we could count on you; thanks to Hela that you're on our side. I can only hope this reward is sufficient.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Intelligence recently intercepted a message sent by a known Minmatar spy mentioning a “military project” of theirs at a hidden station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} ― yes, well within our sovereign space! We have no other information, but naturally the location of this place must be top secret.

The thing is, our scans and recon ships can't find anything out of the ordinary except a couple of unlicensed jump gates that appear to lead nowhere. Internal Security won't authorize any further official investigation, calling the whole affair a wild goose chase, but I think there's more to it. I need you to head out there and see what's going on. It could be that the Minmatar are hiding behind some kind of cloaking array or something.

If you do happen to discover any such arrays, destroy them. It may be that they're concealing the actual gate to this secret base we heard about, as well as the base itself. Regardless, destroy every enemy ship you see, assuming there's anything at all there, and destroy the station if you do find it.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes, there is. Forgive my abruptness, but this is an urgent matter. Let's get straight to it.

I need you to head out there and see what's going on. It could be that the Minmatar are hiding behind some kind of cloaking array or something.

Regardless, destroy every enemy ship you see, assuming there's anything at all there, and destroy the station if you do find it.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: It is finished, {[character]agentID.name}, station destroyed. These Minmatar are getting very cagey, though. Cloaking arrays? Sounds more like a Gallente tactic to me.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: And the possibility of Minmatar resistance means nothing to you?? Be on your way, pilot.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I truly wonder... I wonder, “How would being cloned as often as a capsuleer affect one's IQ?” That's what I wonder.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Is there no end to the audacity of these slaves?! If there is any truth to this secret base, I will find it and crush it.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sounds a bit dull, actually. I'm more of a straightforward “pewpew” kind of captain. So, um, no thanks.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: This assignment smells worse than a week-dead fedo, {[character]agentID.name}. I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Be careful out there, {[character]player.name}. God be with you.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Thank you, {[character]agentID.name}. I understand there's a sensitive matter you need help with?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Bless you! Yes, good point. By God, when will these slave races learn their place?!
