messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: There was a base out there, {[character]agentID.name}, but I've destroyed it. Pretty daring of them to try something like this.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: But, I thought we had a deal?!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Okay. Listen, I hope this doesn't have anything to do with ... you know, when you came in?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Secret Gallente base, eh? Alright, I'll have a look around.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Mmm ... no. No thanks.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: This job is a waste of my time. I'm leaving.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. Be careful out there ― if there really is a base, it's bound to be well guarded.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text:
Oh, whoa, sorry. I'll give you a sec... ahem. All set?

Right, okay, so, yeah, I understand there's a sensitive matter you need some help with? I mean, another sensitive matter? You seemed to have that one well in hand.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
We‘ve found that there was indeed a hidden Gallente base in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but apparently it was dismantled very recently and the location is now abandoned.

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: It certainly is. We shall have to be much more careful with our system scanning in the future.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
{[character]player.name},

Due to your lack of response, I was forced to find another capsuleer to search for the secret base in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Unfortunately, her ship was ambushed by several cloaked Gallente assault cruisers and she was podded in the ensuing firefight. Their base has since been dismantled and the location is now abandoned.

War is brewing, {[character]player.name}. Which side are you on?

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Your hunch was right, {[character]agentID.name}. Good call. There was a base out there. So what the hell does this mean, I wonder?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: But I thought we had a deal!!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I understand completely, {[character]player.name}. But I think the time is near when we shall all have to fight if we value democracy, despite the risks.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: A secret base, eh? Damned Caldari! Alright, I'll go have a look around.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I can't risk my ship when I don't know what might be out there. Hope you understand.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: This is a fool's errand. I'm done.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. Be careful out there ― if there really is a base, it's sure to be well protected.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm told there's an unusual matter you need some help with, {[character]agentID.name}?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
A determined young capsuleer has reported that there was indeed a hidden Caldari base in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but apparently it was dismantled very recently and the location is now abandoned. You are discharged of your duty in this matter.

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Yes, it's all very troubling. We shall have to be much more careful, I fear, we Gallente.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
{[character]player.name},

Due to your lack of a timely response, I was forced to send another capsuleer to search for the secret base in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Unfortunately, his ship was ambushed by several Caldari EW cruisers and she was podded. Their base has since been dismantled and the location is now abandoned.

War is brewing, {[character]player.name}. Whose side are you on?

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've been picking up strange distress signals coming from the site of an old starship battle in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's possible, though unlikely, that there were some survivors aboard one of those wrecked ships and that they've just recently been able to repair their communications systems enough to send out distress signals.

What's more likely, though, is that some explorers or salvage workers got trapped out there, or maybe even that some pirates have set up this phony distress call to lure unsuspecting rescuers out there to their doom. In any case, I want it checked out, just in case there are actually some of our people still out there. Because of the potential danger, though, I'm only willing to send one of our best, most capable pilots out there. And that means you.

Go on out there and see what's causing this signal. You'll be handsomely rewarded for your efforts.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Funny you should ask: I was just about to contact you. Since you're about our best independent capsuleer, I think we need you on this one.

We've been picking up strange distress signals coming from the site of an old starship battle in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, dating back about 8 years or so, where several of our ships were lost. Now, it's possible, though unlikely, that there were some survivors aboard one of those wrecked ships and that they've just recently been able to repair their communications systems enough to send out distress signals. I say it's possible.

What's more likely, though, is that some explorers or salvage workers got trapped out there, or maybe even that some pirates have set up this phony distress call to lure unsuspecting rescuers out to their doom. In any case, I want it checked out, just in case there are actually some of our people still out there. Because of the potential danger, though, I'm only willing to send one of our best, most capable pilots out there. And that means you.

Go on out there and see what's causing this signal. You'll be well rewarded, as always.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: It was a trap, {[character]agentID.name}. The ships were Minmatar, and they seemed to know I'd be there.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I see. Well, that's unfortunate. I don't have many pilots of your caliber to send out on these special assignments.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Yes, well, maybe you are a little more suited to tackling dreadnoughts in that ship of yours, but hey, the ISK was good...

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm on it, {[character]agentID.name}. I'll be back before you know it.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sounds like work for a rookie, as far as I'm concerned. A distress signal? No thanks. Give me some pirates to fight, maybe, or some Minmatar or Gallente!

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Something's come up, I'm afraid, {[character]agentID.name}. Not going to be able to finish this one on time. Sorry.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. My thanks. Do be careful out there ― we have no idea what we're dealing with, really.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Good day, {[character]agentID.name}. You have anything for me?

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Remarkable! Something strange is going on here. Let me see what I can dig up, and then maybe we can take the fight to them.

We've been picking up strange distress signals coming from the site of an old starship battle in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, dating back about 8 years or so, where several of our ships were lost. Now, it's possible, though unlikely, that there were some survivors aboard one of those wrecked ships and that they've just recently been able to repair their communications systems enough to send out distress signals. I say it's possible.

What's more likely, though, is that some explorers or salvage workers got trapped out there, or maybe even that some pirates have set up this phony distress call to lure unsuspecting rescuers out to their doom. In any case, I want it checked out, just in case there are actually some of our people still out there. Because of the potential danger, though, I'm only willing to send one of our best, most capable pilots out there. And that means you.

Go on out there and see what's causing this signal. You'll be well rewarded, as always.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: It was a trap, {[character]agentID.name}. The ships were Caldari, and they seemed to know I'd be there.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I see. Well, that's unfortunate. I don't have many pilots of your caliber to send out on these special assignments.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Yes, well, maybe you are a little more suited to tackling dreadnoughts in that ship of yours, but hey, the ISK was good...

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm on it, {[character]agentID.name}. I'll be back before you know it.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sounds like work for a rookie, as far as I'm concerned. A distress signal? No thanks. Give me some pirates to fight, or some Caldari or Amarr!

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Something's come up, I'm afraid, {[character]agentID.name}. Not going to be able to finish this one on time. Sorry.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. My thanks. Do be careful out there ― we have no idea what we're dealing with, really.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Good day, {[character]agentID.name}. You have anything for me?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I've just received word that the Amarr have actually had the gall to build one of their temple complexes in our space! Well, they're claiming it's their space. And since it's in low-security, we'd be declaring an open act of war by sending in the Republic Navy to remove them. Some day, I think, we'll be ready to do that, but not today.

So what I need you for is this: You know the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system? We cannot allow this humiliating action of theirs to go unpunished. The beauty of sending you in there, as a privateer, is that we can claim complete ignorance. Go there and kill every Amarr you find. Once you've dealt with the defenses, I can send in our people to take care of the rest of the cleanup.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Amarr scum are no more, {[character]agentID.name}. A good fight it was, too.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: {[character]player.name}, we do not always have the luxury of choosing our battles. Think on that. Dangerous times lie ahead. Close ahead.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: “Discretion is the better part of valor,” yes … but it's a fine line between discretion and cowardice.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Those Amarr will pay for their arrogance. I will enjoy this one.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: A fully operational Amarr sanctum? No thanks. You know the kind of defenses they put in place?! It'd be suicide!

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: You'll need to call in someone else on this one, {[character]agentID.name}. The task is beyond me.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Be warned, though: You're likely going to need a few allies. Their “star sanctums” always have strong defenses in place.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Oh? What am I in time for?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Well done. The Amarr will never be fully dealt with until they're extinct, though, I think.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
To complete this mission, you will require a ship with an available cargo capacity of at least 1,000 m3 volume (and preferably 6,000 m3).

So here's what I've been able to find out: The Minmatar have moved, within the past few days, against a number of our free agents such as yourself; unfortunately, not all of the capsuleers they targeted proved as resilient as you. Four of them were podded, may God rest their souls. I don't like this kind of concerted effort on the part of the Minmatar, {[character]player.name}. God knows what it all means.

Now, my spies report, it seems they are growing even more daring, moving against a number of our civilian colonies. With four of our top pilots gone, and even with the Navy pulling its weight, we're going to be hard pressed to protect all of those people. We all need to do our part. I need you to go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} to the civilian outpost there and evacuate those people. Destroy any preliminary Minmatar forces you encounter, get those civilians out of the citizen quarters, and bring them all safely back to me here at {[location]agentStationID.name}.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Well, that distress signal most certainly was a trap ― one intended to catch you. It seems as though the Minmatar have taken notice of a handful of capsuleers who've interfered a great deal with their resistance movement. You're on that list. In fact you show quite highly, if that makes you feel any better.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Alright, the people are safe. Now tell me where to find that Minmatar fleet!

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Those are innocent people out there, {[character]player.name}! And we have no one else!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: {[character]player.name}, whose side are you on, for God‘s sake!?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Dammit, {[character]agentID.name}, these Minmatar are starting to make me angry. They won't like me when I'm angry.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: First an ambush, now a concerted attack against our civilians!? No, I don't think I want any more to do with this Minmatar problem.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Sorry about those civilians, but I can't get there on time. Send in the Navy or something.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: That's good to hear. But remember, your assignment is just to get those civilians to safety. Then we'll think about vengeance.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: What does that mean? What have you found out?

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: That's the spirit, {[character]player.name}. But don't rush in unprepared: This is going to be a tough fight.

I can‘t figure it out. But if it‘s the Federation Navy behind all of this, then it might mean the worst. War.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
This mission is extremely dangerous. You should not undertake it without at least a handful of gang-mates all in powerful, combat-ready ships.

While you were out saving those civilians, the Minmatar, as we suspected they were going to, hit several other habitations; in total, the loss of life is staggering. Casualty reports are still coming in, but already it's numbering in the thousands, and likely it will be tens of thousands by the time we have confirmed intelligence. Thank God you were able to rescue some of our people, at least.

But now it is time to meet these Minmatar in battle. Our scouts report a squad of enemy ships, including carriers, in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Desperate times call for … ah, you know how it goes: I want you to get out there and stop those ships. I'll be honest, {[character]player.name}. I think the likelihood of your returning to me in a new clone is high, but we have no choice ― we must stop them from slaughtering our people. This, like it or not, is war.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I admire your courage, {[character]player.name}, but remember that discretion is the better part of valor. This fleet must be met, yes, but not by a lone ship.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: It was probably the toughest fight of my career, {[character]agentID.name}, but the Minmatar ships are no more. What news?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I see. Very well; I knew this was a difficult task when I sent you. But note this, {[character]player.name}: In war, all must make sacrifices, and no action is too small. And these are not peaceful times.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: {[character]player.name}, this is war! Do you not understand what that means!? I think you capsuleers tend to forget what it is to be human, to have families, children threatened, killed. Phagh! Get out of my sight!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I will stop those ships or clone-jump trying.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: A squadron of capital ships. Are you mad?! How can I do anything but have my ship destroyed? No, a few thousand civilians are not worth that.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: This task is beyond me.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Your name shall be sung among the stars, {[character]player.name}. And your earthly rewards shall be great.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Yes, I know ― there's a capital fleet out there. Now where is it?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Well, we've managed to drive the Minmatar back. The Republic denies all knowledge of the attacks, of course, claiming that the Thukker nomads are responsible. But do not be fooled, {[character]player.name} ― I think war will soon be upon us.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You know the temple complex that was built a few years ago out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}? Well, a bunch of Minmatar slaves, apparently working with outside help from god knows where, have somehow managed to capture this heavily fortified holy place! Yes, unbelievable, I tell you. And now several Minmatar ships from Republic space have joined them there ― yes, in Amarr space! Damn them!

Now they are using our sanctum as a base of operations for their evil business in our space. We cannot allow this humiliating act to go unpunished. Go there and kill them all. Once you've dealt with this matter, I will send in our soldiers to take care of the rest.

It's those damned Minmatar, as usual. As if pirate scum aren't bad enough, but we also have deal with these ungrateful slave folk. I tell you, they've about got me ready to... oh, my ulcer!

You see what happens? Don't ever take a desk job, {[character]player.name}, trust me. Stick to your starships.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: A capsuleer with the sense to admit defeat?? Incredible. I commend you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Oh, to be a capsuleer. “Hm, not interested, thanks.” Life is so easy for you people.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Those Minmatar will rue their interference. Consider it done.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm sorry, but this doesn't sound like any kind of work I'm interested in.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: You'll need to call in the Navy on this one, {[character]agentID.name}. It's beyond me.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Be warned, though: You're likely going to need a few allies. Our sanctum has strong defenses in place.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Oh? What is it that I can do for you?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent. One more lesson taught to the Minmatar. When, I wonder, will they finally learn their place?!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You know the hyperspace complex out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system that the Amarr have been renting from us under treaty? Well, I've just received word that they've actually had the gall to build one of their profane temple complexes in there! In clear breach of the treaty under which they're using the place! And since it's in low-security, we'd be declaring an open act of war by sending in the Federation Navy to remove them.

So what I need you for is this: We cannot allow this disgusting atrocity of theirs to go unpunished. Keeping Minmatar slaves under our very noses! The sheer, unmitigated gall of it!! The beauty of sending you in there, as a privateer, is that we can claim complete ignorance. Go there and destroy every Amarr vessel you find. Once you've dealt with the defenses, I can send in our people to take care of the rest of the cleanup.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Some years ago, the great Emperor Doriam, in the spirit of co-operation and generosity, allowed some Minmatar refugees to set up home in a former Ammatar station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They were not enslaved, but have been allowed to live free folk, as long as they maintained an excise quota on all of their trade. We have allowed them to continue thus in order to honor the reforms undertaken by Emperor Doriam, but recently one of their number took it upon himself to resist an Imperial customs inspection of their homes, killing the officer in question.

The Minmatar attempted to cover it all up, of course, but we soon got to the bottom of the matter. As they have thrown aside our goodwill and struck down one of the Chosen, the Navy has been ordered to dispense God's judgment upon the heathens. The Admiralty, however, feels that this job is best undertaken by a loyal but independent pilot, rather than official Navy forces, and we have chosen you to dispense with our punishment.

Fly to the coordinates provided and destroy any resistance, so that I can send transports in there to bring back the entire population of the habitats, women, children, and all. After that, destroy all the colony structures, and we will then, in our divine mercy, place any survivors into slavery ― if any are innocent ― and begin them on their path to glorious enlightenment through proper service to the Empire.

Now, we have had reports of Minmatar Republic ships in the area, likely attempting to evacuate the inhabitants: If you are fired upon, you have all authority to defend yourself by any means necessary … and by that, I mean kill them all. God's will be done.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: We do not always have the luxury of choosing our battles. When war comes calling, will you simply bow out?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Hm. And here I was under the impression that we all served the Empire. You may be a capsuleer, but you are no emperor.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Given freedom, Minmatar will always show their true colors. Yes, I'll happily help to reclaim these infidels for you.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Surely this task is beneath me. Spend my time against some piddling Minmatar fleet? I, who destroy battle stations as a matter of course?

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Perhaps you'd best send in the Navy after all, {[character]agentID.name}. The task is beyond me.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good, then. Be careful out there: The Minmatar ships in the area are reportedly numerous and powerful.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Very kind of you, {[character]agentID.name}. I understand you have some work for me?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Well done. Let us hope they can serve the Empire better now, as do we all.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Some years ago, the late Amarr Emperor Doriam ―probably the only enlightened Amarrian to ever have lived ― built an Amarr habitation station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} as a gesture of goodwill. Minmatar were welcomed there and were not enslaved, but have been allowed to live free folk. However, recent governors in that station started to levy outrageous excises on all Minmatar tradesfolk and goods there. Things quickly turned ugly, and recently one of our people got in a fight with an Imperial customs agent; things escalated, and our man ended up killing the officer in question. Knowing what was coming, we managed to evacuate the rest of our people, but the situation is far from resolved.

As you might have guessed, the Amarr have taken this event as cause for military action. They've sent in a number of heavily armed ships, and we fear they're going to try to use the colony as a base of operations for surface raids on nearby planets, taking whatever Minmatar they can as slaves when they leave. We can't let that happen. The Republic Fleet has its hands tied, since any action on their part would result in open war, and we're just not ready for that yet. I need you to get in there!

Fly to the coordinates provided and destroy any resistance, and then destroy the colony structures so the Amarr can't use them. We have had reports of many Amarr ships in the area: If you are fired upon, as is likely, you have all authority to defend yourself by any means necessary … and by that, I mean kill them all.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Of course, {[character]agentID.name}. I'll happily clear out the Amarr scum for you.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Amarr may not declare open war against the Republic, but they'll certainly send their assassins after a lone captain. No thanks ― no targets on my head!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Very kind of you, {[character]agentID.name}. I hear you might have some work for me?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Well done. Let's see the Amarrians try to cover up their political machinations now that their ships were destroyed by “unidentified pirates,” eh? Ha!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Some weird disease has spread through a civilian colony out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We quarantined it and sent some scientists in there to study the disease, and they've determined that it's a virus that mutates too quickly to be safely controlled.

The trouble is, some Gallente businessman caught wind of this and has figured out that he can make a profit by getting samples and selling the virus to their military as a weapon. Now, our scientists assure us that the risk is too high without a great deal more research and testing, which is already underway. But we sure as hell don't want the Gallente getting their hands on this stuff.

Trouble is, this Gallente person, or corporation, or whatever, has already moved on it, paying off some government official and thus getting permission to send in mercenary ships to secure the area. We can't send in our military for fear of political repercussions, so I need someone like you to deal with this matter for me.

Fly to the coordinates provided and destroy any Gallente ships there, and then destroy all the colony structures so no one else gets any ideas about collecting samples of this biological weapon. Now, we've had reports of some tough ships in their fleet: Be careful out there, but be sure to kill them all. We don't want any of them escaping with this virus.

Well, we seem to have a bit of a situation here, and I'm hoping you can help me out. You see, some civilian living in a colony complex out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} brought some creature home from a nearby planet ― I guess he was part of a work detail there or something ― and apparently it was a carrier for some weird disease that quickly spread through the colony. We quarantined the colony and sent some scientists in there to contain and study the disease, and they've determined that it's a virus that mutates too quickly to be safely controlled.

The trouble is, some Gallente businessman ― we haven't found out who yet ― caught wind of this and has figured out that he can make a profit by getting samples and selling the virus to their military as a weapon. Now, the idea had crossed our minds too, of course, but our scientists assure us that the risk is too high without a great deal more research and testing, which is already underway. But we sure as hell don't want the Gallente getting their hands on this stuff.

We'll cove the whole thing up as an act of piracy, and it'll soon be forgotten. Besides, we already have samples of the virus for ourselves.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: All done, {[character]agentID.name}. The enemy ships are destroyed, along with the colony itself.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Are you saying you can't do it? Alright, alright, fine. I'll get someone else.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Well, you'd have been at no personal risk, I assure you. But fine, suit yourself.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sure, sounds easy enough. Blow some stuff up. I can do that real well. I'm in.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Biological warfare? Incurable diseases? Uhhm, I think maybe I'll pass on this one. Thanks anyway.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I think you'd better hire one of the big mercenary companies for this one. Mordu's, maybe, or some other goons?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. But I must repeat: The Gallente ships in the area are reportedly numerous and powerful. Be careful.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Thank you, {[character]agentID.name}. What can I do for you?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I knew I could trust you to get the job done. Good work. Now let's keep this whole matter between you and me, okay?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Some weird disease has spread through a civilian colon complex in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We quarantined it and sent some scientists in there to contain and study the disease, and they've determined that it's a virus that mutates too quickly to be safely controlled.

The trouble is, some Caldari corporation caught wind of the problem and has figured out that it can make a profit by getting samples and selling the virus to their military as a weapon. However, our scientists assure us that the risk is too high without a great deal more research and testing. And we sure as hell don't want the Caldari getting their hands on this stuff.

Trouble is, this Caldari corporation has already moved on the civilian complex, no doubt bribing some government official to get permission to send in mercenary ships and thus secure the area. We can't send in our military for fear of political repercussions, so I need someone like you to deal with this matter for me.

Fly to the coordinates provided and destroy any Caldari ships there, and then destroy all the colony structures so no one else gets any ideas about collecting samples of this biological weapon. Be careful out there, but be sure to kill them all, and leave no colony structures intact. We don't want anyone escaping with this virus.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Well, we seem to have a bit of a situation here, and I'm hoping you can help me out. You see, some civilian living in a colony complex out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} brought some creature home from a nearby planet ― I guess he was part of a work detail there or something ― and apparently it was a carrier for some weird disease that quickly spread through the colony. We quarantined the colony and sent some scientists in there to contain and study the disease, and they've determined that it's a virus that mutates too quickly to be safely controlled.

The trouble is, some Caldari corporation ― we haven't found out who exactly ― caught wind of this and has figured out that it can make a profit by getting samples and selling the virus to their military as a weapon. However, our scientists assure us that the risk is too high without a great deal more research and testing. But we sure as hell don't want the Caldari getting their hands on this stuff.

Trouble is, this Caldari corporation has already moved on the civilian complex, no doubt bribing some government official to get permission to send in mercenary ships and thus secure the area. We can't send in our military for fear of political repercussions, so I need someone like you to deal with this matter for me.

Fly to the coordinates provided and destroy any Caldari ships there, and then destroy all the colony structures so no one else gets any ideas about collecting samples of this biological weapon. We'll cove the whole thing up as an act of piracy, and it'll soon be forgotten. Especially by you and me. Right? Okay.

Now, we've had reports of some tough ships in their fleet: Be careful out there, but be sure to kill them all, and leave no colony structures intact. We don't want anyone escaping with this virus.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: All done, {[character]agentID.name}. The enemy ships are destroyed, along with the colony itself.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Are you saying you can't do it? Alright, alright, fine. I'll get someone else.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Well, you'd have been at no personal risk, I assure you. But fine, suit yourself.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sure, sounds easy enough. Blow some stuff up. I can do that real well. I'm in.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Biological warfare? Incurable diseases? Uhhm, I think maybe I'll pass on this one. Thanks anyway.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I think you'd better hire one of the big mercenary companies for this one. I might just be out of my league here.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. But I must repeat: The Caldari ships in the area are reportedly numerous and powerful. Be careful.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Thank you, {[character]agentID.name}. What can I do for you?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I knew I could trust you to get the job done. Good work. Now let's keep this whole matter between you and me, okay?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I recently sent a capsuleer out to investigate disturbing reports from the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system: The number of missing persons cases on some outlying planets there has risen sharply and there have even been reports of lost ships. My capsuleer returned, unfortunately in his pod, but my suspicions were confirmed. What he reported is very disturbing, and we need someone with resources such as you possess to deal with it.

It appears an unprincipled Amarrian Holder has set up a heavily guarded slave breeding facility there. {[character]player.name}, go to this facility, rescue as many of my people as you can, and then reduce the place to cinders! Kill every Amarrian there ― make them pay for what they have done. Leave nothing intact, nothing ― the facilities least of all, lest some other Amarrian come in and occupy them!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I recently sent a capsuleer out to investigate disturbing reports from the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system: The number of missing persons cases on some outlying planets there has risen sharply and there have even been reports of lost ships. The locals are a superstitious lot, so they blame it on angering some spirit or other, but I have no such beliefs ― I suspect foul play. My capsuleer returned, unfortunately in his pod, but my suspicions were confirmed. What he reported is very disturbing, and we need someone with resources such as you possess to deal with it.

It appears an unprincipled Amarrian Holder has set up a heavily guarded slave breeding facility there. You cannot know the sheer horror of these places, our people penned and bred like cattle; the men sold or sent to work camps, the women used mercilessly. The owner no doubt felt that the place would remain undetected in unregulated space, so close here to a ready supply of … well, what I'm sure they would refer to as “livestock.”

{[character]player.name}, go to this facility, rescue as many of my people as you can, and then reduce the place to cinders! Kill every Amarrian there ― make them pay for what they have done. Leave nothing intact, nothing ― the facilities least of all, lest some other Amarrian come in and occupy them!

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've rescued the slaves and destroyed the facility.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: That's truly unfortunate. Now what am I supposed to do?!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Well, I see where your priorities lie…. Good day.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Don't worry, I'll make every one of them pay in blood.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
This type of breeding facility produces Minmatar children ready to assume their place as servants to the Amarr; rumors abound that the slaves in these places hail from other races as well, including even fallen Amarr who are sent here rather than to penal colonies. 
Brood slaves are held within breeder colonies for years for the sole purpose of increasing a slaver's stock. Discarded when they have outlived their usefulness, these poor people have a terribly short life expectancy, although that fact might be a blessing when one considers the misery of their existence. Slavers who use such methods tend to be secretive about it, anchoring their breeding centers in low-security space; these facilities, however profitable, are looked down upon even in Amarrian society (especially since the Doriam reforms).

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I sympathize with the plight of those people, of course, but take on an entire slaver complex by myself? That's suicide. Clones are too expensive for that.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I feel bad about those poor people, but the defenses at that compound are beyond me. I give up.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: See to it. Get those poor people out of that hellhole!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Oh, yeah? What's the problem?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
{[character]player.name},

Scouts inform me that the station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} has been evacuated and disassembled. No doubt the Holder who owned the place caught wind of our efforts, and your tardiness has allowed him time to remove his operation to another system.

May the fates of those slaves weigh on your soul.

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Ah, wonderful. I knew you wouldn't fail. Justice has been done.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
A couple of years ago, the Serpentis Corporation built a station out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and everyone in the constellation has been worried about it since. At first, as always with the Serpentis, things were fine ― they kept up a clean front and acted like a legitimate corporation. More recently, though, they've been pirating nearby gates and causing all kinds of problems for the local police forces. CONCORD intervention is minimal, of course, in low-sec, and they're always careful to make things seem like some other pirate group is responsible.

These raids must be stopped. And here's an interesting thing: Interstellar law states that an unoccupied station can be freely commandeered. And that Serpentis station apparently has some state-of-the-art tech that we'd like to get our hands on. So that's why I need you: {[character]player.name}, I want you to head out there and destroy every damned Serpentis you find there so we can go in and claim the station for our own.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes, indeed. I think the job I have here requires someone of your unique talents.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Serpentis station is defenseless. Good fight, that was.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: {[character]player.name}, this was our first real opportunity to strike back at those bloody pirates. I can't believe this!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Wow, take it easy. I just asked. No harm in asking, is there?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Oh, yeah, take out some Serpentis? For sure! I hate those guys!

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The Serpentis Corporation was founded a few decades ago by V. Salvador Sarpati. At first a legitimate corporation, it was engaged in hi-tech research, but with time its ties to organized crime grew and the Serpentis research stations, scattered around in remote areas, became infamous pirate havens. Sarpati made a deal with the Angel Cartel early on to gain protection for his stations, and the duty was taken on by the Guardian Angels. Both sides have prospered enormously from this deal ― Serpentis can operate in peace, and the Angel Cartel gets access to the illegal research efforts of the Serpentis.

It is strongly believed that Serpentis is the largest developer and manufacturer of illegal neural boosters, especially since Sarpati's father was a renowned specialist in that field. The home of the Serpentis criminal organization is the Phoenix constellation in the Fountain region.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: A Serpentis battle station, and you want me to go in there? Are you mad?! Uh... no! As if...!!

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've reconsidered your offer, and I've found it wanting. Sorry, I‘m out.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I knew I could count on you, {[character]player.name}. Do be careful, though. It won't be an easy job.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Many thanks. I came as soon as I got your message. Is there something I can help you with?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Ha! Well done! I knew you wouldn't let me down, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Some of the top cybernetics experts in the region were recently here at {[location]agentStationID.name} for a conference, and they made me a proposal that I found quite intriguing. These scientists theorize that the Sansha mindslave technology is leaps ahead of anything we currently have in the realm of cerebro-emission communications. You might call what they've got a sort of limited telepathy, I suppose. Anyway, these scientists were having heated arguments about the risks and benefits of toying with Sansha tech. And that's where it gets interesting.

A handful of them approached me after the conference and spoke of a Sansha base in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that they had learned of. They asked if I knew any ships' captains who might be interested in “acquiring” a few Sansha mindslaves for them to experiment on. Now, a friend in the Admiralty tells me the Navy is apparently planning to move against this station very soon, so our window of opportunity is narrow. We'd be doing the authorities a favor, and getting a little something on the side.

Destroy a Sansha tower and pick up some prisoners. What could be easier?

So what do you think? Sound like something you're interested in? Destroy a Sansha tower and pick up some prisoners. What could be easier?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Sansha Battletower is no more, {[character]agentID.name}, and the prisoners are here in station.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Blast it! Oh, fine. I'm sure I can find someone else to share the reward with me.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I understand your reticence, but think of the ISK! Ah, well, your loss.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sansha prisoners, eh? Well, I can set my cargo bay to keep them in cryo-containment, I suppose. Sure, I'm in.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't think I care to bring Sansha aboard my ship, thanks very much. No, find someone else.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I think I'd rather not finish this mission. Sorry, second thoughts: Sansha are too creepy.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. I'll await your return with bated breath … and a heap of ISK.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Thank you, {[character]agentID.name}. I trust you are well. You have some work for me?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Well done. I'll send the reward directly to your Interstellar account.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
{[character]player.name}, an employee of ours, Solen Sagul, has been acting a little odd lately; he comes and goes at strange hours and doesn't say where he is going or where he's been, but he often takes company ships and disappears for days at a time. We are lucky if he shows up for meetings, and when he does appear he utters the strangest things, completely inappropriate and ... well, just unsettling. We could deal with it if we thought he was just insane, but we are afraid it's more than that.

You've heard those stories about people taken alive into rogue drone hives? Well, one of Sagul's co-workers claims he heard the man muttering something about “the hive mother” and “the song of the drones.” We need to be sure that Sagul has not been ... taken by the drones. We had security look around in his logs and they found this location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that he's visited several times in the past months. It's a dark, nasty part of space, though, and I can't send just anyone: Maybe you can take a look and tell us what you find.

Oh, and if you do find anything remarkable there, I need you to get in close and have a good look before you report back to me.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Oh, not much, really... er, well, now, wait! Actually, that's not entirely true. In fact, maybe this is something you could help me out with ― I don't know why I didn't think of you sooner.

{[character]player.name}, an employee of ours, Solen Sagul, has been acting a little odd lately; he comes and goes at strange hours and doesn't say where he is going or where he's been, but he often takes company ships and disappears for days at a time. We are lucky if he shows up for meetings, and when he does appear he utters the strangest things, completely inappropriate and ... well, just unsettling. We could deal with it if we thought he was just insane, but we are afraid it's more than that.

You've heard those stories about people taken alive into rogue drone hives? Well, one of Sagul's co-workers claims he heard the man muttering something about “the hive mother” and “the song of the drones.” We need to be sure that Sagul has not been ... taken by the drones. We had security look around in his logs and they found this location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that he's visited several times in the past months. It's a dark, nasty part of space, though, and I can't send just anyone: Maybe you can take a look and tell us what you find.

Oh, and if you do find anything remarkable there, I need you to get in close and have a good look before you report back to me.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Well, you were certainly right about the drones: There were a ton of them out there, along with some kind of huge structure. I cleaned the place out, though, so no worries.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You know, a quitter is just another kind of loser.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Fine, be that way. But I assure you, there's more to these stories than most would care to admit.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sure, seems easy enough. I assume the ISK's good, as usual?

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: People taken by drones? Yeah, right. No, I think I'll pass on this one.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: This is crazy, {[character]agentID.name}. I can't finish this job for you.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Yes, of course. You might run into some trouble out there, so be careful.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Good day, {[character]agentID.name}. A pleasure to be back here at the {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} offices. Anything new?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
{[character]player.name},

Unfortunately, Solen Sagul has disappeared entirely. Because I hadn‘t heard anything from you, I hired a recon ship to go check the location I told you about in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}; there were signs of drone activity there, but little else. I guess, if there was something more there, it‘s gone now.

I‘m sure you have good reason for not getting this job done on time, but in the future ... do try to be a little more prompt.

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Well, that's good news. But I have bad news too. Just give me a moment to finish up here and I'll explain...

messages.mission.briefing.text:
It seems some cybernetics experts among the Caldari and the god-fearing Amarr have recently made efforts to acquire Sansha mindslave technology. Now, we don't know what they're after, specifically, but we can't afford to let them jump ahead of us. We have a couple of sympathizers among them who we think we can convince to defect, so maybe they can keep us up to date on what has transpired with this Sansha research.

Anyway, we know of a Sansha base in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and a friend of mine in the Admiralty tells me the Navy is apparently planning to move against this base very soon, so I've devised a plan. Our window of opportunity is narrow, so you'd need to be ready to move fast. We'd be doing the authorities a favor, and allowing our people to remain abreast of the most current scientific theory.

You seem a little confused. Oh, I guess I haven't really filled you in on my little brainstorm… Heh. Ok, here it is: Go out there, destroy the Sansha tower, and pick up some prisoners to bring back here. Easy enough, right?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Blast it! Oh, fine. I'm sure I can find someone else to assist me in this.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I understand your reticence, but think of the benefit to science! Ah, well, forget it, then. I'll find someone…

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sansha prisoners, eh? Well, I can set my cargo bay to keep them in cryo-containment, I suppose. Sure, I'm in.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't think I care to bring Sansha aboard my ship, thanks very much. No, find someone else.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I think I'd rather not finish this mission. Sorry, second thoughts: Sansha are too creepy.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. I'll look forward to your victorious return.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Thank you, {[character]agentID.name}. I trust you are well. You have some work for me?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
{[character]player.name},

Unfortunately, the Navy moved in and obliterated the Sansha Battletower in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I guess there are always more Sansha, though.

Oh, that's an awful thought…

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Fine work. I've managed to scrape together a suitable reward for your work. Thanks, my friend.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
Sorry, {[character]player.name}, but I had to hire some mercenaries to get the Sansha prisoners from {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} before the Navy got in there. My apologies, but you were simply taking too long.

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Solen Sagul found a way to sneak back into the research facility here in {[location]agentStationID.name}; he got the help of some old friends in the corporation who had no idea he is ... changed. The problem is that he managed to slip out with copies of some preliminary design documents for a prototype battleship that's going to be built here in the station next year. I take it I don't have to tell you how valuable these documents are, nor what would happen if they fall into the wrong hands.

Now, we managed to get a tracking beacon painted onto Sagul's ship as he blasted out of here, and one of our scanning engineers was then able to track him to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We sent a recon pilot out there, and she was able to pick up some heavy drone activity. We need those copies of the design documents destroyed, {[character]player.name}, along with Sagul and all of his “friends.” If you get out there and he isn't around, don't worry: He's bound to show his face out there eventually.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Wha― Whe― Why? What? Is that a threat?! You may be a capsuleer, {[character]player.name}, but you're not a god! Remember that!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Do you not care about the danger these drones pose if they can control people and steal our most advanced starship plans?! This isn't day-camp, pilot!

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm done with this crappy job and I'm leaving, {[character]agentID.name}, and I don't think you'll want to try to stop me.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. I won't say I'm relieved, at least not yet, but I am glad you're on this job. Be careful: Those drones are sure to put up a hell of a fight.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Thanks. You seem worried. What's the problem?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Inettria Volur found a way to sneak back into the research facility here in {[location]agentStationID.name}; she got the help of some old friends in the corporation who had no idea she's ... changed. The problem is that she managed to slip out with copies of some preliminary design documents for a prototype battleship that's going to be built here in the station next year. I take it I don't have to tell you how valuable these documents are, nor what would happen if they fall into the wrong hands.

Now, we managed to get a tracking beacon painted onto Volur's ship as she blasted out of here, and one of our scanning engineers was then able to track her to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We sent a recon pilot out there, and he was able to pick up some heavy drone activity. We need those copies of the design documents destroyed, {[character]player.name}, along with Volur and all of her “friends.” If you get out there and she isn't around, don't worry: She's bound to show her face out there eventually.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
{[character]player.name}, an employee of ours, Dimitri Ulanus, has been acting a little odd lately; he comes and goes at strange hours and doesn't say where he is going or where he's been, but he often takes company ships and disappears for days at a time. We are lucky if he shows up for meetings, and when he does appear he utters the strangest things, completely inappropriate and ... well, just unsettling. We could deal with it if we thought he was just insane, but we are afraid it's more than that.

You've heard those stories about people taken alive into rogue drone hives? Well, one of Ulanus's co-workers claims he heard the man muttering something about “the hive mother” and “the song of the drones.” We need to be sure that Ulanus has not been ... taken by the drones. We had security look around in his logs and they found this location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that he's visited several times in the past months. It's a dark, nasty part of space, though, and I can't send just anyone: Maybe you can take a look and tell us what you find.

Oh, and if you do find anything remarkable there, I need you to get in close and have a good look before you report back to me.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The Sebiestor tribe hails from the inhospitable steppes of the Mikramurka continent in the northern arctic region on the Minmatar homeworld of Matar. The Sebiestors are the most technically inclined of the Minmatar tribes; they were at the forefront in the tentative space exploration program the Minmatars were undertaking just before the Amarrians arrived to subjugate them. Today, most Minmatar ships, and especially stations, tend to be engineered by Sebiestors.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The oligarchic Caldari State stands for corporate capitalism in its purest form. There are eight great “mega-corporations” that together own more than 90 percentage of all property within the State. Each corporation is made up of thousands of companies of various sizes, each with any number of specific market interests, ranging from simple mining companies to powerful security companies. There is no single, unified government as such; each megacorp rules its territories like a kingdom with little or no interference from the others. 
The eight major corporations are Kaalakiota, Sukuuvestaa, Nugoeihuvi, Ishukone, Wiyrkomi, Hyasyoda, CBD, and Lai Dai.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The Amarr Empire has had its share of religious cults and fanatics in the past, but few have been as successful, or as much feared, as the Blood Raiders. The Raiders are a corrupted sect of an ancient cult called Sani Sabik, which historically used human blood in its rituals. The Blood Raiders believe that cloned bodies have “purer” blood than other bodies, and this explains their penchant for operating mainly in space, attacking unwary spacefarers and draining their bodies of blood.

The Blood Raiders are led by the fearsome Omir Sarikusa, who has remained on top of the DED most wanted list for many years now. Under his leadership, the Raiders have become more organized, and they have firmly established several bases in the Bleak Lands region.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The Serpentis Corporation was founded a few decades ago by V. Salvador Sarpati. At first a legitimate corporation, it was engaged in hi-tech research, but with time its ties to organized crime grew and the Serpentis research stations, scattered around in remote areas, became infamous pirate havens. Sarpati made a deal with the Angel Cartel early on to gain protection for his stations, and the duty was taken on by the Guardian Angels. Both sides have prospered enormously from this deal ― Serpentis can operate in peace, and the Angel Cartel gets access to the illegal research efforts of the Serpentis.

It is strongly believed that Serpentis is the largest developer and manufacturer of illegal neural boosters, especially since Sarpati's father was a renowned specialist in that field. The home of the Serpentis criminal organization is the Phoenix constellation in the Fountain region.

The Angels are divided into several groups, each with a very special function; the organization as a whole is commanded by the “Dominations.” In the century they've been lurking in deep space, they have stolen, plundered, or sabotaged countless ships and kidnapped, harassed, or murdered thousands of people.

The Angels recruit members from all races, and are thus not bound to any one area of operation; their touch reaches almost the entire known EVE universe. Many believe that the Angels got their power by uncovering Jovian technologies hidden in their ancient homes, now infested by the Angel Cartel.

One of our patrols spotted a Mordu's Legion strike force not far from here. We have since received intelligence confirming that the Legion has been hired to assassinate one of our high-ranking officials. We can't let this happen, of course, so we need someone of your caliber to destroy them all. Make sure no one survives.

Of course, we ourselves have used the Legion in the past for … well, for various things. So we don't want to make a big political scene out of this if we ever have to hire them in the future. That's why we mustn't send one of our own ships out to confront them. No, you're the right one for this job. Leave no trace behind; I don't want this biting us in the ass later on.

Oh, and one other thing: Our spies inform us that Taisu Magdesh might actually be part of the Mordu strike force, so be extra careful if he appears ― his reputation is hard won.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The origin of Mordu's Legion is an indirect result of the Gallente-Caldari War, during which a group of Intaki military personnel sided with the Caldari. The Intakis were placed into a separate unit commanded by a Caldari officer named Mordu. After the war, the Intakis settled in Caldari space, but unwillingly became embroiled in a battle against Caldari locals in what is now known as the Waschi Uprising. Mordu's Legion formed at that time as a mercenary fighting force, and after the uprising it stayed active, working for the highest bidder ― but, it is said, acting always with integrity and honor.

Mordu's Legion is loosely associated with the Caldari Navy, but remains independent. The Legion is commonly hired by companies to protect valuable assets in low-security space, most often near the Caldari State; for instance, Outer Ring Excavations pays the Legion handsomely to patrol the Outer Ring region.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Mordu's Legion? An assassination force? Uh, this sounds like some serious shit, so … no. No thanks.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've decided not to do this job for you after all ― no hard feelings, I hope?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Wonderful. Of course, {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} will pay well for this job ― the Mordus are no easy fare.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Well, I had heard that you might have some work for me.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
One of our patrols spotted a Mordu's Legion strike force not far from here. We have since received intelligence confirming that the Legion has been hired to assassinate one of our high-ranking officials. We can't let this happen, of course, so we need someone of your caliber to destroy them all. Make sure no one survives.

Of course, we ourselves have used the Legion in the past for … well, for various things. So we don't want to make a big political scene out of this if we ever have to hire them in the future. That's why we mustn't send one of our own ships out to confront them. No, you're the right one for this job. Leave no trace behind; I don't want this biting us in the ass later on.

Oh, and one other thing: Our spies inform us that Taisu Magdesh might actually be part of the Mordu strike force, so be extra careful if he appears ― his reputation is hard won.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thank you very much, {[character]player.name}. You have saved us from the assassination attempt and guaranteed that this didn't turn into a political blunder.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Done. Missile-spamming monkeys are easy, be they some dumb mercenaries or bell boys for the Caldari State. It's all the same to me.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Hard feelings? No. Some concern? Yeah, I'm definitely what you might call concerned.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: One wonders why certain capsuleers ever bother to get impressive ships when they don't seem to want to fly them…

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Don't worry; I'll take care of it.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The origin of Mordu's Legion is an indirect result of the Gallente-Caldari War, during which a group of Intaki military personnel sided with the Caldari. The Intakis were placed into a separate unit commanded by a Caldari officer named Mordu. After the war, the Intakis settled in Caldari space, but unwillingly became embroiled in a battle against Caldari locals in what is now known as the Waschi Uprising. Mordu's Legion formed at that time as a mercenary fighting force, and after the uprising it stayed active, working for the highest bidder ― but, it is said, acting always with integrity and honor.

Mordu's Legion is loosely associated with the Caldari Navy, but remains independent. The Legion is commonly hired by companies to protect valuable assets in low-security space, most often near the Caldari State; for instance, Outer Ring Excavations pays the Legion handsomely to patrol the Outer Ring region.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Mordu's Legion? An assassination force? Uh, this sounds like some serious shit, so … no. No thanks.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've decided not to do this job for you after all ― no hard feelings, I hope?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Wonderful. Of course, {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} will pay well for this job ― the Mordus are no easy fare.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ha! Upset!? That‘s an understatement. How would you feel if you had just learned that the Angel Cartel had just taken possession of a battle station in the same constellation you live in with your family?! Bad news, I tell you. And it gets worse. Angel ruffians have been showing up in stations all through the system, and in nearby systems too, I hear, pushing some new, experimental drug they're making by the shipload in this station of theirs. “Wrath,” they're calling it. It's too much, I tell you. I need a drink.

Okay, that's a little better. Now, let me fill you in: A couple of years ago, the Serpentis Corporation built a research station out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and that was bad enough. Things were alright at first, despite the Serpentis‘ reputation, but then rumors started spreading that they were making drugs there, not doing any kind of real research.

And then some local freight-runners reported seeing cargo ships pouring in and out of the place, and the station started expanding, adding sentries and missile batteries, and, inevitably, Angel and Serpentis ships started frequenting the place. Piracy ramped up in local shipping lanes. And now this: We find out that the Serpentis have moved on and pretty much left the place in the hands of the Angels.

Now, last week, a friend told me that a couple of scientists who work for his pharmaceutical corporation were kidnapped by the Angels and taken to their glorified floating drug lab. That's the last straw. I want something done about this, and the Navy doesn't seem to care about what's going on. So I've arranged for a nice little reward for the first captain who's willing to go out there and take out that station. I'm serious. Destroy the whole place, and take out all the pirates you see flying around there. And if you can, bring those scientists back here, too; they have families to feed, for god's sake!

{[character]player.name}, are you the capsuleer for this job?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Angel station is destroyed. And I earned every bit of that reward!

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: We can only hope, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Well, it was a long shot. I just hope some other semi-suicidal starship captain is up for the reward...

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Angels? For sure! I hate those guys!

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Operating from the heart of the Curse region, the Angel Cartel is today the largest and best organized of the space-based criminal factions. The Angels are divided into several groups, each with a very special function; the organization as a whole is commanded by the Domination Angels.

The Salvation Angels are the least combative division of the Angel Cartel. They are responsible for building and maintaining the Angels' stations and space ships. To this end, they frequently travel with Angel raiding parties in support ships, salvaging what they need from the wrecks their fellow Angels have left in their wake.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: An Angel battle station? Are you nuts?! Uh, ah no...

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've changed my mind. I‘m sure you can find someone else crazy enough to tackle an Angel battle station.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I knew I could count on you, {[character]player.name}. Be careful out there. It won't be easy.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I've just learned that an Amarr military convoy has somehow “strayed” into our space. Preliminary scans reveal multiple freighter-class vessels with a large escort. Intelligence has informed us that this is a munitions convoy they've been hearing about for some time, but which until now has somehow managed to avoid direct monitoring until sometime yesterday. Intel's theory is made pretty concrete by virtue of the large guard force attached to the Amarr fleet.

This is an opportunity we cannot pass up. The bulk of the convoy is currently sitting in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system waiting for supply ships to catch up for refueling. I want you to intercept the convoy and destroy it before it can leave our territory; the way our interstellar relations stand right now, those weapons they're carrying could easily be turned on us within the year. If this attack is undertaken by independents ? that is, you and whatever allies you can pull in for this mission … and I'd advise you to bring some friends in for this one ? we can easily claim no knowledge of the matter.

Now, we've had a couple of cloaked recon pilots set up jamming beacons in the vicinity to disrupt the Amarrians' communications, so they shouldn't be able to get a distress call out or hail one another when you attack. The rest is up to you. Destroy every last one of the Amarrian ships: I want no survivors. Leave no trace.

Intelligence has informed us that this is a munitions convoy they've been hearing about for some time, but which until now has somehow managed to avoid direct monitoring until sometime yesterday. Intel's theory is made pretty concrete by virtue of the large guard force attached to the Gallente fleet.

This is an opportunity we cannot pass up. The bulk of the convoy is currently sitting in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system waiting for supply ships to catch up for refueling. I want you to intercept the convoy and destroy it before it can leave our territory; the way our interstellar relations stand right now, those weapons they're carrying could easily be turned on us within the year. If this attack is undertaken by independents ? that is, you and whatever allies you can pull in for this mission … and I'd advise you to bring some friends in for this one ? we can easily claim no knowledge of the matter.

Now, we've had a couple of cloaked recon pilots set up jamming beacons in the vicinity to disrupt the Gallenteans' communications, so they shouldn't be able to get a distress call out or hail one another when you attack. The rest is up to you. Destroy every last one of the Gallente ships: I want no survivors. Leave no trace.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: It was a tough one, alright, but the Gallentean weapons convoy is destroyed.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: What!? This was a grand opportunity to knock the Gallente down a peg. And now I have you to thank for letting it slip by.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: {[character]player.name}, I‘d heard you were unstoppable. Well, I guess I should know better than to believe everything I hear.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Fair enough. Sounds like a good fight. Consider it done.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I think destroying an entire military convoy under heavy escort is a little beyond me. Sorry.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: On second thought, I'm going to pass on this mission. A heavily escorted military convoy is a little over the top.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Remember, captain, no survivors.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Glad to be here. Any insurmountable obstacles that need removing?

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent. Most excellent. Good work out there, captain.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've been having problems with a Sansha outpost for a while now. I've finally received clearance to sponsor a raid on the facility. I guess someone got tired of paying for new haulers.

So how about it? Get some of your capsuleer buddies together and destroy every Sansha you find. You'll be a hero; and since the Sansha are all unholy mockeries of all that is human, you don't even have to feel bad about killing them!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: It's done.  We wiped every one of the Sansha out.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Do you have any idea how much these Sansha are costing us on a weekly basis? Never mind. I guess I'll have to contract one of the mercenary companies to take care of it.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Not diving in?  What, are you afraid of a few explosions?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sansha, huh?  Yeah, I think I know some people who might want to space a few.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Sansha's Nation is just this side of rogue drones-- in some ways the Nation is worse. At least drones are machines acting like they're alive. Sansha were people; now they act like machines. Best thing about both is that you can blow the hell out of them and still maintain a clear moral high ground.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Moral high ground or not, I'm not diving into a nest of Sansha.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I was all for clearing out the Sansha, but there were just too many of them.  I have to quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Glad to hear it.  Happy hunting.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: What's this about Sansha?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: I can't wait for you to finish off those Sansha.  Too much pressure from above, you understand.  I have to pass the contract along to a professional mercenary corp.  You just weren't fast enough.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I wish I was there to see it.  There's nothing quite as satisfying as watching the explosive decompression of an enemy ship.  Hope you had fun.  Oh, and thanks for saving all the civvies in system from the Sansha threat, or whatever.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: You can't make up your mind in a timely fashion; I can't just sit on this offer.  The job's moved on to a merc corp.  Now you'll have to watch someone else have all the fun.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Lately, our scouts and agents have been reporting increasing numbers of rogue drones, not just here, but throughout civilized space. We think they are building up for a massive attack in all the empires. Who knows what their goal is, really. Honestly I don't care about what the drones do elsewhere, but I want our sovereign space cleared of these machines.

Some recon scans I received yesterday indicate there's a sizeable drone colony being built in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Go out there, {[character]player.name}, and clean that hive out. I hate vermin, maybe even more than I hate the idea of those damned Jovians ― at least they are somewhat human.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Just in time for a job that requires a capsuleer of your skill.

You've been working for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} long enough that I think I can trust you with this ... situation. You know we try to keep our eyes on pretty much everything and everyone. You know how it is with vermin ― once they get a foothold, there is no stopping them. Hopefully you can deal with them in time before we are overrun by those infernal things and no ships are safe.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Very well. But I think you gravely underestimate the threat these drones represent.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Glad to hear it. Don't be afraid to hurt their feelings. They have none.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work, {[character]player.name}. That's one less thing I have to worry about.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I just received an emergency communication from an insider in the Quafe Corporation. Perhaps you've heard of them, the single biggest soft drink manufacturer in the galaxy? Thanks to Quafe's assistance in resolving the Girani-Fa incident, their presence and political clout within the Empire has grown tremendously.

Anyway, Quafe has been secretly developing a new soft drink called Quafe Unleashed that they say will revolutionize the entire soft drink industry. But only hours ago, the formula was stolen. Security records show that a Quafe employee, an Amarrian named Galin Famis, has just left the station with the top-secret formula in his possession. Quafe representatives believe that he might be on his way to try to sell or deliver the formula to one of Quafe's competitors, and have offered a reward for the recovery of the formula.

Now, the Amarr government has spoken out against this act of corporate terrorism, but so far they haven't taken any overt actions to deal with it. We could make big points if we could find Famis. We were able to track him for a while, and we've just heard that he's now in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. I'll upload the coordinates to your NeoCom. Stop him before he meets his contact, and bring back the formula.

Oh, and make sure you keep this to yourself. Quafe doesn't want it to get out that this formula even exists.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I have the formula right here.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Maybe next time. Are you sure you're ready to be a ship commander? Perhaps you'd be best among the slaves.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Damn! I hope I can find someone else to handle this on such short notice.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll catch him.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Don't waste any time. Galin Famis is already getting away.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: My ears are open and my lips are sealed.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The prisoners you procured for us on your last assignment provided ample information on the Flame of Peace organization. Their leader is a woman calling herself simply "Chosen." Let me make it clear: I want you to go in there and wipe them out. You knocked them off balance with your previous attack. Now you must finish them off.

I've uploaded the location of their hideout in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} into your databank. Now, get going, and don't come back until you've destroyed them.

Do not go into this mission unless you are fully prepared for combat!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Good, my friend. Good. The prisoners you procured for us on your last assignment provided ample information on the Flame of Peace organization. Some of them succumbed admirably to our interrogation techniques, and they have since become newly reformed, docile slaves. But before we wiped their minds, they gave us clues to the location of their leader.

The leader is a woman calling herself simply "Chosen." Apparently she had some sort of delusional religious vision and in a fit of inspiration and creativity, wrote their "sacred text" over the course of a pleasure cruise through the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. And what emerged was the Fellowship of the Flame of Peace.

Let me make it clear: I want you to go in there and wipe them out. You knocked them off balance with your previous attack. Now you must finish them off. I've uploaded the location of their hideout into your databank. Now, get going, and don't come back until you've destroyed them.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Flame of Peace has been extinguished.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You abandon your task now? You are no better than these filthy vermin!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Perhaps you sympathize with these vermin!? Get out of my sight!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll wipe them out.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Leave them alone. They're not harming anyone but themselves.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. God be with you!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I stand ready.
