messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Indeed I am. This new "religion" is one of the most twisted travesties of faith we have ever encountered. They talk much of peace and love, and all such nonsense, but according to their text, they kill and eat one of their members during their most sacred rituals. After the ritual slaughter, they roast their victim's flesh in the so-called Flame of Peace and share it among the congregation. Now you see how dangerous these deranged fanatics are!

This is highest priority. The data crystals gave us a clue to the location of one of their major enclaves. It lies deep in some rugged deadspace area, and they are likely guarding the entrance. Go there, destroy their habitat, and crush all resistance. Capture some of them alive and bring them back for interrogation.

We must find the leaders of this despicable cult and wipe them out.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Mission accomplished. Prisoners on board.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You abandon your task now? Perhaps you sympathize with these vermin!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Perhaps you sympathize with these vermin!? Get out of my sight!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I will not fail.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Leave them alone. They're not harming anyone but themselves.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: You have done well. These prisoners may hold the key to destroying this heinous cult once and for all. Don't stray too far.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Don't forget to bring back prisoners.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Maybe not, but I have a feeling you're going to tell me…

This new "religion" is one of the most twisted travesties of faith we have ever encountered. We know that the cultist have members from all walks of life, civilians and otherwise. Some of them are likely to be experienced combat pilots, though. Don't go out there without fitting your ship for a fight.

We cannot crack the encryption on these odd data crystals you discovered, but the contents appear to be some kind of heretical religious text. Of course, there is only one true religion, so this upstart cult must be stamped out wherever they can be found. However, now that you've destroyed that nest, we need to look for more until these vermin are eradicated.

Deliver the data crystals to the Theology Council's chief cryptographer at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. He has an incredible talent for this sort of thing, and we hope that he can crack the encryption. Perhaps the data inside will offer some clues about this cult's plans and locations.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Data crystal delivered, O Great One.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You cannot make a simple courier run on something this important? I have slaves with more initiative than you!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Your loyalty stands in question, {[character]player.name}. Leave me.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm on my way.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Why not just leave these people alone? I don't have time for this.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Why not just leave these people alone? I don't have time for this.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Splendid. Don't waste a second.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I am. What do you need?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: The encrypted data crystals you discovered had some sort of timed self-destruct mechanism. Now the whole thing is useless.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: The encrypted data crystals you discovered had some sort of timed self-destruct mechanism. Now the thing is useless.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: You have done well. You won't believe the things that we discovered after we broke the encryption! Come back when you have time, will you?

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.head.text: Your lack of initiative disturbs me.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The Theology Council has caught wind of a religious colony, whose leaders are gathering followers on a remote station in this system. They apparently call themselves the Flame of Peace. Their outpost is in the heart of a deadspace pocket, which is more than a little suspicious. The Council wants to know what these people are up to out there. Of course, we cannot allow the slightest deviation from the practices and beliefs of Holy Scripture, so you must determine if they are gathering a following for some strange new heresy.

If you determine that they are indeed heretics, destroy them without mercy and bring back any evidence you can.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I have dispatched the heretics and found this strange encrypted data storage unit.

messages.mission.extrainfo.header.text: Amarrian Society and the Religious Mind

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I didn't think you were capable of this, and now neither does the Theology Council. I think you will find them much less friendly in the future.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Your loyalty stands in question, {[character]player.name}. Leave me.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll check it out.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Amarrian theocracy is millennia old and traces its roots back into ancient times, perhaps even before humans ever set foot among the stars. Religion is the backbone of Amarrian society. Countless wars have been fought and lives lost over the proper interpretation of the Amarrian Scriptures.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: These religious politics don't interest me. I have better things to do.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Great work. I'm sure the Council will want to take a look at this data immediately. However, the crystals are encrypted, so I have another job for you.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Don't forget to bring back any evidence you might find.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Oh? Sounds interesting. What is it?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: You waited too long. The heretics caught wind of us and have moved elsewhere.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: You waited too long. The heretics caught wind of us and have moved elsewhere.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You look pretty green to me, youngster. But we've got a situation here and maybe you can help us out.

The frigate Sunhammer was recently attacked by Angel Cartel pirates; the captain called for reinforcements and managed to warp away, but the Angels scanned him down and pursued him, and the ship was lost... yet not before the fast-thinking captain jettisoned his cargo to avoid the risk of its being destroyed in the firefight. The captain's pod made it back in one piece, and the cargo's mostly expendible, but for one thing: Among the junk they had to ditch was a Brutor Tribe roster with all the history and lineage of tribal members in this sector from over a century ago.

The roster is absolutely unique; it can't be replaced. We need someone to get out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and find the roster. There's a reward in it for you if you succeed. What do you say, {[character]player.name}?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've returned with the roster.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Don't worry! I'll get the roster back!

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Your agent has placed a bookmark in your NeoCom to help you get to the correct location. Open People and Places and go to the Bookmarks tab. Then right-click on the objective item (the roster) and choose "Set Destination." On your ship's control panel, click the Autopilot icon. Your ship will now travel to the appropriate star system. Once you've arrived, your Autopilot will deactivate.

Now go back to your Bookmarks, right-click on the roster and select "Warp to within 0." Once you've arrived at the location, look at your Overview and find the cargo container; right-click on it and select "Approach." Once you've approached to within 1500 meters, right-click the cargo container and open it. A window will now pop up, displaying the container's contents. Click and drag the item(s) into your cargo hold: Once you've done that, you will have obtained the Brutor Tribe roster. All that will remain is to return with it to your agent for your reward.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks and good luck, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm no rookie. I'm a capsuleer. What do you have for me?

The roster is absolutely unique; it can't be replaced. We need someone to get out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and find the roster. There's a reward in it for you if you succeed. What do you say, {[character]player.name}?

Oh, of course there's a good chance the Angels will still be lingering in the vicinity of the cargo, so be prepared for a fight.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work, {[character]player.name}. I'll know who to turn to next time I have a job that needs doing.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You look pretty green to me, youngster. But we've got a situation here and maybe you can help us out.

The transport Santaros had a bulkhead failure in a nearby system and was forced to jettison its cargo. Its crew barely made it back in one piece, and the cargo's mostly a dead loss, but among the junk they had to ditch was a relic from Old Amarr, an item of little value to you or me, but vital to Lord Kendron Horowan, a noble who is friendly with House Tash-Murkon. We need someone to get out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and find the relic. There's a reward in it for you if you succeed, as well as the gratitude of an important nobleman.

I've uploaded the location of the Santaros's cargo dump into your onboard computer. It should appear in your bookmarks. Once you've located the relic, get it back to me here.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've returned with the relic.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Don't worry. I'll get the relic back.

localizedName.text: In the Shadow of War (1 of 5)

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You may have been hearing some scuttlebutt about Caldari fleet movements in the area. We suspect that they're up to something big, something that might presage a general conflict. Needless to say, this constellation's been a powder keg for years, and a single spark will set the whole region alight. We're shorthanded here at {[location]agentStationID.name}, but we've got a number of scouts out combing the region looking for signs of enemy activity.

About an hour ago, we received a distress call from one of our scouts in a damaged escape pod; there's a lot of subspace interference, but we were able to make out his location and ID. It sounds as if he was ambushed by Caldari ships. We need someone to head out here and pick him up before the enemy finds him.

Now, I know it's a big task for a newbie like you, but if you're up to it we're ready to offer generous compensation for your time. I've bookmarked the pilot's last known location for you. So, what do you say?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: He's in bad shape, but he's still alive, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll do my best.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Relations between the Federation and the Caldari have never been good in the best of times, and now, with the region arming for war, there is every possibility that the old hatreds between Gallente and Caldari will be reignited. If the Caldari are indeed massing a fleet nearby, it's the job of every patriotic Gallente fighter to stop it.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Thank god! We're sending him in to intensive care even as I speak; come back in a little while and I'll let you know if there's anything else we need.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks! You don't know what a service you're doing for us!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: How can I help, {[character]agentID.name}?

messages.mission.briefing.text: About an hour ago, we received a distress call from one of our scouts in a damaged escape pod; there's a lot of subspace interference, but we were able to make out his location and ID. It sounds as if he was ambushed by Caldari ships. We need someone to head out here and pick him up before the enemy finds him. I've bookmarked the pilot's last known location for you.

localizedName.text: In the Shadow of War (2 of 5)

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I certainly did. Good timing on your part. That poor devil you brought in didn't make it - his injuries were too severe. But he was able to provide us with some information before he died.

Seems he had jumped a couple of Caldari couriers and hacked a data chip containing information on enemy fleet movements from one of their ships. On his way back here, he ran into an enemy destroyer, but he was able to warp away and jettison the data chip before the Caldari captain tracked him down and destroyed his ship. Our man gave us the location, but now we need someone to go retrieve it. You did well in finding and bringing our guy back, may he rest in peace, and I want you for this job too.

I've uploaded a bookmark to your ship's database; the data chip is at that location, but I'm afraid that there may be enemy fighters about as well looking for the same item. Be careful!

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's the data chip.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm ready to do my duty!

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Good work! I've handed the chip over to the lab boys for decoding. If it contains what I think it does, I'll have more work for you shortly.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You asked me to come back for an update on the situation...?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Seems the pilot you rescued in your last mission had jumped a couple of Caldari couriers and hacked a data chip containing information on enemy fleet movements from one of their ships. On his way back here, he ran into an enemy destroyer, but was able to warp away and jettison the data chip before the Caldari captain tracked him down and destroyed his ship. Our man gave us the location of the chip he jetted, but now we need someone to go retrieve it.

I've uploaded a bookmark to your ship's database; the data chip is at that location. But I'm afraid there may be enemy fighters about looking for the chip as well. Be careful!

localizedName.text: In the Shadow of War (3 of 5)

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes, and thanks to you, our pilot didn't die in vain. The data on that chip is heavily encrypted, and we think it contains some telemetry data regarding enemy ship movements. We just don't have the right personnel here to get at it, though, and some recent subspace interference is preventing us from communicating with our friends over at the {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} facilities.

Time is of the essence; we need to have this chip delivered to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for decryption. Are you fueled up and ready to go, {[character]player.name}?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I dropped off the data chip, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm on it.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Good job. We should be receiving the tracking data shortly -- be sure to check back in soon.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Oh? Have you retrieved the information on that chip?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The data on the chip you recovered for us earlier is heavily encrypted, and we think it contains some telemetry data regarding enemy ship movements. We just don't have the right personnel here to get at it, though, and some recent subspace interference is preventing us from communicating with our friends over at the {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} facilities. Deliver the chip for us for decryption.

Make sure the data chip is in your cargohold before you undock.

localizedName.text: In the Shadow of War (4 of 5)

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We did, yes. This is big, really big. We've decrypted the data and analyzed the telemetry, and the Caldari are definitely amassing near this sector for some reason. Worse still, we suspect that our communication problems aren't the result of excessive ionization after all: We think the Caldari are jamming our transmissions. We sent out some scouts to track down the source of the interference, and they've traced the jamming signals to a location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

Here's the report with all pertinent information; I've added it to your bookmarks. It's vital that we figure out just exactly what they're up to as soon as possible. Enemy scouts may be interdicting any traffic in that system as well, so be on the lookout for enemy vessels. Avoid or destroy them, as you see fit.

There's bound to be a structure of some kind out there that's causing the signal interference, and I need you to see what exactly it's doing. Get a report on whatever you find out there back to me as soon as possible.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's my report, {[character]agentID.name}. There's definitely something fishy going on out there.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: This report is as good as delivered.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Excellent! With your help we'll see to it that those Caldari have a hell of a surprise coming.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I thank you, {[character]player.name}. You're a real patriot.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I take it we had some progress in analyzing that telemetry data?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've decrypted the data and analyzed the telemetry, and the Caldari are definitely amassing near this sector for some reason. Worse still, we suspect that our communication problems aren't the result of excessive ionization after all: We think the Caldari are jamming our transmissions. We sent out some scouts to track down the source of the interference, and they've traced the jamming signals to a location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I've added it to your bookmarks.

It's vital that we figure out just exactly what the Caldari are up to as soon as possible. Enemy scouts may be interdicting any traffic in that system as well, so be on the lookout for enemy vessels. Avoid or destroy them, as you see fit.

There's bound to be a structure of some kind out there that's causing the signal interference, and I need you to see what exactly it's doing; access the structure and bring me whatever Communications Logs you find inside.

localizedName.text: In the Shadow of War (5 of 5)

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We're organizing a pre-emptive strike to take out their fleet, but the thing is, we can only get so many Navy ships in here to do the job in the short time we have available. More importantly, we need someone we can trust to take out one of their communications tower arrays in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} so the Navy ships can get into position for the attack. We need you to take the array out for us.

This will be a tough fight, so make sure your ship is fitted for a full-scale assault! A shield booster or armor repairer is essential, and you should be prepared to warp out for repairs if you're anywhere near taking hull damage.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The com array is down, {[character]agentID.name}. They had some serious defenses out there, but the deed is done.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Those Caldari are an arrogant bunch of bastards. It'll give me pleasure to pay them back in kind.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: That's the spirit, {[character]player.name}! Good luck!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: What do you need me to do, {[character]agentID.name}?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've got those Caldari bastards right where we want them. We're organizing a pre-emptive strike to take out their fleet, but the thing is, we can only get so many Navy ships in here to do the job in the short time we have available. More importantly, we need someone we can trust to take out one of their communications tower arrays in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} so the Navy ships can get into position for the attack.

We need you to take the array out for us. Are you up to this job?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Your service is an example to all capsuleers, {[character]player.name}. Here's your reward; you've earned it!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You look pretty green to me, youngster. Still, we've got a situation here and maybe you can help us out.

Our freighter Bright Prospect struck an asteroid when emerging from warp in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The jump drive was badly damaged and they thought it might blow, but they managed to make it back in one piece. However, among the cargo, which was mostly expendable, was a set of important Ishukone corporate records; they were forced to jettison the records lest they be lost if the ship's warp core blew. At present we don't have backups due to a database malfunction, so those records might be irreplaceable.

We need someone to get out there and recover those records. I've uploaded the location of the Bright Prospect's cargo dump into your onboard computer. It should appear in your bookmarks. Once you've located the records, place them in your cargo hold and bring them back to me here. There's a reward in it for you if you succeed, of course, as well as my gratitude.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've returned with the records.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Don't worry, I'll get those records back for you.

Then right-click on the objective item (the corporate records) and choose "Set Destination." Then go to your ship's control panel and click the Autopilot icon. Your ship will now travel to the appropriate star system. Once you've arrived, your Autopilot will deactivate.

Click and drag the corporate records into your cargo hold. Now return with them to your agent in {[location]agentStationID.name} for your reward.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks and good luck, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Why, sure. What do you have for me?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
So it would seem.

Listen, the courier ship Swiftsure has just had a warp drive mishap in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and was forced to jettison its cargo lest it be damaged or lost if the core blew. They're crawling back to their home station as we speak; however, the cargo they had to ditch was a set of important Federation court records. We don't have backups available, so those records are irreplaceable, and they can't get another courier out there until tomorrow sometime. Bloody couriers. Can't get good help these days.

{[character]player.name}, we need someone to head out there and find those records right away. There's a healthy reward in it for you if you succeed. I've uploaded the location of the Swiftsure's cargo dump into your onboard computer. It should appear in your bookmarks. Once you've located the records, place them in your cargo hold and get it back to me here.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've returned with the records.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Don't worry. I'll get those records back.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Your agent has given you the task of locating some lost records. Once you have accepted the mission and undocked, view your mission details by selecting the 'Agent Missions' icon at the top left of your HUD. Then select the 'Lost Records' entry and then 'Warp to Location'. Once you've arrived at the location, proceed onwards until you locate the cargo container; then right-click on it and select "Approach." Once you've approached to within 2000 meters, right-click the cargo container and select "Open." A window will now open, displaying the container's contents. Select the 'Loot All' button to place the records into your cargo hold. Now return with them to your agent in {[location]agentStationID.name} for your reward.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: That's why I'm here. Guess I timed that one well...

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The courier ship Swiftsure had a warp drive mishap in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and was forced to jettison its cargo lest it be damaged or lost if the core blew. Eventually they managed to make it back in one piece; however, the cargo they had to ditch was a set of important Federation court records. We don't have backups available, so those records are irreplaceable.

{[character]player.name}, we need someone to head out there and find those records. There's a healthy reward in it for you if you succeed. I've uploaded the location of the Swiftsure's cargo dump into your onboard computer. It should appear in your bookmarks. Once you've located the records, place them in your cargo hold and get it back to me here.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work, my friend.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: No need to bother with the ore any longer.  You took too long, and our scientist found other resources.  I hope you know that you have missed a golden opportunity.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Excellent. The famed Dr. Lamia Calus is one of our top nanite research specialists.  She has entered a requisition for 47 units of Green Arisite for her research. If you can procure this substantial quantity of mineral, I'm sure you'll be adequately rewarded. The sooner, the better.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's your ore. Some mercenaries had set up a mining op there, but I dealt with it. Now, you mentioned some other work after this?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Scientific progress grinds to halt, thanks to your lack of initiative.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: That is unfortunate. Ah, well, I'm sure I can find someone else for this lucrative opportunity.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sure thing, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm on it.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
How on earth did they find our secret mining site, I wonder? And who are they working for? Hm.

Well, that's why I needed someone as capable as you to go out there. Listen, I just need a few minutes while I finish entering this data: Come back and see me in a bit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. I've downloaded the coordinates to your NeoCom. Come back soon.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Hm. Okay. Mining doesn't get me in my happy place, but if it's just this one mission and such a small amount...

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The famed Dr. Lamia Calus is one of our top nanite research specialists. She has entered a requisition for 47 units of Green Arisite for her research. If you can procure this mineral, I'm sure you'll be adequately rewarded. I have coordinates here to a mining site of ours where a bit of this rare substance can be found.

Green Arisite is related to Gneiss, which is itself rare and is typically found only in low-sec space; pirates and mercenaries of all stripes are often found in its vicinity. Don't go out there in a defenseless mining scow.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: No need to bother with the ore any longer.  You took too long, and our scientist found other resources.  I hope you know that you have missed a golden opportunity.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.head.text: Your lack of initiative has cost us

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: You failed. You won't find Delainen at that location anymore. He sent us a note saying he'd caught wind of your coming and relocated. He has disappeared once again.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You might remember the preeminent scientist, Dr. Lamia Calus, from your previous mission. Her mentor was the famous particle physicist and AI specialist, Professor Kajurei Delainen. Perhaps you've heard of Delainen's "Seven Pillars of Artificial Intelligence"? No? Well, no matter.

A number of years of ago, Delainen disappeared. He was supposed to report to his laboratory at the appointed time, but he simply never appeared. His living quarters were cleared out and his bank accounts emptied and closed. Yet no evidence of criminal wrongdoing was ever found. In such a vast universe, it can be easy for a person to disappear.

In any case, evidence has just surfaced that he in fact still lives ... and in this very system! Now Dr. Calus has reached a critical stage in her research, and Delainen was once the galaxy's foremost expert on both quantum particle physics and artificial intelligence. He claimed that the two fields were more closely related than anyone realized. His expertise would be invaluable to our current research.

Your mission is to bring him back here. One hitch, though: It is very possible that he will not come willingly. Don't take no for an answer.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I have Delainen with me. Uh, just a word of warning, though: He's completely insane!

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: It seems that apprehending a helpless old man is too much for you.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: It seems that apprehending a helpless old man is too much for you.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Bring back some helpless old man? Piece of cake. Be right back.

messages.mission.timeout.emailheader.text: Your lack of initiative has cost us

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Oh? Well, nonetheless, splendid! Dr. Calus will be pleased.  Stick around, {[character]player.name}; I'll have some more work for you shortly, I imagine.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Do be prompt about this one... and don't hurt him! We need that man unharmed!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: As long as it's not retrieving more ore, I'm good with that.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The letters of Bishop Dalamaid, currently on tour through the Empire, have been stolen by Minmatar terrorists. There's a media lockdown; attention is the only thing the Minmatar could reasonably expect to gain from such a heist. Still, the letters are of extreme importance to the Empire, even if they aren't grounds to mobilize a large force. That's where you come in: I want you to recover the letters for us.

The terrorists were recently spotted in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They're likely using a series of acceleration gates to disguise the true location of their base, a not uncommon tactic. You will have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the terrorists' base. Follow the terrorists, destroy any resistance, and return the letters to me.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
As you may have heard, the letters of Bishop Dalamaid are currently on tour through the Empire. Not only are they of doctrinal significance, but sections dealing with the various scandals of the flesh among the clergy of Dalamaid's time have always been popular. It's a little embarrassing to admit, but these tawdry details are usually the bigger draw, a fact that the Empire has rarely been too ashamed to take advantage of. This tour was one such attempt to use the controversial nature of the letters to get more citizens interested in the Scriptures.

However, the plan has misfired. Minmatar terrorists recently broke into the station where the letters were being kept and have stolen them. There's a media lockdown on the whole thing, for attention is the only thing the Minmatar could reasonably expect to gain from such a heist. Still, the letters are of extreme importance to the Empire, even if they aren't grounds to mobilize a large force. That's where you come in: I want you to recover the letters for us.

The terrorists were recently spotted in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They're likely using a series of acceleration gates to disguise the true location of their base, a not uncommon tactic. You will have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the terrorists' base. Follow the terrorists, destroy any resistance, and return the letters to me.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've returned with Bishop Dalamaid's letters.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: This will not do, not at all. Now I'll have to find someone else to take care of this.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Oh, sure. Maybe rescuing doctrinal works isn't as sexy as rescuing exotic dancers, but I expected better.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll give those Minmatar terrorists exactly the sort of attention they deserve.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Acceleration gates are not an uncommon sight for most pilots. Like warp gates, each acceleration gate can only be configured for one point in space; unlike warp gates, they can only be used for travel to other points within the same solar system. Acceleration gates can also be locked, preventing pilot from using them. Such locking mechanisms can be based on ship type, on the presence of active guard units in the area, or on appropriate codes/keys.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm not going to risk my ship against Minmatar fighters just for some stupid old papers.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: The Minmatar can have the stupid letters. I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Godspeed, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Just in time for...?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: You have taken too long in recovering the letters of Bishop Dalamaid. The Minmatar terrorists have escaped; it will take weeks to track them down. I only hope we will be able to recover the letters safely.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent. More Minmatar terrorists have been sent to their Judgment, and the letters have been returned to Imperial hands. Good work, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I can't hold off on the search anymore. I was hoping you could retrieve the letters of Bishop Dalamaid discreetly, but now I have to mobilize an entire force, attracting exactly the sort of attention the terrorists wanted.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The Achuran White Song bird has been sacred to the Achura throughout their recorded history. The creature mates only in the mountains of Saisio III, and naturally is exceedingly rare. Recently, the remnants of the old Achuran government made a gift of two such birds to the State, a male and a female. These particular birds are quite special, in that they have been genetically modified to mate off-planet. This is a matter of tremendous importance for us, from both a diplomatic and an ecological standpoint.

Twelve hours ago, the birds were stolen. Gallentean eco-terrorists hijacked the diplomatic courier mid-transit. Now, I don't think anyone ever needs an excuse to gun for the Gallente, but these guys are more worthless than the Federation Navy. The terrorists were last spotted at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's likely they are using a series of acceleration gates to hide the true location of their base. You'll have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the terrorists' base. Track down the terrorists, and recover the White Song birds.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
The Achuran White Song bird has been sacred to the Achura throughout their recorded history. The creature mates only in the mountains of Saisio III, and naturally is exceedingly rare. They released a statement claiming that the Caldari State is-- hang on, let me get this right... ah, here it is: "incapable of doing what is best for the longevity of this beautiful species, as demonstrated by their abhorrent destruction of the natural qualities of these rare and fragile..." blah, blah, blah, you get the point.

Now, I don't think anyone ever needs an excuse to gun for the Gallente, but these guys are more worthless than the Federation Navy. The terrorists were last spotted at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's likely they are using a series of acceleration gates to hide the true location of their base. You'll have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the terrorists' base. Track down the terrorists, and recover the White Song birds.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Gallenteans are no more. Sadly, only one of the White Songs survived.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You have no idea what a PR nightmare this will be for the State.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm not going to waste time explaining to you what a mistake this is.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I understand my duty. These terrorists will pay. Dearly.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Acceleration gates are not an uncommon sight for most pilots. Like warp gates, each acceleration gate can only be configured for one point in space; unlike warp gates, they can only be used for travel to other points within the same solar system. Acceleration gates can also be locked, preventing pilot from using them. Such locking mechanisms can be based on ship type, on the presence of active guard units in the area, or on appropriate codes/keys.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Gallente or no, I have more important things to do than rescue a couple of birds.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've had it. This mission is for the-- well, you know.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Get this done, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I am ready for whatever you need.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: The Gallentean terrorists escaped from the system and disappeared. Best intel suggests there was a complication, and that both birds will have died while in their "care." If you had acted faster, all this could have been avoided.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Only one survived? Damn it. Well, I'm sure there was nothing you could do. It was those damned Gallente. We won't be able to populate another world with just one bird, but I suppose we can always engineer more.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: We lost track of the terrorists. If you'd given me an answer, a more timely response could have been put together to prevent this.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You've heard the legends of King Rouvenor, yes? Founded the kingdom of Garoun, reigned for a hundred years of peace, killed the fabled Giant Long-Limb of Lyace? Everyone knows these tales. Well, most believe them only to be tales. However, a recent archaeological dig has found what could be the old city of Amatore itself! Nothing is certain yet, but this could be the biggest find in the history of the Federation. Already artifacts from the dig are being sent around to scholars across the universe.

Enter the Caldari. An artifact we believe to be the armor of Rouvenor himself was on its way to the University of Caille when it was hijacked by Caldari terrorists! They've issued no demands, but it is clear they wish to do harm to this piece of our cultural heritage.

We've tracked the terrorists to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It is likely they are using a series of acceleration gates to conceal the location of their base, as so many pirates are wont to do. You will have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the terrorists' base. Track down these despicable terrorists, and restore the Armor of Rouvenor to its people.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Those damned Caldari aren't content to raze our borders and sabotage our economic concerns abroad. Oh, no! Now the bastards are attempting to defile our cultural history!

You've heard the legends of King Rouvenor, yes? Of course you have -- every Gallentean who went to primary school has. Founded the kingdom of Garoun, reigned for a hundred years of peace, killed the fabled Giant Long-Limb of Lyace? Everyone knows these tales. Well, most believe them only to be tales. However, a recent archaeological dig has found what could be the old city of Amatore itself, the wondrous capitol of King Rouvenor! Nothing is certain yet, but this could be the biggest find in the history of the Federation. Already artifacts from the dig are being sent around to scholars across the universe.

Enter the Caldari. An artifact we believe may be the armor of Rouvenor himself was on its way to the University of Caille when it was hijacked by Caldari terrorists! They've issued no demands, but it is clear they wish to do harm to this piece of our cultural heritage.

We've tracked the terrorists to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It is likely they are using a series of acceleration gates to conceal the location of their base, as so many pirates are wont to do. You will have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the terrorists' base. Track down these despicable terrorists, and restore the Armor of Rouvenor to its people.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I have done it. I give you the Armor of Rouvenor.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You are spitting on our heritage. All you unpatriotic swine will get yours someday.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I had hoped for better from a citizen of the Federation. Get out of my sight.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I will do this thing, for the glory of what Gallente was and will be again.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Acceleration gates are not an uncommon sight for most pilots. Like warp gates, each acceleration gate can only be configured for one point in space; unlike warp gates, they can only be used for travel to other points within the same solar system. Acceleration gates can also be locked, preventing pilot from using them. Such locking mechanisms can be based on ship type, on the presence of active guard units in the area, or on appropriate codes/keys.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I will risk neither my ship nor my life against these children's stories.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: The Caldari can have that hunk of rusted metal. I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: It is good the Federation can still count on pilots like you.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: A chance? What's going on?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: The Caldari terrorists have absconded with the Armor of Rouvenor, and we do not know where they have gone. The Gallentean people have lost an important part of their history because you did not succeed in your mission.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You have the thanks of the entire Federation. With heroes like you, we shall soon bring the peace and glory of Old Gallente to every corner of the universe.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: Not only did the Caldari terrorists escape with the Armor of Rouvenor, but now they are publicly decrying it as a fake. The lows they will stoop to in the pursuit of discrediting the Federation are limitless, but the damage is done. Had you decided sooner, this could have all been avoided.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The Republic needs your help. Twelve hours ago, an Amarrian spy attacked and destroyed a prison convoy in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Most of the guards and prisoners are dead, but one prisoner was rescued: a suspected Amarr sympathizer.

Fortunately, they haven't left the system yet; we've learned that the spy has some sort of forward base established here. He's likely using a series of acceleration gates to disguise the true location of the base, a not uncommon tactic. You will have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the base. Follow the Amarr agent, destroy any resistance, and bring back the sympathizer.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Excellent. Because the Republic needs your help. Twelve hours ago, an Amarrian spy attacked and destroyed a prison convoy in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Most of the guards and prisoners are dead, but one prisoner was rescued: a suspected Amarr sympathizer.

I wish I could say Amarr sympathizers were uncommon. We like to tell ourselves that we cleaned house when we expelled the Nefantar tribe – the Ammatar – from the Republic. But of course life is not so simple. For every ten Minmatar we have fighting to free our brethren from Amarrian captivity or to restore some bit of our displaced old ways, there is one who will sell out his brother for a few ISK. And it only takes one dissenter, one cowardly traitor, to undermine the efforts of hundreds. This is why it is always a top priority for the Republic to ferret out the weak or the corrupt from positions of power. And why the corrupt must be instantly and decisively exterminated.

The prisoner who was rescued is one such figure, formerly a local politician of some influence. He had everyone fooled with his historical conservation initiatives, until an anonymous tip led to his arrest. He was on his way to the Tribunal when the Amarr spy took him ― bastard probably had a deal worked out with the Amarr the whole time.

Fortunately, the Amarr agent hasn't left the system yet; we've learned that he has some sort of forward base established here. He's likely using a series of acceleration gates to disguise the true location of the base, a not uncommon tactic. You will have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the base. Follow the Amarr agent, destroy any resistance, and bring back the sympathizer.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I have sent the Amarr spy back to his God, and I've brought the traitor back to you.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: On the contrary, there is no better use of a Minmatar's time than chasing down a traitor. Be gone.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: On the contrary, there is no better use of a Minmatar's time than chasing down a traitor. Be gone.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I will bring the traitor back to face justice.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Acceleration gates are not an uncommon sight for most pilots. Like warp gates, each acceleration gate can only be configured for one point in space; unlike warp gates, they can only be used for travel to other points within the same solar system. Acceleration gates can also be locked, preventing pilot from using them. Such locking mechanisms can be based on ship type, on the presence of active guard units in the area, or on appropriate codes/keys.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Chasing down a single traitor is not the best use of my time.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Chasing down a single traitor is not the best use of my time. I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Go with the blessings of the tribes.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I am always ready to serve the Republic.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: We've lost track of the Amarr agent. Had you acted more quickly, proper justice might have been served. In lieu of direct action on the traitor, the Republic has performed his sentence on his immediate family, both back and forward one generation. Whatever further Minmatar lives are lost as a result of this are on your head.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Good work, {[character]player.name}, I'll just transfer him to— oh, look, I seem to have accidentally opened the airlock he was being kept in! What a tragedy. And the Republic is safer for it.

Remember this lesson well. The true justice of the Minmatar is swift and uncompromising.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: Justice cannot wait for your decision to act. In lieu of direct action on the traitor, the Republic has performed his sentence on his immediate family, both back and forward one generation. You left the Republic with no other choice.

localizedName.text: New Frontiers - Toward a Solution (3 of 7)

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Dr. Calus has informed me that your delay in procuring the datacore has put her research irrevocably behind schedule. As such, your involvement is no longer welcome.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Well, Dr. Calus is not ready to reveal the nature of her project, but rest assured that it will be huge. However, the good doctors require some critical datacores to help them put their ideas into physical form. Sometimes scientific ideas race ahead of one's ability to fabricate the results effectively.

We need you to go pick up a unique Mechanical Engineering datacore put together for the project by one of Dr. Calus's colleagues not far from here and bring it back as soon as possible. You will be rewarded, of course, as usual.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I have the datacore. You owe me.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Scientific progress grinds to a halt, thanks to you.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Scientific progress grinds to halt, thanks to your lack of initiative.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'd be happy to help. Money's money, eh?

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Now, now: I always pay my debts. And now the project can move into the final stage. I hope you're still willing to help out?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Yes, it will. Never fear.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Interesting. But how can I help?

messages.mission.briefing.text: We need you to go pick up a unique Mechanical Engineering datacore put together for the project by one of Dr. Calus's colleagues not far from here and bring it back as soon as possible. You will be rewarded, of course, as usual.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: Dr. Calus has informed me that your delay in procuring the datacore has put her research irrevocably behind schedule. As such, your involvement is no longer welcome.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: You waited too long. The symbiote has somehow slipped away and eluded us. This is on your head. Who knows the havoc that thing will create, who knows how it will evolve!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Well, that thing is gone, so the station is safe for now. The breached districts have been sealed off until repair crews can get in there. But I suppose you're wondering what happened. Let me back up for a moment.

Dr. Calus's original goal was to create a ship energy system that used advanced nanites to harvest the energy that binds subatomic particles together. The amount of energy that could be produced would be staggering. Think of it. The offensive potential of our ships and weapons systems could be increased a hundred-fold at least, maybe a thousand-fold.

But somehow Delainen subverted Calus's research. He spent years living in close proximity to a nest of rogue drones; he even claimed to have struck up a beneficial relationship with them. Who knows what that does to a person?

They inserted the nanites, programmed by Prof. Delainen, into the battlecruiser's systems, but the things immediately began to malfunction. In less than ten minutes, they had changed the structure of the ship to ... something else. The security 'reels show a flash of light, almost like a jump gate activation, and then Delainen just disappears. Then, immediately, the metallic beast begins to move. We have heard of massive rogue drones, but this is different.

The ship actually spoke to Calus, who was injured during the ship's violent transformation. It said its name was "ROM." Then it blew a hole through the wall of the station into open space and blasted out of there. Everyone in the lab was killed, including Calus.

We believe that the nanites somehow merged Delainen into the ship they had created, making it some sort of bizarre biomechanical symbiote. But we need to know what happened for certain, and this ― well, this Delainen-ROM symbiote, I guess, for lack of a better name ― is the only thing that can give us the answers.

We want you to go out there and confront it; we've tracked its location, and it's still in this system. I'll send the coordinates to your NeoCom. Destroy it if you must, and then sift through the wreckage to find its central AI core. Bring that back for further study.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I have the AI core right here. And it's dripping green goo all over my cargo hold! And the goo is moving!

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You're just letting that thing loose upon the galaxy! Imagine the havoc it will cause!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You're backing out now? Cowardice does not look good in such an experienced ship commander.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll find it.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: That is a tremendous relief. You have done well; now we must study this thing for clues about what went wrong. Stick around.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good, but move quickly, before it jumps elsewhere. It's hiding in an asteroid field in this system.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I must've missed it, sorry. What happened?!

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: You waited too long. The symbiote has somehow slipped away and eluded us. This is on your head. Who knows the havoc that thing will create, who knows how it will evolve!

localizedName.text: New Frontiers - An Unexpected Twist (5 of 7)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Delainen apparently formed some sort of bond or relationship with the rogue drone colony near his previous home. But it's worse than that. Even now there are ongoing subspace transmissions taking place between these drones and the AI unit you recovered ― the thing's intelligence core is most certainly not dead.

The drones have moved around several times, but they're remaining near, for whatever reason. Go to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and destroy that rogue drone colony once and for all. The hive mind CPU and construction center is in the central hive structure. That is your target.

These drones are very, very advanced, and they've had time to build. You might even wish to take some help with you. Once they are all destroyed, salvage the hive mind CPU and return it to us.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes, I did. The good Dr. Calus ― whose value to us necessitates our keeping a clone in place for her ― is studying the Delainen-ROM's AI "brain" as we speak. But there's something else we'd like you to do.

Delainen apparently formed some sort of bond or relationship with the rogue drone colony near his previous home. But it's worse than that. Even now there are ongoing subspace transmissions taking place between these drones and the AI unit you recovered ― the thing's intelligence core is most certainly not dead.

The drones have moved around several times, but they're remaining near, for whatever reason. Go to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and destroy that rogue drone colony once and for all. The hive mind CPU and construction center is in the central hive structure. That is your target. Once the drones there are all destroyed, salvage the hive mind CPU and return it to us.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The drone colony is destroyed. I have the hive mind CPU on board. But do you think it is wise to have it so near the AI core? Weren't they communicating somehow?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: If we had thought you a quitter, we would never have hired you in the first place.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You're backing out now? Cowardice does not look good in such an experienced ship commander.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: More weird drones? Yeah … okay, fine. But this had better be worth it!

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Look, I don't need any weird nanites taking over my ship. I'm done with this.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Look, I don't need any weird nanites taking over my ship. I'm done with this.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Of course, my friend, yes. Of course. Just be careful out there!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Yeah, it's all cleaned up. But thanks for the concern. You mentioned that I should stick around, though?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: You waited too long. Apparently, the Delainen-ROM AI core warned them that we were coming: The drones have disappeared and moved. Now, it is unlikely we will ever have the opportunity to fully understand what happened.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: You waited too long. Apparently, the Delainen-ROM AI core warned them that we were coming: The drones have disappeared and moved. Now, it is unlikely we will ever have the opportunity to fully understand what happened.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: We have little choice, {[character]player.name}; we must understand what has gone on. But we have made progress here as well. Come back when you have time and I'll explain.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've completed Dr. Calus's study of the Delainen-ROM symbiote's AI core and the CPU you got for us. They're like nothing we've ever seen before. A strange combination of human thought patterns, atomic-scale nanites, and constantly evolving neural networks. And the thing wouldn't stop telling bad jokes! But if those nanites were ever loosed, they could easily latch onto the nearest ship and reconstitute themselves. We just can't risk that happening … again.

But it's also too valuable to destroy. We have placed the items in a special cryogenic container for temporary cold storage. The closest station with an adequate facility for long-term cryogenic storage is in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, though. Please take the container over there for safekeeping.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We've completed Dr. Calus's study of the Delainen-ROM symbiote's AI core and the CPU you got for us. They're like nothing we've ever seen before. A strange combination of human thought patterns, atomic-scale nanites, and constantly evolving neural networks. And the thing wouldn't stop telling bad jokes! But if those nanites were ever loosed, they could easily latch onto the nearest ship and reconstitute themselves. Er, itself. Well, whatever. We just can't risk that happening … again. Which is why it's too dangerous to study further ― the chance of a breakout is just too high.

But it's also too valuable to destroy. We have placed the items in a special cryogenic container for temporary cold storage. The closest station with an adequate facility for long-term cryogenic storage is in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, though. Please take the container over there for safekeeping.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Okay, I'm done.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You're quitting now, {[character]player.name}?! After everything you've been through? But this is just a courier mission!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You're quitting now, {[character]player.name}?! After everything you've been through? But this is just a courier mission!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Yeah, sure. At least I won't have to worry about any green goo this time if it's all frozen.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: No, thanks. I'm about done with this stupid drone business.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: On second thought, I'm about done with this stupid drone business. Count me out.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Come back when you're finished.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Sure. Makes sense. How can I help?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Forget it. We'll find someone else to carry this. We can't just leave it lying around. Such a lack of initiative looks poorly on such an experienced ship commander.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: You waited too long, so we found someone else to do this. Such a lack of initiative looks poorly on such an experienced ship commander.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Another job well done, {[character]player.name}. But I need to talk to you again right away ― this isn't over!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
That green goo in your cargohold was far more dangerous than we first realized. Some nanites – perhaps even the very ones from your cargohold – somehow made their way onto a battleship called Solar Cinder, which blasted out of its hangar just a few minutes ago. We don't know what to call this thing now, but it is sentient, and shows many similarities to the Delainen-ROM symbiote. But this is a battleship. An uncontrolled battleship with human-patterned AI ... and capable of self-replication!

We need you to get out there and destroy it! The military is on the way, but they will not be here in force before it has time to escape, if that's what it intends.

This won't be easy. That ship was heavily armed, and the symbiote's drone technology is very advanced. Furthermore, we believe that it can actually "heal" itself. You just might want to get some assistance on this one.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes. Very astute, {[character]player.name}. Do you recall that green goo in your cargohold a while back, when you returned with the drone AI core? That material was far more dangerous – and far more cunning – than we first realized. The nanites in the symbiote's AI core were the size of molecules, with atomic-scale manipulator arms. And because they are so small, they are practically undetectable. A billion of them could hide in the crevices of a speck of dust.

Are you frightened yet? You should be. Because they are loose.

Those nanites – perhaps even the self-same ones from your cargohold – somehow made their way onto a battleship called Solar Cinder, which blasted out of its hangar, with no crew, just a few minutes ago. We don't know what to call this thing now, but it is sentient, and shows many similarities to the Delainen-ROM symbiote. But this is a battleship. An uncontrolled battleship with human-patterned AI ... and capable of self-replication! Given time, it could lay waste to an entire planet!

We need you to get out there and destroy it! The military is on the way, but they will not be here in force before it has time to escape, if that's what it intends.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text:
Mission accomplished at last. The entity is destroyed. The galaxy is safe.

But I have some repair bills to cover, so... about that reward?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You just let that thing loose upon the galaxy! Imagine the havoc it will cause!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You're backing out now? Imagine the havoc that thing will cause!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Solar Cinder, huh? How apt: That thing's as good as cinders, now.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: This could go on forever. Nah, I'm gonna let the military deal with this one. It's out of my league now.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: This is crazy. I'm just gonna let the military deal with this one. It's out of my league now.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. But move quickly. It's hiding in a deadspace location not far from here.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Don't tell me. You mean there's more rogue nanites out there?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: The Solar Cinder drone entity escaped, thanks to you. I must say, I've never been associated with such a shiftless coward.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Your assistance has been invaluable, {[character]player.name}. You are a courageous commander. Enjoy your rewards and my personal gratitude. You've more than earned them.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: The Solar Cinder drone entity escaped, thanks to you. I must say, I've never been associated with such a shiftless coward.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Things are quieting down, so I'm calling off the recon. Any activity now and people will get suspicious.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We don't stand much on formality here: This isn't a post people seek out to advance their careers. Most of us are content to not be noticed. People start making noise, the hard-asses start remembering we're here, and that means more work for everyone.

But speaking of work, I've got some for you. We've been getting a few reports of strange activity in this system. Now, I bet it's just smugglers. And honestly, I'd rather not create too much of a fuss over it ― but it's making the civvies nervous, and they could raise just as much hell for us as any smuggler. So, just go out to these coordinates, poke around a bit, and come back. If anything pokes back, just run.

Or don't do it. I mean, what the hell do I care, really? It may be I can find some other work for you if you'd rather not play scout…

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Yeah, about this whole scouting thing? Seems you've got Gallente out there. And I don't mean a few.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Yeah, I don't blame you. Still, my superiors aren't going to like it. But that doesn't mean I might not have something else for you…

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Something else? Yeah, I've got something for you. Come back in a bit.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sure thing. Consider the area poked.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Quitting missions (or ignoring them until they "time out," which amounts to the same thing) invariably results in a loss of faction standing; it is almost always in a character's best interest to complete all missions he or she accepts.

However, a character may freely decline a mission when it is first offered, as long as it isn't one of those rare "storyline" missions; after that, declining another mission within four hours of the first does result in a loss of standing. Still, in general, a pilot's career is usually long and eventful enough that a few such minor hits to standing may not be too large a price.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I think I'll pass. You suggested you might have something else?

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Gallente? Here? You've got to be kidding. Okay, let me set this show to record… gimme just minute and come back, will you?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Ah, nice. Thanks. My favorite holovid show's about to come on, and I really don't want to miss it.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Just, "hey"? No salute or anything?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've been getting a few reports of strange activity in this system. Now, I bet it's just smugglers. And honestly, I'd rather not create too much of a fuss over it ― but it's making the civvies nervous, and they could raise just as much hell for us as any smuggler. So, just go out to these coordinates, poke around a bit, and come back. If anything pokes back, just run.

Or don't do it at all. I mean, what the hell do I care, really? It may be I can find some other work for you if you'd rather not play scout…

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: Things are quieting down, so I'm calling off the recon. Any activity now and people will get suspicious.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm just having so much fun with this mission that I think I should let someone else do it instead. What else have you got?

localizedName.text: Undue Attention - Helping the Helpful (2 of 3)

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Took your sweet time, huh? Okay, whatever, I know how it is. Anyway, chatter's coming through that the Intaki Syndicate is moving out. In fact, it sounds like someone pushed them out. If it was the Gallente, our job just got harder. Come and see me right away.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yeah, slow, right. It's only the Gallente. No big deal. They're just going to turn this whole place into a libertine drone-lover festival, that's all!!

Okay, think, think.

Alright, we know they're building a jump gate in this system, right? And we can't take on both the guards at that gate and the forces they presumably have building up elsewhere in this system. I'll call in the Navy ― they should be here in a matter of hours, I hope ― but we need to occupy these free-loving jerks in the meantime. We need some sort of a distraction....

Okay, here's what I need you to do. I have a few friends in the Intaki Syndicate who owe me for looking the other way during a few local business deals. I need you to hop over to their base and get their support. Do whatever you can. But be sure you're armed. You can never tell what's going on with the Syndicate.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I found the Intaki. The Gallente were giving them some trouble, but I gave the Gallente more. The Syndicate said they'd help us out.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I don't think you know quite how hairy things are going to get around here. Fine, alright. Get lost, then.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Damn it! You and your stupid ethics. Alright, fine. Give me a minute to think of something else and then come back, okay?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: The Intaki Syndicate, huh? Okay, I'll do my best.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Sometimes a mission might not turn out the way you anticipated. You might have incomplete information from your agent, and conditions can change during the mission. Such changes are generally communicated to you directly, either through a direct pop-up window when using an acceleration gate or by means of a text message appearing in your local chat channel.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm not getting mixed up in criminal affairs. Give me some other option.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: The Federation is moving faster than I thought. Still, with the Syndicate's help, this should be a lot easier.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. Oh, and if their leader mentions anything about anything like… oh, say, a few outstanding debts? Just tell him he's thinking of the wrong {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Calm down. Take it slowly. We can deal with this.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Okay, here's what I need you to do. I have a few friends in the Intaki Syndicate who owe me for looking the other way during a few local business deals. I need you to hop over to their base and get their support. Do whatever you can. But be sure you're armed. You can never tell what's going on with the Syndicate.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
Listen, the Intaki Syndicate is moving out, and so are we. The Navy has arrived to deal with this, finally, and called for a wholesale civilian evacuation, so it's all out of our hands now.

Thanks for nothing.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: This is getting too hairy for me. I'm out.

localizedName.text: Undue Attention - Closing the Gate (3 of 3)

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.head.text: It's all over – you can come out of hiding now

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Fly to the Gallente jump gate and destroy it. I won't lie to you: The gate is almost certainly more heavily fortified than it was before. The gate itself will probably take a crapload of damage before it's disabled. However, there should be fewer enemy pilots to deal with this time, since they'll all be tied up in the larger battle. Once the jump gate is down, not only will the main Gallente force be without reinforcements, but they won't have a clean exit, and they should flee or surrender.

We've picked up some local chatter from the Gallente saying that only frigate-class ships can get to that jump gate.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yeah, it would. That's what we're using. Between my few ships and my friends in the Intaki Syndicate, we have enough to occupy what's over here now until the Navy gets here. The problem is that damned jump gate you found.

I can see you sweating already. Calm down. I know you aren't ready for a major fleet op, not yet. And I want to use that to our advantage. We're staging our battle on the other side of the system ― close enough for the Gallente to take the bait, but far enough that that gate will be beyond their sensor range, especially against a frigate-class ship the size of the one you'll need to be flying.

Fly to the Gallente jump gate and destroy it. I won't lie to you: The gate is almost certainly more heavily fortified than it was before. The gate itself will probably take a crapload of damage before it's disabled. However, there should be fewer enemy pilots to deal with this time, since they'll all be tied up in the larger battle. Once the jump gate is down, not only will the main Gallente force be without reinforcements, but they won't have a clean exit, and they should flee or surrender.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Jump gate destroyed. The Gallente are cut off ― and still stupid to boot.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Damn you! We've risked so much on this operation. The Gallente are pulling out, yeah, but they're mostly escaping with no losses… using the gate you didn't take out. I don't think anyone is going to be calling this a sound victory by any means.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text:
You know, the universe is big. It can be dangerous. But sometimes things need to get done, even if you'd rather just be lying back with a nice cold rum and Quafe.

I only hope we can pull this off. And you― you can leave. Coward.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: The Gallente are in for a nasty surprise. I am going to destroy their precious gate, and their ships along with it.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Sometimes agent missions will require you to destroy large structures such as space stations, wrecks, bunkers, or even jump gates. In general, structures can take a serious beating. In fact, some are altogether impervious ― but luckily, this jump gate isn't one of them. Get to it.

messages.mission.timeout.emailheader.text: It's all over – you can come out of hiding now

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: This is too big for me. I can't do this. Sorry, but I'm out.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Hope for a miracle, because I can't take that gate out.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: That's the spirit. Show those self-righteous Gallente the price of trying to occupy Caldari space.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: End this? It would take a small fleet to handle these Gallente!

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: The battle's over. The Gallente are pulling out. They know that we know where their gate is, and they seem content with having destroyed a good chunk of our forces in this system. They left their gate on a self destruct. It's going to be almost impossible to prove the Gallente were even here. All we have as proof is our dead.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Terrific news, {[character]player.name}, terrific news. Reports are coming in from the battle. The Gallente are being routed. Their entire formation is broken. And even better, we've captured their command ship. That's going to be one hell of a bargaining chip for us here at {[location]agentStationID.name}.

I have to admit, I was not sure we were going to make it through that alive. Of course, the politicians are probably going to cover all of this up; this sort of event could trigger all out war. But we know what happened, and we know we kept the State safe. And you were instrumental in this victory: You have our deepest thanks, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: The battle's over. The Gallente are pulling out. They know that we know where their gate is, and they seem content with having destroyed a good chunk of our forces in this system. They left their gate on a self destruct. It's going to be almost impossible to prove the Gallente were even here. All we have as proof is our dead.

localizedName.text: Undue Attention - What Spacelane Patrol Knows (2 of 3)

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: CBD has taken down their intel offer. Somehow they got the impression we weren't that serious about it. If you had acted a bit faster, we'd have it by now.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Our good friends over at CBD have been picking up some strange local chatter for the past few days. According to them, this chatter has some bearing on what's going on in our system. But I still had to buy the intel from their Spacelane Patrol... I didn't have quite enough favors built up get them to deliver it, and it apparently isn't the sort of thing you just transmit across open space.

Anyway, go get the intelligence report from Spacelane Patrol and bring it back here, would you?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Got your intel here.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Listen, I know I said some stuff before about quitting missions, but it still makes folks uneasy. I mean, it's not a huge deal, but don't make a habit of it.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Just so we're clear, you probably shouldn't pass on every mission. Oh, well, your loss.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: This sounds more to my liking. Sure, I'll do it.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: At first glance, courier missions may seem a waste of a capsuleer's valuable time. After all, a standard crewed (i.e., non-capsule-controlled) ship could ferry material just as well. The difference is in the security capsuleers bring to a shipment versus standard ship crews. As well, a capsule ship requires a far smaller crew, meaning fewer potential leaks regarding shipping schedules, routes, and cargoes. Further, the capsuleers themselves are more reliable and easier to work with than most other ship command structures, making them a favorite for agents throughout the EVE universe.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: No, I think I'll pass on this one too.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
Good work. Let's take a look, here…

Wha―?! Damn! Damn… damn, damn… This isn't good, {[character]player.name}. I'm gonna need your help again.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Try to be quick about it. The faster we get things settled around here, the better.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Well, what do you suggest?

messages.mission.briefing.text: Our good friends over at CBD have been picking up some strange chatter for the past few days. According to them it has some bearing on what's going on in our system. Go get the intelligence report from the Spacelane Patrol station I've added to your bookmarks, and bring it back here.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: CBD has taken down their intel offer. Somehow they got the impression we weren't that serious about it. If you had acted a bit faster, we'd have it by now.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've decided I don't want to play space taxi. Thanks, but no thanks.

I've put together a small force to try to counter the Gallente, but it does not look good. We're going to have to try something absolutely crazy.
