I'm uploading a bookmark to your People & Places databank; it shows the location of a Banidine mining operation. I need you to head out there and mine all the Banidine — should be 18,000 units, my foreman tells me. Once we've made an undisputed claim, we're free to mine there again without interference, and I'll provide you with a little something for your trouble.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's the Banidine ore, {[character]agentID.name}. Seems like a waste of time to me, but hey, you're paying.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm on it.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Most people don't go looking for Banidine: It's virtually worthless, so you simply won't find it on the market.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks, youngster! We'll make a real miner of you yet!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Just say the word.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We recently found a number of new mining fields in adjacent systems, and the usual assortment of pirate trash has come out of the woodwork to exploit it. We'll need them mined soon because even those thieving bastards have friends in places high enough to put the legal status of these sites in doubt. For some reason they've taken an interest even in Banidine, too, and we'll need to find out why; all my workers are busy with the more profitable fields, but I'm not taking any chances.

I'm uploading a bookmark to your People & Places databank; it shows the location of a Banidine mining operation. I need you to head out there and mine all the Banidine. Should be 18,000 units, my foreman tells me. Once we've made an undisputed claim, we're free to mine there again without interference, and I'll provide you with a little something for your trouble.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Listen, just leave the logistics of it all to me, okay? You mine, I plan, you mine some more. That's all you need to know.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Damnation, they're sending them out younger and younger. Are you sure you're old enough to fly a starship? Oh, well, we have to play the hand we're dealt, and if you're the best I can get, I suppose you'll do.

We'll start simple, youngster. Banidine is normally all but worthless, so real miners don't usually bother with the stuff. Still, I've found a buyer who's willing to take whatever we can mine. So, get me 20,000 units of Banidine and I'll make it worth your while. It should be easy, even for a pup like you, but it will show me that you're serious.

There's an asteroid field near here that's lousy with the stuff – I've bookmarked it for you. Get back as soon as you can and I'll arrange a little bonus.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's your ore, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm young, but I'm no rookie – I'll get your ore for you.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The easiest way to travel to a destination system quickly is to use the Overview. Stargates are marked in the Overview settings panel under the "Celestial" group; once you have selected "Stargate" there, right-click on the hyperlinked destination system in the mission details and choose "Set destination." You will notice that the next stargate along your route, both in space and in your Overview, is now yellow.

Next, right-click on the yellow stargate (in space or in the Overview) and select "Warp to within 0m"; turn on your Autopilot, then sit back and relax until you are in the destination system.

After you have completed the mission, if you have problems finding your way back to the agent, simply open the "People and Places" window from your NeoCom and check the Agents tab; the agent you are working for should be displayed there. Right-click on the appropriate agent and select "Set destination," then turn on your Autopilot to make your way back to the agent's system.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks, youngster. You may prove yourself yet.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Yeah, I'm looking for work. Whatever you've got.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Banidine is normally all but worthless, so real miners don't usually bother with the stuff. Still, I've found a buyer who's willing to take whatever we can mine. So, get me 20,000 units of Banidine and I'll make it worth your while.

There's an asteroid field near here that's lousy with the stuff – I've bookmarked it for you. Get back as soon as you can and I'll arrange a little bonus.

Remember to fit a decent miner to your ship before you go. If you're having trouble finding the Banidine at the mission location, loading the "Mining" default overview will show all ores. If you're familiar with creating custom overview settings, Banidine is shown by enabling "Veldspar".

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Not bad, youngster. Not bad.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
My boss wants Banidine; something to do with manufacturing cheaper parts for refrigeration units or something. I don't know. Point is, he's made it my job to get the ore. And now I'm makin' it your job.

There's a few Banidine rocks out at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, enough for 20,000 units, the scouts tell me. Go out there, mine it, bring it back. Should be easy enough, right?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Well, maybe, yeah. Have you ever heard of Banidine? Doesn't matter, you have now. Anyway, my boss wants the stuff. Why? I have no idea — something to do with manufacturing cheaper parts, refrigeration units or something. I don't know. Point is, he's made it my job to get the ore. And now, if you're interested, I'm makin' it your job.

There's a few Banidine rocks out at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, enough for 20,000 units, the scouts tell me. Go out there, mine it, bring it back. Should be easy enough, right?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here're your rocks.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Oh, for the love of... fine. Whatever. I'll get someone else to do it.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Dammit, don't make me mine this crap myself. I hate mining.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Twenty thousand Banidine? That doesn't sound too tough. Sure, I'm good for it.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Most people don't go looking for Banidine: It's virtually worthless, so you won't find it on the market. In fact, most sensor manufacturers don't even bother putting it into their mining packages when they produce ship scanners. If you're having trouble finding the Banidine at the mission location, you can right-click the "Banidine" icon in the mission details and select "Add to Overview."

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Uhh... nah. Sorry. That's a little too pedestrian for me.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: The mining isn't done... but I'm done with it.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Great, great. Maybe now I can get some work done.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You look preoccupied. Something I can help you with?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Look, if you can't point a beam at a few derelict Banidine rocks in a timely manner, I'm just gonna give the mission to someone else. Make sure you're ready to do some work next time you see me.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Excellent! Maybe I'll finally get that raise.

Oh, uh, good job. Here's your payment.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I can't wait around here forever. I'm getting someone else to mine the Banidine.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: I need this done yesterday. I found someone else who can do the job faster.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Look, I need some… ah, building materials, but I've got a client who's a bit particular. He wants it special, from some asteroids that already destroyed a shuttle of his, I guess. He gave me a location; you just go there, mine all 18,000 units of the Banidine that's there, and bring it back. Now, you won't find this stuff anywhere else, so don't go looking to bring me back something similar and easier to come across — you try and rip me off on this, and I'll know. Got it? Alright.

So, you game?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've got your Banidine right here, pal.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Thanks a bundle. I didn't pay ya to think. That's my job. Remember that next time.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Yeah, I'm game.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Most people don't go looking for Banidine: It's virtually worthless, so you won't find it on the market. If you're having trouble finding the Banidine at the mission location, you can right-click the "Banidine" icon in your mission details and select "Add to Overview."

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't work for crazy people.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm done with this weird stuff. Banidine? It's worthless! So I get to wondering… who the hell wants this stuff, and for what? And I decide, maybe I ought not to do this, huh?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Get it quick. I don't like waiting.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You have anything for me?

messages.mission.briefing.text: Mine 18,000 units of Banidine at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and bring it to {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Nice job. I'll remember this.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I got no time for games. I'll find somebody who can get it done.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We need your help right away! We're calling on all ship commanders in this region. A huge asteroid has crashed into one of our stations. The station itself and most of the inhabitants are lost. This asteroid is particularly deadly in that it contains a huge quantity of Augumene, a rare and extremely toxic ore. We need someone to mine out the Augumene so rescue crews can go in there and retrieve the survivors.

I've uploaded a bookmark to your People & Places databank; use it to find the crash site. Mine it all and bring the ore back to me.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I have the ore onboard, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Hundreds more people will die now, thanks to you.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Nice. Well, hopefully someone else will see the value in saving some civilian lives.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll do what I can.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
When mining for specific minerals, you can often use the Overview to help. Click the small white arrow beside the word “Overview”; from there, select “Load default,” and then “Mining.” Then, you can right-click any type of asteroid in your overview and select “Remove from Overview”; keep doing this until only the type you want is left in your overview.

Furthermore, if you plan to mine this type of ore regularly, you can click the Overview arrow again and select “Save current type selection as…”; type in whatever name seems appropriate. Now you can return to this setting anytime you want to simply by using the Overview arrow to select “Load (name).”

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't have time to save a few station-dwellers' lives.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I don't have time to save a few station-dwellers' lives.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Get out there as soon as you can.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm ready.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
A huge asteroid has crashed into one of our stations. The station itself and most of the inhabitants are lost. This asteroid is particularly deadly in that it contains a huge quantity of Augumene, a rare and extremely toxic ore. We need someone to mine out the Augumene so rescue crews can go in there and retrieve the survivors.

I've uploaded a bookmark to your People & Places databank; use it to find the crash site. Mine it all and bring the ore back to me.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great work! I'll send in the rescue crews. I'm sure the families of the survivors will be delighted that you helped save their lives. And we might even find some way to use the Augumene.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.head.text: This task is too urgent for your pace.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've determined that the asteroid that collided with the station was composed of Augumene, which is particularly deadly in that it is a rare and extremely toxic ore. We need someone to mine out the Augumene safely from a starship.

More than that, others may be coming for the Augumene. We can't recover all the sensitive material from the wreckage of the base in time, and a blockade would tip our hand. The only solution is to mine out the Augumene ourselves. We want you to go out and retrieve all of the Augumene from the site. And hurry.

I've uploaded a bookmark to your People & Places databank; use it to find the crash site and then mine all the Augumene and bring the ore back to me.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Something terrible has happened. An asteroid has collided with a research station at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. There's no official death-toll yet, but it's expected to climb into the tens of thousands. Some of our brightest were there, working out the very technologies that would enable us to better defend our way of life from Gallente and Minmatar agressors. Now they're all gone....

I'm sorry. I lost myself there. We've determined that the asteroid that collided with the station was composed of Augumene, a rare and extremely toxic ore. We need someone to mine out the Augumene safely from a starship.

More than that, others may be coming for the Augumene. We can't recover all the sensitive material from the wreckage of the station in time, and a blockade would tip our hand. The only solution is to mine out the Augumene ourselves. We want you to go out and retrieve all 3,600 units of Augumene from the site. And hurry. If we don't get that ore, looters might follow its signal and stumble on what's left of our base.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I have done it. The remains of the station should now attract no unwanted attention.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Disappointing. I thought you seemed reliable.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I understand. It's just this side of grave robbery. Still, desperate times, desperate measures, and all that.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I understand. For the good of all, I'll clear out that Augumene.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Space stations are ideal research locations for most governments. Station crews can perform dangerous experiments that could endanger the civilians near a terrestrial base. Another advantage to the isolation of these stations is that they are harder for enemy factions to find, making espionage or outright destruction more difficult... usually.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm afraid I cannot do such a thing. It's… well, so many lives lost…

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I can't do this anymore. It's too much.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. Get this done. I do not envy you your task.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: What is it?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: You moved too slowly, {[character]player.name}. A recent recon shows that not only is the Augumene gone, but approximately 20 tons of material and data sheets are missing from the wreckage. We can only hope the thieves were merely scavengers.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work, {[character]player.name}. I wish we had not needed this to be done at all, but you did well.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: We cannot wait around forever. The task has gone to someone else.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We've found a conglomeration of Augumene asteroids nearby. The ore's not much good to anyone due to the exorbitant cost of reprocessing, of course, but a couple of our scientists are interested in doing some research on such a rare substance. In any case, hopefully you've been around the block enough times that you can find the ore and bring it in.

You think you're up to this? I've uploaded the location to your People & Places databank.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Augumene is here.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I didn't think you could handle it. Too bad I was right.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Well, I'm sure I can find someone else to handle this.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll see what I can do.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Most people don't go looking for Augumene: It's virtually worthless, so you simply won't find it on the market.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Don't waste any time.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm ready, I think.... Get started at what?

messages.mission.briefing.text: We've found a conglomeration of Augumene asteroids nearby. The ore's not much good to anyone due to the exorbitant cost of reprocessing, of course, but a couple of our scientists are interested in doing some research on such a rare substance. In any case, hopefully you've been around the block enough times that you can find the ore and bring it in.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Not bad! Perhaps I was wrong about you.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A commercial station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} was destroyed in a freak accident. They're saying it was some sort of rogue asteroid, and it's fallen to us to analyze the thing. We're going to need all of it. Most of the asteroid is still at the site of the accident. It's a grim task, I know. But we need to do this if we're going to figure out how this happened.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
No, no, not at all—

Listen, it's just coming over the news channels now. There, see? A commercial station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} was destroyed in a freak accident. They're saying it was some sort of rogue asteroid. Investigators are reporting over ten thousand confirmed dead so far. Naturally, people are demanding answers. The government wants answers, the media wants answers, the people want answers... you get the idea. And nobody seems to have any answers.

To put it simply, this shouldn't have happened. {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and its surrounding systems were cleared of rogue asteroids years ago, or so we thought. In fact, the station's position and orbit were chosen specifically to ensure its safety from collisions with celestial objects. If we don't find out how this asteroid got there, the finger pointing is going to start. Nobody's job will be safe once that starts happening.

It's fallen to us to analyze the asteroid. We're going to need all of it, {[character]player.name}. The asteroid is still at the site of the accident, though it's busted up some, I imagine.

It's a grim task, I know. But it's one we need to undertake if we're going to figure out how this terrible thing happened.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've retrieved all the ore samples.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Damn it, do you want me to lose my job?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You know, if you aren't part of the solution....

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: If it will help, I'll do this.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm not going to do this just to save your job.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I can't continue on with this. Sorry.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you. We need to get this thing settled, and quick.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: What is it? Have I done something wrong?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: About that asteroid collision: Don't worry about it. One of my coworkers just got sacked for it, and he was an idiot anyway. Looks like the whole thing is blowing over. Still, would have been nice to put solving this whole mess on my résumé.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thanks. We'll get this to the boys in the lab immediately.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: Never mind about the investigation. It's been handed off to someone else.

messages.mission.briefing.text: I've just gotten word about a deposit of Augumene in this system. Now, we're not really sure what use we might make of it, but a number of our competitors seem to want it for research, so that means we need to move on it too. Go out to the bookmark I'll provide for you and mine every unit of the stuff you find there for us to study… before anyone else gets their hands on it.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: I've just gotten word about a deposit of Augumene in this system. Now, we're not really sure what use we might make of it, but a number of our competitors seem to want it for research, so that means we need to move on it too. Go out to the bookmark I'll provide for you and mine every unit of the stuff you find there for us to study… before anyone else gets their hands on it.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I found your mystery rocks. Enjoy.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Oh, great! There goes my entire thesis. Four years of preliminary research, all brought to an end by you. Thanks.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You're on their side, aren't you?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sure, I think I can help you out.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes extremely expensive safety precautions — which more than negates any profit to be made from reprocessing the stuff. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm not interested.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm too busy to go looking for your mystery rocks. Sorry.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent! I'll get my lab ready.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Yeah, I'm looking for work.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: I'm working under a deadline here. I'm never going to get my research finished now! I have to find a new topic for my dissertation because of your procrastination.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Wonderful! I'll get to work on this right away.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I've got to get going on this research. I'll get someone else to find me some Augumene before it's too late to finish my dissertation.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: You are too late. The Mercium is now in the hands of our enemies.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Ah, you haven't heard, apparently, or you'd know what I meant. Well, that's a relief. The fact is, we've gotten word of the location of a bunch of Mercium ore here in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but we believe that our information has also been leaked to other factions — including the Gallenteans. It's vital that you collect all the Mercium: It cannot be allowed to fall into enemy hands.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've procured the Mercium for our cause.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: If enemy factions get their hands on that Mercium, it's on your head, not mine.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I can do that. Sure. Where to, again?

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Though Mercium is not commercially viable at present, it remains of scientific interest (and thus potentially of future financial interest) to agents of virtually all factions.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: That sounds lame to me. No thanks.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm not going to all that trouble over some worthless rocks. Sorry, but I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Go quickly. I've uploaded the location to your NeoCom.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Heard…? I hear lots of things. Which thing are you talking about?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've gotten word of the location of a bunch of Mercium ore here in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but we believe that our information has also been leaked to other factions, including the Gallenteans. It's vital that you collect all the Mercium: It cannot be allowed to fall into enemy hands.

Be aware that this amount of raw Mercium ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: {[character]player.name} , you are a credit to your people.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: We can wait no longer. I will seek out someone else to recover the Mercium before it is captured by our enemies.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Oh, right. I was thinking I'd already sent you a com-chat about this. Heh. Sorry.

One of our sources obtained information on the whereabouts of a significant deposit of Mercium ore. It would be disastrous for our cause if this Mercium were to fall into Amarrian or Caldari hands. Unfortunately, we're certain that they already know about it, so as I said, we must work quickly.

Remember, they want that Mercium, so that means we need it more. Get it? You do whatever you have to to get this done quickly, alright?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I got there first, I guess. Here's the ore.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: If they find it first, it's on your head. Not mine.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: If they find it first, it's on your head. Not mine.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I understand. I'll get that ore in no time. No worries.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Though Mercium is not commercially viable at present, it remains of scientific interest (and thus potentially of future financial interest) to agents of virtually all factions.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I can't take that kind of pressure. Sorry.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I couldn't get the Mercium, and I'm not about to do it now. Sorry, but I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Go quickly, then. Time is precious!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Why? Work quickly on what? I'm in the dark here.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
One of our sources obtained information on the whereabouts of a significant deposit of Mercium ore. It would be disastrous for our cause if this Mercium were to fall into Amarrian or Caldari hands. Unfortunately, we're certain that they already know about it, so as I said, we must work quickly.

Be aware that this amount of raw Mercium ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Well done! Glad to have had you on board for this one.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Seems like every government around wants some of this Mercium stuff. I don't know why, but if they all want it, then it might be worth a bundle to me down the road if I can get it first. I mean, no one's willing to pay for it now, but I'm thinking ahead: All four sides bidding, you got any idea how high that might drive the auction prices?

Now, I happen to have the location of some of this stuff. Thing is, I don't have a ship to handle it, so I need you, and I'm willing to put some money up front against this future "investment." Get in, get me that ore, and get out before somebody else pops in there for it. Simple.

Be aware that this amount of raw Mercium ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
This thing: Seems like every government around wants some of this Mercium stuff. I don't know why, but if they all want it, then it might be worth a bundle to me down the road if I can get it first. I mean, no one's willing to pay for it now, but I'm thinking ahead: All four sides bidding, you got any idea how high that might drive the auction prices?

Now, I happen to have the location of some of this stuff. Thing is, I don't have a ship to handle it, so I need you, and I'm willing to put some money up front against this future "investment." Alright? You gotta get in, get me that ore, and get out before somebody else pops in there for it. Simple.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's your Mercium. So, where's my cut?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Don't worry, I'll find someone who's willing to make some decent ISK.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Not everybody's got what it takes. I knew that when I first looked at you.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sounds like a good deal. I'm in.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Though Mercium is not commercially viable at present, it remains of scientific interest (and thus potentially of future financial interest) to agents of virtually all factions.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm not interested in getting caught in a four-way crossfire just to mine some rocks that might be worth something to someone at some point.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Selling to all four of the big empires? Uh... even I don't want to piss off that many people. Nah, I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Remember, move fast. Time's of the essence, huh?

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: What "thing" might that be?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Somebody else already beat you to that Mercium, bonehead. Way to go.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Here you go. Oh, this is gonna be just like hacking into that SCC station computer and making ISK for myself!

Uh, I mean, not that I've ever done that....

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I don't have this kinda time, {[character]player.name}. I gotta move on this Mercium before it's gone.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've found an old mining post in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. But, the thing is, we can't find who used to own it: There are no records of its being built or even existing. It's simply empty. No sign of anyone left there, dead or otherwise. Our initial investigation found extensive fire damage, gas leaks; you name it, it went wrong. Lots of explosive damage, though we can't tell if that was accidental or intentional. And some marks... well, we just don't know what could do that to metal. It's damn creepy, that's for sure.

Anyway, near as we can tell, the miners were working on a large Lyavite deposit. They didn't finish, because there's still about 5,000 units of it at the site. Now, I know Lyavite isn't the most popular rock, but nobody just leaves that much ore lying around. And besides, the brains at the lab figure they can use the stuff for some of their research, so this opportunity is too good to pass up.

That's where you come in. Warp in, mine the Lyavite, and warp out. It's that easy.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Well, we've got a bit of a weird one here. We've found an old mining post in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. But, the thing is, we can't find who used to own it: There are no records of its being built or even existing. It's simply empty. No sign of anyone left there, dead or otherwise. Our initial investigation found extensive fire damage, gas leaks — you name it, it went wrong. Lots of explosive damage, though we can't tell if that was accidental or intentional. And some marks... well, we just don't know what could do that to metal. It's damn creepy, that's for sure.

Warp in, mine the Lyavite, and warp out. It's that easy.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I'm back from the ghost station, ore and all.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'll not ask why. I'm sure you have your reasons.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm not going to force you. But someone has to go.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: If it needs to be done, it needs to be done. I'll get you the Lyavite.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Abandoned posts and stations aren't as uncommon as you might expect. Most are actually only half-built, victims of insufficient funding; often pirates or other drifters move in and patch holes just well enough to prevent decompression. Other times, the stations just aren't profitable or inhabitable, for any number of reasons, and it actually costs less to just leave the station floating there rather than to dismantle it.

But even then, there are usually records, people... something....

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Something weird is going on here, and I'm not touching it. No thanks.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've seen all sorts of crap as a pilot, and this is too creepy even for me. I'm out.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Take care of yourself out there. The investigator I sent out is still having nightmares.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Whatever it is, you know I'm up for it.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Look, I know the mission sounded a bit off, but it needed to get done. My superiors are really putting the pressure on now, and I have to give this to someone else. I'm sorry.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You made it back? You got the Lyavite okay? You didn't... see anything, did you? No? Okay. Good.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
You are not going to believe this. Remember that abandoned mining post I told you about? The one with the Lyavite? It's gone. I don't mean someone else mined it, or it was raided or anything. It's just gone. We've sent five different scouts out there, and they all confirm that the location where the post used to be is just dead space.

Even the dust is gone.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I was talking to some blowhard in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} when his station was destroyed. So, I'm thinking raiders, right? But no, it's even better. I send a few probes out that way, 'cause I want to know who to send the thank you card to. Turns out there were no raiders. Turns out that the whole damn station was hit by an asteroid full of Augumene! Luckily, I know a guy who's willing to pay decent kreds for the stuff, even though it's pretty much worthless! Heh!

It's like some angry, ironic god came down and crushed that jerk with a giant wad of kred notes, all for me! I want you to go out there, and bring me back all of that Augumene.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I'm on the comm, talking to this blowhard I knew back from my days at the academy, right...? So he's going on and on about how his corporation in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} is going to make ISK hand over fist mining some rare ore, blah blah blah. Then all these alarms start going off on his end. And I'm thinking his stupid corp is getting raided or something. Then, all of a sudden, the wall behind him disappears and he's ripped away from the screen! The blowhard got spaced right in front of my eyes!

Now, here's the best part. I send a few probes out that way, 'cause I want to know who to send the thank you card to. Turns out there were no raiders. Turns out that the whole damn station was hit by an asteroid full of Augumene! Luckily, I know a guy who's willing to pay decent kreds for the stuff, even though it's pretty much worthless! Heh! It's like some angry, ironic god came down and crushed that jerk with a giant wad of kred notes, all for me!

So, anyway, I want you to go out there and bring me back all of that Augumene. Do that, and I'll have a nice reward here for you when your come back, alright?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's the Augumene. Where's my ISK?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Don't tell me you're scared of a little rock?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: What? You don't like free ISK?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: You're a little twisted. And I'm okay with that. Yeah, I'll get you your Augumene.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes very expensive safety precautions. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: You seem entirely too happy with all this. And that troubles me. I'm going to decline, I'm afraid.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: This is more than a little weird. I'm not mining this Augumene anymore.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Go get me some of that magnificent ore.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You seem happy. What is it?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Great. You took just long enough for some other vultures to get all the Augumene. That rock was meant for me, but no, you had to prance around until it was too late. Thanks for nothing.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Ah, it even feels like providence. And cold, hard kredits. Speaking of which, here's yours.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I don't have time to wait for you to decide whether you like ISK or not. I'll get someone else to mine my lucky rock. So you can just get lost, okay?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
To be part of the future you need to help build it first. That's what I'm asking you to do.

There's a rare ore called Mercium, similar to Omber, but it's much more difficult to reprocess. Current methods render the ore unusable. It's maddening to no end. I think I might have solved the problem, though. I can't tell you my whole theory, but it's a variant on the standard electrolysis method used by planetside miners. All I need is some Mercium to try it on.

There's a rich deposit of Mercium in this system. Bring me 1,800 units and we might both end up rich.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You simply have no vision.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You simply have no vision.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Most people don't go looking for Mercium, as it doesn't do so well out on the open market. If you are having trouble finding it, you can right click the "Mercium" icon in your mission log and add it to your overview.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I quit. Sorry, but I have better things to do with my time.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Prepare to change the world.

messages.mission.briefing.text: There's a rich deposit of Mercium in this system. Bring me 1,800 units and we might both end up rich.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Well, looks like the research guys have shot several holes in my Mercium reprocessing theory. Son of a… Well, you did your part, anyway: Here's your payment.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
It seems that some rogue scientists just could not leave Creation well enough alone. One man in particular, one "Vilus Seermal," has apparently been performing genetic experiments on the fuzzy little critters, in a hidden laboratory not far from here. While this is not illegal, the ethics of his experiments are certainly in question. He has, for whatever reason, apparently turned the things into cute, cuddly killing machines.

Well, we just received an emergency transmission from the laboratory. Listen.

"We need help immediately! The coordinates are attached within the carrier wave of this frequency. You must help us. They have us trapped in the communications room, and they're chewing through the door as I speak! Hurry! (grinding sounds) No! They're coming through! They've gnawed through! Oh, no! NOOOO... (crashing, squealing sounds, human screams)..."

You get the idea, I think. But there's the most disturbing part. After all the screaming and crashing stops, this comes at the end of the message.

"(Hissing static, distant slurping, and then a small, impish voice) Fooood! Good. Food good! Bring more foooood!"

I shudder to think of it. I'm sure all those scientists are dead, but we can't allow those mutated furriers to mix with the general furrier population. Yet there are environmentalists out there who would protect those little beasts.

Get out there and destroy that laboratory before someone does something incredibly rash.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The vicious vermin are dead!

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Well, let us pray to all that's holy that those vicious vermin die of starvation before anyone finds them.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I hope I can find someone else to handle this on such short notice.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: The furriers must die. And I love playing exterminator.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Furriers are small animals commonly found as pets among the Amarrian higher class. They resemble rabbits in size and temperament, although they can turn vicious from time to time; many royals, the Tash-Murkons in particular, find this trait quite endearing. The creatures are largely mammalian, although they do exhibit some reptilian qualities: They lay eggs rather than giving live birth, and they have distinctly bird-like, scaly facial features.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I can't do this. Whatever those scientists did, these are still innocent creatures.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: On second thought, I can't do this. Whatever those scientists created, these are still innocent creatures.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Don't waste any time.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Oh? Try me. I've heard some crazy stuff in my time...

messages.mission.briefing.text:
It seems that some rogue scientists just could not leave Creation well enough alone. One man in particular, one "Vilus Seermal," has apparently been performing genetic experiments on the fuzzy little critters, in a hidden laboratory not far from here. I shudder to think of it. I'm sure all those scientists are dead, but we can't allow those mutated furriers to mix with the general furrier population. Yet there are environmentalists out there who would protect those little beasts. In fact, I have word that some eco-terrorists might be on their way at this very moment: Get out there and destroy that laboratory before someone does something incredibly rash. And don't let anyone stop you!

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Nice work. I was afraid overzealous animal rights people might get word of this.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: You've heard of Parriaval Mastes, the infamous troublemaker? Well, he's escaped from the prison camp where he was held. We need someone to locate him and bring him back here discreetly. If word of his escape gets out, political dissidents from all across the Empire will start causing trouble. Fortunately, we've tracked the ship he stole and located its signal at a suspected terrorists' outpost in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Are you willing to fly out there and retrieve him? There's a significant reward.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've captured the fugitive as ordered.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Dinner engagement, eh? I see. Going to be wearing any yellow, by chance...?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: That crook won't escape me. I'll leave immediately.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Your agent has placed a bookmark in your NeoCom to help you get to the correct location. Open People and Places, go to Bookmarks, right-click on this mission objective, and choose "Set destination." Then go to your Ship Control Panel and click the Autopilot icon. Your ship will now travel to the appropriate system. Once you've arrived, your Autopilot will deactivate.

Now go back to your Bookmarks, right-click again on this mission, and select "Warp to location." Once you've arrived at the fugitive's location, you'll see him as a red target icon on your Overview. Engage and destroy his ship. Once the fugitive's vessel has been destroyed, a cargo container will eject from it. This is Parriaval's escape capsule. Once you're within 1,500 meters, right-click on the cargo container and select "Open" (or use the "Open" icon above your Overview). A window will now open displaying the contents: Click and hold the prisoner and drag him into your cargo hold.

Congratulations, you've recaptured Parriaval Mastes! Now return to {[character]agentID.name} for your reward.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Well, I'd be happy to help, but I'm afraid I have a dinner engagement elsewhere...

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks for your help! Now get out there and capture that fugitive, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: What do you need me to do?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You have our thanks for a job well done.

Your agent has placed a bookmark in your NeoCom to help you get to the correct location. Open People and Places, go to Bookmarks, right-click on this mission objective, and choose "Set destination." Then go to your Ship Control Panel and click the Autopilot icon. Your ship will now travel to the appropriate system. Once you've arrived, your Autopilot will deactivate.

Now go back to your Bookmarks, right-click again on this mission, and select "Warp to location." Once you've arrived at the fugitive's location, you'll see him as a red target icon on your Overview. Engage and destroy his ship. Once the fugitive's vessel has been destroyed, a cargo container will eject from it. This is the Varshan's escape capsule. Once you're within 1,500 meters, right-click on the cargo container and select "Open" (or use the "Open" icon above your Overview). A window will now open displaying the contents: Click and hold the prisoner and drag him into your cargo hold.

Congratulations, you've recaptured Telos Varshan! Now return to {[character]agentID.name} for your reward.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Well, I'd be happy to help, but I'm afraid I have a dinner engagement elsewhere...

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks for your help! Now get out there and capture that fugitive, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: What do you need me to do?

messages.mission.briefing.text: The terrorist Telos Varshan has escaped from the prison camp where he was held. We need someone to locate him and bring him back here discreetly. Fortunately, we've tracked the ship he stole and located its signal at a suspected terrorists' outpost in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Fly out there and retrieve him. There's a significant reward.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You have our thanks for a job well done.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: The murderer Milare Terhellen has escaped from the prison camp where he was held. We need someone to locate him and bring him back here discreetly. If word of his escape gets out, citizens all across the Republic will start to panic. Fortunately, we've tracked the ship he stole and located its signal at a suspected terrorists' outpost in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Are you willing to fly out there and retrieve him? There's a significant reward.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've captured the fugitive as ordered.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Dinner engagement, eh? I see. Going to be wearing any yellow, by chance...?
