messages.mission.briefing.text:
We are working closely with several bathhouses through Nugoeihuvi to acquire the large number of companions required for SPLET. We are close to completing the contracts. All that is required to finalize is a final inspection, to be performed by the SPLET organizer.

Pick up the NOH prostitute-- I'll upload the station address to your NeoCom-- and return her here. After this last mission, I believe the program will be ready to launch.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Originally, we were going to be hiring the best dancers in Caldari space. It was to be a dazzling performance, with custom arranged music and specially choreographed numbers. It would have been a show both tantalizing and tasteful. But such things are expensive.

We found the best cost-effective solution by working with NOH's bathhouses. Traveling with SPLET will be a "companion army." We are close to completing the contracts. All that is left is a final round of...negotiation by the SPLET chairman.

Pick up the NOH prostitute-- I'll upload the station address to your NeoCom-- and return her here. After this last mission, I believe the program will be ready to launch.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I have brought the— uh— negotiator.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Damn it, the chairman will have my head for this.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: But we were so close to finally being done with this!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I will do this last thing.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The Nugoeihuvi Corporation, or NOH, is the only Caldari mega-corporation that has focused on the entertainment industry. They have always been suspected of strong ties to the Caldari underworld, mainly because many of their products cater to that social element or are on the borderline of legality.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: This task seems to favor the chairman more than the Caldari soldiers.  I will not do it.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I will not continue this mission.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good.  Although SPLET has not become what was originally envisioned, I doubt the soldiers will complain too loudly...

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: What's been cut?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: The chairman has grown impatient with the negotiator's delayed arrival.  He has cancelled SPLET, citing a “personal insult” on the part of NOH.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent.  Thanks to your help, SPLET will soon be making its way through the Caldari ranks.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: The chairman has grown impatient with the negotiator's delayed arrival.  He has cancelled SPLET, citing a “personal insult” on the part of NOH.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Turns out someone got the bright idea that if mining drones mine more ore, bigger drones would mine even more ore. This guy's team slapped some mining drone's AI into non-regulation heavy combat units and threw some mining lasers on. He even hacked the firmware so that the mining brains could control the weaponry, making some sort of self-sufficient mining machines.

Now there's a bunch of haywire drones zipping about this rare mineral that we want. Our guys in the lab need it for research, I guess. The drones aren't even mining the rock, last I heard, but they have tried to bore through any ship we send out there....

It's getting ridiculous. If you can, get out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, neutralize the drones, and bring back all the Mercium; we'll pay you well for your efforts.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You ever try mining with drones? Useful little guys, huh? Yeah, well, to a point…

Turns out someone got the bright idea that if mining drones mine more ore, bigger drones would mine even more ore. This guy's team slapped some mining drone's AI into non-regulation heavy combat units and threw some mining lasers on. He even hacked the firmware so that the mining brains could control the weaponry, making some sort of self-sufficient mining machines. But of course the genius didn't test the things properly before sending them out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} to mine Mercium. And of course now he's made himself scarce.

You can probably guess what happened. Now there's a bunch of haywire drones zipping about this rare mineral that we want — our guys in the lab need it for research, I guess. The drones aren't even mining the rock, last I heard, but they have tried to bore through any ship we send out there....

It's getting ridiculous. If you can, get out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, neutralize the drones, and bring back all the Mercium; we'll pay you well for your efforts.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've returned with your Mercium.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Really, {[character]player.name}, I expected more from you.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: They're still just drones. What's the big deal?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Take out drones, mine Mercium. Got it, chief.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Since their invention sometime around the Gallente-Caldari War, drones have become commonplace in nearly all facets of life. Drones vary in size from that of a human eye up to those that rival the largest frigates, and they have been built to fill the roles of fighters, miners, and repair vehicles, as well as household cleaning units and tiny children's toys — not to mention their various military uses in space stations and on planetary surfaces alike. New uses for drone technology are being developed constantly.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't want to mess with someone else's failed experiments.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I don't have time to mess with this crazy drone business.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Glad to hear it. I'll leave you to it, then.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You know me. I'm always interested in work.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Someone else got to the Mercium before we did; most likely those drones, which have also disappeared. You better start getting on the ball.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I knew those drones wouldn't be that big a deal for you.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I can't just sit on this contract. I'm sending this off to someone with more initiative.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I've just discovered a sizable deposit of Pithix out by an old mining station. The station's been abandoned for a while now, but there are still working sensors in the area; that's how we picked up on the Pithix. Problem is, the transmission's hardly secure. I need you to get out there and bring me back that rock before someone else cleans the place out.

So, are you game?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've got your rocks here. Seems like a waste of time, but it's your ISK…

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Great, now there's no way I'll get someone there in time. Thanks a bunch.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Stop wasting my time, then.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Yeah, okay. I'll do it.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Pithix is virtually worthless, due to the terrible inefficiency of reprocessing it; one is far better off to mine for Jaspet instead. As a result, you won't find the former ore on the market. In fact, most sensor manufacturers don't even bother giving it a unique listing in their mining packages when they produce standard ship scanners.

If you're having trouble finding the Pithix at the mission location, simply right-click the "Pithix" icon in the mission details and select "Add to Overview."

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: No thanks. Not interested.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I don't want to do this anymore. Sorry.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good stuff. Get to it.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Sure. What kind of rocks?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I've just discovered a sizable deposit of Pithix out by an old mining station. The station's been abandoned for a while now, but there are still working sensors in the area; that's how we picked up on the Pithix. Problem is, the transmission's hardly secure. I need you to get out there and bring me back that rock before someone else cleans the place out.

Oh, there might also be some rogue drone activity in the area. Fair warning.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Alright. Now I just have to find a buyer…

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
There's an old mining station not far from here that hasn't been used in months. The mining company gave up their claim when they thought they wiped the area of all valuable materials. About all they left was a bunch of Pithix.

But it just so happens that a couple of scientists who do some work for us want Pithix for some of their research projects. There's about 4,500 units of it out there, and we want all of it. Don't worry, we'll pay you.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I'm back… with your Pithix.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Not motivated enough? This was almost free money!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: This sounds easy enough. I'm in.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Most people don't go looking for Pithix. It doesn't do so well out on the open market. That's why a lot of sensor manufacturers don't even bother to give it its own unique entry in the mining packages they produce for standard ship scanners.

If you are having trouble finding the Pithix 'roids in this mission, you can right-click the "Pithix" icon in your mission log and add it to your overview.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: No deal. Sorry. I'm a lover and a fighter, but I'm no miner.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm pretty bored of this already. See ya.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Alrighty, then, get to it.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Sure. What kind and where?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's an abandoned mining station not far from here that still has a bunch of Pithix 'roids floating around. There's about 4,500 units of it out there, and we want all of it. Don't worry, we'll pay you.

Oh, and keep an eye out for rogue drones. There might be a few roaming around.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I'll take that, and here's your pay. Pleasure doing business.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
There's an old mining station not far from here. The mining company that owned it hasn't been around for months. Something about repeated attacks by "blood thirsty raiders." Heh. When they pulled out, they took everything they could with them. About all they left was a bunch of Pithix.

Now, it just so happens that I know a couple of scientists who want Pithix for some of their research projects. There's about 4,500 units of it out there, and they're willing to pay a good price for all of it. Go get it for me. Don't worry. I'll give you your fair share.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Got your Pithix here.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Not motivated enough? This was almost free money!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: This sounds easy enough.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Most people don't go looking for Pithix. It doesn't do so well out on the open market. That's why a lot of sensor manufacturers don't even bother to give it its own unique entry in the mining packages they produce for standard ship scanners.

If you are having trouble finding the Pithix 'roids in this mission, you can right-click the "Pithix" icon in your mission log and add it to your overview.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: No deal. Sorry. I'm a lover and a fighter, but I'm no miner.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm pretty bored of this already. See ya.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Get to it.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Sure. What kind and where?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's an old mining station not far from here. When they pulled out, they took everything they could with them; about all they left was a bunch of Pithix.

Now, it just so happens that I know a couple of scientists who want Pithix for some of their research projects. There's about 4,500 units of it out there, and they're willing to pay a good price for all of it. Go get it for me. I'll give you your fair share.

Oh, hey, make sure you fit some guns or something - we spotted some rogue drones around here recently.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I'll take that, and here's your pay. Pleasure doing business.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Mine 20 units of Crystalline Icicles. Oh, and watch out for pirates or rogue drones. Lots of them around these parts.

You will need an Ice Harvester module to complete this mission. Also, be aware that this amount of raw Crystalline Icicles ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Right away. But look, this one's a little weird. Just a heads up.

There's this guy who's making these really, truly gigantic ice sculptures — some kinda artsy shit, I don't know. I said, buddy, that much ice, it's gonna melt before you can finish carving it, or it's gonna break under its own weight. He says he knows that, says that's why he's gonna build it in space! Crazy…

Anyway, he's got the money, so what am I gonna say but "how much and how fast?" So, can you get 20 units of Crystalline Icicles over here ASAP? I got a location for you.

You will need an Ice Harvester module to complete this mission. Also, be aware that this amount of raw Crystalline Icicles ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here're your shiny icicles.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You're gonna leave me to deal with a disappointed artist? Oh, that's real nice. Thanks so much.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You're gonna leave me to deal with a disappointed artist? Oh, that's real nice. Thanks so much.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Yeah, I'll help you out.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm not much of an "art" person. So no.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I don't like art anymore. Not when it takes effort. I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Please hurry back with the space ice.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You do? Great, when can I start?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Now he doesn't want that ice! He wants a different kind of ice because now it's a different phase of the moon and the colors don't match anymore! And he won't stop talking about this stuff! Next time, move a little quicker, huh?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Oh, thank you. I was about ready to strangle that guy.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: Now he doesn't want that ice! He wants a different kind of ice because now it's a different phase of the moon and the colors don't match anymore! And he won't stop talking about this stuff! Next time, move a little quicker, huh?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's a field of Azure Ice at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I want to sell it to some less-than-brilliant colonists. It's not as good as Blue Ice, but the they won't know the difference. Bring me back, oh, 20 blocks of it. I'll split the profit with you.

You will need an Ice Harvester module to complete this mission. Also, be aware that this amount of raw Azure Ice may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Alright! You ever been out to some of those backwater colonies? You know the ones I mean. Barren wastelands of rocks and dust where some nut got the bright idea to try to build the agricultural community of tomorrow? Kind of place where the main export is despair? That kind of place?

Well, so happens I know of one that's just starting up. Poor bastards need some fuel. They're willing to pay good money, too. Now, I could sell them the good stuff, but seriously, these jokers wouldn't know good ice if it fell out of the sky and crushed their pet furrier.

There's a field of Azure Ice at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's not as good as Blue Ice, but the colonists won't know the difference. Bring me back about, oh, 20 blocks of it. I'll sell it to the colony goobers and cut you in. Sound good?

You will need an Ice Harvester module to complete this mission. Also, be aware that this amount of raw Azure Ice may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Your "high-quality" Azure Ice is ready.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: As far as I'm concerned, there is never a better use of one's skills than exploiting the ignorant. Go figure.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Those colonists already ruined their lives. What's the harm in making some ISK off of that?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: One order of Azure Ice, coming up.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The open market doesn't bother with Azure Ice. Everyone and their grandmothers know it's not nearly as useful as Blue Ice. Planetary water ice has more demand. Any deal that gets you ISK for Azure Ice is a good sell. And if you ever get stuck with Azure Ice and no mission to turn it in... well, just be glad your docking bay has no volume limit.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Maybe I'll ruin the lives of unsuspecting colonists some other time, but not today.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Maybe ripping off colonists isn't the best use of my abilities.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: You and me, we're gonna go far.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Could be. Let me hear more, my friend.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: You moved too slow. Someone else got the sell. Not only that, but they got the right stuff for the job. How is anyone supposed to get repeat business if customers keep getting what they need?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent. I've already got your share of the money ready. This should keep their colony running just well enough so that they can make more orders.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: You moved too slow. Someone else got the sell. Not only that, but they got the right stuff for the job. How is anyone supposed to get repeat business if customers keep getting what they need?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Drones scare the daylights out of some people. To be completely honest, the big hives even scare me a little. The smaller drone groups are annoying, but more manageable. Usually.

Anyway, there's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that seems to be attracting these wild drones. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just end up replacing them. We've figured out that, for whatever reason, they're attracted to the gas. So the best solution is to just remove the cloud: no cloud, no drones. If you can harvest that cloud out, it'd be a big help.

You must own and be able to use a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission. If you do not or cannot, please just decline; note that you can decline one mission every 4 hours without standing loss.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've harvested the gas cloud. Hopefully the drones won't be so interested in the area now.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Damn. I'll have to find someone else. Thanks for being honest, though.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I can harvest the cloud for you.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Rogue drones and "wild drones" are the terms used for advanced drones that have mutated out of control. A few years ago, a respected Gallentean inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own in every sense like a regular space ship, except for being computer controlled, and hence unmanned.

Unfortunately, the drones became unruly, then unmanageable, and soon developed the ability to "infect" other drones, and eventually even ships, with their capricious artificial intelligence. Needless to say, Gallente soon abandoned this line of research.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm afraid I can't do this.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you. You wouldn't believe how difficult it is to find a good pilot capable of using a gas harvester.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Not at all. Why?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that seems to be attracting these wild drones. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just end up replacing them. We've figured out that, for whatever reason, they're attracted to the gas. So the best solution is to just remove the cloud: no cloud, no drones. If you can harvest that cloud out, it'd be a big help.

You must fit a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission. Of course, you'll also need to deal with whatever drones are there.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great. We'll keep an eye on the area, but I think you've fixed our drone problem.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's attracting all sorts of drones to it. I don't know why. It's like insects to a flame or somethin'. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just take their place. It's annoying as hell.

I figure the best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. Simple. If you can harvest that cloud out, I'll pay you well.

You gotta own and be able to use a Gas Cloud Harvester to do this mission. If you don't or ya can't, just say "no thanks." You can decline one mission about every 4 hours without pissing me off, so no worries.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've harvested the gas cloud. Hopefully the drones won't be so interested in the area now.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Damn. I'll have to find someone else. Hey, thanks for being honest, though.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Consider the cloud harvested.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Rogue drones and "wild drones" are the terms used for advanced drones that have mutated out of control. A few years ago, some ingenious Gallentean inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own in every sense like a regular space ship, except for being computer controlled, hence unmanned. The drones became unruly, then unmanageable. Needless to say, this research was soon abandoned by the Gallenteans.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm afraid I can't do this. So... "no thanks."

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you. You wouldn't believe how difficult it is to find a good gas harvester around here.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You know me, ready for anything.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's attracting all sorts of drones to it. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just take their place. I figure the best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. Simple. If you can harvest that cloud out, I'll pay you well.

You gotta fit a Gas Cloud Harvester to do this mission. And you also gotta deal with any drones there. Fair enough?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great. We'll keep an eye on the area, but I think you've fixed our drone problem.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Well, we've located some asteroids that contain substantial amounts of Polygypsum. It's a comparatively rare mineral, and almost completely unknown in this system. Our guys want to have a look at the stuff and see if they can figure out some way to make use of it; however, we don't have anyone who wants to deal with the stuff. So guess who I thought of first?

You'll need to grab all 2,800 units of the stuff and get it back here. So what do you think? Are you in?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: It was awfully dull, but the reward should make some amends. Here's your ore.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I see. Well, I guess I can find someone else willing to make an easy few ISK.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm on it. Back in a bit.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Polygypsum is widely considered worthless because of the dangers associated with storing and reprocessing it. As a result, you won't find this ore on the market. In fact, for this reason, most sensor manufacturers don't even bother putting it as a unique entry in the computers when they install standard ship scanners.

If you're having trouble finding the correct ore at the mission location, you can right-click the "Polygypsum" icon in the mission details in your Opportunities interface and select "Add to Overview."

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Hm. No, I think I'm going to go, oh… watch some paint dry, actually. Thanks for the offer, though.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent, {[character]player.name}. Thanks.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You know I do. What have you got?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've located some asteroids that contain substantial amounts of Polygypsum — that's a comparatively rare mineral, and almost completely unknown in this system. Our guys want to have a look at the stuff and see if they can figure out some way to make use of it; however, we don't have anyone who wants to deal with it. So guess who I thought of first?

You'll need to grab all 2,800 units of the stuff and get it back here. See you then.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You've earned your reward as far as I'm concerned, {[character]player.name}, that's for sure.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has an unusual request for the right miner. We need a big shipment of Geodite crystals for a client of ours, some gemology lab. Maybe you've heard of Geodite, but if not, it'd be no surprise — the stuff's pretty much worthless. But these gemologists figure they might be able to get some decent stones out of it and make a bit of profit that way. Whatever. They want to pay for it, so it's all good by me. And you'll get your cut, don't worry.

Anyway, if you're interested, I'll send the coordinates over to your ship's NeoCom — the field's in this system.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's your load of Geodite.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Maybe next time. Once again progress grinds to a halt.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Man, I hope I can find someone else to handle this.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sure, I'll see what I can do.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Geodite ore is pretty much worthless because of the poor-quality Nocxium it produces; one is far better off to look for Crokite instead... although that's no easy job. In any case, you won't find Geodite on the market anywhere.

If you're having trouble finding the Geodite at the mission location, you can right-click the "Geodite" icon in the mission's details and select "Add to Overview."

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: That's one boring scenario you've worked out there, my friend. I think I'm gonna pass.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Hm. This is a pretty boring scenario you've worked out here, my friend. I think I'm gonna cut out.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Don't waste any time. These guys are waiting for their ore.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: We do? Or I do? Either way, I'm ready. What's up?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We need a big shipment of Geodite crystals for a client of ours, some gemology lab. These gemologists figure they might be able to get some decent stones out of it and make a bit of profit that way. Whatever. They want to pay for it, so it's all good by me. And you'll get your cut, don't worry.

Geodite takes up a lot of room: You're going to need a big cargo hold, or you'll have to make several trips.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Nice work. I'll keep you in mind when something else comes up.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
War is one of the biggest boons to business you could hope for. It's a hungry giant that will eat anything you can throw at it. And the thing is, if you don't feed it, it will just eat you…. But if you feed it well? Oh, the rewards. Public recognition, sure, but the contracts, the contracts, {[character]player.name}! That's where the real ISK is. And we're going to get those contracts. Oh, yes. But first we need minerals.

Right now, it seems the giant on our doorstep wants Oeryl, and we're going to give it to him. There's a deposit out at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Bring back all 5,600 units of the stuff and I'll make sure you get your share of the reward.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
It's the sound of war! It's been too long since the blaring of military marches has been heard, the stockpiling of weapons undertaken, the murderous idealism of a young generation inveigled. And to me it all seems like the clinking of ISK.

War is one of the biggest boons to business you could hope for. It's a hungry giant that will eat anything you can throw at it. And the thing is, if you don't feed it, it will just eat you…. But if you feed it well? Oh, the rewards. Public recognition, sure, but the contracts, the contracts, {[character]player.name}! That's where the real ISK is. And we're going to get those contracts. Oh, yes. But first we need minerals.

Right now, it seems the giant on our doorstep wants Oeryl, and we're going to give it to him. There's a deposit out at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Bring back all 5,600 units of the stuff and I'll make sure you get your share of the reward.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's the Oeryl. Uh, for the war effort.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Do you want the enemy to win? Do you?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I knew you were one of those spineless sympathizers.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: You know I'm never one to shy away from my patriotic duty.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: It has been nearly a century since the Caldari-Gallente War, the last major war between any of the Great Empires, came to a close. Though skirmishes have broken out here and there, the distractions of the ever-expanding "lawless" space and the efforts of organizations such as CONCORD have helped maintain an uneasy peace. But no peace lasts forever.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm not comfortable with the moral implications of this job.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I can't continue doing this. Sorry, but I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Be quick about it. We don't want to let anyone else beat us to that Oeryl.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Hear what, {[character]agentID.name}?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: In the time it took you to fail this mission, nearly 250 brave pilots lost their lives. You also failed to make a load of money. You need to do better.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work, {[character]player.name}. Just remember, you're not a profiteer — you're securing the financial stability of the homefront.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: While you were puttering around, deciding whether you were going to do the Oeryl job, the government went and got its ore from another seller. Nice effort. Or rather, lack thereof.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Look, I hear there's some Green Arisite that a bunch of people are looking to get their hands on. Now, I don't know why they want it, but if they want it, I want it.

You may have to hunt for it a bit; I hear the belt's got a lot of big broken-up old asteroids floating around. Might be a little creepy, but it shouldn't do you any harm, and I want that damn rock!

Go get it before those other bastards get their grubby hands on it!

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I got there first! Here's your stupid green rock.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Yeah — like a fox! Suit yourself, it's your loss.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: If I cooled off, I wouldn't have a business. Now move along.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Yeah, okay, I'll get your rock…

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Green Arisite is relatively worthless because of the high costs of reprocessing; one is far better off mining Gneiss instead. As a result, you won't find the former ore on the market. If you're having trouble finding the Arisite at the mission location, loading the "Mining" default overview will show all ores. If you're familiar with creating custom overview settings, Green Arisite is shown by enabling "Gneiss".

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I think I'll pass. Also, you might want to cool off a bit.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: On second thought? I'm out of here. And I think you're a little crazy.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Well, get going then! I need that rock!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Hm. Depends on the job…

messages.mission.briefing.text: I hear there's some Green Arisite that a bunch of people are looking to get their hands on. Now, I don't know why they want it, but if they want it, I want it. You may have to hunt for it a bit; I hear the belt's got a lot of big broken-up old asteroids floating around. Might be a little creepy, but it shouldn't do you any harm, and I want that damn rock!

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Hah! Who's the stupid one?! Now I can sell it for a fortune to those other jerks!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I do. And it's going to be a big haul.

Demand for minerals is skyrocketing. All the big empires are stockpiling for the coming fight. Oh, come on, you've seen the signs! Ships, rockets, drones, fortifications — all these things take material. The skirmishes out in 0.0 aren't lessening the demand any, either. Which is good for us. More demand means more profit.

To fill that demand, we're having to turn to some unorthodox ores. Green Arisite, for instance. I know of a large field that's full of the stuff. If you can get it for me, I'll make sure you're reimbursed. We just may be able to make some use of it, with the right tech. Who knows?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Your Green Arisite. But I think you're gonna lose your shirt on this one…

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: What kind of miner are you?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I guess I'll find someone who likes ISK, then.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: If the pay is good, I'm there.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Green Arisite is relatively worthless because of the high costs of reprocessing; one is far better off mining Gneiss instead. As a result, you won't find the former ore on the market. If you're having trouble finding the Arisite at the mission location, just right-click the "Green Arisite" icon in  this mission's details in your Opportunities interface and select "Add to Overview."

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Not today, sorry. Uh, my cousin just asked for help moving some furniture…

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text:
Too. Many. Rocks. Uhhhh…

I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Indeed. And paid you will be.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Why is that? You got something for me?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Demand for minerals is skyrocketing. Which is good for us. More demand means more profit.

To fill that demand, though, we're having to turn to some unorthodox ores: Green Arisite, for instance. I know of a large field that's full of the stuff. If you can get it for me, I'll make sure you're reimbursed. We just may be able to make some use of it, with the right tech. Who knows?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good job. Nice working with you

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
No, no. There are no Gallente. It's those cursed rogue drones. If the Gallente hadn't made those things way back during the Caldari-Gallente War, I wouldn't have this headache to deal with.

Here's the odd thing: There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that seems to be attracting drones. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just end up replacing them. We've figured out that, for whatever reason, they're attracted to the gas. The best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. If you can harvest that cloud out, it'd be a big help.

You must own and be able to use a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission. If you do not or cannot, please just decline; note that you can decline one mission every 4 hours without standing loss.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've harvested the gas cloud. Hopefully the drones won't be so interested in the area now.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Damn. I'll have to find someone else. Thanks for being honest, though.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I can harvest the cloud for you.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Rogue drones and "wild drones" are the terms used for advanced drones that have mutated out of control. A few years ago, some ingenious Gallentean inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own in every sense like a regular space ship, except for being computer controlled, hence unmanned. The drones became unruly, then unmanageable. Needless to say, this research was soon abandoned by the Gallenteans.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm afraid I can't do this.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you. You wouldn't believe how difficult it is to find a good gas harvester around here.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Gallente? I'll take care of them.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that seems to be attracting drones. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just end up replacing them. We've figured out that, for whatever reason, they're attracted to the gas. The best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. If you can harvest that cloud out, it'd be a big help.

You must fit a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission. Of course, you'll also need to deal with whatever drones are there.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great. We'll keep an eye on the area, but I think you've fixed our drone problem.

localizedName.text: Greater Good – Less Distasteful Matters (2 of 5)

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Well, not everyone has the stomach to do what must be done. Do you think you could manage to carry a reporter from point A to point B, or will that strain your moral sensibilities?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've done what you asked.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I've had just about enough of you anyway.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Some people just aren't ready to serve the greater good.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I think I can manage that.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Though Scope (the corporation taking its name from its famed primetime holocast, The Scope), was originally based inside the Gallente Federation, it has expanded to the point where it is now considered the leading news agency throughout the empires.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't want to be involved with anyone who thinks that your methods are acceptable.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I don't want to be involved with anyone who thinks that your methods are acceptable.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Don't forget, we are making sure that the blame for this action falls where it truly belongs: on the Amarr.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Something a little less morally objectionable, yes.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Take the reporter from {[location]agentStationID.name} to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, then report back.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
Good enough. Since someone else took care of that job you couldn't handle, things should still work out alright.

Come back to me when you're ready to do some more work for the cause... assuming you can handle it.

localizedName.text: Greater Good - Not Even Remotely Drastic Measures (4 of 5)

messages.mission.briefing.text: Go pick up the reporter at the location I've given you and bring him back to me.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Weak moral constitution, I suppose. Very well, then.

Go pick up a reporter waiting at a nearby station -- I'll give you the location -- and bring him back to me. Will that be supportable?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I brought back your reporter.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I gave you every opportunity to help our cause.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I gave you every opportunity to help our cause.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Um, okay. You could be a little less of a jerk about it, though.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm not interested in this busy-work.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: You know what? I'm tired of being insulted by a crazy person. I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Sure, chief. Whatever.

Oh, I suppose: At least you're doing something halfways useful.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: That sounds potentially less crazy, yeah.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
The ship was still destroyed, but the Empire managed to dodge the blame again. I've been hearing stories ranging from pirates to equipment failure. If you had done as I originally asked, at least some good would have come of this destruction.

Instead, you couldn't even move a reporter within a reasonable timeframe. Hold your head up high, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
The ship was still destroyed, but the Empire managed to dodge the blame again. I've been hearing stories ranging from pirates to equipment failure. If you had done as I originally asked, at least some good would have come of this destruction.

Instead, you couldn't even move a reporter within a reasonable timeframe. Hold your head up high, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
While you were ferrying that reporter over here, someone else took out that CONCORD committee, so there's still some real progress being made.

Come see me again when you're ready for real action.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
The government says we're prepared for war. You wouldn't know it by looking at our wounded. Space makes everything worse. Just look through the medical bay. Second-degree burns and frostbite are both alarmingly common, and are usually in conjunction with other serious injuries.

I need pain medications badly. I can't just wait for the next delivery. I need to produce my own drugs. For that I'm going to need Gamboge Cytoserocin. I heard a smuggler say there was a pocket at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Go there, and bring back everything you can. I'll try to make it worth your while.

You must own and be able to use a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission. If you do not or cannot, please just decline; note that you can decline one mission every 4 hours without standing loss.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's your gas. Do some good with it.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Okay, that's fine. It's better that you're upfront with these things than not.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: It just so happens I am trained in Gas Harvesters. I'll do it.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Although the compounds that are popularly called "boosters" are illegal in empire space, other legal derivatives of gas cloud materials are used in the medical community. These medicinal drugs are highly controlled, but are often the difference between life and death for many citizens.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm afraid I cannot do this.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you. Get back as quickly as you can.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: What's up? Happy to help.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I need pain medications badly. I can't just wait for the next delivery. I need to produce my own drugs. For that I'm going to need Gamboge Cytoserocin. I heard a smuggler say there was a pocket at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Go there, and bring back everything you can. I'll try to make it worth your while.

You need to fit a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: More good will come from this than you know.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I have a friend in a very difficult situation. He's due for a promotion, you see. More accurately, he would be if there weren't a few other promising individuals ahead of him in line. Such promising individuals, indeed, that I am sure their superiors would miss them dearly if anything were to happen to them.

However, you see, they are all Gallente officers, and for any agent of the State to interfere in Federation matters would be quite wrong, now, wouldn't it? Of course, it's not terribly uncommon for valiant officers, Gallente or otherwise, to meet quite unfortunate ends in any number of... well, mishaps. Yes, {[character]player.name}, it's not uncommon at all, is it? So I'm sure things will work themselves out somehow.

Anyhow, your mission. Well, this is quite embarrassing... I've completely forgotten any mission I might have had for you. Come to think of it, I've forgotten everything I was just talking about. Goodness, I think I'd better go lie down for a while.

But... I don't suppose you could look after my datapad here while I rest? It's quite important, you see, for it has the current coordinates of one of those promising Federation individuals, one of the ones we just discussed. And I wouldn't want that to fall into the wrong hands, now, would I?

And you... you look like you could use a break, too. Maybe a leisurely cruise out into space somewhere nearby, a chance to relax and, oh, I don't know, enjoy some scenery? Maybe pay someone a visit? And by the time I wake up, maybe my worries will have taken care of themselves, hmm?

Your agent's datapad has given you the coordinates to one of the competitors of your agent's "friend" in the Gallente Navy. Your "mission" once you arrive there should be abundantly clear.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
The corporations of the State have many friends, as you know... many friends in many interesting and useful places. Why is this relevant, you ask? Well, it's not at all… it was merely an idle thought I had today that I wanted to impart upon you.

But actually, now I come to think about the topic of friends… I am reminded of a particular friend of mine in a very difficult situation. He's due for a promotion, you see. More accurately, he would be if there weren't a few other promising individuals ahead of him in line. Such promising individuals, indeed, that I am sure their superiors would miss them dearly if anything were to happen to them. But it would be very, er, helpful... for me--for us--if this friend of ours were to get what he wants.

However, you see, they are all Gallente officers, and for any agent of the State to interfere in Federation matters would be quite wrong, now, wouldn't it? Of course, with all the random third party violence these days, it's not terribly uncommon for valiant officers, Gallente or otherwise, to meet quite unfortunate ends in any number of... well, mishaps. Yes, {[character]player.name}, it's not uncommon at all, is it? So I'm sure things will work themselves out somehow.

Anyhow, your mission. Right. Well, this is quite embarrassing... I've completely forgotten any mission I might have had for you. Come to think of it, I've forgotten everything I was just talking about. Goodness, I think I better go and lie down for a while.

But... I don't suppose you could look after my datapad here while I rest? It's quite important, you see, for it has the current coordinates of one of those promising Federation individuals, one of the ones we just discussed. And I wouldn't want that to fall into the wrong hands, now, would I?

And you... you look like you could use a break, too. Maybe a leisurely cruise out into space somewhere nearby, a chance to relax and, oh, I don't know, enjoy some scenery? Maybe pay someone a visit? And by the time I wake up, maybe my worries will have taken care of themselves, hmm?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: It's good to see you so well rested, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm afraid I have some bad news: I've lost your datapad, the one with the coordinates on it? Oh, and I fear that a certain Gallente lieutenant may have run into some trouble as well.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Strange, isn't it.... how someone can just completely forget about a conversation? Though some conversations are best left forgotten, right, {[character]player.name}?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Yes, of course, please forgive me. I'll just get some rest now. Do close the door on your way out. <sigh>

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Yes, just get some rest {[character]agentID.name}. Don't you worry, I'll take good care of your friend's problem for you.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: What the hell are you yammering on about?! I 'm going to go wash down a few Starsi and leave you to your rest. You apparently need it.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I just wanted to let you know that I too forgot everything you were talking about. Seems that now we both forgot, hmm? Guess I'll come back for a real mission later.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Oh, you will? That's so very kind of you, {[character]player.name}. Perhaps we can talk again later, after I've had a little nap.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm ready to serve in any way I can.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: I'm afraid that my datapad went missing on your watch, {[character]player.name}. It is an unfortunate thing, very unfortunate indeed. I'm afraid, also, that I'll have to hold you responsible for its contents and any action--or in this case, inaction--they might have inspired.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Is that so? Dear me... that's quite unfortunate. I am terribly sorry to hear it, {[character]player.name}. Here, take this compensation for the concern you must also be feeling; hopefully it will ease your mind somewhat.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: You seem to have forgotten what I was talking about too, {[character]player.name}! Ah well, perhaps it was a conversation best left forgotten.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: You promised to deal with that company I needed removed, remember? Well, now too much time has passed and they've relocated their headquarters after noticing our scouts. You have let me down, {[character]player.name}, and countless other Caldari as well.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
There has been an ongoing situation in the entertainment industry, the gambling sector in particular. We've started to see Gallente companies buying out the smaller ones here and reaping profits from our own citizens. This isn't entirely new, of course — they've been trying to do it for decades — but it's actually seeing widespread success now.

What concerns us is that the Federation is officially starting to play an active role in all of this. They've offered Navy vessels as security for the companies' spacebound offices, many of which are located here in our own regions. Since these security forces come at a greatly subsidized cost, we're starting to see a few troubling things. First off, the companies obviously have more ISK to fund further acquisitions. More important, however, is this slow build-up inside our space of Gallente military units. They may be relatively inexperienced and poorly equipped, for the most part, but it's the quantity that concerns us, not the quality.

Make no mistake, {[character]player.name}: This is in all likelihood just their first step. Soon the Federation will forge these various companies into a more unified and organized conglomerate, and then we'll see them pushing to allow larger military escorts with better equipment. Their intentions are nothing short of an economic war with us over one of our key industries, followed by a direct assault in our own backyard once we're sufficiently weakened.

So, we're getting loyal pod pilots like you together and sending them off to as many of these "company sites" as we can find. They were supposed to have registered their offices with our officials, but a combination of lazy State bureaucrats and Gallente scheming means there are currently numerous sites out there that we don't have exact coordinates for. Our mistake in part, yes, but we're fixing it now. It's easy enough to disclaim any official involvement in this little removal operation too, since we have your kind doing the work for us.

Anyway, a local recon force recently found such a Gallente Navy headquarters nearby in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Are you ready to act?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: My work is done. You won't be seeing any new acquisition bids from that company.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You disappoint me, {[character]player.name}. Next time you take up a mission, understand that we will expect you to see it through — no matter the cost.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: The State does not ask much of its people. Your lack of loyalty will not be tolerated for very long around these parts, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I can't believe this is allowed to happen! Give me the coordinates. I'll show them the fast route back to Gallente space: via clone replacement.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Gallente Navy ships are not often allowed inside State borders – at least not officially. Conditions determined in the Iyen-Oursta Treaty at the end of the war place strict conditions on the manner in which each nation's fleets enter the other's sovereign space.

One of the current laws allows such deployments, though, if they are hired by a third party as part of usual trade business. Additionally, they must meet stringent size and composition requirements that greatly limit any damage they could potentially cause. Since official search and rescue missions are, by treaty, conducted exclusively by the nation that owns the space, further "hostile" forces cannot legally be sent to recover hired navy forces that go missing.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't think I care enough about your economic concerns to risk my ship over it.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: You know, upon reflection, I'm less sure about this mission now. They're not breaking any laws, so if you want them gone you'll have to find someone else.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent, I'm sure you will, {[character]player.name}. I'm sending the location now.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: How can I help?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There has been an ongoing situation in the entertainment industry, the gambling sector in particular. We've started to see Gallente companies buying out the smaller ones here and reaping profits from our own citizens. Worse, they've offered Navy vessels as security for these companies' spacebound offices, many of which are located here in our own regions.

Make no mistake, {[character]player.name}: This is in all likelihood just their first step. Their intentions are nothing short of an economic war with us over one of our key industries, followed by a direct assault in our own backyard once we're sufficiently weakened.

So, we're getting loyal pod pilots like you together and sending them off to as many of these "company sites" as we can find. A local recon force recently found such a Gallente Navy headquarters nearby in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Get out there and deal with them. This is a standard office complex; an outer layer of security with the offices behind them. Take out all of the guards, then go for their headquarters.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You did? Excellent work, {[character]player.name}. On behalf of the countless Caldari whose jobs you have saved, I thank you.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: Too slow

messages.mission.briefing.text:
One of our people has betrayed us and is planning to defect to the Gallente. This particular traitor is fairly high-profile, you see, which makes it difficult for us to act more openly. I need this situation sorted. We have to send a message that any treacherous behavior against the State will have truly dire consequences.

We have been able to locate the traitor's temporary living quarters, which are still in State space and therefore under our jurisdiction. Can you head over there and deal with this, {[character]player.name}? I don't want this fool making it to Gallente space alive. Oh, and bring what's left of him back to me, just for certainty's sake.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We have a serious matter to deal with, {[character]player.name}. Very serious. One of our people has betrayed us and is planning to defect to the Gallente.

It's not as if he knows anything particularly important. Nor does he pose much of a threat. It's the principle of the thing. And the example this sets for others. This particular traitor is fairly high-profile, you see, which makes it difficult for us to act more openly. We've already lost enough people to the Guristas and the Legion, and if we start losing people to the Federation, who knows where it will end.

I need this situation sorted. We have to send a message that any treacherous behavior against the State has consequences. We have been able to locate the traitor's temporary living quarters, which are still in State space and therefore under our jurisdiction. We have a small window of opportunity to act before he leaves for the Federation. Can you head over there and deal with this, {[character]player.name}? I don't want this fool making it to Gallente space alive.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: It's done: Add one more traitor to the body count... and some ISK to my account, please.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Let him?! And let the Federation propaganda machine turn him against us entirely? A very foolish stance, {[character]player.name}. Your failure to act will only encourage more problems of this kind.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Excuse me? You want to encourage this behavior?! Your lack of loyalty is disconcerting, {[character]player.name}. Not to mention the lack of foresight....

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Yes, it's a distressing trend, I agree. I'll see to it he never makes it to Federation space.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Over the years, the Caldari have seen various citizens desert their posts in search of better futures elsewhere. The Guristas have always recruited disgruntled ex-State pilots into their ranks, while Mordu's Legion has taken in those who were unhappy with their place in the State, but who remained patriotic or were otherwise obligated to maintain good relations.

Recently, however, there has been an increase in defections to various Gallente corporations, usually in the research and security sectors, and even to the Federation Navy. While such a thing was virtually unheard of in the past, the Federation is increasingly becoming the home to a certain class of Caldari: those skilled pilots and technicians who have come to disagree violently with the State, but who, for various reasons, do not want to enter the seedy underworld of galactic piracy. Such people have found the Federation most sympathetic and welcoming.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: What a pointless job! I want to make a difference, maybe get rich along the way... not chase down people who just happen to like Intaki wine. Get back to me with some real work, ok?

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: You know what? I've changed my mind. If this guy wants to run to Gallente so bad, let him.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good to hear. One less leech, we can do without.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I might be. What did you have in mind?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: You have failed us

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Ha! Impressive work, {[character]player.name}. I heard you made a real mess of those traitors. Here is your reward — take it with my thanks.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: Too long

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The Gallente have somehow discovered one of our secret cloning facilities, and I'm told their orders to attack it have come from the most senior of Federation military officials.

I can't stress enough the importance of this mission. If those clone bays go down, we'll have a huge problem on our hands. I don't have the clearance to know exactly whose clones are being stored where, nor if they are the only copies. All I know is that they are holding important people, very important.

Fly over there immediately, and destroy any and all hostiles you see. Once the facility is secure, we can send in the relocation fleet and move it all safely away. You must move quickly, though! This initial force is undoubtedly just the scouting party since they're not attacking the facility yet. We need them cleared out before we have a fleet of Navy Moros besieging the facility.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
It's those damn Gallente, what else!? They're not even trying to maintain the appearance of peace between us anymore! I'm deadly serious, {[character]player.name}. If this isn't a direct act to provoke all-out war, then I don't know what is. We are dealing with a blatant assault on one of our most important facilities, right within our own borders!

Alright, here's the deal: They've somehow discovered one of our secret cloning facilities, and I'm told their orders to attack it have come from the most senior of Federation military officials.

I can't stress enough the importance of this mission. If those clone bays go down, we'll have a huge problem on our hands. Hell, for all we know this could be only the first step before key individuals are targeted, without clones to save them. I don't have the clearance to know exactly whose clones are being stored where, nor if they are the only copies. All I know is that they are holding important people, very important.

You need to fly over there immediately, and destroy any and all hostiles you see. Once the facility is secure, we can send in the relocation fleet and move it all safely away. You must move quickly, though! This initial force is undoubtedly just the scouting party since they're not attacking the facility yet. We need them cleared out before we have a fleet of Navy Moros besieging the facility.

If we can't trust you with this, {[character]player.name}, then I don't know who we can trust anymore.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I told you I had it covered. You can send your fleet in now.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Well… then why did you accept it in the first place?! Damned podders. Where is your loyalty, your commitment!? Get out of here.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Suicide missions!? You have a clone, do you not, {[character]player.name}?! Unlike the many important Caldari whose clones are in peril…! A true Caldari would give anything to serve the State in such an important matter. Clearly you are no such thing.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Okay, relax. I've got this one in the bag. That's why you asked me, remember? I'll get my people together and we'll have a barbecue, Caldari-style.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Following the widespread release of cloning technology, as it became both financially viable and CONCORD-sanctioned, Zainou Biotech enjoyed a period of unprecedented profits. Securing almost one third of the market share in clone sales, the corporation was set to become one of the most important Caldari corporations in the cluster, which would only have added further influence to its parent company, Ishukone.

In those days, Zainou handled all cloning, though, then as today, only the fabulously wealthy could afford the technology. However, since the event known as the "Insorum Imbroglio," when Zainou lost the trust of the other State corporations, the CEP has mandated that the highest levels of office and those of great value to the State would have their clones stored in other facilities.

Little is known about these cloning centers. Details such as their number, location, staff, administrative structure, and resources all remain closely guarded secrets.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Wait… you're actually serious about asking me to do all this? I'm not standing between a Gallente fleet and a target like that! Find someone else for your suicide missions!

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: It's a hopeless situation, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm afraid you're going to have to find another solution. I can't involve myself any further in this; I just don't have the resources to deliver the results.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Ha! Yes… yes indeed. You're a source of inspiration for us all, I assure you. I'll have the transport fleet on standby; report back to me immediately after the area is secure.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Born ready, {[character]agentID.name}. But, uh, what the hell is going on? You look about ready to slit someone's throat.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Because of your inaction, thousands of Caldari lives were lost retaking the cloning facility. I can barely describe the level of profound disappointment I have in you, {[character]player.name}. Do not offer your services in the future unless you truly intend to provide them.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You truly are an asset to the State, {[character]player.name}. I honestly don't know what we would have done without your help. Be proud of the work you have done today.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
It should not take anywhere near this long to decide on a mission of such importance. I cannot wait for you any longer; I've arranged for a more reliable party to secure the facility.

I suggest you fix your attitude.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's any number of memorial sites from the Great War littered around Gallente space. We've always honored the wishes of honest Caldari pilgrims wanting to visit these memorials; we even let them keep a small number of maintenance staff around on the bigger sites.

It seems our trust was misplaced, however. I've recently received reports of their using their memorials as staging grounds for production facilities inside our own space. Those profit-minded slime are seeking to benefit financially from these facilities, without paying taxes… in fact, with nooversight whatsoever.

We've asked them to withdraw and to take down their marketing facilities, but they're acting outraged that we'd even suggest it. Obviously it's a sensitive issue, but even the President has been vocal about the Caldari exploiting such sensitivity over the past war for commercial profit.

Problem is, our requests are nothing but posturing without an independent like you to back them up: We can't send in any official forces to remove them. A capsuleer like yourself, though… that gives us some plausible deniability.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
There's any number of memorial sites from the Great War between us and the Caldari littered around our space. We've always honored the wishes of honest Caldari pilgrims wanting to visit these memorials; we even let them keep a small number of maintenance staff around on the bigger sites.

It seems our trust in them was misplaced, however. I've recently received reports of their using their memorials, of all places, as staging grounds for production facilities inside our own space. Those profit-minded slime are seeking to benefit financially from these facilities, all without paying taxes… in fact, without any oversight whatsoever.

We've asked them to withdraw all staff and take down their marketing facilities, but they're acting outraged that we'd even suggest it. Obviously it's a sensitive issue, but even the President has been vocal about the Caldari exploiting such sensitivity over the past war for commercial profit.

Problem is, our requests are nothing but posturing without an independent like you to back them up: We can't send in any official forces to remove them. A capsuleer like yourself, though… that gives us some plausible deniability.

Can we trust you with this matter, {[character]player.name}?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The area has been cleared of foreign personnel and structures. They defended it surprisingly well, so I think it's safe to say we haven't seen the end of this matter.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: They should do both, {[character]player.name}! We first have to remove them; then and only then will we have proof of what they were up to. I now regret my faith in you; you are capable, no doubt, but short-sighted.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I admire your humanity. This is, however, exactly what they're expecting us to do. They'll just withdraw before the media storm hits and we'll still look like brutal imperialists.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Of course. If the Caldari are going to exploit such sacred places for profit, then I'll be the first one to get in their way.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: That's pretty sickening, I agree, but I don't think we should remove them. Just expose what they're up to and the situation will resolve itself, I'm sure.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've changed my mind about this one, sorry. If they want to make a profit out of their own memorials, then they can answer to their own conscience, not to our guns.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I thought you would agree with me on this. I'm uploading you the location of the memorial site now. Just be prepared for a fight: They won't take kindly to being forcibly removed.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You do? Alright, then, let's hear it.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Did you forget what you promised me, {[character]player.name}? I asked you to clear that memorial site of Caldari presence, and still no word back from you. I'm tired of waiting; I'm going to hand the job over to someone more reliable and deserving.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Disgusting, isn't it? I can only wonder about a nation that cares only for material gain. No doubt it won't be the last time you have to do this sort of thing for us… but at least we have reliable people like you to count on.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
I'm fed up with your indecision, {[character]player.name}. If you weren't interested in clearing the Caldari from the memorial site, you might have just said so. You could have saved me a great deal of time, but instead you've decided to waste it instead.

I suggest you mend your ways — that attitude won't get you far in the Federation.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I have a friend in a very difficult situation. He's due for a promotion, you see. More accurately, he would be if there weren't a few other promising individuals ahead of him in line. Such promising individuals, indeed, that I am sure their superiors would miss them dearly if anything were to happen to them.

However, you see, they are all Gallente officers, and for any agent of the State to interfere in Federation matters would be quite wrong, now, wouldn't it? Of course, it's not terribly uncommon for valiant officers, Gallente or otherwise, to meet quite unfortunate ends in any number of... well, mishaps. Yes, {[character]player.name}, it's not uncommon at all, is it? So I'm sure things will work themselves out somehow.

Anyhow, your mission. Well, this is quite embarrassing... I've completely forgotten any mission I might have had for you. Come to think of it, I've forgotten everything I was just talking about. Goodness, I think I'd better go lie down for a while.

But... I don't suppose you could look after my datapad here while I rest? It's quite important, you see, for it has the current coordinates of one of those promising Federation individuals, one of the ones we just discussed. And I wouldn't want that to fall into the wrong hands, now, would I?

And you... you look like you could use a break, too. Maybe a leisurely cruise out into space somewhere nearby, a chance to relax and, oh, I don't know, enjoy some scenery? Maybe pay someone a visit? And by the time I wake up, maybe my worries will have taken care of themselves, hmm?

Your agent's datapad has given you the coordinates to one of the competitors of your agent's "friend" in the Gallente Navy. Your "mission" once you arrive there should be abundantly clear.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
The corporations of the State have many friends, as you know... many friends in many interesting and useful places. Why is this relevant, you ask? Well, it's not at all… it was merely an idle thought I had today that I wanted to impart upon you.

But actually, now I come to think about the topic of friends… I am reminded of a particular friend of mine in a very difficult situation. He's due for a promotion, you see. More accurately, he would be if there weren't a few other promising individuals ahead of him in line. Such promising individuals, indeed, that I am sure their superiors would miss them dearly if anything were to happen to them. But it would be very, er, helpful... for me — for us — if this friend of ours were to get what he wants.

However, you see, they are all Gallente officers, and for any agent of the State to interfere in Federation matters would be quite wrong, now, wouldn't it? Of course, with all the random third party violence these days, it's not terribly uncommon for valiant officers, Gallente or otherwise, to meet quite unfortunate ends in any number of... well, mishaps. Yes, {[character]player.name}, it's not uncommon at all, is it? So I'm sure things will work themselves out somehow.

Anyhow, your mission. Right. Well, this is quite embarrassing... I've completely forgotten any mission I might have had for you. Come to think of it, I've forgotten everything I was just talking about. Goodness, I think I better go and lie down for a while.

But... I don't suppose you could look after my datapad here while I rest? It's quite important, you see, for it has the current coordinates of one of those promising Federation individuals, one of the ones we just discussed. And I wouldn't want that to fall into the wrong hands, now, would I?

And you... you look like you could use a break, too. Maybe a leisurely cruise out into space somewhere nearby, a chance to relax and, oh, I don't know, enjoy some scenery? Maybe pay someone a visit? And by the time I wake up, maybe my worries will have taken care of themselves, hmm?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: It's good to see you so well rested, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm afraid I have some bad news: I've lost your datapad, the one with the coordinates on it? Oh, and I fear that a certain Gallente captain may have run into some trouble as well.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Strange, isn't it.... how someone can just completely forget about a conversation? Though some conversations are best left forgotten, right, {[character]player.name}?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Yes, of course, please forgive me. I'll just get some rest now. Do close the door on your way out. <sigh>

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Yes, just get some rest {[character]agentID.name}. Don't you worry, I'll take good care of your friend's problem for you.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: What the hell are you yammering on about?! I 'm going to go wash down a few Starsi and leave you to your rest. You apparently need it.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I just wanted to let you know that I too forgot everything you were talking about. Seems that now we both forgot, hmm? Guess I'll come back for a real mission later.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Oh, you will? That's so very kind of you, {[character]player.name}. Perhaps we can talk again later, after I've had a little nap.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm ready to serve in any way I can.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: I'm afraid that my datapad went missing on your watch, {[character]player.name}. It is an unfortunate thing, very unfortunate indeed. I'm afraid, also, that I'll have to hold you responsible for its contents and any action--or in this case, inaction--they might have inspired.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Is that so? Dear me... that's quite unfortunate. I am terribly sorry to hear it, {[character]player.name}. Here, take this compensation for the concern you must also be feeling; hopefully it will ease your mind somewhat.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: You seem to have forgotten what I was talking about too, {[character]player.name}! Ah well, perhaps it was a conversation best left forgotten.
