messages.mission.briefing.text:
An Amarrian Holder we've suspected for some time of black market slave trading has overstepped his bounds and nabbed a few Gallente citizens for his slave pens. You must stop him. He thinks he's getting away unnoticed, but I want you to prove him wrong.

Destroy this scumbag's ship and bring those slaves back to me, {[character]player.name}. We'll make sure they are returned to their homes. After they pay back their transport fees, that is.

You will need a well-armed frigate to accomplish this mission. The slave ship is probably armed, and might have escorts as well.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Alright, then. An Amarrian Holder we've suspected for some time of black market slave trading has overstepped his bounds and nabbed a few loyal Gallente citizens for his slave pens. You must stop him. He thinks he's getting away unnoticed, but I want you to prove him wrong.

Destroy this scumbag's ship and bring those slaves back to me, {[character]player.name}. We'll make sure they are returned to their homes. After they pay back their transport fees, that is.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Alright, I'm back. One less slaver to worry about, assuming he didn't have a clone, and a bunch of Gallenteans happy to be home.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll bring back those citizens, don't you worry.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Amarrian society, a religious oligarchy, relies on slaves to do nearly all of its manual labor and servant work. Of course, Gallenteans despise this practice. Honest workers should be given an honest wage, not kept in bondage.

Amarr's slaves are often taken wherever they can be found. Citizens of the Gallente Federation, as any other nation, sometimes find themselves locked in Amarrian slave collars. Most of the time, there is little to be done about it, especially if the slaves were kidnapped in low-security or otherwise lightly policed areas of space.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good, good. I like your spirit. That's why I asked you to do this job.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You better believe I would!

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent. I'm sure those poor, unwashed people would shower you with gratitude. But first, let's see that they have showers of their own, eh?

localizedName.text: A Railgun Charge Is Worth a Thousand Words

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Pisharpar Corilian is one of the most renowned Amarrian poets of all time. He is also a spy. He has been on a "book tour" of Gallente space for several months now, and our suspicions were confirmed when we tracked a coded transmission coming from his pleasure yacht. We believe he has had secret data chips implanted within his massive rolls of flesh, where he can hide all sorts of sensitive information.

We cannot tolerate this blatant abuse of the arts! We want him terminated immediately… but it must look like piracy. That's where you come in. He is currently traveling to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Warp in, blast him and his entourage to smithereens, and warp out. Simple.

Now, it's likely that a man this respected in Amarrian society has a clone, but at least we'll have destroyed whatever information he's gathered into his data-ridden body. Take care of him, and you'll be doing us all a great favor.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
This, {[character]player.name}: All the great nations in the galaxy have long allowed each other to travel freely in pursuit of commerce, but I've just heard a story that makes me think this time of freedom is near its end.

Pisharpar Corilian is one of Amarr's most renowned poets of all time. He is gifted, but a typical example of a poet. He's effete, arrogant, and overly sensitive — always with his head in the clouds and his feet floating half a meter off the floor. In Corilian's case, this is literal: So obese that his legs can no longer support his weight, he uses a hoverchair to get around.

He is also a spy. He has been on a "book tour" of Gallente space for several months now, and our suspicions were confirmed when we tracked a coded transmission coming from his pleasure yacht. We believe he has had secret data chips implanted within his massive rolls of flesh, where he can hide all sorts of sensitive information.

We cannot tolerate this blatant abuse of the arts! We want him terminated immediately… but it must look like piracy. That's where you come in. He is currently traveling to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Warp in, blast him and his entourage to smithereens, and warp out. Simple.

Now, it's likely that a man this respected in Amarrian society has a clone, but at least we'll have destroyed whatever information he's gathered into his data-ridden body. Take care of him, and you'll be doing us all a great favor — both politically and artistically... (If you've never read his work, you'll have to take my word for it.)

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Chalk up one large, whiny poet. Clone or no, that was a surprising pleasure, I must admit.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You can't handle one pitiful, overweight poet? What kind of capsuleer are you?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Wow, I would never have thought…. Well, I hope I can find someone else to handle this on such short notice.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Very well. It ain't over till... well, er, till the fat man is dead.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: But I myself am a great patron of the arts! I love his work!! I can't kill him!

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Find somebody else to do this. I have better things to do than hunt down some stupid poet, even if he is a spy.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Indeed. Good luck out there.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Uh, okay. Fair enough. Care to explain what's on your mind, though?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Nice work. When news gets out, of course, it will be a "terrible act of piracy"… but in the meantime I think we can drink a toast to that whining bastard's bloated, frozen corpse.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
An informant within the Amarrian Empire has given us a break in our long quest to find the cure for the slave drug, Vitoc. A sample of their most recent version of the drug has been ... diverted to be transported on an industrial ship passing near Gallente space. If we move quickly, we can intercept the industrial ship, steal its top secret cargo, and it will all be blamed on pirates.

Destroy the industrial ship and bring the Vitoc to me.

Amarrian convoys are well guarded when they pass near Gallente space. Be prepared for a fight.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
An informant within the Empire has given us a break in our long quest to find a counter for the slavers' drug, Vitoc. A sample of their most recent version of the drug has been… diverted, to be transported on an industrial ship passing through Gallente space. If we move quickly, we can intercept the ship and steal its cargo, and — the best part? — it will all be blamed on pirates.

Destroy the industrial ship and bring the Vitoc to me. Can you do it?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Alright – those Amarr creeps never knew what hit them, and I've got the Vitoc samples right here.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: This was a golden opportunity to strike a serious blow against Amarr slavery! Have you no guts at all?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I see. Showing your true colors, eh? Well, I just hope I can find a pilot with a sense of moral propriety for this job.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm the capsuleer for this job. Just tell me where to find that ship.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The toxic chemical known as Vitoc is the preferred method Amarrians use to control their slaves. The drug is injected into the slaves, and the slaves must work to retrieve a periodic dose of antidote to the poison. Gallente scientists, among others, have been chasing the formula for Vitoc for years, but without success. The drug behaves in many ways like a virus.

If one could find the cure, the entire Amarrian economy might be crippled… assuming that cure could somehow be supplied to a sufficient number of their slaves.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't care all that much about any Amarrian slaves. I mean, sure, slavery's bad… but risk my ship over it? No, thanks.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I just don't have time for this Vitoc mission. You'll have to find someone else.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I'm uploading you the coordinates as we speak. Your target will not be in this area for long, though, so don't dally.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Wow, great news! How can I help?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent work. I'm glad we can depend on you. Our scientists will want to see this stuff as soon as possible.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We have a research scientist currently in a small, secret outpost near here; he's originally Caldari, but he recognized the error of his upbringing and came over to our side after the war. More importantly, though, he's on the verge of a breakthrough in a high-priority weapons technology project. And likely as a direct result of that research, we think someone's trying to kill him. He has requested secure transport out of there, and we can't risk losing him.

Head over to the location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and bring him back here to me, will you? This mission requires the utmost secrecy, so don't tell anyone where you're going or say anything about your passenger. Got it? He's an important man, and there will be a decent bonus if you get him here discreetly and quickly.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We have a research scientist currently in a small, secret outpost near here; he's originally Caldari, but he recognized the error of his upbringing and came over to our side after the war. More importantly, though, he's on the verge of a breakthrough in a high-priority weapons technology project. And likely as a direct result of that research, we think someone's trying to kill him. He has requested secure transport out of there, and we can't risk losing him.

Head over to the location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and bring him back here to me, will you? This mission requires the utmost secrecy, so don't tell anyone where you're going or say anything about your passenger. Got it? He's an important man, and there will be a decent bonus if you get him here discreetly and quickly.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Looks like your scientist has had, er, a… bit of a setback. Too bad about that.  Hope he had a good clone ready.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You can't be serious…!? Such a lack of initiative looks quite bad, my friend. Quite bad indeed.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Oh, I see. Matters of national importance are too dreary for you, eh? I see it all too clearly…

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm on my way.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Sometimes a mission might not turn out the way you anticipated. You might have incomplete information from your agent, and conditions can change during the mission. Such changes are generally communicated to you directly, either through a direct pop-up window when using an acceleration gate or by means of a text message appearing in your local chat channel.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Let him find his own ride. My time is too valuable to spend it ferrying around some egghead.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: You know, on second thought, let this lapdog scientist of yours find his own ride.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Splendid. Don't waste a second.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Okay, sounds good. What is it?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Well done. You're a resourceful capsuleer. And yes, never fear — we take care of our own.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
{[character]player.name},

Your lack of initiative has allowed that insane Amarrian terrorist to detonate a bomb on the Crystal Boulevard! Where the hell were you?! Thousands are dead, and the repair costs will be astronomical. But you capsuleers never seem to think in such terms. Sickening, really.

I pray, for all our sakes, that you will learn to let your conscience guide you in the future.

{[character]agentID.name}

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We have received word from an informant that an Amarrian terrorist, some religious zealot, is planning to plant a nuclear bomb somewhere on the Crystal Boulevard. Even though the structures of the crystal buildings are hardened against attack, a blast like that would kill thousands, not to mention shutting down the Boulevard — which, I needn't stress, would cause untold losses in profits.

Fortunately, we've just gotten intelligence regarding the lunatic's current whereabouts. Head out there, will you? Stop this madman from executing his fanatic scheme.

Keep in mind though, {[character]player.name}, you must exercise a little stealth in approach. You will need to fly something smaller than a Battleship. Beyond that one restriction, I don't really care what you use. I just don't want you broadcasting your intentions before you even arrive on scene.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The terrorist is now a grease smear on his battlecruiser's smoking wreck.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You would allow a madman to harm our beloved monument? What kind of patriot are you? Gods, I hope I can find someone else to handle this on such short notice.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: This madman will never plant his bomb. Or see another sunrise, for that matter.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The Crystal Boulevard is indeed one of the great monuments of the Gallente Federation. It is perhaps the most stunning sight in the galaxy, a sea of gleaming crystal spires and sparkling lights, teeming with inhabitants and tourists. As such, it is a symbol of pride for the Gallente, a symbol of wealth, a symbol of freedom.

That makes it a wonderful target for enemies of the Federation as well.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: What do I care about the Crystal Boulevard? I never shop there.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: That's precisely what I wanted to hear. I'm glad we understand one another. Don't waste any time.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Okay, I'm officially intrigued. What's up?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We have received word from an informant that an Amarrian terrorist, some religious zealot, is planning to plant a nuclear bomb somewhere on the Crystal Boulevard. Even though the structures of the crystal buildings are hardened against attack, a blast like that would kill thousands, not to mention shutting down the Boulevard — which, I needn't stress, would cause untold losses in profits.

Fortunately, we've just gotten intelligence regarding the lunatic's current whereabouts. Head out to these coordinates in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and stop this madman from executing his scheme.

Keep in mind though, {[character]player.name}, you must exercise a little stealth in approach. You will need to fly something smaller than a Battleship. Beyond that one restriction, I don't really care what you use. I just don't want you broadcasting your intentions before you even arrive on scene.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Ha! Nice work, {[character]player.name}. Enjoy your reward — you've earned it.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
There's been an increase in Caldari activity in surrounding systems. We think those self-righteous bastards might be up to something. Of course, that's nothing new.

We've placed passive reconnaissance units in several nearby locations, but we don't want any direct transmissions from them for fear of attracting Caldari attention. So we've decided to dispatch "unofficial" vessels like yours to pick up the data chips from their base and bring them back here. The Caldari are less likely to suspect--or at least less likely to interfere with--a capsuleer, so they should leave you alone.

If you do get jumped, however, remember that the recon unit is the top priority. Get it out of there if you can. Do it fast and there'll be a substantial bonus.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here are the data chips from your recon base, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I can't say I'm too surprised, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll leave right away.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sorry. I don't want to get involved.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I knew you were good for it, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Yeah, I'm interested in helping out.

messages.mission.briefing.text:

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good job, capsuleer. You show some promise, I must admit.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've found what appears to be a large collection of acceleration gates surrounded by Minmatar ships. These gates have apparently been modified to act as "simple" mass drivers. Theoretically, they could propel asteroids or similar celestial bodies at Amarrian targets. The combination of mass and velocity produced by such a gate could easily destroy a station; I don't even want to think what the results would be for a planetary impact.

We need you to stop the Minmatar before they get a chance to use these devices. Destroy any enemy ships you find. But do not destroy the gates: We do not know how dangerous that would be… and in any case, our scientists want to take a closer look.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We just received intel from one of our patrols. They were following up reports of strange gravimetric fluctuations in a small region of space. What they found—

It appears to be a large collection of acceleration gates. And they're surrounded by Minmatar ships. The gates have apparently been modified to act as "simple" mass drivers. If they actually work, they could propel asteroids at Amarrian targets. The combination of mass and velocity produced by such a gate could easily destroy a station. I don't even want to think what the results would be for a planetary impact.

We need you to stop the Minmatar before they get a chance to use these devices. Destroy any enemy ships you find. But do not destroy the gates. We do not know how dangerous that would be… and in any case, our scientists want to take a closer look.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The system is safe.  The Minmatar have been destroyed.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Disappointing, to say the least.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: We'll see how sorry you are when the Minmatar start throwing asteroids through your house.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: The Minmatar will be driven from the system.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Acceleration gates are one of the main means of intrastellar travel. They can propel space craft great distances without the need for a large gravitational body as an end point.  If the enemy has found a way to quickly and properly configure an acceleration gate to be used as a weapon, the consequences could be dire indeed.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm sorry, but I'm not going to go against the Minmatar over some supposed super-weapon that probably won't work anyway.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm sorry, but I can't clear the Minmatar from the acceleration gates. Don't ask me why. I just can't.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Remember, only destroy the enemy ships. The gates are not to be harmed.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: What is it?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: We've detected several large explosions coming from the enemy mass driver cluster. Apparently their experiment failed. We simply lucked out on this. Had you responded faster, though, we might have secured the technology and developed it properly for ourselves.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work. Our agents are over there now, dismantling the gates for study. This technology could go a long way to helping us destroy the Minmatar threat once and for all.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
One of our intelligence technicians has gone rogue. He isn't a very high-level operator, but he has access to some sensitive passwords, code keys, and patrol routes. We think he was bought off by the Caldari and is headed out of system.

We've located him in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and we need someone to stop him and grab his ship's log if possible. It may contain information about his destination and, more importantly, about who recruited him. It's an important mission. Are you game?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've eliminated the traitor and obtained his log book.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll find him!

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Good job! We'll analyze the data right away. Come back in a few hours and we may have some more work for you.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Now get to it, before that bastard gets away.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: How can I assist you?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
One of our intelligence technicians has gone rogue. He isn't a very high-level operator, but he has access to some sensitive passwords, code keys, and patrol routes. We think he was bought off by the Caldari and is headed out of system.

We've located him in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and we need someone to stop him and grab his ship's log if possible. It may contain information about his destination and, more importantly, about who recruited him. It's an important mission.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We've analyzed the data you brought back from the traitor's ship. He was on his way to meet up with his contact, some Caldari spy, in the asteroid fields of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. With luck, the contact is still out there waiting for the traitor's arrival.

Can you head on out to that system and take him down? His ship is likely to be pretty powerful, but if you can capture him alive we'll provide you with a substantial bounty.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The contact has been dealt with, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll get him and bring him back.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Not really interested. Seems like this should be something for the Navy, anyway, no?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Move quickly, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'm always ready to help. What's going on?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Turns out the traitor was on his way to meet up with his contact, a Caldari spy, in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. With luck, the contact is still out there waiting for the traitor's arrival.

Head out there and take him down.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent job! You've helped deal a major blow to the Caldari spy network.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
There's been an outbreak of commerce raiding in this sector. We strongly suspect the Caldari are behind it, either directly or through something like Mordu's Legion. Whoever it is, they've hit a convoy in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but it seems there was too much cargo for them to loot immediately. We suspect that they'll be returning in a few hours with a transport and some escorts.

We want to strike back, of course, but also to learn something about who these raiders are and whether the Caldari are really behind the attacks. Take out the transport and escorts when they arrive in-system, and return to us with any logs or transponders you're able to recover.

Take these guys down and we'll make it worth your time. You might even get a piece of the action if we find out who's behind the raids. The lost cargo is also yours if you want it. Insurance has already covered those losses, so consider that a little extra bonus for yourself.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've defeated the raiders and found the information you requested.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll do it. Send me the coordinates.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: You're a hell of a pilot, {[character]player.name}. Come back in a bit and I'll let you know if there's more work for you.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: See you when you return, my friend.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Sounds good, {[character]agentID.name}. What do you need?

messages.mission.briefing.text:

Insurance has already covered those losses, so consider that a little extra bonus for yourself.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We've got some more information from the data you brought back. It seems that these enemies are indeed Mordu's Legion, with their squadron insignia obscured. That means the Caldari are likely behind the raids and we need to send them a message that we know about it.

There's a Caldari supply depot located at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that we want destroyed. We can't offer you much support, but we know you don't really need it. That's why we're sending you in, and not some Navy rookie. We want the Caldari to know that we can cause them grief with only a single ship. It doesn't take us a whole fleet.

So, you want to go in? I won't lie, it's risky--the depot is likely to be guarded, and they may send reinforcements once the action begins.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: That was fun.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Let me at 'em!

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Alright, then, capsuleer, go take some Caldari names.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Nothing I'd enjoy more…

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's a Caldari supply depot located at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that we want destroyed. We can't offer you much support, but we know you don't really need it. That's why we're sending you in, and not some Navy rookie. We want the Caldari to know that we can cause them grief with only a single ship. It doesn't take us a whole fleet.

I won't lie, it's risky.The depot is likely to be guarded, and they may send reinforcements once the action begins.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great work! I suspect we won't be seeing anymore Caldari raiders in this sector for a while.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
An Amarrian slaver has found a way to hack the Egonics signal, at least at short range. Security cameras in a nearby station show hundreds of people--all of them wearing Egonics devices--simply walking into the cargohold of an Amarrian Bestower. It wasn't until after the ship had departed the station and the missing persons reports starting coming in that we realized anything was amiss. Security found that this Amarrian "citizen" had inserted subliminal commands into the Egonics signals at the station.

If you can get all of those citizens back, there's a big reward for you.

There are over 1,000 people missing. You will need a large cargo capacity to carry them all at once, unless you intend to make multiple runs to the deadspace location where the Amarrain ship is located.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
What's wrong? Listen to this. Egonics headsets: They're the fashion, right? All the kids have to have them. But some people, including me, have always been afraid that something like this could happen.

Apparently some Amarrian slaver has found a way to hack the Egonics signal, at least at short range. Security cameras in a nearby station show hundreds of people — all of them wearing Egonics devices — simply walking into the cargohold of an Amarrian Bestower. This strange exodus went unnoticed because, other than their destination, the people seemed to be behaving normally. It wasn't until after the ship had departed the station and the missing persons reports starting coming in that we realized anything was amiss.

Security found that this Amarrian "citizen" had inserted subliminal commands into the Egonics signals at the station. Of course, they thought their network security was iron-clad, but now I can assure you they're rethinking their assumptions. This is a catastrophe of the highest order, {[character]player.name}!

Just imagine what a tragedy this would be if it wasn't Federation policy to put a tracking beacon on every Bestower that docks in our sovereignty!

If you can get all of those Gallente citizens back, there's a big reward for you. And if you can keep the Egonics corporate name out of it, so much the better… If you see any Scope reporters nosing around as you leave, pray, ignore them.

There are over 1,000 people missing. You will need a large cargo capacity to carry them all at once, unless you intend to make multiple runs to the deadspace location where the Amarrain ship is located.

The slaver ship likely has escorts, as well.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: All of the kidnapped citizens are safe at home now. They seem a bit groggy, but otherwise none the worse for wear.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You're just going to let that slaver get away with a thousand kids? What kind of person are you? Perhaps you should work out of Amarr space from now on!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Not worth…?! Wha—? I can't believe you can say that! Get out of here, will you? I have to find someone else to save those kids.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I can't believe this! And here I was just going to pick up an Egonics headset for each of my cousin's kids… Okay, don't worry, just get me that ship's coordinates.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Egonics, Inc. is unique in the Gallente music industry. Extremely popular among young citizens of virtually every star nation, Egonics produces the only entertainment headset that transmits music directly into the user's brain. The company's contracted musical artists tailor the music to the individual tastes of every listener.

The technology's growing popularity has caused it spread across the galaxy, except in the Amarr Empire, where possession of Egonics tech is outlawed.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: What do I care about a few numbskull music freaks? Not worth my time.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Forget it. I've changed my mind. Let the Navy deal with this.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You seem upset. What's wrong?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Magnificent, {[character]player.name}. Their families will be so happy to have them back. You've done a great deed today, my friend.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: Amarrian slaver captured

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
A gang of pirates has been terrorizing the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system for some time. And they've been using their base in that system as a launching point to strike out into neighboring systems as well. Of course, pirates are to be expected these days, but these pirates are different. They are well funded, well equipped, and commanded by some canny ship commanders.

A survivor of the pirate raids told us that at least two of the ship captains — including the pirates' leader himself — were once high-ranking officers in the Gallente Navy. In fact, we believe the Gallente government has sanctioned these pirates as privateers. The damage they have already caused to Amarrian interests is incalculable. Go out there and wipe them out. Yes, this one's a “terminate with extreme prejudice.”

The bounty on the pirate commander is sizeable, but you'll need proof of his death to collect it. Bring back his head and you'll be well-rewarded for your efforts.

You're going to face a sizable force of pirates. You'll likely need at least a battlecruiser, and maybe even a few allies.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Mission accomplished. The pirates are dead, and I have the commander's filthy gob in a jar in my cargo.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Don't have the stones? I'm sure there are plenty of ship captains courageous enough to grab this bounty.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Don't have the stones, huh? Well, I'm sure there are plenty of ship captains courageous enough to grab this bounty.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: This Gallente pirate is a dead man.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: You know, this sounds pretty risky. And I just had my ship cleaned and repainted. Nah, I'm gonna pass, thanks.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. But move quickly. These "pirates" could disappear at any time.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Hey, I'm all about dealing with pirates. What's the problem?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
These pirates in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} are well funded, well equipped, and commanded by some canny ship commanders. In fact, we believe the Gallente government has sanctioned these "pirates" as privateers.

Go out there and wipe them out. Yes, this is a “terminate with extreme prejudice” matter. The bounty on the pirate commander is sizeable, but you'll need proof of his death to collect it: Bring back his head and you'll be well-rewarded for your efforts.

You're going to face a sizable force of pirates. You'll likely need at least a battlecruiser, and maybe even a few allies.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thank you for your assistance. You are a courageous pilot, {[character]player.name}. Enjoy your rewards. You've earned them.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: Don't have the stones? Good thing there are plenty of ship captains courageous enough to grab this bounty. Consider yourself un-hired.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
There's been a lot of Amarrian activity along the frontier lately. We think they're preparing for war with the Minmatar, but there's no love lost between them and us, as you know. Or perhaps they want to start a conflict that will involve all four major powers. We can't say.

What we do know is that there is a flotilla of Amarrian ships operating out of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. To avoid the political confrontation, we'd been leaving them alone until now, but they've been snooping where they aren't welcome, and we think they may even be raiding some of our supply convoys. We need you to go take them out--leave as much wreckage as you can so the Empire can't deny it had an illegal military outpost in our space.

Now, we're not sure how many fleet resources they have in the region, so it might be a tough fight. A real tough fight. Are you up for it?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I took out the enemy vessels. Good fight, just like you said.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I guess you can't take the heat. There are others who will.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm sorry to hear that, {[character]player.name}. I'll find someone else, I suppose.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sounds like quite a challenge. Sure, I'll help.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sorry, but I can't do it, {[character]agentID.name}. Pressing business elsewhere.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've changed my mind — these odds are too uncertain. I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good hunting, my friend.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Good day, {[character]agentID.name}. What can you offer me?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's a flotilla of Amarrian ships operating illegally out of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We need you to go take them out. Leave as much wreckage as you can so the Empire can't deny its actions in our space.

Now, we're not sure how many fleet resources they have in the region, so it might be a tough fight. A real tough fight.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent work! That'll put the fear of their bloodthirsty god right into them.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
So glad to hear it. Good, good.

Okay, we believe that the Caldari are helping the Amarrians plan an offensive in this sector; the Caldari are deploying subspace beacons deep in obscure star systems to support it. We're developing a plan to destroy the beacons and strand some of the Caldari flotillas in this sector.

The most powerful of these beacons are located in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system, and since you're the best commander we've got involved, we want you to go there and destroy them quickly. There will be ships guarding the beacons, and they'll no doubt put up a strong resistance.

What do you say? Do you want the mission?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The beacons are all destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}. Along with the Caldari bastards who put them there.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I see. Well, I suppose this is a difficult job I've offered you. Still— Oh, well, I'll find someone…

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I will destroy the beacons, never fear.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: This sounds pretty dangerous, going up against the Caldari. No, I think I'll pass.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Your loyalty and bravery continue to astonish us all.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I think so, yes. Sounds like you need the help.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The Caldari are helping the Amarrians plan an offensive in this sector by deploying subspace beacons deep in obscure star systems. We need to destroy the beacons and strand some of the Caldari in this sector.

The most powerful of these beacons are located in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system; go there and destroy them quickly. There will be ships guarding the beacons, and they'll no doubt put up a very strong resistance.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: That's got them! Well done, {[character]player.name}!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
All hell's broken loose out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The Amarrians have chosen to create an incident that they're hoping will escalate into war.

A group of Ammatar "nationals" in a small outpost out there claim that they were beaten up by our security guards and then arrested on trumped-up charges. The Empire has dispatched a fleet to blockade the outpost "in protest," they say, "on behalf of our friends and allies"; they are demanding that the prisoners be turned over to them.

We're in a no-win situation: If we hold the Nefantar, the Amarr fleet will bombard the station and force a confrontation, but if we turn them over it will be seen as a sign of weakness. We need to raise the blockade, while at the same time avoiding direct official intervention in the situation. That's why we need a capsuleer. We need you.

{[character]player.name}, please — fly to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and take out the fleet that is amassing there. It's a tough job, but from what we've heard you're up to it. What do you say?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The prisoners should be safe to pick up now, {[character]agentID.name}. Oh, by the way, the Imperial Navy is also down a few warships.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You've really let the Republic down, {[character]player.name}. Don't expect to keep up this sort of behavior without some lasting effect.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Damnation, {[character]player.name}! You were our best hope. I just pray I can find someone else.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: It sounds like a very difficult job. Of course I'll do it!

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I like to stay out of political squabbles. Find yourself another capsuleer.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: This mission isn't worth the risk. I'm sorry, but I have to withdraw.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I knew we could count on you, {[character]player.name}. Please hurry.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: An emergency? Sure, how can I help?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
A group of Ammatar "nationals" in a small outpost out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} claim that they were beaten up by our security guards and then arrested on trumped-up charges. The Amarr Empire has dispatched a fleet to blockade the outpost; they are demanding that the prisoners be turned over to them.

We're in a no-win situation: If we hold the Nefantar, the Amarr fleet will bombard the station and force a confrontation, but if we turn them over it will be seen as a sign of weakness. We need to raise the blockade, while at the same time avoiding direct official intervention in the situation.

Fly to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, take out the fleet that is amassing there.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good job! We've scored a major victory here, thanks to you!

messages.mission.briefing.text: The Sansha recently began a campaign of expansion. Our forces have contained them so far, but every day it gets harder. A new Sansha base has recently been discovered on our side of the line. We don't have the men to spare to handle it right now. I need you to take care of it. Destroy the station and any Sansha craft that may be defending it.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Understand that what I'm about to tell you is classified. If word of this got out, there would be a system-wide panic.

The Sansha recently began a campaign of expansion. Our forces have contained them so far, but every day it gets harder. The Sansha do not sleep. They do not flinch. They do not run. They have our guys running triple shifts just to keep up. The cracks in our line are already starting to show.

A new Sansha base has recently been discovered on our side of the line. We don't have the men to spare to handle it right now. I need you to take care of it. Destroy the station and any Sansha craft that may be defending it.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The station has been destroyed.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm not about to force you to go back, but I am disappointed.  We trusted you to do this.  You've made life a lot harder for my boys.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Fair enough. I can't order you.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: That station is as good as dust.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Sansha's Nation was founded more than a century ago. Sansha was a Caldari tycoon who set out to create a utopian state. He started experiments, combining capsule technology with the human mind, creating zombie-like creatures that had the cold, calculating minds of computers, but the ingenuity of humans. When this became public knowledge, Sansha was condemned and his forces were decimated, but remnants still remain.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm not ready for an operation on this scale.  Not against the Nation.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: There were Sansha everywhere.  I'm not going back out there, man.  You can't make me.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Have at them.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I am a dedicated problem solver.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Things are going badly. Because you were slow to act, the Sansha station we found launched a raid against one of our facilities. Now I have to pull people off the line to handle the mess.  Next time, make sure you can do what needs to be done.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thanks to your efforts, we've been able to focus on pushing the Sansha back. We've driven them back to where they started, but the fighting is still hard. You've done well, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: The situation with the Sansha station cannot wait any longer. I need someone who can decide and commit, not lollygag.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Excellent. Now, first off, I must stress that this is all strictly confidential. If any word of this matter were to get out, it could tarnish our appearance in the public eye, not to mention damage Federation morale.

It looks as if one of our public confidence operatives has turned. What's a public confidence operative? A person whose job it is to spread good news and make sure the general public doesn't lose faith in the government. Yes, I guess you could call it "propaganda management"… but hell, what's a government without propaganda?

Anyway, it seems those fascists in the Caldari State have managed to turn the guy, and he's heading for enemy space with a computer full of our public confidence procedures. He's met up with some Caldari warships, and they're escorting him to the frontier. We need to stop them, destroy that ship, and get back the computer with the... public confidence procedures.

Keep it on the sly, {[character]player.name}, and you'll be well rewarded. What do you think?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's that data chip you wanted. And don't worry, there's no one left to talk about this matter.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Your loss, {[character]player.name}. Remember: Keep your mouth shut about this.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Always happy to help, but especially when there's ISK involved.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: You want me to help you lie to the people of our fair and just Federation?! You're crazy.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Alright, get moving, then — that bastard's getting away!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Thanks for your consideration, {[character]agentID.name}. And yes, I believe I am.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
It looks as if one of our public confidence operatives has turned. What's a public confidence operative? A person whose job it is to spread good news and make sure the general public doesn't lose faith in the government. Yes, I guess you could call it "propaganda management"… but hell, what's a government without propaganda?

Anyway, it seems those fascists in the Caldari State have managed to turn the guy, and he's heading for enemy space with a computer full of our public confidence procedures. He's met up with some Caldari warships, and they're escorting him to the frontier.

Stop them, destroy their ships, and bring back the data chip containing the public confidence procedures.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thanks to you, our people will remain happy now!

A new Sansha base has recently been discovered on our side of the line. We don't have the men to spare to handle it right now. I need you to take care of it. Destroy the station and any Sansha craft that may be defending it.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: The situation with the Sansha station cannot wait any longer. I need someone who can decide and commit, not lollygag.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You may already know that Amarr is preparing for war. It seems that they want to take back what they feel was once rightfully theirs and make us all slaves in the process. It will be the Day of Darkness all over again, if they have their way.

But they will not. We Minmatar will not kneel to that sociopathic, god-mongering cult run by feeble cybernetic monstrosities. The Amarrians will either perish or slay us to the last — either way, they will never again make us their slaves.

We've not come to open warfare yet, but the Imperials have been raiding along the frontier, trying to provoke us into a fight. A few hours ago they hit a refugee convoy in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The Amarrians have gone, but we've picked up a distress transmission that claims there are survivors. It could be a trap, or the Amarrians may be planning to return and capture the survivors for sale as slaves in the Empire.

So, we need a good, capable captain who's willing to warp over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and investigate. If there really are any survivors, get them before the Amarrians do; survivors may not last long out there, so you'll need to move quickly.

If it proves an ambush, then take out any Amarrian bastards who show themselves. Will you do it?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The refugees are safe and the Amarrian ships are destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm… shocked. My reports have you a fearless, dedicated veteran. I am supremely disappointed, both in you and in my intelligence.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I will help you to the best of my ability. The Republic!

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I know it's important, but the danger sounds too great. I can't risk my ship over a few civilians.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: On your way, captain. Death to Amarr!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I'll serve the Republic any way I can, {[character]agentID.name}. What is needed of me?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
A few hours ago, an Amarrian strike force hit a refugee convoy in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The Amarrians have gone now, but we've picked up a distress transmission that claims there are survivors. It could be a trap, or the Amarrians may be planning to return and capture the survivors for sale as slaves in the Empire.

Warp over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and investigate. If there really are any survivors, get them before the Amarrians do; you'll need to move quickly. And if it proves an ambush, then take out any Amarrian bastards who show themselves.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thank god! We'll see to the refugees' comfort. Take your reward and my personal gratitude.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A gang of Serpentis cartel thugs is being used by Federation intelligence to slip assets into the State during drugs runs. You are to intercept one of these runs in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system, destroy the Serpentis vessels there, and recover any prisoners you can find. Bring them back to your agent so that they can be remanded to Tribunal custody.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We've recently received intelligence that a deal is going down in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system between a Caldari buyer and a minor, local branch of the Serpentis drug cartel. While this is a bit of a concern in and of itself, the bigger problem is that we believe the cartel is being paid by elements within the Federation intelligence community; their goal, apparently, is to use this particular drug route as a way to insert intelligence assets into the State. That is of considerably greater concern to us.

We would like you to fly to the coordinates of this rendezvous, eliminate the Serpentis vessels there, and recover any prisoners that you can find. We'll turn them over to the Tribunal for further questioning.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The drug runners' ships have been destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}, and I managed to bring back a few of them alive for interrogation.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I thought you had a bit more fortitude. It's people like you that allow the Federation to get away with committing this kind of treachery.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Most disappointing, pilot. How can you sit idly by while the Federation poisons our bodies and our minds? Hopefully someone else will have the courage to stand up to them.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll take care of the problem, {[character]agentID.name}. This intrusion must be stopped.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Some critics might argue that the State has a complicated relationship with organized crime. While the various criminal enterprises in the State (including the Guristas) do cut into the bottom line of the megacorporations, these enterprises are also used by said corporations as a means of arm's-length corporate espionage. Or so the pundits say.

Therefore, these cynical observers aver, while corporate security generally tries to keep a firm hand against the criminal syndicates, their upper management simultaneously ensures that the symbiotic relationship between the corporations and the syndicates is preserved, often to the frustration of the security forces and the Navy.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't think I feel like dealing with this mess right now.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I... I've decided that I don't want to go after these Serpentis guys. You did hear what they did to the last guy who tried, right?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Here's the coordinates for where the deal is going down. Good hunting, kirjuun.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: How can I be of service to {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} and the State, kirjuun?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: You failed to stop the drug deal, and likely Federation penetration of our borders as well. There is little doubt that this will put us at an even greater disadvantage against our enemies than we were already dealing with. While I hope for your sake that I am wrong, I fear that you have cost us more than you can possibly imagine.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work, {[character]player.name}. You've done a great job for the State and this corporation.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: Due to your lack of action, {[character]player.name}, I was forced to find another pilot to carry out this mission. Hopefully, in the future, you will be more punctual, pilot.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You heard me, {[character]player.name}. Animal problems. And stop lookin' at me like I'm crazy or I'll be tempted to do somthin' we'll both regret. Just shut up and listen.

This is what happens: You scour the land, lookin' hard and far and wide and all that. After much of that business, you find yourself a good bunny. Real proper, no poser crap – the real deal. Least that's what you think. You give this bunny everything of yourself. All your knowledge, all your expertise, all your damn money. Hell… all your love, even. I said stop lookin' at me like that!

What was I–? Oh… right.

So, for a while that works well – with a real big emphasis on the "for a while" bit. This little bunny looks after itself proper, looks after you real good in turn too. As it damn well should, little bugger. Then one day, outta the blue, it seems to think it's had enough. Thinks it will just hop on over to the Mordus Legion and work for them instead. After everything you've done for it. "Better money," it says. "Doing what's right," it says. Dumb bunny. Real damn stupid.

You know what you do next, right? Go on, tell me what you do and prove you're not as green as you look.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Hop, hop, bang. "Crap, I'm dead." I think it's payday.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Eh… useless after all. I knew it. I could smell the fear on you, ya damn rookie! Howsabout you forget about that next time, eh? You got a damn pod, what more could ya want?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Wrong answer, Rookie. Howsabout you take that tub of yours and paddle back to State space before you figure out you can't swim with the big fish.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: You take it out back, have one last look at it, then put a bullet in its furry little head.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
A traditional Caldari privateer's song

Oh, poor old man, your bunny will die.
And we say so, and we know so.
Oh, poor old man, your bunny gonna die
Oh, poor old man!

We'll drag it down to the State line,
We'll drop it down inside the border,
We'll drop it off into the void, hey.

We'll drop it off into the void, now,
Sing it down with a long, long roll.
The peggies can have its body,
And the devil can have its soul.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Uhm… what I do is… or what someone needs to do, at least, is stop gobbling the ol' Blue Pill. I think you need to get some rest… and maybe some rehab. Sheesh.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I forgot what I was supposed to do, so I figure I'll just do nothing instead. Seeya.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Huh. That's right. Guess you might be useful after all. Alright, then, my young protégé: Stage two – here's the coordinates. I'm not giving you a damn thing. Go show me you're more than just talk!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Uh… wha-?! Like, vermin in your apartment or something? You know I'm a capsuleer, right?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
This is a pre-recorded message: Why are you lookin' here? You forget somethin'? Are you stupid, 's that it? We're barely done talkin' and it all already slipped outta your head? GO KILL THE DAMN TRAITOR.

Damn rookies.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work, Rookie! Now go and have yourself a party on me. Oh, and remember: this is what happens to bad bunnies. Don't get any funny ideas under those long, furry ears of yours.

messages.mission.briefing.text: The "Brothers of Freedom" have set up an FTL transmitter in the area of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and are broadcasting anti-corporate propaganda into the State, with the help of some Minmatar sympathizers. This situation is completely unacceptable; the transmitter must be destroyed, and we want you take care of it. Eliminate the transmitter and any hostile ships nearby. If the Minmatar Navy interferes, you can take out their vessels as well, but it's not strictly necessary.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
In the last few weeks, we've become aware of an FTL transmitter in the area which has been broadcasting anti-corporate propaganda into the State. Usually, the Federation isn't quite this bold in its slander of our state, so a number of corporate intelligence offices looked into the matter and found to our surprise that this transmitter is actually being run by someone we are all too familiar with: Melarius Torvil and his so-called “Brothers of Freedom.”

Obviously, we cannot allow this situation to continue. Torvil's persistent ability to elude capture by Caldari authorities is frustrating enough, but we cannot simply stand by while he rubs it in our faces. Frankly, the fact that the Republic is allowing this kind of dangerous nonsense makes me thankful our militia capsuleers are giving them a hard time.

Anyway, we would like you to fly to the transmitter in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}: Destroy it and any Minmatar vessels in the area. If the Republic Navy sends any ships to assist, feel free to eliminate them as well, but it isn't necessary; I don't think they'll be willing to stick their necks out over what is a rather diplomatically shady activity anyway.

What do you say? Can you handle this for me?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The transmitter has been destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm just disappointed I didn't catch Torvil there himself.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm not sure you're thinking this through: the Brothers of Freedom are more of a threat than you realize. Perhaps you'll learn before it's too late.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Don't tell me you actually sympathize with these morons? For your sake, I hope you don't.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll hit ‘em hard for you, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Formerly an extremist labor movement in the State, the Brothers of Freedom led a widespread revolt against corporate security forces on a number of Caldari planets a number of years ago -- some time before Tibus Heth's vastly more successful revolt of a similar nature -- after 65,000 protesters were killed by Caldari paramilitary forces while trying to force their way onto a CEP station in the New Caldari system. After months of dogged pursuit by Caldari authorities, the riots were put down and most of the leaders were killed or arrested.

Some of the leadership, including the ringleader Melarius Torvil, did manage to escape the final Caldari Navy operation that crushed the Brothers' movement. Torvil and a small group of associates fled to the Minmatar Republic and applied for asylum from Caldari persecution, which was granted by then-President Midular's Gallente-friendly government.

Today, though they have been largely eliminated as a major force in the State, the Brothers of Freedom continue to spread anti-corporate propaganda and speak out against the CEP's government in the Gallente Federation and the Minmatar Nation, as well as outlying State settlements and facilities.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't think I want to mess with it if it's inside the Republic. I hear they eat their prisoners.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've decided it's not worth risking my hide just to shut up someone who's making fun of you. Do your own dirty work.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. Here are the coordinates for the transmitter; remember, you must destroy it and any vessels that would defend it, but it isn't necessary to engage the Republic Navy ships. Get out if you have to.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Oh? What sort of mission is that?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Because you couldn't take out the Brothers of Freedom transmitter, some soft-headed fools at one of our border mining colonies seem to have taken their “sermons” to heart and, in the wake of Heth's recent successes, have begun a wildcat strike, setting back production and causing a number of injuries and even a few deaths. I hope you realize what your failure here cost us, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work, {[character]player.name}. Perhaps Torvil will restrict himself to overpaid speaking engagements for bleeding-heart, over-privileged Gallente from now on, instead of trying to spit in our faces.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I never heard back from you, {[character]player.name}, so I'm going to assume you don't have the stomach to take care of this Brothers of Freedom tyuui. That's unfortunate, but thankfully there are plenty of other loyal Caldari pilots out there looking for work.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You don't say! Well, yes, in fact, I do have something I could use you for.

You've heard of the "Athran Brotherhood"? No? Well, that's no surprise, really. They're little more than a nuisance, and few in number. But they can be a pain at times. And we're pretty sure there's a chapter of them hereabouts. But we don't know where they're hiding out. That's what I want you to find out for me, actually.

There's a small station built into an old asteroid near here. Used to be a mining outpost till they hollowed the thing out. It's been abandoned for a few years now, but some rumors of activity in that area have been surfacing. I need you to go check those rumors out and let me know what you find.

Seem like something you'd be interested in?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Alright, I went out there, and I definitely picked up some Athran radio transmissions. I also picked up some carbon scoring when they opened fire on me...

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Seems straightforward enough. Are these Athrans hostile?

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Sometimes calling itself "The Scions of Athra," the Athran Brotherhood is a group of Khanid secessionists with headquarters located on the Khanid homeworld of Amarr Prime (called Athra in the Old Khanid tongue). This group tends to rise perhaps every other generation or so, seemingly from its own ashes, making trouble for local government and interstellar trade alike.

Given the many large pirate organizations and other independent "freebooters" of New Eden, not to mention the constant weight of intergalactic politics and the ongoing "Minmatar Problem," Amarr rulers cannot generally spare a large-scale military effort to deal with these relatively minor troublemakers. Perhaps this is the reason the Brotherhood seems never to die, but always reappears just when authorities start to think they've rid themselves of the nuisance.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sounds pretty dull, actually. I think I'll pass.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Yeah, I got your ship's logs once you docked. Stick around and talk to me again in a bit, would you? We need to get to the bottom of this.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: It's possible, but not generally, no. If they do engage, don't feel obliged to mess with them, unless you feel you're in no danger.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Well, thanks. I'm just wondering if you might have some work for a recent graduate. I'm a decent combat pilot.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You've heard of the "Athran Brotherhood"? No? Well, that's no surprise, really. They're little more than a nuisance, and few in number. But they can be a pain at times. That's what I want you to find out for me, actually.

There's a small station built into an old asteroid near here: It used to be a mining outpost till they hollowed the thing out. It's been abandoned for a few years now, but some rumors of activity in that area have been surfacing. And I suspect it may have become the hideout for a chapter of the Athran Brotherhood. I need you to go check those rumors out and let me know what you find.

All you need to do is fly close to the structure and see if you pick up any short-range radio transmissions or see any other signs of activity. Then get back here and let me know what you found.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've given it some more thought, and actually I'm not sure I'm up to tracking down these Athrans for you. Sorry.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes. We put a covert ops ship out there around the same time you left for your last mission, and the pilot corroborated your story. He also reports that the remaining Athrans pulled out as soon as you left. Fortunately, he was able to trail them to another location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

{[character]player.name}, I want you to head out there and find out what's going on. See what these Athrans are up to, and report any suspicious activity back to me. And if they open fire on you again, you're fully authorized to shoot back. Don't take any chances.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I found those Athrans, alright. And they're in league with the Minmatar, it would seem. They made pretty short work of a chapel structure out there.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I had doubts about you all along, to be honest. Just goes to show I'm still a good judge of character.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Suit yourself. I was giving you a chance to be of service to your nation, but if you want to hide behind your degree, well… I can't stop you.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: You bet. I'll be back before you can say, "Hey, where'd you go?"

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Always be ready to warp out if you start taking heavy damage, whether in a mission or in lawless space. Sometimes it's a good idea to have a jump route selected before going into a mission so you can simply click your autopilot to get out quickly; this is a valid approach only with relatively small ships, though. Eventually, once you get into something like a Battleship, aligning to warp can take so long — especially if you begin once you're already taking heavy damage — that your ship might be destroyed by the time you actually start your warp.

Remember too that if you take damage in battle, you can always return to a nearby station for repairs; also be sure to replenish your ammunition while you're there if you're running low. Combat in EVE can be deadly and costly, so do what you can to cut your losses.

"It's better to warp away and fight again another day."

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: What if it's a trap? I mean, they seemed to know I was coming last time, right? Sorry, but I just can't risk my ship....

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: The Athrans seem pretty dangerous. I think I'm throwing in the towel. Sorry.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: That's what I like to hear. Be careful out there, eh? These Athrans seem more... volatile than most.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Excellent. More Athran harassment?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've learned that the remaining Athrans pulled out as soon as you left your last mission. Fortunately, one of our recon pilots was able to trail them to another location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

{[character]player.name}, head out there and find out what's going on. See what these Athrans are up to, and report any suspicious activity back to me. And if they open fire on you again, you're fully authorized to shoot back. Don't take any chances.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: I wonder what was so important about that chapel… Hm. Give me a while to look into this, then come back and see me, will you? Thanks.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Well, it seems they're simply trying to disrupt the local infrastructure. What they seek to gain by doing so, I don't know... but that's the terrorist mentality for you.

But what's more interesting is that I've discovered they have an ammunitions depot not far from here. If we can take it out, we'll seriously disrupt their plans, whatever they might be. In fact, they have a Bestower full of explosives docking shortly: Get over there and take out that ship, then deal with the depot itself. They're sure to have some guards, but you've proven yourself capable of dealing with them. God speed.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Woo! That was one big explosion. That's my kind of mission.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You can't always take the safe way out, you know. Sometimes a warrior has to bleed a little to serve his nation... or hers. Point is, danger is part of the job.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Finally, we're taking the fight to them. I'll be there in moments.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Hm, I don't know. Their munitions depot is bound to be heavily guarded. Maybe you should get someone more experienced to handle this one. Too risky.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Uh, I've decided this mission isn't for me. Sorry, but you'll have to find someone else.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good show. But be careful out there: They may know you're coming.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I certainly am. Have you been able to discover what the Athrans were after?

messages.mission.briefing.text: The Athran Brotherhood has an ammunitions depot located in this very system. If we can take it out, we'll seriously disrupt their plans, whatever they might be. In fact, they have a Bestower full of explosives docking there shortly: Get over there and take out that ship, then deal with the depot itself. They're sure to have some guards, but you've proven yourself capable of dealing with them.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Glad you enjoyed it. Listen, this all may not be over yet, so don't wander too far off, okay?

localizedName.text: A New Venture – Healthy Competition (3 of 5)

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: I see that my competitors have just put up a new selection of construction tools on the market. I assume then that you did not intercept the shipment, else I would have a shiny new set of tools.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
There's a small family-run corporation operating in the neighboring system. A real pain, you know? They've got a corner on just about every small commodity in the region. I can't even get any of their suppliers to sell to me, and it's pissing me off.

I've got a plan, though. They keep getting exclusive contracts because they keep their shipments secret and secure. But I've figured out where they go. I know when and where one of their supply shipments are going to be. And even better, it's in a dead space pocket that CONCORD doesn't monitor.

Intercept the ship, blow it up, and bring the supplies--construction tools, I think-- back to me.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: It's done. Here are the construction tools.

messages.mission.extrainfo.header.text: Attacking Couriers or Haulers in Hi-sec

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Not going to-but it's just a courier! They were made to be popped!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Come on, this is a professional hauler. He almost doesn't even count as a person.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: A chance to take out one of those spineless couriers without risking CONCORD? Consider it done!

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Truth be told, nowhere in the universe is safe for the humble courier. Even though CONCORD patrols the so-called "hi-sec" areas of space (security rating 0.5-1.0), that doesn't ensure your protection one hundred percent. It is possible for a capsuleer of sufficient skill or equipment to take out another capsuleer before CONCORD fully retaliates. Usually the certainty of losing a ship to CONCORD is enough to dissuade hi-sec attacks, but if the payout or cargo is worth enough, an attacker might think it worth the trouble.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm not going to take out a lowly courier, risk or no risk.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Hah! Let's see how they do without their exclusive stock! Don't go anywhere. There's more to be done.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: That's what I like to hear!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Nothing like a little healthy competition, right?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's a small family-run corporation operating in the neighboring system. They keep getting exclusive contracts because they keep their shipments secret and secure. But I've figured out where they go.

Intercept the ship, blow it up, and bring the supplies--construction tools, I think-- back to me.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I see that my competitors have just put up a new selection of construction tools on the market. You missed the window of opportunity. I need timely and punctual help, not indecisive help.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm not going to take out a lowly courier, risk or no risk.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
The Athrans seem to have vanished, so either we dealt with the last of them, or the remaining few have gone deep into hiding. Either way, it looks like we've seen the end of their plotting.

All that remains is for you to give a report to the Assistant Chief Security Officer for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}. He's currently at a meeting at our office in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. So how about it? Do you mind flying over there and letting him know what's been happening? You'll be generously reimbursed for your time, of course.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Well, looks like the Minmatar were trying pretty hard to cover their tracks. Sorry I couldn't deliver the report — and, er... it looks like {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has some cleanup to do over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Not much left of your offices there.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You know, our security personnel just barely stopped an attempt on my life. We are still in danger, and you just walk away? This isn't over yet. I'll never understand you capsuleers, I swear.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I guess my ISK and my friendship aren't incentive enough, huh? I see where we stand. Hmph. Thanks. For nothing.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sure, I can take it over there for you. I mean, you're paying me, right?

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Not really interested in playing delivery-stooge, no. Thanks anyway.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've had enough of this. Sorry, but I can't finish this mission. Keep your reward.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Of course, yes. One does not ask a favor of a capsuleer otherwise, you know...

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Of course, {[character]agentID.name}. What do you need?

messages.mission.briefing.text: Prepare an oral report regarding your actions in the Athran Uprising for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}'s Assistant Chief Security Officer. He's currently at a meeting at our office in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
You're not alone in being attacked. Our security personnel barely stopped an attempt on my life just a few minutes after you left for that last mission. My life flashed before my eyes, I swear!

Listen, we need to end this. Let me look into this a bit further; come back and talk to me soon, though, okay? I'm not going to be able to sleep until we finish this thing.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We know who their leader is, {[character]player.name}: some woman called Cosensin Thrand. And it seems she's hiding out in this very star system. Now we can take these nut-jobs out once and for all.

I'll upload the coordinates of the deadspace location they're using as a hideout. Get on out there and deal with these creeps, and you'll be well rewarded. Good luck!

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Cosensin Thrand and her henchmen are no longer… well, they're just no longer. If you take my meaning.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text:
I see. Well, I must assume you have good reason.

Until next time.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: There is no room for cowardice in a capsuleer. I mean, you're virtually immortal! It's shameful.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: My pleasure. I'm going to enjoy this mission.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text:
Hm. These guys are pretty dangerous. And you want me to take out their leader? I don't know…

Nah, sounds too risky.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: This might be a problem for you, but I can't finish this mission. Sorry. I just can't.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I thought you might, {[character]player.name}. I thought you might.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: How so? What did you find?

messages.mission.briefing.text: Head out to the deadspace location they Athrans are using as a hideout. Deal with those creeps and take out their leader, Cosensin Thrand.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent news! I knew you would conclude this matter admirably. I shall speak on your behalf to my associates. God speed. And thank you.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Well, I need someone who can handle a ship, but who also knows how to rip ore. If you can do that, then we might be able to come to an agreement.

You've heard of Augumene ore before? It's not too common because it's too costly to refine safely. Thing is, though, a team of scientists working for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} think they've figured out a way to do it cheaply. We need someone to procure some of the ore, though, so they can run some tests.

Interested?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've got your Augumene here. Good luck making any use of it.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: But you won't be building any cred with {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} while you mine that way. Ah, well — your choice, not mine.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Yeah, I'm a decent 'roid miner. I'll have this Augumene back to you in a jiffy.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare.
