messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Fine work, my friend. Here's your reward.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Our spies have intercepted a leaked transmission from a mining survey crew who reported the discovery of an abandoned jump gate. Now, that may not sound exciting, but based on what the mining crew's description of the gate's position and general design, we think it could be a lost Jovian jump gate, able to access their space.

I want you to travel to the gate coordinates and secure that location until the elite forces arrive. Sounds easy, but it's going to be anything but.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Our spies have intercepted a leaked transmission from a mining survey crew who reported the discovery of an abandoned jump gate. Now, that may not sound exciting, but based on what the mining crew's description of the gate's position and general design, we think it could be a lost Jovian jump gate, able to access their space.

I want you to travel to the gate coordinates and secure that location until the elite forces arrive. Sounds easy, but it's going to be anything but.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: That space is a graveyard now. But it's a secure, Cartel-owned graveyard.

messages.mission.extrainfo.header.text: Tales of the Lost Jovian Gate

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Get out of my sight.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You must've come to the wrong office. Missions for those lacking guts are down the hall, to the right.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll secure the gate for you, piece of cake.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Many bars have their fair share of tall tales, but one recurring favorite is that of the fabled “lost Jovian gate.” This tale always follows a similar narrative: the friend-of-a-friend was traveling in one of the outer regions, when, suddenly, his ship dropped out of warp. The crew found themselves in the middle of nowhere, with an inactive jump gate of strange design just in front of them.

As they approached the gate, it suddenly activated, propelling the crew into Jovian space, which was either some sort of utopia or a place of blackest horror. Before the crew could gather any evidence, some sort of danger-- usually a Jovian warship of marvelous design-- immediately appeared to force the pilot back through the gate, undertaking an emergency warp as back on the other side. Invariably, the ship's log was somehow erased. The gate, of course, cannot be rediscovered, and is once more lost to time.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Is this a “take it or leave it” option?  If so, I'll leave it.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: It's hell out there! I'm not losing my stuff over some antique jump gate – I quit!

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Make sure you take plenty of ammo-- this gate is the sort of thing our competition will sacrifice almost anything to secure.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: It usually is. Please, go on.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Do you understand how important this mission was to the Cartel? We're now forced into a major military action to take the gate from the forces established there. Don't think we'll forget your incompetence any time soon.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You've given us the opportunity to study the gate, which could lead to some considerable technological advances. Good work.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: What are you doing? Securing the asset before any of the other factions arrived was a matter of timing as well as firepower! I'll find someone else, as you're obviously not up to the task.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Certain unofficial militia groups in several Caldari systems are very interested in acquiring themselves some serious firepower. They must also have some well-connected financial backers, as they want to pay top ISK to get their hands on these weapons, and in large quantities, ASAP.

You've got a solid reputation with us, so I want you to broker the deal on my behalf. Meet my man at the rendezvous point provided. He'll have the weapons cache. Everything goes well; the Caldari will show up, you'll trade the stuff, the end. But if the deal goes south, I want you to take out every last one of them and bring the weapons back here.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Have you been following the news? All that unrest over in Caldari space? Certain unofficial militia groups in several Caldari systems are very interested in acquiring themselves some serious firepower. They must also have some well-connected financial backers, as they want to pay top ISK to get their hands on these weapons, and in large quantities, ASAP.

You've got a solid reputation with us, so I want you to broker the deal on my behalf. Meet my man at the rendezvous point provided. He'll have the weapons cache. Everything goes well; the Caldari will show up, you'll trade the stuff, the end. But if the deal goes south, I want you to take out every last one of them and bring the weapons back here.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Well, the "deal" proved to be a straight setup, but I showed them what it means to mess with the Cartel.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Let's forgo the exit interview-- just remember that you can't keep messing us around like this and retain all of your body parts.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Easy there, I'm not gonna make you do it. I'll just find another pilot to represent me at the deal.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I have no problem handling weapons-- have you seen my ship lately? I'll happily broker the deal.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: So, the odds of something going wrong are high enough that you want me to go instead of you? I'll pass, thanks.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I had a bad feeling about this when I took the mission, and now things are just bad all around. I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Get going, champ; they'll be waiting.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: When you say "negotiation", I'm assuming you mean "shooting." What's happening?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Because of you, the deal has fallen through. If you weren't one of those “elite” pilots, you'd be out of an airlock by now. Sleep lightly, friend.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Really? I never thought such shady, anonymous characters would even consider betrayal. How about that?

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: If you didn't want the gig, you should've said so to begin with. I'll go find someone who's actually interested and reliable.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Engage the hostile fleet.  Watch out for reinforcements.  Kill as many as you can and then get out.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: We have reports of a strange Angel fleet massing in a nearby system.  The reports say they're all small ships, but I'm not sure if I'd trust that.  I need a pilot to round up some mates and go take them out.  You game?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Man, that was a lot of little ships.  What the heck was that all about?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Funny, I thought you were a combat pilot.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Oh, so I suppose you want to do something a little less dangerous?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Hell yeah, let me at ‘em!

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: There are rumors of Angels attempting to outmaneuver their enemies with squads of small ships, sacrificing firepower for mobility. While these are just rumors, there may be some merit to their tactics. Be wary.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sounds risky. I think I'll pass.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: This is too much work. Find some other chump.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Stellar. Get to it.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: That depends. You got something interesting for me?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Or were you just too busy watching vids?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent!  Nice shooting out there.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: Had to send someone else. Sorry, chump.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Oh, we have a number of possibilities, but only a few really choice assignments for especially trustworthy capsuleers like yourself.

These are definitely dangerous times, {[character]player.name}. The corsairs are getting bolder, crime is rampant, and the empires are pretty much at war, which will plunge us all into chaos and cost millions of lives. Unfortunately for people like me, there's not much we can do to change the inevitable; all we can do is try to make sure that what comes costs us as little as possible — in lives, worlds, and materials. To that end, I'm overseeing a lot of war prep in this region, and I'm in need of good pilots who know their stuff and aren't afraid to take some risks now and again.

This has been a hot sector lately. The Angel Cartel is especially active, but fortunately for us they're equal opportunity raiders, and have been as hard on the Caldari and the Amarr as they have on us. Amarr, for their part, have been sending in reconnaissance craft, which suggests either that they have designs on this region or they think we'll be using it as a staging area.

In fact, we think Imperial forces are rebuilding an abandoned CONCORD station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and will be using it to service their vessels, so they may be planning a more long-term presence in the region. These are just the opening moves in the great game, I assure you, but we can't let ourselves be outmaneuvered.

We're short-handed right now, so we're not above hiring independents; we'd like you to take out this station. There may be some Amarrian ships in the area, but we don't anticipate anything like a full-scale defense. Get in, destroy the base, and get out, and you'll have earned yourself a nice reward... and helped to keep the Empire out of this sector.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Base and enemy vessels destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}. It looks as if the Angel Cartel took some interest in things as well.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: This isn't going to look good to my superiors, {[character]player.name}, but I accept your decision.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Too bad. Soon we're all going to have to help out whether we want to or not.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll take care of the Amarrians for you, happily.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Doesn't interest me. Sorry.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm taking more damage than I expected. I need to bail out of this mission, {[character]agentID.name}. Sorry.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I... we appreciate your assistance.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I just might be, yes. What have you got?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We think Imperial forces are rebuilding an abandoned CONCORD station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and will be using it to service their vessels, so they may be planning a more long-term presence in the region. These are just the opening moves in the great war, I assure you, but we can't let ourselves be outmaneuvered.

We're short-handed right now, so we're not above hiring independents; we'd like you to take out this station. There may be some Amarrian ships in the area, but we don't anticipate anything like a full-scale defense. Get in, destroy the base, and get out.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work. I guess the Angels really are interested in this sector.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Destroy the three enemy shipyards and the control tower at the specified location.  Defend yourself and destroy any resistance.  You may need backup for this one.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
The Republic needs your help with this one. We've discovered one of the facilities of a corporation that's a major supplier for the Amarrian Navy. By destroying it, we'll deliver a serious blow to their military buildup, which can only help the Republic.

Expect major resistance on this-- you'll need some backup of your own. Think you can handle this?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The shipyard is down.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I thought you were a warrior of the Republic. I must've been thinking of somebody else.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Oh, so I suppose you want to do something a little less dangerous?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll need to round up my wingmen, but consider that shipyard dust.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sounds risky. I'll pass.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Okay, this is a bit much. I'm gonna have to quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Fight well.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You need something handled?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: People were counting on you!

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Unbelievable. You destroyed the shipyard and their fleet. And you came back, which is a bonus.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I'll just get someone who has some balls, then.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
A customs officer has long been suspected of taking bribes from the Amarr. There is an old smuggler's gate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that is supposed to have been deactivated, but lately ships have been registered coming through it. We believe it is the customs officer, allowing illegal slavers to bypass our normal checkpoints and bring slaves through the Federation.

We want you to fly out to the stargate and catch him in the act. Once you do, you're free to eliminate him with extreme prejudice.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
It is a sad day when you cannot trust your own citizens, don't you agree? Well, today is a sad day. You see, one of our customs agents may be accepting bribes. What's worse, he may actually be helping those Amarr slaver scum smuggle slaves through the Federation.

We have long suspected the officer, but never had any concrete proof. He has been incredibly careful in covering his tracks. But finally, we think we've got him. There's an old smuggler's stargate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that's supposed to be inactive. It seems the transmission logger isn't inactive, though, and it recently sent us a traffic report… and several industrial ships belonging to "Imperial Human Resources," a well-known Amarrian slave company, were recorded passing through the gate.

We believe the customs official is the one opening the gate for the smugglers, and he just left the station a short time ago. We planted a bug on his ship, so we have his current location. I want you to fly out there, catch the customs official in the act of opening the gate, and destroy him.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: You were right: the customs official was letting slaves into the Federation. But he won't be doing so any longer.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Great. Unless something is done, this problem will just continue to grow. I never thought you would be so selfish.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I am surprised. I wouldn't have taken you for someone who'd allow such an injustice to continue.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I will do anything necessary to ensure that the Federation remains a bastion of freedom!

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Shouldn't this really be something the police could take care of?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Now, get out there and catch this scumbag. And vaporize the smugglers as well. They're not our main targets, but eliminating a few of them should help you let off some steam.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: If you're paying well, then you're right — I am perfect for it.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work. The Federation does its utmost to make sure our enemies cannot undermine our way of life, and you've struck a great blow today in that pursuit.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
There's a badly damaged Gallente convoy nearby. One or two of the vessels may be capable of defending themselves, but we don't think they're up to much of a fight. We want you to head out there; finish them off and get as much of that salvage as you can. Somewhere in all that cargo and salvage, there's a sealed container of great value to the Cartel, so we'll provide you with a generous bonus if you get it back to us intact.

Oh, yes, one more thing... The Gallente convoy got off a distress signal, so you might have to contend with a Gallente rescue mission. And we've heard some chatter from the Serpentis saying that they might be sending ships soon, so best be on your guard. Our intelligence says that neither of those factions has very much in the way of resources in the area, so you shouldn't have too much to do.

Things might get dicey, but I'm sure it's nothing you can't handle.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: You were definitely low-balling the risk, {[character]agentID.name}. Here's your precious container.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I never said you wouldn't get your hair a little mussed. I'm sorry that the mean ol' bad guys scratched up your precious paint job.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Your loss, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sure, I'll give it a shot, {[character]agentID.name}. When do I leave?

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I think you're low-balling the risk here. I'll look for opportunities elsewhere.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Holy crap, where are all those ships coming from? I'm taking too much damage. I quit!

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: ASAP, {[character]player.name}. See you when you get back.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I've been busy. What've you got cooking?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's a badly damaged Gallente convoy nearby. One or two of the vessels may be capable of defending themselves, but we don't think they're up to much of a fight. We want you to head out there; finish them off and get as much of that salvage as you can. Somewhere in all that cargo and salvage there's a sealed container of great value to the Cartel, so we'll provide you with a generous bonus if you get it back to us intact.

Oh, yes, one more thing... The Gallente convoy got off a distress signal, so you might have to contend with a Gallente rescue mission. And we've heard some chatter from the Serpentis saying that they might be sending ships soon, so best be on your guard. Our intelligence says that neither of those factions has very much in the way of resources in the area, so you shouldn't have too much to do.

Things might get dicey, but I'm sure it's nothing you can't handle.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I can't imagine why you're complaining. You got the job done, after all.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ehh, politics, I believe. Oh, I never get tired of them. Dear, sweet politics. Oh, wait. No. I hate politics.

But without politics, our great democratic and free society would collapse. It's the nature of the beast, I'm afraid. And, well, the Federation has numerous laws to prevent politicians from being abusive with their politicking. Now, some dirtside political office is up for grabs after the incumbent died of a heart attack after a night at a pleasure hub. "Vice Commissioner of Waste Management for the Civic Council" or something unimportant like that.

Normally, we wouldn't even bother with something this trivial. Those silly dirtside hillhuggers and their governments aren't much to look at. But one of them had to go and break some laws, and now it's our job to clean it up. You see, someone has hijacked some broadcast waves and is sending out a constant message denouncing one of the candidates. And because it's a space-based satellite doing the broadcasting, we're the ones that have to deal with it.

Now, we don't know who it is that's making the broadcasts, and frankly, I don't care. As long as they're stopped, I'm happy with it. We've pinned down the offending satellite, so I want you to fly over there and blow it up. There might be some automated defenses, but it's just some mudsucker's place, so they can't be that great.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've destroyed the satellite, but I think there's something more going on here than meets the eye.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Great. You can't get the job done, so now I'll have to deal with it even more.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You're really turning me down? If I have to deal directly with those dust-snufflers, I'll scream.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: You really must not like people who grew up planetside. Anyway, I'll take care of it.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The Gallente Federation is a massive democracy. It is divided up into several regions, which are subdivided into districts, which are further divided into sub-districts… which make up several individual systems, each of which has one or more planetary governments, each of which further has additional subdivisions. Though every planet follows some basic rules, such as having regular elections with universal suffrage, the systems on each planet are as varied as the Gallente people.

For most observers, planetary politics in the Federation are incredibly tedious. Some, however, count the politics of the planets as the most fascinating and vital part of the democracy. There is a huge amount of bureaucracy involved, which makes it too dense for most to penetrate. But the amount of energy put forth by many individuals (who are unlikely to be remembered once their terms are finished) exemplifies the true spirit of the Federation.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Wow, you know, I have something more important to do. Like... uh... yeah — no thanks.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: What? Caldari forces protecting that satellite? Great. Just great. Now we'll have to launch a whole investigation into the matter. I might even get sent planetside. I do hate this job sometimes.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: The sooner you deal with this, the better. I hate having to interact with those petty land-lice.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text:
You know what they say about assumptions, right? …something about, uh, sums and options… I think.

Why am I here again?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Someone has illegally hijacked a broadcast satellite and is using it to play a message denigrating a local politician running for office. I could care less, but those sand-sifters won't stop nagging me about it. We've found the offending satellite, we just need it destroyed — the sooner, the better. That way I'll stop having to hear complaints about it.

Oh, there might be some automated defenses, but they probably won't be that hard to handle.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Hey, I didn't sign up for this when I accepted your mission!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
So, it turns out that the Caldari Navy is the one behind those transmissions. The question is, why? Why do the Caldari care who wins some meaningless election on some planetary hovel? That's what we have to find out now. The first step in taking care of this will be to question the candidate they were broadcasting about.

Now, I've received word that the man is vacationing with his family a few systems away. We've already sent word over to have him recalled as a matter of official Federation business. By the time you get there, he should be ready for pick up.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Well, it turns out that the Caldari Navy is behind those transmissions. The question is why… Why do the Caldari care who wins some meaningless election on some planetary hovel? That's what we have to find out now. The first step in taking care of this will be to question the candidate they were broadcasting about.

Now, I've received word that the man is vacationing with his family a few systems away. We've already sent word over to have him recalled as a matter of official Federation business. By the time you get there, he should be ready for pick up.

What, I didn't mention that? Yes, you get the great pleasure of taxiing that earthbounder back to us. I know you'll accept, won't you?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I brought the politician back, as asked.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I don't want to deal with this any more than you do. You're really quitting on me?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I suppose I'll have to send someone else to do it for me.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I've carried worse around. One politician shouldn't be too bad.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Zzzz... What? Huh? Oh, you should find someone else, I guess, since your proposal's making me fall asleep.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm too lazy to finish your mission. Sorry.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Hurry over there and get him. The sooner he's back, the sooner I can get rid of him.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text:
Technically, I had nothing to do with getting you into this in the first place. I was just...

Ah, never mind. What do you need?

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Alright, now I've got to go have a little chat with our politician. Come back to me later to see what I've discovered.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Our politician friend managed to annoy a Caldari Navy officer back in the day and now that officer is out for revenge. He's the one behind all these broadcasts. I guess he figured since it was such a meaningless, tiny local election, the Federation wouldn't stop his revenge.

I guess he doesn't know that we'll take any opportunity there is to blow up a few Caldari Navy vessels.

We've tracked his base down and want you to go over there and take him out. The sooner this headache is over, the better.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
No, it's true. I know I always speak glowingly of them, but really, they get under my skin.

Anyway, my questioning finally got some answers out of that damn fool politician. It turns out that there is no vast conspiracy after all. Not really. It turns out the idiot is just a little too loud-mouthed for his own good. He used to be in the Navy… before he was discharged because he kept fainting every time he went onto the battlefield. But before he demonstrated that bit of heroism, he managed to piss off a Caldari Navy officer by throwing up on him during a diplomatic summit.

Apparently, the officer in question never lived it down and still gets heckled about the event to this day. And now he's out for revenge by trying to disrupt our man, the stupid politician. It's… it's so tedious and… stupid.

Anyway, I guess this officer figured that, since it was such a meaningless little election, the Federation wouldn't bother to interfere with his revenge. Heh. I guess he doesn't know that we'll take any opportunity there is to blow up a few Caldari Navy vessels. We've tracked his base down and want you to go over there and take him out.

The sooner this headache is over, the better.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Caldari have learned not to mess with our local district elections.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You couldn't even take care of one lone Caldari officer? What kind of pod pilot are you?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Nnnggg.... You're just trying to give me an aneurysm, aren't you?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: At last, something interesting! I'll do it!

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm sorry, but I'm not going to handle someone else's bully.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: It turns out those Caldari Navy guys are pretty tough. I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I've uploaded the location to your NeoCom.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Really? You can't? I would never have guessed.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good. Of course, now everyone thinks our politician's some great hero, important enough for the Caldari Navy to try and get rid of him. The fool will probably become President some day. Makes my skin crawl just thinking about it.

messages.mission.briefing.text: The daughter of a prominent Holder has eloped with a famous Gallente holo star, despite having a proper marriage with an Amarr man awaiting her at home. Retrieve her from this seducer and kill him.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes, I have work for you. The daughter of a prominent Holder has been seduced by a famous Gallente holo star. She's run away with him, likely planning to get married as soon as she is out of her family's reach.

She was already betrothed to a perfectly suitable Amarrian man, a match approved by her family and her faith. Obviously, she must be brought back into the fold.

You will be well rewarded if you can deliver her back to her family before she can shame herself any further. If you destroy this seducer in the process-- well, that's all the better.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I, uh, found the girl. You take her.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: And I thought you were a true Amarr. You cannot expect to keep a good reputation if you fail to do these jobs.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: And I thought you were a good Amarr. You cannot expect to keep a good reputation if you won't put in any effort.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Of course I'll do it.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The Gallente are great lovers of wealth and luxury, and especially of beauty. They produce countless holos, from the cheapest porn flicks to high-priced stage shows and beyond. The stars of these productions are greatly esteemed for the entertainment they provide, and therefore hold influence and power in some circles.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't have time to chase down some runaway. I have more important things to do.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I don't have time to chase down some runaway. I have more important things to do.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I knew you were the right person for the job. Take care, as this holo star does have bodyguards.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I heard you had a job for me.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Thanks to you, {[character]player.name}, the Holder's daughter has married the Gallente holo star and brought shame to her family and to the Amarr. Do not think that you can let things like this happen without suffering any consequences.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I knew I could count on you. You are indeed a faithful Amarr; your reputation will only benefit from the work you have done.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: Thanks to you, {[character]player.name}, the Holder's daughter has married the Gallente holo star and brought shame to her family and to the Amarr. Do not think that you can let things like this happen and without suffering any consequences.

messages.mission.briefing.text: The Minmatar are attempting to form an alliance with the Khanid Kingdom in order to gain an ally against the Amarr Empire. This could be dangerous to the Empire, as the Khanid may know much that could help Amarr's enemies. Find, intercept and destroy the Minmatar ambassador's vessel and its escorts and bring the ambassador back for interrogation.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
That is correct.

The Minmatar, deceitful devils that they are, are attempting to form an alliance with the Khanid Kingdom. Khanid is a traitor to our beliefs, and he knows much about us that the Minmatar could exploit if they manage to forge an alliance.

We cannot risk the chance that the Minmatar might succeed. Go find the Minmatar vessel and destroy it before it reaches Khanid. Take care to bring the ambassador back for questioning. Be cautious, however – the Minmatar have the distasteful habit of thinking they can fight back against us.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I found and destroyed the Minmatar ambassador's ship. I've brought you the "envoy" for questioning.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I thought you were a better pod pilot than that. A true Amarr would understand how much this refusal could damage a reputation.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I am disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}. I thought you would see the importance of this mission.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Nothing would please me more than to put a stop to this plot.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The Amarr Empire is ruled by the Emperor and the five Heirs. When the Emperor dies, these Heirs go through a set of ritual competitions to become the next Emperor.

In 22762 AD, Khanid was the Heir of one of the other five families, but he refused to acknowledge the election of the new Emperor. He also refused to commit ritual suicide, which is done by the remaining Heirs in order to keep resentments and past problems from interfering with the new ruler's regime.

Instead of being obedient and faithful, Khanid fled Amarr and set out to create his own empire. He formed the Khanid Kingdom, which is also known as the “Dark Amarr.”

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't see this as a threat to us. Khanid might not conform as he should, but he is still Amarr.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I don't have time to hunt down these Minmatar vessels. You'll have to find someone else.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Wonderful! Remember to take care – Minmatar are always hard to break.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I heard that you needed someone willing to do a combat mission.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: I cannot believe that you could not find and destroy the Minmatar vessels. You are not the pod pilot I thought you were. As a result of this failure, the Khanid Kingdom may have leaked dangerous secrets to the Minmatar.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent. Thank you for your efforts.  Here is your reward.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: You should make decisions more quickly, capsuleer. As a result of your failure to destroy the ship, the Minmatar ambassador met with someone within the Khanid Kingdom; whether or not an alliance will be forged is still unknown.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Some Minmatar slaves have rebelled, killing several Amarr and stealing a ship. Track them down so that they can be returned to their owner.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
So the news is out.

It's true, some slaves have rebelled, and their actions have caused the deaths of several people. They have stolen a ship, and thus far they've managed to evade capture as well. This is insult on top of injury and cannot be tolerated.

I want you to track them down so that they can be returned to their owner.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've brought the slaves back.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Be careful or people will begin to think you support the barbarians.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Be careful or people will begin to think you support the barbarians.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll find them and bring them back.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
When the Amarr Empire first came across the Minmatar, they began raiding this new people for slaves as they had with every other race they'd come across, a practice that is sanctified and even encouraged by the Amarr religion.

Though the Minmatar have since rebelled and managed to expel the Amarr and their allies from Minmatar space, approximately a third of all Minmatar are still enslaved under the Amarr.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: They aren't worth the trouble.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: I knew I could count on you to retrieve those upstarts. Stay close: I suspect I'll have another mission for you shortly.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: God's will be with you. You will be greatly rewarded when you bring them back.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I've heard rumors about a slave uprising.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Inaction speaks, pilot. Be careful or people will begin to think you support the barbarians.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: These slaves aren't worth the trouble I've gone to; get someone else to hunt them down.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
If you're willing. Given the current state of interstellar affairs, Mordu's Legion is in the thick of things. They've been engaging in raids and reconnaissance, harassing merchant traffic, and generally making trouble for us. In this sector, at least, they're doing just what the Caldari want them to — keeping our fleet tied down so those greedy bastards can martial their own forces in relative peace.

We might have an ace in the hole, however. We have good intelligence that many Intaki inside the Caldari State are growing impatient and restless, suffering discrimination and unemployment. Many blame the Caldari for their woes, and with the right incentive they might even be persuaded to secede back to the Federation. An incident involving the State-sanctioned Mordu's Legion may be just enough to tip the scales.

We've been monitoring subspace chatter, and we think that the Legion may be planning on hitting one of our bases in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We're planning on making it known that the base is full of Intaki refugees, but just to clinch the deal, it would be best if some heroic pilot caught the Mordus in the act and drove them off before the base was completely destroyed.

What we'd like you to do is get over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and take up position near the station. When the Legion ships arrive, destroy them or drive them off. We'll be monitoring things by video drone, so we'll have clear evidence of the attack.

Oh, and the Legion may be coming in strength, so you might want to bring some friends along. So, what do you say?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Mordu's Legion fleet is defeated. And the Caldari have egg all over their faces.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: That isn't what we're doing at all! But it's obvious to me you don't want the job, so forget it anyway.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'm up for anything that will embarrass the Caldari. I'll do it.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Mordu's Legion is descended from a group of Intaki military personnel who sided with the Caldari State when it chose to secede from the Gallente Federation. It was led by a brilliant Caldari officer named Muryia Mordu, who fought the Gallente with great distinction.

After the war, the Intaki were given land around Waschi City on the planet Kamokor IV, but soon racial tensions flared between them and Caldari nationalists, who called for the expulsion of all foreigners. The Intaki called upon their hero Mordu for assistance, and the aging commander emerged from retirement to lead an independent mercenary group dedicated to preserving Intaki rights and property. Mordu's Legion helped defeat the nationalists and made peace with the Caldari authorities.

Today, the Legion remains a well-known mercenary band that often works closely with the Caldari State. Many Intaki continue to suffer discrimination at the hands of the xenophobic Caldari and have grown disillusioned with life in the corporate state. Nevertheless, Mordu remains a revered character among the Intaki, many of whom see him as a savior who will one day return to deliver his adopted people from the repression and poverty that they suffer from today.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: That sounds awfully fishy to me. I prefer to let other people get dirty with the propaganda machine.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm encountering more difficulty than I'd anticipated. I have to to withdraw from the mission, {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Well done. The system coordinates have been sent to your NeoCom.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: What's up, {[character]agentID.name}? I take it you have some work for me.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We think that Mordu's Legion may be planning on hitting one of our bases in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. What we'd like you to do is get over there and take up position near the station. When the Legion ships arrive, destroy them or drive them off. We'll be monitoring things by video drone, so we'll have clear evidence of the attack.

Oh, and the Legion may be coming in strength, so you might want to bring some friends along.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent. Your reward has been entered into your interstellar account. Many thanks, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Well, we've had some suspicious activity in this system lately. We suspect that someone — Angel Cartel, or possibly Serpentis, maybe even the Amarrians — might be sneaking in and prepping the system for attack with hidden bases, supplies, and the like. There may even be a hidden jumpgate somewhere in the vicinity; we've certainly detected some suspicious warp signatures and have been able to triangulate them down to several potential locations, all quite close to each other.

If we make a move with a large fleet, though, we might spook the enemy, so we're looking for a freelancer who's willing to take a risk on behalf of the Federation. We need someone to fly to the possible locations of the acceleration gate and see what's there. I'll enter the location of the first acceleration gate into your NeoCom; you should be able to reach the others using whatever internal gate array they've put in place. Fly through each one in turn and check the area for any gates that look suspicious. If you find one, you need to blast it before the enemy can jump any more ships around in this system.

Mind you, if there are enemy ships, you might have to fight them too, and no one can say for sure what might come through the gate. There might even be static defense turrets or drones as well. Who knows?

Once the gate is destroyed, return here and report; do it quickly and you'll earn yourself a nice bonus. Are you in?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The enemy gate is destroyed, along with some of their hardware, {[character]agentID.name}. Thanks for the mission.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I expected better from you, to be honest. You are a capsuleer, right? You're not just impersonating one?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: That's too bad, {[character]player.name}. Nothing else available right now, I'm afraid.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sounds like a decent job. I'll do it.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: That doesn't sound very interesting. Have you got anything else?

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm taking too much damage, and this is taking too long. I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks for your help. The coordinates are in your NeoCom, along with my instructions.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Might be, {[character]agentID.name}. What have you got?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We need someone to fly to the possible locations of the secret gate and see what's there. I'll enter the location of the first acceleration gate into your NeoCom; you should be able to reach the others using whatever internal gate array they've put in place. Fly through each one in turn and check the area for any gates that look suspicious. If you find one, you need to blast it before the enemy can jump any more ships around in this system.

Mind you, if there are enemy ships, you might have to fight them too, and no one can say for sure what might come through the gate. There might even be static defense turrets or drones as well.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Your assistance is appreciated, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: You've waited too long to do what I asked. You've taught me not to mistake you for dependable.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes. We interrogated several of the Minmatar slaves you brought back after they escaped.

It seems that the errant Minmatar were headed to a group of their own kind within the Gallente Federation. In fact, they might not have managed to escape at all without the help of a Gallente contact.

When we applied more pressure, the slaves could only provide us with a location. There was supposed to be a data chip in a dead drop at this rendezvous. In the interest of preventing further mayhem, I need you to bring me that chip.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's the data chip.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'll have to find someone else.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: And here I thought you were a brave one.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sounds important. I'll take care of it.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: A significant percentage of the Minmatar population resides within the Gallente Federation, forming a rather powerful political bloc. This bloc is one reason that the relations between Amarr and Gallente remain constantly tense.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't want to risk angering the Gallente. I'll pass.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Good work. Let me see what this says; I may have another mission for you shortly.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I look forward to seeing what you find.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You said you might have more work for me?

messages.mission.briefing.text: The slaves provided us with a location. There was supposed to be a data chip in a dead drop at this rendezvous. In the interest of preventing further mayhem, I need you to bring me that chip.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I've waited too long for your reply. You've taught me not to mistake you for dependable.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Something else has come up. I quit.

messages.mission.briefing.text: The data cube yielded the name of a single member of the powerful Minmatar political bloc in the Federation. This man was the contact that helped the slaves escape. Kill him and any who protect him.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes, we found some very useful information on it.

It seems that the Minmatar faction within the Federation has garnered the secret support of some influential members of the Gallente government.

Those officials were not named, but the slaves' contact within the Minmatar faction was. I want you to go to the location that the data chip indicated, and kill that contact and any who defend him.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: You won't have any more problems with that Minmatar collaborator.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: And here I thought you were brave, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I thought you were brave, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll make certain that he doesn't cause any more trouble.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: A significant percentage of the Minmatar population resides within the Gallente Federation, forming a rather powerful political bloc. This bloc is one reason that the relations between Amarr and Gallente remain constantly tense.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: It isn't wise to go after someone with such high connections. I won't do it.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I don't want to go after someone with such high connections. I'm done with this.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I knew I could count on you. Remember that we're setting an example here.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Did that data chip have anything interesting on it?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: I hope I can find someone capable who'll be able to kill the Gallente contact before he finds out that he's a target. I am disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Nicely done.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I hope I can find someone capable who'll be able to kill the Gallente contact before he finds out that he's a target. I am disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text: While mining ore in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, a small group of mining pirates uncovered a religious artifact of uncertain origin. Find these rogues and retrieve the artifact from them.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I always have work for a good pod pilot.

It has recently come to my attention that a small group of nearby pirates stumbled across something rather unusual. While mining for ore, they made a lucky discovery-- they uncovered what appears to be a religious artifact.

As you know, such an object is of great importance to all Amarr. There are many Holders who would pay large sums to get their hands on such a find; even better, there are collectors among the royal family who would give large rewards to add such a thing to their private collections.

I want you to find these rogue miners and retrieve this artifact from them. Bring it here, and you will be well rewarded.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I hope you find this as valuable as you thought it would be. The miners have already paid with their lives.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I am disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I am disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I would be honored to undertake such a mission.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Due in large part to the values and teachings of the Amarr faith, the Amarr have the most extensive libraries, archives, and collections of artifacts pertaining to post-Eden life and, possibly, the EVE gate.

One of the heirs of the Ardishapur family, hailed as a paragon of the faith, has amassed what may be the largest array of religious artifacts in a private collection. Some of his pieces are even suspected to pre-date the closure of the EVE gate.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm not going to go haring off over some unidentified piece of ancient junk. My time's worth more than that.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm done haring off over some unidentified piece of ancient junk. My time's worth more than this.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I knew I could count on you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: I thought you might have some work for me today.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Due to your sloth, the miners who discovered the artifact found another buyer, one from outside the faith. Thanks to your neglect, we may never discover the true religious significance of this piece of living history.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Here is your reward. You have truly earned it.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: Due to your sloth, the miners who discovered the artifact found another buyer, one from outside the faith. Thanks to your neglect, we may never discover the true religious significance of this piece of living history.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A new race track is being built in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. During the final stages of building, we received reports of some ships bearing Gallente markings, and several suspicious "accidents" have occurred. Sabotage is suspected. Go find these ships and destroy them so that no harm will come to participants or viewers during the big race.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I have a task that must be done quickly, and it requires punitive force.

A new race track is being designed and built in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and it is supposed to be the grandest and most beautiful and complicated tracks yet ever to exist in all of the known sectors! A substantial quantity of money and work have gone into this track, and there are plans to hold one of the largest races ever as soon as the track is finished.

However, some suspicious ships have been seen in the vicinity. They evade patrols, but we've received reports that they bear Gallente markings. A couple of "accidents" have already occurred while testing the track, and investigations have led to suspicion of sabotage.

We think that these Gallente ships have been sabotaging this new track, probably in hopes of killing many Holders and their families when the time comes for the great inaugural race.

I want you to put a stop to this nonsense before it has any further impact. Destroy those ships; it's time we sent a message.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've disposed of the Gallente miscreants.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You are not the pilot I thought you were. I'll be sure to spread the word of your laziness and ingratitude.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You are not the pilot I thought you were. I'll be sure to spread the word of your laziness and ingratitude.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: You can count on me.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Ship racing has become very popular in the past few years. Pilots race their ships to see who can complete a circuit the fastest and thus show off proper ship handling, attention to quick course corrections, and how much power can be coaxed out of a ship.

The Amarr have some of the best racers in the sector and to commemorate their successes, they are building a new racing area in one of our poorer systems to help stimulate the economy, while at the same time showcasing Amarr skill in flying the best ships in pod pilot hands today.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't have time to play hide-and-seek with some phantom troublemakers. Find someone else who has nothing better to do.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Your intelligence must be wrong because I can't find these mysterious ships. Find someone else who has nothing better to do than playing hide-and-seek with phantom troublemakers.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Do take care. Our intelligence on these ships is sketchy at best, so they may be more powerful than we know.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You have work for me, then?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: The Gallente ships were finally found, but not before they caused further serious damage to the track. You are lucky that they were discovered before the great race, or else you would have many more Amarr lives on your conscience. You may rest assured that I will spread the word of your laziness and ingratitude.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I knew you were the right pilot for the job.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: The Gallente ships were finally found, but not before they caused further serious damage to the track. You are lucky that they were discovered before the great race, or else you would have many more Amarr lives on your conscience. You may rest assured that I will spread the word of your laziness and ingratitude.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I do, in fact, have a little matter that needs your attention. It's rather... delicate.

My corporation recently had a small misunderstanding with a Caldari business rival. Fortunately, after some of our folks met with the Caldari to have a… discussion, our people managed to limp back here; unfortunately, they left the wreckage of the Caldari ship intact, including the ship's log.

Now, it would impact any future dealings we might have with the Caldari if this dispute became known to their authorities. I'm sure they'd insist on petty things like vengeance. So we'd rather that didn't happen. We'd like you to go destroy all evidence of the Caldari cruiser. It can be found at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

So, will you be a pal and do this for me?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Caldari cruiser is now dust. Would have been nice of you to let me know about the Guristas, though.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: That's so funny, {[character]player.name}, because I just got this funny sensation behind my eyes when I saw you walk in — sort of like an ulcer, but in my brain.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm sorry, {[character]player.name}, but the way you dress, I thought you were a janitor. My mistake!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sounds simple enough, {[character]agentID.name}.  I'll get on it right away.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The worst enemy is the one who was once an ally. This is a lesson not lost on the Caldari Navy, for it was from within their own ranks that the seeds of the Guristas pirates were born.

The Guristas were founded by two ex-Caldari Navy members now known only as "Fatal" and "The Rabbit." Utilizing their knowledge of the Navy's procedures — and thus its weaknesses — these two renegades have confounded their previous employers for many years with their persistence and ingenuity.

The Guristas cannot totally disown their militaristic origins: among pirates, they remain arguably the most honorable among a dishonorable bunch. Yet spacefarers shouldn't take too much comfort from that fact, or from their amusing bunny-skull logo. The Guristas will still slit your throat if there's profit involved.

Honor, as many have learned, goes only so far when ISK is concerned.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: If you want a clean-up job, hire a janitor.  Not interested.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: I'm so happy to hear the ship is no longer an issue for us — and especially that you're okay, {[character]player.name}. And so sorry about those Guristas. You're right, I should have said something...

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: {[character]player.name} — you are the absolute best! I knew today was my lucky day!

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Then I take it you've got a high-paying job for me, right?

messages.mission.briefing.text: Destroy the Caldari cruiser at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} along with any other hostile ships you may encounter. No witnesses!

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm getting a really bad feeling about this job, and I've learned to trust my gut. I'm out. And go easy on batting those eyelashes, {[character]agentID.name} — you'll pull a muscle.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}  and destroy the Guristas pirates there. Don't forget to recover the ship log that they stole from the Caldari cruiser. They won't be there long, so please hurry!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I'm so sorry about those Guristas! You're right. I should have said something... but I knew you'd be able to handle it.

Anyway, it seems they boarded that Caldari cruiser before you arrived and took the ship's log. Now they're threatening to turn it over to the Caldari Navy if we don't pay up. We've got enough on our plate at the moment without fomenting open war with Caldari. Amarr'd just love that, huh?

So, we've tracked them to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. If you could go and take care of them, I'd be really, really grateful.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I destroyed those Guristas, {[character]agentID.name}, and I got the ship log. But, uh, I checked it to make sure it's the right log, and it… well, it has some interesting information. Is there something you want to tell me?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text:
You surprise me, to be honest. I would have thought that kind of complex addition quite beyond you.

Bye now.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I did say I was sorry about forgetting to mention the pirates… but it seems obvious you're just afraid to fight. Run along then, little egger, run along.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: This job just keeps getting better and better. And yes, that's sarcasm. But yes, I'll do it — for the ISK. I can't spend your gratitude.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Sorry, {[character]agentID.name}, but no thanks. You seem about as trustworthy as a Thukker ship salesman. Go play some other sucker, 'cause I'm gone.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've just done the math, {[character]agentID.name}. Bunch of Guristas + me not trusting you = I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: It speaks very well of you that you aren't running away when things get hot, {[character]player.name}. I like that in a capsuleer.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Funny you should mention the Guristas, because I kind of wanted an explanation about that. You knew they'd be there?

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
Hey {[character]player.name},

Just a quick note to let you know your laxity in retrieving that ship log has led to several Caldari vigilante attacks on my corporation. At last count, 200 people are dead. Have a nice day!

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
Oh, yeah, {[character]player.name}, about that....

Listen, give me a minute to wrap this up, and then come back and I'll explain everything, okay?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Your agent wants you to meet with the buyer at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

And you might want to keep an eye out for the Guristas. They might be a little peeved with you.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Okay, I haven't been totally honest with you. I'm currently working on behalf of a Covert Ops agent for the Republic Navy.

That Caldari ship? Belonged to a disgruntled military scientist who was going to sell us a bio-weapon prototype. Unfortunately, we had a small misunderstanding over price, and now he's dead. Things happen, you know? I hired you to retrieve the ship logs so we could have a little thing called "plausible deniability" if things went badly. Like they kinda did.

{[character]player.name}, here's the new plan. First of all, the weapon is useless — the scientist was as terrible a researcher as he was a negotiator. But rumors we whispered into the right ears have got people believing otherwise. This whole operation was about raising funds for Navy Covert Ops, after all. Spy stuff isn't cheap!

Anyway, we need you to meet with the buyer at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Will you do this for me?

Sorry about all the fibs. Please? Pretty please?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Well, it's done. Maybe not the way you wanted, but it's done. The buyer is dead, the pirates are dead, you've got your secret package back, and I need a drink. Now pay up!

messages.mission.extrainfo.header.text: The Murky World of Covert Ops

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Wow. What a build-up to the letdown you turned out to be, {[character]player.name}. Oh, well — there must remain some expendable suckers out there I can use, I'm sure.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: But I'm really in deep with Covert Ops! I have an honorary badge and everything! And a set of spy glasses, too. I'm the real deal!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: You've lied to me, you've manipulated me, and you've almost gotten me killed. I've got to admit, {[character]agentID.name} — I'm starting to like your style. I'm in!

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Few have the skills to enter the world of Covert Ops, and fewer still survive long once they enter it. And of those who do survive, rare are those who can claim to be totally sane afterwards.

One of the first lessons in Covert Ops is "plausible deniability"; this, along with the selective use of misinformation, allows a government and or a military entity to distance itself from its spies and operatives should their activities become known. Paradoxically, though, while every government and military organization requires Covert Ops to survive, it can be extremely harmful to admit such groups' existence, at least without a feasible back-up story — a story usually provided by the covert agents themselves.

At times, the distance between a Covert Ops agency and its parent organization can become so byzantine that funding can present a dangerous optic. When that occurs, operatives may have to raise funds themselves, in ways only they can...

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Newsflash, {[character]agentID.name}! You're obviously out of your mind. I'm putting as much distance between you and me as humanly possible. See ya, crackpot!

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I've just had a sudden attack of common sense, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm out of here before I end up in either a casket or a rubber room.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I knew you'd never let me down, {[character]player.name}.  Just hurry before this buyer comes to his senses (or you do…). Oh — did I say that out loud?

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Well, maybe. Kinda depends on what it is you tell me now and what you want next, really.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text:
{[character]player.name},

How difficult was it to just deliver the prototype? What, the thought of a few Guristas out for revenge stopped you? Maybe you just didn't want it enough. Ever think of that? Very, very disappointed, me.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Congratulations, {[character]player.name}! Not only have you done the impossible, but you've made me 100,000 ISK in a side bet! My partners thought you'd die long before this! Thanks a bunch! Here's your reward, and a little extra besides! Don't spend it all in one place, champ.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text:
{[character]player.name},

It seems unfortunate that you would go so far in this operation only to wander off right at the end. And since you had the prototype, we couldn't get paid, either. Not a good idea to upset Covert Ops that way, you know? Really Bad Idea.

localizedName.text: Driving a Wedge - Get the Gallente (1 of 2)

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: I thought you were taking care of that matter in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that we discussed. And now I find out from my source that the summit went on unimpeded. What have you been up to all this time? I'm beginning to think you're not as trustworthy as I'd been led to believe. Rest assured, you're going to have to work hard to get back into my good graces.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ah, my apologies for being cross with you, but it's been a busy day. As if fighting the Gallente on our front doorstep isn't bad enough, the Minmatar are becoming more active of late.

The biggest risk is that our two enemies will start closely coordinating their attacks. The State cannot allow this to happen. To that end, there is a summit meeting in need of disrupting. If I give you the coordinates for the meeting site, can you go over there and blow up a diplomat?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The Gallente exploded, and the Minmatar ran off.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Then stop wasting my time!

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: I'll take out that Gallente.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I could take out that Minmatar instead.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm not going to be able to finish this job after all.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. Come back when you can tell me that the Gallente is done for.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: Um, I need a job...

messages.mission.briefing.text: As if fighting the Gallente on our front doorstep wasn't bad enough, the Minmatar are becoming more active of late. The biggest risk is that our two enemies will start closely coordinating their attacks. The State cannot allow this to happen. To that end, there is a summit meeting in need of disrupting. Killing the Gallente diplomat should do the trick.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: As I did not receive word from you about the summit we discussed, I have handled the problem by assigning another pilot.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Give me just a moment to check something.

localizedName.text: Driving a Wedge - Delegation Destruction (2 of 2)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The attack on the meeting between the Gallente and Minmatar emissaries went perfectly. Now we need to finish the job. After escaping the scene of the attack, the Minmatar ambassador was whisked away to a nearby staging area.

A raid on the Minmatar delegation now will look like a reprisal raid from the Gallente delegation, and since the Minmatar know they weren't responsible for the initial attack, they'll be even angrier. We have reason to believe that the enemy diplomats have been transferred aboard the Minmatar flagship to ensure their safety. It's the only battleship in the delegation, and it must be destroyed.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
The attack on the meeting between the Gallente and Minmatar emissaries went perfectly. Now we need to finish the job. After escaping the scene of the attack, the Minmatar ambassador was whisked away to a nearby staging area.

A raid on the Minmatar delegation now will look like a reprisal raid from the Gallente delegation, and since the Minmatar know they weren't responsible for the initial attack, they'll be even angrier. We have reason to believe that the enemy diplomats have been transferred aboard the Minmatar flagship to ensure their safety. It's the only battleship in the delegation, and it must be destroyed. Are you game?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: The enemy flagship is no more.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: What happened to “no problem?” You capsuleers are all alike – as soon as the going gets tough you cut and run.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You're letting a great opportunity slip away, but it's your call.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Only one battleship? No problem.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: Attack a battleship and its entire convoy? No thanks.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Find someone else to take this on. I'm busy.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: For your sake, I hope not. Good luck.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You mentioned an opportunity?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Apparently we did not strike while the iron was hot. In the time since I've talked to you, my source has indicated that the Minmatar emissaries have safely made it back to their own space. Worse still, they appear to have sorted things out with the Gallente, or at least allayed some of their suspicions.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I knew you were up to it. Good work, {[character]player.name}!
