messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
It appears that the CPF investigation team is in Onirvura because of some intel – intel I believe we can manipulate. I have learned that they partially decrypted a communication between my people here and our blueprint buyers in KFR-ZE. Fortunately for us, they couldn't fully decipher the location we were transmitting to, thank the Maker. My guys re-encrypt their comms every few seconds, so all they know is that this area is where the transmission originated and the destination system started with KF, and has a Z and E in its name. Still, too close for comfort.

Ever heard of KFIE-Z, {[character]player.name}? It's a dead-end system in Delve. The Headquarters of the Blood Raider Covenant, in fact. It's the perfect decoy for us; we can make it look as if opportunistic Blood Raiders hit the Serpentis facility, and there was little more to it all than that. We just need to sell the lie.

There is an old Blood Raider compound not far from here. Inside it, there should be a transmitter system we can use. All you need to do is secure the area and deliver my people safely to the Communications Tower so they can send out a fake transmission. The CPF should pick it up and follow the signal down to Delve… if they're feeling suicidal, that is.

Rumor has it the place has long since been abandoned, but I've come to distrust intel I don't get first-hand. Besides, any time those Sani Sabik cultists are not making noise, you should be concerned. The quiet ones are the very worst. I suggest you go in expecting exactly that.

messages.root.agentsays.text: I really hate Blood Raiders…

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Upon speaking with Isha again, I have learned that the CPF investigation team is chasing up their only lead; a fragment of an intercepted transmission that suggests the culprits are in a nullsec system starting with “KF” and with a Z and E in the name. Isha wants me to fool them into thinking the system is KFIE-Z, the Blood Raiders HQ. From what he describes, the task will not be an easy one. I am told to expect the “very worst” of the Covenant given their silence, which Isha tells me is not a good sign.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Failure is not an option, {[character]player.name}. I will find someone else.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Refusal is unacceptable, I will find someone else. Goodbye {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: It is not unheard of for Blood Raider vessels to stray into State space. Having something of a relationship with the Guristas in the north, the Covenant has erected various safe havens for members who make the long journey up to Venal through Caldari space.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I managed to secure the Blood Raider Facility and safely deliver the Nugoeihuvi signal operators to the Communications Tower. Isha tells me that they have already begun their work transmitting the misleading intelligence to the CPF investigation team. We should be in the clear now. He also expressed a desire for me to meet one of his friends when I am ready for more work.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Misdirection, then. Good. This will give you a chance to appreciate how we often like to approach problems here in Nugoeihuvi.

Hmm, very well, {[character]player.name}. Try not to lose your ship out there; your crew would not like their new masters.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The CPF investigation team is in Onirvura because of some intel – intel I believe we can manipulate. I have learned that they partially decrypted a communication between my people here and our blueprint buyers in KFR-ZE. Fortunately for us, they couldn't fully decipher the location we were transmitting to, so all they know is that this area is where the transmission originated and that the destination system started with KF and has a Z and E in its name.

Your assignment is to secure a nearby Blood Raider facility and safely deliver our own signal operators to the Communications Tower inside. They will use it to transmit fake intelligence to the CPF team, and hopefully, lead them to KFIE-Z.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
I heard you tore them apart, {[character]player.name}. I can't say I'm surprised, either by their presence or by their swift disappearance at your hands. You are a constant reminder of why I should bother with the hassle of enlisting capsuleers.

I've received word from the operators that the comms tower is onlining now. They'll begin transmitting shortly. It looks like we're in the clear. Excellent news, I'm sure you'll agree.

When you feel up to it, I still had someone I wanted you to meet, now that our first order of business is finally settled.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
It sounds like Sinas is on to something. I want you there to help him in any way you can. He's headed back to his post in Astoh, so you're off to Black Rise to meet him, {[character]player.name}. If you've never been there, then you should know that it can be a dangerous place; the leadership of the Federation's capsuleer militia has set its sights on nothing less than total Gallentean occupation of the region. An absurd goal, but they're welcome to try.

From the sounds of it, Sinas will need you for something around there. My advice would be to start by flying an interceptor or frigate down that way. If on the off chance he needs you to do some heavy lifting, then you can go back for something larger. My impression is that he'll want speed and discretion here though; if it was something a fleet of Ravens could hit he'd have handled it with his own crew already.

Anyhow, fly out there, see what's up, and keep in mind what I told you about him. If you can trust me, you should trust him.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Isha is sending me off to meet Sinas in person and handle whatever work he has for me. He advised me to bring a small vessel there, suspecting that the work ahead of me will rely on speed and discretion.

messages.root.agentsays.text: You should see Sinas as soon as possible.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Fine. I will find someone else. You disappoint me {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Fine. I will find someone else. You disappoint me {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: A cursory glance at the Black Rise region reveals a great deal to those with even the most basic understanding of Caldari internal politics. Kaalakiota, Lai Dai and Wiyrkomi led the charge in colonization, each flanked by their private security forces. Supplemented by the Caldari Navy, the State War Academy and Caldari Constructions, the colonization has all the hallmarks of a Patriot faction power play.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I was sent by Isha to personally meet Sinas in the system of Astoh, Black Rise, where he is currently deployed with the Navy. I managed to find my way to his compound and discuss the work ahead of us.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Don't let my friend down out there, {[character]player.name}. You're representing us both.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
It sounds like Sinas is on to something. I want you there to help him in any way you can. He's headed back to his post in Astoh, so you're off to Black Rise to meet him.

From the sounds of it, Sinas will need you for something around there. My advice would be to start by flying an interceptor or frigate down that way. If on the off chance he needs you to do some heavy lifting, then you can go back for something larger. My impression is that he'll want speed and discretion here though; if it was something a fleet of Ravens could hit he'd have handled it with his own crew already.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
As I mentioned before, there was someone I wanted you to meet. I'm afraid I can't do it myself; he and I must be careful not to be associated with one another. This is not for any good reason, {[character]player.name}, it is simply the way our judgmental world works. A Caldari Navy officer of his kind cannot afford the rumors that a friendship with me brings. You will learn though, in time, how little truth there is to them. You've already shown a great capacity to see through the surface of things, to the heart. You wouldn't be here still if that wasn't the case.

My friend's name is Sinas Egassuo. He is a man in a similar position to me, working quietly in the engine room, seeking results, not glory. He too, works as an Advisor, and almost every important operation undertaken by our Navy in the last decade bears his imprint. You will hear talk of Caldari patriots in your time in the State, and doubtless already have. This man is a living definition of one.

You will find him somewhere around {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, just look for the Caldari Navy compound in the system, and be careful. He may not be known and loved by the Caldari people, but the leadership of the Gallente Navy is well acquainted with him and his work, and has long wanted him dead. His outfit deals with assassins and bounty hunters on a daily basis. Expect nothing less when you find the compound.

Oh, and if his surname seems familiar that's because you've probably met his sister. She works as a capsuleer liaison for the Navy's Command Division in Motsu. I wouldn't mention anything about her though; sisters are a sore spot for him.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: You have reached the Nugoeihuvi Corporation Advisory Office, Poinen. No-one is available to take your call at this moment. Please try again later.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Isha expressed a desire for me to meet someone in his stead; a Caldari Navy officer who he tells me is some kind of high-ranking, behind-the-scenes operative. His name is Sinas Egassuo, apparently the brother of Toras, a well-known Commander in Motsu. It appears that Isha and Sinas cannot be seen associating with one another, thanks to the so-called “rumors” that follow Isha around.

messages.root.agentsays.text: You have reached the Nugoeihuvi Corporation Advisory Office, Poinen. No-one is available to take your call at this moment. Please try again later.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ah, a capsuleer, are you? Fortunate.

I am Kandus Sandar, the Ministry of Internal Order officer in charge of Pirate Affairs in this area. Under normal circumstances, I would send you to one of our many agents for proper work, but I have a special task for you .

I am waiting for one of my investigators. He is now several hours overdue in delivering his reports. Fly out to his last known location. Despite whatever you may find there, I need those reports.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Kandus Sandar's investigator is missing.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Your story matches these reports. Sansha activity is on the rise. The Sansha that frequent this region are usually nothing more than opportunists, salvaging for parts and human life wherever they can find it.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: That is unfortunate. I was expecting you to finish this for me.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I suppose I can't blame you. Tracking down a truant employee is not the most exciting work.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: The Sansha ambushed and destroyed an MIO investigator.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
I would fly out there, but a capsuleer like yourself will have less trouble should you encounter any complications. Plus, if you do encounter danger, you at least have a pod to save you. I do not have that luxury.

I have uploaded the location of the last communique to your NeoCom. Head over there immediately. I cannot have more delays.

messages.mission.briefing.text: I am waiting for one of my investigators. He is now several hours overdue in delivering his reports. I need someone to fly out to his last known location. Despite whatever you may find there, I need those reports.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: A Sansha ambush is disturbing. The Sansha that frequent this region are usually nothing more than rampaging drones, salvaging for parts and human life wherever they can find it. But an attack on my investigator implies purpose.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: These reports suggest that a group of Sansha's Nation ships were seen heading for a listening outpost owned by one Lord Touraj Miyan, a local Holder. The Sansha must have killed my agent to prevent this information from getting out. Head over to the outpost and give the Sansha a surprise.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: A listening outpost owned by Lord Miyan is under attack.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Are you giving up so easily?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: What are risks to a capsuleer like you?

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: The Sansha attempted to destroy an outpost owned by Lord Touraj Miyan.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Remember, destroy any and all Sansha. We don't want any escaping this fight.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A group of Sansha's Nation ships are attacking a listening outpost owned by Lord Touraj Miyan. Head to the outpost and stop them from destroying that outpost. I will retrieve logs from the fight from your ship's computer once you return.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I've taken the liberty of examining your ship's logs. That outpost was unmanned, in disrepair, and not particularly valuable. There's no reason a group of marauders would attack it. There must be something more.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
This needs to be taken care of quickly, {[character]player.name}. Another group of Sansha's Nation ships has launched an attack. This time, they targeted a slave convoy belonging to - take a guess - Lord Touraj Miyan.

However, we've got word that an unusual ship joined the Sansha in the attack. The transmission cut off before we could get concrete details on who or what it was, but I'm willing to bet it's the commander of the bunch. The fleet is large, but should be a non-issue for a capsuleer.

Stop the Sansha and their commander.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Sansha are attacking a slave convoy. Their commander is present.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: How could you let them get away?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: How could you refuse me? After all this?

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: The Sansha were driven away from one of Miyan's slave convoys, but the commander escaped.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Get to it.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A Sansha's Nation fleet attacked a slave convoy belonging to Touraj Miyan. Their commander may be present at the conflict. Your primary object is to discover the identity of their commander and destroy him.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good job, but it's not over yet. I've got a lock on the commander that ran away.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Okay, we have his location. Follow the bookmark and take him down.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: The Sansha commander is on the run.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Do you have the commander yet?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: No! We were so close to catching him!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: We're so close to getting this guy and you quit now?

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: The commander escaped, aided by a third party flying Amarr ships.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: You handle the commander, I'll figure out how the Sansha are getting past our defenses.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Chase down the Sansha commander.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I can't believe the commander got away again! Who was flying those Amarr ships? And where did that gate come from?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We need to get to the bottom of this. Those Amarr ships came from somewhere and someone.

I can't do the legwork myself. My MIO clearance can open a lot of doors, but there's too much red tape for me to jump through. You, however, can do what I can't. You can break this thing wide open.

You need to talk to someone with both a knowledge of the Sansha and local connections. Luckily, I have just such a contact: Aralin Jick.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Kandus recommends you speak with Aralin Jick in Nishah.

messages.root.agentsays.text: You'll find Jick in the Nishah system. Follow his lead. Empress be with you.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You're giving up the chase now?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You're giving up the chase now?

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: You met Aralin Jick, your local contact.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
He has a rather intimate knowledge of Sansha's Nation. I'll let him decide if he wants to share the details with you.

Since he works directly for the Kor-Azor Family, he is in a position to do more digging in the area than I can, and he'll step on toes if necessary.

Just remember: Whoever is leading these Sansha is targeting a Holder. There aren't many people we can trust, so be diligent.

messages.mission.briefing.text: We need to get to the bottom of this. You can break this thing wide open. You need to talk to someone with both a knowledge of the Sansha and has local connections. Luckily, I have just such a contact: Aralin Jick.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Sandar sent you, eh? He probably sent you to me to keep an eye on me as much as anything else.  Did he tell you my history? No, of course not. I'm going to help you anyway, because despite whatever Sandar thinks, I want the Sansha gone.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Sansha's Nation is targeting Touraj Miyan. Why? Miyan is a fool, yes, but the Sansha are unlikely to care about an ineffectual noble. The other Holders, however, are sharks. They can smell weakness. Miyan already lost about half of his domains back in YC 110. The Holders are just circling, waiting for their chance to take another bite.

If it wasn't for the efforts of Lord Miyan's staff, he'd be dead already. His current security chief, Riff Hebian, is a smart but skeptical man, and difficult to sway. Head over to Miyan's manor and convince Hebian that the Sansha are targeting Miyan directly. His help and trust would be invaluable.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Riff Hebian isn't going to believe me. A capsuleer, however....

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Aralin Jick wants you to convince Riff Hebian of the Sansha threat.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Disappointing.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Very well. Go find someone else to bother then.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Even though many Holder titles extend back thousands of years, the position is a precarious one. Families waxed and waned over the centuries. Most families realize the rule of fools is inevitable; all they can do is hope too much damage isn't done before a proper ruler can ascend again.

House Miyan has ruled much of the Jatari constellation for centuries. Miyan grew to be one of the top Holder houses, rivaling Kor-Azor in local influence. In 109, Lord Miyan died and passed his title to his only son, Touraj Miyan.

Touraj is considered a dolt, accused of being more likely to make a pass at subordinate Holders' wives than realize his chief advisor is dipping into senility. Lord Iraj Darabi, a minor but well-respected neighboring Holder, used Touraj's unpopularity and foolishness to his own advantage. In 110, he annexed two of the systems under House Miyan control for himself, sparking a minor conflict between the two Houses.

In the end, Darabi's superior commanders and advisors forced Miyan to surrender. So far, Miyan has managed to hold on to his remaining lands.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: An opportune attack by the Sansha convinced Security Chief Riff Hebian that Lord Miyan was the target of their attacks.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent.

messages.mission.briefing.text: The Sansha attacks are obviously targeted at Touraj Miyan. Riff Hebian, Miyan's chief of security, is smart but skeptical. Head to Miyan's manor in Nebian and convince Hebian of the threat.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: The Sansha attacked? The Empress' grace is upon us, friend. If we weren't going to kill every one of them, I'd give whoever ordered that Sansha attack a medal.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Touraj Miyan has a lot of people who hate him. They want him dead, want his land, or just want to embarrass him. Some of these people are more powerful than others. It will take a while to investigate them all.

First up is Lady Temari Jariza. Among Holders, she's a nobody. She doesn't even technically own any land holdings, just a small, floating citadel in Amdonen granted to her five-times-great grandfather for exceptional service in putting down a rebellion.

Unlike her ancestors, Lady Jariza actually has ambitions. Unfortunately for her, she's not taken very seriously. She's attempted to improve her standing through most of the common channels, ranging from patronage to marriage. She's even tried to court Lord Miyan numerous times, but she has thus far been unsuccessful. It's for this reason that she's on the suspect list. She has motive, but I need to know if she's had the means and opportunity.

I need you to hack the encrypted communications array in her territory. This should provide you with logs of all the communications and transactions in recent weeks. Bring these logs back to me.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Lady Jariza was once rejected by Lord Miyan. Her communications array may hide signs of a revenge plot.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you retrieved those logs from the communications array yet?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You couldn't do it? I thought you were made of sterner stuff.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Stopping Sansha's Nation is the utmost priority. If you have a weak stomach, I think you should look elsewhere.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Lady Jariza, a minor Holder who was rejected by Lord Miyan for political marriage, has been courting Lord Darabi in recent months.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Lady Jariza may be a minor noble, but she can still afford a small army. Don't mess with her guards directly unless you want a needless fight on your hands.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The first suspect is Lady Temari Jariza. She doesn't even technically own any land holdings, just a small, floating citadel in Amdonen.

I need you to hack the encrypted communications array in her territory. This should provide you with logs of all the communications and transactions in recent weeks. Bring these logs back to me.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Let me look over these logs.

Strange. There's a lot of chatter between Lady Jariza and Lord Darabi, another local Holder. Been a lot of money transactions from him, too. Although Lord Darabi is a rival of Miyan, there's nothing here that appears sinister. Most likely Lady Jariza has merely given up on courting Miyan and is trying for the next titled family.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I have a few contacts in Lord Darabi's territory. Maybe something will turn up with this Jariza connection, but I doubt it.

I've learned of a more pressing lead for you. Remember those Amarr ships you ran into? It seems that one Lord Manik has been shopping around for mercenaries.

I'm giving you the meeting location I found while innocently perusing Manik's records. There should be a mercenary contact. You're going to find out who they are, and then we're going to wipe them out. I'll have more instructions when you reach the site.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Has the deal happened? What's going on?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: You are to stake out a meeting between Lord Manik's people and mercenaries.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: We didn't even get to the blowing-stuff-up part.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You're backing out now? I can't believe you'd do that.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Aralin Jick suspects the Amarr ships you encountered were mercenaries hired by Lord Manik. You successfully tracked the mercenaries back to their camp.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good luck. I'll contact you remotely when you're done.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Remember those Amarr ships you ran into? It seems that one Lord Manik has been shopping around for mercenaries.

I'm giving you the meeting location I found while innocently perusing Manik's records. There should be a mercenary contact. You're going to find out who they are, and then we're going to wipe them out. I'll have more instructions when you reach the site.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I've got a lock on the contact. I know where he's going.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: I'm sending you the mercenary's coordinates. This should be the base they've been operating out of. Wipe them out. Leave no opportunity to rebuild.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: You know the location of the mercenary camp.

messages.root.agentsays.text: How fare our mercenary friends?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Killing mercs isn't even morally objectionable!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Killing mercs isn't even morally objectionable!

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: You severely ruined the mercenaries' day.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: They're not Sansha, but popping mercs will do in a pinch.

messages.mission.briefing.text: I've got the coordinates to the mercenary camp. Tear down everything you find. Time to ruin someone's day.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I wish I was there. Looking at the damage estimates, I bet that gang will never be able to rebuild.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ah, the famous {[character]player.name}. Welcome! I don't get to mingle with an egger every day, so it's an honor to finally meet you face to face -- or close enough to it anyways.

I assume you've come to help with my next holoreel project here at Impetus? Yes, well, quite a few setbacks already, I'm afraid. As someone like you might appreciate, I didn't fully understand what I was getting into when I decided to film everything in space. Things have become a little more difficult than I expected. We could really use an experienced capsuleer like you to keep everything on track. Frankly, I don't know why we didn't consider the option sooner.

If you're able to help out, then your first task would be to investigate a possible filming location. We're not expecting any major problems, but after an accident last week scouting a similar location, I'd rather have these matters handled by someone who really knows what they're doing. I don't suppose you'd be free and willing to scout the area?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I met with Gian Perele, an Impetus holoreel director. His next project involves filming scenes in space, and so he needs the help of a pilot like me. I've been offered a job scouting out one of their shooting locations and making sure it will be safe for them to move in.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Any new information on the site?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: No problem, {[character]player.name}. I understand how precious an egger's time can be. Thank you for trying, in any case.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I understand, {[character]player.name}. Thanks for taking the time to listen, at least, and if you see anyone else in your travels who might be able to help, let me know.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Impetus is the main producer of holoreels in New Eden, creating anything from epic historical movies to cheap porn flicks. Their cadre of established directors alone number in the tens of thousands; the actors they employ are literally countless. On one hand, the near infinite nature of their resources allows for the production of many risky, experimental holoreel projects, and yet at the same time, it is all too easy for an aspiring holoreel actress to get lost among a thousand other beautiful faces.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I met with Gian Perele, an Impetus holoreel director. His next project involves filming scenes in space, and so he asked for my assistance. I accepted a job scouting out one of his team's shooting locations. The place was swarming with rogue drones, and I also noticed a gang of Minmatar pilots in combat cruisers loitering a good distance away. Gian figures them for vagrants and doesn't seem worried. It looks like his crew is going to head in and start filming there soon.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I appreciate you stepping in to help us out. I'll talk with accounting about sorting out some pay for your troubles; that shouldn't be a problem. I'll leave my comms link open; once you've scouted the area and it's safe to proceed, get back in touch with me.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Your first task is to investigate a possible filming location. We're not expecting any major problems, but after an accident last week scouting a similar location, I'd rather have these matters handled by someone who really knows what they're doing. I'll leave my comms link open; once you've scouted the area and it's safe to proceed, get back in touch with me.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Rogue drones and Minmatar, eh? Hmm. Yes, well, I've heard rumors, but I thought that was all just a scary tale to keep people out of there. The place has a history, you see. That's partly why we wanted to film there in the first place, and probably what made those Minnie vagrants think it was a safe place to squat. I suppose we can shoot the area from certain angles to exclude the damn drone hive, but I'll have to check it out myself. At least we can proceed with that, thanks to your good work.

There's a few other favors I'd ask of you, {[character]player.name}, if you're still free. Get back to me if you're interested.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
The shining star in this holoreel project of mine is a fairly high profile individual, as you might expect. His name is Ralie Ardanne; the son of a low-profile Senator. He's a real knockout at fourteen years old, and he already has a budding endorsements empire with all the major clothing labels. Now he's looking to expand into holoreels, which is where Impetus comes in. 
His parents have prospered from senatorial life, and they spared no expense on Ralie's cosmetic enhancements. It shows too: He really makes a mark in the 12-16 year old female demographic. Of course, a boy his age and with his connections shouldn't be travelling the spacelanes unguarded. I was hoping you'd be interested in meeting him at his father's senatorial residence? It wouldn't be every day you get to see a place like that, {[character]player.name}, even as an egger. What do you say?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Gian has hired someone high profile to star in his next holoreel. His name is Ralie Ardanne, and he's the son of a Senator (and apparently a successful young model). I've been asked to fly over to the Ardenne senatorial residence and escort the kid back to the set.

messages.root.agentsays.text: You should go meet Ralie; the senatorial staff are expecting your visit.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: How disappointing. I actually expected better from you, {[character]player.name}. I'm afraid I won't be able to offer you any further work.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Really? Huh, ok then {[character]player.name}. Safe travels, and thanks for all the time you spared.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Gian started by explaining to me that he'd hired a high profile child model to star in his next holoreel. The kid's name is Ralie Ardanne, and he's the son of a Senator. When I arrived at the senatorial residence, the place was in tatters. Most of the security had been disabled, and  I saw the same group Gian mistook for vagrants -- the Minmatar calling themselves the Pator 6 -- hovering around Ralie's ship before it was boarded. Gian tells me that Impetus would like me to head up the investigation and recovery effort.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I will tell Ralie's guardian that you're on the way to pick him up. Let me know when you've arrived.

messages.mission.briefing.text: The shining star in this holoreel project of mine is a fairly high profile individual, as you might expect. His name is Ralie Ardanne, and he's the son of a low-profile Senator. He's looking to expand his already vast popularity into holoreels, which is where Impetus comes in. Of course, a boy his age and with his connections shouldn't be travelling the spacelanes unguarded. I was hoping you would be interested in meeting him at his father's senatorial residence. I'll let Ralie's guardians know that you are on the way to pick him up. Let me know when you've arrived.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: The Federation authorities have asked for your continued assistance, under the provisional direction of Impetus. I'm not sure if you were interested in sticking with us, {[character]player.name}, but we could use the help. Let me know if you're interested.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We've hit upon a lead for you to follow, {[character]player.name}. Our proximity to the Amarr border attracts just the sort of criminals who might have masterminded this terrible act. People smugglers, pimps, slaveholders: There are all sorts of dark corners in the Elalan constellation, with darker motives strewn throughout these recesses.

There's a place not far from here in the Averon system known as “The Exchange.” It's a hangout for lowlifes and criminals, a real nasty place. After talking with some friends in The Scope they pointed us in that direction. Seems this Minmatar crew -- the Pator 6 -- is known around these parts for raiding unwary travelers.

Your assignment is a dangerous one, {[character]player.name}. You will need to fly into the trading hub and see if there are any further leads. Maybe even one of those Minmatar gang members is still flying around. Are you up to the task?

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you managed to investigate the Averon Exchange yet, {[character]player.name}?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Gian has spoken with The Scope and learned that the Pator 6 gang that kidnapped Ralie will likely be found at a people-smuggling hub in nearby Averon system. I've been asked to investigate the area and find what leads I can.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Fine, but don't expect me to count on you again in the future.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Then I suppose this is where we part {[character]player.name}. Thanks for the help you contributed; here's hoping I can still salvage this holoreel.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Averon lies just a few jumps out from the Genesis border, and the intermingling of Gallente and Amarr cultures is evident on the system's station. Curiously, the station is a Caldari facility with a typically Caldari reputation for unscrupulousness. It's a melting pot of dark, cultural undertones, from the Gallente with their unrestrained hedonism, to the Caldari with their lust for ISK, and even Amarr slavers, ever keen to make some quick money selling captives and other tortured souls.

Although the cultural might of the Federation has influenced the bordering systems in the Genesis region, the reverse is also true, if lesser known. Catering to the endless hunger for flesh that exists in certain Gallente circles, the Amarr slavers have few qualms or problems smuggling people a little way inside Federation borders. It has been said that some of the Federation's most depraved nightclubs and bars can be found in the systems where cheap slaves are only a few jumps away.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: After following a lead given to us by The Scope, I investigated a smuggling trade hub known as the Averon Exchange. Some members of the Pator 6 warband that kidnapped Ralie tried to ambush me. Despite destroying their ships, I wasn't able to recover any information about where Ralie might be now. Gian has been asked to hand the matter over to his superiors, who he can refer me to, if I'm interested.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I had a feeling I could count on you. I'm giving you the coordinates now. Good luck out there.

messages.mission.briefing.text: We've hit upon a lead for you to follow. There's a place not far from here in the Averon system known as “The Exchange.” It's a hangout for lowlifes and criminals, a real nasty place. After talking with some friends in The Scope, they pointed us in that direction. Seems this Minmatar crew -- the Pator 6 -- is known around these parts for raiding unwary travelers. You would need to fly into the trading hub and see if you could find any further leads, and hopefully even locate one of those Minmatar gang members. Are you up to the task?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I've spoken with my superiors, and they'd like me to hand this matter off to them now. I am only a low-level holoreel director, after all. You'd be better advised by people who have some experience with these matters. Let me know if you're ok with that, and I'll get the ball rolling.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I'm glad to see that you're willing to stick around with us on this, {[character]player.name}. The person I've been instructed to refer you to is our Regional Director. I don't have his current location, but I can put you in touch with one of his secretaries. You can find her at Impetus offices in Stetille, Planet 2.

I can tell them you're on the way, if you think you have time to make the appointment?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I've been asked to speak with the Regional Director for Impetus about the kidnapping of Ralie Ardanne. If I want to find him, I'll first have to meet with one of his secretaries at the Impetus offices in Stetille.

messages.root.agentsays.text: They're waiting for you at Stetille, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Don't worry, I'm sure I can find someone else to continue your good work. Thank you for your assistance, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I understand. I'm sure I can find someone else to continue your good work. Thank you for your assistance, {[character]player.name}.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Gian Parele asked me to speak with the Regional Director for Impetus about the kidnapping of the Ralie Ardanne. I met with one of his secretaries at the Impetus offices in Stetille, who gave me the coordinates of his personal office complex.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you.

messages.mission.briefing.text: The person I've been instructed to refer you to is our Regional Director. I don't have his current location, but I can put you in touch with one of his secretaries.  You can find her at Impetus offices in Stetille, Planet 2.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Welcome to Stetille, {[character]player.name}. My name is Eron Viette. Gian said you'd been invaluable to us recently, so if there is any way I can further assist you, please let me know.

I understand that you're seeking a meeting with our Sinq Laison Regional Director. That would be Mr. Roire, Audalle Roire. He spends most of his time at our space-bound office complex here in Stetille. I'm afraid he's not very fond of the media, and since they have free docking access to any of our publicly listed stations, you can most often guess he won't be in any of them.

I'll patch the coordinates to the offices if you like?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Eron Viette, the assistant to the Sinq Laison Regional Director, has offered to put me in touch with the Director, Audalle Roire. I'm told I can find him at their space-bound offices, if I am interested.

messages.root.agentsays.text: you found Regional Director Roire?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: No problem, {[character]player.name}. On behalf of Impetus, we're grateful for what help you could give us already.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: course, not a problem. On behalf of Impetus, let me thank you for your time so far

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I met with Audalle Roire, the Sinq Laison Regional Director for Impetus. His assistant, Eron Viette, told me where I could find him. As soon as I arrived at his offices, we were ambushed by another pack of Pator 6 combat vessels, who I can only guess followed me to the location. I secured the area, but the Director didn't seem too pleased. He has referred me back to Eron, who can help me now that the Director is aware of what I'm after.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Very well, here they are. If you have any trouble finding him out there, just look for the Luxury Yacht on your scanner.

messages.mission.briefing.text: I understand that you're seeking a meeting with our Sinq Laison Regional Director. That would be Mr. Roire, Audalle Roire. He spends most of his time at our space-bound office complex here in Stetille. I'm afraid he's not very fond of the media, and since they have free docking access to any of our publicly-listed stations, you can most often guess he won't be in any of them. If you have any trouble finding him out there, just look for the Luxury Yacht on your scanner.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You did well out there, {[character]player.name}. Don't worry too much about the Matari that followed you, they seem to know a thing or two about surveillance.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: After making the sale in Syndicate, I contacted Katsen Isha once more. He told me that Hyasyoda had launched an investigation into our raid on the facility. I committed myself to stopping the Corporate Police Force investigation before it could uncover anything.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
{[character]player.name}, good. I hope you've recovered from the Syndicate trip. Once again, good work out there. Unfortunately, it turns out we have one more loose end to tie up.

My people tell me that Hyasyoda have already launched an investigation into theformula theft. I suppose this is a play to lend an air of legitimacy to the racket they've been running. The situation is an amusing one, yet also dangerous for us. Our tracks are well covered, but – as they often say at Hyasyoda itself – only the paranoid survive.

They've deployed their security wing, the Corporate Police Force, into “various locations of interest.” I've learned that Onirvura was listed as an area to investigate. They're right here in the constellation, setting up a temporary base for interrogation and imprisonment. Fortunately for us, the CPF has hired a mercenary crew to handle facility defense while they set up. This gives us an opportunity to strike at them without it constituting a direct attack on Hyasyoda personnel. That would muddy the waters a bit, as I'm sure you can appreciate. Mercs or not, though, they're getting a little too close for comfort.

I should mention also that we can still resolve this peacefully too, if you prefer. The intel that has brought them here can be manipulated, perhaps, and lead them elsewhere. I care very little about how you want us to proceed, as long as this situation is dealt with. I want to go to sleep tonight knowing our assets and our reputations are safe.

{[character]player.name}, good. I hope you've recovered from the Syndicate trip. Once again, good work out there. Unfortunately, it turns out we have one more loose end to tie up.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: After making the sale in Syndicate, I contacted Katsen Isha once more. He tells me that Hyasyoda has launched an investigation into our raid on the facility. I must stop the Corporate Police Force investigation before it can uncover anything. Isha says we can either simply kill the mercenaries defending their base of operations or else fool them into thinking the culprits are elsewhere, far away from Poinen.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Excuse me! Can I trouble you for a minute? Impetus needs your help with our next holoreel. Can you go meet with one of our directors? If you do a good enough job, I'm sure we can get you in the credits for that reel. You can find him over in Tolle. Look for the studio we have set up in that system. The director is probably in his luxurious pleasure cruiser. You know, the holoreel lifestyle can be really difficult sometimes.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I am supposed to meet with Gian Parele, an Impetus holoreel director in Tolle. Apparently, he has some business suitable for a capsuleer. I can't imagine what it could be.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you met with Gian yet?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I guess the glamour and allure of holoreels is not for everyone. The universe needs miners, too, you know.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Fair enough. I'm sure I can find some other capsuleer interested in becoming a star.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Impetus needs my help, and I met with one of their holoreel directors. He has some important work for me. There's no telling what they would need a capsuleer for, but it had better be good. Or at least I'd better meet a holoreel star or two.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Don't ask me what the title of the project is. I'm not allowed to divulge that. But let's just say it'll be epic.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Impetus needs your help with our next holoreel. Can you go meet with one of our directors? If you do a good enough job, I'm sure we get you in the credits for that reel. You can find him over in Tolle. Look for the studio we have set up in that system. The director is probably in his pleasure yacht. You know, the holoreel lifestyle can be really difficult sometimes.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I see. Let's discuss that option, then.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I continued my efforts on Hyasyoda's behalf to uncover what Nugoeihuvi is up to. Isha was keen to have me shift the formula far away from his vicinity. I had to choose between taking it all the way out to one of their nullsec offices in Syndicate or to a bordering lowsec system in Solitude.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Welcome back, {[character]player.name}. I hope your time has been well spent considering our options.

Hyasyoda seems to have calmed down a little for now, but it's when they get quiet that I actually start to worry. They likely already have something in motion. I'm not interested in seeing if my instincts are right. We should shift these formulas as soon as possible.

As I told you before, I've already lined up a buyer for us. All you need to do is move the goods. As I also explained, my associates – that is, the ones with an interest in highly illegal booster manufacture – they're stationed at a somewhat remote NOH office outside of CONCORD jurisdiction, where the Chief Executive Panel finds it difficult to keep a close eye on everything.

Ideally, I would like you to deliver the goods to our facility in KFR-ZE yourself, but I can make arrangements for the staff at KFR to retrieve it from a nearby low-security system if you prefer. That will, of course, reduce your cut of the profits. If you can fly a Covert Ops or an Interceptor or anything like that, then I would recommend you make use of it now, but how you proceed in light of this situation is up to you. All I want is for the sale to be made soon; I don't care how.

Hyasyoda seems to have calmed down a little for now, but it's when they get quiet that I actually start to worry. They likely already have something in motion. I'm not interested in seeing if my instincts are right, though. We should shift these formulas as soon as possible.

As I told you before, I've already lined up a buyer for us. All you need to do is move the goods. As I also explained, my associates – that is, the ones with an interest in highly illegal booster manufacture – they're stationed at a somewhat remote NOH office outside of CONCORD jurisdiction, where the Chief Executive Panel finds it difficult to keep a close eye on everything.

Ideally, I would like you to deliver the goods to our facility in KFR-ZE yourself, but I can make arrangements for the staff at KFR to retrieve it from a nearby low-security system if you prefer. That will, of course, reduce your cut of the profits. If you can fly a Covert Ops or an Interceptor, anything like that, then I would recommend you make use of it now. How you proceed in light of this situation is up to you though. All I want is for the sale to be made soon; I don't care how.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: On the instructions of Arikio Kuretsu, I returned to Katsen Isha. He seems to have noticed a change in Hyasyoda's operations, but doesn't appear to suspect me personally of anything. Isha would like me to take the formula sheets all the way out to Syndicate, a fairly dangerous journey but no doubt the most lucrative. The second option isn't much safer, but Isha has let me know that – if I desire – I can take it only to the border of Syndicate and his people will do the rest. That would let me avoid the nullsec systems.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
With the destruction of the mercenary camp, Lord Manik is denying he ever had any contact with them. I have a copy of your ship's logs from their meeting, but it may prove difficult to pin him with any conspiracy charges.

Good thing I've got a new lead. Remember Lord Darabi, Miyan's rival and the new target of Jariza's wooing? His daughter, Mina, has been one of my contacts. Mina says she has key information, but she will only tell me in person.

This is where the fun part comes in. Daddy Darabi has kept Mina under tight surveillance because of a scandal that happened a few years ago. Thus, we have to stage a kidnapping. This is going to get bloody, but I trust Mina when she says her information is worth it.

Fly to the Darabi estate where Mina is being kept and "kidnap" Mina Darabi. Any guards are expendable.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Where's Mina?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Mina Darabi has information on the Sansha investigation, but must be rescued from her father's estate.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Lord Darabi's forces were too much for me. I've got to quit your mission.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: What have I been paying you for?

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Rumor has it that Lord Darabi was imprisoned by Karsoth for daring to publicly disagree (albeit slightly) with Karsoth's policies about the Succession. When Empress Sarum returned, Darabi was freed, but rumors persist that  he is not in the most stable condition.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Mina Darabi, Aralin Jick's contact and the daughter of Lord Darabi, was successfully retrieved in your violent "kidnapping."

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Lord Darabi's manor is in the Reteka system. Do what you must.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Daddy Darabi has kept Mina under tight surveillance because of a  scandal that occurred a few years ago. Thus, we have to stage a kidnapping. This is going to get bloody, but I trust Mina when she says her information is worth it. Fly to the Darabi estate where Mina is being kept and "kidnap" Mina Darabi. Any guards are expendable.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
If everything Mina says is true, then we're not going to blow this case wide open.

We're going to blow it up.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Mina has quite a story to tell. Jariza has been courting Lord Darabi for some time. Jariza's been so good at winning Darabi's trust that Mina became suspicious. Mina proved an amazing spy: She's not only traced funds flowing from Darabi to Jariza, but she also found an interesting communication from one Rahsa Teff.

Rahsa Teff is a known felon and former Blood Raider. The MIO lost track of him a year ago. Rumor was another pirate group poached him. It sounds as if the rumor is true. Not only is Rahsa Teff with the Sansha, but you met him already. He's the Sansha commander who kept eluding us.

I've traced the source of Rahsa's message. We know where he and the Sansha are located. Let's end this. Eliminate the Sansha base, and capture Rahsa Teff.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Mina has revealed the location of Rahsa Teff, the Sansha commander who has continuously eluded capture.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Where is Rahsa Teff? Has the Sansha base been eliminated?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: What do you mean he got away? Get out of my sight!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I don't understand. You've come this far, why are you backing out now? Bah, I don't have time for this! Get out of my sight.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Mina Darabi revealed that Jariza funneled money from Lord Darabi and was in contact with Rahsa Teff, the Sansha commander. You judiciously eliminated the Sansha base and captured Teff.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Once you eliminate the base, the Sansha will be without a central hub in this region.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Thanks to Mina's information, we've discovered the location of the Sansha base and Rahsa Teff. Destroy the Sansha base and capture Rahsa Teff, and the Sansha will fall back into their pattern of mindless aggression.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
You've eliminated the Sansha base? Excellent!

Now the question remains: What do we do with Rahsa Teff?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Hang on just a second. They must have changed socket sizes….

There. I present you one decoy Rahsa. Not a bad piece of work, if I do say so myself. Whoever Rahsa's friends were, they're probably looking for our departed Sansha right now. This device will mimic Rahsa's personal frequency: Just plug it in to a broadcast tower and you've got yourself an escapee Rahsa. Or the next best thing.

There's the perfect broadcast tower in Shaha. Place the homemade Sansha beacon in the tower, and then wait to see if "rescue" arrives. Then blow them out of the sky.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: You possess a homemade Sansha beacon, perfect for trapping traitors.

messages.root.agentsays.text: How goes the hunt?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You're giving up?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: But my device is so awesome!

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Luring his forces into the open using the head of Rahsa, you revealed the Amarrian traitor to be Terrius Harkan, former commander of Miyan's security.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Here's hoping his friends are looking.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Whoever Rahsa's friends were, they're probably looking for our departed Sansha right now. This device will mimic Rahsa's personal frequency. Just plug it in to a broadcast tower and you have a fake escapee Rahsa.

There's the perfect broadcast tower in Shaha. Place the homemade Sansha beacon in the tower, and wait to see if "rescue" arrives. Then blow them out of the sky.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Harkan?! Terrus Harkan is the traitor? Harkan, former head of Lord Miyan's security and hero of the countless military campaigns, is the traitor?

This is very bad.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: So Rahsa has something more to say? Give my people a few minutes alone with him....

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Aralin has a plan to track down Rahsa's accomplice.

messages.root.agentsays.text: You track down those stragglers yet? They're our best shot at thecommand signal receiver.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I can't believe you're giving up. If that's the case, I suppose I must continue using my own people.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Are you really leaving? I suppose I'll have to go it alone.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Interrogating Rahsa revealed that he had help within the Amarr Empire. You retrieved a Sansha command signal receiver for Aralin's plan to capture the traitor.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
So Rahsa has something more to say? Give my people a few minutes alone with him.... ah, there's a message coming in now.

Hm. I'll be damned. You were right. Someone else was working with him. He managed to activate some sort of suicide short in his socket before we got a name out of him. Too bad for him he's still useful to us.

What I need right now is a Sansha command signal receiver. They're found on Sansha ships to keep the crew going. And I know where some survivors of your last attack are right now. Eliminate these stragglers, and I'm sure you'll find a command signal receiver among them.

messages.mission.briefing.text: What I need right now is a Sansha command signal receiver. They're found on Sansha ships to keep the crew going. And I know where some survivors of your last attack are right now. Eliminate these stragglers, and I'm sure you'll find a command signal receiver among them.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: This is exactly what I was looking for. Now, sit back and watch a master at work.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Welcome to Astoh, {[character]player.name}. I appreciate you coming by. Katsen just sent me the ISK, too. Thank you for being our middle man on that one. You may want to make yourself comfortable in that egg for a moment; I've a bit to cover here for your briefing.

As you know, my name is Sinas Egassuo. As you probably do not know, my job is to coordinate search and rescue operations, as well as the liberation of Caldari Prisoners of War taken during battle in Black Rise. This duty I have fulfilled without hesitation, and I am proud to have led such operations.

It is by carrying out this task, however, that I've come to notice something strange. Whenever we rescue people, there are often less Ishukone crew members and staff than the rest. It's never enough to be conspicuous or noticeable, but I notice it, and I find it conspicuous. I can't explain it though, and neither can the people we recover.

My suspicion is that Ishukone personnel are being taken elsewhere, perhaps being treated more kindly due to their Liberal philosophies and good history with the Gallente. It wouldn't surprise me to see the Federation trying to divide us over something like that, but we'd have to know about it first, and they don't seem keen on that happening.

I need you to investigate the matter for me and find out what's going on. I can brief you on the details of the assignment once you accept, but until I have that commitment, I'm not willing to trust you with the information. Sorry {[character]player.name}, but Katsen's recommendation only gets you so far.

So, are you committed to the fight ahead of us or not?

messages.root.agentsays.text: Get going, {[character]player.name}.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text:
After making my way to Astoh to meet Sinas, he asked for my help in making sense of something. He started by explaining that his work involves search and rescue operations, recovering Caldari P.O.Ws from Gallente Federation prison camps and similar operations. Although he can't find anyone to corroborate his claims, he seems certain that the numbers of Ishukone prisoners are frequently lower than the rest, conspicuously so.

He wants me to follow up on his hunch. My first task is to acquire a Federation Navy ID tag given out to P.O.W transports operating in Black Rise. I'll need to first secure, and then hack into a Shipyard in order to get my hands on one of these. Sinas tells me the job won't be an easy one.

messages.mission.extrainfo.header.text: New Region connected to Stargate Networks by Caldari State, Scope Article, June 11th, YC 110

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: From what Isha said about you, I didn't expect this. I guess I'll find someone else.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: From what Isha said about you, I didn't expect this. I guess I'll find someone else.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
In yet another twist in the recent events, multiple reports are coming in of new stargates appearing in systems on the fringes of Caldari and Gallente space. It would appear that the volume of space known as Black Rise - previously thought to be completely impenetrable - has been secretly colonized by Caldari forces.

Initial reports from capsuleers indicate that the new region contains a wealth of virgin systems, full of resources unexploited thus far by the four empires. Additionally, early cartography has revealed that the region opens an additional border between Caldari and Gallente sovereign space, something officials on both sides are scrambling to prepare for as they readjust strategies. Even as they do so, pod pilots both loyalist and independent are rushing into the area to stake a claim of their own.

It remains unclear exactly how the phenomena shrouding this area were penetrated, or indeed how the Caldari State has managed to colonize the area in complete secrecy. State officials have so far remained tight-lipped on any details, providing no explanations. After such startling events in recent times however, and with officials from all three Empires as well as CONCORD pushing for answers on the matter, it is something they will likely have to address in the nearby future.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Excellent.

Your first step will be to acquire a special type of security ID handed out to Federation Navy P.O.W transports operating in Black Rise. I'm uploading the coordinates of the facility where they can be found.

The target will be a shipyard that implants these ID tags on ships. First, you'll need to secure it, which may not be easy. I have reliable intelligence claiming that an initial strike on their Communications Array will mean they can't call out for reinforcements, however, so you may want to factor that in to your battle plan.

Once the area is cleared, you'll need to hack into the shipyard, so train up some basic hacking skills if you've never done so before. Even at the most basic level of training, a Data Analyzer in the hands of a capsuleer can tear most security systems into shreds, and that's all we need for this job.

In case I gave you the wrong impression earlier {[character]player.name}, this facility will be heavily defended. If you brought down a faster, smaller ship to Astoh then leave it here. We'll need it soon enough, don't worry. For now though, I suggest you arm yourself to the teeth. This won't be easy.

And that's it. Briefing over, {[character]player.name}. Good luck.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ah, hello, {[character]player.name}. I suppose you heard that I was looking for work?

Well, that was half right. I'm just an intermediary; Katsen Isha is the man you need to report to. He asked me to arrange for some extra assistance with a few jobs he has in mind.

I should warn you, though: sometimes business dealings with Isha can get a little involved. He's the typical hard-working Deteis type and will expect the same of anyone on his payroll.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I met Aursa Kunivuri, a representative of Nugoeihuvi and an intermediary for Katsen Isha. He said if I was seeking work then I should go speak with the man myself.

messages.root.agentsays.text: You're back? I thought I told you to go speak with Katsen Isha? There's nothing more I can do for you {[character]player.name}, he is the one who has the work, not me.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Ok, I'll terminate the contract now then. Thank you for the notification.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Not interested? Makes no difference to me.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The Caldari State's answer to the cultural powerhouses of the Federation, Nugoeihuvi Corporation (more commonly known as simply “NOH”) is one of the leading entertainment providers of the cluster.

Nugoeihuvi Corporation is rumored to have dealings with criminals and others of questionable moral character, although their working relationship with the real-estate giant Sukuuvestaa Corporation, for instance, has helped the company maintain at least the appearance of discretion at most times. Every day, all sorts of NOH goods flow freely to consumers across State space, frequently with little or no questions asked.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Upon the instructions of his intermediary Aursa Kunivuri, I met with Katsen Isha to discuss the possibility of future work with him and Nugoeihuvi.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Very well, {[character]player.name}. I don't have much in the way of ISK to give you, but my associates have some information that would not usually come cheap. You may find it useful when dealing with Isha. Here is a verification key, take it to the center a few kilometers from here and my subordinates will retrieve the relevant documents.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Katsen Isha, over at the Nugoeihuvi Corporation station in Poinen, is the man you need to report to. I should warn you though; sometimes business dealings with Isha can get a little involved. He's the typical hard-working Deteis type and will expect the same of anyone on his payroll.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
A visitor, and a capsuleer no less. I can tell my day is about to get more interesting.

Hello {[character]player.name}. I'm guessing you flew out here because you heard I was handing out work, right? Well, I do have something for you. Nothing amazingly difficult and nothing someone without a pod could handle easily, either. If you can pull this off, we can see about maybe getting you in on some other things. Maybe.

We Matari are known for our ingenuity. Civilization owes us a great debt, and the Amarr owe it twice over. Before they came, we were by far the most advanced nation; our technological achievements were regarded with envy by the rest of the cluster. You eggers know a lot, but did you know that?

Well, regardless of history, and regardless of your race, you will need to demonstrate an understanding of this if you want to work with us. Prove your resourcefulness by bringing me an Olfei Medallion. You will have to explore as only a capsuleer can and find one somewhere in the Sveipar constellation, near our homeworld Pator. Of course, some other egger can milk your wallet in exchange for doing the thinking and grunt work for you. That works too. Whether you scan it down inside an Angel Cartel fortress, or buy it for 2 ISK on the market - I don't really care. Results are what matter most.

You'll go far with me if you keep that in mind.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I met with a Brutor named Arsten Takalo. He seems to have some real work for me, but won't trust me with it until I can prove myself. I have been asked to acquire an “Olfei Medallion” – whatever that is – and return it to him as proof that I can handle further work.  He suggested I should be exploring around the Sveipar constellation, scanning for its location. Alternatively, if I can't find it, he suggested that he wouldn't care if I simply bought one from the markets. Apparently, results are all that matters to him, and this task is supposed to prove that.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Keep searching, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: If that's too much for you then yeah, it's best we part ways now.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: If that's too much for you then yeah, it's best we part ways now.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The fortunes of the Minmatar have ebbed and flowed continuously. At one time they had a flourishing empire with a level of mechanical excellence never before or since seen anywhere. Later, however, they had to endure centuries of enslavement, toiling and dying for the benefit of foreign masters. Today most of them have regained their freedom, but the legacy of their enslavement has been the diaspora of the race.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I met with a Brutor named Arsten Takalo. He seemed to have some real work for me, but wouldn't elaborate on it until I could prove myself. Upon his instruction, I acquired an “Olfei Medallion” and returned it to him. He seemed impressed with this, and said that if I was interested in getting started I should meet him again.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Alright then. Let's see what you got.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Now that we're past the small talk perhaps you're ready for some proper work. I guess we'll see.

There's this Gallentean guy, a historian named Aillon Boufin…yeah, I know. The story is that he's been studying Minmatar history for years now, and as you'd expect, he's come across a whole shipload of information and documents in that time. Apparently he has one of the largest unofficial collections of documents and artifacts from our earlier days. We're talking real old here, {[character]player.name}, some of it - going back to when it was just us, alone against the Amarr.

Now, I'm told that normally whenever we want to look at something of his, there aren't too many problems. Recently however, when some of our academics from the Republic University asked to see a particular document known as the Hauteker Memoirs, they were denied. Since that time, they have bent over backwards for this guy. They have even tried to buy it back - this document that Matari people wrote, this document that belongs to us. They have tried that repeatedly, raising and raising the price and yet each of these times more refusals.

This is when things got ugly. Boufin recently made a statement to the University, saying he is only trying to “preserve Minmatar heritage”. After that insult, they called us in. The implication that RU staff would somehow endanger our own history by simply studying a document...it's almost like he was trying to piss us all off.

Well, the insults stop here. The Brutor tribe has arrived, and with a capsuleer to back their word on the matter no less. It has been decided by the tribe that the return of this document to Matari hands represents a higher priority than staying on good terms with some overprotective historian, Gallente or not. You will see to this. And before you go jumping in, there is a 5m ISK collateral to cover associated risks. The tribe is not willing to risk our own property falling into foreign hands again. Perhaps you can see why we're looking to hire an egger? With that kind of money it's not really an option.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Any updates on the historian?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: It seems I've earned Arsten's trust, at least enough to be given another job…with a 5m ISK collateral. He tells me there is a Gallentean historian named Aillon Boufin who has been living in Minmatar space collecting documents for years, and  yet is now refusing to hand over a particular record to the Republic. Whatever it is, they're willing to have me kill him for it.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Huh, after the Olfei Medallion I wasn't expecting that. Very well {[character]player.name}, I suppose I'll find another egger to take over. Shouldn't be too hard to find one with 5m in my pocket…

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Ok, thanks, bye.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: For many citizens of the Minmatar Republic, the friendship with the Gallente Federation has been a costly one. Some view the recent abandonment of the parliamentary system as the most potent symbol yet that the Federation's influence hasn't always been to their benefit. Indeed, there are some Matari who view the return to a Tribal Republic as the last necessary step out from under the shadow of foreign empires. Whatever the claims may be, few deny that the relationship still has some fundamental challenges to overcome.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: It seems I earned Arsten's trust, at least enough to be given another job…with a 5m ISK collateral. He told me about a Gallentean historian named Aillon Boufin who had been living in Minmatar space collecting documents for years, and  yet was now refusing to hand over a particular record to the Republic. I was sent in to recover it, and upon my arrival Boufin immediately retaliated. I had to kill him and recover the document forcefully.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. Let's see some results, {[character]player.name}.
