messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
So things spiraled out of control in there. Don't stress it, {[character]player.name}. It was to be expected, and if it wasn't you out there, it'd be Republic Fleet vessels with clone-less crews. You did a good thing, don't doubt it for a second.

Hopefully the foreign press will let this one slide, they've got enough of us in their own borders to sit on it, but there's always a few. So long as the big outlets hold their tongues I'm happy.

Here's your ISK back, plus some extra as thanks. Don't blow it all away though, you'll be doing other work that requires collateral. I may be starting to respect you, but trust is a damn long way off. We'll need a moment to pass this on to our friends from the University, but they've asked us to hang around, and by us, they mean you.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Good thing you're still about, we'll need you again for this one.

The Republic University guys had a look over the document and it has what they're after: directions. There's a mention in one of the sections of an old Nefantar bloodline, and where they buried their dead. I'm told they're important because of some old folktale about how they buried a special type of Khumaak with one of their leaders. Pretty odd stuff, but also kinda interesting.

They're on a myth-busting mission, though, that's the thing. There is no actual Khumaak, just a bunch of old Ammatar bones, probably. Still, you go there, check it out, and then they can say in their report that the area was inspected by a capsuleer and turned up nothing. They put that together with the proof in this old book that you inspected the right area and, I dunno, write an essay about how clever they are. The important thing for me was just getting our own history back, and that's what you should remember too.

So anyways, you feel like digging up some graves? The coordinates will be 2.5m in collateral, to cover associated risks yet again. If for some crazy reason there is actually a unique Khumaak out there, it belongs in a museum, not your cargo bay. 2.5m ISK would buy a lot of museums, you see. Whatever way it goes, our history won't lose out again.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Let me know once you've inspected the site.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Arsten has asked for further help with the Republic University's historical research. Apparently the memoirs I recovered had directions to a burial site in San Matar. The site is supposed to house remains of an old Ammatar family that died out. What makes them important for us is a myth about one of their leaders being buried with some special kind of Khumaak. The RU academics want to debunk the myth, so my job is to fly out to the site and prove that it is empty.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You guys just pick things up then put 'em right back down, don't you?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You guys just pick things up then put 'em right back down, don't you?

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The Ammatars are descendants of Minmatar that collaborated with the Amarrians during the latter occupation of the Minmatar worlds. When the Amarrians were thrown out during the Minmatar Rebellion their collaborators fled with them. The Amarrians helped their Minmatar allies to settle in a few systems not far from the newly formed Minmatar Republic. The Ammatars regard themselves as the true rulers of the Minmatars, mainly based around the fact that a fair proportion of the old Minmatar aristocracy, or tribal leaders, were among them. In this vein they named their domain San Matar, meaning ‘true home'.

The term Ammatar was first used by the Gallenteans to distinguish between the two groups. Out of convenience even the Ammatars themselves started using it, stating that, with the help of the Amarrians, they had progressed beyond the old social structure of the Minmatar tribes. Indeed, the Ammatars have very deliberately abolished many age-old traditions of the Minmatar tribal society and embraced some Amarrian ones instead.

In the months following the Elder War of YC110, the Ammatar Mandate was beset with turmoil and uncertainty. During the war, its lucrative tsula plantations -- the Mandate's largest export crop and arguably the backbone of its economy -- were systematically destroyed by Chamberlain Karsoth's forces in retaliation for the Mandate government's harboring of Starkmanir Minmatar tribesmen, a clan lineage long-since thought extinct. After Empress Jamyl I rose to power in the Amarr Empire, however, appointing Royal Heir Yonis Ardishapur as Ammatar's savior and protector, the nation has entered into something of a renaissance. Aid now flows in a steady stream from the Empire's coffers, command hierarchies are being reinforced and morale is on the rise. It appears the star of Ammatar will soon shine bright once more.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text:
I was asked by Arsten to continue to help the Republic University with their historical research. The memoirs I recovered earlier had directions to a burial site in San Matar, which I was tasked with investigating. The site housed the remains of an old Ammatar family that died out. What made them important for us was a myth about one of their leaders being buried with some special kind of Khumaak. The RU academics expected to debunk the myth by sending me out there. They didn't think I would actually find anything.

Well, I did. I found something in one of the tombs; a “wildfire” Khumaak. The academics can hardly contain themselves – they think it could represent a major discovery. Arsten seems uneasy about all of this, and just wants the item escorted to somewhere safe as soon as possible.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Here are the coordinates. And uh…all jokes aside, {[character]player.name}, try to respect the dead while you're looking around, if only to keep a low profile and an old Brutor happy.

messages.mission.briefing.text: You guys just pick things up then put 'em right back down, don't you?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Wait, you found a Khumaak out there? What the hell is a Wildfire Khumaak? I'm dying to look at it, I admit, but we can't screw around here. We need to get this thing somewhere safe before we start trying to figure anything out. I have a bad feeling about all of this {[character]player.name}. Boufin was strangely protective, Angels were all over the burial site, and the Amarr were plenty aware of its location too. With that many people involved, I doubt nobody noticed us lifting that thing out of the tombs.

I have an idea about where to take it, but I need to make a quick holovid call first. Talk to me again in a few moments, ok?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ever heard of the Defiants, {[character]player.name}? Well, either way, you're about to meet them – if you think you're ready for it. They're one of the few groups the Brutor tribe can trust these days. I once had the honor of meeting their leader, Karishal Muritor, before our own Fleet had him put down like a dog for daring to fight the Amarr. A shameful day for us all, it was.

Still, it showed us who will fight, and who can be trusted. There is no group of people I personally would want more than them to handle this. We don't know how significant this Khumaak is, but let me tell you friend, some of our people are very excited about its discovery. They think it may shed new light on our past. Me, I'm excited too I guess, but more concerned than anything. I'll relax once this is in the Defiants' hands, not any earlier.

So, can we count on you to make the delivery? I think you and I are past collateral now, {[character]player.name}. I'm happy to trust you with the current location of their camp, if only because you have no chance of finding them after this meeting. The Defiants are only discovered when they want to be.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Let me know as soon as you've made the delivery.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: After discovering the Wildfire Khumaak at the Hauteker burial site, I was asked by Arsten to deliver it safely to the Defiants, a rebel group thought to have been eradicated as they defended the Thukker-Elder retreat. The Brutor tribe has concerns for the artifacts' safety after seeing so many groups already involved in the matter.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Really? Ok then, {[character]player.name}, if you've had enough, then I'll find someone else.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Really? Ok then, {[character]player.name}, if you've had enough, then I'll find someone else.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The Defiants were a splinter group of the Republic Fleet commanded by Admiral Karishal Muritor, a Brutor warrior and figure of great renown within military circles. Skirting the edge of all-out conflict with the Amarr Empire, the Defiants waged constant guerilla warfare with Amarr forces in the years leading up to the Elder Fleet Invasion of YC110, despite insistent urgings from the Republic to back down. Though the good Admiral is now fallen and most of his force gone -- lost while covering the retreat of the Elder Fleet -- a small contingent lives on, scheming to stamp themselves once again into the hearts and minds of freedom-loving Minmatar.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Upon Arsten's instruction, I met with the Defiants, a rebel group thought to have been eradicated during their defense of the Thukker-Elder retreat. They have promised to safeguard the Wildfire Khumaak as we wait for academics to arrive and study it. The Brutor tribe is concerned for the artifact's safety after seeing so many groups already involved one way or another in the matter.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I knew you'd say yes. Alright, here is their location, but don't waste time screwing around, they move constantly and won't be there forever.

messages.mission.briefing.text:

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work, {[character]player.name}. I'm relieved to hear the Khumaak made it safely to the Defiants. I'm going to make a few arrangements to have some of the Republic's most trusted historians pay a visit to their caravan.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
{[character]player.name}, you're not gonna like this. Only moments ago the Angel Cartel launched an attack on the Defiant base to recover what was taken from them. Seems they only realized now that they were sitting on something of value. Hell, we barely even know what we're sitting on right now.

The Defiants have fled the camp, which has now been converted into a base of operations for the Angel's invasion fleet. The Defiants can easily evade a bunch of Angel thugs, but they have asked that we put this chase to an end quickly and violently. Your task will be to smash the Angel's operational base. That will sever the attacking forces still chasing our brothers from their reinforcements. As soon as that happens, the Defiants can stop running and turn to meet their attackers in a fair fight. They've never lost one, {[character]player.name}. Those Angels will drop like sacks of fedo crap once they have their support pulled out from under them.

You have your orders, {[character]player.name}, will you accept them?

messages.root.agentsays.text: Get going! Those Angels won't stop chasing our boys until you cut their umbilical cord.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: The Angel Cartel just launched an attack on the Defiant base, most likely to take back what was stolen from them. Arsten is confident that the Cartel wasn't even aware what they were sitting on though, since basically nobody realized that Wildfire Khumaaks actually existed. My job is to bring down the Angel's operational base. That will mean a fair fight for the Defiants being chased – something I'm told they're not in any risk of losing.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Then rack off. We have work that needs doing here.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Then rack off. We have work that needs doing here.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The Minmatar Republic and the Angel Cartel have a long and checkered history of locked horns and uneasy handshakes. A century back, when the Angel Cartel was building its reputation as a ruthless mercenary organization but had not yet crossed over into out-and-out piracy, the Republic was rumored to frequently contract the Cartel for operations deemed too politically sensitive for the Republic's armed forces. While these rumors have never been confirmed by either side, certain other occurrences -- such as the Cartel's immediate and unexplained withdrawal from their Skarkon sovereignty bid in YC110 -- seem to corroborate the idea of a nebulous connection between the two giant entities' top levels.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text:
The Angel Cartel attempted to launch an attack on the Defiant base, most likely to take back what was stolen from them. Arsten was confident that the Cartel wasn't even aware what they were sitting on though, since basically nobody realized that Wildfire Khumaaks even existed. My job was to bring down the Angel's operational base, which I managed. That meant a fair fight for the Defiants being chased, so they stopped running, turned around, and then killed their pursuers, Arsten tells me.

Now we have another problem. The RSS had sent some kind of Spy to the camp to advise the Defiants on the Khumaak, but he's gone missing, right as the Angels showed up. The various leaders are talking it out now, but Arsten has a hunch I'm going to be called up to investigate the matter further.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: We're lucky to have you working with us, now go kick their teeth in. For Muritor!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Only moments ago the Angel Cartel launched an attack on the Defiant base to recover what was taken from them. Seems they only realized now that they were sitting on something of value.

The Defiants have fled the camp, which has now been converted into a base of operations for the Angel's invasion fleet. The Defiants can easily evade a bunch of Angel thugs, but they have asked that we put this chase to an end quickly and violently. Your task will be to smash the Angel's operational base; our scouts traced their communications back to it, it's not far from here. That will sever the attacking forces from their reinforcements. As soon as that happens, the Defiants can stop running and turn to meet their attackers in a fair fight. They've never lost one, {[character]player.name}. Those Angels will drop like sacks of fedo crap once they have their support pulled out from under them.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Nice flying out there {[character]player.name}. The Defiants dealt with the remains of the attacking fleet easily once you took out their support.

As for the situation with this RSS Agent, we're still discussing our options amongst the tribal leadership, but chances are that this guy was operating on his own. That means basically nobody knew what he was doing or why the Wildfire Khumaak grabbed his attention. You're probably going to have to take that guy's passkey and go in there yourself, if the RSS lets us. We're still talking with them about the situation. Some people are looking at his disappearance in an entirely different light, if you get me. RSS operative shows up and not much later so do a bunch of Angels. Yeah…still a few discussions yet to be had, I reckon.

Anyways, get back to me again soon and we'll have a plan ready for you. You've more than proven yourself now, so I'd be more than happy to trust you with whatever comes next.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Alright, we've talked it out and I was right. You're going in there. The RSS almost threatened to have you killed for attempting it, but with the accusations being leveled at them right now they're just gonna have to get over it. We needed someone independent, not tied to any one faction, and who we knew we could trust. You were the obvious answer; I didn't even have to suggest it.

The RSS has given us the location of the compound where this agent was doing his work. Your task will be to fly to Alakgur and investigate it. We're looking for anything that would give us further insight into why he was visiting the Defiants. All they could tell us was that he expressed an interest in examining the Khumaak and then suddenly showed up. The Angels followed shortly after.

It's a politically delicate assignment {[character]player.name}, but a pretty easy one from your end. Just fly in there, have a poke around, and bring back anything you think may be relevant to our investigations. I'll be plugged into your camera drones for this one, along with the rest of the RSS, heh. We'll tell you what to look for too, if we see anything in there. Sorry about the invasive measures, but it was either that or a 500m ISK collateral to the RSS.

You down for this?

messages.root.agentsays.text: You should head out to Alakgur as soon as possible.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: It seems Arsten was right. I've been asked to head into the RSS compound and investigate things myself. Apparently my unique status and standing means I'm the preferred – and currently, the most trusted – candidate. My understanding is that various involved parties will be watching in through a camera drone feed. Arsten himself has promised to give further instructions once I get out there.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Man…alright…but damn, you're lucky I talked the RSS outta that 500m ISK collateral. Sheesh.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Really? I didn't see that one coming…alright then {[character]player.name}. I guess you have other things that need doing. Later then.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Perhaps less is known about the Republic Security Services than any other national intelligence agency in the universe of New Eden. Their numbers, their spheres of operation, the scope of their involvement in affairs national and international: all these things are hidden in a fog of silence and misdirection. In the absence of concrete recorded information, the only detectable pattern is composed of reports from those few times the agency has revealed itself. Pieced together, a picture begins to emerge: grim, humorless, determined and fierce, these men and women stalk the underworld and mingle with its demons so their brethren may live in the sunshine.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text:
Arsten was right in the end. I was asked to head into the RSS compound and look around for any explanation as to why an RSS agent wanted to advise the Defiants on the Wildfire Khumaak.

After a while spent searching emptied facilities, we found some data in the cache of the radio telescope – lots of communications from this agent. I'm not entirely sure what to make of it, but the impression given from the logs is that he was handling some kind of highly-placed spy in the Ammatar Consulate. He also appears to have been one of only two people who knew about the job, so secrecy is paramount here. The RSS staff on hand claimed to have been learning of this project as we were.

Given that we found the first Wildfire Khumaak at the burial grounds of an ancient Ammatar bloodline, I'm guessing this woman – whoever she is – knows something about their history too.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks {[character]player.name}. I owe you one.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Alright, we've talked it out and I was right. You're going in there. The RSS almost threatened to have you killed for attempting it, but with the accusations being leveled at them right now they're just gonna have to get over it. Sorry about the invasive measures, but it was either that or a 500m ISK collateral to the RSS.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Excellent work out there, {[character]player.name}. We're making copies of the data you recovered now. It looks like we'll have more than enough here to work from.

From first impressions, it looks like this RSS agent was working almost entirely alone on some operation involving a highly-placed Ammatar defector and the Wildfire Khumaak. The RSS people here with me are claiming they've never heard of this matter before. I'm seeing reports here to suggest that this Ammatar “sister” was a source for historical information on the Wildfire.

I don't like the name of that RSS operation though, {[character]player.name}. Stillwater? That's basically the opposite of “Wildfire”. We should be careful not to trust the RSS too much on this one, I think.

In fact, I have an idea. I'll speak with you again after I've made a few arrangements with the RSS.

messages.mission.option1.charsays.text: Good guys. If you see this text in-game, defect it.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
So this man, Rahsa Teff, was behind it all. Rahsa Teff was a native to this region and wanted Miyan out. He knew his Sansha buddies were attracting attention, so he used Jariza to pull funds from Darabi. Rahsa then gave the money to Manik to fund his little mercenary gang. Manik's build up was a distraction the whole time, as were the Amarr ships you encountered when chasing Rahsa down.

Now that we have Rahsa Teff in my custody, the question is what to do with him. We could keep him around for more questioning, but I'd just as soon blow him out the airlock. What do you think? Is his life worth it?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Aralin Jick ponders the fate of Rahsa Teff.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Rahsa Teff's fate was decided.

messages.mission.option2.charsays.text: Bad guys. If you see this text in-game, defect it.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Now that we have Rahsa Teff in custody, the question is what to do with him. We could keep him around for more questioning, but I'd just as soon blow him out the airlock. What do you think? Is his life worth it?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Harkan must be dealt with immediately. His knowledge of Kor-Azor security and security codes make him a serious threat. I'll contact Kandus Sandar to get the MIO moving. Right now you need to arrest Harkan. He was granted a small fief upon his retirement. You have a good chance of catching him there.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: You are to arrest Harkan before he gets away.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You can't let Harkan get away with this.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Harkan was too daunting for you?

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Commodore Harkan is an old guard of the Kor-Azor family. After multiple tours with the Imperial Navy, he became the chief security officer for House Miyan. In his decades of service, he has only had one blemish. In YC 109, he led Miyan's forces into battle against those of Lord Darabi in Fensi, a battle which he lost when Miyan surrendered. Harkan's big mistake was objecting to Miyan's surrender in public. It was not long after that Harkan retired.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: You were sent to arrest Harkan before any more damage was done, but the traitor apparently committed suicide by destroying his own home upon your arrival.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Be careful on this. Harkan has certainly already learned about the Rahsa trap. He is a skilled military commander and will most likely not go down without a fight.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Go to Harkan's manor and place him under arrest. Be careful on this. Harkan has certainly already learned about the Rahsa trap. He is a skilled military commander and will most likely not go down without a fight.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
No! We were so close.

He knew we were coming for him. By killing himself before we could make an arrest, he's effectively secured his legacy before it could be tarnished. No one will sully the name of a dead hero, guilty or not.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: You must inform Riff Hebian of Harkan's demise. He was very fond of the man, so he should be informed personally.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Hebian can be found patrolling the Palas system in his battleship.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Riff Hebian must be informed of Harkan's death.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: We weren't done yet.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: We weren't done yet.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: In Harkan's final years, he became a vocal critic of current Amarr slavery techniques. Though still in favor of slave labor, Harkan argued that the Empire's reliance on old methods of control such as Vitoc were too limiting. His views were cemented after the Elder invasion, which saw millions of slaves violently rebelling after they were freed of their Vitoc dependency. Harkan left the public eye after an outburst against Empress Jamyl's emancipation of ninth generation slaves cost him the favor of local Holders.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Riff Hebian was informed of Harkan's death.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Hebian is on patrol in the Palas system. Godspeed.

messages.mission.briefing.text: You must inform Riff Hebian of Harkan's demise. He was very fond of the man, so he should be informed personally. He can be found patrolling the Palas system in his battleship.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I have to apologize to you for my skepticism of your aims earlier. We've been increasing our security since the attack on Miyan's manor. But we never imagined one of our own was a threat. You have to understand that many of us have nothing but reverence for the Commodore. To find out he was a traitor...

But he's gone. The task of judgment is out of our hands now.

Only one task remains. With the destruction of their base and the deaths of Rahsa and now Harkan, the remaining Sansha are panicking. They're throwing a last ditch assault at one of Miyan's facilities. Lord Miyan himself is perfectly safe. Per our heightened security measures, I've sent him to a hidden safe house far from there.

The Sansha attacked my Lord and corrupted my predecessor. Annihilate them.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Are the Sansha finally defeated?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: The last remnant of Rahsa's forces are attacking a Miyan outpost.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I, too, am tired of the Sansha's meddling, but I have a job to do.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I, too, am tired of the Sansha's meddling, but I have a job to do.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Lady Jariza is under investigation for her role in all of this, but the only charge we could actually bring is conspiracy. And accusing a noble of conspiracy is about as useful as charging a Slaverhound with indecent exposure. It's the nature of the beast.

Lord Darabi has been cleared of any wrong doing. His daughter Mina has returned to their estate and is taking a larger role in family affairs.

Lord Manik and Lord Miyan reached a gentleman's agreement after the destruction of Manik's mercenary fleet. A number of Manik's agricultural worlds have been given as a gift to House Miyan. Lord Miyan accepted the gift, and has declared a clean slate between them.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: What was believed to be the last remnant of Rahsa's forces attacked a House Miyan outpost. After engaging the enemy the Sansha ran, revealing themselves to be a diversion.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Get to it.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Only one task remains. With the destruction of their base and the deaths of Rahsa and now Harkan, the remaining Sansha are panicking. They're throwing a last ditch assault at one of Miyan's facilities. Miyan's perfectly safe. Per our heightened security measures, I've sent him to a hidden safe house.

The Sansha attacked my Holder and corrupted my predecessor. Annihilate them.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: God damn him! It was all a ruse!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Harkan's not dead! He's just launched an attack on Lord Miyan's safe house! Lord Miyan is in danger!

He's already broken past the main acceleration gate. Harkan knows our systems inside out. Our automated defenses are useless. Worse, I've reports that several of our own security forces are helping him!

The safe house is in Choga. I need your help to rescue Miyan from Harkan's forces. I can't rely on my own security forces, because I don't know how many more will turn.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Lord Miyan's safe house is besieged by Harkan's forces.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Is Lord Miyan safe?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: The situation is too dire for me to waste time on a quitter.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: The situation is too dire for me to waste time on a quitter.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Lord Harkan emerged alive after all, and launched a surprise assault on Lord Miyan's safe house. You bravely broke through the corrupted defenses and turncoats. The traitor Harkan fell to your superior flying, allowing Lord Miyan to continue his rightful rule.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Find Miyan's safe house in the Choga system. Consider every Amarr ship you find a traitor.

Be careful. Harkan is a fierce military commander.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Lord Harkan has launched an attack on Lord Miyan's safe house! He's bypassed automated defenses and has turned several of Miyan's security forces against their Lord. I can only trust you to aid Lord Miyan.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Lord Miyan is safe. The political situation is returning to what passes for normal.

The few remnants of the Sansha forces are fleeing back to Stain. The crews of the Amarr ships that joined Harkan's failed rebellion have been stripped of their ranks and any titles. Their commanders have the Empress' justice to look forward to.

As for Harkan himself? His death allowed him to escape temporal justice. His name is being stripped from the Miyan records of service. My lord's men are tracking down Harkan's kin to end his line. In a generation, when the living memory of Harkan's betrayal fades with us, there will be no sign of Harkan's passing .

You, {[character]player.name}, will be remembered long after this. I envy your Capsuleer lifespan, and pray you continue your good works in the name of the Empire for years to come.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
It's time for you to put that ID tag to use and see firsthand what it is we're fighting against down here.

Though you've no doubt heard of the fearless and capable pilots in the Caldari Militia, I wouldn't make the mistake of thinking that the situation in Black Rise is a stable one. The region is a war-zone, and will probably remain that way for some time. Even though they're capsuleers like you, our militia cannot be everywhere at once, and it is in their absence that the Federation often makes progress.

We've been receiving reports of a new prison facility being erected somewhere in the Aokinen constellation. Your mission is to discover its location, bypass the security forces and slip inside. Once you've made your way inside, there will be people of ours to free. My suspicion though, is that you will not find any Ishukone crew to rescue. I suppose we'll see what happens.

If you've never done any exploratory scanning before, then now would be a good time to learn. The Federation is skilled at hiding their secrets, but I have a feeling that a facility this size will be found easily enough. If you are struggling to locate it, don't lose hope - that's exactly what the enemy wants us to do.

You will need a Data Analyzer to complete this mission.

What do you say, {[character]player.name}?

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you discovered the prison facility yet?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Now that I have recovered a Federation Navy ID tag, Sinas wants me to use it to infiltrate one of their prisons and liberate the Caldari being held there. I'm told that the facility is hidden somewhere in the Aokinen constellation, but where exactly, he doesn't know.

messages.mission.extrainfo.header.text: Two Bloodlines, one Race: the Raata spirit in the Deteis and Civire soul

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Then our time together is over, {[character]player.name}. I need people who can commit.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Then our time together is over, {[character]player.name}. I need people who can commit.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
“Look at each other,” Cold Wind told them. “How do you tell one man from the other? How do you know which man to kill?”

The men struggled to stand up and looked at their armors; the symbols of their Houses were torn and broken, not visible anymore.

“No two men on this field have the same face, but can you tell them apart now?”

The men gazed at each other trying to distinguish brothers from enemies, yet the blood covering their faces made all of them alike.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text:
Sinas wanted me to use the Federation Navy ID tag I recovered to infiltrate a Gallente prison and liberate the Caldari being held there. After some time scanning, I discovered the compound and managed to slip past the outer defenses and inside.

What I saw was rows of prisons, each of them dividing Caldari P.O.W into their corporate families. The Ishukone prison was empty. After evacuating just one of the prisons, self-destruct timers initiated on the rest. This wasn't a rescue mission, it was a mercy killing.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent, our Black Ops wing will stand down and let you proceed. I'll issue any further instructions over comms as the need arises. Good luck.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
It's time for you to put that ID tag to use and see firsthand what it is we're fighting against down here. We've been receiving reports of a new prison facility being erected somewhere in the Aokinen constellation.

Your mission is to discover the prison's location, bypass the security forces and slip inside. Once you've made your way through there will be people of ours to free. Your only concern is saving them. If you can expedite their recovery by avoiding conflicts in the outer perimeter then you should do so. Our priority is our people, above all else.

If you've never done any exploratory scanning before, then now would be a good time to learn. The Federation is skilled at hiding their secrets, but I have a feeling that a facility this size will be found easily enough. If you can't find it at first, don't lose hope - that's exactly what the enemy wants us to do.

You will need a Data Analyzer to complete this mission.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
You did well, {[character]player.name}, despite the circumstances. I hope this operation has opened your eyes to the truth of this war.

The empty Ishukone facility you discovered is the strongest proof yet that there is something going on here. I'm beginning to see it in a new light, too. I hate to say it, but my suspicion is that Ishukone has some kind of prisoner exchange program with the Federation. It's the only explanation that accounts for everything I've seen so far.

Stick around, {[character]player.name}. I have another lead that you can follow up for me.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
It seems Ishukone are playing a dangerous game here, {[character]player.name}. Before we make any moves though, we have to be absolutely certain that things actually are what they look like. What does that mean? It means I need you for another infiltration mission.

We've been monitoring the movement of selected Ishukone vessels over the last few days. Our focus is on the handful of diplomatic emissaries they've deployed inside Black Rise. Why does Ishukone have diplomats down here? We wondered the same thing, and that's why we had them followed.

While tracking one particular Ishukone vessel, our surveillance team lost them. They appear to have warped into a derelict research facility, conveniently located inside an area riddled with electromagnetic interference. Now, it's quite possible that their actions were entirely legitimate. We just don't know though, I ordered my men not to pursue.

I'm betting that we can send you in there without any trouble, no matter what goes down. You capsuleers are invaluable for these sorts of missions where you have no idea how it will go. Would you be willing to scout the area for us and report back what you find?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Sinas is becoming increasingly convinced the Ishukone have some kind of prisoner exchange arrangement with the Federation. He told me that Ishukone diplomatic vessels were spotted in Black Rise and tailed by Caldari Navy forces. One such diplomat vanished into an old research compound riddled with electromagnetic interference – the perfect place to hold a meeting without anyone tapping into your conversation. I've been asked to investigate this area and report back on anything I can find inside.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you been to the meeting place yet?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'll find someone else then. Thank you for all you did for us, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'll find someone else then. Thank you for all you did for us, {[character]player.name}.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text:
Sinas is growing increasingly convinced the Ishukone have some kind of prisoner exchange arrangement with the Federation. He told me that Ishukone diplomatic vessels were spotted in Black Rise and tailed by Caldari Navy forces. One such diplomat vanished into an old research compound riddled with electromagnetic interference – the perfect place to hold a meeting without anyone tapping into your conversation.

I was asked to investigate the area and report back on anything I found inside. There wasn't much to be found there and the place was empty, but I did uncover a data node. Strangely enough, it used proprietary encryption software that appeared to be a mixture of Gallentean and Caldari designs. Sinas is going to arrange to have it decoded, after which he'll likely want me for another mission.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
I knew you'd say yes.

I'm not sure how to advise you here, {[character]player.name}, but my suspicion is that this will rely more on scouting and less on combat, so perhaps a small and agile frigate is in order. We just have no idea what's in there though, I'm afraid, so there's no hard intel to support that assumption.

Your task is to investigate this area and uncover anything you can to shed more light on Ishukone's recent actions. You will most probably only need a frigate for this, but we obviously have no intel to guide you one way or the other.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
So…an encrypted data fragment, and the cipher appears to be a proprietary mix of Gallente and Caldari designs. That alone is quite telling, but I won't rush to judgment even now, not until we get this decoded.

Give me a moment to speak with my sister Toras. She can pass a message on to Katsen that we need someone who can decrypt this thing. I'll be available again in a moment {[character]player.name}, bear with me.

messages.mission.option1.charsays.text:
Due to the serious nature of this situation, our Regional Director greatly suggests contacting the authorities for further assistance. The FIO have a very strong presence in the area, and the Black Eagles have been extremely helpful to us in the past. I recommend talking to Mourmarie Mone, the Constellation Director for the Black Eagles. She is located in Noghere. Here are the coordinates of her office.

Good luck, and thank you for your continued business with Impetus.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: There are two ways we can go about this situation, {[character]player.name}. The Regional Director has instructed me to offer you these two options. He would like you to know that this is a very important decision; he would also like to wish you good luck in your choice.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I have two options ahead of me: Go to the Feds, or go to the media.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I was given a choice: Go to the Feds, or go to the media.

messages.mission.option2.charsays.text:
Although our Regional Director would like this matter taken to the authorities, there is a more discreet option open to you in handing this delicate situation. As a universal leader in the entertainment industry, Impetus maintains many close ties with other media outlets. One of our many partners is the Scope, which has been very kind in reviewing our various blockbuster holoreels over the past few years. I can send you to Veine Coructie, a local editor for the Scope. He is very trustworthy, and he can provide a lot of information about suspicious activity in the area.

I must warn you that choosing this route will take you into low-security space. Though I do not recommend this choice, there may be more lucrative opportunities with the Scope than with the FIO. Any news agency would pay dearly for the information you have, and the Scope is without question one of the biggest news agencies around. There are more risks involved with this option, but I want to make sure you are aware of your choice.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Very well.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I have reached a dead end with Impetus, so they directed me to the regional authorities, namely one Mourmarie Mone. I can't find any publicly listed file on her, but with a sensitive case such as this, it makes sense for me to go straight for the FIO. Eron has given me coordinates to Mourmarie's office; let's hope I made the right choice.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Do you need me to give you the coordinates to Mourmarie Mone again? I would be more than happy to help.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Thank you for your time, {[character]player.name}. We appreciate your continued business with Impetus Development Studios. Have a good day, and remember to watch for the latest holoreel hits from Impetus, New Eden's leader in entertainment.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Thank you for your time, {[character]player.name}. We appreciate your continued business with Impetus Development Studios. Have a good day, and remember to watch for the latest holoreel hits from Impetus, New Eden's leader in entertainment.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: This situation is starting to get complicated, so I decided to go straight to the Feds. Eron Viette directed me to the Black Eagles, a relatively new division of the FIO. They have a dark reputation, but at least I know I'm covering my ass by talking to them. Wouldn't want this situation to get any worse than it already is.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good luck with your mission, {[character]player.name}. We appreciate your time with Impetus Development Studios. Have a good day, and remember to watch for the latest holoreel hits from Impetus, New Eden's leader in entertainment.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I have reached a dead end with Impetus, so they directed me to a regional office of the Scope. Though my instincts tell me I should contact the authorities, I feel that the better option would be to keep this situation under wraps, or at least to have the option of using the media to snuff out the bad guys. This Scope office is in Vitrauze, a lowsec system. Let's hope I made the right choice.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Do you need me to give you the coordinates to Veine Coructie again? I would be more than happy to help.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Thank you for your time, {[character]player.name}. We appreciate your continued business with Impetus Development Studios. Have a good day, and remember to watch for the latest holoreel hits from Impetus, New Eden's leader in entertainment.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Veine Coructie is in Vitrauze, a lowsec system of New Eden. CONCORD's presence is barely felt in that area, and pirates and other dangers lurk throughout. Be prepared for a fight while flying through lowsec.

However, the less secure the space, the more lucrative the opportunities. There are riches to be found in lowsec, if one can survive long enough to reach them.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: This situation is starting to get complicated, and I feel that this is the wrong time to go to the authorities. Eron Viette directed me to the Scope. They know the area better than anyone, probably better than the FIO. Plus, I know they can be discreet with situations like this. If nothing else, I can probably get them to pay handsomely for the information. You can always count on that.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Thank you for your time, {[character]player.name}. We appreciate your continued business with Impetus Development Studios. Have a good day, and remember to watch for the latest holoreel hits from Impetus, New Eden's leader in entertainment.

He is very trustworthy, and he can provide a lot of information about suspicious activity in the area.

I must warn you that choosing this route will take you into low-security space. Though I do not recommend this choice, there may be more lucrative opportunities with the Scope than here with the FIO. Any news agency would pay dearly for the information you have, and the Scope is one of the biggest news agencies around. However, there are more risks involved with this option.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
No time for small talk. We have a very serious situation on our hands, and I need the utmost discretion from you. That kid may be a goner if we don't act fast. Unfortunately, we don't know much about this “Pator 6” gang except for a few rumblings here and there. A lot of pirates use this area as a haven. Most of them are small-time criminals, no more than thugs looking for an easy mark. The Serpentis have some hold in this area, though I doubt we're looking at any sort of leech on the underbelly of the booster industry. No, this looks suspicious, and not like Serpentis at all. This sounds personal, or at least desperate.

Alright, so it looks like we'll be fishing for information. Since it was some Minmatar thugs that took the senator's kid, I guess we'll pound some Matari heads in first. This region is crawling with those people. I don't know who is a bigger drain on the Federation, the criminals or the Minmatar.

Anyway, there's a colony of them in Charmerout. Go in there and start shooting up buildings. Hopefully that'll scare up some leads for us. If not…well, we'll have fewer Matari clogging up the Federation resources. Frankly, I'm fine with that.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: When stepping into the underground, you're bound to get your hands dirty. This mission is no exception. The Black Eagles asked for me to rough up a Minmatar colony, hoping that someone in there would have info on the Pator 6. These FIO agents mean business, and I don't think any of it is clean.

messages.root.agentsays.text: There's no time to hesitate. We need info ASAP.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Figures that a capsuleer would balk at the first sign of danger. You're a disgrace to the Federation. In fact, some would say you're just as bad as them

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Figures that a capsuleer would balk at the first sign of danger. You're a disgrace to the Federation.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: My first step into the underworld produced few leads. At the insistence of Mourmarie Mone, a Black Eagle agent, I roughed up a colony of Minmatar refugees. After destroying a few of their buildings, I managed to bring out their Elder. He didn't have much to tell me, except to go look in a place called the “Underground Circus.” I've heard of this place, and Mourmarie appears to know it as well.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: There's no room for pity when you're dealing with bottom-dwellers. The underground is a dirty, nasty place, and you have to adapt to its environments in order to destroy it. This is the price we pay for freedom, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text: We don't know much about this “Pator 6” gang except a few rumblings here and there. Look like we'll be fishing for information. Since it was some Minmatar thugs that took the senator's kid, I guess we'll pound some Matari heads first. This region is crawling with those people. I don't know who is a bigger drain on the Federation, the criminals or the Minmatar. There's a colony of them in Charmerout. Go in there and start shooting up buildings. Hopefully that'll scare up some leads for us. If not, well, we'll have a fewer Matari clogging up the Federation resources. Frankly, I'm fine with that.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Even though I feel we can't trust any information from the Matari, they're our only lead. The Underground Circus is a ruthless place, a stain on our region's image. But it's our only chance.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Our sources have caught wind of the situation, {[character]player.name}, though I'm glad you contacted us. We won't go public with this information yet, as that would be against our ethics as journalists. However, we will aid you in uncovering information on the missing child. Senator Ardanne has not always been kind to the media, but there's no reason to hold a grudge against him in a time like this.

We've been keeping tabs on the Pator 6 for a while now. They're mostly low-level criminals, but their name has been popping up a lot recently, especially in relation to kidnapping cases. I haven't seen them do anything this high profile, though.

Our first course of action is to see if we can plant a bug in a known Pator 6 hangout. Hodts Ergre, one of our more experienced investigative reporters, managed to acquire an access code to this place. We'd like you to place a covert recording device in their hideout. Hodts will open the gate, and you'll sneak in and plant the goods. This is a stealth operation, so it would probably be best if you fly something inconspicuous. I'm not saying you should go out there completely defenseless; as you know there are more pirates around here than just the Pator 6.

You can take any ship you want, but I highly recommend a frigate-sized vessel. A battleship will definitely tip them off that you‘re up to no good.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Veine Coructie, an editor at the Scope station in Vitrauze, has caught wind of this kidnapping business and is willing to help. I'll accompany Hodts Ergre, an investigative reporter, and plant a bug in a known Pator 6 hangout. I'm in lowsec territory, so I need to watch out for pirates and other criminals.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Did you plant the covert recording device yet?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: We can't keep this story under wraps for very long. Word has a tendency to spread rather quickly, and the difference between rumor and fact can get muddied. I'd hate to see something like that happen here, especially when there's a kid's life at stake. Would be a shame, you know? Especially if it involved a frightened and shamed capsuleer.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: We can't keep this story under wraps for very long. Word has a tendency to spread rather quickly, and the difference between rumor and fact can get muddied. I'd hate to see something like that happen here, especially when there's a kid's life at stake. Would be a shame, you know?

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Veine Coructie, an editor at the Scope station in Vitrauze, caught wind of this kidnapping business. I escorted Hodts Ergre, an investigative reporter, to a known Pator 6 hangout. We were ambushed, and Hodts was killed. He did not die in vain, however, as I managed to gain access to the hangout and place the covert recording device in their hideout.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Use your cloaking device as much as possible when travelling in this area. You can't get hit if you can't be seen, right? Above all, be careful out there.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Our first course of action is to see if we can plant a bug in a known Pator 6 hangout. Hodts Ergre, one of our more experienced investigative reporters, managed to acquire an access code to this place. We'd like you to place a covert recording device in their hideout. I'm not saying you should go out there completely defenseless; as you know there are more pirates around here than just the Pator 6.

You can take any ship you want, but I highly recommend a frigate-sized vessel. A battleship will definitely tip them off that you‘re up to no good.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Hodts is dead? Oh no. No. That is tragic. He was the bravest reporter I've ever worked with.

Please give me a minute. I'm rather shocked about this news. Come back to me in a few moments.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
The Underground Circus represents everything wrong with our Federation, the exploitation of personal liberties for the sick desires of depraved “citizens.” True Gallente have respect for themselves and treat their freedom with dignity, respect, and class. I should have known that the Circus would have something to do with this kidnapping business: Children are commodities in a dump like that.

Looks like it's time for us to bring in the Ringmaster, the owner/operator of the Underground Circus. Don't let her name fool you: She's ruthless, cunning, and manipulative. I've worked with her before, back when she was a legit businesswoman. She's degraded into a broker of sin and filth, a mockery of what she once was. Find her and bring her to me. With a bit of heavy questioning, we'll get the right information from her.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Don't let the Ringmaster and her Circus fool you. It's a trap that catches many people, all for naught. When you bring her to me, I'll make sure her penance is just.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: The Underground Circus is an infamous den of sin in these parts, and it appears to be the best place for finding a lost kid. I'm supposed to find the Circus' owner/operator, the Ringmaster, whoever she is. Looks like the Eagles want to do some heavy-handed interrogation of her. I don't know what to expect from this place, but it can't be all that bad. I think this Mone woman may be a little too uptight, even for a Gallente.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Cowardice is a trait I've seen a lot in you capsuleers. That explains your immortality: Those who fear death cannot understand the honor of living. Go back to your mercenary ways, {[character]player.name}, and I hope I don't catch you around these parts again.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I am wholly suspicious of your decision, and I have half a mind to report you to my superiors. I must warn you, {[character]player.name}, that if I catch you sniffing around the Circus, I will arrest you immediately. There is neither freedom nor pleasure in a Federation prison, though I relish the idea of watching a demigod like yourself rot in a jail cell.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
“Guilt is unknown in the Gallente Federation. Pleasure, desire, lust, avarice: These are the rights of all people, laws be damned. Our economy is built not upon currency or scarcity, but on the supply and demand of needs, wants, and yearnings. A guilty pleasure is the highest right of the Gallente; my Circus is here to satisfy and fulfill this right. Let us redefine what it is to be guilty.”

-The Ringmaster, on the opening of the Underground Circus, YC 108

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I visited the Underground Circus, a den of sin and pleasure, much of it questionably legal. I captured the owner/operator of the joint, a woman who calls herself the Ringmaster, and took her back to the Black Eagles for questioning. I hope that she'll provide us with some answers after a bit of questioning. I may not agree with the Black Eagles' tactics, but they sure know how to get the job done.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: The glitz and glamour of the Underground Circus is a siren song for many people. Don't let yourself get trapped by its allure, no matter how decadent and desirable it may seem. That is the path to ruin, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Looks like it's time to bring in the Ringmaster, the owner/operator of the Underground Circus. Don't let her name fool you: She's ruthless, cunning, and manipulative. I've worked with her before, back when she was a legit businesswoman. She's degraded into a broker cesspool of sin and filth, a mockery of what she once was. Find her and bring her to me. With a bit of heavy questioning, we'll get the right information from her.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: It's good to see you again, Ringmaster. Been a long time. We have questions for you, and we'll make sure we get the answers we want. This will hurt you more than it will me, but I admit I'll enjoy it nonetheless.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
The bug appears to be working well. We've been picking up a lot of messages from the Pator 6. For such a relatively small-time gang, they have quite a large network established. I don't know why we haven't noticed them earlier. We'll have to keep this bug going for a bit. There are a few breaking stories in there, or at least some info we could sell.

While the Pator 6 has a rather large foothold throughout the region, we heard one system repeated over and over again: {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I asked some of my sources in that system, and they sent me the coordinates of some sort of junkyard with a lot of traffic from unlicensed Minmatar pilots. I have a distinct feeling that the kid is there, or at least he was at one point...

Hang on. We just intercepted a message from our bug. Looks like the Pator 6 is expecting company soon. Time to crash the party. See who the meeting is with, and try to bring back something we can pin on the gang. We need evidence that Ralie was there if we're going to bust this case open. Gotta warn you, though: A battleship won't be much good here. From what I've seen, they have a means of keeping battleships out of their hideouts. Thus, don't take one on this mission.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: The covert recording device appears to be working as planned. The Pator 6 is really busy in this region. With the information gleaned through the bug and Veine's incessant networking, the location of the gang's major headquarters was finally discovered. Or at least we think it's their HQ. A last minute message from the bug presages an important meeting between the Pator 6 and their associates. If I make it in time, I can learn who the gang is working for, or at least get some evidence of the kidnapping for use against them.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Well, who is the Pator 6 working with?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: We were so close to the big scoop. Do you have any idea how big those ratings would have been?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You'd make a terrible reporter, you know. No guts, no story.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: The bug I planted worked as planned. Veine Coructie, using that device in conjunction with his massive network of contacts, managed to discover the Pator 6's headquarters. When I flew there, I witnessed a meeting between the gang and their criminal associates. Looks like the Syndicate are behind this. I don't know why they'd be involved in this region; this situation may be bigger than I imagined. Even though they attacked me, I managed to escape with some evidence that Ralie was with the Pator 6. This evidence should help in getting closer to that poor kid.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: The Pator 6 is working for somebody big. A high-profile crime like this is well above their level. I don't know who could have orchestrated this, but I think we're about to find out. Either way, we need hard evidence in order to corroborate our story. That's Journalism 101, my friend.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
While the Pator 6 has a rather large foothold throughout the region, we heard one system repeated over and over again: {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I asked some of my sources in that system, and they sent me the coordinates of some sort of junkyard with a lot of traffic from unlicensed Minmatar pilots. I have a distinct feeling that the kid is there, or at least he was at one point...

Hang on. We just intercepted a message from our bug. Looks like the Pator 6 is expecting company soon. Time to crash the party. See who the meeting is with, and try to bring back something we can pin on the gang. We need evidence that Ralie was there if we're going to bust this case open. Gotta warn you, though: A battleship won't be much good here. From what I've seen, they have a means of keeping battleships out of their hideouts. Thus, don't take one on this mission.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: The Syndicate? In this space? That's practically unheard of. What would they want from Senator Ardanne? At least we have proof now, hard evidence that we can use. That's some great reporting, {[character]player.name}. You know, when this is over, we could use your investigation skills. You can't teach those at any Journo School.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
After a bit of interrogation, the Ringmaster gave us the information we're looking for. Funny, we barely put any effort into it: She succumbed pretty quickly. Oh well. Since we have her in custody, we'll use her for more questioning later, just as soon as she's rested up and ready for another round.

Anyway, based on her information, we've learned of a nearby Intaki settlement that has some loose association with the Pator 6. You know what the Intaki are like — one big mess of criminals. I don't believe the lies they tell us in the media: All Intaki are a part of the Syndicate, directly or not. If it were up to me, I'd lock all the Intaki up for good, or maybe just send them all back to their cesspool of a home planet.

Go to Pemene and find those Intaki. Keep an eye out for the Pator 6, and report back with any information you receive about the senator's son. You may have to open fire on their settlement in order to get them to talk. If you run into any opposition, use force. You have the authorities on your side.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: The Ringmaster gave us a lead on an Intaki colony with loose associations to the Pator 6. Mourmarie thinks that I'll find some info there. I can't tell if this is a legit lead or not: It is entirely possible that Mourmarie's prejudices are getting in the way of her judgment. But it's the only clue we have to go on, so I will move forward and hope something comes of it.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Well? Did you find anything?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Are you a sympathizer with the Intaki cause? I'd get out of here real quick, unless you wanted the wrath of the Federation on you.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Are you a sympathizer with the Intaki cause? I'd get out of here real quick, unless you wanted the wrath of the Federation on you.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: The Ringmaster's lead was correct. I found the Pator 6 at the Intaki colony. Turns out they were working for the Syndicate all along. I was warned to stay away from Syndicate business, but I'm not afraid of their threats. At least I know the kid is still alive. There's hope yet.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: You are doing a service for the Federation and its true citizens. There are a lot of criminals that must be brought to justice, and we are getting closer to punishing this bunch of them. Nobody we apprehend is innocent; everyone here is guilty.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Go to Pemene and find those Intaki. Keep an eye out for the Pator 6, and report back with any information you receive about the senator's son. You may have to open fire on their settlement in order to get them to talk. If you run into any opposition, use force. You have the authorities on your side.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: This information confirms my suspicions. Those damn Intaki are all criminals, and this proves it. I don't know why the Syndicate would involve themselves in this space; they know better than to enter this region. I don't know what they want with the senator's kid, either. But at least we know who has the kid, and that he's still alive.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Truth is the fundamental goal of any good reporter, and we've uncovered enough of it to create a media storm. The power of the press is unprecedented in its ability to sway the general public, create massive sympathy for an unknown issue, and to create a massive backlash against nefarious groups. When we present this evidence on the holovids, there's no hope for the Syndicate. Their reputation will be ruined if anything happens to the kid. This is the power of the media.

We have a satellite station that we like to use for these important broadcasts. It's safely hidden in a secret location in case there's any blowback from our special reports. Take this evidence and drop it off at the station. We'll use that to raise awareness of this case, blow it right open, and turn the wrath of the unwashed masses on the Syndicate.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: The Scope is ready to run a full expose on this kidnapping case, direct via holovid from one of their secret satellite stations. I'm supposed to deliver the evidence to the station for the report. The hope is that this will shed the spotlight on the kidnapping, forcing it into the public arena and showing the Syndicate in a terrible light. If anything happens to Ralie from here, the Syndicate will never be able to live it down.

messages.root.agentsays.text: We need that evidence for our expose. Where is it?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: This is our chance to put the spotlight on a delicate situation and you bail out at the last minute? I'll never understand you eggers.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: This is our chance to put the spotlight on a delicate situation and you bail out at the last minute? I'll never understand you eggers.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I delivered the evidence to the Scope station, but the Black Eagles intercepted the package shortly afterward. The Feds have stepped in and are forcing their agenda on me. I don't like the way they're handling this, but it looks like I have no choice. There's no use trusting authority.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Of course, we'll get plenty of good ratings, too. That's the most important thing.

messages.mission.briefing.text: We have a satellite station that we like to use for these important broadcasts. It's safely hidden in a secret location in case there's any blowback from our special reports. Take this evidence and drop it off at the station. We'll use that to raise awareness of this case, blow it right open, and turn the wrath of the unwashed masses on the Syndicate.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Damn Black Eagles. I don't know how they knew about our satellite location. This does not bode well for our business. Those rat bastards are no good at all. I might have to push my story on them a little earlier than expected. They'll learn how much power we really have…

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I've managed to get a message over to Katsen. He's already begun to make some arrangements but I have to say {[character]player.name}, this is going to be a particularly dicey assignment, for all of us.

Katsen is convinced he knows the man for this job. In fact, he claims that if anyone can decipher this data node, it will be this man. His name is Vira Mikano, and he's a senior decryption analyst with Ishukone Watch.

Yeah that's right, I said Ishukone Watch.

Katsen's plan is to have some of his people “redirect” Mr. Mikano from his office in Oipo to your personal hangar on the station. From there, you will put him aboard your ship and safely escort him back here to Astoh.

Let me stress something before you leap in, {[character]player.name}. Mikano is a family man, and a well-respected Caldari too. Hell, I once had drinks with him. If the lives of many more Caldari weren't at stake here, I wouldn't consider abducting him for even a moment, but desperate situations call for practical solutions. We need him to help us, and there is no chance in hell he'd do that without a little pressure, but he must not come to any harm whatsoever.

Only accept this assignment if you're absolutely ready for it. I'll relay your acceptance to Katsen the moment you give me the nod. After that, there's no turning back.

messages.root.agentsays.text: {[character]player.name}, move it!

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Things are starting to escalate, it seems. Sinas and Katsen have made arrangements to have the data node decoded, but it will require the knowledge of a man named Vira Mikano. This guy works for Ishukone Watch, meaning he won't help us without being coerced. The plan is to have Katsen's people “redirect” him from his office in Oipo to my personal hangar on the station. After that, my job is to get the hell out of there and back to Astoh before people realize the truth about Mikano's absence.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Pressure can make or break a Caldari. I'm surprised after everything you've done that this was too much for you. Very well, {[character]player.name}, I'll find someone else.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Pressure can make or break a Caldari. I'm surprised after everything you've done that this was too much for you. Very well, {[character]player.name}, I'll find someone else.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The glossy tropes of the public relations holoreels and the beige glamour of stylized war worship stand in stark contrast to the reality of these agencies, but most people have only a muddy awareness of the dichotomy.

A man can be rudely treated by a brusque and superior Ishukone Watch officer and silently curse him for hours, but as soon as he gets home that evening he is just as likely to prop his feet up and enjoy a rousing serial where the Ishukone Watch's superior technology and cunning allows it to root out Gurista spies and double-cross them into revealing their hideout. So pervasive is the propaganda that it is highly doubtful this man ever draws a parallel between the real thing and the image; the connection he draws, instead, is between the image and the mother corporation it represents.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Things are starting to escalate, it seems. Sinas and Katsen made arrangements to have the data node decoded, but it required the knowledge of a man named Vira Mikano; one of Ishukone Watch's senior intelligence officers. There was no chance he was going to help us without being coerced, so the plan was to have Katsen's people “redirect” him from his office in Oipo to my personal hangar on the station. After that, I just burned it back down to Astoh before anyone could even realize he'd gone missing. Now I wait, and hope that he can decipher this thing.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Here goes nothing then. I'll see you shortly, {[character]player.name}. Good luck.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Katsen is convinced that if anyone can decipher this data node, it will be Vira Mikano, a senior decryption analyst with Ishukone Watch.

Katsen's plan is to have some of his people “redirect” Mr. Mikano from his office in Oipo to your personal hangar on the station. From there, you will put him aboard your ship and safely escort him back here to Astoh.

Let me stress something before you leap in, {[character]player.name}. Mikano is a family man, and a well-respected Caldari too. . We need him to help us, and there is no chance in hell he'd do that without a little pressure, but he must not come to any harm whatsoever.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
I think we may have just pulled it off, {[character]player.name}. Unbelievable, but then most of Katsen's plans are.

We'll take care of Mikano from here. He'll be more than safe, don't worry. Once he has given us what we need he'll be promptly returned to his families.

We've taken a scan copy of the data node you uncovered. Katsen says it won't be long before Mikano decodes it for us.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
If we're going to get to the Syndicate, then you'll have to go undercover for us, {[character]player.name}. Otherwise, they would see us coming from an AU away.

Not to worry, though. I have a person in mind who can help: Ascain Adeset. We nabbed her a few years back for human trafficking. She was on some crazy booster as well, and took out four of our cruisers before we brought her down. We lost a lot of good officers in that raid. After serving a few years in prison, she saw the light and joined our side. Now she's one of our best informants in the area.

I planted her in TransStellar to ensure that she keeps that company legit. We have a very close eye on her in case she decides to change sides again. If she does, she'll be lucky to make it back to prison at all.

You can find her in Mesybier.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: The Black Eagles have planted a rat in TransStellar with a history in human trafficking. Though she's legit now, the Eagles use her for information on the seedier parts of the region. I have to find her in Mesybier and work with her on getting the kid back. The Syndicate will be able to see the Feds coming; they won't expect a one-man army, though.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Turning your back and running at a critical time like this implies either cowardice or a complete lack of humanity. Both are crucial traits of a capsuleer.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Turning your back and running at a critical time like this implies either cowardice or a complete lack of humanity. Both are crucial traits of a capsuleer.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: The Black Eagles have planted a rat in TransStellar with a history in human trafficking. Though she's legit now, the Eagles use her for information on the seedier parts of the region. I found her in Mesybier and will work with her on getting the kid back. The Syndicate will be able to see the Feds coming; they won't expect a one-man army, though.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Even though she's clean, I still wouldn't trust her fully. A rat is a rat: That's all there is to it. But in her case, she knows better than to betray us. She's had experience.
