messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Abdiel Verat, Angel Cartel.

I look out for talented people such as you who are interested in work. And times have certainly made our work interesting.

Since you're an egger, I'm guessing you know your way around wormholes, yes? While they've been a great aid for our scientists, they've also brought some problems to our doorstop, some of which is not good for business.

Our explorers have discovered a wormhole in a nearby system, but we cannot spare the manpower to lock it down. If you help us out by scouting the area, then I may have other more lucrative tasks to follow.

messages.root.agentsays.text: I'll be waiting for your report. You needn't return here, {[character]player.name}. Just open up comms once you have a clear idea of the situation.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I met with Abdiel Verat, one of the Angel Cartel's capsuleer liaisons.  She had a job for me: scout a nearby wormhole and report the presence of any hostiles.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Then stop wasting my time.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Then stop wasting my time.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The sudden appearance of wormholes across New Eden proved to be a boon to scientific communities of all disciplines. Nearly everyone in the cluster has some vested interest in the wormholes.

The Angel Cartel has been investing heavily into wormhole exploration. They not only scavenge the Sleeper ruins for new technology, but also exploit the wormholes' ability to link otherwise distant points. A wormhole can potentially turn an eighty-jump trip from Curse to Fountain into a twenty-minute jaunt. Although these opportunities represent significant logistical advantages, they are always fleeting, and every effort to map wormhole space has thus far failed.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I met with Abdiel Verat, one of the Angel Cartel's capsuleer liaisons. She had a job for me: scout a nearby wormhole and report the presence of any hostiles. When I arrived I found a gang of Sansha ships already there. She wants it dealt with.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: The wormhole is in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Investigate the area and then report back to me with what you've found.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Abdiel Verat, Angel Cartel.

I look out for talented people such as you who are interested in work. And times have certainly made our work interesting.

Since you're an egger, I'm guessing you know your way around wormholes, yes? While they've been a great aid for our scientists, they've also brought some problems to our doorstop, some of which is not good for business.

Our explorers have discovered a wormhole in a nearby system, but we cannot spare the manpower to lock it down. If you help us out by scouting the area, then I may have other more lucrative tasks to follow.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Sansha. Alright, let me relay this information up the chain of command. Stick around; we'll be calling on you to deal with this.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
At the moment I have more work than I have people, so you need to choose how you want to proceed.

We also have a shipment of important research material that needs to make it to Serpentis hands. The Inquest scientists in charge of the operation have been delayed, and moving the goods is a high-priority task we need someone to take over. We may also require an investigation into the reasons for the delay at Serpentis' end.

Both tasks need to be followed up. I don't care what you choose; we'll give one to you, and one to the next egger brave or stupid enough to show up down here.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Faced with the Sansha's Nation blockade around the wormhole, Abdiel offered me a choice of what to do next. I can either take the Nation on directly in the name of the Cartel, or I can provide direct support for their research project.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Faced with the Sansha's Nation blockade around the wormhole, Abdiel offered me a choice of what to do next. I can either take the Nation on directly in the name of the Cartel, or I can provide direct support for their research project.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Alright then.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
At the moment I have more work than I have people, so you need to choose how you want to proceed.

Obviously, the Sansha need to be cleared from our wormhole site. If you can prove yourself on this, chances are I'll be able to request more assignments to give you. We have early reports of more problems abroad, so I'm sure we can keep you moving from target to target out there.

We also have a shipment of important research material that needs to make it to Serpentis hands. The Inquest scientists in charge of the operation have been delayed, and moving the goods is a high-priority task we need someone to take over. We may also require an investigation into the reasons for the delay at Serpentis' end.

Both tasks need to be followed up. I don't care what you choose; we'll give one to you, and one to the next egger brave or stupid enough to show up down here.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Alright, I need to relay your decision to my superiors and arrange to have the work you've passed on taken over by someone else. Just one moment, {[character]player.name}…

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Oh, great, another one.

Look, I don't know where you're getting your intel, but I've got absolutely nothing to do with the Cartel. I'm not your “connection” in any sense of the word. Some scumbag was envious of my service record in Curse and decided to come up with that little story to explain away my success. You've been played, {[character]player.name}.

I don't know anything more about the Cartel than the next person. I have no idea about any pirate invasions that they could potentially need help with. And I certainly don't know that Abdiel Verat would be the person you should talk to if you wanted to know more.

As you can see, I can't help you, and even if I did have valuable information, it would be reported immediately to my superiors. I have a reputation to uphold.

Now, if you don't mind, I have important Navy matters to attend to. I hope you understand.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: While I was in Sendaya, I came across an agent of the Imperial Navy. She seemed to be implying in a roundabout way that the Angels were under attack in Curse and might need capsuleer assistance. She never came right out and said, however. That kind of treachery within the Navy would be punishable by death.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Yes?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Quit what? I don't remember giving you any assignment. I think you have become confused, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Decline what? We're having a conversation, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
This is a high-level stealth operation that will send you to nullsec. It is strongly recommended that you use an interceptor to move about freely in the depths of 0.0 space and complete these missions.

The journey into nullsec is a dangerous one. You should only accept the assignment if you are prepared to encounter (and evade) high-risk situations such as interdiction bubble camps and entire alliances wanting to kill you.

The Imperial Navy is in no way liable for any assets or personnel lost as a result of accepting this assignment. The Imperial Navy does not endorse this assignment and will deny all knowledge of its issuance. If you have received this message in error, please consult the nearest Ministry of Internal Order bureau for assistance. It is your legal obligation to report erroneous messages within 7 days.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text:
While I was in Sendaya, I came across an agent of the Imperial Navy named Arajna Ashia. She implied that the Angels were under attack in Curse and might need capsuleer assistance. She never came right out and said, however. That kind of treachery within the Navy would be punishable by death.

She dropped the name “Abdiel Verat” as the person I should talk to about this matter. It seems Verat is deep inside Curse, and that if I want to follow this matter up, I will need to be too.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Hmm? You're off then? Fly safe.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I don't know anything more about the Cartel than the next person. I have no idea about any pirate invasions that they could potentially need help with. And I certainly don't know that Abdiel Verat would be the person you should talk to if you wanted to know more.

As you can see, I can't help you, and even if I did have valuable information, it would be reported immediately to my superiors. I have a reputation to uphold.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Welcome to my humble little shop, pilot!

Ah... sorry, the identifier system was lagging, an' I didn't see you were an egger, heh.

Stin's the name, or at least, it's the one I'm using for this operation. I'm here to recruit some fresh blood for the battles in Curse. Seems you lot have started to wander off right when we need capsuleers the most.

If you're interested, I can hook you up with Abdiel Verat. She's the primary point of contact for capsuleers in Curse.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Yes?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: While I was in Konora, I came across an agent of the Agent Cartel, Ellar Stin. She told me that the Cartel is looking for more pod pilots to help them out with the “battles” down in Curse. If I'm interested, she can arrange a meeting with one of her associates down there.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Whatever.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Whatever.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
This is a high-level stealth operation that will send you to nullsec. It is strongly recommended that you use an interceptor to move about freely in the depths of 0.0 space and complete these missions.

The journey into nullsec is a dangerous one. You should only accept the assignment if you are prepared to encounter (and evade) high-risk situations such as interdiction bubble camps and entire alliances wanting to kill you.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: While I was in Konora I came across an agent of the Angel Cartel, Ellar Stine. She told me that the Cartel is looking for more pod pilots to help them out with their “battles” down in Curse. I've been given the name of a new contact down in Curse, Abdiel Verat. If I want to follow the matter up, I should meet with her.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good then, here's the details.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Stin's the name, or at least, it's the one I'm using for this operation. I'm here to recruit some fresh blood for the battles in Curse. Seems you lot have started to wander off right when we need capsuleers the most.

If you're interested, I can hook you up with Abdiel Verat. She's the primary point of contact for capsuleers in Curse.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Hey, man.

If you're out here in a shithole like Egbinger, then maybe there's a chance you can help me out with something. We just had a bunch of Republic Fleet guys dock up and repair here. They'd been out in Curse dealing with some Angel Cartel raiders.

They were describing how the Cartel is having trouble right now with some other pirate groups. Seems there's a Guristas commander tearing them a new hole down there, as well as some Sansha meandering about causing problems. From the sounds of it, the Cartel's taking some significant losses.

Anyways, I was hoping you could fly down and check it out. While the Fleet was docked up, I had my boys go over their comms system. We've got ourselves the name of a Cartel agent involved in the invasion. Abdiel Verat.

It may sound strange to hear it, {[character]player.name}, but if you can find some way to deal with those Guristas and Sansha, I'd be thankful. The Cartel may give us grief, but they've done good things for the Minmatar people too, even if nobody has a damn clue why, or what's in it for them.

All I know is that I'd prefer the Cartel to Guristas thugs and Sansha freaks. If you can, go and deal with their problems. Just don't go helping them too much, got it?

messages.root.agentsays.text: Get going, {[character]player.name}. Don't forget an interceptor; chances are you'll need one.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text:
While I was in Egbinger, I came across a shipyard that was repairing some Republic Fleet vessels. One of the staff there, Aton Hordner, relayed a story about the Angel Cartel's woes in Curse. Apparently they're being slaughtered from two sides by Guristas and Sansha.

Hordner is concerned about the balance of power there, and asked that I find some way to ensure the Cartel's continued dominance over Curse. His rationale is that the Angels make for better enemies than Guristas thugs and Sansha “zombies.” It's hard to find fault with his reasoning.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Fair enough.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Fair enough.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
This is a high-level stealth operation that will send you to nullsec. It is strongly recommended that you use an interceptor to move about freely in the depths of 0.0 space and complete these missions.

The journey into nullsec is a dangerous one. You should only accept the assignment if you are prepared to encounter (and evade) high-risk situations such as interdiction bubble camps and entire alliances wanting to kill you.

The Republic Security Service is in no way liable for any assets or personnel lost as a result of accepting this assignment.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text:
While I was in Egbinger, I came across a shipyard that was repairing some Republic Fleet vessels. One of the staff there, Aton Hordner, relayed a story about the Angel Cartel's woes in Curse. Apparently they're being slaughtered from two sides by Guristas and the Sansha.

Hordner is concerned about the balance of power there, and asked that I find some way to ensure the Cartel's continued dominance over Curse. His rationale is that the Angels make for better enemies than Guristas thugs and Sansha “zombies.” It's hard to find fault with his reasoning.

I've been given the name of a Cartel agent that the RSS repair crew pilfered from one of the ship's comms system. Abdiel Verat is her name, and I'll find her deep inside the Curse region.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Alright, good luck out there.

If you're out here in a shithole like Egbinger then maybe there's a chance you can help me out with something. We just had a bunch of Republic Fleet guys dock up and repair here. They'd been out in Curse dealing with some Angel Cartel raiders.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Obviously, the Sansha need to be cleared from our wormhole site. If you can prove yourself on this, chances are I'll be able to request more assignments to give you. We have early reports of more problems abroad, so I'm sure we can keep you moving from target to target out there.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I decided to take down the Sansha and clear the wormhole for the Cartel. Abdiel told me that I needed to take out their Overseer, since without him, the rest of the Nation ships would be without clear direction.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Damn Sansha freaks...

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You've wasted enough of my time then.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You've wasted enough of my time then.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Naturally, I decided to take down the Sansha and clear the wormhole for the Cartel. I'd taken down bigger threats before. Abdiel told me that I needed to take out their Overseer, since without him, the rest of the Nation ships would be without clear direction. It took a little doing, the Overseer didn't want to stick his neck out just for one little capsuleer. But after I took down plenty of his men, he had no choice. He was tougher than I expected, but went down eventually nonetheless.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Alright, you want to pursue the Sansha? That works for me.

Once you've dealt with them report back to me. I'll keep my comms link open.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Dislodging the Sansha won't be easy after they've already begun to settle themselves in, but we can focus on their weak points. If they're doing things by the book, the Sansha forces will have an Overseer there directing the group from a safe distance. Take out enough of the fodder vessels and you'll provoke its appearance. Once you destroy the Overseer their whole operation will fall apart. Think of it as a decapitation.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Nice flying, {[character]player.name}. I'll be sure to include your name in the report.

I'm ordering our exploration team to go in right now. They'll see if it links up to any systems near Fountain.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Perhaps it's not worth the trouble to take down the Sansha encampment. They might have already gone in and destabilized the wormhole. We play by risk and reward, and the reward here looks like it'll be too low.

There's a high-priority shipment that has been sitting around waiting for someone capable enough to move it. It's headed to the Serpentis research facilities in Fountain, but Sarpati's crew is going to handle moving it from Curse over to their Headquarters. They were supposed to take it directly from this station but we've lost contact with the research team in charge of that operation. The job is yours if you want it. All you need to do is get it to nearby Serpentis Corp. transport hub, from there they'll handle the rest.

The cargo is small so you could easily fit it inside an interceptor or covert ops and I would suggest you do just that, {[character]player.name}. I will not accept any excuses for the cargo's disappearance.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I chose to aid Abdiel by delivering sensitive research data to the Serpentis myself.

messages.root.agentsays.text: You have a delivery to make. Get to it.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: A foolish move, {[character]player.name}. Your failure will be noted in our records.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Then you are useless to me, goodbye.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The partnership between the Angel Cartel and the Serpentis is a perfect match. The Cartel has all the things the Serpentis lack: massive manpower, a gigantic network of dealers and thugs, a cold vicious enthusiasm for crime, and the organizational skills needed to help spread the Serpentis supply of boosters to new markets. Without the Cartel, the Serpentis would never have expanded to become as powerful and pervasive as it is today, and many say, the reverse is also true.

Despite all the success the partnership has brought the Serpentis, it may be the Cartel who got the better end of the bargain. Not only do the Serpentis supply the Cartel with the most-addictive and highest quality boosters in the cluster, they also provide unparalleled research. The Cartel has long had access to dozens of ancient Jovian ruins, but previously lacked the expertise to truly take advantage of them. The Serpentis changed all that, and many think the Cartel's latest ship designs – and many other secret breakthroughs – come straight from Serpentis minds.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I chose to aid Abdiel by delivering sensitive research data to the Serpentis myself. I managed to deliver the cargo without incident. The Cartel used a proprietary fullerene-based sealant on the cargo. They went to a lot of effort to keep the contents private.

messages.mission.briefing.text: There's a high-priority shipment that has been sitting around waiting for someone capable enough to move it. It's headed to the Serpentis research facilities in Fountain, but Sarpati's crew is going to handle moving it from Curse over to their Headquarters. All you need to do is get it to nearby Serpentis Corp. transport hub, from there they'll handle the rest.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Serpentis acknowledged receipt of the goods, but they've asked for our help in another matter. That research team that you just filled in for is missing for a good reason, it seems.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I just discovered why that research team never arrived to pick up the goods you ferried: their labs are under siege by Guristas forces. I don't know what the hell the Guristas think they're going to achieve down here, but if we don't quickly shut them down we risk them gaining a foothold.

This attack was fierce and well-coordinated. They managed to overwhelm our defenses. All of our other forces are either too far away to assist or on other important missions they can't be diverted from. You're our best shot. I want you to save that research station from the Guristas assault.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Move out!

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: The Guristas are making trouble for the Serpentis, raiding one of their research facilities and decimating the Guardian Angel security force there. With no one else in the area who can handle the threat, the Cartel has asked me to step in and put an end to it.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Then you're useless to us. Goodbye.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Then you're useless to us. Goodbye.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The Angel Cartel and Guristas have a lot in common on the surface. Both seem to be the classical thugs, engaging in all the brutish activities attributed to base criminals. But while the two do have some overlapping interests, their methods and core desires are different.

The Angel Cartel is closer to a criminal mafia, dedicated to pushing drugs, running protection rackets, taking out assassination contracts, and involving themselves in all manner of nefarious research projects. The Guristas, however, are opportunistic pirates. They prowl the space lanes and hit any target that looks half-valuable or vulnerable. They loot and plunder what they can, ransom off the valuable survivors, and then hit the bars to celebrate.

The Cartel sees the Guristas as chaotic malcontents, disrupting trade, causing economic difficulties, and generally making it more difficult for them to ply their illicit trades. The Guristas see the Cartel as dishonorable brutes, skulking in the darkness and using trickery and deception to dull the minds and sensibilities of their clients.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: The Guristas raided a Serpentis research facility, decimating the Guardian Angel security force. The Cartel asked that I step in and put an end to the siege. I destroyed most of the Guristas, but a few warped off. Their commander was a capsuleer named Yukiro Demense. Verat has a plan to deal with him.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. I want you to send a clear message, {[character]player.name}. Let nobody survive.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I just discovered why that research team never arrived to pick up the goods you ferried: their labs are under siege by Guristas forces. I don't know what the hell the Guristas think they're going to achieve down here, but if we don't quickly shut them down we risk them gaining a foothold.

This attack was fierce and well-coordinated. They managed to overwhelm our defenses. All of our other forces are either too far away to assist or on other important missions they can't be diverted from. You're our best shot. I want you to save that research station from the Guristas assault.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work clearing off the remainders, but this “Demense” issue will have to be dealt with. Open comms with me again when you're ready to see to that.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Okay, the exploration team is away. If the Serpentis eggheads are right, they should arrive in Fountain securely and in record time.

Speak of the devil. I'm getting a report that one of our shipments coming back from Fountain just got hit by Guristas. It's always something.

There's a salvage crew nearby that can pick up the tech, but they aren't equipped to handle Guristas. If you clear out the Guristas, I can send in the recovery team. As always you'll be well paid.

messages.root.agentsays.text: How's the mission going?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Abdiel received word that the Guristas have assaulted a convoy from Fountain containing recent research data. I am to drive off the Guristas attackers until the recovery team can arrive.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: If I can't trust you to do a simply cleaning op, what use are you?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Sounds too tough, does it? Run along now. Find something more your speed.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The Jove left Curse behind long ago. Their ruins in the form of stations and forgotten outposts. Centuries later the Angel Cartel moved.

The Angels have managed to scavenge a good deal of information from these Jovian relics. This is most obviously reflected in Angel ships, which bear striking designs and unique capabilities. But the Cartel has yet to understand more than a fraction of the old Jovian technologies. Even the Serpentis, whose research capabilities surpass the Cartel's by leaps and bounds, have great difficulty even understanding the principles of Jovian engineering.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Abdiel received word that the Guristas have assaulted a convoy from Fountain containing recent research data. When I arrived at the scene the Angel ship was already destroyed. I destroyed every one of the Guristas ships. The Angels sent a recovery team when all the hard work was done.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: The Guristas are a tough bunch. They won't scatter if you pop the leader the way Sansha do. You're going to have to kill every one of the bunnies.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Getting a report that one of our shipments coming back from Fountain just got hit by Guristas. It's always something.

There's a salvage crew nearby that can pick up the tech, but they aren't equipped to handle Guristas. If you clear out the Guristas, I can send in the recovery team. As always you'll be well paid.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You're proving yourself to be a valuable asset to the Angel Cartel.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Our biggest competition in the Tech III race is not the Guristas or the Sansha. Hell, it's not even the empires. It's your kind. Capsuleers. I'll admit you guys have been giving us a run for our money. You're uniquely suited to wormhole space. Thankfully a few of you have been less than careful in normal space.

There's a capsuleer named Renton that makes his home nearby. We know he's been exploring wormhole space, and he's likely been stockpiling Sleeper tech at this base. He's only been a minor nuisance so far, but his tech cache could be useful. We would do the raid ourselves, but it's more effective to have capsuleers take care of each other, much less bloodshed.

Find Renton's base. Eliminate him. I'll be able to send an another recovery team once you've wiped out all hostiles.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: A troublesome capsuleer named Renton has recently returned from W-space with a stockpile of Sleeper relics. Abdiel wants me to find his base and eliminate him so that the Cartel can claim his cache.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Then stop wasting my time.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Then stop wasting my time.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Although there are many theories, few know what happened to the Sleepers. Their ruins were already old when the Amarr reached space.

For most, the Sleepers were little more than a curiosity; an ancient civilization lost and forgotten. Then wormholes opened across the cluster. Explorers that ventured into the strange space beyond were met with highly-advanced drones protecting relics that we now know once belonged to the Sleepers. Apart from the drones themselves, the only structures found are lifeless ruins. But the Sleeper drones themselves function all too well, despite what must be centuries of neglect.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: A troublesome capsuleer named Renton returned from W-space with a stockpile of Sleeper relics. Abdiel sent me to find his base eliminate him. The base was sparsely defended, so taking care of the inhabitations was easy enough.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Renton's base is poorly defended by most corporation standards. Kill everyone you see.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Our biggest competition in the Tech III race is not the Guristas or the Sansha. Hell, it's not even the empires. It's your kind. Capsuleers. I'll admit you guys have been giving us a run for our money. You're uniquely suited to wormhole space. Thankfully a few of you have been less than careful in normal space.

There's a capsuleer named Renton that makes his home nearby. We know he's been exploring wormhole space, and he's likely been stockpiling Sleeper tech at this base. He's only been a minor nuisance so far, but his tech cache could be useful. Find Renton's base. It's poorly defended by most corporation standards. Kill everyone you see. I'll be able to send an another recovery team once you've secured the area.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent work. I'll have my men sort through Renton's haul. There's a lesson in there about complacency for you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Alright, you're ready to take care of this Guristas commander? Good.

Yukiro Demense is a capsuleer. With all those clones, he'll be a tough one to break, but we have plenty of experience when it comes to dealing with this sort of problem. Our friends over at Serpentis Inquest were also more than willing to offer their expertise on this matter after the Guristas attacked their research facility. This Demense punk just made some very powerful enemies.

You'll be travelling to a local black market cloning facility, one that we've been happy to ignore until now. The facility administrator took a heavy bribe from Demense to allow one of his clones access, and so of course, they had their license and all good standings with us permanently revoked. Intelligence indicates that Demense is reliant on this facility to support his raids. With a clone backup available locally, he has been able to return to the fight without re-cloning in Venal up north.

Your first task is to storm this facility and make an example of the people there. Let nobody survive; their deaths must send a message across Curse. Once you have dealt with this indiscretion, you need to deliver a special data payload into their central database hub. As soon as you approach the hub, the data will auto-transmit a special virus engineered by our Inquest friends.

Do this and report back to me. I will have further instructions for you at that point.

messages.root.agentsays.text: We're waiting, {[character]player.name}.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: The Guristas commander, Yukiro Demense, has a clone contract with a small facility nearby. Verat wants the staff at the facility killed for letting Demense establish himself down here. Their deaths will send a message to other companies operating under the Cartel's protection in Curse. Once I have cleared the area, I am to upload a virus to their central database.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Then you are useless to me. Our business is concluded.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Then you are useless to me. Our business is concluded.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Hundreds of small companies exist in the fringes of space that cater to those who either can't afford or are banned from the big-name cloning companies. Naturally, there is a much greater risk with these organizations. No regulations means there are no guarantees of revival, and there are many stories of capsuleers waking up in distant backup cloning facilities after their local clone never activated. For most capsuleers this represents only a minor inconvenience, since very few are foolish enough to place their lives in the hands of questionable company.

For those criminals who can pay, the clones are nearly as safe as the Empire ones, a fact that has stymied efforts to curb the proliferation of capsuleer outlaws, and allowed them to move about the cluster with the freedom capsuleers are famous for.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: The Guristas commander, Yukiro Demense, had a clone contract with a small cloning facility nearby. My slaughter of the staff there has sent a warning to other companies operating under the Cartel's protection in Curse. With the area cleared, I uploaded a virus engineered by Serpentis Inquest scientists. Demense's local clone is now compromised.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I'm uploading the data to your Fluid Router now. Good luck, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Yukiro Demense is a capsuleer. With all those clones, he'll be a tough one to break, but we have plenty of experience when it comes to dealing with this sort of problem. Our friends over at Serpentis Inquest were also more than willing to offer their expertise on this matter after the Guristas attacked their research facility. This Demense punk just made some very powerful enemies.

You'll be travelling to a local black market cloning facility, one that we've been happy to ignore until now. The facility administrator took a heavy bribe from Demense to allow one of his clones access, and so of course, they had their license and all good standings with us permanently revoked. Intelligence indicates that Demense is reliant on this facility to support his raids. With a clone backup available locally, he has been able to return to the fight without re-cloning in Venal up north.

Your first task is to storm this facility and make an example of the people there. Let nobody survive; their deaths must send a message across Curse. Once you have dealt with this indiscretion, you need to deliver a special data payload into their central database hub. As soon as you approach the hub, the data will auto-transmit a special virus engineered by our Inquest friends.

Do this and report back to me. I will have further instructions for you at that point.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
You've done well. The traitorous administrator and his peons were justly removed from the picture and Demense's local clone is now compromised.

The next step is getting him to reanimate into it.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Demense is still in Curse. I'd say his superiors have become aware that the hammer of a thousand Angels is about to come crashing down on him and are keeping the fool out here on “deployment."

Your task is to put the insolent little maggot down. Once he reanimates into that new clone, he'll be a non-issue. As I said before, {[character]player.name}, the man made some powerful enemies. We have chosen our friends wisely, and if you only knew what they were capable of doing to your clone, you'd understand why we want them on our side.

Go, kill him. If you succeed, perhaps I will share the true nature of Demense's fate with you.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Yukiro Demense's current clone has been targeted for assassination by the Cartel. I am to carry out their will and force his reanimation into a compromised clone.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Move it, {[character]player.name}. You have your orders.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Useless.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Then piss off and stop wasting my time.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Yukiro Demense's clone was targeted for assassination by the Cartel. I carried out their will and brought its life to an end. Verat told me that the Inquest scientists confirmed his reanimation into the compromised clone. Verat remained coy about Yukiro's new fate, but trusted me enough to reveal that he has been infected with some kind of disease, one that will follow him from clone to clone.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Be ready for a fight. Even the simplest of brutes can be competent fighters, and he likely won't go down so easily now he knows what you're capable of.

messages.mission.briefing.text:

Go, kill him. If you succeed, perhaps I will share the true nature of Demense's fate with you.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Serpentis Inquest just confirmed the reanimation of his local clone. You've done well, {[character]player.name}. Loyalty and a capacity to deliver results, these are both admirable qualities that will get you far within our organization.

You've caught the attention of my superiors, in fact. It seems they have a need for a capsuleer, and one who has already proven themselves trustworthy and capable. When you want the details for your new contact, I can pass them along.

Demense's fate? Let's just say that he has contracted a disease which is going to follow him from clone to clone. Eternity is not all it's cracked up to be.

Let me know when you're ready to move on.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
All that's left to do is transport the tech you've helped us collect back up to Fountain. No, we're not asking you to haul. We've got a crew for that. Your job is more exciting.

We know there are Guristas still in the area, possibly with their Sansha pals. They want these parts badly enough to dare raiding in our territory. So, we decided to use their eagerness against them. We let the details leak about the timing of this shipment. They think they'll be ambushing a defenseless industrial. What they're going to find is you.

Kill every vessel that shows up.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: The research materials I helped secure are ready for transport up to Fountain. Before it leaves, Abdiel wants to use it as bait to trap the Guristas. When the pirates warp in to attack the hauler, I'll be there to meet them.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Get moving, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Goodbye.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Goodbye.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: The research materials I helped secure have been transported up to Fountain. Before it left, Abdiel used it as bait to trap the Guristas. Waves of pirates poured through to take out the hauler, even a capsuleer named Yukiro Demense. I destroyed them all.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Show those them how true professionals roll.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
All that's left to do is transport the tech you've helped us collect back up to Fountain. No, we're not asking you to haul. We've got a crew for that. Your job is more exciting.

We let the details leak about the timing of this shipment. They think they'll be ambushing a defenseless industrial. What they're going to find is you.

Kill every vessel that shows up.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Even had a capsuleer show up, eh? Good. Nice to have a survivor to spread the story of their utter defeat.

You've done amazing work for us, and the Angels take notice of their friends. In fact, there's someone in the Dominations asking for you. Let me know if you want me to go ahead and arrange the meeting.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You've attracted the attention of Kadeja Dulche, one of the most important people in the Dominations. If he has a mission for you, the odds are good you'll be shooting some important people.

You best get going. I'd thank you for the assistance you provided, but an invitation to a meeting with a Domination agent says more than any words of mine will.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Talked to Ms. Dulche yet?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: My success against Demense caught the attention of a local Dominations member named Kadeja Dulche. I've been invited to meet with her back in K-QWHE.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: If that's how you feel, then yes, it's best we forego the meeting and send you on your way.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: If that's how you feel, then yes, it's best we forego the meeting and send you on your way.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The Dominations represent the command division of the Angel Cartel. The Dominations are elusive and mysterious, preferring to shroud their agendas in secrecy and obfuscation. Many of their membership seldom venture far from their bases in the Curse region, but CONCORD agents have reported sightings of highly-placed Cartel leaders as far north as Lonetrek.

Little is known about the identities of the Angel Cartel leadership, though it is understood that – as with the rest of the organization – they come from all the races and backgrounds.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: My success against Demense caught the attention of a local Dominations member named Kadeja Dulche.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Fly safe, {[character]player.name}.

Ready to move on then, I take it?

You'll be working with Kadeja Dulche of the Dominations from here on out. Don't ask me what he wants of you; it's not my business to know these things.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Never keep a Domination waiting, {[character]player.name}.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text:
I met with Kadeja Dulche, one of the chief field researchers for the Angel Cartel. She congratulated me on my good work with Abdiel. She wants my help to eliminate a Boundless Creations facility encroaching into Angel space.

I was faced with a choice. I can either make a direct assault at their full strength or first disable a communications array to lessen their ability to call reinforcements.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
{[character]player.name}, I've been waiting.

You've done well for us dealing with the Guristas and Sansha. Clashes with other frontier organizations come with the territory, however, and are never that much of a problem. The Archangels are more than capable of handling this aspect of daily operations. It is when other entities begin to stray outside their usual boundaries and establish themselves in our space that people begin to become rightly concerned. In these situations, we are called in to deal with them.

One Minmatar corporation, Boundless Creations, has made the mistake of conducting research in our space. They have come here on the misunderstanding that, just because their research is illegal, we will turn a blind eye to their presence. We've not corrected them on this false assumption. Rather, we've let them move in all of their assets and staff and slowly build themselves up. The time has now come to reveal to them where they truly stand with the Cartel.

Your mission is to destroy their research facility entirely, costing the interlopers billions. You can go about this whatever way you see fit. You can storm the facility head on, or weaken the defenses by knocking out their communications arrays first.

Either way, everyone in that place needs to be dealt with.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text:
I met with Kadeja Dulche, one of the chief field researchers for the Angel Cartel. She congratulated me on my good work with Abdiel. She wants my help to eliminate a Boundless Creations facility encroaching into Angel space.

I was faced with a choice. I can either make a direct assault at their full strength or first disable a communications array to lessen their ability to call reinforcements.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Going for the straight shot? You're a pilot after my own heart.

The base is split into three sections. Each section contains a data center that houses all of Boundless Creations' illegal research. You must destroy these. Each data center serves as a redundant backup for the others, so it needs to be all or nothing.

The Cartel is putting a lot of trust in you. Make it happen.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I've chosen to storm the Boundless Creations facility head-on and destroy their data centers. This should cripple their research capabilities and leave their million-ISK investment as nothing more than a scrap yard.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Keep your enemies close, {[character]player.name}. Always.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Your recommendations were overstated.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Your recommendations were overstated.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I chose to storm the Boundless Creations facility head-on and destroy their data centers. I've crippled their research capabilities and left their million-ISK investment as nothing more than a scrap yard. Boundless Creations will be forced to abandon their projects in Curse.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good, send a message.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The base is split into three sections. Each section contains a data center that houses all of Boundless Creations' illegal research. You must destroy these. Each data center serves as a redundant backup for the others, so it needs to be all or nothing.

The Cartel is putting a lot of trust in you. If you're going to storm the front, you better be ready to deliver.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Most impressive.

When it comes down to it, I find most eggers to be rather disappointing. For immortals, so many of you have such petty fears and such trivial concerns. Only a few of you have managed to break free from that. It is those rare few that we in the Dominations value most.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Boundless Creations has a communications array keeping tabs on the research base. If you attack the base now, they'll call in reinforcements and make your life difficult.

The good news is that they've attempted to hide the array inside a gas cloud rather than protect it in the open. They expect it to be undetected, and to most people it would be. Our scouts have uncovered the area though, and have observed engineers living at the compound. They will be carrying a security code which you must recover. You will be able to use it to deactivate the array without alerting the main Boundless Creation fleet.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I am to assault a base belonging to Boundless Creations. However, the first step is to silence a nearby communications array to prevent any calls for reinforcements.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Get moving, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Useless.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Useless.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I am to assault a base belonging to Boundless Creations. However, first I silenced a nearby communications array to prevent any calls for reinforcements.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good luck.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work. Now for the next step.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: With the communications array blinded, I'm ready to go destroy the data centers of Boundless Creations. I don't have much time before they catch on to their communications problem.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Get moving.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Your recommendations were overstated.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Your recommendations were overstated.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: With their communications array blinded, I devastated the Boundless Creations data centers. I've crippled their research capabilities and left their million-ISK investment as nothing more than a scrap yard. Boundless Creations will be forced to abandon their projects in Curse, and their failed venture should send a message to others.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Nice work. You've proven yourself to be a competent pilot, and you've garnered some attention from the higher-ups. Being a capsuleer certainly helps your case. I requested that another agent handle your work with the Guristas. I feel that you have the potential to rise high in our ranks. One of my old associates jumped at the chance to have you. One of her lieutenants has gone missing, and she needs a capable pilot to assist her.

So it's done. Consider it a promotion. You'll be working with Cilis Leglise. I brought her in, actually. She was Federation Intelligence before I convinced her to turn against the Empires. I got her to defect, and she's risen through the ranks at breakneck speed.

Cilis and Irichi Tsunikabda are handling our work against the Navy in this section of Venal. The Navy's been making efforts to clean this region up recently. Every operation they attempt against us, CIlis is there to ruin their mission. Cilis is their unrelenting, ubiquitous scourge.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I'm being sent to talk with Cilis Leglise. Kori Latamaki seems to think it was the only way to advance my involvement with Gurista affairs.

messages.root.agentsays.text: She's waiting to hear from you. There was something in her voice, but I wouldn't make too much of it.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm leaving my comms open in case you reconsider.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Not enough time? Too much pressure?  I'll let her know what you said. I'm sure she'll be thrilled with the news.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I've been handed off to Kori Latamaki's superior, Cilis Leglise. She's a defected Gallente agent, brought into the Guristas years ago by Kori. She was pleased with my performance at the shipyard. My efforts so far have earned me some respect within the Guristas, and working for Cilis is considered quite the reward.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Cilis takes things very seriously, so don't let her down. She's a capsuleer, but in recent times, she's refused to update her clone. I've spent time trying to figure out her motives; most of them are beyond me. She's always been hard to read and doesn't talk about her experiences in the pod.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Travel to 6NJ8-V and talk to Cilis Leglise. She has more assignments for you. Consider this a promotion.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I was hoping you'd contact me. You've made quite the impression among the Guristas ranks, so I had to jump at the chance of working with the hot, new capsuleer.

We've been picking up increased Navy activity in the region. It's really gutsy of them to come this far into Venal. This is our turf, after all. Before we can draw them into an ambush or respond in any meaningful (and hopefully humiliating) way, we need to know more about their activities. Luckily, Kori's provided me with some rather juicy information on a communications station that the Navy has erected. I need you to take it out.

According to our intel, the State uses the Venal Regional Comms tower to feed their forces information about our movements within this region. I don't know: This is pretty dirty, even by Caldari standards. We can change this situation, though. If you hack the tower, it'll redirect the signal to follow the Navy's movements instead of ours.

Take this Data Analyzer and hack the tower. You'll have to hang around the tower for a bit once you've successfully hacked the signal. Something may turn up, possibly some more trouble. Roll with the punches on this one, and think on your feet. I assume you know what you're doing. After all, we capsuleers are invincible warriors, right?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Cilis Leglise asked me to approach the Venal Regional Comms tower, a logistics station that's been a nexus of increased naval communications activity. I must attempt to hack into the tower in order to reroute the signal.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Found anything interesting?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'll make sure your career with the Guristas is over. Leave Venal now, or pay the price.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You're a capsuleer. I know what you're capable of. I guess you must be a coward.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The Guristas code is simple: Everything goes.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Cilis Leglise asked me to approach the Venal Regional Comms tower, a logistics station that's been a nexus of increased naval communications activity. I hacked into the tower in order to reroute the signal. Afterwards, I got a comms message from another Guristas agent, Irichi Tsunikabda, who led me to a secret holoreel.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Great.  I can sleep a little better knowing you're on the case, {[character]player.name}. Don't get killed. Not like that'll matter much, really.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Goddamnit, what is Irichi doing? That bastard is losing his mind. He hasn't been the same since he lost his legs, and he blames me for that. Well, I guess he should. I was the one who tortured him when I was working for the Federation. But we're Guristas now, and we pirates have to stick together, right? It's the pirate's code. That, and “every pirate for herself."

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Thanks to your work back at the comms tower, we've discovered the locations of a budding Navy fleet. This Navy group is much larger than ones we've seen in recent times. It looks like they're trying to weaken our hold on the fringe systems and consolidate power in Venal.

Not quite a bad plan on paper, to be completely honest. But they're becoming cocky, expecting to sneak up on us and take out our forces with ease. We'll do them one better, though, and surprise them. If we strike first, they won't be able to muster their forces enough to overwhelm us. And that's where you come in.

The fleet is docked at a fueling station, preparing for their attack. They're sitting ducks, or fish in a barrel, or whatever cliché you want to use. What makes this a great opportunity for us is their fueling depots. Those silos have enough energy stored in them to take out three fleets, if they happen to catch on fire. And that's what you'll be doing. Destroy at least one of the fuel depots, which will cascade and destroy the surrounding ships. Ignore the big ships and go straight for the fuel depots. There may be some guards there, but your main targets are the fuel depots. This is way more bang for your buck than you were expecting, huh?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Using the information from the hacked Venal Regional Comms tower, Cilis discovered the location of burgeoning Caldari Navy fleet. Stationed at a fueling depot, gearing up for an inclement strike on the Guristas, the fleet was prone, an easy target to pick off. Cilis's plan was to have me attack the fuel silos, so the explosion would cascade and destroy the ships as they wait to refuel. The damage done in this strike took out a significant portion of the Navy fleet.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Having fun out there?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: We'll make arrangements, but you'd be mistaken to think that we'll just forget this.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: We'll make arrangements, but you'd be mistaken to think that we'll just forget this.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Using the information from the hacked Venal Regional Comms tower, Cilis discovered the location of burgeoning Caldari Navy fleet. Cilis's plan is to have me attack the fuel silos, which will cascade and destroy the ships as they wait to refuel. Any damage done in this strike will take out a significant portion of the Navy fleet.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: The Navy has a habit of locking their gates before a big strike so that only smaller ships can get through. This is a stealth operation: run and gun. You may be flying something small, but you'll take out so much more than your ship should be capable of. Wanton destruction is a rather satisfying feeling, to be sure.

What makes this a great opportunity for us is their fueling depots. Those silos have enough energy stored in them to take out three fleets, if they happen to catch on fire. There may be some guards there, but your main targets are the fuel depots. This is way more bang for your buck than you were expecting, huh?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Congratulations. Pound for pound, you have caused much more destruction than most pilots of your caliber. We've bloodied their noses with this strike. Now, it's time for the knockout punch.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You have no idea how much you frightened the Navy with that last strike. They're completely demoralized and retreating to a rally point in a nearby deadspace pocket. Turns out, they had a carrier waiting in their midst to bring extra destruction to our members. Well, we'll take care of that.

The fleet is pinned down, but we're having trouble getting to them. They've locked themselves in the pocket, only allowing shuttles to get through their gates. We thought we'd have a large siege on our hands, but a rather brilliant idea came to me. I am, of course, a capsuleer like yourself; we think differently than the mortals we have to deal with.

Time for a suicide run. Doesn't that sound like fun? We'll give you a shuttle to take specifically for this mission. (We have quite a stockpile of useless Caldari shuttles, for some reason.) You can join our talented Guristas Capsuleer Fleet, which specializes in suicide missions. Meet with the fleet at the deadspace pocket, pick up some of our “dirty” explosives from a fellow fleet member, and fly at the carrier. You'll lose the shuttle, but you'll take out that carrier. I wish I could go on this mission, but I've got my own orders to follow.

You will lose this shuttle that we have provided you, but you won't get podded. However, you will be a very easy target for wayward pirates in the area. Not to worry, though: You can minimize the risk for this mission. Besides, I'll make sure that you're handsomely rewarded for this effort. Hell, the thrill of the kill should be enough, right?

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: The Navy fleet suffered a significant blow at the fuel depot. They are retreating and have locked themselves in a deadspace pocket. A carrier is there, and the Guristas have organized a fleet of shuttles armed with “dirty” explosives to destroy the remaining Navy ships. This mission is a suicide run of sorts, but the result is supposed to knock the Navy fleet out of commission. Cilis gave me a shuttle, and I am supposed to pick up a “dirty” bomb at the deadspace pocket, then use it to destroy the carrier.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Having fun?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You're quitting this mission because you're scared, aren't you? Coward.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You're declining this mission because you're scared, aren't you? Coward.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: The Navy fleet suffered a significant blow at the fuel depot. They retreated and  locked themselves in a deadspace pocket. A carrier was there, and the Guristas organized a fleet of shuttles armed with “dirty” explosives to destroy the remaining Navy ships. This mission was a suicide run of sorts, but the result knocked the Navy fleet out of commission. Cilis gave me a shuttle, and I picked up a “dirty” bomb at the deadspace pocket, using the explosive in a kamikaze flight to destroy the carrier.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: This is one of the perks of being a capsuleer. When death isn't an issue, you can let yourself go with wild abandon. Ok, enough ruminating: Go deliver that knockout punch to the Navy!

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Time for a suicide run. Doesn't that sound like fun? We'll give you a shuttle to take specifically for this mission. (We have quite a stockpile of useless Caldari shuttles, for some reason.) You can join our talented Guristas Capsuleer Fleet, which specializes in suicide missions. Meet with the fleet at the deadspace pocket, pick up some of our “dirty” explosives from a fellow fleet member, and fly at the carrier. You'll lose the shuttle, but you'll take out that carrier. I wish I could go on this mission, but I've got my own orders to follow.

You will lose this shuttle that we have provided you, but you won't get podded. However, you will be a very easy target for wayward pirates in the area. Not to worry, though: You can minimize the risk for this mission. Besides, I'll make sure that you're handsomely rewarded for this effort. Hell, the thrill of the kill should be enough, right?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Beautiful. You just brought a tear to my eye. This is poetry in motion. Makes me want to get back in my pod again.

We took out that Navy fleet, but something isn't quite right. I'll explain more later. We have a spy to root out.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Abdiel Verat, Angel Cartel.

I look out for talented people such as you who are interested in work. And times have certainly made our work interesting.

Since you're an egger, I'm guessing you know your way around wormholes, yes? While they've been a great aid for our scientists, they've also brought some problems to our doorstop, some of which is not good for business.

Our explorers have discovered a wormhole in a nearby system, but we cannot spare the manpower to lock it down. If you help us out by scouting the area, then I may have other more lucrative tasks to follow.

messages.root.agentsays.text: I'll be waiting for your report. You needn't return here, {[character]player.name}. Just open up comms once you have a clear idea of the situation.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I met with Abdiel Verat, one of the Angel Cartel's capsuleer liaisons.  She had a job for me: scout a nearby wormhole and report the presence of any hostiles.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Then stop wasting my time.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Then stop wasting my time.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The sudden appearance of wormholes across New Eden proved to be a boon to scientific communities of all disciplines. Nearly everyone in the cluster has some vested interest in the wormholes.

The Angel Cartel has been investing heavily into wormhole exploration. They not only scavenge the Sleeper ruins for new technology, but also exploit the wormholes' ability to link otherwise distant points. A wormhole can potentially turn an eighty-jump trip from Curse to Fountain into a twenty-minute jaunt. Although these opportunities represent significant logistical advantages, they are always fleeting, and every effort to map wormhole space has thus far failed.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I met with Abdiel Verat, one of the Angel Cartel's capsuleer liaisons. She had a job for me: scout a nearby wormhole and report the presence of any hostiles. When I arrived I found a gang of Sansha ships already there. She wants it dealt with.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: The wormhole is in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Investigate the area and then report back to me with what you've found.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Abdiel Verat, Angel Cartel.

I look out for talented people such as you who are interested in work. And times have certainly made our work interesting.

Since you're an egger, I'm guessing you know your way around wormholes, yes? While they've been a great aid for our scientists, they've also brought some problems to our doorstop, some of which is not good for business.

Our explorers have discovered a wormhole in a nearby system, but we cannot spare the manpower to lock it down. If you help us out by scouting the area, then I may have other more lucrative tasks to follow.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Sansha. Alright, let me relay this information up the chain of command. Stick around; we'll be calling on you to deal with this.

messages.mission.option1.charsays.text:
You've made your choice then? Alright. Irichi. There is a small chance you may have worked with him before. He was a Lai Dai ordinance engineer who failed one of his annual psychological evaluations. From there, he stowed away aboard a capsuleer's ship heading into lowsec space. His mistake. The capsuleer's crew found him, and he became the capsuleer's toy for two years before he escaped, absolutely insane and missing half of his body parts. We've been taking care of him ever since, and when he's lucid, Irichi is actually quite brilliant. He has made some small recoveries, but we're not out to make him normal. If we did, he might not want to be a pirate any longer. See the problem in that?

The notes you found make a lot more sense under that context, don't they? The fact that he's sending you missives on his “transformation,” or whatever the hell he's calling it, means you're either his favorite culprit at the moment, as is any capsuleer that he comes across, or he suspects someone you're working with. That worries me. Fly out to meet him at his station, and see if he gives you anything to do.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I've come across a problem in my operations. You may have noticed a lot of interloping on the part of other agents. Whether it's Kori trying to get you to show a modicum of mercy to the Navy or, as I strongly suspect, Irichi leaving those messages, I'm done with people trying to influence my business. I can't have all this politics messing with my operations, especially not where a valuable asset like you is concerned.

I want you to choose one of these offenders and follow their activity. They're both so eager to take you off my hands. I suspect one, or both, of them are actively betraying the Guristas in some fashion. Call me paranoid, but I just don't trust them. Thus, you will be my mole and try to determine who is undermining my operations. This previous operation went well, but I suspect some tampering from them. Operations like this don't normally go this well without a major disaster occurring directly afterwards. Let's try to avoid a fiasco, OK?

Once I have this information, I'll be able to send them the appropriate message. No, I'm not going to do anything extreme. I'm not going to do anything as stupid as encourage open infighting while the Navy is so active. Consider this a setting of boundaries; but yes, I'm essentially asking you to help me screw up another agent's operation. We'll see how they like it.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I've been asked to choose between two other Guristas members who have been meddling with Leglise's operations in Venal.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I've chosen an agent to investigate. Cilis suspects this agent has been meddling in her affairs, and she would like me to search for exploitable weaknesses. She admitted that she is essentially asking me to screw up another agent's operations.

messages.mission.option2.charsays.text:
I have a hunch that Kori's our spy. I've been monitoring his transmissions to you in the field, and I'm very sure that he's working with the Navy.

He won't be willing to work with you directly right now. I've arranged for you to meet with one of his operatives, Eroma Eralen. You'll meet him in a deadspace pocket at these coordinates. Be careful, though: Eroma is renowned for his technological ability. He's not good at anything else, but he sure does know his way around illegal pirate tech, especially wavelength and frequency modulation. Meet with him and see what he knows. He owes me a favor, anyway.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Ok, we'll go with your choice.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Alright. Irichi. There is a small chance you may have worked with him before. He was a Lai Dai ordinance engineer who failed one of his annual psychological evaluations. The fact that he's sending you missives on his “transformation,” or whatever the hell he's calling it, means you're either his favorite culprit at the moment, as is any capsuleer that he comes across, or he suspects someone you're working with. That worries me.

Any time he becomes particularly active in this sort of way, somebody gets killed. Don't believe anything he says about me unless you think it's gonna somehow give you an advantage, okay? He's dangerous, and even if he sees you as some kind of instrument, it's not beyond him to kill your for amusement. Be careful.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Cilis has asked me to spy on one of two agents, and I selected Irichi Tsunikabda. He's not exactly stable, and I've been warned that he may try to get me killed. He's also been begging to work with me since the shipyard op. CIlis strongly believes that he's the one who has been leaving those recordings for me.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you reported to Irichi yet?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Very well. I can understand that the prospect of working with Irchi might be off-putting. I'll have someone else look into it. I'll keep my comms open just in case you change your mind. I'm going to urge you to reconsider; this work has to be done, preferably by a knowing accomplice that I trust.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: This is work that needs to be done. I can find someone else to do it, but you're not going to want to disappoint me too often in the future.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I've met with Irichi, and I am now working for him. While I'm under his assignment, Cilis will be monitoring his communications with me in the field to see if they match the signal type of the traitor or if he poses any particular threat to her operations.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Good. You're proving to be as trustworthy as I was hoping you'd be. Show up at his base of operations in PF-QHK. He should be ecstatic to see you.

One last thing: Keep an eye out for my missing lieutenant. I have come to believe that Irichi is somehow responsible for his disappearance.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You've made your choice then? Alright. Irichi. There is a small chance you may have worked with him before. He was a Lai Dai ordinance engineer who failed one of his annual psychological evaluations. The capsuleer's crew found him, and he became the capsuleer's toy for two years before he escaped, absolutely insane and missing half of his body parts.
