That worries me. Fly out to meet him at his station, and see if he gives you anything to do.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I've been begging my handlers to let me get a hold of you. Just look at you, a genuine capsuleer . We have a lot of pretenders around here. They'll do a few things for us here and there and then they'll blow some of our boys out of the sky for the bounties on their heads.

I have my doubts, but we'll see.

I was sent to the Venal region a bit ago. The Navy and other State corps are moving in and trying to clean us honest rogues out, which is why we need to teach them fear.

Ytiri has a base they've built up in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We'll be taking it, but that's not where you fit in. It's not enough to simply take the base: We need to curtail their ability to operate in this region. We need to destroy all of the ships assigned to this base, let them know it's not worth the wasted time and resources in trying to reclaim their property or their territory.

We're going to take that station over in the name of Gurista, and I have just the men to do it. I'll hand over a platoon of soldiers, trained professionals within our ranks. They're known as the Dread Guristas, and this is their strike force. Take them to the base, and let them do their magic. Wait for the strike force to take control while you eliminate any enemies in the sky. Don't worry: They know what they're doing.

But so do you, I guess. Well, I'll give you the reins on this one.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Irichi has a test for me to determine if he could trust me or not. The mission is to deliver a Dread Guristas strike force to an Ytiri base in order to take it over from the inside. While the strike force does its business, I'm supposed to handle the surrounding space, clearing the air while the ground support performs its duty.

messages.root.agentsays.text: What's your status, egger? You lure those ships to their end yet? Or have you lured our guys to theirs?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Who are you?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: About as fickle as I expected. Clear out if you aren't going to contribute. You eggers make the place smell.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Irichi had a test for me to determine if he could trust me or not. The mission was to deliver a Dread Guristas strike force to an Ytiri base in order to take it over from the inside. While the strike force did its business, I handled the surrounding space, clearing the air while the ground support performed its duty.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I'm feeling better about you already. Maybe all those things Cilis and Kori said about you were true after all. We'll see.  It's not as though I trust Cilis. Something about her silhouette is familiar, if you know what I mean? Do you? Come on, you know. You don't?

messages.mission.briefing.text: We're going to take that station over in the name of Gurista, and I have just the men to do it. I'll hand over a platoon of soldiers, trained professionals within our ranks. They're known as the Dread Guristas, and this is their strike force. Take them to the base, and let them do their magic. Wait for the strike force to take control while you eliminate any enemies in the sky. Don't worry: They know what they're doing.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
I'll admit I had doubts about you. You think you can do anything you want to anyone without reason or plan. I think you might be different. Cilis seems to think so. But then again, Cilis was an egger, too.

Anyhow, smash up job. I couldn't be more pleased. I like it when a target is surprised to see death waiting for him. It's one of the most beautiful things you can do as a pirate. The egger who held me taught me that. Her crew chief helped me get away, but the container I was in busted on impact. In the madness, I found myself re-forged. Even though I will kill the person who did this to me, I have to thank them as well for making me what I am.

The recordings you've received in the field are from me. Anyhow, what you did will certainly help, but there's a lot of work to be done, and I can promise you that I'll pay well. You had better have the stomach for it.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Kori is one of the reasons I came over to the Guristas. But he's become soft, and he meddles. I've been monitoring his transmissions to you in the field, and I'm sure he's working with the Navy.

He won't be willing to work with you directly right now. I've arranged for you to meet with one of his operatives, Eroma Eralen. You'll meet him in a deadspace pocket at these coordinates. Be careful, though: Eroma is renowned for his technological ability. He's not good at anything else, but he sure does know his way around illegal pirate tech, especially wavelength and frequency modulation. Meet with him and see what he knows. He owes me a favor, anyway.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I've selected Kori as the agent to investigate. I have to meet his operative, Eroma Eralen, and see if he knows anything about Kori's meddling. Luckily, Eroma owes Cilis a favor, so he should give some information without a hitch.

messages.root.agentsays.text: I'll be contacting you as soon as it's over.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'll leave my comms open in case you want to change your mind. But I'll be watching you: You may be a spy for Kori.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'll leave my comms open in case you want to change your mind. But I'll be watching you: You may be a spy for Kori.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I met with Kori's operative, Eroma Eralen, though I didn't get the information I wanted. Instead, I got some background information on the relationships between Cilis, Kori, and Irichi – they have a long history together. Eroma Eralen is a master of technology, and he was able to string me along that deadspace pocket for quite some time. I finally met him, though, and he gave me some interesting information.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Kori's aware that the two of you are meeting, though he doesn't know what this is about. I don't think he's suspicious. He should be. I want you to be careful on this one. Kori's operative has heard of you. He knows you've been working with me, and Kori teaches his people to be meticulous and paranoid in everything.

It's one of the qualities that I used to find so endearing about him.

In any event, all you have to do is meet with Eroma. Actually, though that sounds easy enough, he'll probably have some tricks up his sleeve.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I have a hunch that Kori's our spy. I've been monitoring his transmissions to you in the field, and I'm very sure that he's working with the Navy.

He won't be willing to work with you directly right now. I've arranged for you to meet with one of his operatives, Eroma Eralen. You'll meet him in a deadspace pocket at these coordinates. Be careful, though: Eroma is renowned for his technological ability. He's not good at anything else, but he sure does know his way around illegal pirate tech, especially wavelength and frequency modulation. Meet with him and see what he knows. He owes me a favor, anyway.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Kipo? At the Rabbit Hole? Why would anyone go there? I wasn't expecting this information. This must mean that Kori is involved, somehow. Now it's personal.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Here are the coordinates for the Rabbit Hole. If Kipo is there, get him and bring him back. He's been missing for a long time, and I've had no leads on his whereabouts. I'll explain on the way. If Kori has anything to do with this, I'll make sure he pays for his this crime. Go get Kipo!

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: According to Kori's operative, Eroma Eralen, Cilis Leglise's missing lieutenant is located at a place known as “The Rabbit Hole.” Cilis suspects that Kori was involved with his kidnapping. I am to visit this place and recover Lt. Kipo.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Kipo?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I can't believe this. Why aren't you helping me get my lieutenant?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I can't believe this. Why aren't you helping me get my lieutenant?

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Irichi and Kori captured one of Cilis Leglise's lieutenants, hiding him at a place called “The Rabbit Hole.” An abandoned Guristas landmark, the place is a profane mockery of the Caldari State's patriotic public works. Irichi and Kori had been working together on this kidnapping, but when I went to retrieve Lt. Kipo, their deal went south. Kori's sentries attacked me, and the Caldari Navy turned up – Kori tipped them off. I recovered Lt. Kipo, whose body was mutilated by Irichi, and I delivered him to Cilis.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: You'll be with me soon, Foxfire. I hope.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Here are the coordinates for the Rabbit Hole. If Kipo is there, get him and bring him back. He's been missing for a long time, and I've had no leads on his whereabouts. I'll explain on the way. If Kori has anything to do with this, I'll make sure he pays for his this crime. Go get Kipo!

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Please give me a minute while I go talk to my lieutenant. We still have work to do. Kori has to pay for this.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Lt. Kipo will never be the same again. He was my best operative, my closest lieutenant, and the best pirate under my command. He is a shell of a man, a mutilated sack of meat, nearly useless as a soldier. I'll have to take care of him, one way or the other…

In the meantime, Kori must pay. I know he's a traitor and has been working for the Caldari Navy. What I don't have is proof, however. Lt. Kipo, though he is mostly unintelligible at this point, was able to form a coherent sentence or two. And that dumb bastard Irichi told him of some of Kori's future plans. Looks like Kori is sending our old friend Eroma to meet with the Navy very soon, and Eralen has a special transponder to get through the tough Navy security. Your mission is to ambush Eralen, grab the transponder, and enter the Caldari base. Once you have this Caldari Navy Overlay Transponder, the Navy ships won't hassle you. I think. I'm looking for a special dossier, Correspondence Log KL-513. That should be everything I need to blackmail Kori and get him out of the Guristas.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Cilis requires proof that Kori is working for the Caldari Navy. Lt. Kipo offered a clue about his next meeting with the State. Eroma Eralen will be meeting with them soon, and he'll have a special transponder to get into their base. My mission is to ambush Eroma, take the transponder, and sneak into the base. Once inside, I am to grab a correspondence log that is proof of Kori's affiliation with the Caldari Navy.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Where're those logs?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Get out of this space, coward. You don't belong with the Guristas.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Get out of this space, coward. You don't belong with the Guristas.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Cilis required proof that Kori was working for the Caldari Navy. Lt. Kipo offered a clue about his next meeting with the State. Eroma Eralen was to meet with them soon, and using a special transponder to get into their base. My mission was to ambush Eroma, take the transponder, and sneak into the base. Once inside, however, Kori alerted the Navy of my presence. It was a scramble to get the evidence, but I eventually did. I received the proof, a correspondence log that included detailed information of Kori's deals with the Caldari Navy. Cilis will use this information to blackmail Kori. Looks like their feud won't end there, though. Cilis had nothing more to offer me, but thanked me for my services. Mission accomplished.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Once you've completed this mission, I will reward you handsomely for your services. I may even have a lieutenant position available soon. We'll see how this goes.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Looks like Kori is sending our old friend Eroma to meet with the Navy very soon, and Eralen has a special transponder to get through the tough Navy security. Your mission is to ambush Eralen, grab the transponder, and enter the Caldari base. Once you have this Caldari Navy Overlay Transponder, the Navy ships won't hassle you. I think. I'm looking for a special dossier, Correspondence Log KL-513. That should be everything I need to blackmail Kori and get him out of the Guristas.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
We're a big, happy family, aren't we? You thought a pirate's life was all fun and plunder, profit and murder, the thrill of being an outlaw. We have our own problems, our internal strife. Sometimes, I don't know why I chose this lifestyle.

But I'm a capsuleer, and life has a different quality to it. You probably know what I'm talking about. All this backstabbing and in-fighting, these land-grabs and territorial bickering. What does this matter for a demigod? For us, it's all a matter of attrition: The last clone standing wins all the worthless, empty space in the universe.

Oh well. It's fun while it lasts, right? Kori was right: This isn't over between us. It never will be. But I'll win out in the end. He'll die, I'll die, Irichi'll die. But then I'll hop into my next clone, and I'll win. That makes it worth it, right?

This feud is between us Guristas; you have your own battles to fight. So fly well, egger. Maybe we'll work together again someday.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Cilis Leglise's lieutenant has been missing for quite some time, and nobody knows where he is. Except for Kori Latamaki and me. Kori helped me capture him and offered to hide him from Cilis. My intentions are pure: I want to cleanse his soul, and by extension, cleanse Cilis's as well. However, that required me to rebuild him, purify him, and make him stronger. You might think I'm a monster, but I assure you that I'm not. Rather, I am here to bring light to the pirates, to show them the true path, to evolve them. Lt. Kipo is the first step in this metamorphosis. His evolution mirrors my own; the others will follow suit.

We are holding him at the Rabbit Hole. I'll give you the coordinates. Fly there and retrieve them; Kori should be expecting you.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Irichi and Kori captured one of Cilis Leglise's lieutenants, and they are now prepared to return him to Cilis. I will be their courier, retrieving Lt. Kipo at a place called “The Rabbit Hole.” Kori should be expecting me.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Do you have Lt. Kipo?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Do you not want to achieve the sublime?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Do you not want to achieve the sublime?

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Irichi and Kori captured one of Cilis Leglise's lieutenants, hiding him at a place called “The Rabbit Hole.” An abandoned Guristas landmark, the place is a profane mockery of the Caldari State's patriotic public works. Irichi and Kori had been working together on this kidnapping, but when I went to retrieve Lt. Kipo, the deal went south. Kori's sentries attacked me, and the Caldari Navy turned up – Kori tipped them off. I recovered Lt. Kipo, whose body was mutilated by Irichi, and now I am to deliver him to Cilis.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I'll explain more when you get there. The Rabbit Hole is special to the Guristas. It was their first step to enlightenment. I will show them the rest of the path.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
The transformation is nearly complete. We are on the road to a new future, the fourth stage of humanity. And it will start with the Guristas.

You have Lt. Kipo, yes? You will deliver him to Cilis. I have let her know that you are en route. Kori may show up, and if he does, I apologize. He has rejected the future and continues to stumble in this aimless void.

I forgot one thing. In exchange for the return of Foxfire, Cilis has promised to give me a special holoreel. This holoreel is very important to my development, and it must be returned to me. Drop Kipo off at the Cilis's headquarters, and then get the holoreel.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Lt. Kipo, though heavily mutilated and modified by Irichi, is ready to be delivered to Cilis Leglise at one of her stations. Once I hand him over to Cilis, she will give me a special holoreel for Irichi.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Do you have my holoreel?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Do you not want to achieve enlightenment?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Do you not want to achieve enlightenment?

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I delivered Lt. Kipo to Cilis Leglise. Shortly after he was returned to her station, it exploded, destroying Cilis's headquarters. Irichi had loaded Kipo's mutilated body with explosives, claiming that Kipo willfully allowed the sacrifice. While attempting to get the holoreel, a Caldari Navy fleet appeared, no doubt at the behest of Kori Latamaki. I fought through the ships and recovered the holoreel. This was the last assignment that Irichi had for me, though it appears that the infighting between the Guristas agents will not cease anytime soon. Regardless, I have completed my objectives with the Guristas pirates and aided them in their battles throughout Venal. Mission accomplished.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Humanity's inherent problem is its constant insistence on adhering to the primal instincts of nature, science, and the hidden rules of the physical world. Once we discover that mind, the inner void of thought and expression, is the ultimate key to enlightenment, then we will become the truly powerful beings of creation. Until then, all of our feuds, our battles, our quarrels, and our tensions will only contribute to the persistent nihilism of eternal space. In a way, my brethren in the Guristas have it right: Nothingness is the way. But they are going about it in the wrong manner. I hope you can help show them the truth.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Cilis must have told you that I was crazy. That might be true; who am I to say? You can judge for yourself, but remember what you have experienced here. I have mastered my transformation; I am now perfect. Can't you tell? Don't you understand?

This bickering among us, between Cilis and Kori and me, must come to an end. If they want to achieve my level of humanity, then this bickering must end, the feuds must stop, and they must trust in their fellow pirate. That is what I hoped to achieve with Lt. Kipo: He was the impetus for change. He accepted his mind, rejected his body, and willfully sacrificed himself for the betterment of the Guristas, and humanity.

The holoreel was a reminder of my life before this incarnation, when social interactions, my body, my loved ones were important to me. A memento mori of a forsaken existence. Thank you; it was the final piece to true understanding.

I doubt that my efforts were successful today. Cilis and Kori will most likely maintain their blood feud, their bitter struggle for supremacy in this meaningless void. I will not relent, however: As long as they continue down that path, I will be there to usher them into a new beginning, the perfect world, and the true way. This will never end until our bodies wither and our minds burn with truth.

Thank you for your services, capsuleer. I know how you demigods value material possessions, so please accept this gift. You have been immeasurably helpful in assisting the Guristas. I hope we may cross paths again in the future. If you ever want to achieve enlightenment, please come find me again.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Listen, {[character]player.name}, the Federation is in dire straits. I'm sure you know that the Caldari megacorporations have “bought” some Gallente systems in Tibus Heth's illegal blind auction. Those bastards have some nerve. But it's time the Federation took it all back!

Nugoeihuvi is attempting to form a foothold in Iges. They've got the early stages of a mining base established and plan to begin production very soon. From the looks of it, Nugoeihuvi plans to be there for a long time. We need you to spoil their plans. Take out all the industrial vessels you can find at this base. Be wary of any escorts, though: they do not look willing to leave.

< font color = #EE3B3B >Be careful: This mission will take you into lowsec. I would recommend switching to a ship designed for inter-capsuleer conflicts, just in case your piratical brethren want a piece of you en route. Once you get to the site itself, though, you shouldn't receive very much resistance. The megacorporations aren't exactly known for the might of their security forces.

messages.mission.extrainfo.header.text:
The Caldari Providence Directorate has today announced the winning bids for their recent auction of Gallente space. Big winners include Kaalakiota and Sukuuvestaa, while Ishukone makes do with just a single system. The winning corporations are now authorized to exploit these systems to the fullest for as long as they remain in Caldari hands.

As expected, the "blind auction" format seems to have made it difficult for even comparatively wealthy sub-megas, such as perennially successful Ytiri, to gain any kind of foothold. All eight megacorps had at least one successful bid, with Suvee leading the charge and claiming fourteen systems. Meanwhile, in a move many are describing as "baffling," Ishukone has laid claim to a single system: Intaki, generally considered the least promising prospect in the auction due to its comparative lack of mineral wealth and vast native population. Sources believe that this was the only bid Ishukone made, and several political commentators have questioned where the financially struggling megacorp managed to find the money.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you taken out the mining base yet?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I hope you don't expect me to show good favor toward you in the future. Declining this mission was a poor course of action.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: The Caldari must pay for their pride.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Welcome, {[character]player.name}. I'm told you want to learn some of the more advanced aspects of warfare.

A friend of mine has been summoned to a face-to-face meeting by a local pirate cartel, who've recently been attempting to blackmail him. I want you to take my friend's place and kill these criminals.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Good work out there. As a show of thanks, my friend passed along part of the blackmail money he'd accumulated. You're clearly ready for bigger things, so let me know when you're ready to learn more.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. I'll tell my friend to stand by while you deal with the problem. Good luck out there, {[character]player.name}. Show us all what you're made of.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We've discovered the headquarters of the pirate group you dispatched in your last mission, and it's time to take them out for good. I'm going to give you a frigate loaded with proximity-based explosive charges, and your job is to fly it directly into their headquarters.

As your frigate explodes, you'll be perfectly safe inside your capsule, so just relax and get back to me when you're done.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
Good work. You've now seen for yourself that losing a ship isn't the end of the world. You capsuleers have a saying, though: "Don't fly what you can't afford to lose." If you stick to affordable ships and modules, you'll be able to learn without risking everything you own.

When you're ready for another assignment, let me know.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Here is the frigate, then. Good luck out there.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Next up is a kind of interdiction called warp disruption. When activated on another targeted ship, these kinds of modules "tackle" it, disabling its warp drive.

Tackling only works if you keep the target within your module's range and can overpower its Warp Strength. A Warp Disruptor lowers a ship's Warp Strength by 1, while the more powerful Warp Scrambler modules reduce it by 2.

I'll give you a Civilian Warp Disruptor to test out on a pirate that escaped from the headquarters you just blew up. Pin him down, but don't blow him up.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
Nicely done, {[character]player.name}. It looks like our pirate friends got the message loud and clear. Hopefully you understand the basics of warp disruption now. There's more to it, of course, but regardless of how each different type of module works, the principle is always the same – pin them down and keep them there.

Next up, I want to show you something a little more on the defensive end of things. Let me know when you're ready for the next assignment.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Great. Remember, I don't want him dead; just scare him and then get out. It'll send more of a message to the others than just killing him will.

But of course, if he has any escorts, feel free to wipe them out. We'll be watching from a safe distance to make sure you carry out these instructions properly.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Remote repair capabilities can often prove useful, as they increase your companions' chance of withstanding concentrated fire from the enemy. Remote assistance isn't limited to repair modules, either - it may include enhancements of your allies' electronics systems (Remote Sensor Boosting), their gun tracking, and other functions.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A vessel nearby was attacked by pirates, with the only survivor left for dead in a disabled vessel. We need you to repair his ship with Remote Shield Booster modules, so he can return to safety. Let me stress again that you are to repair the vessel. Not blow it up. I know you capsuleers have an itchy trigger finger at the best of times.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Good work out there. Our agent reported a safe journey back home. I hope you've come to learn something in the process, too. I arranged for a skill book to be made available to you as a reward. If you're interested in the use of shield transfer modules, then you'll want to train it up eventually.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good, but please hurry, his ship is venting oxygen as we speak.

I arranged for a skill book to be made available to you as a reward. If you're interested in the use of remote armor repair modules, then you'll want to train it up eventually.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good, but please hurry, his ship is venting oxygen as we speak.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
There are various situations where you may end up drawing fire, either by accident or intention, and risking the loss of your ship.

You may be scouting a dangerous area that turns out to contain an enemy fleet, or acting as bait to draw fire from enemy ships. The rule remains the same: Never fly anything you cannot afford to lose.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Alright, this next assignment is going to test your nerves. We're sending you into a much larger and better defended pirate base. It is unlikely you will defeat all their forces; just put up the best fight you can before being destroyed.

I'll provide you with a combat frigate, but you'll have to fit it with your own modules. I'd keep the fittings cheap — you're not expected to come out of this one intact, although we do expect you to make at least one kill.

Let me stress this point, {[character]player.name}: We want you to kill at least one pirate and then hold out as long as you can, so you may not leave the area until your ship has been destroyed or by some miracle, you survive the fight. Use the frigate I'm giving you since if you lose your own, I will not be replacing it.

messages.mission.extrainfo.header.text: Putting your ship on the line

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Not bad, {[character]player.name}. You did well out there against overwhelming odds. Hopefully, that allowed you to wrestle with the threat of ship loss. In these early days, you probably won't find yourself in such challenging situations, but it's helpful to know how to face them. Whether you lose a ship or not, you can always rise to the next challenge.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Welcome back. Now we're going for speed.

You can use two types of active propulsion modules: Afterburners and their bigger brother Microwarpdrives (or MWDs). We're about to teach you how to use Afterburners.

Afterburners don't increase your speed as drastically as MWDs, but they suffer less penalties: They use only a moderate amount of capacitor to run and cannot be disabled by Warp Scramblers. Afterburners are also much easier to fit to your ship - they use less power grid and less CPU, and have no fitting penalties.

We've got an area riddled with dangerous electromagnetic interference that will damage your ship periodically. Your task is to fly through the clouds of EM disturbance using an Afterburner, and make it to the other side in one piece.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
Good work — you made it through the gauntlet alive.

You should take a moment to consider all that you've learned so far and how it all ties together. No module works in isolation. Warp Scramblers, for example (the close-range interdiction modules), don't work well unless you can close in on your enemy, and for that you need an Afterburner. Similarly, if you're using a Warp Disruptor, the long-range variants, you will perhaps want to keep your enemy away from you… so again, Afterburners become useful. Dictating range is a crucial aspect of any engagement, but when you are tackling, it becomes particularly important.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good luck out there. Just keep the Afterburner going and don't look back.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We Minmatar use projectile guns, the best option of all. We don't need any capacitor to fire our weapons, unlike Amarr lasers, which can run a ship dry of capacitor in a matter of minutes. We also have the best weapons for skirmish tactics, allowing us to hit and run with ease.

We've cornered a pirate nearby. I'll provide you with a Civilian Gatling Autocannon, and I hope you finish him off with it.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
Excellent work out there. Ideally, you've built a little on your understanding of our nation's warfare methods.

Just keep in mind that if you prefer one system over another, you can train into it. None of the empires restrict access to their weapons technology. Of course, Minmatar weapons work best on Minmatar ships, which often give exclusive bonuses to fitting Projectile weapons — so if you tend to like any other type of weapon system, then chances are you'll want to train or cross-train into that race's starships as well.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent, good luck out there. I suggest you use the weapon I gave you — it's part of the training process.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We Amarr use lasers, the best option of all. Lasers employ reuseable ammunition, which means you won't run dry in the middle of a fight. They deal Electromagnetic (EM) and Thermal damage, a particularly potent combination against ships that use shield boosting instead of armor repair. Shields are vulnerable to EM damage, and lasers can dish out a lot of it.

We've cornered a pirate nearby. I'll provide you with a Civilian Gatling Pulse Laser, and I hope you finish him off with it.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:

Just keep in mind that if you prefer one system over another, you can train into it. None of the empires restrict access to their weapons technology. Of course, Amarr weapons work best on Amarr ships, which often give exclusive bonuses to fitting Laser weapons — so if you tend to like any other type of weapon system, then chances are you'll want to train or cross-train into that race's starships as well.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent, good luck out there. I suggest you use the weapon I gave you — it's part of the training process.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Alongside Hybrid guns, we Caldari use missiles, the best option of all. While weapons from other factions damn near lock you into dealing a single type of damage - EM, Thermal, Kinetic or Explosive - Caldari missiles can deal any kind, and we can switch them out on the fly. We even have Auto-Targeting Missiles that don't require you to lock on to the enemy, which is particularly useful when your electronics systems have been compromised.

We've cornered a pirate nearby. I'll provide you with a Civilian Light Missile Launcher, and I hope you finish him off with it.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:

Of course, Caldari weapons work best on Caldari ships, which often give exclusive bonuses to fitting our weapons — so if you tend to like any other type of weapon system, then chances are you'll want to train or cross-train into that race's starships as well.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent, good luck out there. I suggest you use the weapon I gave you — it's part of the training process.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Alongside Hybrid guns, we Gallente use drones, the best option of all. They are highly versatile, with different types capable of anything from head-on rush tactics to electronic disruption. Moreover, they can allow you to fight from a safe distance - in fact, if someone compromises your electronics system and you can't even lock them, your drones will sense that aggression and come to your aid. The only limits to their number are your ship's drone bay and its drone bandwidth.

We've cornered a pirate nearby. I'll provide you with a Civilian Drone, and I hope you finish him off with it.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
Excellent work out there. Ideally, you've built a little on your understanding of our nation's warfare methods.

Just keep in mind that if you prefer one system over another, you can train into it. None of the empires restrict access to their weapons technology. Of course, Gallente weapons work best on Gallente ships, which often give exclusive bonuses to fitting Hybrid weapons or drones — so if you tend to like any other type of weapon system, then chances are you'll want to train or cross-train into that race's starships as well.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent, good luck out there. I suggest you use the weapon I gave you — it's part of the training process.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Capsuleer fleets fight each other by focusing their fire on a single enemy ship, killing it swiftly and moving on to the next target in a prioritized fashion. These priorities, with targets often designated "primary" and "secondary", will be communicated by the FC and should be heeded.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Fleet Warfare is common in New Eden, and in any fleet, the Fleet Commander (often referred to as 'FC') is the most important voice to listen to.

For your next assignment, you will join one of our local anti-piracy fleets as auxiliary support for a hostage rescue. You will take your orders from a local CONCORD FC, and your job will be explained to you once you arrive at the perimeter of the base. Follow the instructions carefully; the lives of those hostages and the completion of your own training depend on it.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Well done out there. You followed your orders, as I hoped you would. There's a lot more to being a competent fleet pilot, of course, but so often it is these simple lessons that are forgotten the fastest. Discipline counts for a great deal.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Alright, good luck then. Pay close attention to your orders as they are given; don't just charge in and start shooting.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Stasis Webifiers are most commonly known as "webs" or "webbers".  They work very well in combination with Warp Scramblers - using them both on the same target will scramble it for two "points", halve its speed, and render it unable to use Microwarpdrives. Without a scrambler, a target may use its MWD to escape you.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We're returning to interdiction tactics by having you test out a Stasis Webifier module. When activated on a target ship, the Stasis Webifier will encase it in a containment field and slow it down dramatically.

Time for you to see for yourself. We've chased a pirate down to a nearby hideout and we want you to pin him down. We'll provide you with a Civilian Stasis Webifier, and you may want to fit an afterburner, too.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text:
Nicely done. You applied just the right amount of firepower necessary, something which can often yield more than outright slaughter.

You've almost completed your training with us. Once you're done, we plan to recommend you to our nation's capsuleer militia: The Tribal Liberation Force. What you have learned from us would be quickly overshadowed by what you could learn while fighting to free your brothers and sisters. You might think money would be a more suitable reward, but reputation matters a great deal in New Eden, and so does finding somewhere you can call a home.

To belong to the Liberation Force though, you must prove yourself as a combat pilot. That is what lies ahead, {[character]player.name} — get a combat ship fitted out and get yourself ready for a fight.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Be prepared for him to use a Warp Disruptor and Stasis Webifier. I do not suggest you fit Warp Core Stabilizers, though - they will negatively impact your locking time and locking range, and take up precious low power slots that could be used to increase your damage, your capacitor recharge, or your repair abilities.

Also, keep your eyes on the prize: Your primary target is the terrorist, not his wingmen, and it's your call whether you need to take them down as well. If you do, you may need to start by picking off the weakest targets from a distance, possibly with varying ammunition types.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Alright, time to apply everything you've learned. One of our patrols has spotted a group of suspicious vessels headed towards a local pleasure hub. One of the pilots is a known terrorist responsible for dozens of station bombings.

A CONCORD raid would alert them too early and we'd risk the terrorist escaping. We need this murderer taken out while we have his location, so you must move in by yourself and assassinate him.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Excellent work, {[character]player.name}! You've proven you know how to handle yourself in deadly situations.

We can always use good pilots like yourself, you should consider enlisting in Factional Warfare, where you can fight alongside other pilots pledged to the Republic. If instead, you would rather broaden your skills, you can start a conversation with any of my fellow Career Agents right here in this station.

Whatever you choose to do next, I thank you for the help you've given us. Fly safe, Captain.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Stay focused out there, {[character]player.name}. Once you commit yourself to this fight, it won't end until one of you loses a ship.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
We're going to be stepping back on this one and letting you take control of the situation. One of our patrols spotted a small group of suspicious vessels headed towards a local pleasure hub. After processing their ship's ID tags, we've determined that one of the pilots is a known terrorist responsible for dozens of station bombings.

A CONCORD raid into the premises would be picked up by the terrorists well before the ships actually arrived. We need this murderer taken out while we have his location, so you must move in yourself and then assassinate him, understand?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Excellent work, {[character]player.name}! You've proven you know how to handle yourself in deadly situations.

We can always use good pilots like yourself, you should consider enlisting in Factional Warfare, where you can fight alongside other pilots pledged to the Empire. If instead, you would rather broaden your skills, you can start a conversation with any of my fellow Career Agents right here in this station.

Whatever you choose to do next, I thank you for the help you've given us. Fly safe, Captain.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Stay focused out there, {[character]player.name}. Once you commit yourself to this fight, it won't end until one of you loses a ship.

Whatever you choose to do next, I thank you for the help you've given us. Fly safe, Captain.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
So you want to fly for the Guristas? Welcome aboard, egger. You get to do some rookie stuff.

We've leaked information on the location of a particularly rich group of asteroids within Venal. We expect a Minedrill expedition to show up soon, and we want someone to be there to greet them. You can expect their expedition to be made up of several combat escorts and an industrial.

Take out the industrial and grab its crew. Knowing Minedrill, this'll just be a research team – they need to test the rocks first before sending in those expensive barges. But once we have their people, we can mine their personnel for any intelligence on future ops.

If you haven't picked up on this already, we're a cautious bunch. We like to make sure whatever op we run goes off right. We have weapon caches, safe houses, and agents everywhere we plan to operate, even in empire space. The Guristas have contingencies for everything, even in dealing with someone like you.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: I've contacted Kori Latamaki, a mission planner for the Guristas. He directed me to lie in wait for a Minedrill expedition. I'm supposed to dispose of the combat escorts and take the Minedrill industrial crew.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I knew that we were taking a gamble by using a capsuleer. Get out of here, and go back to your safety net. Good luck with those bubble camps, though.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I knew that we were taking a gamble by using a capsuleer. Get out of here, and go back to your safety net. Good luck with those bubble camps, though.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: I ambushed a Minedrill expedition and took the Minedrill crew prisoners. Latamaki seems confident that they'll be providing useful information in the very near future. He presumes that Minedrill is gathering resources for the Navy, and that my help will be needed again soon.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: We're not just a bunch of swashbuckling goons. Despite the slander from the empires, we know what we're doing, and we're damn good at it. Stick with us, egger. You'll get rich if you do.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Wait for the Minedrill expedition. When they arrive, take out the expedition fleet and bring back the industrial's crew.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great. We should be getting reliable intelligence from them soon. If I were you, I'd take it easy for a bit. Based on Minedrill's recent activity, it's fair to say they have a major contract with somebody; probably the Navy.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Have they shown up yet? What's your status?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Aren't you the lucky one? All the carnage you've inflicted on our enemies has caught the attention of SARO. They are the best that CONCORD has to offer, and they're not to be balked at.

This particular SARO pilot's name is Treonis, and she's been asking for you personally. My guess? Taking you out is her bid at a promotion.

Normally, we would launch a whole campaign to remove CONCORD scum from our space, but my superiors want to see you handle this situation. If you can destroy Treonis, I'm authorized to reward you with a single run blueprint for one of our rarer ships, the Cynabal.

Treonis is waiting for you by an abandoned colony in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Destroy her, and the blueprint is yours.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: My exploits caught the attention of a SARO agent named Treonis. The Angels would normally handle the disposal of a CONCORD pilot on their own, but someone high up in the Cartel wants to use this as a final test. If I can eliminate Treonis, the Angels will reward me with a Cynabal BPC.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: My superiors will be disappointed. We do not offer our technology to just anyone.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: My superiors will be disappointed. We do not offer our technology to just anyone.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Despite CONCORD's strong association with empire space, they occasionally sponsor larger campaigns out in nullsec. These excursions are targeted at the "pirate" factions under the justification of returning the violence committed in high security space. CONCORD's Special Affairs for Regulations & Order (SARO) is uniquely suited for these campaigns. Their training, hardware, and skill make them a threat not to be taken lightly.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text:
My exploits caught the attention of a SARO agent named Treonis. Normally the Angels would handle the disposal of a CONCORD pilot on their own. After I fought other pirate factions, destroyed capsuleers, and drove out an empire corporation, someone high up in the Cartel wanted to use the extermination of a CONCORD pilot as a final test.

I passed.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I envy your chance to space a CONCORD pilot.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
All the carnage you've inflicted on our enemies has caught the attention of a SARO pilot, Treonis. Taking you out is her bid at a promotion. My superiors want to see you handle this situation alone.

Treonis is waiting for you by an abandoned colony in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Destroy her, and the blueprint is yours.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
My superiors are impressed. It's the rare pilot who can take on SARO agents and live.

Take this blueprint as a sign of our appreciation, not only for what you've done, but also for what you have become. I'm sure we'll be crossing paths again someday, whether you realize it or not.

Fly safe, {[character]player.name}. Remind the galaxy why they fear Angels.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Is that SARO pilot, Treonis, still alive?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Hey, {[character]player.name}, ever been screwed over by the big corporations? Well, here's a chance for some payback. There's controversy out in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system, where ORE lays dubious mining claim to a massive asteroid field. Problem is, independent groups working the field are at risk of being consumed – literally. There's something strange going on out there. Interested in finding out what's happening, and striking a blow for the little guy?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Yes, I suppose the blood money offered elsewhere might be more lucrative.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Yes, I suppose the blood money offered elsewhere might be more lucrative.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good, because there's no time to lose. We received a distress signal from a small operation. They were trying to get what they could from the field before the ORE hulks blew through. Something seems to have gone wrong. Find out what happened and save the crew, materiel and product that you can.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Travel to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system where miners are in conflict over an asteroid field. Find out what's happened to a small, independent mining operation fallen silent. Also, keep an eye on any messages in your Local channel. I don't want you bringing the crew back here, but they might need to be moved to someplace safe.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: What's your progress on offering aid to those miners? Without their independent streak, the big corps might take over that entire system. And don't be bringing any of the miners to my front door, either.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
While I enjoy the tremendous service capsuleers provide agents like me, I can't begin to count how many times I've been let down over the years by those lacking the proper skills, judgment, diligence, or a rudimentary attention span. It seems that the last few I hired to provide an armed escort for a convoy of civilian transports has gone missing, probably lured away by a more lucrative job.

I need you to head to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and meet up with the convoy at once. If they‘re in any kind of trouble when you arrive, please take care of it.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You're kidding me, right?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: What a surprise.  Yet another unreliable capsuleer.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Well done fending off those pirates. Some of them escaped, you say?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: There's really no more time to waste with conversation.  Head out at once.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A convoy of civilian ships traveling through a region known to be rife with pirate activity has become vulnerable due to its contingent of escort combat vessels not showing up for some reason.  Their distress signal has been picked up in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: You shouldn't be chatting with me when you have work to do.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Hey, {[character]player.name}, ever been screwed over by the big corporations? Well, here's a chance for some payback.
