Find out what's happened to a small, independent mining operation fallen silent. Also, keep an eye on any messages in your Local channel. I don't want you bringing the crew back here, but they might need to be moved to someplace safe.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: There's hope yet for the small entrepreneur! ORE's dismissive attitude toward miner claims in that system has brought a lot of bad publicity on the corporation. Your efforts have gone a long way toward causing that.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: What's your progress on offering aid to those miners? Without their independent streak, the big corps might take over that entire system. And don't be bringing any of the miners to my front door, either.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
The Seven? I was hoping it wasn't that particular gang again.

While we're very grateful that you managed to prevent most of the civilians from being kidnapped, there is still the issue of the ones that were taken. When they warped away from the last encounter, we were able to track them down and obtain the coordinates of that hideout. I'm prepared to grant you the authority, on behalf of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}, to hunt down these criminals. What do you say? Are you still willing to help?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Hey, I understand.  We all have priorities in life.  Mine just happen to be productivity, compassion, and loyalty, while yours appear to be somewhere between lethargy and unscrupulousness.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Whatever.  I'll find someone else to clean up your mess.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: I'd flatter you with congratulations, but there's still work to be done.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Great!  You should depart at once if you're going to catch the Seven before the hostages are moved to another facility.

messages.mission.briefing.text: After only being able to make off with a fraction of the civilians from their raid, The Seven were tracked back to their hideout.  Attacking them there should eliminate their local base of operations and allow for the remaining hostages to be rescued.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: It might be a good idea to maintain radio silence during this particular mission, don't you think?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
One of those hostages you rescued turned out to be quite resourceful. While aboard the pirate's vessel, she hacked into its communication logs and discovered something interesting. One of The Seven's core members, a man named Phenod, has managed to strand himself in space on his way to pick up some victims that were kidnapped some time ago.

We have a golden opportunity here to not only strike a blow to The Seven, but recover some of our earlier losses as well. Head out to these coordinates at once and blast Phenod to pieces, but be sure to scrape some of his DNA off the front of your ship before returning. We'll use it to forge an identification transponder for your next mission.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Seriously?  Phenod is too much for you to handle?  I've heard he's The Seven's resident idiot.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Am I going to have to take care of this myself?

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Stick around, there's more to do.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Quickly, before he gets away!

messages.mission.briefing.text: Phenod, the resident idiot of The Seven's organization, has stranded himself on his way to pick up some hostages.  With his DNA, a suitable transponder disguise can be forged allowing some undercover work against the gang.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Do you have a sample of Phenod's DNA yet?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I hope you didn't have too much trouble with Phenod.

Our engineers have completed the fake transponder and installed it in a shuttle, which is ready for you to take it to the rendezvous point. The story is that Phenod's ship was disabled and he's been forced to limp to the rendezvous point in an ordinary shuttle. I don't know who's going to meet you there, but it'll probably be another officer from The Seven, so try not to pick a fight. Remember, this shuttle is unarmed and doesn't have any real defenses, so if your disguise fails, you'll have to make a run for it.

Oh, and there's one last thing: That shuttle doesn't have the oxygen capacity to hold that many people for very long, so you won't be able to make it back here. We're sending a rescue vessel to linger nearby, but for obvious reasons it can't be anywhere inside sensor range of this meeting. Use the acceleration gate in the area to meet up with it and drop off the hostages.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Oh well, let's just hope CONCORD doesn't see you in that shuttle broadcasting a pirate faction signature.  Good luck!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: So you've gotten this far only to give up now?

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Now that was some really impressive flying, I have to admit!  The hostages are quite grateful to have been returned safely.  In fact, I have a message for you from one of them, if you can stick around for a minute or two.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Not many capsuleers volunteer for this kind of duty outside the comforts of their preferred ship.  I admire your courage.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Using Phenod's DNA to concoct a disguised transponder beacon, the shuttle provided by the agent should be large enough to retrieve the additional hostages and bring them to safety.  The only problem is that, if whoever shows up to drop off the hostages isn't fooled, the shuttle will be unable to respond.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Shh!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Here's the rescued hostage's message:

“Brave Capsuleer,

Allow me to offer my sincere thanks for your efforts to rescue me and my fellow hostages from the clutches of The Seven. If you would be interested, I've offered {[character]agentID.name} a sum of ISK to pay you in exchange for doing me a little favor.

During my time with The Seven, one of their officers was so cruel that I‘m inclined to seek revenge on a personal level. Seeing as you have become quite familiar with their organization and tactics, I can think of no one better suited for carrying out this task. Please destroy his ship for me.

If you‘re interested, the target‘s name is Locced and I happen to know where he‘ll be in the near future, as one of his lieutenants let the information slip during casual conversation when I was nearby.

Once again, thank you for freeing me from The Seven‘s clutches. I hope you find my offer appealing.“

Well, {[character]player.name}, what do you say?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm going to assume Locced beat you down like a helpless child, at least that's what I'm going to tell every other capsuleer I deal with from this point forward.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: That former hostage is going to be heartbroken.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: The former hostage will be very excited to hear you accepted the offer.  Here are Locced's coordinates.

messages.mission.briefing.text: One of the hostages rescued during the previous mission has offered a reward for destroying Locced's ship and provided coordinates to his current location.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
What am I, your receptionist? Here's another message from that hostage you rescued:

“Trustworthy Capsuleer,

It's going to take Locced quite a while to replace that ship. Well done, and thank you again for all of your efforts against The Seven.”

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: The former hostage is eagerly awaiting news of your victory.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: {[character]player.name}, a mission of mercy needs your immediate attention. One of our ships has suffered an almost complete power loss near a spatial rift, and is adrift toward the anomaly. There's no time to lose. Get to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, find the ship, and help get it operational again.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: {[character]player.name}, what are you doing? Our people are going to die out there. “Can't do it?” You mean “Won't do it”! Bloody pirate!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: What? Maybe I didn't make myself clear. There are lives at stake!

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. You have no time to lose.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Travel to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} here a disabled ship is in jeopardy. Save the crew by addressing whatever problem afflicts the vessel.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work. Your efforts have not gone unnoticed. We'll try to get that model upgraded to avoid this kind of problem again.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: What are you doing? Our people are dying in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. There's no time for this!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
{[character]player.name}? Good. I have a job that's probably outside your normal scope. This one is humanitarian.

A pandemic has broken out on a planet in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Fortunately, a cure was already developed and mass-produced. The contagion originated on another planet nearby, you see, so the people of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} already have experience in dealing with this particular disease.

The Sisters of Eve sent a medical drone with the vaccine onboard down to the planet, but some degenerate pirates have intercepted the craft, disabled it, and are now trying to demand a ransom for its release. The Sisters say that if the drone is destroyed it could be days before we can mass-produce more vaccine – something about being unable to accelerate the bacterial cultivation. A few more days with this disease uncontrolled could mean everything. We must recapture the drone.

We're depending on you here, {[character]player.name}. Once you've secured the drone, they can deploy repair teams and send it back on its way.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I should have known. Your kind disgusts me.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: What? You're telling me profit is more important than innocent lives?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: You're doing the right thing. Countless lives depend on you.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
A pandemic has broken out on a planet in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Fortunately, a cure was already developed and mass-produced. The contagion originated on another planet, you see, so the people of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} have experience in dealing with this particular disease.

The Sisters of Eve sent a medical drone with the vaccine onboard down to the planet, but some degenerate pirates have intercepted the craft and are trying to ransom it. The SSoE say that if the drone is destroyed, it could be days before we can mass-produce more vaccine – something about being unable to accelerate the bacterial cultivation. A few more days with this disease uncontrolled could mean everything. We must recapture the drone.

Once you've secured the drone, they can deploy repair teams and send it back on its way.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You've done a great thing! Countless people owe you their lives. We should have just enough time to get the medicine to the planet. The Sisters are coordinating with Mordu's Legion this time. They'll escort it safely to the people of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: We don't have any time to waste. Get moving.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ever heard of The Anomaly? Lots of superstition around that name - it's one of our ships that vanished completely while testing an experimental jump drive. A trading vessel heard The Anomaly's signal last week and so we sent out a salvage crew, The Paryi, to investigate the site where it reappeared, but something went wrong. We received The Paryi's distress call yesterday and can't make sense of it. It seems some of them were killed in an explosion near The Anomaly, and the survivors escaped in life pods but are trapped there by gravity waves exuding from the ship. But the other things they said… well, some of them must have cracked under the stress. If there were any survivors from The Anomaly, they would've contacted us, after all.

You need to rescue The Paryi's survivors, especially Dr. Fajah Ateshi. Once we learn what they uncovered, we'll have a better sense of how to proceed. The Anomaly was a very expensive project, and some very powerful people are invested in figuring out how it vanished.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: That's your call. Honestly, I don't blame you for backing out now - I'm not superstitious, but this situation spooks me out.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: That's your call. Honestly, I don't blame you for backing out now - I'm not superstitious, but this situation spooks me out.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Great job, risking your neck like that! I mean, I'm sure there was no risk at all - in any case, we've already spoken with Dr. Ateshi about how to proceed.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. There are at least three survivors who escaped in life pods. Find them, and we'll be able to figure out what went wrong. And be careful out there - it's an experimental ship, and we don't know what kind of threat it might pose.

messages.mission.briefing.text: You need to rescue The Paryi's survivors and learn what they know. The Anomaly was a very expensive project and some very powerful people are invested in figuring out how it vanished.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Have you rescued the crew of The Paryi yet? I've got some very important people breathing down my neck about this.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We've spoken with Fajah Ateshi about The Anomaly, and I'm afraid things look dire. Her readings were damaged from the explosion aboard The Paryi, and she needs to return to The Anomaly to get further information. Since the two of you are the only ones who've come near the ship and retained both your lives and sanity, we have to send you out again.

We're still not entirely sure if anyone is alive aboard there, though Dr. Ateshi insists that she heard garbled transmissions from survivors disoriented from radiation sickness. I tell you, all this mystery doesn't make me comfortable, and it makes the people at the top very, very unhappy. If you find survivors, excellent, but your survival and Dr. Ateshi's readings are more important. You need to attach her Neurowave Pattern Scanner to The Anomaly.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I don't think you understand what you're turning down here. The fate of The Anomaly is important to a great many very powerful people, and they won't be happy.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I don't think you understand what you're turning down here. The fate of The Anomaly is important to a great many very powerful people, and they won't be happy.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Finally, we have all the information necessary to make an informed decision. I'll see what Dr. Ateshi has to say.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. Dr. Ateshi will accompany you to the ship and give you details on delivering the scanner. Get in, drop the scanner, get out.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Travel to The Anomaly and deliver the Neurowave Pattern Scanner.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Have you delivered the Neurowave Pattern Scanner yet? There's a lot of pressure on me to get this done.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Dr. Ateshi has provided proof that The Anomaly is active and dangerous. The experimental warp drive successfully opened a wormhole, but it was unstable and the resulting radiation fried the crew's equipment, and their brains. They've been trapped in the darkest parts of space for two decades, slowly succumbing to the sickness - there's nothing human left about them. Now that they're back in our space, the radiation is a risk not just to us but everything for hundreds of kilometers around.

My superiors have determined that it's not worth the risk of retrieving the warp drive; you need to destroy the ship entirely before the damage spreads. Fortunately, we know where they went: They jumped into the middle of a rogue drone hive. Dr. Ateshi thinks they're trying to feed off the rogue drones' power to recharge. If you can get her to one of the surrounding ships, she can jam their equipment and make them vulnerable.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: After coming so far? Do you know what they're going to do to me when they find out you quit?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: After coming so far? Do you know what they're going to do to me when they find out you quit?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I'm so relieved to hear that. Keep your wits about you and you should do just fine. Remember, don't bother shooting until Dr. Ateshi has deactivated their shield rechargers.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Destroy The Anomaly before it can do further damage. Bring Dr. Ateshi to the rogue drone hive where the ship is hiding so that she can deactivate its shields.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Shame about Dr. Ateshi, but she knew the risks. Good job - you've earned everything coming to you.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Have you destroyed The Anomaly yet? It's essential that you do it before it has the chance to jump away again!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Hey there, {[character]player.name}. I've got a routine run for you...just a second. I've got emergency messages coming in. Hm. You up for a rescue mission?

I just received an alert across multiple communication channels asking for evacuation help. A diplomatic station, not far from here, is undergoing a traumatic systems shut-down cascade. It's all going, and people need off that station. The rescue requires a smaller ship than what they have available to get in past the field of debris now ringing the station.

That's what happens when none of the empires will trust the others enough to allow them to send in their best station engineers and construction teams, and so they all agree on a third-party freelance company to build their stations. Happens all the time, I hear. Ridiculous.
Anyway – are you interested?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Really? That's it? You're quitting? Why'd you agree to do it in the first place, then?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Can't say I blame you, though I'm going to have to let you go for now. Getting these kinds of jobs filled can bring an agent like me to the notice of important people, you know? Talk to you later.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Great. You get out there, and you've got some rescue money coming your way. I don't really care who you rescue, just so long as you rescue someone. Fair warning, though – the ones you don't rescue are likely to remember it.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A diplomatic station not far from here is undergoing a traumatic systems shut-down cascade. It's all going, and people need off that station.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good job, {[character]player.name}. Enjoy your reward, and the limelight for being a hero to those folks – you've earned it. You should know, however, that the folks you didn't save have already made it very clear that they're not happy with you.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: How's that rescue operation going?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Have you heard those crazy sermons that people are talking about? The ones delivered by this self-proclaimed “prophet” who calls himself Tolmak? Yeah, that freak who's trying to create a religion. He's got a lot of converts among the discontents of our little corner of the universe. But he's also got a lot of enemies, people who don't like what he's been spewing. People who might try to kill him. Thing is, certain powerful people find him useful. A nice distraction from more political pursuits. They'd like him alive.

One of his acolytes set up shop in our little corner of the universe and began preaching to the locals. This “priest” is not exactly causing trouble, but he's making certain powerful people uncomfortable. Not only that, but we've heard reports of violence against this cult in other sectors. We'd like to quietly remove this man from the picture and avoid any possibility for backlash in our own areas. At the same time, we don't want to make a martyr out of him and build further support for this cult. The situation needs to be handled discreetly.

He's currently preaching on Yunshin Z, a refining complex. This is a low population industrial center with little contact to the outside world. We can afford to make bold moves here. Your task is to find this preacher and return him to us. We'll handle the rest.

messages.mission.extrainfo.header.text: The Prophet of the Seventh Sphere

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Disappointing, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Very well, I'll find someone else.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Religious freaks like to spread all sorts of apocalyptic messages, and in recent times there are few who have captured the imagination of conspiracy theorists in the way that Tolmak has. The so-called “Prophet of the Seventh Sphere,” Tolmak is an enigmatic and elusive character. He has never shown himself publicly for fear of reprisal, and relies instead of proxies to spread his word. Others say his real strength comes from the media outlets that cover these preachers. Outlets that, for their own part, are mostly concerned with the profit to be made from the inevitable controversy his message brings.

Among other things, Tolmak's elaborate revelations paint a universe governed by demonic forces that secretly control the heads of all the empires. He reserves special bile for the capsuleer class, teaching that their clones are not actually the same person reborn, but are instead, demonic simulacra.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Be careful out there, {[character]player.name}. We've also had reports of unusual fleet movements around the refinery. You may not be the only one looking for this preacher.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Have you heard those crazy prophecies which have been picking up publicity? No, not Macaper's, I mean the ones delivered by this “prophet” who calls himself Tolmak?

In any case, all you need to know is that this fool is trying to create his own religion, and he's had some successes recently in building up his numbers. It seems each new day he lures more discontented people into his cult, and recently we've been affected by this new trend.

One of his acolytes set up shop in our little corner of the universe and began preaching to the locals. This “priest” is not exactly causing trouble, but he's making certain powerful people uncomfortable. Not only that, but we've heard reports of violence against this cult in other sectors. We'd like to quietly remove this preacher from the picture to avoid any possibility for backlash in our own areas. At the same time, we don't want to make a martyr out of him and build further support for this cult. The situation needs to be handled discretely.

He's currently preaching on Yunshin Z, a refining complex. This is a low population industrial center with little contact to the outside world. We can afford to make bold moves here. Your task is to find this preacher and return him to us. We'll handle the rest.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Ah, you have him? Good work, {[character]player.name}. I hadn't heard any reports of conflict at the refinery, so I can only assume the mission went smoothly.

In fact, I'd rather continue to keep on assuming that, if you get me. My paperwork is going to indicate that Tolmak's friend came willingly, without a struggle, and that the entire operation was conducted peacefully and with the utmost respect to all involved parties.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: I hope the capture of this preacher is worth the cost of hiring you.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: They're as good as gone.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Since the scouting party is dead and gone, we've got the primary fleet hanging around in space and practically begging for someone to blow them to pieces. Seeing as how you did such a thorough job with their scouts, you were naturally our first choice for taking on their big guns. Once you're finished with them, Okelle won't have anyone to help him except his brother. And once our interrogators are done with Okelle, he'll have given us all the information we need to hunt down Martogar. It's only a matter of time - that is, unless the primary fleet manages to deploy more scouts and continue their murderous rampage, so you better get on your way to stop them.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Just when you think scars from the first Gallente-Caldari War begin to heal, something comes along and the old wounds reopen. We recently intercepted chatter about a missing contingent of Federation soldiers from that conflict who were recently recovered. They were stranded out in a 'roid field after engaging the enemy. Supplies ran out. Neither side came to the rescue.

It's a depressing story, sure, but there's a happy ending if you want to be a part of it. The Federation is willing to pay for secure, respectful transport for our war dead so they can finally be laid to rest in their respective homeworlds. This may sound easy, but it's not. The Caldari have also become aware of the battle site, and already have forces onsite. They refuse to allow us a proper retrieval.

You must go to the battle site and clear out the Caldari forces. Remember, they are invaders still, and recovering our soldiers is of paramount importance.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Well, they've waited this long. They can wait a little longer yet, I guess.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Well, they've waited this long. They can wait a little longer yet, I guess.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Glad to have you onboard. I appreciate that you're willing to do this for the Gallente people. Symbols are important in these politically volatile times.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}  and retrieve the missing war dead. Destroy all Caldari standing in your way.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good flying, egger. Thanks to you, we'll be able to put these soldiers to rest. It's long overdue.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: How is the retrieval going?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We need someone to escort a convoy running humanitarian aid into {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Well, mostly humanitarian aid. We're moving medicine and food, as well as aid workers from the Sisters of EVE. But, there're also military personnel and equipment hidden among those ships. There's a big operation planned in that system, and our forces will need all the help that they can get.

Essentially, there's sensitive cargo onboard, and not everybody needs to know about it. We're posing this convoy as a peaceful operation to keep the State off our backs, but that doesn't mean other groups would be interested in the convoy as a potential target. We don't want to lose it, and we certainly don't want to lose it to someone like the Syndicate or the Serpentis. Unfortunately, we don't have a lot of time before these things are needed, so please forgive me for omitting classified details. This is one of their “blanket operations,” whatever that means. We need you to make sure the coast is clear and that the convoy makes it to their destination safely.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: That's all right. We can find other pilots if you don't like this job. Thanks for your time.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: That's all right. We can find other pilots if you don't like this job. Thanks for your time.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: “When you made a mistake as a child and you were in a rush to hide it, what did you do? You covered it with a blanket and hoped that nobody noticed. Sometimes, we never grow out of this line of thinking.” –Sister Evetelle Boun, organizer of Operation Hope.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: You'll be joining them in the most dangerous leg of their journey, right in the middle of a remote outpost. I can't give you many details about this place, though. Push through this deadspace pocket and make sure the convoy gets to their destination. More instructions will follow when you get there.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and clear the area for the humanitarian convoy.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You actually lost a few ships, but things could have been much worse if you hadn't been there. We'll consider this matter closed, though it looks like the navy will disavow any knowledge of this event ever taking place.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: What's your status?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
In the past several months, several cruise ships carrying close to 100,000 Amarr citizens have vanished without a trace. Of course, we first believed these disappearances to be accidents. We enlisted the help of several ISK-strapped capsuleers to poke around neighboring systems and scan the planets and moons for something.

One of these pilots discovered a Blood Raider installation in a system three jumps from the last known transport ship disappearance. Over the local comms channels, this brave pilot overheard the Raiders refer to it as a "Blood Farm."

We know now that the ships were hijacked and our citizens taken to this installation. There, they were systematically butchered.

I need you to go to this Blood Farm and eliminate anything that even smells like a Blood Raider operation. Don't stop until every last heretic has been utterly and completely destroyed. If there are any tourists still alive, bring them home.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Too much Amarr blood for you, eh?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I understand. Defending the blood of our ancestors is a serious task. Most capsuleers simply cannot find the strength for that type of commitment.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The Blood Raider Covenant is a particularly gruesome sect of the generally reviled Sani Sabik cult. While some modern Sani Sabik rituals use blood in some manner or another, the Covenant places particular value on the blood of cloned humans, and they are utterly ruthless in obtaining it, regularly boarding other spacecraft and abducting all aboard. From their base in Delve they launch lightning-fast raiding parties and surprisingly well-coordinated incursions deep into Empire space in pursuit of their goals.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Make sure that the Blood Farm can never be used to massacre our people ever again.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Destroy the Blood Raider installation and any ships trying to defend it. Bring back any tourists that are somehow still alive and in one piece. Remember, the Blood Raiders treat their victims like cattle to be drained and consumed. Therefore, search any cargo containers you discover. Each ship may have its own supply.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: So few left alive. I can't imagine the horrors they faced. Thank you for your service. Now I must inform the families of those who didn't make it.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: We can't let them massacre any more of our citizens. Get to that station and wipe it from existence.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Perhaps you know the history of Further Foodstuffs? It provides food and supplies to both the Sarum Family and the Ardishapur Family, as well as to the Imperial Navy. Some dissidents, however, believe that this organization denies the military essential supplies that are necessary in the continuing struggles against our enemies.

Some of these low-life dissidents are attempting to disrupt the food supply to the royal families who run this corporation as a way of emphasizing their belief systems. How the scum were able to procure a fleet of ships is beyond my understanding. Perhaps they had help from members of the military who actually believe their propaganda? Regardless, they have amassed a great deal of firepower. If they hurt Further Foodstuffs, they hurt themselves. Does that make any sense to you?

Eliminate this rag-tag fleet.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Are you kidding me? I spent a great deal of time searching for a good pilot.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Better now than later. At least I still have time to find someone dependable.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Further Foodstuffs is a small agricultural company jointly owned by the Ardishapur and Sarum families. The products of Further Foodstuffs are mostly used by the subjects of these two families, while what little surplus is left is sold on the open market. This has curbed the expansion opportunities of the company, though it means the fleets of Ardishapur and Sarum will never lack for food.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Time is of the essence. Get going, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Stop the dissidents' fleet by destroying every last one of them.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good job. Now the two most prominent families in the Empire (and our hard-working military, of course) won't feel the loss of their favorite delicacies.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Are you there yet?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: A job well done, friend! Here is that reward I promised.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Apparently, a rival corporation is afraid of our rapid growth in the field of starship design. An “associate” of ours has informed us that a shipment of datacores heading to one of our research stations is to be intercepted by a fleet of Guristas mercenaries. What's disturbing is that an Amarr corporation has allegedly hired the pirates to do this dirty work.

We want you to intercept and eliminate the Guristas threat. What we need is proof that our rivals are pulling their strings or that they have nothing to do with this whatsoever.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Apparently, a rival corporation is afraid of our rapid growth in the field of starship design. An “associate” of ours has informed us that a shipment of datacores heading to one of our research stations is to be intercepted by a fleet of Guristas mercenaries. What's disturbing is that an Amarr corporation has allegedly hired the pirates to do this dirty work. If that's true, there is a major shift in philosophy among our adversaries, both in the boardroom and in space. We need more information before we can act upon this.

We want you to intercept and eliminate the Guristas threat. Find out, if you can, who is behind this. What we need is proof that our rivals are pulling their strings or that they have nothing to do with this whatsoever.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Coward! I knew I shouldn't have trusted you.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: A hefty award awaits you upon successful completion of this mission.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Good to see you again, {[character]player.name}. We've got something you'd be perfect for.

It appears the Gallente have been making hostile moves again in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. They've been continuously launching attacks from a command vessel somewhere in a deadspace pocket. Our scouts have located the Federation admiral responsible for these raids and now we just need her taken care of.

We've dealt with this thing before, so we're confident that removing her from the picture will disrupt the rest of the Gallente operations in our area. The only issue is that the Navy won't be able to mobilize against her in time – they're the Navy after all, not a hit squad. I've been asked to recruit a capsuleer if possible, so we can bypass internal military procedures altogether.

That's where you come in {[character]player.name}. We need you to travel over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, enter the deadspace pocket our scouts have found, then kill the commander and her fleet.

She'll undoubtedly be back at some point even if your mission is successful. The Gallente are a persistent enemy, so after you've killed her, leave the body in the communication array she's been coordinating the forces out of. That should send a message. It might even spook her into seeking reassignment elsewhere, away from our corporation's space.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm afraid your name was already put forward to deal with this. This won't reflect well on you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I thought a patriot like you would be up for this. I'll leave your name out of my report to the Navy, but I am a little disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. I have uploaded the coordinates to the mission details in your Opportunity interface.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
It appears the Gallente have been making hostile moves again in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. They've been continuously launching attacks from a command vessel somewhere in a deadspace pocket. Our scouts have located the Federation admiral responsible for these raids and now we just need her taken care of.

The only issue is that the Navy won't be able to mobilize against her in time – they're the Navy after all, not a hit squad. I've been asked to recruit a capsuleer if possible, so we can bypass internal military procedures altogether.
