She'll undoubtedly be back at some point even if your mission is successful. The Gallente are a persistent enemy, so after you've killed her, leave the body in the communication array she's been coordinating the forces out of. That should send a message. It might even spook her into seeking reassignment elsewhere, away from our corporation's space.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great work, {[character]player.name}. Intel places her at a cloning station deep inside Federation space. I imagine it will be a while before she tries that move again, and if she does, you've left a reminder on how it will end.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: The admiral isn't going to stay in that location for very long. Take her out as quickly as you can.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I'm glad to see you made it over, {[character]player.name}. I have a problem with some Gallente miners that I think you'd be perfect for.

The Gallente have set up another mining operation near one of our asteroid belts. They bring in semi-mobile reprocessing stations and then mine the location dry. You have to recognize this as just another act of war, {[character]player.name}. {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has lost millions of ISK to these Federation parasites. It's almost as damaging as a direct attack, but it doesn't draw the sort of military response an overt assault would, which is why we need capsuleer assistance to deal with this quickly.

We know they've set up mining outpost at one of the smaller deadspace asteroid pockets {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} frequents. They do this in the hope that nobody will come after them. I need you to send the Federation a message that they're wrong – that the State will pursue them every time. You must show them that there's no profit to be made from illegally mining belts we have claimed.

Go to the outpost and destroy absolutely everything; all the miners and any reprocessing stations you see. Level the place entirely. The loss of personnel and equipment will set them back and send a clear message to stick to their own space.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm surprised that someone like you would be afraid to take on a few rogue miners.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I will have to find someone else more capable, then. I'm surprised you couldn't handle this, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Great to hear. I've uploaded the coordinates.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
The Gallente have set up another mining operation near one of our asteroid belts. They bring in semi-mobile reprocessing stations and then mine the location dry. You have to recognize this as just another act of war, {[character]player.name}. {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has lost millions of ISK to these Federation parasites. It's almost as damaging as a direct attack, but it doesn't draw the sort of military response an overt assault would, which is why we need capsuleer assistance to deal with this quickly.

We know they've set up mining outpost at one of the smaller deadspace asteroid pockets {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} frequents. They do this in the hope that nobody will come after them. I need you to send the Federation a message that they're wrong – that the State will pursue them every time. You must show them that there's no profit to be made from illegally mining belts we have claimed.

Go to the outpost and destroy absolutely everything; all the miners and any reprocessing stations you see. Level the place entirely. The loss of personnel and equipment will set them back and send a clear message to stick to their own space.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great work; hopefully those thieves won't come back any time soon.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Move quickly, {[character]player.name}. Every hour that passes means more profit lost.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Sometimes it's easy to forget we're at war with the Gallente. Maybe not for you, of course, since it's you capsuleers who are doing most of the fighting, but for the rest of us things can seem awfully “business as usual” at times.

I'm saying this because we've had a development recently; something that's reminded a lot of senior people there's a war still going on. They've asked me to scout for capsuleers willing to deal with this situation, and that request has brought you to me, {[character]player.name}.

We have credible intel that sometime within the next week the Gallente Federation will officially claim sovereignty over the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and relocate an entire Navy division to support this claim. They will justify these actions by citing a recent worker's riot as proof of “a desire for democracy”. In reality, they just want to inflame the few unhappy people further and cost our entire corporation massive amounts of ISK in the process. They have no desire to genuinely help anyone but themselves.

The Federation has moved a division of their Navy into the system, and if we don't forcibly push them out soon the riots could escalate further. We must do everything we can to avoid a repeat of the Brothers of Freedom. The State has seen enough high-profile dissenters in recent years; yet another would not help our people. We obviously cannot allow this claim to ever happen, or for this Federation task force to gain any momentum whatsoever.

We need you to slip past the Navy forces and destroy the Gallente command ship leading them. This will throw the rest of the division into disarray momentarily, and at that point, the Caldari Navy will move in. We've discovered a deadspace route that will allow you to strike the command ship and its escorts from a rear flank. They shouldn't even see you coming.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You've made us both look bad, {[character]player.name}, and if we don't stop that force, the entire State will look even worse. We do not have the luxury of failing. Someone more reliable will have to be found to replace you.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I set this task aside just for you, and you repay me by throwing it back in my face? We're done here.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Formerly an extremist labor movement in the State, the Brothers of Freedom led a widespread revolt against corporate security forces on a number of Caldari planets in YC 109 – some time before Tibus Heth's vastly more successful revolt of a similar nature -- after 65,000 protesters were killed by Caldari paramilitary forces while trying to force their way onto a CEP station in the New Caldari system. After months of dogged pursuit by Caldari authorities, the riots were put down and most of the leaders were killed or arrested.

Some of the leadership, including the ringleader Melarius Torvil, did manage to escape the final Caldari Navy operation that crushed the Brothers' movement. Torvil and a small group of associates fled to the Minmatar Republic and applied for asylum from Caldari persecution, which was granted by the late President Midular's Gallente-friendly government.

Today, though they have been largely eliminated as a major force in the State, the Brothers of Freedom continue to spread anti-corporate propaganda and speak out against the CEP's government in the Gallente Federation and the Minmatar Nation, as well as outlying State settlements and facilities.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
I knew I was right to choose you for this. I've added the command vessel's location to the mission details in your Opportunity interface.

I'd expect a difficult battle, {[character]player.name}. You're about the draw the attention of an entire Federation Navy division. You will likely have to fight your way through to the commander once they realize you've breached.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Within the next week the Gallente Federation will officially claim sovereignty over the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} , citing a recent worker's riot as proof of “a desire for democracy”. The Federation has moved a division of their Navy into the system, and if we don't forcibly push them out soon the riots could escalate further.

Slip past the Navy forces from their rear flank and destroy the Gallente command ship and its escorts.. This will throw the rest of the division into disarray momentarily, and at that point, the Caldari Navy will move in.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great job {[character]player.name}. We've already taken care of most of the forces in one decisive sweep. The Federation will surely be on the retreat soon.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: The Navy is waiting on you to take out that command vessel. As soon as you do, they'll make their move.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
A confidential informant has warned us of an impending kidnapping attempt on a young noble by a notorious Minmatar mercenary. One of my associates, who owes me a lifetime worth of favors, discovered the plot during a card game. The merc's mouth and ego are both the size of New Eden itself. He talked openly about his plan without a second thought. We need your help in stopping him before he can carry out his plans.

His staging ground is at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Find and kill him with any and all means at your disposal. He's a crafty SOB, so expect not just a fight, but some unorthodox challenges when he realizes you're on to him. He's especially fond of drawing pursuers into hazardous clouds. Odds are good he'll have some ex-Navy Minnies flying back-up. He might be a braggart, but he's still a paranoid merc. Be careful.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Too tough for you, eh?  This merc has defeated greater men than you, so don't let it hurt your ego too much.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I have to find a braver pilot than you, apparently.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: A significant number of Minmatar make their living on the darker side of the law, acting as pirates, smugglers and peddlers in all kinds of illegal goods. Many of the larger criminal groups in the world of EVE are run by Minmatar.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: The Amarr Empire thanks you for your assistance in this matter. Please use all speed and discretion in apprehending this degenerate.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A Minmatar merc plans to kidnap an Amarr young noble, so we need you to take him out before he can even make the attempt.  We know where he is preparing his plan.  You need to get in and dispose of him before he can even make his attempt. . He's a crafty SOB, so expect not just a fight, but some unorthodox challenges when he realizes you're on to him. He's especially fond of drawing pursuers into hazardous clouds.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great job, {[character]player.name}.  The Amarr Empire is in your debt.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: The merc's sneaky.  He will use every trick he knows to escape.  Keep your eyes open for clues he may leave behind!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
A maintenance team assigned to a top secret acceleration gate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} has stopped transmitting progress reports. As this gate leads to one of our new listening outposts, alarm rang out in military circles.

Travel to the acceleration gate. Destroy any hostiles. Use the acceleration gate and check on the outpost. If the outpost's location has been compromised, you are ordered to eliminate the hostiles and then destroy the gate. You must ensure that the enemy cannot return to the exact location of our outpost.

You have your orders. Will you execute them to the best of your ability?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Damn, just what I need.  Another political firestorm.  I had better find a way to fix this quickly.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Very well.  I will find someone else.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: As to those citizens stationed at the outpost, yes, they will be cut off from all outside contact until a new acceleration gate can be built.  The good news is that the outpost is equipped with a Stealth Emitter Array that will keep it hidden until we can return.  The not-so-good news is that those citizens could experience some long term side effects from the energies emitted by the array, but they knew the risks when they signed on.  Secrecy is paramount, both from a political and a military perspective.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent.  Remember, this operation is classified as top secret.  You are not to discuss it with anyone.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
A maintenance team assigned to a top secret acceleration gate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} has stopped transmitting progress reports. As this gate leads to one of our new listening outposts, alarm rang out in military circles.

Travel to the acceleration gate. Destroy any hostiles. Use the acceleration gate and check on the outpost. If the outpost's location has been compromised, you are ordered to eliminate the hostiles and then destroy the gate. You must ensure that the enemy cannot return to the exact location of our outpost.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: It had to be done.  We'll get another gate built out there and a military presence to protect it.  In the meantime, the citizens at the listening post will have to make due with the supplies they have.  Rest assured that we will do everything we can to get back to them as quickly as possible.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Still nothing from the maintenance team.  Advise me on your status.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Glad my invitation reached you, {[character]player.name}. A portion of the fleet  is preparing a set of protracted war games in the next few days. I've been put in charge of constructing decoy ships and structures, but there was some mix up with a circuitry order that I only just found out about.
I found a replacement vendo. All my subordinates are too occupied to retrieve it.
You'll be picking up the goods direct from a production line, not through their public market. I haven't had time to check reports on local piracy though. There may be hostiles. Be ready for a fight. I don't care if you have to blow the storage facility apart, we need those chips.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You're kidding. This is one disaster after another.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Well so much for all that wasted time.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Production for all types of goods can be found in all corners of New Eden. Every so often, though, something of a specific design is required that must be produced from a specific area. Sometimes this is due to patents, sometimes it's more to do with a sudden requirement for obsolete or cutting edge equipment.  Desperation on the part of the buyer can lead to major holes in market security.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I'll thank you later. Please get going.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A portion of the fleet is preparing a set of protracted war games  in the next few days. There was some mix up with a circuitry order that I only just found out about. Collect the custom circuitry from the production line in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The level of piracy in the area is unknown.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You were attacked? What would they want with training drone AI ? Wonderful, now we'll have to hold up the war games   for a security check of the entire shipment. I didn't realize Angel Cartel could be subtle. Given how this went for them, maybe they should stick to the direct approach.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: I don't have anything else for you {[character]player.name}. What are you waiting for?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Have you ever heard of the band Quantum Entanglement? They're a heavy metal rock opera group with a theatric, costumed stage presence. Seriously, they're all the rage among the Federation's youth. The front man is none other than Halo Axegrinder, who was one of the founding members of Starved Fedo. Remember them?

Okay, personally I can't stand that garbage, but billions of fans can't be wrong, right? Anyway, their manager is one of my old school chums and he's asked me for a personal favor. He says they thrive on adrenalin, and since most of their songs are about war, he thinks they might be inspired by experiencing a little combat action.

Coincidentally, I've got a little pirate attack that needs to be dealt with in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system; it's a task I would usually allocate to some rookie capsuleer far below your standing with the corporation. If you're packing the kind of firepower I think you are, you should be able to take this installation down without breaking a sweat. Let a few hits bounce off of your defenses to give these guys the ride of their lives and that should give them enough inspiration for a lifetime of edgy, hard-hitting chart-toppers. I think that's the right terminology.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: What went wrong? You've put me in a spot here. I can't say I appreciate this but it's not like I can do anything about it.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Well, thanks for your time. I'll just have to tell their manager to hold on while I find another reputable pilot. Lucky me.  You cap-pilots are common these days, but not ones I'd be willing to work with.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: This heavy metal rock opera band was made famous by their first album's cover, which depicted two naked individuals engaging in sexual intercourse while floating in space without spacesuits. Gallente politicians tried to have the album, called Unprotected, banned. Not because of the adult content, they claimed, but because it promoted unsafe extravehicular activities.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you for doing this. Entertainment is becoming more and more important to the citizens of the Federation, and it's widely believed that whatever troubles may befall us, we'll overcome them based on our willingness to defend our culture.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, drop the band off at their manager's station, and take care of the pirates.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Outstanding work, egger. The label was still willing to pay your fee, and the producer was recovered and brought up on charges.

On a side note, the entire band was psyched about what you did. I think you inspired a real creative explosion in them, and I hope we can look forward to better music.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Are they getting on your nerves yet?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We just lost a fleet out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's a waste of hardware and personnel, but at the very least, we'd like to recover the data cores of each ship. If the vultures haven't started in on the carcass yet, they will soon. We can't afford a whole recovery effort, but we'd rather hire a capsuleer like you then let those blood-suckers run off with our data.

Keep anything else you like from the site, and if a few raiders and pirates end up dead, I doubt anyone would complain, if you know what I mean.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Damn. We were hoping to attract someone of your reputation and firepower. We'll see if we can't settle for someone else.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Damn. We were hoping to attract someone of your reputation and firepower. We'll see if we can't settle for someone else.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: It's all yours. We'll upload the identification beacons to your ship now.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Find the lost fleet in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and recover the data cores; destroy anything that stands in your way.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: That's fantastic news! Thanks!

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Time is running out. By the time you get there, it might already be picked clean.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I've got a delicate yet dangerous task that just wouldn't suit anyone other than a capsuleer. Here's the situation:

We caught a Caldari operative trying to walk out of the University of Callie with, and I say this literally, an armful of data cores stolen from the university's research hospital. We've had him locked down at a penal instillation in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} since then, but our more convincing interrogators have changed his mind about giving up some information.

The catch is that he's demanded to be transferred to a more "dignified" location before he offers his full cooperation. That's where you come in.

Pick up the Caldari operative and bring him back here immediately.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You're leaving me in a spot here. I'll have to get another trusted courier and contact the jail again.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Sorry to hear that. You sure? Simple, lucrative work doesn't come around every day.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Good. Head out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I've sent word, so they should know to hand him over to you when you get there. They haven't responded yet, but it's an old installation, and a busy one, too. I'm sure it's nothing.

When you get him, bring him back here.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Go pick up the Caldari operative from the penal station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and bring him back.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good work. You really thought on your feet for that one. We'll be debriefing the operative shortly. Your payment is well deserved, unfortunately the Caldari did get away with a lot of prisoners.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: What's your status?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
A rogue drone virus has gone live at a mining colony. The machinery is malfunctioning and the problem spreading throughout the entire network. We sent a small rescue crew and it took over their systems. The crews are still alive but they're held hostage by their own ships. Unfortunately, we can't let that cloud our judgment. The infection must be destroyed… completely.

We have reason to believe your capsuleer vessel will be able to withstand infection long enough to eradicate the problem.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: That doesn't leave me many options. You couldn't have told me earlier? No matter.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Can't say I blame you, but it still doesn't help me out any. You'll have to excuse me.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Rogue drones and wild drones are the terms used over advanced drones that mutated out of control. A few years ago some ingenious Gallente inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own - in essence acting in every sense like a regular space ship except being unmanned and computer controlled. First prototypes were encouraging, but then disaster struck. The drones became unruly, then unmanageable. Some of these were huge - the largest drones ever constructed, these drones were even equipped with warp drives and equipped with the latest advancements in artificial intelligence. These mother drones, as they were called, along with several lesser drones soon managed to spread out, not only within the same system as the research facility that birthed them, but also to other systems. Only later men discovered exactly how - the drones attacked and took over space ships, then used them to jump to other systems, the drones themselves safely hidden within the ship. Needless to say the super-drone research was soon abandoned by the Gallente.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good luck out there.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A drone network virus seems has taken over a mining colony and is infecting any ship that approaches. Eradicate all infected ships and destroy the virus before it infects yours.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: That was close. A shame for those that lost their lives, but you did incredible work out there. We'll send a scuttle crew out to sweep up and find out what happened.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Please try to maintain radio silence during this mission; I don't want that virus ending up in our computers here on the station!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I can tell you're a bit more experienced than the average capsuleer, which means you might be interested in something a little more challenging than the usual chores.

A small gang of pirates has carved a niche for itself in the evidence disposal business. They've setup a base near an uncharted acidic cloud, which allows them to charge huge sums of money to other pirate factions that need to get rid of salvage, bodies, data cores, or whatever in a discrete location.

Unfortunately, they're currently holding some hostages that we need to have recovered. I think you can figure out the rest on your own.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'll find someone else.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'll find someone else.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I don't think I need to remind you that, if you fail, a bunch of innocent people are going to get jettisoned into a cloud of acid, where they will be simultaneously decompressed, frozen, and dissolved.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A pirate faction in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system has taken hostages and plan on executing them shortly. The innocent people need to be rescued and returned to the agent as soon as possible.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Clever capsuleer, you've done it! On behalf of my corporation and the hostages you rescued, thank you very much!

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: I'm no starship pilot, but it seems like it would be a good idea to avoid the acid cloud.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We've gotten reports of missing passenger ships in and around {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We've lost track of three of them just this week. We'd like you to go out and see what's happening to the ships. If possible, recover the crew as well. Thousands of people are missing because of these lost ships – the worst incident so far. I'm afraid that this situation could gain a lot of unwanted attention very quickly.

I want you to look into it. I'd like to be optimistic and say that they've simply had technical difficulties, but we're past the breaking point here. Bring back any survivors you can find.

messages.mission.extrainfo.header.text: A Quote from Admiral Edan Gore, Federation Navy

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Sorry to hear that. You'll be happy to know that CONCORD has taken notice of this case and they'll be dispatching a squadron to look into the disappearances.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: The Federation will not look kindly on your inaction.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: "Honor does not exist in this day and age, not out in space and especially not among the capsuleer communities. The only honor left is down here, planet side, where we do not resort to domestic terrorism, and where respect for the basic rights of the private citizen still exists. The stars shine on fear."

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you.  I have no idea who would be disrupting our space lanes like this. Whoever it is, they're bold to take on the Federation. We'll have medical specialists on standby to take of the survivors.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and look for signs of the missing passenger ships. Evacuate any survivors you find and bring them back here.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: This mission was a bigger story than I imagined. Looks like the State was using these mercenaries as a source of domestic warfare within the Federation. That's low, especially for the State. But you know what they say about war, right? Anyway, I'll report this incident to the higher-ups in the FIO. They'll be very interested in the State's recent activities.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Any news yet?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You've shown a great deal of loyalty to the Republic, {[character]player.name}. I wonder if that speaks as much to your feelings towards the Amarr, or if it's a matter of convenience. It's been my experience that the older a capsuleer is, the more uncertain his or her motives become.

Mortals are slightly less difficult. Fervent extremists particularly. A particularly troubled Minmatar has apparently taken it upon himself to conduct a personal war against the Empire. Ordinarily, my superiors and I would quietly applaud his effort and wait for word of his death. This particular person, however, managed to commandeer a prototype stealth ship to carry out his war.

We can't let the ship fall into Amarrian hands, but we can't send the fleet in either. With him already in Amarr territory, they could easily construe it as a sanctioned act of war. As much as I want to cut out my tongue for saying it, we need you to help the Amarr kill one of our own. We'll have to smooth out the political mess through our liaison with CONCORD.

Reports place him somewhere in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. If you can manage it, bring back his remains. I don't want to think how those pious... how the Amarr would treat him.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I understand how distasteful the whole deal is, but this doesn't help.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You're leaving us with dangerously few options, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Reflecting on the personal toll invariably endured, a wise figure once offered this advice to anyone considering a career in politics: “Don't.” In New Eden, with so many different factions all delicately counterbalanced, such sage advice may have never been more humanitarian.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I hope you won't mind if I don't thank you outright. Oh, and don't expect the Amarr to welcome your assistance either.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Hunt down the rogue Minmatar in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.  Destroy his pirated prototype ship and deliver his corpse to Minmatar caretakers.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Our rampaging kinsman is gone? His ship, too? If you'll take a bit of advice from a lowly mortal, {[character]player.name}; when unethical decisions are made, eventually you're left with nothing but unethical options.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: I have nothing else to tell you, {[character]player.name}. Please just contact me when this is finished.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We have a lead on a potential slave trade in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and I need someone to patrol that area and find out what's happening. We think they're trading Gallente citizens, which is an open act of hostility against the Federation, so we need to shut this ring down as soon as possible. But first, we have to know who's behind it.

Understand that you won't be trying to actually stop the slavers; all we need is information on who's behind it. If you encounter any hostiles, however, please take care of them.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You're aware of what you're doing? These people need immediate help.  We'll scramble some pilots now, but you're leaving us high and dry.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Some other time.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: That's what I like to hear. A capsuleer will really be able to send these slavers a message. Thank you for agreeing to be the voice of our culture.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}  to monitor and disperse the slave trading operation that has set up shop there.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I've dispatched ships to pick up the slaves. They'll receive counseling and be sent back to their respective home worlds, courtesy of Interbus. It's safe to say I'm not satisfied with this outcome. I've never heard of the Serpentis dealing in human traffic, but I hope that this isn't indicative of a larger trend in that organization. But we've got the information we need, and the Federation can move forward based on your intel. Good work.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Interesting that you should contact me. Is it done?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
There is an old saying: “Money makes the world go round.” Actually, it's gravity and thermodynamics, among other things, but money and physics all come together in a big way when you're talking about wormholes.

However, wormholes rarely occur in civilized space; take a wild guess what that means. I hope you have some experience in dealing with pirates, {[character]player.name}. Specifically, the Sansha. They seem particularly fixated on wormhole research, so much so that they've been a major pain for scientific ventures regardless of ownership.

There's no word of sanctions against the “Nation,” so we'll have to take care of it ourselves. More work for you, anyway.

We'd send a fleet detachment to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} to reclaim a wormhole we've been studying recently, but we'd rather outsource to a capsuleer like you and humiliate them.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You were supposed to embarrass those androids, not your employers. I'll call in the fleet.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I expected someone with your reputation to jump at the chance for a little rough play. I'm sure some up and coming fleet captain will be eager for the assignment.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The inner workings of a wormhole were apparently well understood at one time. Since the Dark Ages, however, the best New Eden has managed is basic reverse engineering of ancient jump gates, significantly less powerful than the natural phenomena. This makes the appearance of a natural wormhole a dangerously valuable occurrence, over which factions will openly oppose each other in order to study and utilize the anomalies exclusively.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good hunting. Personally, I suggested we just spray the area with used motor oil.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Wipe out the Sansha hijackers in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The more humiliating, the better.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: What do you mean they came through from the other end? You're suggesting they were able to predict of the most random, unpredictable pathway in existence?

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Our scientists can't safely get back to work until you've sent the cyborgs running, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Hang on, I need to finish this call.

Really, another one? That same station, huh? Well, I don't know what the capsuleer was flying. What do you want me to do, hold their hands? No, don't even joke about that. One more? Do you really think it's going to be any different? Okay, but don't blame me if this one fails, too.

Okay now, where were we? Oh, yes, the exciting opportunity I have for you today! It's a bit run-of-the-mill, but I think you've earned an easy one, friend. It's just a tiny little rogue drone problem. There couldn't be more than half a dozen of the little bastards. I'll bet if you just zip in there and rattle off a few shots at the infested station, they'll scatter like frightened children. What do you say?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You flew all the way out here just to decline a simple task like this?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You flew all the way out here just to decline a simple task like this?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Perfect! Run over to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and clean up those pesky drones.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A rogue drone infestation in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system is causing problems and needs to be taken care of.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: You actually did it? You destroyed that infested station? Do you have any idea how many capsuleers lost their- Uhm, I mean, great work! I'll keep you in mind when I come across important missions like this in the future.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: How is that cleanup coming along?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Tattoos are more than art to the Minmatar, {[character]player.name}. We have entire ceremonies built up around the markings we come to wear in our lives. Not to bore you with details, but ours aren't the simple ink-and-needle hatchet jobs most people think of. Exactly how the chemical process works is a closely guarded secret even within our own culture.

Word has reached my office that some Amarr splinter faction is working on their own chemical in order to contaminate Minmatar ceremonial supplies. It could mean anything from the appearance of Amarr propagandist symbols to some unexplored form of chemical dependence on the Empire.

The logistics of such a plan actually working are laughably impossible, and of course we'll never be able to tie anything back to mainline Imperial channels. Still, any threat to our freedom must be treated seriously. Well, that and the whole concept is just insulting.

We want you to bring us a sample of this chemical. I can't pinpoint exactly where the chemicals are being made. Our best information points to a deadspace complex in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

I mentioned the insult of the program. Tear through the place. I don't care how many structures you have to obliterate, just bring us this new ink.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Why haven't you brought me the chemical yet? Did you turn every structure inside out, because they probably won't be hiding it in some ship's cargo bay.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I didn't expect a capsuleer to have a weak stomach.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Discretion can be the better part of valor. I'm sure there's a less scrupulous capsuleer out there somewhere.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The Minmatar coming-of-age ceremony, known as the Voluval, involves an injection of a hallucinatory chemical which puts the youth in a trance. As the visions wear off, the individual finds him or herself marked with a tattoo of an unpredictable pattern on an unpredictable portion of body. The chemical used to induce trance and create the mark is so well guarded, even some Minmatar wonder if there is not more to the process than their elders admit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Don't expect them to roll over and hand you the formula. Leave no stone unturned, and what I mean by that is don't be afraid to destroy every structure you see in search of your objective.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Find the tainted tattoo chemical being developed in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.  The exact location of the chemical is unknown.  Be prepared to destroy any number of large structures.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: If you felt the least bit heartless blasting through them, remember which side consciously chose to use innocent victims as living shields, {[character]player.name}. We've already sent teams in behind you to rescue who we can. Or capture, as the case may be. I'll be interested to learn exactly what this substance is supposed to do.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Please, you have to help me! I hired a group of mercenaries to escort a friend's cargo shipment; however, I just learned that the people I sent are pirate agents!

I know it would be helpful if you knew who you were going up against, but all I have is a few fragments of information here; there are no specifics so be ready for anything!

I need you to intercept that convoy and eliminate the pirates!

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Damn it. I need to find someone to help and quick. Time is running out.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Damn it. I need to find someone to help and quick. Time is running out.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: It's a common misconception that it is CONCORD that engages pirates with below -5.0 security status in high security space, while it is in fact the local navy that does so. CONCORD will only engage if the outlaw has incurred a GCC (Global Criminal Countdown) caused by committing a crime in Empire Space. The local navies are not as powerful as CONCORD and it is possible to survive their onslaught and limp back to the gate, or even escape before they warp scramble the ship.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you for doing this. The convoy should be passing through {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} very soon. There's still time to head them off!

messages.mission.briefing.text: According to your agent, a convoy was sent out with a group of pirates pretending to be security. Intercept the convoy and take out its escort.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I cannot properly express how helpful you've been, so hopefully this reward will do.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: What are you doing? Time is running out!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I'm glad you're here {[character]player.name}, {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is in desperate need of your help.

Only a few moments ago the CEO from one of our subsidiaries was attacked and ransomed by Guristas, right in front of our trade delegation, too. Local security forces were overwhelmed and the pirates managed to escape. Our scouts pursued the Guristas vessels back to a Federation detention facility, which suggests the Guristas are only acting as mercenaries and the Gallente are really the ones to blame.

We have scouts hidden near the detention facility, and they're monitoring communications to look for evidence of a connection, but in the meantime we want to make an attempt to get our people out using capsuleer assistance. We're concerned that more reinforcements could be on the way, and that if they arrive, we'll lose our people for good. You need to act quickly.

Your assignment is to assault the facility and return our people to us before things escalate any further. Can we count on you for this?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: If that CEO dies, it'll be on your head! I don't know how you sleep at night.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: What? I pray to the Maker that I can find someone else in time.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The Guristas are famous for their raids into civilized territory, something that very few pirate clans are willing or able to do. The mission of these raids is most often simply to steal cargo or passengers (for ransom) from freighters, but on numerous occasions their main intention seems to be to sabotage empire installations (mining facilities, sentry guns, and the like). This has led to speculations that some unscrupulous empire companies or even governments are hiring the Guristas to take out property of the competition.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Understood. Be careful how you approach this, {[character]player.name}; the Guristas must be getting paid a fortune for such a brazen attack, and they will fight to the death for that money.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Only a few moments ago the CEO from one of our subsidiaries was attacked and ransomed by Guristas, right in front of our trade delegation. Local security forces were overwhelmed and the pirates managed to escape. Our scouts pursued the Guristas vessels back to a Federation detention facility, which suggests the Guristas are only acting as mercenaries and the Gallente are really the ones to blame.

We have scouts holding above the detention facility, and they're tapping communications to look for evidence of a connection, but in the meantime we want to make an attempt to get our people out using capsuleer assistance. We're concerned that more reinforcements could be on the way, and that if they arrive, we'll lose our people for good. You need to act quickly.

Your assignment is to assault the facility and return our people to us before things escalate any further.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: The best possible result, and proof once again that hiring capsuleers is the way to get that. Thank you, {[character]player.name}, you've made us both look good. I'll be sure to pass my recommendations along, right after I take a few calls about some pay adjustments of my own.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Time is of the essence. Get moving {[character]player.name}!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Ah, {[character]player.name}, I'm glad to see you received my mail. I have something that requires complete discretion. It's entirely legal of course, but this will need to be kept quiet all the same. You've proven yourself trustworthy so if you want the assignment I'll hand it over to you.

During a routine system scan, some of my people stumbled upon something that may be a significant archaeological find. I can't just call in anyone to confirm it, though, that would risk a leak. I don't want anyone else claiming this discovery as their own, especially if it turns out to be a lucrative one.

What we could do is rig your vessel's camera drones to relay a live feed of the site back to me and a friend of mine at the House of Records. From there, my friend would be able to direct you around the area to observe places of interest. What you relay back could help us confirm or disprove our earlier findings. The site is in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, so you wouldn't be travelling very far to investigate, either. Our scouts reported there was a light pirate presence, and interference was making the use of microwarpdrives impossible in there, but I'm sure you can deal with a few Guristas and using afterburner.

Not the usual assignment I know, but one of potentially great importance…and profit. It would be ideal if we could rely on capsuleer assistance for this. What do you say?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Fine. I will find someone else.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Then it would be in your best interests to forget we ever had this discussion.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Shortly after jump gate technology was jointly discovered by the Gallente and the Caldari a little over five hundred years before the Federation formed, the Caldari corporations had started their own interstellar surveying and colonization, separate from that conducted by the Gallente. It was these colonies, kept as a secret from the Gallenteans, that became the source of friction between the Gallenteans and the Caldari, culminating in the latter's defection from the Federation and an ensuing war between the two races.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
I knew I chose the right person. I'm uploading the coordinates to you now.

Once you arrive at the archaeological site, I will issue further instructions.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Ah, {[character]player.name}, I'm glad to see you received my mail. I have something that requires complete discretion. It's entirely legal of course, but this will need to be kept quiet all the same. You've proven yourself trustworthy so if you want the assignment I'll hand it over to you.

I don't want anyone else claiming this discovery as their own, especially if it turns out to be a lucrative one.

The site is in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, so you wouldn't be travelling very far to investigate, either. The only problem my scouts reported was a light pirate presence. I'm sure you can deal with a few Guristas.

Not the usual assignment I know, but one of potentially great importance…and profit. It would be ideal if we could rely on capsuleer assistance for this.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
You've done well, {[character]player.name}. Exceptionally well. It will take a little longer to fully confirm, but we believe we've discovered an ancient Caldari outpost – one of the first established after we broke away from the Federation. If true, this would be a welcome injection to the system's local tourism industry, and we'll get a commission on the money earned there. Here's your cut of the deal.

Even if it turns out to be a false discovery we're insured against the ISK, so I see no reason not to give it to you now. Thanks once again.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: We stand to make a lot of ISK if that site is what we think it is.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Glad to have you here, {[character]player.name}. I have some work for you.

A few days ago, a passenger vessel was passing through an asteroid belt, when it had a critical failure of its navigational computer. The vessel slammed into the asteroids and suffered critical damage. Before the vessel's reactor went critical, {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} personnel evacuated the passengers and got them to safety.

While this story has a happy ending, there seems to be something suspicious about the crash. A small corporation with alleged ties to the Guristas is having money troubles, and {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} suspects the incident may have not been an accident. Things just seem a little too perfect and well-timed.

{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} needs you to go to the crash site and investigate the wreckage. Look for any evidence that might hint at the real cause of the accident. Bring any evidence back to me and I will submit it to the proper authorities.

I don't want to tell you how to do your job, but a salvager might help you get to the bottom of this a little faster than just looking around with your on-board sensors.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I was relying on you to figure out what went wrong. I just hope the evidence is still there by the time I find someone else.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: There are millions of ISK resting on this investigation. Who I am supposed to find to do this?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Great to hear, {[character]player.name}. I have uploaded the coordinates to your NeoCom.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Your agent's corporation suspects a rival corporation may have caused a transport crash. Go to the location in the mission details and investigate the wreckage you find. Bring any evidence back to your agent.

You will require a salvager.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: This is some interesting evidence. Now we can bring some people to justice.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: I have a feeling there might be a cover up in the works, so get moving.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
{[character]player.name}, thanks for stopping by. Every now and then I get handed another assignment to clean up our spacelanes and clamp down on narcotics smuggling. I was hoping I could count on you to handle this one as we've had some problems in the past with other capsuleers.

There's been an influx of neural boosters to our area recently and {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is trying to stem the flow. We understand that boosters will never truly go away; we're not trying to be overbearing here, quite the opposite in fact. We normally turn a blind eye to light drug trafficking, and usually this has proven to be good business, but that only seems to have encouraged the local smugglers in recent times. They've been flooding this system and others nearby with cheap, more dangerous drugs, which is absolutely not good for business.

We know where they base out of, a station in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system which we've already taken the liberty of blockading. We'd rather have the matter dealt with on a corporate basis though, before anyone goes alerting the Chief Executive Panel or CONCORD authorities, so your discretion is important here.

We've set up a check point outside the station. What we need is a capsuleer who can go in there and check out some of the larger vessels currently in holding. We're concerned that some of these vessels are not only heavily loaded with boosters, but also heavily armed. It would be best to have someone like you on standby for the inspection process. You are of course cleared to engage anyone caught with illegal boosters in their cargo, although if you catch anyone, be prepared for some shooting.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I heard you were having problems dealing with this. Well, thanks for letting me know of your failure first-hand, I suppose.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Very well, if you're not interested I can find others. An unexpected refusal though, I must say.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Here are the coordinates. Don't hesitate out there, {[character]player.name};  be ready for a fight.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's been an influx of neural boosters to our area recently, and {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is trying to stem the flow. We normally turn a blind eye to light drug trafficking but that only seems to have encouraged the local smugglers, who are now flooding the area with cheap, more dangerous drugs.

We know where they base out of, however, and have already taken the liberty of blockading their station in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. What we need is a capsuleer who can go in there and check out some of the larger vessels currently in holding. You are of course cleared to engage anyone caught with illegal boosters in their cargo, although if you catch anyone be prepared for them to start shooting.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great Work, {[character]player.name}. It should be a long time, or a lot of ISK in bribes, before they can re-establish themselves around here again.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: There's a number of ships holding outside the station. They won't be able to dock until you inspect them for contraband. Try not to keep the innocent ones waiting.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You're just the kind of capsuleer I've been waiting for, {[character]player.name}. If you're interested, I've got something important that needs to get done, something I can't trust just anyone with. Your loyalty to the Republic is becoming legendary.

We're working on something big, {[character]player.name}, something very big. I can't go into specifics, but I can tell you that {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has been tasked with gathering materials from anywhere we can find them. Luckily, two of our objectives coincide.

It just happens that our old friends, the Angel Cartel, are sitting on a veritable treasure trove of spare parts and salvage out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. What do you say we kill two birds with one stone? Swing out there, vaporize all the Angel clowns you like, and bring us back some salvaged electronics. Sound good?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Oh, so you're too good to help out the Republic when it needs you? You capsuleers are all the same.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I can't imagine what you have to do that's more important than this, but I understand.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I see your reputation was well-deserved! I look forward to adding my name to your list of recommendations, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Fly to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and obtain the salvaged electronics, then return them to your agent in {[location]agentStationID.name}. Destroy any Angel Cartel ships that get in the way.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Yes, this is perfect. You've done the Republic a great service, {[character]player.name}. When the time comes and you witness our greatest accomplishment, you'll be able to say that you had a small part in paving the way for the future of all Minmatar!

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Sometimes I regret taking this desk job. Hey, while you're out there, blast a few Angel goons for me, would you?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
{[character]player.name}, it's good to see you. I have something a little outside of the ordinary that needs taking care of. A personal business opportunity for the both of us, I guess you could say.

Have you ever heard of Anire Scarlet? Well, she's practically an urban legend among the local pirates. It seems any outlaw with a clone bay and rhetorical skills can amass a following these days. The sorts of degenerates that hang around this area are easily impressed too. It seems Anire has built quite a posse, but then, that could just be another one of the myths about her.

As for where you come in: all this attention has earned her a CONCORD bounty. I'd very much like to claim that ISK, {[character]player.name}, with your help. I've hired an undercover surveillance team to locate her, and they've had some luck turning up a lead. If you're able to follow it up and take her out then we can split the bounty money equally. The surveillance team found her flagship vessel, The Crimson Dawn. She is sure to be either inside it, or very close by. If you think yourself capable of eliminating her, then I'll trade you the coordinates.

What do you say? Do we have a deal?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Too much for you to handle, huh?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Well, I can't say I blame you. I hear Anire Scarlet's pirates are pretty rough. They're all hell-bent on impressing their “Queen.”

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Though I doubt she'll run from a fight, you might want to bring a warp scrambler or disruptor to stop her from running deeper into cover.

Oh, and if you see some merchant vessels loitering around, hold your fire. That's my surveillance team. They may have some further intel once you arrive.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Nicely handled, {[character]player.name}. I'll keep you in mind for another bounty contract if she ever shows her head again.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: You have a bounty to collect, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Hello {[character]player.name}, up for some action? I have just received an offer from followers of the notorious pirate Zazzmatazz. The mission is to break him out of a private prison, Consolidated Holdings Inc. , which has a contract with Concord. Zazz is being held there, somewhat unexpectedly, for a very short time.

The client warns that once you have broken into the prison complex you will need to FINISH IT IN ONE run. Retreating is failure! The upside is that the client has promised some significant rewards if you prove capable and as a bonus, Consolidated Holdings Inc. is rumored to hold many secrets.

Are you up for it?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I guess I overestimated your abilities and the strength of your network of friends.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Alright! It is a little disappointing, but it's your call. This kind of mission doesn't float by every day.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Zazzmatazz may have eluded you but our client might settle for his DNA instead. It is better than nothing at least. Contact me soon for his response, it shouldn't take long.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good! There are several deadspace acceleration gates that and need to be unlocked one at a time in isolated deadspace pockets while a strike force moves in through the complex and finds Zazzmatazz.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Break Zazzmatazz out of Consolidated Holdings Inc.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Bring Zazzmatazz back as soon as you spring him out. There is a lot of heat on us because of this and I'm trying to stay out of the limelight.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Hello {[character]player.name}. Our client was furious about Zazzmatazz not being retrieved, but is willing to negotiate for his DNA. However, Consolidated Holdings, Inc., also contacted me about making a deal to get his DNA back. I'll leave it up to you who to deal with. I have arranged a meeting with Consolidated Holdings, but the pirate contact said he will be in touch with you. His real name is Ragnar Bloodthorn. When you've met them, make a decision quick, please — this is one problem I'd like out of my hands!

So, do you want to go to the meeting?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I thought you were taking care of that DNA business! Now I have both Bloodthorn and Consolidated Holdings breathing down my neck because of you.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Alright! Keep Zazzmatazz's DNA for yourself, then. I don't want anything more to do with it.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Alright, the locations for both targets are in the mission briefing. I'll see you around.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Deliver Zazzmatazz – or his DNA, to be more exact – to either Consolidated Holdings, Inc., or to the pirate Ragnar Bloodthorn. Consolidated Holdings has set up a meeting with your agent, and Ragnar Bloodthorn said he will be in touch. Both clients are very angry over the turn of events: Bloodthorn was expecting Zazzmatazz himself from your initial services, not his DNA, and Consolidated Holdings has lost a lot of assets and taken a blow to its reputation. Both have a score to settle with you, but they desperately need your cooperation as well, at least until they have secured Zazzmatazz's DNA.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good job, {[character]player.name}; this played out nicely. Consolidated Holdings, Inc., and this Ragnar Bloodthorn now have something to yell into the emptiness of space – they both got what they deserved!

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Get back to me when you have delivered Zazzmatazz's DNA to either party.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
{[character]player.name}? Good. I have a job that's probably outside your normal scope. This one is humanitarian.

A pandemic has broken out on a planet in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Fortunately, a cure was already developed and mass-produced. The contagion originated on another planet nearby, you see, so the people of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} already have experience in dealing with this particular disease.

The Sisters of Eve sent a medical drone with the vaccine onboard down to the planet, but some degenerate pirates have intercepted the craft, disabled it, and are now trying to demand a ransom for its release. The Sisters say that if the drone is destroyed it could be days before we can mass-produce more vaccine – something about being unable to accelerate the bacterial cultivation. A few more days with this disease uncontrolled could mean everything. We must recapture the drone.

We're depending on you here, {[character]player.name}. Once you've secured the drone, they can deploy repair teams and send it back on its way.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I should have known. Your kind disgusts me.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: What? You're telling me profit is more important than innocent lives?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: You're doing the right thing. Countless lives depend on you.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
A pandemic has broken out on a planet in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Fortunately, a cure was already developed and mass-produced. The contagion originated on another planet, you see, so the people of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} have experience in dealing with this particular disease.

The Sisters of Eve sent a medical drone with the vaccine onboard down to the planet, but some degenerate pirates have intercepted the craft and are trying to ransom it. The SSoE say that if the drone is destroyed, it could be days before we can mass-produce more vaccine – something about being unable to accelerate the bacterial cultivation. A few more days with this disease uncontrolled could mean everything. We must recapture the drone.

Once you've secured the drone, they can deploy repair teams and send it back on its way.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: We don't have any time to waste. Get moving.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Really? That's it? You're quitting? Why'd you agree to do it in the first place, then?

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: You will lose standing with those factions you choose not to rescue. Fair warning.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Great. You get out there, and you've got some rescue money coming your way. I don't really care who you rescue, just so long as you rescue someone. Fair warning, though – the ones you don't rescue are likely to remember it.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I just received an alert across multiple communication channels asking for evacuation help. A diplomatic station not far from here is undergoing a traumatic systems shut-down cascade. It's all going, and people need off that station. The rescue requires a smaller ship than what they have available to get in past the field of debris now ringing the station. That's what happens when none of the empires will trust the others enough to allow them to send in their best station engineers and construction teams, and so they all agree on a third-party freelance company to build their stations. Happens all the time, I hear. Ridiculous.

Anyway – are you interested?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good job, {[character]player.name}. Enjoy your reward, and the limelight for being a hero to those folks – you've earned it. You should know, however, that the folks you didn't save have already made it very clear that they're not happy with you.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: How's that rescue operation going?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Thank you for coming, pilot. As you know, the Amarr Empire is in a constant state of conflict. Our enemies have included organized criminal gangs, drug traffickers, terrorists of every conceivable motivation, pirates, unpacified slave populations, and even the occasional low level skirmish against our fair-weather friends, the Caldari, Gallente, and, lest we forget, the Minmatar. This requires the Empire to always remain vigilant to any situations that may call for the use of force on levels ranging from simple urban pacification to outright military combat. What you do not know is that a high-level internal Empire report has revealed that our casualty levels have been steadily increasing over the last several years, often requiring evacuation to more robust – and already overburdened – medical facilities.

In the “recommendations” section of this report, the researchers concluded that the single most identifiable cause of these excessive casualties is a systemic problem with our lightweight body armor. This armor is standard issue for millions of police and security personnel, as well as our military reconnaissance units. Unless a drastic improvement in the quality and durability of this body armor can be found, we will continue to suffer the consequences.

This morning I received a priority communication from an Amarr Intelligence Officer claiming that his team had just “obtained” a revolutionary new fabric that, if properly processed, could literally double the strength of our existing armor. I know this officer only by reputation, and it is best not to pry any further into how his team came across this “miracle cloth.” Nonetheless, we have been advised that they will arrive at this station within moments to transfer the fabric here for transshipment to a more secure facility.

So, pilot, will you transport this prototype body armor fabric to the station facility we designate?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Quitting mid-mission is not something I expected from you. Now I am going to have to answer to the intelligence team. Oh, and don't expect any further jobs from me until your failure here has been long forgotten. Damn… I need a stress pill….

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I must say I am disappointed in your decision to turn down this mission. I vouched for you personally, given what I have seen in your files about your excellent mission completion record. I will not soon forget your refusal.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Lightweight body armor is a common and often required element of any police or security forces' operational gear. Modern armor of this type can stop most projectile, laser, and other light weapon fire. However, as small arms weaponry continued to evolve with regard to the amount of damage it can inflict, so to must the defensive technologies designed to maintain parity with these weapons. On rare occasions, a corporation, military laboratory, or other entity will produce a light body armor system that represents nothing short of a generational leap in design and protection. The multilayered fabrics used in these latter applications are usually amongst the most highly guarded secrets of any civilization, for many reasons. The most advanced of these contain nanotechnology which also can change color and density depending on ambient conditions and/or input from the wearer.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: That is very good to hear, thank you. We will transfer the cargo to your hangar immediately, along with a small element of the intelligence team, who have stated that they will provide security through to the final destination station. You'd best head to your ship quickly, as I wouldn't want those guys on board my ship without an escort, especially as the rather unique weapons they usually carry are easily capable of punching a nice little hole in your hull.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Our security and military ground forces have been experiencing a slow but steady increase in the numbers and severity of injuries suffered during a wide range of armed conflicts. A recent stuffy by Amarr military scientists has determined that the primary cause of this has been a failure to adequately improve the lightweight body armor worn by millions of our soldiers, Marines, police, and other fighting forces. As fate would have it, one of our intelligence units has obtained what they claim to be a revolutionary new fabric that could provide fifty percent better protection across the board in all types of engagements. We need you to deliver this very sensitive cargo to a station we designate.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Outstanding, pilot. You were even a bit ahead of schedule. Our offloading team is en route to your ship, and the Intel guards will stay with the shipment until that has been completed. I will keep your name in my “go to” list should any more missions come up in the future.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Thank you for the update pilot, but no need to contact me until you arrive. The Intel security team on your ship is keeping me quite well informed.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
One of our Caldari Navy Special Forces units conducting clandestine reconnaissance of a contested ocean planet – a Gallente-claimed planet, by the way, with extremely rare seabed minerals – sent an emergency burst communication to the covert ops ship in orbit above the planet, requesting immediate extraction. This signal was, in turn, transmitted to the classified comms center here on this station. When we attempted to contact both the team and the ship, however, we received no response. Our immediate reaction was to divert one of our long range Crow-class interceptors, which was in the region on an unrelated mission, to investigate. Soon after its arrival, its sensors confirmed that the covert ops ship had been destroyed.

There is nothing we can do for our lost covops ship; however, this series of events has left the Special Forces team alone and without a means to evacuate the planet. Even worse was a fragment from the original communication indicating that the team was on the run and low on food, water, weapons, and ammunition. They have taken refuge in a disused ocean mining facility, though it is doubtful that they will stay hidden for long. There simply aren't many places to hide on that planet, given the fact that it is mostly covered by massive oceans, with very little land mass. It will not take long for the Gallente to track down our team and either kill them or, worse, capture them for interrogation.

The good news in all this is that we have an extraction team in place, along with a shuttle-equipped vessel to deliver them to the planet. However, given the immediacy of this mission, they had to leave their original base without much of their usual equipment and weaponry. This is where you come in. We need you to transport several containers of highly specialized small arms and related equipment to the station at which the extraction team is currently located. Once you drop off this cargo, the team will gear-up and shuttle down to the planet to rescue the stranded team.

So, pilot, what is it gonna be? Will you help us?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our military personnel at great risk. It is doubtful that we will be able to find anyone else to get this critical shipment to the station in time.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Your refusal to accept this mission will almost certainly result in the loss of this Special Forces team, not to mention placing the now-dangerously unequipped extraction team at great risk.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you for accepting this important, time-sensitive mission. You have been given priority clearance for station undock, so please leave as soon as possible.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A small, platoon-sized Caldari special operation team is in hiding on a Gallente planet and in danger of being captured or killed. They are low on water, food, weapons, and other equipment and will not last long unless they are extracted. We have a rescue standing by; however, we need you to deliver the required materials to their station so that they can then proceed with this critical rescue mission.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: We have received word that the extraction team has taken delivery of your cargo and is now en route to the planet. Given the speed with which you delivered this essential shipment, we assess a high likelihood that the stranded team will be safely extracted. Well done!

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Do not contact us until you have completed this shipment. There is simply no time for idle chatter, not to mention the likelihood that the enemy is almost certainly listening in.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Let me start at the beginning. As you have probably seen on the news channels, a prominent Caldari mining company is in the middle of a very nasty battle for economic survival with a new, up-and-coming mining company from within the same large conglomerate. Both of these companies specialize in the extraction of ores from some of the more inhospitable and dangerous locations in this and several adjoining systems. While this can be hazardous with regard to men and equipment, the profit potential from these largely untapped ore reserves can be quite significant, which brings me to our current predicament.

As you may know, the specialized manual labor required for some of these mines can be significant in terms of numbers. Well, the Mining Health and Safety Commission, or MHSC, for this region recently conducted a survey of the first company's operations, and found that their mining practices at certain locations may have resulted in excessive pollution, then further alleged a corresponding link to long-term miner health problems. The company has loudly complained that this is a ridiculous witch hunt brought about by their new competitor, which happens to have several “friends” on the commission. While they work to ensure they are equally “represented” on that commission, the recent finding has mandated that they immediately improve worker conditions and reduce pollution or risk losing their mining rights. To remedy this problem, they recently purchased a large number of the latest environmentally-friendly – and obscenely expensive – manportable drills, which seems to have assuaged the MHSC for the moment. They do, however, have a deadline for actually putting these new drills into the hands of the miners, which brings us to the reason I contacted you.

We need you to deliver a rather large shipment of drills and other related equipment to a station that serves as a central service hub. From there, logistics pilots will deliver this and other items to the various mines in the system. Will you take on this important job?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: We are shocked to hear that you have chosen to quit this job in the middle of the contract. We will now have to pay another pilot double to pick up where you left off. You should have let us know from the outset that you could not take on this important job. Hopefully, we will never have to rely on you again.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Well, I must say we are quite disappointed that you would turn down this very easy contract. We shall find another pilot and move your name to the bottom of our list. Don't call us, we'll call you.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I certainly do appreciate your help, pilot. Hopefully, if we can get these drills into the hands of the miners in short order, the company should be able to retain its mining rights and return to profitability.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Due to a recent series of inspections by the regional mine monitoring commission, we have found it necessary to purchase a large quantity of the latest generation of environmentally-friendly drills and related equipment.

In order to avoid financial penalties and the possible loss of our mining rights, that company must get these quite expensive new drills into the hands of the miners as soon as possible. If you can deliver this cargo to the station that serves as our logistical hub for this system, they can then have their own pilots transship them to the required planetary mining locations.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Job well done. Our logistics teams are loading your shipment into their transport vessels as we speak, and we should have the drills and equipment in place shortly. We will definitely contact you again, should we require your services.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: You seem to be on schedule and we look forward to the prompt delivery of the equipment to the designated station. Contact us through the usual channels after you have offloaded this gear.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
As you know, there are many hundreds of thousands of Minmatar slaves working to provide essential services to the Empire, just as they have for centuries. Given their considerable natural physical abilities, they have always made up one of the most important and valuable ethnic groups within the vast Amarr slave workforce.
