Specifically, they want our entire stockpile of our rarest and most expensive metal, quantrium – one found only in the wiring of electronic countermeasures (ECM) equipment of the Caldari Navy's Rook-class combat reconnaissance ships.

What I need you to do is to quickly move this quantrium to the designated station for transshipment to the slavers' rendezvous point. We will take it from there.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: The kidnappers have been listening to our comms, and have heard that you have chosen to quit. They have let us know that we will not see the executive's daughter again. I hope your reasons for quitting are worth the life of an innocent young girl.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: We were counting on you. You were our only hope for the safe return of the CEO's daughter. I hope your cowardice here today will haunt you for the rest of your miserable life!

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you for agreeing to help us. We will have the quantrium moved into your item hangar as soon as possible. You have already been cleared for emergency departure.

messages.mission.briefing.text: The daughter of a Caldari executive was kidnapped this morning by a group of slavers while she was on holiday. They are demanding we provide them a large quantity of our rarest and most expensive metal, quantrium, in exchange for her life. There is no time to mount a rescue operation, so our only choice is to provide this shipment immediately. We will deal with those criminals once the girl has been released to us. However, time is of the essence, and our primary mission now is to deliver this shipment to a transshipment station for further transportation to the slavers' designated rendezvous point.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: We just got word from the hotel security staff – the executive's daughter was returned to them safe and sound, as the kidnappers promised!  We owe you a debt I hope we can repay one day! We will not forget you!

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Please, pilot, do make haste. The quantrium must be delivered as soon as possible. If we are even one minute late to the rendezvous, the slavers will assume we have involved the authorities, and we will never see the young girl again.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Greetings, {[character]player.name}. Several days ago, an internal security team identified a Gallente deep cover saboteur working at one of our clandestine shipyards producing the current generation of Widow-class Black Ops battleships. He swallowed a hidden poison tablet as we moved in to arrest him, so he is no longer a threat.

However, during a routine quality control check, the shipyard's scientific team was shocked to discover a highly advanced nanite swarm that the saboteur had somehow introduced into the shipyard's stockpile of advanced adhesives used to bond sensor-absorbing coatings to the hulls of our newly-constructed Widows. The effect of this harmful agent is to slowly erode this protective coating, thus increasing the ship's signature radius, making it much easier for our enemies to detect and attack.

Given the slow-acting nature of this particular breed of nanite, it is unlikely that this gradual loss of stealth capability would be noticeable under routine operating conditions, thus placing the ship and its crew at mortal risk when operating in hostile space. Essentially, the Widow's commander would not know that his ship had lost its critical operational advantage until he was detected and targeted by hostile combatants. Given the very specialized role of this ship, not only would the Widow be compromised, but it is possible than any ships he might be bridging in via its covert jump portal generator could be unknowingly hot dropped near a waiting enemy fleet, instead of empty space.

In order to remedy this critical situation, we need you to immediately transport a large quantity of our new aerogel counteragent to a station for further distribution to the fleet. This shipment represents our best and only hope to quickly repair the damage done by the Gallente spy and ensure the safety of our brave Widow pilots and crew.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our Black Ops teams at great risk. We will have to find another operative elsewhere.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: We are disappointed that you've chosen not to accept this critical mission. We will have to find another pilot elsewhere.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Produced by the Kaalakiota megacorporation, the Widow-class Black Ops battleship represents the current edge technology for Caldari military vessels used in covert operations. The primary function of the Widow is to conduct infiltration and espionage behind enemy lines. Specifically, when equipped with covert cynosural field generators and covert jump portal generators, the ship can create a “bridge” through which conventional ships are instantly transported, much like a jump gate. The effect of this is to surprise an enemy by instantly “hot dropping” a combat fleet into what was, moments prior, only empty space. In addition, it can also be fitted with ECM modules and cruise missiles such that it can provide jamming capabilities and supporting firepower if necessary. Using this technology, the Widow represents a significant force multiplier in the ongoing conflicts faced by the Caldari State.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: We are relieved to hear that you've accepted this important mission. It is imperative that you deliver this cargo with all possible haste.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Several days ago, an internal security team identified a Gallente deep cover saboteur working at one of our clandestine shipyards producing the current generation of Widow-class Black Ops battleships. During a routine quality control check, the shipyard's scientific team was shocked to discover a highly advanced nanite swarm that the saboteur had somehow introduced into the shipyard's stockpile of advanced adhesives used to bond sensor-absorbing coatings to the hulls of our newly-constructed Widows. The effect of this harmful agent is to slowly erode this protective coating, thus increasing the ship's sensor cross-section, making it much easier to detect and attack. Given the slow-acting nature of this particular breed of nanite, it is unlikely that this gradual loss of stealth capability would be noticeable under routine operating conditions, thus placing the ship and its crew at mortal risk when operating in hostile space. Therefore, we need you to immediately transport a large quantity of our new aerogel counteragent to a station for further distribution to the fleet.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Your successful delivery of the prototype nanites will undoubtedly save the lives of many Black Ops pilots and crew. You have the makings of a good counter operative!

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Do not contact me on an open channel until this mission is complete. Remember, this is a clandestine operation!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Before we begin, I must make one thing perfectly clear: You were never here, and this meeting never took place. You do understand what I mean, yes?

We are in need of a pilot who can deliver a very sensitive cargo from this station to a nearby station, without attracting any undue attention. You may have heard in the news or the local gossip channels that a Caldari regional director for mining operations was murdered yesterday by unknown assailants while touring an asteroid field in his personal shuttle. That much is indeed true. However, what has not been reported is that we have, in the last few hours, learned the identity of the assassin, a mercenary who goes by the name “Black Dog”, and that he and his team have already begun to plan for an ongoing hit-and-run campaign designed to try and scare off Caldari corporations from any future mining activities in the region.

Of course, we cannot allow this kind of disruption to what has proven a highly lucrative endeavor – the Board and our shareholders simply will not tolerate any further dips in revenues. To remedy this interruption, one of our sister companies that specializes in, shall we say, discrete solutions, has loaned us one of their most highly trained specialists to resolve this issue. His name, as you might expect, is Mr. Smith. His mission, in brief, is to liquidate Black Dog, along with any associates that may be operating with him at the time.

What we need from you, and need soon, is for you to transport Mr. Smith and his entourage to a station closer to the action – one with a hangar walkway the leads directly to an unmarked office. Once you have dropped him off, your role in this action will be complete.

So, what is it going to be, pilot? We need a yes or no right now if this operation is to stay on schedule.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our executives and even our miners at significant risk from these mercenaries.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Your unwillingness to assist us in this matter is going to cost this corporation a great deal of isk until we can find some other way to resolve it. Mr. Smith may soon take a personal interest in you, as you've now disrupted his lucrative contract. I certainly don't want to be in your shoes once he gets the word.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: We all know the saying, “business is war.” Nowhere is this adage practiced more seriously than in the Caldari corporate world. The soldiers in this fight are typically thought of as the salesmen, managers, executives, and other boardroom warriors. However, from time to time a very special skill set is required to deal with an equally specific threat. For these situations, corporate assassins are sometimes required to resolve issues that cannot be otherwise remedied through conventional channels. In the most extreme cases, these highly-trained operatives, most of whom served particularly arduous and dangerous careers in the Caldari Special Forces and intelligence groups, are hired to carry out very selective missions with very limited goals. The missions they are paid, - highly paid at that - to undertake would rival any holovid espionage movie, though the consequences are, of course, much more serious. You don't want to mess with these guys, and gals, as it is usually the last thing you'll ever do.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. We appreciate your assistance in this matter. Please ensure this operation continues to enjoy the level of security that we've been able to sustain so far. Make no stops, scheduled or unscheduled, between this station and the final destination.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A team of mercenaries led by a man calling himself “Black Dog” has killed one of our senior managers as he toured an asteroid field not far from here. Intelligence has indicated that he intends to continue these operations into the foreseeable future. To remedy this unacceptable situation, we need you to transport a trained assassin and his entourage to a station closer to the scene of the crime. Once this is done, you will have completed the terms of this contract. We appreciate your discretion in this endeavor.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: We just received word from Mr. Smith that you did indeed deliver him on time and without attracting any unusual inquiries. We hope the compensation for this mission was worth your time. The Caldari State can use more competent and discretionary pilots like you.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Why are you contacting me?

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Our engineering scientists, working at our highly secure, clandestine R&D facility on a nearby planet have produced a new type of cloaking device that, when fitted to Covert Ops ships, could theoretically enable them to jump through stargates without uncloaking! And yes, I can see by the look on your face that you must think I've had far too many Extra Strength Quafe sodas today. However, I can assure you that, while it may be many years before this technology is perfected and suitable for even experimental use, the science behind it is quite real, and this is where this story takes a very important twist.

Our internal security teams have managed to uncover a plan formulated by one of our competitors to steal the prototype cloaking system at some point between the time it leaves the lab up until it arrives at the field testing facility over in the next system. Problem is, we don't yet know who the spy is, so we devised a plan to get that spy to expose himself so that we can then move in and make the arrest.

To this end, you will be delivering is a very detailed mock-up series of the actual prototype, one that will withstand an initial visual and electronic scrutiny on the part of the thief. In all practical terms, however, these devices could no more cloak a ship than it could cook your morning breakfast. We are naming this event Operation Doorstop, which is our planning team's attempt at humor, given the uselessness of this particular lump of metal and wires. What we do need, though, is your absolute confidentiality on this shipment. If the spy gets any whiff that this is a set-up, we will likely never know who he or she is, and we will remain at ongoing risk of one of our most important R&D projects potentially falling into the wrong hands.

So, what do you say, {[character]player.name}? Willing to take on this rather interesting assignment?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: By quitting mid-mission you've singlehandedly compromised the whole operation! I doubt we'll be able to flush out the spy now, given the fact that you've interrupted the shipment – no doubt he will sense something is up and simply remain unknown to us.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Well, we are disappointed that you've turned this one down. We'll have to use one of our own transportation pilots to get this done.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I'm glad to hear you're going to help us out here. We aren't expecting any trouble with this one, but with corporate espionage, you never know – keep your eyes open.

messages.mission.briefing.text: One of our R&D facilities has been working hard to produce a new type of cloaking device for Covert Ops vessels that will allow those ships to remain cloaked while jumping stargates. However, it has recently been brought to our attention that a corporate espionage agent sent by a rival company is targeting this new technology, for obvious reasons. In order to flush him out and arrest him, however, we need to catch him in the act. So, we are asking you to transport a decoy prototype cloaking device from this station to one we designate. With such a juicy target, we feel the spy will not be able to resist making an attempt to steal it somewhere between here and there. We need you to fly this device to that station utilizing absolute secrecy.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Outstanding job, {[character]player.name}! As you may have heard by now, the spy was caught trying to remove the device from the offload cargo bay on the station. Needless to say, he has a very uncomfortable future ahead of him in one of our interrogation facilities. Thanks to your piloting skills and discretion, our work on the new cloak remains a well guarded secret.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: We know the mission is proceeding well, as we've got a cloaked Covert Ops ship following you at a discrete distance. Please contact me only in the event of an emergency.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
History has shown us that a properly motivated slave work force can work harder and longer - especially in harsh conditions - if they are provided the means to enhance their everyday lives. Well, for many decades, the provision of various stimulant drugs to slave laborers was considered a standard method of doing business. However, the downside to this was that, while the use of stims typically increased productivity, more often than not it resulted in significant long term health problems for the slaves leading to shortened lifespans and, more importantly, to decreased profits. So, while the use of stimulants has largely been discontinued, the idea that drugs could increase slave output never entirely went away, though it did require a new approach.

To this end, my company recently developed an inexpensive new drug that works on the pleasure centers of the brain, providing what we might call a “reward” for hard work. Importantly, this drug, known as Blue Paradise, or "Beep" as the techs call it, has been proven in real-world testing to increase slave labor output by as much as twenty percent across the board, without any known long term health problems. As you can guess, the increased profit potential here is, well, staggering. Equally important is the fact that we have not reported this new drug to the various control boards; nor do we intend to at this juncture.

We need you to deliver a very large shipment of this drug to a forward logistics hub station from which it will be transshipped to ore mines, agricultural farms, and other slave-intensive operations. I can give you my guarantee that this cargo will not be flagged by customs or the police, as it is not yet deemed an illegal substance.

So, can we count on you to deliver this?

messages.mission.extrainfo.header.text: Biochemical Agents for Improved Slave Workloads

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: There are few things I despise more than a quitter. If you come back to my station I am sure we can find you a position on the station slave labor gang, scrubbing the personal hygiene tanks with a toothbrush for the next six months.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Well, you have certainly wasted my very valuable time. I thought we could count on you, but obviously I was misinformed. Don't count on working for me any time soon.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
We all know that there have been a long series of proclamations, laws, and rules banning the transportation of illegal drugs (and some legal drugs) in Amarr space for use in slave labor. These prohibitions have typically had no real teeth, unless of course the Empress herself sets forth an official decree specifically banning a given substance. The logical, time-tested way around this has been to create entirely new generations of performance enhancing biochemical drugs.

As slaves are typically wary of any pills or other obvious means of altering their behavior (recalling, as we must, the various slave uprisings that have occurred when we tried to openly force drugs on them), we've had to resort to less obvious methods. For example, we have surreptitiously and gradually delivered the drugs into laborer's systems through aerosols in their habitat ventilation systems, impregnated substances into their foodstuffs and water supplies, and other rather clever means, I won't go into here. What is important is that the result has almost always been a positive one, with significant increases in worker productivity.

The downside to this, however, has been a decline in overall slave lifespans due to the long term effects of these drugs. Normally, this would be considered simple attrition; a cost of doing businesses. However, as it continues to become more and more difficult to obtain new slaves (particularly given the intolerable and unjust interference of the other empires), this solution is less and less viable. We need them to live as long as possible. This reality, of course, leads us to the only other benign option – drugs as a part of a rewards system for those slaves who meet a certain work quota each day.

To this end, we shall continue to develop new substances to both avoid interference by Customs and police forces and to ensure the maximum possible output by our slave laborers.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good, glad to hear it. I will immediately order the refrigerated secure containers moved into your cargo hold for your prompt departure.

messages.mission.briefing.text: In order to get around the laws pertaining to the transportation of illegal drugs through Amarr Empire space, we have been forced to create new and unknown substances for use on, or by, rather, our various slave labor enclaves. This new drug, Blue Paradise, does away with many of the harmful chemicals previously used while actually increasing the pleasurable effects. We are certain that, properly controlled and distributed, introduction of this drug into the slave labor workforce will increase productivity by a substantial margin. We are counting on you to deliver it to the designation transshipment station as soon as possible.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent. We are transferring your cargo to a dozen smaller ships equipped for high speed runs to the more remote work sites in the region. I see a lot of profit in your future, {[character]player.name}, if you stick with us.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: See, I told you this would be a smooth run. Customs and the police have been advised that you will be transiting their space and that you are not to be disturbed. Have a safe flight. Hell, you can practically autopilot this one!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I'm sure you're all too aware of our war with the Caldari State. It's been dragging on for years with no end in sight... until now, that is. We've been making some good headway on the active front and our research and development has been busy behind the scenes. Military scientists have developed a hybrid round that works like single-target burst ECM, and it's time to introduce it to the military for an active field-test.

Take these over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you finished your delivery, {[character]player.name}?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm disappointed, {[character]player.name}. If we find that you've shared this with the Caldari, it will not go well for you.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}. I thought your loyalty might mean more to you.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: There has always been contention over the effectiveness of the Federation's sensor-dampening ewar tactics against the State's ECM. Some military scientists feel that, in adding ECM to the hybrid arsenal, the Federation would be admitting to a weakness and confirming the State's superiority; others argue that turning the enemy's tactics against them is an essential facet of wartime, and that rejecting the opportunity is effectively signing off on the Federation's defeat. The debate rages in both the staterooms and the laboratories even as research and development continues.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Do not fail us, {[character]player.name}. The Federation is depending on you.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Federation R&D specialists have been working to find counters for Caldari military tactics; the latest development is a special type of ammunition that works similarly to a lock breaker bomb, but on a single target. I want you to take it over to a navy base for testing, and you need to keep word of this development from going very far.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. You are a true child of the Federation.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
A short time ago, Minmatar terrorists in a combined fleet of frigates and cruisers attacked one of our Harbinger-class strategic cruisers as it was transporting slaves from a recently closed mine to a new mineral harvesting facility in a nearby system. While all but one of the attackers was annihilated, our convoy's escorts were destroyed and our cruiser is burning. Making a bad situation worse, we are anticipating that the terrorists will return in force within the next several hours to attempt the theft of our slaves, as they almost certainly know the cruiser is alone and all but helpless.

Our concern is that if the terrorists feel that they have a window of opportunity to recover these slaves, it is likely that they will throw everything they have into the effort. Our intelligence assessments of the terrorists' fleet assets are even less reassuring: we believe that they could send as many as four battlecruisers into this fight – more than enough to wipe out the arriving frigates and forcefully board our heavily damaged strategic cruiser. However, we have calculated that if we can delay any terrorist boarding parties long enough, this should give us enough time for the much larger main rescue fleet to arrive.

The only bright side to this situation, in what is unquestionably an act of divine providence, is that a large contingent of marines are aboard this station as we speak, having just completed specialized refresher training in counter-boarding operations. We need you to deliver them to the station closest to the last reported position of our cruiser. From there, we will transport a combined team of marines, engineers, medics, and other essential personnel to hopefully stop the fire and save the ship - along with its cargo of highly valuable slaves. However, this mission must be undertaken immediately. Any delay will surely doom the Harbinger and her brave crew.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Quitting? Now?  You have placed our marines and hundreds of other personnel in grave danger by abandoning them mid-mission. We will have to find some way to get them to our damaged strategic cruiser, though I feel it is now too late.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: We will not forget this – the moment you chose to abandon our people in a time of great need. Your assistance could have turned the tide of this whole disaster. Do not contact me again.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Our deepest thanks for taking on this mission. I can tell you that our best analysts feel that you should be fairly safe in this mission, as the terrorist will have to focus all their efforts on targeting the stricken cruiser. They simply won't have the ships or the time to even attempt to interdict your ship as you make your way to the destination station.

messages.mission.briefing.text: While transporting Minmatar slaves from a recently close ore mine to a new mineral harvesting facility in nearby system, the convoy was attacked by terrorists, destroying the escort frigates and heavily damaging the Harbinger-class battlecruiser carrying the slaves. We believe it is likely that the terrorists will return, and in larger ships, to attempt a rescue of the slaves before we can respond with reinforcements. The window of opportunity for the terrorists is short, so it is imperative that we immediately render as much help as possible. What we need you to do is deliver a contingent of heavily armed marines recently trained in counter-boarding operations to a station closer to the site of the battle. From there, they will join other Amarr military and rescue teams for immediate transportation to the damaged cruiser.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: We've received confirmation that you did indeed fulfill your promise and deliver the Marines to the station. As we speak, the combined rescue team is loading into other ship for immediate transport to the Harbinger. Hopefully, we will reach them in time.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Excellent news, pilot, thank you for updating us as to your position and condition. Please make all possible speed to the destination so that we can then dispatch the combined rescue team package.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
This is a list of people I want you to escort to a meeting. They have quite a large security entourage, and as you can see from some of the names, they have a reason for it. These people are members of the Angel Cartel. While the Cartel are thugs and pirate scum, and are not particularly welcome in Minmatar space, it does not mean that some corporations don't have certain dealings with them.

This isn't your usual business meeting this time, however. Evidently, the Cartel overstepped their bounds, and the corporation took it to the Republic. Escort these Angel representatives to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; we'll take care of the rest. For the sake of appearances, try to treat them politely. We don't want them to know it's a set-up until they get to the boardroom.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Hello, {[character]player.name}. Have you finished your work for me?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm extremely disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}, but I can understand why you might decline.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The Angel Cartel's reputation for engaging in any activity regardless of its legality has earned it the DED's description of the most dangerous criminal organization in the cluster. With a corporate command structure and open recruitment policy, the Cartel are less thugs than sharks in pinstripe suits, capable of operating on all levels of society. With a major operational base in Etherium Reach on the edge of Minmatar space, the Cartel is held with deep suspicion within the Republic. Their annexation of the Skarkon system in YC 110 and sudden withdrawal left many unanswered questions regarding both the Cartel's intentions towards the Republic and what deals were forged under the table to make them leave... and what those deals might have cost.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. Please hurry.

messages.mission.briefing.text: I have to request a difficult task of you: play nice with a swarm of Angel Cartel representatives and their entourage on your ship. Hopefully they won't try to cause you trouble.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent, thank you, {[character]player.name}. I think we got our point across to them; there are some things you do not try to push in the Republic.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: There's a fitness initiative going through Federation schools. I'm sure you've heard about it? A weird luddite group called The Natural Way wants to get kids to stop relying on modding to stay in shape, and they're tossing cred around like water to do so. No school would turn down money in exchange for a couple hours' fitness classes a week. Take these {[item]objectiveTypeID.name} over to one of their facilities at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and we'll see some of that money, too.

messages.root.agentsays.text: You haven't WATCHED those, have you?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Well, fine. But burn the holos. We don't want normal people watching that stuff.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: What? Who doesn't want to take advantage of anti-tech crazies?

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Body modification, or "modding," is widely accepted throughout the Federation, primarily for cosmetic purposes. Color-changing tattoos which move, programmable "makeup" which is implanted in subcutaneous layers, piercings and body-shaping are the most common forms, so normal they're barely worth mentioning. The wilder forms of modding, however, can frequently give people the wrong idea. Parents who want to discourage their children from engaging in extreme modding may sometimes turn to groups which support lower-tech ways of life for educational programs, particularly in the tumultuous teenage years when youngsters start to seek their personal identity.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Just don't watch those, okay? They gave me nightmares.

messages.mission.briefing.text: The Natural Way is a group which promotes a lower-tech way of life. They're throwing around a lot of cred to start a fitness initiative encouraging kids to stay away from body modding, and I see nothing wrong with encouraging them in exchange for a little ISK.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. My mother's been giving those to my kids for their birthdays every year, and I was afraid I'd never get rid of them.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: The Federal Talent Showcase is upon us, that time of year where all the artists and “artists” come out of hiding and shove the products of the past year in our faces. {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is playing host to a fashion show and we need someone to pick up the models and fashionistas from {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. You can kind of guess what they're like – a normal pilot just isn't good enough for them, so I have to find a capsuleer I think is level-headed enough to not vent cargo into space if they get too annoying. I know you can handle it, it's not like you have to speak with them face to face, anyway.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you picked up the models yet? The show's only a few hours away!

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm disappointed, {[character]player.name}. We have a reputation to maintain.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Regrettable, but I can't say I blame you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: In a culture as materialistic and appearance-conscious as the Gallente, the ability to stay on the bleeding edge is a valuable asset. “Clothes,” fashion critic Marko Envaumier said in a well-known interview with the Scope, “are an outward expression of man's inner nature and outlook toward life. Professional secretaries study fashion alongside the other office skills ... to learn to gauge the worth of both potential clients and employees for the companies that hire them. Next time you walk into an office, remember that the boy or girl behind the desk is checking your tailoring.”

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. I'll make it worth your while.

messages.mission.briefing.text: {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is hosting a fashion show for publicity, and your agent needs you to pick up the models. For some reason, they think you won't get fed up and drop them all off in orbit around the nearest moon.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! I imagine you're happy to have that lot off your hands.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You are aware, no doubt, of the rumors of extremist antislavery terrorist groups within the Amarr Empire itself. Well, you know then that their loyalty to the Empire is indeed secondary to their overarching desire to see all slaves freed and made equal members of society. This is a condition that we, as the greatest state in all of New Eden, simply cannot tolerate. However, our efforts at arresting and reeducating those insurgents have largely failed to permanently change the mindsets of these rather fanatical individuals.

This system has been particularly hard hit by this and other like-minded groups. Most recently, an Anathema-class covert ops ship, specially configured to transport elite slaves to the estates of senior Amarr leaders in the region, was somehow decloaked, its weapons and sensors jammed, and ruthlessly attacked to the point of near-total structure failure. The terrorists then demanded the pilot transfer the slaves to this mystery ship, on threat of the total destruction of the covert ops vessel. The pilot complied, though he has since been punished for his cowardice.

It is for this reason that I called you here today. I need you to transport a new shipment of elite slaves to a nearby station for further transshipment to the residence of one of the regional governors. This shipment is of particular urgency as the governor is hosting his annual gala event at his estate, and the usual staff of slaves simply will not do. We need these specific slaves, as they have been trained in protocol, proper food and drink service, entertainment, and numerous other talents that I need not mention here.

Will you take on this courier mission on behalf of the Empire and deliver these highly trained and extremely expensive slaves to the designated station?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You must be kidding?!? I have already guaranteed the governor's office that you are en route and will arrive at the scheduled time. This act on your part is probably going to get me reassigned to some asteroid in an uncharted system a million light years from here. Well, I will make sure I'm not the only one who will feel the heat for this failure.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: While I must say I am rather shocked at your refusal to undertake this mission, we are fortunate in that we do have contingency plans in place. So, while we will have to risk the crew and slaves in another run, I feel confident that only you will bear the negative feedback for failing us here today.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: While it might seem impossible at first glance, there are indeed small bands of terrorists who seek to upset the very core foundation of our society by working to eliminate slavery throughout the Empire. We have had significant success in disrupting these groups, with many members killed or taken prisoner. Nonetheless, like a hydra they continue to grow and adapt to our tactics and operations, making them a quite annoying thorn in our side. The Amarr Empire is devoting increasing resources to the eradication of these groups; however, even the most optimistic analysts concede that it may be quite some time before this nascent insurgency can be eradicated.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: That is very good news, pilot. I will contact the governor's aide myself to let her know that you have accepted and will be departing shortly.

messages.mission.briefing.text: We have recently been experiencing an increase in terrorist attacks by groups seeking to free Amarr slaves in this region. Their raids have become more complex and lethal, resulting in the loss of untold millions of ISK worth of valuable property. More importantly, one of the regional governors is having his annual gala event at his estate on a nearby planet. We need you to deliver a cargo of elite conditioned slaves to a station we will designate. From there they will be transported to the governor's estate by heavily armed ships.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great job, {[character]player.name}. The slaves are being offloaded now and will be en route to the governor's estate shortly. I can't thank you enough for your reliability and promptness.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Thank you for the update pilot, it is rather reassuring that you are flying without any interference from our unwanted friends. Please contact me again when you are being towed in to the dock, as only then will I feel assured that this courier mission was a success.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You need to keep this quiet, {[character]player.name}. I know you capsuleers aren't accustomed to being told how to do your job, but this is bigger than anything else and if word gets out, all this effort will be for nothing.

We've acquired samples of the Amarr's latest experimental starship tech. Don't ask me how, I don't want to know, and neither do you. We're not sure what these pieces do; our source is suggesting it's a system that reduces the effectiveness of our electronic warfare systems. This could be bad news for us. Get the stuff over to the lab at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. And keep your trap shut. We don't want it getting back to the Amarr that we have this.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you delivered that stuff to the lab, {[character]player.name}?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I guess your loyalty isn't worth as much as I thought.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I guess your loyalty isn't worth as much as I thought.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The current war between the Republic and the Empire is not solely left to warfare in space. Spies and sympathizers work behind the scenes to sabotage war efforts and uncover the Empire's secrets, helping the Republic to meet the Empire's forces equally. The Empire has its own spies, however, and the underlying conflict can sap morale and lead to high levels of paranoia.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. I knew we could count on you.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Our spies have succeeded in smuggling pieces of the latest experimental Amarrian starship technology back to the Republic. I need you to take the samples on to the lab where they can be properly analyzed.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good job, {[character]player.name}. Our research team is saying the tech deflects target painter beams away towards an area of space just behind the ship it's fitted on. Our torpedoes will start missing targets if they manage to make this widely available. We need to find a way to counter this, and fast.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
{[character]player.name}! Glad you could make it on such short notice. Let me get right to the point: Yesterday, as you almost certainly know, a regional governor delivered her State of the Region address. Needless to say, we were quite excited and thus put forth a maximum effort to ensure that her speech was broadcast on every possible channel and to the maximum ranges of our civilian and military communications networks.

However, for various reasons at many remote locations, this signal did not reach many who would have otherwise benefitted from this opportunity. For all our efforts, there are some locations that can only be reached the hard way -- ferrying holoreels directly to each and every one of them. We have already dispatched messengers, primarily in interceptors and other fast ships, to these more dangerous destinations.

We need you to transport a quantity of holoreels containing the State of the Region speech to one station in particular and hand them over to an agent who will be waiting for them there. He will then handle all further distribution of the 'reels.

So, can you help us with what should be a straightforward courier job?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Well, I was not expecting this. All we needed was for you to make a simple run from this station to the designated station and drop off our cargo. Well, suffice to say, you will not be receiving any prayers of blessing from me tonight!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I must say we are quite disappointed. As you know, all of our pilots are gone, taking these 'reels to the faithful. Your refusal leaves a gap in this coverage that will leave many faithful Amarr without this important message from the governor.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you a million times over, pilot, for taking on this mission. The hearts and minds of the Amarr faithful in that station and elsewhere will benefit immeasurably from your prompt delivery of these hallowed holoreels.

messages.mission.briefing.text: The regional governor herself delivered an important State of the Region speech yesterday to all her billions of faithful followers. Due to technical problems, however, this message did not reach as many citizens as it should have. Fortunately, we have managed to correct this rather quickly through dispatching a small fleet of interceptors to the problem locations. We need you, however, to take a shipment of holoreels to the station we designate, as our usual contact there is indisposed at the moment and may not be available for some time. When you deliver these to that station, our contact's second-in-command will take charge of the cargo and facilitate further broadcasting.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thank you so very much, {[character]player.name}. The Amarr representative has already informed us that he is offloading the holoreels as we speak. We will not forget this service to the Empire.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Our hearts are glad to know that you are en route to the station and will be docking there shortly. Please contact me on arrival.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I know the security screening process at this station has been time-consuming and a bit, well, intrusive. Now that you have passed our various tests, however, I feel confident that I can now let you in on the reason you are here.

One of our regional governors had recently been planning an unannounced visit to one of the new planetary command centers in a nearby system. For security reasons, this information was restricted to only those in the governor's inner circle, to include the commander of his personal security detail. Well, this commander decided to test his internal security prior to this event, to best ensure the governor's safe travel. So, for this exercise, he created a painstakingly detailed agenda, identical in every detail to an actual state visit. In this scenario, the governor was to travel by chartered high-speed maglev train to a number of the new planetary command centers.

As the Governor's decoy train traveled through a large canyon, however, a series of explosive charges detonated on the rail line, sending the train off its track and into the canyon wall. As it turned out, the security commander's ruse had worked perfectly; someone in the governor's inner circle had tipped his or her hand and provided information to unknown assassins.

So far, however, we have not been able to determine the traitor's identity, and each member of the inner circle is vehemently denying any involvement, despite our best chemical interrogations. So, what this investigation will likely boil down to is to what clues can be solved from the train wreckage, the destroyed maglev track sections, and the soil around the site of the blasts.

We need you to transport several investigative teams, along with a considerable amount of equipment, to a nearby station where they will then be transported via shuttle to the planet. Will you take on this mission?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: We are extremely disappointed in your decision to leave this mission. I am quite sure the Regional Governor's office will not soon forget this offense to the Empire.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: We are disappointed in your decision not to assist the Empire in its hour of need. However, we do have another pilot waiting in the next room, so you may leave. And I need not remind you of the consequences should you discuss any of what you have been told here today.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you for agreeing to aid the Empire in this matter. My assistant will provide you all the details you will need to deliver these personnel to the designated station.

messages.mission.briefing.text: During a high-level security assessment, a decoy maglev train designed to mimic the regional governor's chartered train was destroyed by unknown saboteurs while traveling at very high speed. Our investigation has yet to uncover the traitors; however, we are confident that a prompt scientific examination of the wreckage will provide the clues we need to resolve this internal security matter. We are sending a team of senior investigators to the wreck site so that they might help determine the identities of the attackers. We are counting on you to fly them to the designated station.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent work, pilot. The personnel you transported for us have already developed some interesting leads, and it seems – at least at this early juncture – that the assassins may be of Minmatar descent. Further testing, we expect, will confirm this. We will retain your contact information, should this incident require more of your courier skills.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Trust me, pilot, we are watching you, and we know you are on time and flying via the preprogrammed waypoints. Contact us only on your arrival.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
As you probably know all too well, speed is the lifeblood of the Republic's defense fleets, particularly for the smaller frigates and cruisers. There's a lot that goes into it: low-density reactor engines, kinesthetic maneuvering thrusters, hyper-responsive gyroscopic stabilizers. All the housings are built using nanofiber rather than the more heavyweight materials the other empires use; it was simply more conveniently available back when the ships were first designed, but it gives them that little bit of extra boost that's become our signature.

The lighter construction does have the drawback of making the systems more fragile. Our R&D specialists have been working on a more efficient design for the inertial compensators which keep the drive components from shaking themselves to bits; I want you to take this batch over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for application and field testing.

messages.root.agentsays.text: I haven't received confirmation of your delivery yet, {[character]player.name}. Is there a problem?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Disappointing, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I am most disappointed.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Smaller ships rely upon their speed and smaller signature radius to make it difficult for larger ships to track and target them. The heat output from propulsion systems increases signature radius, making a small target much easier to track; the greater the speed, the greater the heat production. Specialized coatings help to reduce the effect and prevent expansion of the parts within propulsion systems, helping them to operate much more efficiently.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text: {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}'s R&D branch has been working on more efficient version of the inertial compensator units used in starship propulsion systems. I need you to take the latest batch to the testing facility.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. The testers have already submitted a preliminary report. The results seem favorable towards our new design, and we've received permission to begin a small first-run production.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: Okay, take a look at this. You know what this is? Yes, yes, it's a rock. It's a rare mineral, actually, called Mesarchonite. It has industrial applications, but it's mostly used in security systems. The reason it's in a special containment field is that it's also fairly radioactive. Take this shipment over to the manufacturers at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and don't bloody open it!

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you delivered that Mesarchonite, {[character]player.name}? You don't want to expose your ship to it for much longer.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I am disappointed, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I am disappointed, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Security systems on stations are all-in-one, monitoring room occupancy, ambient temperature and humidity, and the gas mix from environmental control. It can be set to go on alert for various stimuli, and contains several redundant systems to ensure that an interrupt on one line does not prevent a problem being reported. Small pieces of radioactive material which are sensitive to various stimuli are an integral part of such systems.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. Do try to hurry, you don't want this stuff sitting around too long in your cargo hold.

messages.mission.briefing.text: This shipment of Mesarchonite needs to be taken to the manufacturer on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. The cargo is radioactive, and while the containment units are good enough for a short period, the mineral really requires an industrial containment in a stable and controlled environment.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good to hear, {[character]player.name}!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: One of our archaeological teams has unearthed a load of pre-Federation tech from a moon in this system. We're really excited about this; I don't think I need to explain to you how the results of this find could give us a leg up on the competition. Get this lot over to the labs at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and don't tell anyone!

messages.root.agentsays.text: {[character]player.name}, have you delivered those artifacts yet?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: This greatly displeases me, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Sad. I thought you'd have more interest than that.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Corporations often sponsor archaeological and research projects, paying for work permits and equipment when the people involved need them. In exchange, the corporations obtain exclusive rights to any discoveries which are made. This includes the right to display and charge viewing fees, or to make new developments based upon information obtained from the artifacts.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good to hear!

messages.mission.briefing.text: One of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}'s archaeological teams has uncovered a load of pre-Federation relics. I need you to transport the pieces to a laboratory for analysis.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thank you for your help, {[character]player.name}. The minerals that society was focusing on are pretty worthless to us -- it's just crystalline octenase, borealt and the like -- but it looks like they were used in the basic construction of the ship they used for the outpost. Who would have thought of coating low-density tritanium panels with a lassenium compound? With a little work, we can find out where their culture came from, and why they're not here anymore.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Oh! {[character]player.name}, perfect timing!

One of our research outposts in Molden Heath came under attack by rogue drones last week. This is highly unusual, since drones are rarely seen beyond Etherium Reach. The outpost's defense systems managed to keep our scientists safe, and the downed drones were retrieved for examination. They found unusual mineral deposits replacing the drones' original microboard networks, which appear to work far more efficiently.

Of course we don't want anyone else getting ahold of the samples before we can replicate them. The samples have been in transit via a series of drops in order to keep them safe. Take them on to the labs at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.

messages.root.agentsays.text: {[character]player.name}, have you done what I asked?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Sad, {[character]player.name}. I thought I could trust you for this.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Sad, {[character]player.name}. I thought I could trust you for this.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Rogue drones began innocently enough, as part of a Gallente scientist's research into drones that could learn and operate independently. The artificial intelligence he created was in itself fairly primitive and non-threatening, but in its self-perpetuation it developed beyond the scope of the scientist's work, and the drones began to truly think for themselves.
Using the justification that the results had produced extreme and life-threatening risk to human life, CONCORD declared all research into artificial intelligence illegal unless performed in a controlled and isolated environment under the watchful eye of DED experts. Proposals for engaging in such research are vetted carefully and the scientists presenting the proposals are subject to extreme background scrutiny.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! I can't wait to see what we've got.

messages.mission.briefing.text: While examining wrecked rogue drones following a failed attack, strange minerals were found which replaced some of the drones' usual systems. The compounds seem to run more efficiently than the parts they replaced, and your agent has hired you to take the find to researchers for examination.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent work, {[character]player.name}. We're one step closer to the forefront of technological advancement!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I'm in a bit of an awkward position here, {[character]player.name}. With all the people being released from slavery in the Empire, we're getting more and more families who practice the Amarr religion. No thanks to Jamyl, she knew this would happen. The edict from our government is that we need to respect the poor deluded people and gently introduce them to a new way of thinking. It won't be easy, and it's putting a strain on all of us.

My problem right now is that a bunch of the refugee families have requested that some Amarr Scriptures be included in the course structure at the schools we've set up for their children. It's our own people doing the teaching, so we can slowly steer the education in the right direction, but we all still feel dirty for having to use it.

Do you think you'd be willing to take a shipment of books over to one of the schools?

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you delivered those books, {[character]player.name}?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm very disappointed, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm very disappointed, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: With the release of several generations of slaves from the Empire, Jamyl struck a blow at the heart of Minmatar culture, forcing the Republic to accept those who have known only the ways of Amarr and what little Minmatar tradition they had been able to maintain through the years. Inducting such people into modern Republic society has proven troublesome and at times outright frustrating; allowing released slaves to practice the religion they grew up with has been a bitter necessity as counselors struggle to help the people adapt to their new lives.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. I knew I could count on you.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Against my better judgment, I've been asked to order several sets of educational packages of the Amarr Scriptures for the children of families who have been released by the Empire. It leaves a sour taste in the mouth, but maybe we can use the teaching materials to our own ends.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. I know it's an unsavory business, but our instructions from on high are to try to get along and help these people adjust.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
A severe accident has occurred on another station, {[character]player.name}; they suffered a freak blowout in primary life-support, and the station's environmental control shut down entirely. No, don't panic, they stabilized the atmosphere as soon as they could, so the people on the station won't asphyxiate. But the internal heating units have yet to be replaced. People are bundling up as their heat bleeds out – the external insulation is some protection, but it's not enough.

Fortunately for them, we've been developing some hyper-efficient portable heaters here. Donating a bunch will be good publicity for us. It'll also be a good field test for the heaters, and we may get a few preorders from it if people like them. Take these over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and make sure you let them know who donated them.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you delivered the heating units yet?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You're heartless, {[character]player.name}. What about all those people?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Well, I'm certain we can find someone who values their job more.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: The most vital systems on a space station or starship, life-support covers everything from atmosphere generation and recycling to environmental control to the recycling of drinking and pumping water. Originally a series of tanks containing specialized filters, as residence in space extended from long-term to lifetimes, advances in bioengineering developed hydroponics systems for stations which both produce and recycle air and water efficiently. Environmental control, which cycles water and air through the station and maintains an even internal temperature despite the cold of space outside nibbling at the edges, runs off the same generator as the internal electrical circuits. External electrical devices, such as guide-lights, shielding and containment fields, security systems and communications, run from separate generators with extensive backup arrays.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A nearby station has suffered a life-support failure. They got the atmospheric regulators working again, but the interior temperature is starting to drop. Get the heating units over there quickly, before the place gets too cold.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thanks, {[character]player.name}! The field-test was invaluable. Turns out the units couldn't handle consistent use for more than 16 hours, something we never tested for in the labs. The next version of the heaters will be much better!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: One of our subsidiaries has recently suffered a major setback, {[character]player.name}. A hurricane wiped out half their planetside crops and wrecked the equipment. Most of it was already falling apart, the storm just finished it off. Obviously, this is a big problem for them, and us, but it's still the early part of the first growing season. Deliver these parts to the assembly plant at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so we can replace the equipment before they lose too much from this harvest.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you delivered those parts yet, {[character]player.name}?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I am greatly disappointed, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I am greatly disappointed, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Despite the increasing popularity of fully-automated hydroponics farms, many planetary economies continue to rely on large-scale land-farming to provide jobs and food for local populations. On particularly fertile worlds even small start-up farms can be instantly successful, but in order to compete with larger farms in the market, these smaller farms frequently approach large corporations, offering to supply certain vital organic produce in exchange for controlling market shares.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text: One of our planetside subsidiaries has recently lost a lot of farming equipment to a storm. I need you to take these parts to the assembly plant so we can recoup our losses.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thank you for your help, {[character]player.name}. Our subsidiary has managed to save more than they first thought of the initial crops and they're good to go for the second growing season.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I hope I can trust you to be discreet, {[character]player.name}.

As part of a goodwill gesture to the Nefantar tribe, the Republic has offered allotments of planetary territory within our space on which to build embassies or summer homes or whatever else they need land for. I don't care what it is, I don't trust ‘em, but the government is determined to make sure we all get along.

Yesterday I got an alert from one of my colleagues; it seems one Nefantar house is in collusion with elements from the Empire. Obviously we can't just point fingers without evidence, but I'm in a perfect position to obtain that. The contractor they hired to design and build a house on their new property is a friend of mine. He's given us one shipment of interior facing materials to seed with nanite spyware. Take the load to the depot at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; I know I can trust you to keep quiet about the additions to the cargo.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you delivered your cargo for me, {[character]player.name}?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm beginning to question your loyalty, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I am disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
The day Drupar Maak struck down Arkon Ardishapur on Starkman Prime with the Heir's own sceptre began the darkest night for his people. In retribution for the death of his father and their attempted rebellion, Idonis Ardishapur ordered the annihilation of the Starkmanir tribe.

At the same time, the Nefantar tribe approached the Empire with an offer, making a bargain for mercy in exchange for assisting in the subjugation of the Minmatar. The tribe took on many aspects of the Empire, including open practise of their faith and owning Minmatar slaves, themselves. Despite the recent revelation that their conversion helped to protect the last Starkmanir to survive the purge, many within the Republic are hesitant to forgive the Nefantar for their actions.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. If anyone asks where those came from, the manifest will show their usual station.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A Nefantar House is relocating to a planet within the Republic, and we've had a tip-off that they're working against us for someone in the Empire. We've planted surveillance nanobots in a shipment of materials for their planetside home; take it over to the depot. The logs will show nothing amiss.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thanks to your assistance, {[character]player.name}, we've been able to record some rather incriminating communications from these people already. They wasted no time in contacting their associates in the Empire to let them know they were settled in.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes, I have some work for you.

We have several research outposts in various w-space systems. It's common, one of those things that nobody discusses but everybody knows about anyway. A while ago, they recovered bits of ancient technology which seemed to have unusual properties.. We thought for a while it might be some sort of Sleeper computer core, but now it appears to be Talocan in origin. Another of our laboratories has more pieces, and they're suggesting it's actually the core of a station's life-support system, with multiple redundant modules that can back each other up and be easily replaced if they fail. They're setting up to test their theory right now at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. I need you to take our samples over so they can complete the network they've pieced together.

messages.root.agentsays.text: I've not received a receipt for the cargo yet, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: This displeases me, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: If it's not worth your time, you could have just said so.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Capsuleers aren't the only people to explore the systems accessible via wormholes. Every corporation wants to be the first to make the Next Big Discovery, and then market the developments from researching it. Most corporations will categorically deny that this is what they're doing, creating an atmosphere of both paranoia and plausible deniability if their explorations turn up nothing of value.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. Hurry up! This could be our biggest breakthrough yet!

messages.mission.briefing.text: {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has a number of outposts in w-space systems, exploring what lies beyond known space. They've turned up some unusual pieces which I need you to take to a more extensive laboratory for identification.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: The strangest thing happened when they got all the pieces slotted together: the light inside them stopped flickering and turned blue. We're not certain what that means, since nothing else happened, but it appears to be a sign we're on the right track!

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Yes, yes, perhaps you could help me out.

A well-known politician is having a vacation suite commissioned in another station, and decided that he just could not live without an ornamental water-garden. One of our daughter-companies was hired for the work, and it could be just the break they need to make a name for themselves in the interior design industry.

Thing is, on stations, such gardens need to be self-supporting ecosystems in their own right. He had a load of very pretty frogs shipped in to add color and control the inevitable insect populations, but those lovely little Leina's Darters are also beautifully toxic, and the fish that eat them are dying. We've finally discovered a variety that won't prevent the fish from reproducing. Take this load over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and quickly, before His Honor decides he wants a rock garden instead and we lose our investment.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you delivered those frogs yet, {[character]player.name}?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: But what about the frogs?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I'm sorry to hear that, {[character]player.name}. I'll just have to find someone else.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Nothing boasts of a flexible wallet than a private garden within the walls of one's apartment. Society's elite will spend a great deal of money to obtain a perfect replica of the Intaki rainforests or Mannar seaside in which to entertain guests and impress prospective clients. Extra emphasis is placed on making such gardens self-supporting, including specially-engineered fauna to keep the flora happy.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A small startup that {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has recently invested in has been hired to build a water garden for a Gallente politician, but the frogs he wanted are too dangerous to the fish. Fortunately, there's a variety that are just as ornamental without the side effects. I need you to take them over before we lose our investment.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thanks to your work, it looks like Holistic Habitat, LLC is on its way up. The politician can't praise the quality of his water-garden enough.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Okay, here's one for you. Don't look at me like that. Yes, it's a load of metal scraps we need taken to a reclamation facility at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Contrary to popular belief, our ships are not made solely of scrap-metal, utility adhesive and chewing gum, but we do recycle extensively.

The reason I'm asking you to do this rather than hiring a much cheaper regular captain is that these bits are industrial quality, or they will be once they've been processed. They're worth a lot of cred on the black market – peanuts to you capsuleers, but a year's wages to anyone else.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you finished your work for me, {[character]player.name}?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Sad, {[character]player.name}. I had hoped you were the reliable sort.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I am very disappointed, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text:
Since its dawning days, New Eden's landscape has been riddled with conflict, both political and physical. Battles waged and lost have left scars upon planets and littered constellations with floating wrecks. Close to where the Eve Gate lies in Genesis, abandoned stations pose navigational threats to pilots, and many stars are developing orbital rings of human-made space junk.

Despite the risks inherent in a single scrap of metal the size of a man, hurtling through space at just below light-speed – never mind something as vast as a wrecked starship – governments either cannot afford or cannot be bothered to send teams to clean them up. The most dangerous pieces are towed out of the primary space-lanes, then left adrift in deadspace, marked with tracking-beacons. Scavenging is publicly discouraged, though authorities tend to turn a blind eye when various pieces end up on the market. Most of the finds end up in the hands of artists, inventors and archaeologists. One large piece of hull-plating found on the market, still bearing the much-corroded legend MAF Commandant Aurora, was identified as belonging to one of the earliest Gallente interplanetary shuttles, and now forms part of a wall in a museum on Gallente Prime.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. It's not a glamorous job but someone's gotta do it.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Our salvagers have built up a load of industrial-quality scrap metal to be used in ship building. I need you to take it to the reclamation facility so we can recover the useable parts.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Good! You've been a big help, {[character]player.name}.

localizedName.text: A Little Work On The Side

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I like nice things, {[character]player.name}. Who doesn't? Handing missions out to you people all day doesn't offer nearly enough to cover my expenses, so a friend and I run a shipping business out to Syndicate space. Nothing big enough to interfere with the Syndicate itself, mind you. We provide a humanitarian service importing the latest holos from the heart of civilization. It's the only way they can get the things for a reasonable cost – buying them direct from the companies in the Federation incurs immense shipping charges.

Our usual courier is out of commission today, with her ship in for repairs after a pirate attack. If you want to make yourself useful, take the latest shipment over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and ask for Amelyn. They'll know who you mean, just say that “Imba” sent you.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Amelyn hasn't contacted me yet, {[character]player.name}. What's the hold up?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: What? Why now? Couldn't you just have refused at the start? Now we'll have to move our operation elsewhere.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Fine. It's not like anyone would believe you if you told them, anyway.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Founded by Intaki exiles after the first Caldari-Gallente war, Syndicate rapidly became a safe haven for criminals and the more unsavoury sorts of businesses which can't operate as freely in Empire space. Anything and everything can be found on the market, including things people would rather not be shared openly. Secrets – both personal and professional – fetch a good price, and the sellers rarely care who the money comes from.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good, good. Get going, would you?

messages.mission.briefing.text: A friend and I are running a small holoreel bootlegging operation on the side. The shipments are bound for Syndicate, but I only need you to take them on to where my business partner is operating from. The cargo has been disguised as standard holoreels, an effective disguise provided nobody looks too closely at the contents.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thanks for your help, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Do you read the gossip rags? I wouldn't expect you to; you capsuleers obviously have greater concerns than who's mocking whom this week. The big news right now is this wedding being planned by Ahvir en Foilien, the former co-star of Under Wraps. He's not been heard from since he got canned as the host of the Sugar Sweep game show, but now he's caused a ruckus by arranging a marriage to the daughter of Material Acquisition bigwig Hemy Selvah. A lot of money obviously changed hands to manage this, since Selvah's daughter isn't quite ten years old, and en Foilien already has a wife, a husband and a few playmates on the side.

If you believe what the tabloids say, that is. Who knows what the truth might be?

En Foilien has arranged a lavish party on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} which is undoubtedly meant to encourage the public and the reporters to overlook the dodgy circumstances and remind them that he used to be important. It doesn't really matter. He's ordered several crates of Feille d'Marnne champagne to loosen them up and assist with the memory loss.

messages.root.agentsays.text: I haven't received a receipt for that champagne yet. What's the hold up?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm not laughing, {[character]player.name}. I have a reputation to maintain, you know.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Fine, I'll find someone else, hopefully before it's too late.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Nobody loves a good party more than the Gallente. The hedonistic stereotype is one that the Federation revels in and flaunts shamelessly. Public figures actively compete to host the wildest and most fashionable affairs, vying for the attention of news services and gossip magazines. Among the celebrity elite, a wedding, birth or even a funeral is simply another excuse to splash out and stand in the limelight. Occasionally, an event will be engineered so a falling star can make a desperate final grasp at publicity and salvage a faded career.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thanks, {[character]player.name}, I knew we could count on you.

messages.mission.briefing.text: A pair of civilians too wealthy for their own good are holding a decadent reception for their wedding, and ordered a tremendously expensive champagne to keep their guests entertained. A regular pilot can't be trusted to ship the drinks in, but what's a thousand-ISK bottle of wine to a capsuleer?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. That party isn't one the glitterati will soon forget; Selvah's daughter threw her entire glass of champagne in en Foilien's face and called him some very unflattering schoolyard names. Of course it was all caught on camera, and the media is having a field day.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text: One of my clients asked me to send over drones to replace the ones his company's been losing in the line of work. That's all he said. He never said anything about needing mining drones; of course I sent him a set of scout drones, and he was very upset at me for not being able to read his mind. People should be more specific about things. Take these mining drones over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for him, and if he asks why the paint looks new, tell him they're fresh off the production line.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Have you finished your work for me, {[character]player.name}?
