messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Are the Marines behaving themselves? Good. Please continue to make all possible haste in delivering them to the station. They tend to get a bit rowdy when they are cooped up too long.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I know the security screening process at this station has been time-consuming and a bit, well, intrusive. Now that you have passed our various tests, however, I feel confident that I can now let you in on the reason you are here.

One of our regional governors had recently been planning an unannounced visit to one of the new planetary command centers in a nearby system. For security reasons, this information was restricted to only those in the governor's inner circle, to include the commander of his personal security detail. Well, this commander decided to test his internal security prior to this event, to best ensure the governor's safe travel. So, for this exercise, he created a painstakingly detailed agenda, identical in every detail to an actual state visit. In this scenario, the governor was to travel by chartered high-speed maglev train to a number of the new planetary command centers.

As the Governor's decoy train traveled through a large canyon, however, a series of explosive charges detonated on the rail line, sending the train off its track and into the canyon wall. As it turned out, the security commander's ruse had worked perfectly; someone in the governor's inner circle had tipped his or her hand and provided information to unknown assassins.

So far, however, we have not been able to determine the traitor's identity, and each member of the inner circle is vehemently denying any involvement, despite our best chemical interrogations. So, what this investigation will likely boil down to is to what clues can be solved from the train wreckage, the destroyed maglev track sections, and the soil around the site of the blasts.

We need you to transport several investigative teams, along with a considerable amount of equipment, to a nearby station where they will then be transported via shuttle to the planet. Will you take on this mission?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: We are extremely disappointed in your decision to leave this mission. I am quite sure the Regional Governor's office will not soon forget this offense to the Empire.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: We are disappointed in your decision not to assist the Empire in its hour of need. However, we do have another pilot waiting in the next room, so you may leave. And I need not remind you of the consequences should you discuss any of what you have been told here today.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you for agreeing to aid the Empire in this matter. My assistant will provide you all the details you will need to deliver these personnel to the designated station.

messages.mission.briefing.text: During a high-level security assessment, a decoy maglev train designed to mimic the regional governor's chartered train was destroyed by unknown saboteurs while traveling at very high speed. Our investigation has yet to uncover the traitors; however, we are confident that a prompt scientific examination of the wreckage will provide the clues we need to resolve this internal security matter. We are sending a team of senior investigators to the wreck site so that they might help determine the identities of the attackers. We are counting on you to fly them to the designated station.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent work, pilot. The personnel you transported for us have already developed some interesting leads, and it seems – at least at this early juncture – that the assassins may be of Minmatar descent. Further testing, we expect, will confirm this. We will retain your contact information, should this incident require more of your courier skills.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Trust me, pilot, we are watching you, and we know you are on time and flying via the preprogrammed waypoints. Contact us only on your arrival.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
{[character]player.name}! Glad you could make it on such short notice. Let me get right to the point: Yesterday, as you almost certainly know, a regional governor delivered her State of the Region address. Needless to say, we were quite excited and thus put forth a maximum effort to ensure that her speech was broadcast on every possible channel and to the maximum ranges of our civilian and military communications networks.

However, for various reasons at many remote locations, this signal did not reach many who would have otherwise benefitted from this opportunity. For all our efforts, there are some locations that can only be reached the hard way -- ferrying holoreels directly to each and every one of them. We have already dispatched messengers, primarily in interceptors and other fast ships, to these more dangerous destinations.

We need you to transport a quantity of holoreels containing the State of the Region speech to one station in particular and hand them over to an agent who will be waiting for them there. He will then handle all further distribution of the 'reels.

So, can you help us with what should be a straightforward courier job?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Well, I was not expecting this. All we needed was for you to make a simple run from this station to the designated station and drop off our cargo. Well, suffice to say, you will not be receiving any prayers of blessing from me tonight!

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I must say we are quite disappointed. As you know, all of our pilots are gone, taking these 'reels to the faithful. Your refusal leaves a gap in this coverage that will leave many faithful Amarr without this important message from the governor.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you a million times over, pilot, for taking on this mission. The hearts and minds of the Amarr faithful in that station and elsewhere will benefit immeasurably from your prompt delivery of these hallowed holoreels.

messages.mission.briefing.text: The regional governor herself delivered an important State of the Region speech yesterday to all her billions of faithful followers. Due to technical problems, however, this message did not reach as many citizens as it should have. Fortunately, we have managed to correct this rather quickly through dispatching a small fleet of interceptors to the problem locations. We need you, however, to take a shipment of holoreels to the station we designate, as our usual contact there is indisposed at the moment and may not be available for some time. When you deliver these to that station, our contact's second-in-command will take charge of the cargo and facilitate further broadcasting.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thank you so very much, {[character]player.name}. The Amarr representative has already informed us that he is offloading the holoreels as we speak. We will not forget this service to the Empire.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Our hearts are glad to know that you are en route to the station and will be docking there shortly. Please contact me on arrival.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
A short time ago, Minmatar terrorists in a combined fleet of frigates and cruisers attacked one of our Harbinger-class battlecruisers as it was transporting slaves from a recently closed mine to a new mineral harvesting facility in a nearby system. While all but one of the attackers was annihilated, our convoy's escorts were destroyed and our cruiser is burning. Making a bad situation worse, we are anticipating that the terrorists will return in force within the next several hours to attempt the theft of our slaves, as they almost certainly know the cruiser is alone and all but helpless.

Our concern is that if the terrorists feel that they have a window of opportunity to recover these slaves, it is likely that they will throw everything they have into the effort. Our intelligence assessments of the terrorists' fleet assets are even less reassuring: we believe that they could send as many as four battlecruisers into this fight – more than enough to wipe out the arriving frigates and forcefully board our heavily damaged strategic cruiser. However, we have calculated that if we can delay any terrorist boarding parties long enough, this should give us enough time for the much larger main rescue fleet to arrive.

The only bright side to this situation, in what is unquestionably an act of divine providence, is that a large contingent of marines are aboard this station as we speak, having just completed specialized refresher training in counter-boarding operations. We need you to deliver them to the station closest to the last reported position of our cruiser. From there, we will transport a combined team of marines, engineers, medics, and other essential personnel to hopefully stop the fire and save the ship - along with its cargo of highly valuable slaves. However, this mission must be undertaken immediately. Any delay will surely doom the Harbinger and her brave crew.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Quitting? Now?  You have placed our marines and hundreds of other personnel in grave danger by abandoning them mid-mission. We will have to find some way to get them to our damaged strategic cruiser, though I feel it is now too late.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: We will not forget this – the moment you chose to abandon our people in a time of great need. Your assistance could have turned the tide of this whole disaster. Do not contact me again.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Our deepest thanks for taking on this mission. I can tell you that our best analysts feel that you should be fairly safe in this mission, as the terrorist will have to focus all their efforts on targeting the stricken cruiser. They simply won't have the ships or the time to even attempt to interdict your ship as you make your way to the destination station.

messages.mission.briefing.text: While transporting Minmatar slaves from a recently close ore mine to a new mineral harvesting facility in nearby system, the convoy was attacked by terrorists, destroying the escort frigates and heavily damaging the Harbinger-class strategic cruiser carrying the slaves. We believe it is likely that the terrorists will return, and in larger ships, to attempt a rescue of the slaves before we can respond with reinforcements. The window of opportunity for the terrorists is short, so it is imperative that we immediately render as much help as possible. What we need you to do is deliver a contingent of heavily armed marines recently trained in counter-boarding operations to a station closer to the site of the battle. From there, they will join other Amarr military and rescue teams for immediate transportation to the damaged cruiser.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: We've received confirmation that you did indeed fulfill your promise and deliver the Marines to the station. As we speak, the combined rescue team is loading into other ship for immediate transport to the Harbinger. Hopefully, we will reach them in time.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Excellent news, pilot, thank you for updating us as to your position and condition. Please make all possible speed to the destination so that we can then dispatch the combined rescue team package.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You are aware, no doubt, of the rumors of extremist antislavery terrorist groups within the Amarr Empire itself. Well, you know then that their loyalty to the Empire is indeed secondary to their overarching desire to see all slaves freed and made equal members of society. This is a condition that we, as the greatest state in all of New Eden, simply cannot tolerate. However, our efforts at arresting and reeducating those insurgents have largely failed to permanently change the mindsets of these rather fanatical individuals.

This system has been particularly hard hit by this and other like-minded groups. Most recently, an Anathema-class covert ops ship, specially configured to transport elite slaves to the estates of senior Amarr leaders in the region, was somehow decloaked, its weapons and sensors jammed, and ruthlessly attacked to the point of near-total structure failure. The terrorists then demanded the pilot transfer the slaves to this mystery ship, on threat of the total destruction of the covert ops vessel. The pilot complied, though he has since been punished for his cowardice.

It is for this reason that I called you here today. I need you to transport a new shipment of elite slaves to a nearby station for further transshipment to the residence of one of the regional governors. This shipment is of particular urgency as the governor is hosting his annual gala event at his estate, and the usual staff of slaves simply will not do. We need these specific slaves, as they have been trained in protocol, proper food and drink service, entertainment, and numerous other talents that I need not mention here.

Will you take on this courier mission on behalf of the Empire and deliver these highly trained and extremely expensive slaves to the designated station?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You must be kidding?!? I have already guaranteed the governor's office that you are en route and will arrive at the scheduled time. This act on your part is probably going to get me reassigned to some asteroid in an uncharted system a million light years from here. Well, I will make sure I'm not the only one who will feel the heat for this failure.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: While I must say I am rather shocked at your refusal to undertake this mission, we are fortunate in that we do have contingency plans in place. So, while we will have to risk the crew and slaves in another run, I feel confident that only you will bear the negative feedback for failing us here today.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: While it might seem impossible at first glance, there are indeed small bands of terrorists who seek to upset the very core foundation of our society by working to eliminate slavery throughout the Empire. We have had significant success in disrupting these groups, with many members killed or taken prisoner. Nonetheless, like a hydra they continue to grow and adapt to our tactics and operations, making them a quite annoying thorn in our side. The Amarr Empire is devoting increasing resources to the eradication of these groups; however, even the most optimistic analysts concede that it may be quite some time before this nascent insurgency can be eradicated.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: That is very good news, pilot. I will contact the governor's aide myself to let her know that you have accepted and will be departing shortly.

messages.mission.briefing.text: We have recently been experiencing an increase in terrorist attacks by groups seeking to free Amarr slaves in this region. Their raids have become more complex and lethal, resulting in the loss of untold millions of ISK worth of valuable property. More importantly, one of the regional governors is having his annual gala event at his estate on a nearby planet. We need you to deliver a cargo of elite conditioned slaves to a station we will designate. From there they will be transported to the governor's estate by heavily armed ships.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great job, {[character]player.name}. The slaves are being offloaded now and will be en route to the governor's estate shortly. I can't thank you enough for your reliability and promptness.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Thank you for the update pilot, it is rather reassuring that you are flying without any interference from our unwanted friends. Please contact me again when you are being towed in to the dock, as only then will I feel assured that this courier mission was a success.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I'm not going to beat around the bush with you on this one, as there isn't any time. We have a developing emergency in {[location]objectiveLocationSystemID.name}. Several of our commercial convoys have been ripped to shreds in the last few months by an extremely dangerous band of terrorists. As you can see from these camera drone recordings, they have even been willing to fly their ships directly into our freighters and other unarmed haulers. And yes, before you ask, we have been escorting these convoys with heavily armed security vessels, though to little effect.

As these terrorists are obviously willing to die for their cause, they aren't bothering to attack our warships. They simply seem to appear out of nowhere, accelerate to high speeds and slam into the cargo ships. Depending on the cargo, this action can, at best, tear open the cargo bays and release the contents into the vacuum of space, or, at worst, strike a shipment of fuels or ammunition, and destroy the freighter in one huge explosion. One such explosion destroyed an entire convoy.

However, an ultra-secure communications intercept satellite recently picked up a communication that we believe indicates the terrorists are now considering turning their deadly tactic against some unidentified stations in the region. Given our huge civilian population on these stations, the decision has been made to conduct a partial evacuation of all potential target stations.

What we need from you is your help in getting these civilians – mostly the spouses and children of station personnel – to a station that is further away from the terrorists' known area of operation. Normally, I would not ask this of a capsuleer, but I am begging you: will you help us evacuate these people until this threat has passed? We need to know right now, as we have already begun to organize the evacuation fleet; can we count you in?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You are quitting on us now? In the middle of an evacuation? Fine. Just deliver those men, women, and children to the nearest safe location, and we will send someone to get them. You are a despicable coward and you'd better hope you never need to transit through this system ever again.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: I cannot believe what I'm hearing – you are refusing to help save these people? Well, I don't know where we are going to find another ship at this late hour.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: We have virtually no information on these new threats, other than that they have access to very fast ships filled to the brim with high explosives. Their tactics are simple – they seem to appear out of nowhere, then accelerate their ships to maximum velocity and, ignoring defensive fire, fly directly into the cargo bays of our freighters and other haulers. We are currently working with Caldari Naval Intelligence to determine the source of this scourge; however, early indications from their ship markings are that they belong to an extremists environmental cult that views the Caldari State as the ultimate evil in the universe. They will stop at nothing to destroy us, especially as we expand planetary industry and resource harvesting.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you. That is a big load off my shoulders. We need all the good pilots we can get to help us get these people to safety before the terrorists attempt any suicide attack against this station.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Suicide terrorists have been attacking and destroying our commercial convoys as they have passed through their usual transit zones, despite the presence of heavy security escort vessels. A communications intercept, partially decoded, indicates that these individual intend to step up the level of their attacks by targeting the stations themselves. While we can defend against some of these attackers, based on analysis of their previous attack profiles, we have never had to defend against pilots and ships who fully intend to die by throwing themselves against us without regard for their own lives. Tactical analysis indicates that they will get through our defense and may cause catastrophic damage, likely killing hundreds if not thousands of our civilian workforce and their families. We need you to help us evacuate them immediately!

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: I will never be able to thank you for helping us in our most dire hour. The Caldari Navy should be arriving soon to provide additional security, but that's no guarantee that the terrorists won't follow through with their insidious plans. I will be sure to pass the word throughout the comms networks of the great service you did for all of us today.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Thank you for the update. I am glad to hear the passengers are doing well. I can't tell you how much it means to us that you are willing to divert from more profitable ventures to save these innocent lives.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I'm supposed to transport these reports to the Caldari Navy station in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, but I really have a tight schedule at the moment. The contents of the reports are confidential, something about the new recruits we've been getting. Apparently the Navy has been on the lookout for some pilots to hire for various jobs, and they want some background info. That's why I couldn't just send this information via a transmission: Caldari law prohibits doing that with personal information since such transmissions can be hacked.

If you do the job for me, I'll give you a nice reward. And even a bonus if you get it done quickly.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I'm supposed to transport these reports to the Caldari Navy station in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, but I really have a tight schedule at the moment. The contents of the reports are confidential, something about the new recruits we've been getting. Apparently the Navy has been on the lookout for some pilots to hire for various jobs, and they want some background info. That's why I couldn't just send this information via a transmission: Caldari law prohibits doing that with personal information since such transmissions can be hacked.

If you do the job for me, I'll give you a nice reward. And even a bonus if you get it done quickly!

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great! Your achievements for us have not gone unnoticed.

messages.mission.briefing.text: We are escalating our production so we can increase our military strength in light of recent political upheavals in the world. Increased production requires more minerals. I want you to get {[item]objectiveTypeID.quantityName, quantity=objectiveQuantity} to one of our main production facilities. Your help will undoubtedly get a positive response from other corporate members.

Hello, {[character]player.name}. At the moment, all you have to fly is a capsule. Our first priority is to get you into a starship.

Your assignment: Follow the tutorial steps, I will guide you to a hidden location in space.

If you ever get lost, remember to use the back and next buttons and read the tutorial slides or you can quit the mission and start over again from the beginning.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Mission 1 in progress.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You want to restart the mission, {[character]player.name}? I understand. Just open a conversation again whenever you are ready.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You want to restart the mission, {[character]player.name}? I understand. Just open a conversation again whenever you are ready.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Mission 1 completed.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good luck, {[character]player.name}.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
At the moment, all you have to fly is a capsule. Our first priority is to get you into a starship.

Your assignment: Follow the tutorial steps, I will guide you to a hidden location in space.

If you ever get lost, remember to use the back and next buttons and read the tutorial slides or you can quit the mission and start over again from the beginning.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Excellent work, {[character]player.name}.

For completing the mission, you have received a reward. Note that for some missions this reward will be an item that the agent will drop in your hangar, while in others it will be a transfer to your wallet of Interstellar Kredits (ISK), the currency used by pod pilots.

Your next mission will involve combat, so you should learn to fit your new starship now. When you're ready for that, click the Request Mission button.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Your ship and the item I've asked you to retrieve are located at a site in this system.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You're doing well so far, {[character]player.name}. Your next test will involve some basic combat training.

When you are ready, you'll be provided with some modules to fit to your starship. Make sure to keep following the tutorial, I will explain how to fit the modules. Once you are fitted, you will fly out to a location in space to begin your combat training.

Once again, you will be provided with tutorials to guide you along the way.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Mission 2 in progress.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You want to restart the mission, {[character]player.name}? I understand. Just open a conversation again whenever you are ready.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You want to restart the mission, {[character]player.name}? I understand. Just open a conversation again whenever you are ready.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Mission 2 completed.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Good. Now you must learn how to fit modules to your ship.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You're doing well so far, {[character]player.name}. Your next test will involve some basic combat training.

When you are ready, you'll be provided with some modules to fit to your starship. Make sure to keep following the tutorial, I will explain how to fit the modules. Once you are fitted, you will fly out to a location in space to begin your combat training.

Once again, you will be provided with tutorials to guide you along the way.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
You've done well, {[character]player.name}.

You're almost ready to begin your career as a capsuleer but there is one last task. You must retrieve your Pilot Certification from one of our local academies. Request the next mission when you are ready.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text: Pirates are a blight on New Eden. Make sure you kill every last one, or they will scatter and regather somewhere else.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You've been learning quickly, {[character]player.name}. You're ready to start setting your own goals soon, but before you head out on your own you should stop off at a local academy of ours.

Follow the tutorial steps to guide you to a neighboring system where you will receive your certification documents proving you completed this course.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Mission 3 in progress.

messages.root.agentsays.text: Take your time at the academy, {[character]player.name}. There is a lot to see out there.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You want to restart the mission, {[character]player.name}? I understand. Just open a conversation again whenever you are ready.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You want to restart the mission, {[character]player.name}? I understand. Just open a conversation again whenever you are ready.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Mission 3 completed.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: You're ready to depart? Excellent.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
You've been learning quickly, {[character]player.name}. You're ready to start setting your own goals soon, but before you head out on your own you should stop off at a local academy of ours.

Follow the tutorial steps to guide you to a neighboring system where you will receive your certification documents proving you completed this course.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Congratulations, {[character]player.name}, you have graduated from the pilot's certification course. I'll be providing you with some basic information now on where to go. Request a new mission whenever you're ready.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
I was talking to some blowhard in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} when his station was destroyed. So, I'm thinking raiders, right? But no, it's even better. I send a few probes out that way, 'cause I want to know who to send the thank you card to. Turns out there were no raiders. Turns out that the whole damn station was hit by an asteroid full of Augumene! Luckily, I know a guy who's willing to pay decent kreds for the stuff, even though it's pretty much worthless! Heh!

It's like some angry, ironic god came down and crushed that jerk with a giant wad of kred notes, all for me! I want you to go out there, and bring me back all of that Augumene.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
I'm on the comm, talking to this blowhard I knew back from my days at the academy, right...? So he's going on and on about how his corporation in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} is going to make ISK hand over fist mining some rare ore, blah blah blah. Then all these alarms start going off on his end. And I'm thinking his stupid corp is getting raided or something. Then, all of a sudden, the wall behind him disappears and he's ripped away from the screen! The blowhard got spaced right in front of my eyes!

Now, here's the best part. I send a few probes out that way, 'cause I want to know who to send the thank you card to. Turns out there were no raiders. Turns out that the whole damn station was hit by an asteroid full of Augumene! Luckily, I know a guy who's willing to pay decent kreds for the stuff, even though it's pretty much worthless! Heh! It's like some angry, ironic god came down and crushed that jerk with a giant wad of kred notes, all for me!

So, anyway, I want you to go out there and bring me back all of that Augumene. Do that, and I'll have a nice reward here for you when your come back, alright?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's the Augumene. Where's my ISK?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Don't tell me you're scared of a little rock?

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: What? You don't like free ISK?

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: You're a little twisted. And I'm okay with that. Yeah, I'll get you your Augumene.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes very expensive safety precautions. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: You seem entirely too happy with all this. And that troubles me. I'm going to decline, I'm afraid.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: This is more than a little weird. I'm not mining this Augumene anymore.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Excellent. Go get me some of that magnificent ore.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You seem happy. What is it?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Great. You took just long enough for some other vultures to get all the Augumene. That rock was meant for me, but no, you had to prance around until it was too late. Thanks for nothing.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Ah, it even feels like providence. And cold, hard kredits. Speaking of which, here's yours.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I don't have time to wait for you to decide whether you like ISK or not. I'll get someone else to mine my lucky rock. So you can just get lost, okay?

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Seems like every government around wants some of this Mercium stuff. I don't know why, but if they all want it, then it might be worth a bundle to me down the road if I can get it first. I mean, no one's willing to pay for it now, but I'm thinking ahead: All four sides bidding, you got any idea how high that might drive the auction prices?

Now, I happen to have the location of some of this stuff. Thing is, I don't have a ship to handle it, so I need you, and I'm willing to put some money up front against this future "investment." Get in, get me that ore, and get out before somebody else pops in there for it. Simple.

Be aware that this amount of raw Mercium ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
This thing: Seems like every government around wants some of this Mercium stuff. I don't know why, but if they all want it, then it might be worth a bundle to me down the road if I can get it first. I mean, no one's willing to pay for it now, but I'm thinking ahead: All four sides bidding, you got any idea how high that might drive the auction prices?

Now, I happen to have the location of some of this stuff. Thing is, I don't have a ship to handle it, so I need you, and I'm willing to put some money up front against this future "investment." Alright? You gotta get in, get me that ore, and get out before somebody else pops in there for it. Simple.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: Here's your Mercium. So, where's my cut?

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Don't worry, I'll find someone who's willing to make some decent ISK.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Not everybody's got what it takes. I knew that when I first looked at you.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Sounds like a good deal. I'm in.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Though Mercium is not commercially viable at present, it remains of scientific interest (and thus potentially of future financial interest) to agents of virtually all factions.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm not interested in getting caught in a four-way crossfire just to mine some rocks that might be worth something to someone at some point.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: Selling to all four of the big empires? Uh... even I don't want to piss off that many people. Nah, I quit.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Remember, move fast. Time's of the essence, huh?

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: What "thing" might that be?

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: Somebody else already beat you to that Mercium, bonehead. Way to go.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Here you go. Oh, this is gonna be just like hacking into that SCC station computer and making ISK for myself!

Uh, I mean, not that I've ever done that....

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I don't have this kinda time, {[character]player.name}. I gotta move on this Mercium before it's gone.

messages.mission.timeout.emailbody.text: I need this done yesterday. I found someone else who can do the job faster.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Look, I need some… ah, building materials, but I've got a client who's a bit particular. He wants it special, from some asteroids that already destroyed a shuttle of his, I guess. He gave me a location; you just go there, mine all 18,000 units of the Banidine that's there, and bring it back. Now, you won't find this stuff anywhere else, so don't go looking to bring me back something similar and easier to come across — you try and rip me off on this, and I'll know. Got it? Alright.

So, you game?

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've got your Banidine right here, pal.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Thanks a bundle. I didn't pay ya to think. That's my job. Remember that next time.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Yeah, I'm game.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Most people don't go looking for Banidine: It's virtually worthless, so you won't find it on the market. If you're having trouble finding the Banidine at the mission location, you can right-click the "Banidine" icon in the mission details in your Opportunities interface  and select "Add to Overview."

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I don't work for crazy people.

messages.mission.quit.charsays.text: I'm done with this weird stuff. Banidine? It's worthless! So I get to wondering… who the hell wants this stuff, and for what? And I decide, maybe I ought not to do this, huh?

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Get it quick. I don't like waiting.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You have anything for me?

messages.mission.briefing.text: Mine 18,000 units of Banidine at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and bring it to {[character]agentID.name}.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Nice job. I'll remember this.

messages.mission.offerexpired.email.body.text: I got no time for games. I'll find somebody who can get it done.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's attracting all sorts of drones to it. I don't know why. It's like insects to a flame or somethin'. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just take their place. It's annoying as hell.

I figure the best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. Simple. If you can harvest that cloud out, I'll pay you well.

You gotta own and be able to use a Gas Cloud Harvester to do this mission. If you don't or ya can't, just say "no thanks." You can decline one mission about every 4 hours without pissing me off, so no worries.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: I've harvested the gas cloud. Hopefully the drones won't be so interested in the area now.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Damn. I'll have to find someone else. Hey, thanks for being honest, though.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: Consider the cloud harvested.

messages.mission.extrainfo.body.text: Rogue drones and "wild drones" are the terms used for advanced drones that have mutated out of control. A few years ago, some ingenious Gallentean inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own in every sense like a regular space ship, except for being computer controlled, hence unmanned. The drones became unruly, then unmanageable. Needless to say, this research was soon abandoned by the Gallenteans.

messages.mission.decline.charsays.text: I'm afraid I can't do this. So... "no thanks."

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Thank you. You wouldn't believe how difficult it is to find a good gas harvester around here.

messages.mission.ask.charsays.text: You know me, ready for anything.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's attracting all sorts of drones to it. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just take their place. I figure the best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. Simple. If you can harvest that cloud out, I'll pay you well.

You gotta fit a Gas Cloud Harvester to do this mission. And you also gotta deal with any drones there. Fair enough?

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Great. We'll keep an eye on the area, but I think you've fixed our drone problem.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You've completed your basic training, {[character]player.name}. Now you're ready for something more involving.

There are a number of career training agents not far from here who can teach you about all the various activities and careers available to you. They'll let you get hands-on training and experience with everything from asteroid mining to deep space exploration.

When you're ready, I will refer you to them. You should take everything else with you as well, since you probably won't be coming back here afterward.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Mission 4 in progress.

messages.root.agentsays.text: The career advisor agents will be able to help you choose what skills to train, and how to specialize as a capsule pilot.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: You want to restart the mission, {[character]player.name}? I understand. Just open a conversation again whenever you are ready.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You want to restart the mission, {[character]player.name}? I understand. Just open a conversation again whenever you are ready.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Mission 4 completed.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text:
Excellent. These are the coordinates of the nearest training center, and here are your clearance papers. Take them with you to the station.

Good luck, {[character]player.name}, and remember: I'm never far if you need help.

Hello, {[character]player.name}. At the moment, all you have to fly is a capsule. Our first priority is to get you into a starship.

Your assignment: Follow the tutorial steps, I will guide you to a hidden location in space.

If you ever get lost, remember to use the back and next buttons and read the tutorial slides or you can quit the mission and start over again from the beginning.

For completing the mission, you have received a reward. Note that for some missions this reward will be an item that the agent will drop in your hangar, while in others it will be a transfer to your wallet of Interstellar Kredits (ISK), the currency used by pod pilots.

Once again, you will be provided with tutorials to guide you along the way.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You capsuleers spend so much time in the midst of mayhem and destruction, and you leave countless wreckages in your wake. Now, though, you and I have an opportunity to help sustain new life. I want you to transport some large crates of frozen plant seeds for me.

It will not surprise you that we are always trying to establish new colonies in even the most desolate parts of space. Colonization is always an exciting opportunity, not only for the settlers who dare venture out into space and stake their fortunes on some desolate rock, but for local entrepreneurs, businesses and politicians to support them. You won't hear of these, because your kind is so far up above piddly little local events, but it's a big deal for those involved.

Unfortunately, local support can't last forever. After the initial interest has waned, the citizens on those colonies have to fend for themselves. Sometimes they manage to create self-sustaining habitats where no outside intervention is needed. Occasionally they get lucky, and the outcome of their scientific experiments, ore search, or whatever else they were up to, makes them enough money that they can buy whatever they need off local orbitals.

All too often, though, we have to step in. Your cargo, once delivered to their colony, will hopefully enable them to bootstrap themselves to a self-sustaining life cycle. Colony life is hard enough as it is.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I am greatly disappointed. Their food stores were already running low.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Really? Ah well, back to destruction it is.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Take care to keep those seeds frozen at all times.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Colonists eking out a living on godforsaken rocks in space are finding it hard to maintain food production, so we're giving them a boost. The moment you've brought those crates of frozen plant seeds over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, our caravans will pick them up and haul them to those thankful pioneers.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent. Caravans will take the seeds to the colony. You have earned back some of your karma, capsuleer.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Most often we leave the shipment of entertainment material to the more slow-moving vessels in our employ. Every so often, though, we receive sufficient premium orders from other stations and the planets in their vicinity that we dispatch a special courier with the payload.

That courier is you, and the payload is huge stacks of holoreels, most of them ordered on some manner of timed interstellar delivery offer.

This isn't the primary business of our own corporation as such, but we have enough ties to the producers of all this material - as would any corporation large enough to have gone interstellar - that it's incumbent on us to find ways of delivering it to the customers.

Believe me, I wish we could just transfer all of this digitally, but for most of this cargo that is simply not an option. Some of these holoreels are under trade restrictions that prevent them from being beamed over and saved or stamped on the spot; others are special collectors' editions that may include anything from specially signed copies to boxed sets weighed down with any number of collectable objects.

Please ensure your crew doesn't open any of the crates, either. These people are collectors and paid a galactic premium for their items. If they so much as smell another human being's presence on the merchandise, they will resort either to lawsuits or assassinations.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: The customers will not be happy with this.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Very well. They'll just have to watch empty screens for a little longer.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Don't open any of those sealed special editions, you hear?

messages.mission.briefing.text: Some entertainment-hungry collectors out there are waiting for a lot of specially ordered holoreels that were manufactured, stamped, signed and compiled in special editions elsewhere in the cluster. I need you to bring these large holoreel crates to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} before they risk starting something silly like reading books.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Excellent. Your crew left the holoreels untouched, I trust.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
In all honesty, I find it just unbelievable that in this day and age we are expending actual capsuleer man-hours, not to mention the time and effort of your crew, and asking actual spaceships to travel interstellar distances only to shift around a cargohold of something as pitiable as actual garbage. Garbage. Especially the type we've got here, which takes up a bunch of room, has to be stored in nonporous containers, and, frankly, is starting to smell.

Nonetheless, here we are. We could have this cargo sent down planetside and destroyed, except that while those people are perfectly happy to toss up any number of shipments with whatever trinkets the station clientele is demanding that week, they have frothing conniptions if we so much as suggest that we might want to send anything like this back down in return. The merest whisper of it is enough for them to drag out the lawyers. It's not as if they don't have the space.

You aren't too big to help out, I trust. All we need you to do is haul this smelly, half-liquidized garbage to another station, where they'll have ways to get rid of it without endless complaints or moral qualms. I swear, if the PR department would just let us stop accepting all these colony refugees, we wouldn't have this problem.

Actually, forget I said that last part.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I am disappointed. I hope you didn't root around in the cargo.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Look, it was just normal, everyday garbage. There was no reason for you not to take this on.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: If your crew tells you that anything was moving in the garbage, don't believe them.

messages.mission.briefing.text: We have come into possession of large amounts of garbage, and since we can't legally rid ourselves of it here, I need you to transport it over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. They have some good people there who don't have ethical qualms about destroying any kind of trash, even if a limb or two is dangling out of the crate.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thanks. Now we have them off our hands. The garbage, I mean.  Off our hands.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Our people at a nearby station are in need of more firepower. They are going to have to subdue unruly refugees from destroyed colonies and crews from recently destroyed ships.

I know it sounds ludicrous. The thing is, when you have near-death experiences of that kind, you may come to the realization that life is fickle, short and dangerous, and that everything you took for granted may be taken from you in the blink of an eye. It tends to upset people, make them aggressive and reckless.

That is, if they're mortal. You being a capsuleer, you'll just have to take my word for it. I'm sure death has a great impact on your sense of the world, but thus far in my experience, it doesn't make you half as crazy as near-death, and at least your type has the sense to take it outside when you feel the need to blow something up.

Incidentally, there are always claims - by silly local news outlets nobody listens to - that representatives of our corporation may not always react immediately when they hear that people are floating out there in escape pods, waiting in to be rescued. Do not let those claims bother you. Those same people are sitting in the midst of a deadly capsuleer battlefield and are in dire need of learning the blessed virtue of patience.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm disappointed. I hope you're not siding with these rebellious people.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Alright. We'll have to find other ways of subduing them, then.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I know you have plenty of firepower, too, but let's leave this one to station personnel.

messages.mission.briefing.text: We have a small outburst of violent behavior to deal with on a nearby station. Refugees from interstellar violence have begun gathering forces and are demanding compensation, hearings and whatnot. Now, this is just a damn stupid situation, and we have people who can put it right, but they need a bit of a boost. That's where you come in. Transport these large crates of small arms to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and we'll take it from there.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Thanks! And don't feel bad for those people - I'm sure there'll be some survivors.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Quafe is preparing for one of their routine planetside campaigns, and as a premium they want to offer special bottles of the ubiquitous drink.

To be honest, there is nothing special about the drink. It's the same cola, with the same water, color, sugar, additives and perfectly legal trace elements, that you'd find on any civilized planet in the cluster. What's important isn't so much the brand as the bottles themselves . They were manufactured on another planet, so their design is subtly different from what's available where you're taking them, and the labeling indicates their origins.

People go crazy for this stuff. I'm serious. This will be hard for a capsuleer to understand, but most people don't even travel that much between the continents on their own planets. To hold in your hand an item that was manufactured in another solar system is an experience that's truly special to a huge number of people.

This only works for things like Quafe, mind you. Taking anything this thoroughly familiar and changing it just slightly has a higher excitement freakout value than even if you'd brought in some unknown artifact made by actual aliens.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: That's a disappointment. If you and your crew drank it all, it's okay to say so. You're not the only ones with a habit.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: You sure? But everybody loves Quafe!

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Keep moving. I don't trust the sealants on those crates, and I'd hate for the Quafe to go flat.

messages.mission.briefing.text: You have a juicy and slightly sticky mission on your hands. Quafe is conducting one of their local marketing campaigns and are in need of exotic drinks - which in this case means another shipment of Quafe manufactured in another solar system. Bring these large crates of quafe over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and you'll make a lot of thirsty people very happy.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Perfect. Help yourself to a nice, cool, fizzy drink as a reward.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
You capsuleers are amazing. Not only have you got the interstellar corporations doing crazy business in ore, minerals, modules and ammunition, but you also routinely exhaust our storages for the equipment that's required to even keep you people in the air. I need you to transport something that's vital for your own continued success.

I'm not referring to the capsules themselves or the unimaginably complex electronics that help you interface with your ship. No, this is something much more mundane. We need to replenish our vats of pod fluid, and for that, we need ectoplasm. This way, whenever you visit our fair station, we can drain and replace your capsule if our tests show that its contents have become a little too stale.

Also, should you have a clone contract with any of our stations and later on find yourself inconvenienced to the point of ... well, to the point of death, we want to ensure that we can put you into a new capsule filled to the brim with pod fluid that's proper, fresh and new. Nothing's quite as disgusting as waking up in a brand new body only to realize that it's been plunged into someone else's used pod fluid.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Really? Alright, but don't be surprised if your pod starts to thicken up a little in time.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: Fair enough. Keep floating in your own goo, then.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: You'll ... not want to taste the cargo. Trust me.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Our pod fluid vats in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} are in dire need of refilling, lest you find yourself floating in something that's more like a swamp lake after a hot summer. Collect from your hangar those large crates of ectoplasm we dredged up and haul them over there as soon as you can!

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Wonderful. We'll happily let you try out the first batch.

localizedName.text: Whispers in the Dark - First Contact (1 of 4)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
So good to see you, {[character]player.name}. I've been on a pretty tight schedule for the past two weeks, ever since we discovered the strange, and increasing, Serpentis activity in the system. Our CEO demands an explanation, yet we still don't know enough about the situation to determine what's really going on. And that's where you come in.

Serpentis activity on this scale in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} is unheard of, and quite frankly we aren't well enough prepared at the moment to deal with any major conflict with them. Not only that, but those greedy pirates are insatiable, and news of their appearance around here has sent the trade lanes into a state of panic. People are leaving this station already, making my superiors ... less than content if you know what I mean. We're losing good people because of this unacceptable situation and we need to put an end to it.

The first thing I want you to do is undertake a reconnaisance mission for us into an area where we have witnessed most of the Serpentis activity. We've already lost a few patrols that ventured into this area, so be careful. If you do find any Serpentis ships out there, eliminate them. We don't want any prisoners, interrogating these deviants won't do us any good. Report your findings to me a.s.a.p.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Watch your back out there, {[character]player.name}.  And whatever you do, don't let them take you prisoner, I've heard they have some insidious ways of making you spill your secrets...

localizedName.text: Whispers in the Dark - Lay And Pray (2 of 4)

messages.mission.briefing.text: Because of your successful reconnaissance mission, we've managed to narrow down the location of the main Serpentis activity a bit.  The data that we extracted from your system scanner also revealed to us a few Serpentis ships that were not mentioned in your preliminary report.  It appears to be some sort of convoy, at least one of their ships was clearly an industrial.  Because of this we guess that it may be a routine shipment, meaning that they might get a convoy at regular intervals.  We'd like you to fly out there, preferably with a cloaking device, and lay in wait for any possible sign of another Serpentis convoy.  If you do see one, destroy it and bring back the contents of the industrials to me for inspection.

messages.mission.completed.nextmission.a.text: Construction blocks?  I was afraid of that.  This doesn't seem to be a mere smuggling operation, but something much more sinister.  But we still don't know what they are building ... And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!

localizedName.text: Whispers in the Dark - The Spy Drones (3 of 4)

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Now that we've established the general location of the Serpentis activity within {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}, it's actually time to find out exactly what they are building. In your last mission you destroyed one of their construction block transports, but this brings us no closer to finding their base of operations. We've had no luck interrogating these pirates before, and the surveillance teams we have sent to investigate the area have either found nothing or disappeared. This leaves us with very few options. But after brainstorming possible solutions to our problem, I came up with a devious plan.

We have in our possession so called 'spy drones', straight from our science labs, which attach themselves to a nearby ships hull and emits a low frequency signal which is picked up by one of our beacons which are strewn around {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}, which in turn sends a high frequency signal to our control tower in {[location]agentStationID.name}.

Now we know that an agent of the Serpentis Corporation regularly picks up shipments of Ectoplasm at a certain station near here. If we can place the spy drone into his next shipment, this might allow us to track his ship to its destination.

Our men have placed beacons throughout our constellation, so everything is in place. All you need to do is take these crates filled with ectoplasm, and our spy drones, to the station specified in the mission details, our agents there will take care of the rest. With luck we'll soon know the location of the Serpentis base.

localizedName.text: Whispers in the Dark - The Outpost (4 of 4)

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Magnificent job, {[character]player.name}.  Those Serpentis really put up a fight didn't they?  However I believe you've done as much for us as we can possibly expect of you, the Serpentis data sheets you brought back with you have confirmed our worst fears, the Serpentis Corporation has a fully functional colony inside {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}!  It will take a massive force to take it out, and we can't expect you to handle a mission like that yet.  Good luck on your future endeavors.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
After reviewing the intel we received from the spy drones which you transferred for us in your last mission, we managed to pinpoint the location of a military outpost they are building in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It appears to be a part of a defensive perimeter that they are setting up around their territory, which has elevated our fears that they have actually managed to erect a large colony inside our solarsystem.

But for now let's keep our sights on the current task, to breach a hole in their defensive wall. We believe that the outpost in question hasn't been fully built, and therefore will be a fairly easy target for you if it's defensive installations aren't complete. Contact with the spy drones was cut off before we could fully analyze the Serpentis forces in the area. But one thing's for sure, there will most certainly be guards nearby, and they will have to be dealt with. You will receive a bookmark to the location of the outpost, and your instructions are simple, destroy the habitat of their construction workers. That should slow them down a bit. Good luck.

I have a special optional mission for you, we won’t penalize you if you decline it.

A single individual, a rogue element of the Angel Cartel, has struck out on their own. We don't know why, but we want you to hunt them down.
They have all scans open, so we can't go there in force. We've acquired their coordinates and need someone to sneak in and take them out. It's you against them.

Only frigate sized ships can gain entry to the hideout, so don’t try to bring anything bigger.
This pirate will be flying a shield boosted Dramiel frigate, with an extremely small signature radius. He tends to deal most of his damage with Domination Fusion ammo, supplemented with Mjolnir rockets. Survivors of his previous attacks claim that he likes to orbit his opponents at very close range at high speed to make himself hard to hit. He always flies with a Stasis Webifier and Warp Scrambler fit.

A word of warning: this rogue pirate is extremely dangerous and has proven very capable of destroying capsuleer ships. If you choose to decline this mission or if you fail to complete it, you will not lose any standings.

messages.mission.complete.charsays.text: He's dead, now where's my money?!

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: No hard feelings, not everyone is capable of taking on a pirate this brutal.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: No hard feelings, not everyone is capable of taking on a pirate this brutal.

messages.mission.accept.charsays.text: He's as good as dead!

I have a special optional and extremely difficult mission for you, we won’t penalize you if you decline it.

It appears that a small group of Serpentis corporation test pilots have absconded with some prototype battlecruisers being developed for smuggling operations. We’ve located three of these pilots in a base they’ve established not far from here.
They have all scans open, so we can't go there in force. If you accept this mission, it's you against them.

Only medium sized ships can gain entry to the hideout, so don’t try to bring anything bigger.
These rogue pirates are flying advanced prototype battlecruisers capable of dealing damage at long range. Our intelligence reports indicate that they are armed with railguns loaded with Spike ammunition. Survivors of our last failed attack against their compound indicate that they use long ranges combined with powerful sensor dampeners to avoid danger. Their base is also equipped with a huge minefield of proximity-activated autoturrets. These turrets deal EM damage and will cause you problems if they activate, but they remain dormant unless a ship enters within 10km of them. Fly carefully to avoid the turrets. These pirates always fly with a Warp Disruptors fit.

A word of warning: these rogue pirates are extremely dangerous and have proven very capable of destroying capsuleer ships. If you choose to decline this mission or if you fail to complete it, you will not lose any standings.

It appears that some local Blood Raider conflicts over Sani Sabik religions doctrine have boiled over and caused a prominent pirate captain to declare herself independent from the rest of the Covenant. This particular pirate seems obsessed with the Drifters and is collecting capsuleer bodies to use as some sort of “bait” for attracting them. She has started to collect her own fanatical followers and this could get out of hand quickly if not dealt with soon.
They have all scans open, so we can't go there in force. If you accept this mission, it's you against them.

Only medium sized ships can gain entry to the hideout, so don’t try to bring anything bigger.
This rogue pirate is flying an extremely well fitted Ashimmu cruiser sporting powerful Nosferatu modules and long-range Stasis Webifiers. Our intelligence reports indicate that she is armed with beam lasers that deal EM and Thermal damage.
She also has two wingmen flying Sentinel class Electronic Attack Frigates. The Sentinel wingmen are equipped with autocannons loaded with Barrage ammo. They also sport extremely effective tracking disruptors and have been seen supporting their leader by destroying any hostile drones they see. These pirates always fly with a Warp Scrambler and long-range Stasis Webifiers fit.

A word of warning: these rogue pirates are extremely dangerous and have proven very capable of destroying capsuleer ships. If you choose to decline this mission or if you fail to complete it, you will not lose any standings.

The Wyvern-class Supercarrier Antero was recently stolen from the Caldari by a group of hijackers funded by the Guristas. They seem to have somehow double-crossed their employers, and now both the Caldari Navy and the Guristas are after them. Their Supercarrier is severely damaged, but still commands a powerful contingent of heavily modified fighters.
I wouldn’t normally care too much about this ship, except that it just showed up outside a nearby repair depot demanding repairs and threatening violence. If they damage that depot I’m going to personally lose a significant investment, and we can’t let that happen. If you accept this mission, you’ll need to get over there and convince them that there are better depots to hold up than mine. There’s no way that you’ll be able to kill it, but if you wipe out enough of its fighters I’m sure they’ll get the hint.

Only medium sized ships can gain entry to the repair yard, so don’t try to bring anything bigger.
These rogue pirates have waves of heavily modified fighters and fighter bombers with strong shield tanks and small signatures. They deal all four damage types, with their modified Dragonfly fighters spewing Explosive, Kinetic and Thermal at close range, and their modified Mantis fighter-bombers lobbing EM damage from longer ranges. They always fly with Stasis Webifiers and Warp Scramblers fit. To save my repair depot you’ll need to keep destroying waves of fighters until the Wyvern decides to cut its losses and leave.

A word of warning: these rogue pirates are extremely dangerous and have proven very capable of destroying capsuleer ships. If you choose to decline this mission or if you fail to complete it, you will not lose any standings.

Several survey vessels are sent to collect asteroid data from nearby systems. We have lost contact with one of them. This happens occasionally and it's probably nothing to be worried about. Find the survey vessel and get their data dump. If worse comes to worst, just retrieve the black box. This mission requires a Data Analyzer.

Our ships are armed so unless it's a serious threat, they should be able to handle most problems. Yet we've lost another one in the area.

We've narrowed it down to a listening post nearby. According to their latest reports, logistics say the post had been requesting more replacement parts than usual. Make of that what you will.

Good luck.

Drones going rogue? How does this even happen? They've been stealing parts from our long-range survey towers for a while. Now they are attacking our survey ships. This has to stop.

Based on data from numerous sources, we've found a gathering of these drones. A nest, if you will. Destroy them.

We have located a couple of wrecks. It doesn't matter to us what happened but we got the salvage rights. Well, it seems someone else has been stealthily salvaging them. That won't do.

Bring back the scrap metal and black boxes, you can keep the rest.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
Hello there, Captain. I could use your help.

A close friend of mine who was working at ORE, Batya Sarnai, is missing, presumed dead. No one will tell me or her family what happened. I need your help to uncover the truth.

I’ve tracked down her old work crew and got you on their work roster. I need you to go uncover as an ORE miner, hack their mainframe, and steal any data on Sarnai.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text:
Elias' friend Sarnai is missing, presumed dead, and he wants your help finding out what happened. 

Disguise yourself as a member of Sarnai’s old ORE work crew so you can hack their mainframe and steal any data on why Sarnai went missing.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: I'm disappointed, but I understand. Fly safe.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text:
I cannot say I am not disappointed.

If you change your mind, come back and see me. My friend deserves justice, and I need your help to get it.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: You snuck onto an ORE work crew to retrieve information about the missing Sarnai. The data you found points to some unique mineral isotopes. Perhaps Elias knows someone who can help.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Incredible, together we can figure out what is going on here. I will see you at the ORE site.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
A close friend of mine who was working at ORE, Batya Sarnai, is missing, presumed dead. No one will tell me or her family what happened. I need your help to uncover the truth.

I’ve tracked down her old work crew and got you on their work roster. I need you to go undercover as an ORE miner, hack their mainframe, and steal any data on Sarnai.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Those ORE miners will not be happy that we stole their data, but it was worth it.

The data contains the details of some unique mineral isotopes. Why Sarnai’s name is listed alongside them, I don’t know, but I may just know someone who can help us make sense of this.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text:
Need a reminder? No problem.

A close friend of mine who was working at ORE, Batya Sarnai, is missing, presumed dead. No one will tell me or her family what happened. I need your help to uncover the truth.

I’ve tracked down her old work crew and got you on their work roster. I need you to go undercover as an ORE miner, hack their mainframe, and steal any data on Sarnai.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
We’ve got the data, now we just need to know what it means.

The good news, a friend of mine in the Sisters of EVE has agreed to help us investigate the mineral isotopes mentioned alongside Sarnai in the data. Even better, he says he’s managed to track some of them down. The only snag is that he needs our help to investigate them.

I’ve sent the coordinates to your ship’s computer. Meet him at the site with a mining ship and a surveyor, and help him investigate the correct isotopes.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text:
Elias' friend in the Sisters of EVE has agreed to help us investigate these mineral isotopes. Even better, he says he’s managed to track some of them down. The only snag is that he needs your help to investigate them.

Elias has sent the coordinates to your ship’s computer. Meet the SOE scientist at the site. Bring a mining ship and a surveyor, and help him investigate the correct isotopes.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: When we were so close...? Alright. Goodbye.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text:
Damn, without your help this data is just useless bytes.

If you change your mind, come and see me again.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: With the help of Brother Jacques Quelouse of the SOE, you were able to determine the isotopes' origin, an explosion at an unknown Upwell facility. Investigating that sight may just give Elias the answers he seeks.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: I was hoping you would say that. Now, let’s go see a man about some rocks.

messages.mission.briefing.text:
Good news, a friend of mine in the Sisters of EVE has agreed to help us investigate these mineral isotopes. Even better, he says he’s managed to track some of them down. The only snag is that he needs our help to investigate them.

I’ve sent the coordinates to your ship’s computer. Meet him at the site with a mining ship and a surveyor, and help him investigate the correct isotopes.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text: Brother Jaques sent us the isotopes' points of origin. When you’re ready, come speak to me again, and we can finally find out the truth.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text:
Need a reminder? No problem.

The good news, a friend of mine in the Sisters of EVE has agreed to help us investigate the mineral isotopes mentioned alongside Sarnai in the data. Even better, he says he’s managed to track some of them down. The only snag is that he needs our help to investigate them.

I’ve sent the coordinates to your ship’s computer. Meet him at the site with a mining ship and a surveyor, and help him investigate the correct isotopes.

messages.mission.offered.agentsays.text:
This is it.

Whatever happened to Sarnai happened at this abandoned Upwell site. With your help we can uncover the truth and give Sarnai’s legacy the ending it deserves.

messages.epicMission.journalText.inProgr.text: Whatever happened to Sarnai happened at this abandoned Upwell site. With your help, Elias can uncover the truth and give Sarnai’s legacy the ending it deserves.

messages.mission.quitted.agentsays.text: Fine. Goodbye.

messages.mission.declined.agentsays.text: What! We’re in too deep to quit now. Please, think it over, come back and talk to me. I know you’ll do the right thing.

messages.epicMission.journalText.complet.text: Batya Sarnai’s tale has come to an end. Elias has learned the truth and can be satisfied that he gave Sarnai’s legacy the honor it deserves.

messages.mission.accepted.agentsays.text: Time for the grand finale, let’s head out.

messages.mission.briefing.text: Whatever happened to Sarnai happened at this abandoned Upwell site. With your help we can uncover the truth and give Sarnai’s legacy the ending it deserves.

messages.mission.completed.agentsays.text:
Finally, I can put Sarnai to rest. It’s not what she deserved, she deserved to live a full life, grow old, and die in comfort. But, it’s what she would have wanted, and there’s honor in that.

Thank you, Captain, I couldn't have made it through without you.

messages.root.missioninprogress.agentsay.text:
No need to wait around.

Whatever happened to Sarnai happened at this abandoned Upwell site. With your help we can uncover the truth and give Sarnai’s legacy the ending it deserves.
